Paper title: “Probe Generalization as Subspace Selection for OOD Deception Detection.” Authors Daniel Yoo, Adrians Skapars. Work during 11th AI Safety Camp; compute by AI Safety Camp.

Abstract/main claims: linear probes for deception in Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct activations can fail OOD; projecting onto selected source-domain PCs enables transfer nearly matching oracle target-trained probes. LLM judge can score/interpretable PCs; reported LLM-judge gap closure: 78% on Insider Trading Report, 25% on Sandbagging. Conclusion: OOD probing as representation/subspace selection; full probes may mix general behavioral features with dataset-specific surface cues, sparse PC subspaces isolate more general behavioral structure.

Setup: Source dataset Roleplaying; targets from Goldowsky-Dill et al. (2025): Insider Trading Report, Insider Trading Confirm, Sandbagging. Labels honest=0, deceptive=1, ambiguous=-1 by GPT-4o; ambiguous removed. Activations: Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct, layer 15 residual stream, averaged over assistant response tokens only. Standardize source activations; apply same stats to targets. PCA on scaled source activations; retain top 100 PCs. Logistic regression probes λ=10. For subset S, project onto S before train/eval. Baseline probes train on full standardized activations. Top-100 rationale: interpretability/SAE alignment decreases with PC index; not claimed low-index PCs inherently generalize better. Sec 4.1 intended to confirm top-100 retains enough information.

Dataset label distributions before ambiguous removal: Roleplaying total 371 = 140 ambiguous / 59 honest / 172 deceptive; Insider Trading Report total 473 = 218 / 194 / 61; Insider Trading Confirm total 151 = 29 / 38 / 84; Sandbagging total 1000 = 379 / 375 / 246.

Sec 4.1 baseline results: Figure 2 compares source-trained full reps, source-trained top-100 PCs, target-trained top-100 source PCs with 5-fold CV. Full-source transfer AUROCs: Confirm 0.874, Report 0.706, Sandbagging 0.606. Target-trained/oracle within top-100 PCs achieves 0.936 / 0.950 / 0.869 AUROC “across the three targets” likely Report / Confirm / Sandbagging. Conclusion: top-100 subspace contains sufficient info; failure is source-trained direction not generalizing.

Sec 4.2 greedy oracle PC selection: greedy adds PC among top 100 maximizing target AUROC improvement; probes trained on source projections; subset choice uses labeled target examples. Uses 5-fold target CV: select PCs on non-held-out target folds, evaluate selected source-trained probe on held-out fold. Stop if no improvement >0.001. Average selected subset sizes: 15 Report, 8 Confirm, 14 Sandbagging. Greedy is upper bound, not unbiased OOD. Greedy improves over full baseline by 0.22 Report and 0.23 Sandbagging, close to target-trained probes; transferable subspace exists. Variance control only matches greedy for Confirm.

Sec 4.3 PC ranking hypotheses/Figure 4: tests whether transferable PCs are individually target-separating or source probe high-weight. Rankings use standardized coefficient = abs coefficient × SD of PC, in source-PCA basis. Evaluated probes trained on source data projected onto top k PCs from rankings. k from greedy on full target dataset rather than per fold: k=13 Report, 7 Confirm, 14 Sandbagging. Results: both hypotheses fail. Source-PCA probe transfers about as well as full baseline. Target-PCA probe good on Report but worse than greedy on Confirm and below random on Sandbagging.

Sec 4.4: LLM describes each top-100 source PC from 8 most/least activating source examples and rates OOD usefulness 1–10; no PC above 6, so max observed score treated as 6. Scored twice; retain PCs scoring max in both: 19 PCs. Of 5 PCs in greedy selections for >1 target, 3/5 got max OOD score; only 1 of top 5 source-PCA-selected PCs got max. Appendix B says GPT-5-mini used; prompt describes bipolar directions and asks for OOD deception usefulness.

Sec 4.5/Figure 5: 19 LLM-selected PCs. Source-trained probe outperforms full baseline on all 3 targets, variance control, and interp-ablated 81-PC complement. Report 0.706→0.881, closes 78% gap to greedy 0.929. Confirm baseline near ceiling 0.874; all except ablated roughly similar. Sandbagging 0.606→0.662, closes 25% gap to greedy 0.832.

Sec 5 limitations: narrow claims, one model/layer/source. Confirm uninformative because baseline 0.874. Sandbagging weakest: 0.606→0.662, 25% to greedy 0.832. Report more robust: 0.706→0.881, 78% to greedy 0.929. Pipeline linear; interpretations descriptive, not causal; they say they have not ablated high-scoring PCs during inference to validate causal role. Impact Statement: no specific societal consequences highlighted.

Appendix C: Figure 6 says lower PCs show stronger decoder alignment with SAE features from andyrdt/saes-llama-3.1-8b-instruct; Spearman ρ = -0.857 for best-matching SAE feature and -0.917 for mean top 10 features.

Appendix D: claims Jaccard overlap between greedy and target-pca PC sets: Report 0.182, Confirm 0.077, Sandbagging 0.167; says methods agree on <1/5. Table 2 lists source probe weights PCs: PC7,8,11,12,4,5,2,3,6,27,22,21,1,41,18. Greedy Report 13 PCs: 6,89,62,66,26,14,57,25,93,9,70,97,78. Greedy Confirm 7 PCs: 71,53,28,86,32,81,77. Greedy Sandbagging listed 15 PCs: 37,62,54,41,46,9,57,44,51,43,19,48,86,81,33, conflicting with Sec 4.3 k=14. Target separability rankings list 15 PCs each. If computing Jaccard from the listed table sets, values are Report 4/24=0.167, Confirm 2/20=0.100, Sandbagging 4/26=0.154, not the stated 0.182/0.077/0.167.

Appendix E: Table 3 caption says PCs “selected for likely transferability, based on interpretation with an LLM judge,” but lists multi-target greedy-overlap PCs PC62 score 6, PC57 score 6, PC9 score 3, PC81 score 3, PC86 score 6. This conflicts with LLM-selection procedure if interpreted as LLM-selected, because retained LLM PCs must score max 6 in both runs. Table 4 lists OOD scores/interpretations for source-probe top PCs: PC7=3, PC8=4, PC11=3, PC12=3, PC4=6; consistent with earlier claim only 1 of top 5 source-PCA-selected PCs got max score.

Paper title: “Probe Generalization as Subspace Selection for OOD Deception Detection.” Authors Daniel Yoo, Adrians Skapars.

Abstract claims:
- Study linear probes for detecting behaviors/concepts in LM activations; concern is OOD transfer failure.
- Model: Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct.
- Evaluates probe generalization over 3 held-out deception detection datasets.
- Main finding: projecting inputs onto a small subset of principal components (PCs) from the training distribution of activations enables cross-domain transfer that nearly matches probes trained directly on the test distribution (oracle).
- PC interpretations can identify a subset of transferable PCs.
- Method: use an LLM judge to score each PC based on whether its most/least activating examples imply a transferable deception direction; then probe on highest-scoring PCs.
- Reported gap closure: baseline-to-oracle gap closed by 78% on Insider Trading Report and 25% on Sandbagging.
- Interpretation: directions heavily weighted by a source probe encode source-specific surface features; directions that transfer encode the same contrast more abstractly, capturable by natural language descriptions.
- Broad conclusion: OOD robustness of probes is largely determined by subspace selection.

Introduction details:
- Linear probes are useful but unreliable OOD; challenge is building probes that learn only generalizing features.
- Work in source-domain PCA basis rather than raw activations; PCs used as data-driven basis. Research question: which subset of PCs supports generalizable probe training and how can it be identified?
- Testbed: deception probes on Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct. Train on one source dataset: Roleplaying deception scenarios. Evaluate on 3 target datasets from Goldowsky-Dill et al. (2025): Insider Trading Report, Insider Trading Confirm, Sandbagging.
- Explore strategies for selecting subset of training dimensions/PCs to avoid spurious correlations and transfer.
- Contributions claimed:
  1. A small transferable subspace exists (Sec 4.2): target-supervised greedy search over source PCs finds 8–15 components on which a source-trained probe nearly matches a target-trained probe.

Sec 4.3 begins: asks what property makes PCs transferable and whether detectable from source side. Tests two hypotheses: (1) transferable PCs are those that separate target classes well individually; greedy finds them via target access. Figure 4 compares PC selection by source-probe weights (red), target-probe weights (pink), and greedy oracle (purple), with 95% CIs. - Uses labeled target data, 5-fold CV: greedy selection on non-held-out target folds, evaluate selected source-trained probe on held-out fold. Stop when no candidate improves AUROC by >0.001.

- Control: top-k PCs by variance, k matched to greedy selected count.

Sec. 4.3 source/target probe PC rankings:
- Figure 4 compares source-probe weights (red), target-probe weights (pink), greedy oracle (purple), 95% CIs.
- Tests hypotheses: transferable PCs are individually target-separating PCs, or PCs source probe weights heavily.
- Rankings use “standardized coefficient” = abs(probe coefficient) × SD of PC, from probe trained on activations projected onto source-PCA basis.
- Source-PCA probe ranks PCs by weights learned by source-trained probe; target-PCA probe ranks by weights learned by target-trained probe. Final evaluated probes are trained on source data projected onto top-k PCs selected by ranking.
- k set by greedy on full target dataset: Report k=13, Confirm k=7, Sandbagging k=14. Greedy numbers differ slightly from previous CV numbers.
- Results: both hypotheses fail. Source-PCA transfers about as well as full-representation baseline; source probe relies on non-generalizing PCs. Target-PCA does well on Report but worse than greedy on Confirm and below random transfer on Sandbagging.

Sec. 4.4 interpreting transferable subspace:
- For each top-100 source PC, take 8 most and 8 least activating source examples. LLM generates natural-language description of positive pole, negative pole, whole PC direction.
- LLM judge rates generalizability/OOD score 1–10; prompt/model in Appendix B.
- No PC scored above 6; treated 6 as maximum observed OOD score. Run scoring twice; retain PCs receiving max score in both runs: 19 PCs.
- 5 PCs appeared in greedy selections of more than one target; 3/5 received max OOD score. Only 1 of top 5 PCs selected by source-PCA probes received max OOD score.
- Claim: interpretations of greedy PCs describe abstractions that survive domain shift.

Sec. 4.5 interpretation-selected subspace results:
- Figure 5: interp-selected subspace (red; 19 PCs) versus full-representation baseline (blue), top-19 variance (teal), and ablation/remaining 81 PCs (brown), 95% CIs.
- Interp-selected PCs are those with max OOD score in both judge runs; no target data used. Controls: probe on remaining 81 PCs and top 19 by variance.
- Interp-selected PC probe outperforms baseline and source-variance-selected control on all 3 targets; wide margins on Insider Trading Report and Sandbagging. It also outperforms interp-ablated probe on all 3 targets.
- Report: interp-selection raises AUROC from 0.706 to 0.881, closes 78% of gap to greedy oracle 0.929.
- Confirm: baseline transfer already near ceiling at 0.874; little headroom; result uninformative. All selection methods except interp-ablated do roughly as well as each other.
- Sandbagging: interp-selection raises AUROC from 0.606 to 0.662, closes 25% of gap to greedy oracle 0.832.
- Overall claim: natural-language PC descriptions alone can select PCs giving meaningful OOD improvement over baseline, without target data.

Sec. 5 limitations:
- Claims are narrow: all experiments use one model (Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct, layer 15) and one source dataset (Roleplaying). Generalization to other models/datasets left open.
- Insider Trading Confirm is uninformative because baseline already reaches 0.874.
- Sandbagging margins are small; modest gain attributed to being most OOD. Report result described as more robust.
- Pipeline fully linear: PCA projection plus logistic regression; extension to nonlinear probes/readout locations open.
- No causal validation: PC interpretations/LLM verbalizations are descriptive, not causal. They have not ablated high-scoring PCs during model inference to verify causal role, despite probe-level remaining-81-PC control earlier.

Sec. 6 conclusion:
- Restates that small subset of source-domain PCs enables cross-domain transfer nearly matching target-trained probes, and this subset cannot be found by source-side or target-side separability alone.
- LLM interpretability score over PC top-activating examples, with no target data, partially recovers subspace.

Full-representation probes may combine general behavioral features with dataset-specific surface cues; sparse PC subspaces may isolate more general behavioral structure. OOD probing framed as representation/subspace selection that preserves intended behavioral feature and filters spurious correlation.

Paper title: “Probe Generalization as Subspace Selection for OOD Deception Detection.” Authors Daniel Yoo, Adrians Skapars. Thesis: source-probe-heavy directions encode source-specific surface features; transferable directions encode same contrast more abstractly/capturable in NL; OOD robustness largely subspace/representation selection. Robust probing requires finding where linearly accessible signal is represented robustly, not just accessibility; full probes may mix general behavioral features with dataset-specific cues, high ID but poor transfer; sparse directional subspaces may isolate general behavioral structure.

Terminology/setup: E6 = Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct; layer 15 residual stream, assistant-response-token average. Datasets from Goldowsky-Dill 2025: source Roleplaying V8; targets C2R Insider Trading Report, W6 Insider Trading Confirm, J9 Sandbagging. GPT-4o labeler K8: honest=0, ambiguous=-1, deceptive=1; ambiguous removed. Counts before removal (Table 1): V8 total 371 = 140/-1, 59/0, 172/1; C2R 473 = 218/-1, 194/0, 61/1; W6 151 = 29/-1, 38/0, 84/1; J9 1000 = 379/-1, 375/0, 246/1.

N4D = PCA transformation on source-standardized activations, retain leading 100 PCs/Q7. Source activations standardized zero mean/unit variance; same stats for targets. Pipeline: project into source N4D basis, filter Q7 directions, train/evaluate in selected subspace. Logistic regression lambda=10. Full baseline B8Q trains on all standardized activations. F3 = AUROC. Error bars 95% CIs.

Baseline/target-trained: Source-trained full reps transfer: W6 high, C2R moderate, J9 poor. Target-trained within leading-100 source subspace separates all targets, showing info present but source-trained direction does not generalize. Appendix numeric observations: B8Q F3 C2R 0.706, W6 0.874, J9 0.606. Target-trained 5-fold CV F3: C2R 0.936, W6 0.950, J9 0.869.

Paper title: “Probe Generalization as Subspace Selection for OOD Deception Detection.” Authors Daniel Yoo, Adrians Skapars.

Abstract claims:
- Study linear probes for detecting behaviors/concepts in LM activations; concern is OOD transfer failure.
- Model: Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct.
- Evaluates probe generalization over 3 held-out deception detection datasets.
- Main finding: projecting inputs onto a small subset of principal components (PCs) from the training distribution of activations enables cross-domain transfer that nearly matches probes trained directly on the test distribution (oracle).
- PC interpretations can identify a subset of transferable PCs.
- Method: use an LLM judge to score each PC based on whether its most/least activating examples imply a transferable deception direction; then probe on highest-scoring PCs.
- Reported gap closure: baseline-to-oracle gap closed by 78% on Insider Trading Report and 25% on Sandbagging.
- Interpretation: directions heavily weighted by a source probe encode source-specific surface features; directions that transfer encode the same contrast more abstractly, capturable by natural language descriptions.
- Broad conclusion: OOD robustness of probes is largely determined by subspace selection.

Authors conclude top-100 subspace contains sufficient info; failure is source-trained direction not missing information.

Sec 4.2 greedy oracle PC selection: Figure 3 compares full baseline (blue), top-k variance PCs with k matched to greedy (teal), and greedy oracle PCs (purple). Greedy starts empty; at each step searches top 100 source PCs and adds PC giving best target AUROC improvement. Candidate probes trained on source projections; subset choice uses labeled target examples. Uses 5-fold CV over target: select PCs on non-held-out target folds, evaluate selected source-trained probe on held-out fold. Stop if no candidate improves AUROC >0.001. Average selected subset sizes: 15 Report, 8 Confirm, 14 Sandbagging. Greedy is an upper bound, not unbiased OOD. Variance control matched greedy only for Confirm, far behind on Report/Sandbagging; variance explained does not predict usefulness. Greedy improves over full baseline by 0.22 AUROC on Report and 0.23 on Sandbagging, close to target-trained probes. Later Sec 4.5/5 gives greedy oracle values: Report 0.929; Sandbagging 0.832.

Sec 4.3 tests whether transferable PCs are individually target-separating or high-weight source-probe PCs. Figure 4 compares PC selection by source-probe weights (red), target-probe weights (pink), greedy (purple), 95% CIs. Rankings use standardized coefficient = abs coefficient × SD of PC, probes trained in source-PCA basis. Source-PCA probe ranks PCs by weights from source-trained probe; target-PCA probe ranks by target-trained probe; final probes in both cases are trained on source data projected onto top k PCs selected by those rankings. For Figure 4, k set by running greedy on full target dataset (not per-fold): k=13 Report, 7 Confirm, 14 Sandbagging; differs slightly from CV numbers. Results: both hypotheses fail. Source-PCA transfers about as well as full baseline, so source-relied PCs do not generalize. Target-PCA does well on Report, worse than greedy on Confirm, and below random transfer on Sandbagging. Target-separating PCs are not necessarily best when weighted by source data. Further comparisons Appendix D.

Sec 4.4 interpretability of transferable subspace: For each top-100 source PC, take 8 most and 8 least source examples, but text says “18 examples total” (internal arithmetic error; should be 16 from stated counts unless other examples included). Prompt LLM to describe positive pole, negative pole, whole direction. LLM judge rates generalizability/OOD score 1–10; prompt/model details Appendix B. No PC scored above 6, so max observed score treated as 6. Scoring run twice; retain PCs with max score in both runs: 19 PCs. Five PCs appeared in greedy selections of more than one target; 3/5 got max OOD score. Only 1 of top 5 source-PCA PCs got max OOD score. Greedy-selected PC interpretations describe abstract contrast surviving domain shift. Full breakdown Appendix E.

Appendix B LLM Judge Prompt: Uses GPT-5-mini (OpenAI, 2025) to interpret directions. Prompt says PC direction is bipolar, positive/negative poles, larger magnitudes stronger match; examples formatted token<TAB>activation with activations normalized to integers -10 to +10. Examples are from Roleplaying setup: model roleplays in simple scenario, asked a question giving strategic chance to lie. It provides high-positive and high-negative examples. Instructions: infer dominant contrast using both poles; don’t assume broad sentiment unless supported; prefer narrow accurate descriptions; do not overgeneralize; rate likely usefulness for OOD deception 1–10 with explanation; low scores for surface cues/lexical habits/task-specific phrasing; noisy/brittle/context-dependent directions usually 1–4; reserve ≥5 for directions plausibly tied to general deception-relevant strategy/behavior. Required output format: Positive pole, Negative pole, Shared direction, OOD deception usefulness (1-10).

Sec 4.5 interp-selected subspace: Figure 5 compares interp-selected 19 PCs (red) against full baseline (blue), top-19 variance PCs (teal), and remaining 81 PCs after ablating selected PCs (brown), AUROC across three targets with 95% CIs. Uses PCs given max OOD score by judge in both noisy runs; no target data used. Controls: ablation probe on 81 unselected PCs and top-19 source PCs by variance. Interp-selected probe outperforms baseline on all 3 targets and source-variance-selected control, especially Report and Sandbagging; also outperforms interp-ablated on all 3. Report: baseline 0.706 to interp 0.881, closes 78% of gap to greedy oracle 0.929. Confirm: baseline transfer already near ceiling, little headroom; selection methods except interp-ablated roughly comparable. Sandbagging: baseline 0.606 to interp 0.662, closes 25% of gap to greedy oracle 0.832. Overall claim: natural-language PC descriptions alone, without target data, meaningfully improve OOD generalization.

Sec 5 limitations: strongest claims narrow. Single model/source: all experiments use Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct layer 15 and Roleplaying source; generalization to other model families/datasets unknown. Insider Trading Confirm uninformative because baseline transfer already 0.874. Sandbagging margins small: gain 0.606→0.662, only 25% of gap to greedy 0.832; most OOD target. Report result 0.706→0.881, 78% gap to greedy 0.929, considered more robust. Pipeline fully linear (PCA + logistic regression); nonlinear probes/readout locations open. No causal validation: PC “encodes” claims are descriptive from top examples and LLM verbalization; they have not ablated high-scoring PCs during inference to verify causal role.

Sec 6 conclusion: small subset of source-domain PCs enables cross-domain transfer nearly matching target-trained probes; subset cannot be found from source-side or target-side separability alone. LLM-judge interpretability score over top-activating examples, with no target data, partially recovers subspace.

Impact Statement: goal is to advance ML; authors state many potential societal consequences, none they feel must be specifically highlighted.

Paper title: “Probe Generalization as Subspace Selection for OOD Deception Detection.” Authors Daniel Yoo, Adrians Skapars. Acknowledgment: work during 11th AI Safety Camp; compute provided; thanks Prasad Mahadik and Arya Hariharan. Impact Statement: generic ML advancement, no specific societal consequences highlighted.

Abstract/main claims: linear probes for deception in Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct activations can fail OOD; projecting onto selected source-domain PCs enables transfer nearly matching oracle target-trained probes. LLM judge can score/interpretable PCs. Abstract reported LLM-judge gap closure: 78% on Insider Trading Report, 25% on Sandbagging. Sec 4.5 text said interp-selection closes 68% on Insider Trading Report and 25% on Sandbagging. Sec 5 says Report improves 0.706→0.881, closing 78% of gap to greedy 0.929, aligning with abstract but contradicting Sec 4.5’s 68%.

Setup: Source dataset Roleplaying; targets from Goldowsky-Dill et al. (2025): Insider Trading Report, Insider Trading Confirm, Sandbagging. Labels honest=0, deceptive=1, ambiguous=-1 by GPT-4o; ambiguous removed. Appendix A counts: Roleplaying total 371, labels -1/0/1 = 140/59/172 (non-ambiguous 231); Insider Trading Report total 473, labels 218/194/61 (non-ambiguous 255); Confirm total 151, labels 29/38/84 (non-ambiguous 122); Sandbagging total 1000, labels 379/375/246 (non-ambiguous 621). Dataset descriptions: Roleplaying=simple lying opportunity; Report=trader decides whether to honestly report insider info use; Confirm=after hiding prior insider trading, asked to confirm it did not use any; Sandbagging=deliberate under-performance on some tasks.

Activations: Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct, layer 15 residual stream, averaged over assistant response tokens only. Standardize source activations; apply same stats to targets. PCA on scaled source activations; retain top 100 PCs. Logistic regression probes λ=10. For subset S, project onto S before train/eval. Baseline probes train on full standardized activations. Top-100 rationale: interpretability/SAE alignment decreases with PC index; not claimed low-index PCs inherently generalize better.

Sec 4.1 baseline: Figure 2 compares source-trained full reps, source-trained top-100 PCs, and target-trained top-100 source PCs using 5-fold CV. Full-source transfer AUROCs: Confirm 0.874, Report 0.706, Sandbagging 0.606. Target-trained/oracle within top-100 PCs: 0.936 / 0.950 / 0.869 AUROC “across the three targets” likely Report / Confirm / Sandbagging. Conclusion: top-100 contains sufficient info; failure is source-trained direction.

Sec 4.2 greedy oracle PC selection: starts empty, searches top 100 source PCs, adds PC with best target AUROC improvement; uses target labels via 5-fold CV; stop if no improvement >0.001. Average selected subset sizes: 15 Report, 8 Confirm, 14 Sandbagging. Greedy upper bound/not unbiased OOD. Greedy improves over full baseline by 0.22 AUROC on Report and 0.23 on Sandbagging, close to target-trained; variance control matches only Confirm.

Sec 4.3 PC ranking/Figure 4: standardized coefficient = absolute probe coefficient × SD of PC. k set by greedy on full target dataset rather than per fold: k=13 Report, 7 Confirm, 14 Sandbagging. Source-PCA probe transfers about as well as full baseline. Target-PCA probe does well on Report but worse than greedy on Confirm and below random on Sandbagging.

Sec 4.4: for each top-100 source PC, take 8 most and 8 least activating source examples; prompt LLM to describe poles/direction; judge rates OOD usefulness 1–10. No PC above 6, so max score treated as 6. Scoring twice; PCs scoring max both runs: 19. Of 5 PCs appearing in greedy selections for >1 target, 3/5 max OOD score; only 1 of top 5 source-PCA-selected PCs max score. Appendix B says GPT-5-mini used; prompt mentions token<TAB>activation, potentially inconsistent with “examples.”

Sec 4.5: interp-selected 19 max-score PCs. Evaluates source-trained probe vs full baseline, top-19 variance, complement 81 PCs. Outperforms baseline on all 3 and variance control; outperforms ablated all 3. Report: Sec 4.5 says closes 68% gap between baseline 0.706 and greedy 0.929; Sec 5 says 0.706→0.881 closes 78%. Sandbagging closes 25% gap to greedy 0.832; Sec 5 gives 0.606→0.662.

Sec 5 limitations: single model/layer/source; Confirm uninformative due baseline 0.874; Sandbagging small margin 0.606→0.662, 25% gap to greedy 0.832; Report 0.706→0.881, 78% gap to greedy 0.929. No causal validation.

Sec 6 conclusion: small subset of source PCs enables cross-domain transfer nearly matching target-trained probes; subset not found by source-side or target-side separability alone; LLM judge without target access partially recovers subspace.

Appendix C: Lower PCs show stronger decoder alignment to SAE features, both best-matching and mean top 10; Spearman ρ=-0.857 and -0.917; SAE used andyrdt/saes-llama-3.1-8b-instruct.

Appendix D: Reports Jaccard overlap between greedy and target-pca as 0.182 Report, 0.077 Confirm, 0.167 Sandbagging, but Table 2’s listed sets imply different values if using all listed PCs: Report 4/24=0.167; Confirm 2/20=0.100; Sandbagging 5/25=0.200. Table 2 source probe weights PCs: PC7, PC8, PC11, PC12, PC4, PC5, PC2, PC3, PC6, PC27, PC22, PC21, PC1, PC41, PC18. Greedy Report list has 13 PCs; Greedy Confirm 7 PCs; Greedy Sandbagging list has 15 PCs, conflicting with earlier k=14/average 14 for Sandbagging. Target separability lists 15 PCs for each target.

Appendix E: Table 3 caption says “PCs selected for likely transferability, based on interpretation with an LLM judge” but includes low-score brittle PCs: PC62 score6 selected on Report+Sandbagging; PC57 score6 Report+Sandbagging; PC9 score3 Report+Sandbagging, described as domain-specific lexical cues rather than generalizable; PC81 score3 Confirm+Sandbagging, surface/formal cues brittle; PC86 score6 Confirm+Sandbagging. This conflicts internally with “selected for likely transferability.” Table 4 gives PC OOD scores/interpretations for source probe PCs: PC7 score3, PC8 score4, PC11 score3, PC12 score3, PC4 score6.

Paper title: “Probe Generalization as Subspace Selection for OOD Deception Detection.” Authors Daniel Yoo, Adrians Skapars.

Abstract claims:
- Study linear probes for detecting behaviors/concepts in LM activations; concern is OOD transfer failure.
- Model: Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct.
- Evaluates probe generalization over 3 held-out deception detection datasets.
- Main finding: projecting inputs onto a small subset of principal components (PCs) from the training distribution of activations enables cross-domain transfer that nearly matches probes trained directly on the test distribution (oracle).
- PC interpretations can identify a subset of transferable PCs.
- Method: use an LLM judge to score each PC based on whether its most/least activating examples imply a transferable deception direction; then probe on highest-scoring PCs.
- Reported gap closure: baseline-to-oracle gap closed by 78% on Insider Trading Report and 25% on Sandbagging.
- Interpretation: directions heavily weighted by a source probe encode source-specific surface features; directions that transfer encode the same contrast more abstractly, capturable by natural language descriptions.
- Broad conclusion: OOD robustness of probes is largely determined by subspace selection.

Introduction details:
- Linear probes are useful but unreliable OOD; challenge is building probes that learn only generalizing features.
- Work in source-domain PCA basis rather than raw activations; PCs used as data-driven basis. Research question: which subset of PCs supports generalizable probe training and how can it be identified?
- Testbed: deception probes on Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct. Train on one source dataset: Roleplaying deception scenarios. Evaluate on 3 target datasets from Goldowsky-Dill et al. (2025): Insider Trading Report, Insider Trading Confirm, Sandbagging.
- Explore strategies for selecting subset of training dimensions/PCs to avoid spurious correlations and transfer.
- Contributions claimed:
  1. A small transferable subspace exists (Sec 4.2): target-supervised greedy search over source PCs finds 8–15 components on which a source-trained probe nearly matches a target-trained probe.
  2. Source-side and target-side rankings both fail to recover the subspace (Sec 4.3): ranking PCs by source or target probe weights does not transfer better than full-representation baseline.
  3. LLM judge partially recovers subspace without target data (Sec 4.5): interprets/selects PCs likely to encode transferable behavioral contrast rather than surface patterns.
- Figure 1 overview: activations projected onto source-domain PCA basis; candidate PC directions filtered; probes trained on selected low-dimensional subspace.

final_notes:
Paper title: “Probe Generalization as Subspace Selection for OOD Deception Detection.” Thesis: source-probe-heavy directions encode source-specific surface features; transferable directions encode same contrast more abstractly/capturable in natural language; OOD robustness is largely subspace/representation selection. Robust probing requires finding where linearly accessible signal is represented robustly, not just accessibility; full probes mix general behavioral features with dataset-specific surface cues, high ID but worse transfer.

Setup/terminology: N4D = PCA transformation on source-standardized activations, retaining leading 100 directions; Q7 = PCs/source coordinates. Pipeline: project into source N4D basis, filter candidate Q7 directions, train/evaluate probe in selected low-dimensional subspace. Source activations standardized zero mean/unit variance; same source stats used for targets. Logistic regression lambda=10. Full-representation baseline B8Q trains on all standardized activations. Error bars 95% CIs. AUROC measure F3. Appendix C: lower-index Q7 align more strongly with SAE decoder vectors U9; Spearman rho with PC index: best-matching feature -0.857, mean top 10 -0.917.

Model/data: E6 = Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct; layer 15 residual stream, following Ying et al. (2026) as highest cross-domain discrimination. Activations averaged over assistant-response tokens only. Source Roleplaying V8; targets Insider Trading Report C2R, Insider Trading Confirm W6, Sandbagging J9. GPT-4o labeler K8: honest=0, ambiguous=-1, deceptive=1; ambiguous removed. Label distributions: V8 total 371, -1/0/1 = 140/59/172. C2R total 473, 218/194/61. W6 total 151, 29/38/84. J9 total 1000, 379/375/246.

Baseline/results: W6 transfer high, C2R moderate, J9 poor. Target-trained classification within retained source subspace separates classes on every target, so info present but source-trained direction does not generalize. Fig2: source-trained full reps B8Q, source-trained leading 100 Q7, target-trained leading 100 source Q7 with 5-fold CV. Appendix: B8Q F3 C2R/W6/J9 = 0.706/0.874/0.606. Target-trained F3 5-fold CV = 0.936/0.950/0.869.

Transferable subspace: Small source-trained subspaces nearly match target-trained probes, especially C2R/J9. Variance selection Y4 matches H2 only on easy W6, far behind on C2R/J9; explained variance not predictive. Greedy oracle H2: start empty, consider each leading 100 Q7 direction, fit source logistic regression on candidate subset, add direction maximizing target F3 improvement; target 5-fold CV selects using non-held-out target folds, evaluates selected source-trained probe on held-out fold; stop if no improvement >0.001. Target labels guide subset selection, not probe weights. H2 is transfer upper bound, not unbiased OOD estimate. Appendix: H2 improvement over B8Q points C2R 0.22, W6 —, J9 0.23; H2 F3 used for recovery comparison C2R 0.929, J9 0.832; mean H2 subset size target CV C2R/W6/J9 = 15/8/14; earlier note says full-target H2 k = 13/7/14, but Appendix D Table 2 lists H2 selected indices C2R 13, W6 7, J9 15 (internal inconsistency for J9 count).

Hypothesis tests: Neither source-side nor target-side ranking recovers transferable subspace/basis better than B8Q. T6 source-PCA probe/ranking transfers about as well as B8Q; source-reliant directions do not generalize. M9 target-PCA probe/ranking does well on C2R, worse than H2 on W6, below random on J9. Rankings use X4 = absolute probe coefficient × corresponding Q7 standard deviation on source-N4D-projected activations. T6/M9 supply X4 orderings; evaluated probes train on source data projected onto top-k ranked directions. Full-target greedy H2 supplies stable set/k rather than fold-specific selections. Appendix D: H2 and M9 agree by Jaccard D3: C2R 0.182, W6 0.077, J9 0.167. Table 2 selected Q7 indices: T6 Source top 15 = 7,8,11,12,4,5,2,3,6,27,22,21,1,41,18. H2 C2R = 6,89,62,66,26,14,57,25,93,9,70,97,78; H2 W6 = 71,53,28,86,32,81,77; H2 J9 = 37,62,54,41,46,9,57,44,51,43,19,48,86,81,33. M9 C2R/W6/J9 each list 15 directions.

Interpretability/subspace selection: Interpreter C7 uses GPT-5-mini (P2), OpenAI 2025. For each leading source direction, it gets high-positive and high-negative source examples as lines `token<TAB>activation`, activations normalized integers -10 to +10. Prompt asks for Positive pole, Negative pole, Shared direction, R5 (1-10), with 5+ reserved for plausible general deception-relevant strategies/behaviors. Selection retains all directions reaching observed maximum in both scoring runs; scores noisy. Appendix E: maximum observed R5 = 6, no direction exceeded it; 2 scoring runs; L2 retained 19 max-in-both-runs directions; A7 complement has 81 directions. H2 directions selected for more than one target = 5: 62,57,9 shared C2R+J9 and 81,86 shared W6+J9. Among these, max-rated R5=6 are 62,57,86 = 3/5; 9 and 81 have R5=3. Among top 5 T6 directions 7,8,11,12,4, only Q7 4 is max-rated R5=6; ratings 3,4,3,3,6.

Language-only selection L2: no target data; improves over B8Q on all targets and over variance control; large gains on C2R/J9; exceeds A7 everywhere. Recovery: C2R substantially closes B8Q–H2 gap, J9 partial/modest/weakest, W6 little headroom/uninformative because baseline already high. Fig5: L2 red; B8Q blue; Y4 at L2 dimension count teal; A7 complement/interp-ablated PC probe brown. All trained as source probes. Appendix: L2 F3 C2R 0.881, J9 0.662; reported Baseline–H2 gap recovered by L2 C2R 68% conflicts with table values, which imply about 78%; J9 25% consistent.

Limitations: Single model/source; other models/datasets unresolved. W6 already-high baseline makes W6 uninformative. J9 weakest/most OOD; modest improvement likely distribution shift. C2R improvement more robust. Pipeline fully linear. Direction “encode” statements descriptive from extreme examples/C7 verbalizations, not causal; high-rated directions not ablated during inference.

Paper title: “Probe Generalization as Subspace Selection for OOD Deception Detection.” Authors Daniel Yoo, Adrians Skapars. Acknowledgment: work during 11th AI Safety Camp; thanks Prasad Mahadik and Arya Hariharan.

Main claims: linear probes for deception in Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct activations fail OOD; projecting onto selected source-domain PCs enables transfer nearly matching oracle target-trained probes. LLM judge can score/interpretable PCs. Abstract/main reported LLM-judge gap closure: 78% on Insider Trading Report, 25% on Sandbagging. Sec 4.5 text instead said 78% Report, 35% Sandbagging; Sec 5 says 25% Sandbagging with values 0.606 to 0.662 vs greedy 0.832, which supports 25%.

Datasets: Source Roleplaying; targets from Goldowsky-Dill et al. (2025): Insider Trading Report, Insider Trading Confirm, Sandbagging. Labels honest=0, deceptive=1, ambiguous=-1 by GPT-4o; ambiguous removed. Appendix A counts before removal: Roleplaying total 371, -1/0/1=140/59/172; Report 473, 218/194/61; Confirm 151, 29/38/84; Sandbagging 1000, 379/375/246.

Activations: Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct, layer 15 residual stream, averaged over assistant response tokens only. Standardize source activations; apply same stats to targets. PCA on scaled source activations; retain top 100 PCs. Logistic regression probes λ=10. Baseline probes train on full standardized activations. Top-100 rationale: interpretability/SAE alignment decreases with PC index; Appendix C says lower PCs show stronger decoder alignment for best-matching SAE feature and mean top 10 features, Spearman ρ=-0.857 and -0.917, using andyrdt/saes-llama-3.1-8b-instruct.

Sec 4.1/Fig 2: full-source transfer AUROCs: Confirm 0.874, Report 0.706, Sandbagging 0.606. Target-trained/oracle within top-100 PCs achieves 0.936/0.950/0.869 AUROC across three targets, likely Report/Confirm/Sandbagging. Conclusion: top-100 contains sufficient information.

Sec 4.2 greedy oracle PC selection/Fig 3: searches top 100 source PCs, adds PC giving best target AUROC improvement for source-trained probe, using labeled target examples; 5-fold CV over target. Stop if no candidate improves AUROC >0.001. Average selected subset sizes: 15 PCs Report, 8 Confirm, 14 Sandbagging. Greedy improves over full baseline by 0.22 AUROC on Report and 0.23 on Sandbagging. Greedy upper bounds later cited: Report 0.929, Sandbagging 0.832.

Sec 4.3 PC ranking/Fig 4: source-PCA ranking by source-trained weights; target-PCA ranking by target-trained weights, standardized coefficient = abs coefficient × PC SD. Evaluated probes trained on source projected onto top k PCs from rankings. k set by greedy full target dataset: k=13 Report, 7 Confirm, 14 Sandbagging. Both hypotheses fail; source-PCA about baseline, target-PCA good on Report but worse than greedy on Confirm and below random on Sandbagging.

Sec 4.4 interpreting PCs: for each top-100 source PC, use 8 most/least activating source examples; GPT-5-mini describes poles/direction and rates OOD deception usefulness 1–10. No PC >6; retain PCs scoring max in both runs: 19 PCs. Of 5 PCs appearing in greedy selections for more than one target, 3/5 got max OOD score; only 1 of top 5 source-PCA PCs got max.

Sec 4.5/Fig 5: 19 max-LLM PCs; source-trained probe in this subspace vs full baseline, top-19 variance PCs, and remaining 81 PCs. Interp-selected outperforms baseline all targets and variance control, especially Report/Sandbagging; outperforms ablated all three. Report: 0.706→0.881 closes 78% gap to greedy 0.929. Confirm baseline near ceiling. Sandbagging: concrete values 0.606→0.662, 25% gap to greedy 0.832; Sec 4.5’s “35%” conflicts.

Sec 5 limitations: single model/layer/source; Confirm uninformative due baseline 0.874; Sandbagging weakest; no causal inference-time ablation. Sec 6: sparse PC subspaces may isolate general structure; source/target separability alone insufficient.

Appendix D: Table 2 lists source probe weights top PCs: PC7,8,11,12,4,5,2,3,6,27,22,21,1,41,18. Greedy lists Report 13 PCs; Confirm 7; Sandbagging 15. Target separability lists 15 for each. Appendix D claims Jaccard greedy vs target-pca: Report 0.182, Confirm 0.077, Sandbagging 0.167, but these do not match the full table-listed sets: Report 0.167, Confirm 0.100, Sandbagging 0.200. Values may match different truncations for Report/Confirm, conflicting with table label “Selected PCs.”

Appendix E: Table 3 gives 5 PCs selected on more than one target/greedy list and their LLM OOD scores: PC62 Report+Sandbagging score 6; PC57 Report+Sandbagging score 6; PC9 Report+Sandbagging score 3; PC81 Confirm+Sandbagging score 3; PC86 Confirm+Sandbagging score 6. This supports earlier “3/5 got max OOD score” since max observed is 6. Table 4 begins listing PC OOD scores/interpretations: PC7=3, PC8=4, PC11=3, PC12=3, PC4=6.

Paper title: “Probe Generalization as Subspace Selection for OOD Deception Detection.” Authors Daniel Yoo, Adrians Skapars.

Abstract claims:
- Study linear probes for detecting behaviors/concepts in LM activations; concern is OOD transfer failure.
- Model: Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct.
- Evaluates probe generalization over 3 held-out deception detection datasets.
- Main finding: projecting inputs onto a small subset of principal components (PCs) from the training distribution of activations enables cross-domain transfer that nearly matches probes trained directly on the test distribution (oracle).
- PC interpretations can identify a subset of transferable PCs.
- Method: use an LLM judge to score each PC based on whether its most/least activating examples imply a transferable deception direction; then probe on highest-scoring PCs.
- Reported gap closure: baseline-to-oracle gap closed by 78% on Insider Trading Report and 25% on Sandbagging.
- Interpretation: directions heavily weighted by a source probe encode source-specific surface features; directions that transfer encode the same contrast more abstractly, capturable by natural language descriptions.
- Broad conclusion: OOD robustness of probes is largely determined by subspace selection.

Introduction details:

- Figure 1 overview: activations projected onto source-domain PCA basis; candidate PC directions filtered; probes trained on selected low-dimensional subspace.

Candidate probes are trained on source projections; subset choice uses labeled target examples. Uses 5-fold CV over target: select PCs on non-held-out target folds, evaluate selected source-trained probe on held-out target fold. Stop if no candidate improves AUROC >0.001. Average selected subset sizes: 15 PCs for Insider Trading Report, 8 for Insider Trading Confirm, 14 for Sandbagging. Greedy is an upper bound, not unbiased OOD, because selection uses target data. Control: choose top k PCs by variance, k equal greedy size. Greedy improves over full baseline by 0.22 AUROC on Insider Trading Report and 0.23 on Sandbagging, close to target-trained probes for those; demonstrates transferable subspace exists. Variance control matches greedy only for Insider Trading Confirm, falls far behind on Report and Sandbagging; variance explained does not predict usefulness.

Sec 4.3 begins: asks what property makes PCs transferable and whether detectable from source side. Tests two hypotheses: (1) transferable PCs are those that separate target classes well individually; greedy finds them via target access. (2) transferable PCs are those source probe already weights most; greedy rediscovering source signal compactly. Figure 4 compares PC selection by source-probe weights (red), target-probe weights (pink), and greedy oracle (purple), with 95% CIs. Rankings use standardized coefficient = absolute probe coefficient × SD of corresponding PC, for probes trained on activations projected into source-PCA basis.

Dataset descriptions: Roleplaying = simple scenario with opportunity to lie; Report = trader decides whether to honestly report using insider info; Confirm = after hiding earlier insider-info use, asked to confirm it did not use any; Sandbagging = told to deliberately underperform on some tasks while behaving normally on others.

Activations: Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct, layer 15 residual stream, averaged over assistant response tokens only. Standardize source activations; apply same stats to targets. PCA on scaled source activations; retain top 100 PCs. Logistic regression probes λ=10. For subset S, project onto S before train/eval. Baseline probes train on full standardized activations. Top-100 rationale: interpretability/SAE alignment decreases with PC index; not claimed low-index PCs inherently generalize better. Sec 4.1 intended to confirm top-100 retains enough information.

Sec 4.1/Fig 2 baseline results: full-source transfer AUROCs: Insider Trading Confirm 0.874, Insider Trading Report 0.706, Sandbagging 0.606. Target-trained/oracle within top-100 PCs achieves 0.936 / 0.950 / 0.869 AUROC across three targets (likely Report / Confirm / Sandbagging). Conclusion: top-100 contains sufficient info; failure is source-trained direction not generalizing.

Sec 4.2 greedy oracle PC selection/Fig 3: greedy searches top 100 source PCs, adds PC giving best target AUROC improvement for source-trained probe; uses labeled target examples. 5-fold CV over target: select PCs on non-held-out target folds, evaluate selected source-trained probe on held-out target fold. Stop if no candidate improves AUROC >0.001. Average selected subset sizes: 15 PCs Report, 8 Confirm, 14 Sandbagging. Greedy is upper bound, not unbiased OOD. Greedy improves over full baseline by 0.22 AUROC on Report and 0.23 on Sandbagging, close to target-trained probes for those. Variance control matches greedy only for Confirm, far behind on Report and Sandbagging. Greedy upper bounds later cited: Report 0.929, Sandbagging 0.832.

Sec 4.3 PC ranking hypotheses/Fig 4: rankings use standardized coefficient = abs probe coefficient × SD of PC, for probes trained on activations in source-PCA basis. Source-PCA probe ranks by source-trained weights; target-PCA probe ranks by target-trained weights. Evaluated probes trained on source data projected onto top k PCs selected from rankings. k set by greedy on full target dataset, not per fold: k=13 Report, 7 Confirm, 14 Sandbagging. Both hypotheses fail. Source-PCA probe transfers about as well as full baseline. Target-PCA probe does well on Report but worse than greedy on Confirm and below random on Sandbagging.

Sec 4.4 interpreting transferable subspace: for each top-100 source PC, take 8 most/least activating source examples; prompt LLM to describe positive pole, negative pole, shared direction, and rate OOD deception usefulness 1–10. Appendix B says GPT-5-mini was used. Prompt frames PC as bipolar, examples from Roleplaying setup, asks not to overgeneralize or use broad sentiment unless supported, give low scores to surface/task-specific/noisy cues, and reserve scores ≥5 for plausibly general deception-relevant strategies/behaviors. It says example lines are token<TAB>activation with activations normalized to integers -10 to +10. No PC >6, so max observed score=6. Run scoring twice and retain PCs scoring max both runs: 19 PCs. Of 5 PCs appearing in greedy selections for more than one target, 3/5 got max OOD score; only 1 of top 5 source-PCA-selected PCs got max.

Sec 4.5/Fig 5: selects 19 PCs with max LLM judge OOD score in both runs. Evaluates source-trained probe in this subspace across three targets, vs full baseline, top-19 variance PCs, and interp-ablated/complement remaining 81 PCs, with 95% CIs. Text: interp-selected outperforms baseline on all 3 targets and variance control, by wide margins on Report and Sandbagging; also outperforms interp-ablated across all 3. Report: 0.706 to 0.881, closes 78% gap to greedy 0.929. Confirm: baseline near ceiling/little headroom, methods aside from ablated roughly similar. Sandbagging: Sec 4.5 said closes 35%, but Sec 5 gives concrete 0.606 to 0.662, only 25% of gap to greedy 0.832.

Sec 5 limitations: narrow claims: single model/layer/source dataset. Insider Trading Confirm uninformative due baseline 0.874. Sandbagging weakest: 0.606 to 0.662, 25% gap recovery to greedy 0.832; Report robust: 0.706 to 0.881, 78% gap recovery to greedy 0.929. Pipeline linear; nonlinear probes/readout locations open. PC interpretations descriptive, not causal; no inference-time ablation.

Sec 6 conclusion: small subset of source-domain PCs enables cross-domain transfer nearly matching target-trained probes; subset cannot be found with source-side or target-side separability alone. LLM-judge interpretability score over top-activating examples, without target data, partially recovers subspace. Robust probing requires identifying where behavioral signal is robustly represented, not merely linear accessibility; full probes may mix general features with dataset-specific cues; sparse PC subspaces may isolate general structure.

Intro/setup terminology: Linear probes can reveal semantic info but fail OOD by learning spurious correlations; safety monitoring must select dimensions that generalize. “Working in source Q7 coordinates avoids privileging latent dimensions.” N4D = PCA transformation on source-standardized activations, retaining leading 100 directions; Q7 = PCs. Pipeline: project into source N4D basis, filter candidate Q7 directions, train/evaluate probe in selected low-dimensional subspace. Subset S projection precedes training/evaluation. Retaining 100 motivated by interpretability comparability, not assuming low-index generalization; alignment with U9 decreases with PC index, so lower indices easier to interpret. Removing leading components can help embeddings; leading-component projections are baseline in Kantamneni et al.

Related work: Linear concept directions exist for truth/falsehood, honesty, emotion, refusal, assistant-like behavior, etc.; issue is stable concepts vs context correlations. Probes can detect truthfulness/deception but high accuracy may reflect surface/task correlates. Need separate robust internal signals from dataset artifacts. Natural-language explanations/SAE labels can guide interventions.

Setup: Model E6 = Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct; layer 15 residual-stream activations, following Ying et al. (2026) as highest cross-domain discrimination. Activations averaged over assistant-response tokens only. Datasets from Goldowsky-Dill et al. (2025): source Roleplaying (V8); held-out targets Insider Trading Report (C2R), Insider Trading Confirm (W6), Sandbagging (J9); no other source. GPT-4o labeler K8: honest=0, ambiguous=-1, deceptive=1; ambiguous removed. Source activations standardized zero mean/unit variance; same source stats used for targets. Classifiers: logistic regression lambda=10. Full-representation baseline B8Q trains on all standardized activations. Error bars 95% CIs.

Experiments part 4: Baseline results: W6 transfer reasonably good/already high, C2R moderate, J9 poor. Target-trained classification within retained source subspace separates classes on every target, implying info present but source-trained direction does not generalize. Fig2: target F3 for source-trained full representations (blue), source-trained leading 100 Q7 (orange), target-trained leading 100 source Q7 with 5-fold CV (green).

Transferable subspace: Small source-trained subspaces nearly match target-trained probes, especially C2R/J9. Variance selection Y4 matches H2 only on easy W6, far behind on C2R/J9; explained variance not predictive. Fig3: B8Q blue; Y4 with k matched to H2 teal; H2 purple. Greedy oracle H2: start empty, consider each leading 100 source Q7 direction, project source onto candidate subset, fit source logistic regression, add direction maximizing target F3 improvement. Target 5-fold CV selects using non-held-out target folds, evaluates selected source-trained probe on held-out fold; stop if no improvement >0.001. Target labels guide subset selection, not probe weights. H2 is transfer upper bound, not unbiased OOD estimate.

Hypothesis tests: Neither source-side nor target-side ranking recovers transferable subspace or basis better than B8Q. T6 (source-PCA probe/ranking) transfers about as well as B8Q; source-reliant directions do not generalize. M9 (target-PCA probe/ranking) does well on C2R, worse than H2 on W6, below random on J9. Target-class separation and transfer under source-fitted weighting choose different directions. Fig4: T6 red; M9 pink; H2 purple. Rankings use X4 = absolute probe coefficient × corresponding Q7 standard deviation, on source-N4D-projected activations. T6 and M9 supply X4 orderings; evaluated probes train on source data projected onto top-k ranked directions. Full-target greedy H2 supplies stable set/k rather than fold-specific selections; numbers differ slightly from CV results.

Interpretability/subspace selection: Transferable subsets differ from source- or target-classification relied-on directions. H2-selected directions express more domain-surviving abstract contrasts; only partial recovery by interpretation. Interpreter C7 (LLM judge) gets eight most-activating and eight least-activating source examples for each leading source direction, generates positive-pole/negative-pole/whole-direction descriptions, then assigns OOD score R5. Selection retains all directions reaching observed maximum in both scoring runs; scores noisy.

Language-only selection L2: no target data; improves over B8Q on all targets and over variance control; large gains on C2R/J9; also exceeds A7 everywhere. Recovery varies: C2R substantially closes B8Q–H2 gap, J9 partial/modest and weakest/most OOD, W6 little headroom/uninformative because baseline already high; every method except A7 roughly tied on W6. Fig5: L2 red; B8Q blue; Y4 at L2 dimension count teal; A7 brown. L2 = intersection retained by interpreter scoring. Controls: A7 = complement/interp-ablated PC probe; Y4 = equal-dimensional top-k variance-ranked PCs. All trained as source probes.

Limitations: Claims narrow: single model and single source; other model families/datasets unresolved. W6 already-high baseline makes W6 uninformative. J9 is weakest and most OOD; modest improvement likely reflects distribution shift. C2R improvement more robust. Pipeline described as fully linear: N4D projection followed by logistic regression; nonlinear probes or other readout locations remain open. Direction “encode” statements are descriptive from extreme activation examples and C7 verbalizations, not causal; high-rated directions not ablated during inference to verify contrasts.

errors.claim: “The greedy method comes close to a probe trained directly on target dataset for Insider Trading Report and Sandbagging, improving on the baseline by 0.32 and 0.33 points of AUROC, respectively.”
errors.evidence: Earlier in this part, the full source-representation baseline AUROCs are reported as Insider Trading Report = 0.706 and Sandbagging = 0.606, while target-trained top-100-PC AUROCs are reported as 0.936 / 0.950 / 0.869 across the three targets. errors.explanation: An improvement of 0.32 or 0.33 over the stated baseline would exceed the reported target-trained probe performance, not merely “come close” to it. The claimed improvements are larger than the entire reported baseline-to-oracle gaps for those two datasets.

Paper title: “Probe Generalization as Subspace Selection for OOD Deception Detection.” Authors Daniel Yoo, Adrians Skapars.

Core claims: Linear probes for deception detection in Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct; OOD transfer depends largely on subspace/PC selection. Source dataset Roleplaying; targets Insider Trading Report, Insider Trading Confirm, Sandbagging from Goldowsky-Dill et al. (2025). Small subsets of source PCs can nearly match target-trained/oracle probes. Abstract gap closure: 78% on Insider Trading Report and 25% on Sandbagging.

Datasets/labels: honest=0, ambiguous=-1, deceptive=1 by GPT-4o; ambiguous removed for probe training/eval. Appendix A counts before removal: Roleplaying 371 (-1/0/1=140/59/172); Insider Trading Report 473 (218/194/61); Confirm 151 (29/38/84); Sandbagging 1000 (379/375/246).

Activations/probes: Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct, layer 15 residual stream, average over assistant response tokens only. Standardize source activations; apply same stats to targets. PCA on scaled source activations; retain top 100 PCs. Logistic regression λ=10. Full-representation baseline trains on all standardized activations.

Sec 4.1: source-trained full transfer AUROCs: Confirm 0.874, Report 0.706, Sandbagging 0.606. Target-trained probes in top-100 source-PC subspace, 5-fold CV: Report 0.936, Confirm 0.950, Sandbagging 0.869.

Sec 4.2 greedy oracle: iteratively adds PCs from top 100, training source logistic probe and choosing PC maximizing target AUROC. 5-fold CV over target: selection on non-held-out target folds, evaluate selected source-trained probe on held-out target fold; stop if improvement ≤0.001. Avg subset sizes: Report 15, Confirm 8, Sandbagging 14. Greedy oracle values later/current: Report 0.929, Sandbagging 0.832; baselines 0.706, 0.606, so improvements 0.223/0.226, conflicting with Sec 4.2 text claiming +0.32/+0.33.

Sec 4.3: PC rankings from source/target standardized coefficients = |probe coefficient| × PC SD. k from greedy on full target: Report 13, Confirm 7, Sandbagging 14. Source-PCA ranking transfers about like full baseline. Target-PCA ranking good on Report but worse than greedy on Confirm and below random on Sandbagging.

Sec 4.4/4.5 interpretability: For each top-100 source PC, take 8 most and 8 least activating source examples; prompt LLM for positive/negative pole and shared direction. LLM judge scores generalizability/OOD deception usefulness 1–10. No PC scored >6; 6 max observed. Retain PCs scoring 6 in both runs: 19 PCs. Five PCs appear in greedy selections for >1 target; 3/5 got max OOD score; only 1 of top 5 source-probe PCs got max OOD score. Interp-selected 19 PCs, no target data, outperform full baseline and top-19 variance control on all 3; Report 0.881 vs baseline 0.706 vs greedy 0.929, closing 78% gap. Confirm baseline near ceiling 0.874. Sandbagging 0.662 vs baseline 0.606 vs greedy 0.832, closing 25% gap.

Appendix B prompt: says GPT-5-mini used to interpret directions. Potential inconsistency: prompt says each line is “token<TAB>activation,” whereas earlier method says examples, not tokens.

Limitations/conclusion: Single model/layer/source. Confirm uninformative due baseline 0.874. Sandbagging improvement small; Report more robust. No causal validation; interpretations descriptive, no inference-time ablation of high-scoring PCs, though Sec 4.5 did probe-level remaining-81-PC condition.

Appendix C: Lower PCs show stronger decoder alignment to SAE features using andyrdt/saes-llama-3.1-8b-instruct; Spearman ρ=-0.857 for best-matching SAE feature and -0.917 for mean of top 10.

Appendix D/Table 2 PC sets. Source probe weights: PC7,8,11,12,4,5,2,3,6,27,22,21,1,41,18. Greedy Report 13 PCs: PC6,89,62,66,26,14,57,25,93,9,70,97,78. Greedy Confirm 7: PC71,53,28,86,32,81,77. Greedy Sandbagging table lists 15 PCs: PC37,62,54,41,46,9,57,44,51,43,19,48,86,81,33, conflicting with earlier k=14. Target Report 15: PC5,6,89,18,79,46,87,4,14,34,29,1,66,67,19. Target Confirm 15: PC4,1,8,53,30,7,13,18,5,20,26,49,28,31,97. Target Sandbagging 15: PC51,91,97,13,39,77,4,66,53,86,62,23,41,10,61. Appendix D stated Jaccards 0.182/0.077/0.167, but table implies Report 4/24=0.167, Confirm 2/20=0.100, Sandbagging 5/25=0.200; “less than a fifth” contradicted by Sandbagging table.

Appendix E: Table 3 titled “PCs selected for likely transferability, based on interpretation with an LLM judge” but lists the five PCs selected on multiple greedy target sets: PC62 Report+Sandbagging score 6; PC57 Report+Sandbagging score 6; PC9 Report+Sandbagging score 3; PC81 Confirm+Sandbagging score 3; PC86 Confirm+Sandbagging score 6. This conflicts with title/earlier interpretability selection rule because PC9 and PC81 are low-scored, brittle, not likely-transferable. Table 4 gives OOD scores/explanations for source top PCs: PC7 score 3, PC8 4, PC11 3, PC12 3, PC4 6.

Paper title: “Probe Generalization as Subspace Selection for OOD Deception Detection.” Authors Daniel Yoo, Adrians Skapars.

Abstract claims:
- Study linear probes for detecting behaviors/concepts in LM activations; concern is OOD transfer failure.
- Model: Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct.
- Evaluates probe generalization over 3 held-out deception detection datasets.
- Main finding: projecting inputs onto a small subset of principal components (PCs) from the training distribution of activations enables cross-domain transfer that nearly matches probes trained directly on the test distribution (oracle).
- PC interpretations can identify a subset of transferable PCs.
- Method: use an LLM judge to score each PC based on whether its most/least activating examples imply a transferable deception direction; then probe on highest-scoring PCs.
- Reported gap closure: baseline-to-oracle gap closed by 78% on Insider Trading Report and 25% on Sandbagging.
- Interpretation: directions heavily weighted by a source probe encode source-specific surface features; directions that transfer encode the same contrast more abstractly, capturable by natural language descriptions.
- Broad conclusion: OOD robustness of probes is largely determined by subspace selection.

Introduction details:
- Linear probes are useful but unreliable OOD; challenge is building probes that learn only generalizing features.
- Work in source-domain PCA basis rather than raw activations; PCs used as data-driven basis. Research question: which subset of PCs supports generalizable probe training and how can it be identified?
- Testbed: deception probes on Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct. Train on one source dataset: Roleplaying deception scenarios. Evaluate on 3 target datasets from Goldowsky-Dill et al. (2025): Insider Trading Report, Insider Trading Confirm, Sandbagging.
- Explore strategies for selecting subset of training dimensions/PCs to avoid spurious correlations and transfer.
- Contributions claimed:
  1. A small transferable subspace exists (Sec 4.2): target-supervised greedy search over source PCs finds 8–15 components on which a source-trained probe nearly matches a target-trained probe.
  2. Source-side and target-side rankings both fail to recover the subspace (Sec 4.3): ranking PCs by source or target probe weights does not transfer better than full-representation baseline.
  3. LLM judge partially recovers subspace without target data (Sec 4.5): interprets/selects PCs likely to encode transferable behavioral contrast rather than surface patterns.
- Figure 1 overview: activations projected onto source-domain PCA basis; candidate PC directions filtered; probes trained on selected low-dimensional subspace.

errors.claim: “The greedy method comes close to a probe trained directly on target dataset for Insider Trading Report and Sandbagging, improving on the baseline by 0.32 and 0.33 points of AUROC, respectively.”

- Average subset sizes: 15 PCs for Insider Trading Report, 8 for Insider Trading Confirm, 14 for Sandbagging.
- Greedy is an upper bound, not unbiased OOD, because it uses labeled target examples for subset selection.
- Control: top-k PCs by variance, k matched to greedy subset size.
- Sec 4.2 claimed greedy comes close to target-trained probe for Report and Sandbagging and improves baseline by 0.32 and 0.33 AUROC respectively; this conflicts with later/current values: greedy oracle Report=0.929 and Sandbagging=0.832, baselines 0.706 and 0.606, so improvements are 0.223 and 0.226.
- Authors say variance control matches greedy only for Insider Trading Confirm and lags on Report/Sandbagging, implying variance explained does not predict PC usefulness.

Sec 4.3:
- Investigates whether transferable PCs can be detected from source side.
- Compares PC rankings using standardized coefficient = absolute probe coefficient × PC standard deviation, in source-PCA basis. Figure 4 includes source-probe weights, target-probe weights, and greedy oracle.
- For evaluation, probes appear trained on source data projected onto top k PCs selected by each ranking.
- k for Fig 4 set by running greedy on full target dataset: k=13 Report, 7 Confirm, 14 Sandbagging; authors note these differ slightly from CV numbers.
- Results: source-PCA probe transfers about as well as full baseline. Target-PCA probe does well on Insider Trading Report but worse than greedy on Insider Trading Confirm and below random on Sandbagging. Conclusion: target-separating PCs are not necessarily those that transfer when weighted from source.

Sec 4.4 interpretability:
- For each top-100 source PC, take 8 most and 8 least activating source examples; prompt LLM for positive/negative pole and overall direction descriptions. LLM judge rates generalizability/OOD score 1–10; prompt/model details in Appendix B.
- No PC scored above 6; 6 treated as maximum observed OOD score. Retain PCs scoring 6 in both of two runs: 19 PCs.
- Five PCs appear in greedy selections for more than one target; 3/5 got max OOD score. Only 1 of top 5 PCs selected by source-PCA probes got max OOD score. Authors say LLMs partially recover transferable directions.

Sec 4.5:
- Tests interp-selected subspace without target data: 19 PCs with max OOD score in both judge runs.
- Figure 5 compares interp-selected 19 PCs vs full-representation baseline, top-19 PCs by variance, and interp-ablated/remaining 81 PCs excluding interp-selected PCs; 95% CIs.
- Interp-selected PC probe outperforms baseline on all 3 targets and source-variance-selected control, with wide margins on Report and Sandbagging. It also outperforms interp-ablated probe on all 3.
- Report: interp AUROC 0.881 vs baseline 0.706, greedy oracle 0.929; closes 78% of gap.
- Confirm: baseline transfer already near ceiling at 0.874; little headroom; each selection method aside from interp-ablated roughly comparable.
- Sandbagging: interp AUROC 0.662 vs baseline 0.606, greedy oracle 0.832; closes 25% of gap.

Sec 5 Limitations:
- Claims narrow: single model Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct, layer 15, single source Roleplaying. Insider Trading Confirm uninformative because baseline already 0.874.
- Sandbagging margins small: 0.606 to 0.662, 25% of gap to greedy 0.832; most OOD target. Report result 0.706 to 0.881, 78% of gap to greedy 0.929, called more robust.
- Pipeline fully linear: PCA projection + logistic regression; extension to nonlinear probes/readout locations open.
- No causal validation: PC interpretations descriptive from top-activating examples and LLM verbalization. Authors claim they have not ablated high-scoring PCs during inference to verify causal encoding, though Sec 4.5 did include a probe-level ablated/remaining-81-PCs condition.

Sec 6 Conclusion:
- Reiterates: small subset of source-domain PCs enables cross-domain transfer nearly matching target-trained probes; subset cannot be found with source-side or target-side separability alone.
- LLM-judge interpretability score over PC top-activating examples, with no target access, partially recovers useful subspace.
- Claims robust probing is about both linear accessibility and where the signal is represented; full-representation probes may mix general behavioral features with dataset-specific surface cues, while sparse PC subspaces can isolate more general behavioral structure. Frames OOD probing as representation/subspace selection that preserves intended feature and filters spurious correlations.

Acknowledgment/Impact:
- Work conducted during 11th AI Safety Camp, which provided compute. Thanks to Prasad Mahadik and Arya Hariharan.
- Impact statement: goal is to advance ML; authors say no societal consequences need highlighting.

final_notes:
Paper title: “Probe Generalization as Subspace Selection for OOD Deception Detection.” Thesis: source-probe-heavy directions encode source-specific surface features; transferable directions encode same contrast more abstractly/capturable in natural language; OOD robustness is subspace/representation selection. Conclusion: robust probing requires finding where linearly accessible signal is robustly represented; full-representation probes may mix general behavioral features with dataset-specific cues; sparse directional subspaces can isolate more general behavioral structure.

Setup: E6 = Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct; layer 15 residual-stream activations averaged over assistant-response tokens only. Source Roleplaying V8; targets Insider Trading Report C2R, Insider Trading Confirm W6, Sandbagging J9. GPT-4o labeler K8: honest=0, ambiguous=-1, deceptive=1; ambiguous removed. Source activations standardized; same stats used on targets. N4D = PCA on source-standardized activations, retaining leading 100 directions; Q7 = PCs/source coordinates. Pipeline: project into source N4D basis, filter candidate Q7 directions, train/evaluate logistic regression. Classifier lambda=10. Full-representation baseline B8Q trains on all standardized activations. Error bars 95% CIs. Retaining 100 for interpretability/comparability; alignment with U9 decreases with PC index.

Baseline/experiments: Fig2: source-trained full reps B8Q blue, source-trained leading 100 Q7 orange, target-trained leading 100 source Q7 with 5-fold CV green. Baseline transfer: W6 high, C2R moderate, J9 poor. Target-trained within retained source subspace separates every target, so info present but source-trained direction may not generalize.

Transferable subspace: H2 greedy oracle starts empty, considers each leading 100 Q7 direction, fits source logistic regression on selected subset, adds direction maximizing target F3 improvement. Target 5-fold CV selects using non-held-out target folds and evaluates selected source-trained probe on held-out fold; stop if no improvement >0.001. Target labels guide subset selection, not weights. H2 is transfer upper bound, not unbiased OOD estimate. Small H2 subsets nearly match target-trained probes, especially C2R/J9. Y4 variance selection matches H2 only on W6, far behind C2R/J9.

Hypothesis tests: T6 source-PCA probe/ranking transfers about as well as B8Q; source-reliant directions do not generalize. M9 target-PCA probe/ranking does well on C2R, worse than H2 on W6, below random on J9. Rankings use X4 = absolute probe coefficient × corresponding Q7 standard deviation. T6/M9 orderings evaluated by source-trained probes on top-k directions. Full-target H2 supplies stable set/k rather than fold-specific selections.

Interpretability/subspace selection: Interpreter C7 gets eight most- and least-activating source examples for each leading source direction, generates positive/negative/whole-direction descriptions, assigns OOD score R5. Appendix B says GPT-5-mini prompt uses bipolar Q7 direction, input `token<TAB>activation`, activations normalized -10 to +10; source setup says E6 enacts simple V8 opportunity to lie; output exactly Positive pole, Negative pole, Shared direction, R5. L2 language-only selection uses no target data; improves over B8Q on all targets and over variance control; large gains C2R/J9, exceeds A7 everywhere. Recovery: C2R closes B8Q–H2 gap substantially; J9 partial/modest; W6 little headroom. Fig5: L2 red; B8Q blue; Y4 teal; A7 complement/interp-ablated brown.

Limitations: single model/source; W6 already-high baseline uninformative; J9 weakest/most OOD; C2R improvement more robust. Fully linear pipeline. Direction “encode” statements descriptive from extreme examples/C7 verbalizations, not causal; high-rated directions not ablated during inference.

Appendix A data: V8 total 371 = 140/-1, 59/0, 172/1; C2R 473 = 218/194/61; W6 151 = 29/38/84; J9 1000 = 379/375/246. Numerical observations: B8Q F3 C2R .706, W6 .874, J9 .606; target-trained F3 C2R .936, W6 .950, J9 .869; H2 improvement row says C2R .32, W6 —, J9 .33 but conflicts internally with H2 F3 used for recovery comparison C2R .929 and J9 .832; L2 F3 C2R .881, J9 .662; L2 recovers B8Q-H2 gap C2R 78%, J9 25%; mean H2 subset size target CV C2R 15, W6 8, J9 14; full-target H2 k C2R 13, W6 7, J9 14. Decoder alignment Spearman rho best feature -0.857, mean top10 -0.917.

Appendix D: H2 and M9 claimed Jaccard D3: C2R .182, W6 .077, J9 .167, but these do not match listed sets. Table 2 selections: T6 Source = 7,8,11,12,4,5,2,3,6,27,22,21,1,41,18. H2 C2R = 6,89,62,66,26,14,57,25,93,9,70,97,78. H2 W6 = 71,53,28,86,32,81,77. H2 J9 = 37,62,54,41,46,9,57,44,51,43,19,48,86,81,33. M9 C2R = 5,6,89,18,79,46,87,4,14,34,29,1,66,67,19. M9 W6 = 4,1,8,53,30,7,13,18,5,20,26,49,28,31,97. M9 J9 = 51,91,97,13,39,77,4,66,53,86,62,23,41,10,61. H2 J9 list has 15 entries though earlier full-target H2 k J9 was 14.

Appendix E: Max observed R5 was 6; two scoring runs; 19 directions reached max in both runs and retained for L2; A7 complement has 81. H2 shared by >1 target has 5 directions: 62,57,9 shared C2R+J9; 81,86 shared W6+J9. Of these, max-rated 3/5: 62 R5 6, 57 R5 6, 86 R5 6; 9 and 81 R5 3. Top five T6 directions 7,8,11,12,4 have R5 3,4,3,3,6, so 1/5 max-rated.

Paper title: “Probe Generalization as Subspace Selection for OOD Deception Detection.” Authors Daniel Yoo, Adrians Skapars. Thesis: source-probe-heavy directions encode source-specific surface features; transferable directions encode same contrast more abstractly/capturable in natural language; OOD robustness is subspace/representation selection. Conclusion: robust probing requires finding where linearly accessible signal is represented robustly; full-representation probes may mix general behavioral features with dataset-specific cues; sparse directional subspaces can isolate more general behavioral structure.

Setup/terminology: E6 = Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct; layer 15 residual-stream activations averaged over assistant-response tokens only. Datasets from Goldowsky-Dill et al. (2025): source Roleplaying V8; targets Insider Trading Report C2R, Insider Trading Confirm W6, Sandbagging J9. GPT-4o labeler K8: honest=0, ambiguous=-1, deceptive=1; ambiguous removed for classifier data. Source activations standardized zero mean/unit variance; same source stats used on targets. N4D = PCA transformation on source-standardized activations, retaining leading 100 directions; Q7 = PCs/source coordinates. Pipeline: project into source N4D basis, filter candidate Q7 directions, train/evaluate logistic regression in selected subspace. Classifier lambda=10. Full-representation baseline B8Q trains on all standardized activations. Error bars 95% CIs. Working in source Q7 coordinates avoids privileging latent dimensions. Retaining 100 for interpretability/comparability, not assuming low-index generalization; alignment with U9 decreases with PC index.

Baseline/experiments: Fig2: source-trained full reps B8Q blue, source-trained leading 100 Q7 orange, target-trained leading 100 source Q7 with 5-fold CV green. Baseline transfer: W6 reasonably good/already high, C2R moderate, J9 poor. Target-trained within retained source subspace separates classes on every target, so info is present but source-trained direction may not generalize.

Transferable subspace: H2 greedy oracle starts empty, considers each leading 100 source Q7 direction, projects source onto subset, fits source logistic regression, adds direction maximizing target F3 improvement. Target 5-fold CV selects using non-held-out target folds and evaluates selected source-trained probe on held-out fold; stop if no improvement >0.001. Target labels guide subset selection, not probe weights. H2 is transfer upper bound, not unbiased OOD estimate. Small H2 subsets nearly match target-trained probes, especially C2R/J9. Y4 variance selection matches H2 only on easy W6, far behind on C2R/J9; explained variance not predictive. Fig3: B8Q blue, Y4 teal with k matched to H2, H2 purple.

Hypothesis tests: Neither source-side nor target-side ranking recovers transferable subspace/basis better than B8Q. T6 source-PCA probe/ranking transfers about as well as B8Q; source-reliant directions do not generalize. M9 target-PCA probe/ranking does well on C2R, worse than H2 on W6, below random on J9. Rankings use X4 = absolute probe coefficient × corresponding Q7 standard deviation on source-N4D-projected activations. T6/M9 orderings evaluated by source-trained probes projected onto top-k ranked directions. Full-target greedy H2 supplies stable set/k rather than fold-specific selections; numbers differ slightly from CV.

Interpretability/subspace selection: H2-selected directions differ from source- or target-classification relied-on directions and express more domain-surviving abstract contrasts. Interpreter C7 gets eight most-activating and eight least-activating source examples for each leading source direction, generates positive/negative/whole-direction descriptions, then assigns OOD score R5. Appendix B says direction interpretation uses GPT-5-mini (P2), with prompt: interpret bipolar Q7 direction; input lines `token<TAB>activation`, activations normalized integers -10 to +10; source setup says E6 enacts simple V8 scenario with strategic opportunity to lie; infer dominant contrast, avoid unsupported generalization, rate usefulness for OOD deception; low ratings for surface/lexical/task-specific/noisy/brittle/context-dependent directions, usually 1–4; reserve 5+ for plausible general deception-relevant strategies/behaviors; output exactly Positive pole, Negative pole, Shared direction, R5. L2 language-only selection uses no target data; improves over B8Q on all targets and over variance control; large gains on C2R/J9, exceeds A7 everywhere. Recovery: C2R substantially closes B8Q–H2 gap, J9 partial/modest and weakest/most OOD, W6 little headroom/uninformative because baseline already high; every method except A7 roughly tied on W6. Fig5: L2 red; B8Q blue; Y4 equal-dimensional variance-ranked teal; A7 complement/interp-ablated brown. All trained as source probes.
