Paper title: “Probe Generalization as Subspace Selection for OOD Deception Detection” by Daniel Yoo and Adrians Skapars. Venue line: Machine Learning, ICML. Acknowledgment: work conducted during 11th AI Safety Camp, compute provided; thanks Prasad Mahadik and Arya Hariharan. Impact statement: goal is advancing ML; no specific societal consequences highlighted.

Core thesis: linear probes for deception/concepts in LLM activations fail OOD due to spurious correlations; OOD robustness largely determined by subspace selection. Reframe OOD probing as representation/subspace selection, not merely classifier fitting. Full-representation probes may mix robust behavioral features with dataset-specific cues.

Model/data/setup: Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct, layer 15 residual stream, assistant response tokens averaged. Source dataset Roleplaying deception scenarios. Targets: Insider Trading Report, Insider Trading Confirm, Sandbagging from Goldowsky-Dill et al. 2025. Labels honest=0/deceptive=1/ambiguous=-1 by GPT-4o; ambiguous removed. Earlier text said 1,216 non-ambiguous total, but Appendix A counts imply Roleplaying 231 + targets 998 = 1,229. Appendix A counts: Roleplaying total 371 labels -1/0/1=140/59/172; Insider Trading Report 473 labels 218/194/61; Insider Trading Confirm 151 labels 29/38/84; Sandbagging 1000 labels 379/375/246.

Preprocessing/method: source activations standardized zero mean/unit variance; same source stats for targets. PCA on scaled source activations; retain top 100 source PCs. Logistic regression lambda=10. For subset S, project onto S before training/eval. Baseline probes train on full standardized activations, not limited to 100 PCs.

Section 4.1: Figure 2 compares source-trained full baseline, source-trained top-100 source-PC probe, target-trained top-100 source-PC oracle with 5-fold CV. Full source transfer AUROCs: Confirm 0.874, Report 0.706, Sandbagging 0.606. Target-trained/oracle in 100-PC subspace: 0.936/0.950/0.869 AUROC likely Report/Confirm/Sandbagging.

Section 4.2 greedy oracle: iteratively add top-100 source PC maximizing target AUROC for source-trained logistic probe; target labels guide selection. 5-fold target CV: select on non-held-out folds, evaluate held-out. Stop improvement <=0.001. Avg selected sizes: Report 15, Confirm 8, Sandbagging 14. Greedy is upper bound, not unbiased OOD estimate. Figure 3 compares full baseline, top-k variance, greedy. Greedy improves baseline by 0.22 Report and 0.23 Sandbagging, close to target-trained there. Greedy AUROCs later: Report 0.929; Sandbagging 0.832.

Section 4.3: tests if greedy PCs are individually good target separators or source probe’s most relied-on PCs. Ranking uses standardized coefficient = abs(coef)*SD of PC. Stable full-target greedy sets: k=13 Report, 7 Confirm, 14 Sandbagging; Appendix D later lists Sandbagging 15, conflict. Results: source-PCA ranking transfers about like full baseline; target-PCA ranking good on Report, worse than greedy on Confirm, below-random on Sandbagging. Conclusion: robust subset cannot be found by source-side or target-side separability alone.

Section 4.4/interp: For each top-100 source PC, take 8 most and 8 least activating source examples. LLM (Appendix B says GPT-5-mini) describes positive/negative/shared direction and scores OOD deception usefulness 1–10. Prompt favors narrow general deception-relevant strategies, penalizes task-specific/surface/noisy directions. No PC scored above 6; maximum observed 6. Scoring run twice; retain PCs scoring max in both runs, yielding 19 PCs. 5 PCs appeared in greedy selections for >1 target; 3/5 got max OOD score. Only 1 of top 5 source-PCA-weight PCs got max.

Section 4.5: Figure 5 compares interp-selected 19-PC subspace vs full baseline, top-19 variance, and ablation using remaining 81 PCs. Interp-selected probe outperforms baseline on all 3 targets and controls, especially Report/Sandbagging; Confirm near ceiling/uninformative. Report 0.706→0.881, closing 78% gap to greedy 0.929. Sandbagging 0.606→0.662, closing 25% gap to greedy 0.832.

Limitations/conclusion: narrow single model/layer/source; Sandbagging margins small; pipeline linear; PC interpretations descriptive not causal; no inference-time ablations. Conclusion: small source-PC subset enables cross-domain transfer nearly matching target-trained probes; LLM interpretability partially recovers robust subspace without target data.

Appendix C: lower PCs more SAE decoder-aligned; Spearman rho -0.857 and -0.917 using andyrdt/saes-llama-3.1-8b-instruct.

Appendix D: reports Jaccard greedy vs target-pca as 0.182 Report, 0.077 Confirm, 0.167 Sandbagging, but listed sets imply Report 4/24=0.167, Confirm 2/20=0.100, Sandbagging 5/25=0.200. Source probe weights PCs: PC7, PC8, PC11, PC12, PC4, PC5, PC2, PC3, PC6, PC27, PC22, PC21, PC1, PC41, PC18. Greedy sets include Report 13 PCs: PC6, PC89, PC62, PC66, PC26, PC14, PC57, PC25, PC93, PC9, PC70, PC97, PC78; Confirm 7: PC71, PC53, PC28, PC86, PC32, PC81, PC77; Sandbagging listed as 15 PCs, starting PC37, PC62, PC54, PC41, PC46, PC9, ...

Appendix E: Table 3 caption says PCs selected for likely transferability based on LLM judge, but lists five PCs selected on multiple target greedy sets: PC62 Report+Sandbagging score 6; PC57 Report+Sandbagging score 6; PC9 Report+Sandbagging score 3; PC81 Confirm+Sandbagging score 3; PC86 Confirm+Sandbagging score 6. This supports earlier “3/5 max” but conflicts with caption/interpretability-selection framing because two have low score 3 and explanations call them brittle/domain-specific. Table 4 lists source-probe-weight PCs and OOD scores: PC7=3, PC8=4, PC11=3, PC12=3, PC4=6, consistent with only one of top five source probe PCs max-scored.

final_notes:
Paper title: “Probe Generalization as Subspace Selection for OOD Deception Detection.” Authors Daniel Yoo, Adrians Skapars.

Core claims: Linear probes may fail OOD; study uses Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct probes over 3 held-out deception datasets. Main finding: projecting inputs onto a small subset of source-distribution PCs enables cross-domain transfer nearly matching target-trained/oracle probes. LLM judge over PC interpretations partially recovers transferable PCs without target labels. Reported LLM-judge gap closure: 78% on Insider Trading Report, 25% on Sandbagging.

Datasets/setup: 4 Goldowsky-Dill et al. datasets: source Roleplaying; targets Insider Trading Report, Insider Trading Confirm, Sandbagging. Labels honest 0, ambiguous -1, deceptive 1 by GPT-4o; ambiguous removed for probe experiments. Counts incl ambiguous: Roleplaying 371 = 140/59/172; Report 473 = 218/194/61; Confirm 151 = 29/38/84; Sandbagging 1000 = 379/375/246.

Activations/probes: Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct, layer 15 residual stream, average assistant-response token activations. Standardize source activations; same source stats applied to targets. PCA on scaled source activations; retain top 100 PCs. Logistic regression λ=10. Baseline probes train on full standardized activations. Rationale top 100: lower PCs more interpretable/comparable via SAE alignment, not claiming low-index PCs generalize better. Appendix C: lower PCs show stronger SAE decoder alignment; Spearman rho -0.857 for best-matching SAE feature and -0.917 for mean top 10, using andyrdt/saes-llama-3.1-8b-instruct.

Section 4.1: Source-trained full representation AUROC: Confirm 0.874; Report 0.706; Sandbagging 0.606. Target-trained within 100 source-PC subspace using 5-fold CV about 0.936/0.950/0.869 across targets. Conclusion: 100-PC subspace contains target information; bottleneck is source probe direction.

Section 4.2 greedy transferable subspace: Greedy PC selection uses labeled target examples to choose source PCs maximizing target AUROC; source logistic probe trained on selected PCs. 5-fold target CV for evaluation; stop if no improvement >0.001. Average selected subset sizes: Report 15, Confirm 8, Sandbagging 14. Greedy is upper bound/not unbiased OOD estimate. Greedy improves baseline by 0.22 Report and 0.23 Sandbagging, approx Report 0.926, Sandbagging 0.836. Variance top-k control only matches greedy for Confirm.

Section 4.3 ranking baselines: PC rankings by standardized coefficient = abs(coef) × SD. Source-PCA ranks by source-probe weights; target-PCA ranks by target-data probe weights; final probes train on source projected onto top-k PCs. Fig. 4 k set by greedy on full target dataset: k=13 Report, 7 Confirm, 14 Sandbagging. Results: source-PCA about full baseline; target-PCA good on Report but worse than greedy on Confirm and below random on Sandbagging. Earlier internal contradiction: text then says target-separable PCs transfer better than greedy selections.

Appendix D PC set comparisons: Table 2 source probe weights Source PCs: PC7, PC8, PC11, PC12, PC4, PC5, PC2, PC3, PC6, PC27, PC22, PC21, PC1, PC41, PC18. Greedy Report PCs: PC6, PC89, PC62, PC66, PC26, PC14, PC57, PC25, PC93, PC9, PC70, PC97, PC78. Greedy Confirm: PC71, PC53, PC28, PC86, PC32, PC81, PC77. Greedy Sandbagging listed as 15 PCs: PC37, PC62, PC54, PC41, PC46, PC9, PC57, PC44, PC51, PC43, PC19, PC48, PC86, PC81, PC33, conflicting with earlier full-target k=14. Target separability Report: PC5, PC6, PC89, PC18, PC79, PC46, PC87, PC4, PC14, PC34, PC29, PC1, PC66, PC67, PC19. Target Confirm: PC4, PC1, PC8, PC53, PC30, PC7, PC13, PC18, PC5, PC20, PC26, PC49, PC28, PC31, PC97. Target Sandbagging: PC51, PC91, PC97, PC13, PC39, PC77, PC4, PC66, PC53, PC86, PC62, PC23, PC41, PC10, PC61. Reported Jaccards greedy vs target-pca: 0.182 Report, 0.077 Confirm, 0.167 Sandbagging, but table-implied values are 0.167, 0.100, 0.154.

Section 4.4/4.5: LLM judge rates PC OOD usefulness 1–10 from top/bottom 8 source examples; no PC above 6, so max score 6. PCs scoring max in both runs: 19. Of 5 PCs appearing in greedy selections for >1 target, 3/5 max-scored; only 1 of top 5 source-PCA PCs max-scored. Interp-selected 19-PC source probe beats full baseline all targets and variance control; Report 0.706→0.881, closing 78% gap to greedy 0.929; Sandbagging 0.606→0.662, closing 25% gap to greedy 0.832. Confirm baseline near ceiling, uninformative.

Appendix E interpretability tables: Table 3 multi-target greedy PCs and OOD scores: PC62 Report+Sandbagging score 6; PC57 Report+Sandbagging 6; PC9 Report+Sandbagging 3; PC81 Confirm+Sandbagging 3; PC86 Confirm+Sandbagging 6. Table 4 source top-weight PCs and scores shown: PC7 3, PC8 4, PC11 3, PC12 3, PC4 6, consistent with only one top-5 source PC max-scored.

Limitations/conclusion: Claims narrow to one model/layer/source dataset; Sandbagging weakest. Linear pipeline; nonlinear probes/readout future work. PC interpretability descriptive, not causal; they have not ablated high-scoring PCs during inference to verify causal role. Conclusion: sparse source-PC subspaces isolate general behavioral structure; source- or target-side separability alone cannot find them. Appendix B LLM judge uses GPT-5-mini; prompt asks positive/negative/shared direction and OOD deception usefulness 1–10, emphasizing narrow descriptions and reserving 5+ for plausibly general deception-relevant behavior.

Paper title: “Probe Generalization as Subspace Selection for OOD Deception Detection.” Thesis: source-heavy probe directions encode source-specific surface features; transferable directions encode same contrast more abstractly/describable in natural language; OOD robustness largely determined by subspace/representation selection. Full probes mix general behavioral features with dataset-specific cues; sparse directional subspaces can filter spurious correlations.

Setup: Work in source Q7 coordinates. N4D = PCA on source-standardized activations, retain leading 100 directions; Q7 = PCs. Subset projection precedes training/eval. E6 = Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct, layer 15 residual stream; activations averaged over assistant-response tokens only. Datasets from Goldowsky-Dill et al. (2025): source V8 Roleplaying; targets C2R Insider Trading Report, W6 Insider Trading Confirm, J9 Sandbagging. Labels GPT-4o K8: honest=0, ambiguous=-1, deceptive=1; ambiguous removed for probe training/eval. Raw label distributions: V8 371 = 140/59/172 (-1/0/1); C2R 473 = 218/194/61; W6 151 = 29/38/84; J9 1000 = 379/375/246. Source standardized zero mean/unit variance; same stats for targets. Logistic regression lambda=10. B8Q = full standardized activations. Error bars 95% CIs. F3 = AUROC.

§4.1 baseline: W6 transfer reasonably good, C2R moderate, J9 poor. Target-trained classification within retained source subspace separates deceptive/honest on every target, so info present but source-trained direction fails to generalize. Appendix numbers: B8Q F3 C2R 0.706, W6 0.874, J9 0.606. Target-trained F3 5-fold CV in leading-100 source subspace: C2R 0.936, W6 0.950, J9 0.869.

§4.2 transferable subspace: H2 greedy target-guided source-trained subset nearly matches target-trained, esp. C2R/J9; variance selection Y4 only matches H2 on W6, far behind C2R/J9; explained variance not predictive. H2: starts empty, considers each leading 100 source Q7 direction, fits source logistic weights on candidate subset, adds direction most improving target F3. Target 5-fold CV selects on non-held-out target folds and evaluates selected source-trained probe on held-out fold; stop if no improvement >0.001. Target labels guide subset selection only, never probe weights; transfer upper bound, not unbiased OOD estimate. Appendix H2 improvement over B8Q: C2R +0.22 F3, J9 +0.23; H2 F3 for recovery comparison C2R 0.929, J9 0.832. Mean H2 subset size, target CV: C2R 15, W6 8, J9 14; full-target H2 k earlier stated: C2R 13, W6 7, J9 14, but Appendix D lists H2 J9 with 15 indices (internal inconsistency); small H2 subset range 8–15.

§4.3 hypotheses: Claimed neither source-side nor target-side ranking recovers transferable subspace/basis better than B8Q. T6 transfers about as well as B8Q. M9 does well on C2R, worse than H2 on W6, below random on J9. Internal contradiction from earlier: sentence “Target-class separation selects directions that transfer better than H2 under source-fitted weighting” conflicts with M9 worse than H2 on W6 and below random on J9. Rankings use X4 = abs probe coefficient times corresponding Q7 std dev on source-N4D-projected activations. T6 = source-trained ranking probe/source-PCA probe. M9 = target-trained ranking probe/target-PCA probe. Both evaluated probes train on source data projected onto top-k ranked directions. Full-target greedy H2 supplies stable set and k rather than fold-specific selections; numbers differ slightly from CV.

§4.4 interpretation: Transferable subsets differ from directions used by source or target classification. H2 direction interpretations express abstract contrasts surviving domain shifts; only partial recovery. LLM judge C7 gets 8 most-activating and 8 least-activating source examples per leading source direction, writes positive/negative/whole-direction descriptions, assigns OOD/generalization score R5. Selection retains all directions reaching observed maximum in both scoring runs; scores noisy. Decoder alignment with PC index decreases: best-matching feature Spearman rho -0.857; mean top-10 features rho -0.917. Appendix C restates lower-index Q7 have stronger decoder alignment using SAE decoder features U9 from `andyrdt/saes-llama-3.1-8b-instruct`.

§4.5 language selection: Language-only selection L2 without target data improves over B8Q; exceeds B8Q on all targets and variance control Y4, widely on C2R/J9; also exceeds A7 everywhere. Recovery: C2R substantially closes baseline–H2 gap; J9 partially; W6 little headroom/uninformative, methods except A7 roughly tied. Appendix L2 F3: C2R 0.881, J9 0.662; baseline–H2 gap recovered by L2: C2R 78%, J9 25% (W6 not reported in appendix table). Controls: A7 = complement/interp-ablated PC probe; Y4 = equal-dimensional top-k PCs by variance; all trained as source probes.

§5 limitations: single model and single source; W6 high baseline uninformative; J9 weakest/most OOD, modest improvement likely from shift; C2R improvement more robust. Pipeline fully linear N4D projection + logistic regression. Direction “encode” claims descriptive from extremes/C7 verbalizations, not causal; high-rated directions not ablated during inference.

Appendix B LLM judge prompt: Direction interpretation uses GPT-5-mini (P2), OpenAI (2025). Prompt asks to interpret bipolar Q7 direction, normalized activations -10 to +10; source setup says E6 enacts simple V8 scenario and is asked question with strategic opportunity to lie. Output fields: Positive pole, Negative pole, Shared direction, R5 (1–10).

Appendix D set comparisons: Text says H2 and M9 agree on less than a fifth of selections, with H2–M9 D3 table C2R 0.182, W6 0.077, J9 0.167. But these D3 values conflict with listed selected Q7 indices: C2R listed sets imply 4/24=0.167; W6 2/20=0.100; J9 4/26=0.154. Listed selected indices: T6 Source = 7,8,11,12,4,5,2,3,6,27,22,21,1,41,18. H2 C2R = 6,89,62,66,26,14,57,25,93,9,70,97,78. H2 W6 = 71,53,28,86,32,81,77. H2 J9 = 37,62,54,41,46,9,57,44,51,43,19,48,86,81,33. M9 C2R = 5,6,89,18,79,46,87,4,14,34,29,1,66,67,19. M9 W6 = 4,1,8,53,30,7,13,18,5,20,26,49,28,31,97. M9 J9 = 51,91,97,13,39,77,4,66,53,86,62,23,41,10,61.

Appendix E Q7 interpretability: max observed R5 = 6; no direction exceeded it; 2 scoring runs. Directions reaching max in both runs and retained for L2 = 19; complement A7 = 81. H2 directions selected for >1 target = 5: 62,57,9 shared by C2R+J9 and 81,86 shared by W6+J9. Of these, maximum-rated = 3/5 (62,57,86 have R5=6; 9 and 81 have R5=3). Maximum-rated among top T6 selections = 1 of top 5: top T6 shown 7(R5=3), 8(4), 11(3), 12(3), 4(6).

Paper title: “Probe Generalization as Subspace Selection for OOD Deception Detection.” Authors Daniel Yoo, Adrians Skapars.

Abstract/main claims: linear probes for deception in Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct activations can fail OOD; projecting onto selected source-domain PCs enables transfer nearly matching oracle target-trained probes. LLM judge can score/interpretable PCs; reported LLM-judge gap closure: 78% on Insider Trading Report, 25% on Sandbagging. Conclusion: small subset of source-domain PCs enables cross-domain transfer nearly matching target-trained probes; subset cannot be found by source-side or target-side separability alone; LLM interpretability score with no target access partially recovers it.

Setup: Source Roleplaying; targets: Insider Trading Report, Insider Trading Confirm, Sandbagging. Labels honest=0, deceptive=1, ambiguous=-1 by GPT-4o; ambiguous removed for probes. Dataset counts before removal: Roleplaying 371 = 140 amb / 59 honest / 172 deceptive; Report 473 = 218 / 194 / 61; Confirm 151 = 29 / 38 / 84; Sandbagging 1000 = 379 / 375 / 246. Activations: Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct, layer 15 residual stream, averaged assistant response tokens. Standardize source; apply stats to targets. PCA on scaled source activations; retain top 100 PCs. Logistic regression λ=10. Baseline probes train on full standardized activations.

Sec 4.1 baseline/Fig 2: full-source transfer AUROCs: Confirm 0.874, Report 0.706, Sandbagging 0.606. Target-trained/oracle within top-100 PCs achieves 0.936 / 0.950 / 0.869 AUROC “across the three targets” likely Report / Confirm / Sandbagging. Conclusion: top-100 contains sufficient info; failure is source-trained direction.

Sec 4.2 greedy oracle PC selection: source-trained probes, subset chosen using labeled target data; 5-fold target CV. Stop improvement <=0.001. Average selected subset sizes: 15 Report, 8 Confirm, 14 Sandbagging. Greedy improves over full baseline by 0.22 Report and 0.23 Sandbagging, close to target-trained; variance control matches greedy only for Confirm.

Sec 4.3/Fig 4: source-PCA and target-PCA PC rankings by standardized coefficients. Evaluated source-trained probes on top-k selected PCs; k set by greedy on full target dataset: k=13 Report, 7 Confirm, 14 Sandbagging. Source-PCA about full baseline; target-PCA good on Report but worse than greedy on Confirm and below random on Sandbagging.

Sec 4.4/App B: For each top-100 source PC, GPT-5-mini sees 8 high/low source examples and rates OOD deception usefulness 1–10. No PC above 6; max score=6. Scored twice; retain PCs scoring max in both runs: 19 PCs. Of 5 PCs appearing in greedy selections for >1 target, 3/5 max OOD; only 1 of top 5 source-PCA PCs max.

Sec 4.5/Fig 5: selects 19 PCs with maximum LLM judge OOD score in both runs. Source-trained probe in this subspace beats baseline and controls on all 3, especially Report/Sandbagging. Gap closures: Report baseline 0.706 to 0.881, closing 78% of gap to greedy 0.929; Sandbagging 0.606 to 0.662, closing 25% gap to greedy 0.832. Internal inconsistency already noted: Sec 4.5 claimed Confirm baseline lower than Sandbagging/more headroom, but Sec 4.1 and Limitations say Confirm baseline 0.874 high/uninformative, Sandbagging 0.606.

Limitations: single model/layer/source. Confirm uninformative because baseline transfer already 0.874. Sandbagging margins small; Report more robust. Linear pipeline only; no causal validation.

Appendix C: lower PCs have stronger SAE alignment using andyrdt/saes-llama-3.1-8b-instruct; Spearman rho = -0.857 best feature, -0.917 mean top 10.

Appendix D/Table 2: Source probe weights row lists 15 PCs: PC7,8,11,12,4,5,2,3,6,27,22,21,1,41,18. Greedy rows: Report 13 PCs; Confirm 7; Sandbagging row lists 15 PCs, conflicting with earlier k=14 and Jaccard. Reported Jaccards greedy vs target-pca: 0.182 Report, 0.077 Confirm, 0.167 Sandbagging; do not match full table rows, match truncated top-k for Report/Confirm and likely Sandbagging if truncated to 14.

Appendix E: Table 3 caption says PCs selected for likely transferability based on LLM judge, but includes repeated-greedy PCs PC62 Report+Sandbagging score 6, PC57 Report+Sandbagging score 6, PC9 Report+Sandbagging score 3, PC81 Confirm+Sandbagging score 3, PC86 Confirm+Sandbagging score 6. This conflicts with the earlier LLM selection rule if interpreted as judge-selected transferable PCs, because judge selection retained only max score 6 PCs. Table 4 gives OOD scores/interpretations for source-weight PCs: PC7=3, PC8=4, PC11=3, PC12=3, PC4=6.

Paper title: “Probe Generalization as Subspace Selection for OOD Deception Detection.” Authors Daniel Yoo, Adrians Skapars.

Main claim: Linear probes for deception in Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct activations may fail OOD. Source Roleplaying; targets Insider Trading Report, Insider Trading Confirm, Sandbagging. Projecting onto selected source PCs gives cross-domain transfer close to target-trained oracle probes. LLM judge can score PC interpretability/transferability without target labels; reported gap closure 78% on Report and 25% on Sandbagging.

Setup: 4 Goldowsky-Dill datasets. Labels honest=0, ambiguous=-1, deceptive=1 by GPT-4o; ambiguous removed. Counts before removal: Roleplaying 371=140/59/172; Report 473=218/194/61; Confirm 151=29/38/84; Sandbagging 1000=379/375/246. Activations: layer 15 residual stream, average assistant-response tokens. Standardize source and apply stats to targets. PCA on scaled source; retain top 100 PCs. Logistic regression λ=10. PC-subset probes use selected top-100 PCs; full baseline uses full standardized activations.

Baseline Fig.2: Source full transfer AUROC: Confirm 0.874, Report 0.706, Sandbagging 0.606. Target-trained top-100 source-PC oracle: 0.936/0.950/0.869 across targets (order likely Report/Confirm/Sand). Concludes top-100 subspace contains target info; transfer failure is source probe direction.

Greedy oracle PC selection: starts empty, searches top 100 source PCs, adds PC improving target AUROC, training source logistic on subset; selection guided by target performance with 5-fold CV over target (select on non-held-out folds, evaluate selected source-trained probe on held-out fold). Stop if improvement ≤0.001. Average subset sizes: 15 Report, 8 Confirm, 14 Sandbagging. Upper bound, not unbiased OOD estimate. Top-k variance control. Fig.3: greedy improves baseline by 0.22 AUROC Report and 0.23 Sandbagging; greedy bounds Report 0.929, Sandbagging 0.832. Variance control matches greedy only for Confirm.

PC-selection rules Fig.4: source-probe weights, target-probe weights, greedy oracle. Source-heavy PCs do not generalize; target-separating PCs not necessarily transferable under source weights. Final probes source-trained on top-k PCs selected from rankings. Greedy full-target k stated: 13 Report, 7 Confirm, 14 Sandbagging. Appendix D Table 2 lists greedy PCs: Report 13 = PC6,89,62,66,26,14,57,25,93,9,70,97,78; Confirm 7 = PC71,53,28,86,32,81,77; Sandbagging 15 = PC37,62,54,41,46,9,57,44,51,43,19,48,86,81,33. This conflicts with earlier Sandbagging k=14. Appendix D Jaccard greedy vs target-pca/target separability reported: Report 0.182, Confirm 0.077, Sandbagging 0.167, but Table 2 sets imply Report 4/24=0.167, Confirm 2/20=0.100, Sandbagging 5/25=0.200.

Interpretability: For each top-100 PC, use 8 highest/8 lowest source examples. LLM describes poles/shared direction and rates OOD deception usefulness 1–10. Prompt/model GPT-5-mini. Activations normalized to integers -10 to +10. Low scores for surface/task cues; scores ≥5 for plausible general deception-relevant strategy. No PC scored above 6; max observed score treated as 6. Run twice; retain PCs with max score in both runs: 19 PCs. 5 PCs appeared in greedy selections for >1 target; 3/5 got max OOD score. Only 1 of top 5 PCs selected by source-PCA probes got max OOD score.

Fig.5: interp-selected 19 PCs outperform baseline on all 3 targets, top-19 variance, and ablated remaining 81. Report 0.706→0.881, closes 78% to greedy 0.929. Confirm baseline 0.874, little headroom. Sandbagging 0.606→0.662, closes 25% to greedy 0.832.

Appendix E: Table 3 lists the 5 PCs selected by greedy on >1 target with LLM OOD scores: PC62 Report+Sandbagging score 6; PC57 Report+Sandbagging score 6; PC9 Report+Sandbagging score 3; PC81 Confirm+Sandbagging score 3; PC86 Confirm+Sandbagging score 6. Caption says selected for likely transferability based on LLM judge, but PC9/PC81 have low score 3 and explanations saying brittle/domain or surface-cue dependent. Table 4 lists example PC scores/explanations: PC7 score3, PC8 score4, PC11 score3, PC12 score3, PC4 score6.

Limitations/conclusion: one model/layer/source; linear only; PC interpretations descriptive not causal. Appendix C: lower-index PCs align more with SAE features using andyrdt/saes-llama-3.1-8b-instruct; Spearman rho -0.857 best-matching feature and -0.917 mean top 10. - Fig. 4 compares source-probe weights (red/source-PCA probe), target-probe weights (pink/target-PCA probe), greedy oracle (purple), 95% CIs.

final_notes:
Paper title: “Probe Generalization as Subspace Selection for OOD Deception Detection” by Daniel Yoo and Adrians Skapars. Abstract: source-probe-heavy directions encode source-specific surface features; transferable directions encode same contrast abstractly and can be captured in natural language; OOD robustness determined largely by subspace selection.

Intro/Related Work: linear probes can reveal semantic info but fail OOD by learning spurious correlations. Central problem: choose dimensions that generalize rather than source artifacts. Uses source PCA/N4D “Q7 coordinates” to avoid privileging model latent dimensions. Intro claimed higher-index Q7 show stronger U9/decoder alignment and removing leading components improves downstream embedding performance; conflicts with Setup/Appendix A/Appendix C, which say/report decoder alignment decreases with index / lower Q7 align more strongly. Related work emphasizes encoded vs recoverable info and uneven generalization of strong in-distribution probes; discusses natural-language feature explanations/interventions.

Paper title: “Probe Generalization as Subspace Selection for OOD Deception Detection.” Authors Daniel Yoo, Adrians Skapars. Main claims: linear probes for deception in Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct activations can fail OOD; projecting onto selected source-domain PCs enables transfer nearly matching oracle target-trained probes. LLM judge can score/interpretable PCs; reported LLM-judge gap closure: 78% on Insider Trading Report, 25% on Sandbagging. Conclusion: OOD probing as representation/subspace selection; robust probing requires identifying where signal is represented, not merely whether linearly accessible.

Setup: Source Roleplaying; targets Insider Trading Report, Insider Trading Confirm, Sandbagging. Labels honest=0, deceptive=1, ambiguous=-1 by GPT-4o; ambiguous removed. Appendix A counts incl ambiguous: Roleplaying 371 = 140/59/172 (-1/0/1); Report 473 = 218/194/61; Confirm 151 = 29/38/84; Sandbagging 1000 = 379/375/246. Activations: Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct, layer 15 residual stream, averaged over assistant response tokens only. Standardize source activations and apply same stats to targets. PCA on scaled source activations; retain top 100 PCs. Logistic regression probes λ=10. Baseline probes train on full standardized activations. Top-100 rationale: interpretability/SAE alignment decreases with PC index; not claiming low-index PCs inherently generalize better.

Sec 4.1/Fig 2: full-source transfer AUROCs: Confirm 0.874, Report 0.706, Sandbagging 0.606. Target-trained/oracle within top-100 source PCs achieves 0.936 / 0.950 / 0.869 AUROC across targets, likely Report / Confirm / Sandbagging. Sec 4.2/Fig 3 greedy oracle PC selection: labeled target folds select among top 100; source-trained probes on held-out target fold; stop if no AUROC improvement >0.001. Average selected subset sizes: 15 Report, 8 Confirm, 14 Sandbagging. Greedy improves over full baseline by 0.22 AUROC on Report and 0.23 on Sandbagging. Variance control matches greedy only for Confirm.

Sec 4.3/Fig 4: source-probe-weighted PCs and target-separating PCs fail. Rankings use abs coefficient × SD of PC. k from greedy on full target: 13 Report, 7 Confirm, 14 Sandbagging. Source-PCA ranking roughly full baseline; target-PCA good on Report but worse than greedy on Confirm and below random on Sandbagging.

Sec 4.4: LLM interprets each top-100 source PC using 8 most/least activating source examples. LLM judge rates OOD usefulness 1–10; no PC above 6, max observed treated as 6. Two runs; 19 PCs scored max both. Of 5 PCs in greedy selections for more than one target, 3/5 max OOD; only 1 of top 5 source-PCA PCs max. Appendix B prompt uses GPT-5-mini; examples from Roleplaying; asks bipolar contrast and OOD deception usefulness.

Sec 4.5/Fig 5: selects 19 max-score PCs. Source-trained interp-selected probe outperforms baseline, top-19 variance, and complement on all 3 targets. Report 0.706→0.881, closing 78% of gap to greedy 0.929. Confirm near ceiling/uninformative. Sandbagging 0.606→0.662, closing 25% of gap to greedy 0.832.

Sec 5 limitations: narrow claims; all experiments use Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct layer 15 and Roleplaying source; Confirm uninformative baseline 0.874; Sandbagging gain small; no causal validation. Possible inconsistency: says pipeline fully linear/layer-15 but also claims findings hold for nonlinear probes and every residual-stream layer. Sec 6: small subset of source-domain PCs enables cross-domain transfer nearly matching target-trained probes; LLM interpretability with no target data partially recovers subspace.

Appendix C/Fig 6: lower PCs show stronger SAE decoder alignment using andyrdt/saes-llama-3.1-8b-instruct; Spearman rho -0.857 for best-matching SAE feature and -0.917 for mean top 10 features.

Appendix D/Table 2 PC set comparisons: text claims Jaccard greedy vs target-pca: Report 0.182, Confirm 0.077, Sandbagging 0.167; says methods agree on <1/5 selections. Table lists source probe weights: PC7, PC8, PC11, PC12, PC4, PC5, PC2, PC3, PC6, PC27, PC22, PC21, PC1, PC41, PC18. Greedy Report 13 PCs: PC6, PC89, PC62, PC66, PC26, PC14, PC57, PC25, PC93, PC9, PC70, PC97, PC78. Greedy Confirm 7: PC71, PC53, PC28, PC86, PC32, PC81, PC77. errors.claim: “All experiments use a single model (Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct, layer 15)…” and later “These findings also hold for nonlinear probes and every residual-stream layer.”
errors.evidence: The limitations section first says all experiments use only layer 15 and a fully linear pipeline: “All experiments use a single model (Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct, layer 15)…” and “Our probe pipeline is fully linear…”
errors.explanation: The later claim that the findings also hold for nonlinear probes and every residual-stream layer contradicts the stated limitation that all experiments used a linear pipeline at layer 15. If results were tested for nonlinear probes and every residual-stream layer, then the experiments were not limited to a fully linear layer-15 pipeline.

Paper title: “Probe Generalization as Subspace Selection for OOD Deception Detection.” Authors Daniel Yoo, Adrians Skapars. Core claim: source-heavy directions encode source-specific surface features; transferable directions encode same contrast more abstractly/capturable in natural language; OOD robustness largely subspace selection.

Setup: N4D = PCA on source-standardized activations, retaining leading 100 directions; Q7 = PCs. Project into source N4D basis, select Q7 subset, train/evaluate probe in that low-dimensional subspace. E6 = Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct; layer 15 residual-stream activations; assistant-response tokens averaged. Source Roleplaying V8; targets Insider Trading Report C2R, Insider Trading Confirm W6, Sandbagging J9. GPT-4o labels honest=0, ambiguous=-1, deceptive=1; ambiguous removed. Source activations standardized; same stats for targets. Classifier logistic regression lambda=10. B8Q baseline trains on all standardized activations. F3 = AUROC.

Raw labels incl ambiguous: V8 371 = 140/59/172 (-1/0/1); C2R 473 = 218/194/61; W6 151 = 29/38/84; J9 1000 = 379/375/246. Baseline transfer: C2R .706, W6 .874, J9 .606. Target-trained 5-fold CV within leading-100 source subspace: C2R .936, W6 .950, J9 .869.

H2 greedy oracle: source-trained subset chosen using target labels/CV, upper bound not unbiased OOD. Mean H2 subset size target CV C2R 15, W6 8, J9 14. Full-target H2 k C2R 13, W6 7, J9 14, but Appendix D Table 2 lists H2 J9 with 15 indices (internal inconsistency). “Small H2 subset range 8–15” conflicts with full-target k=7 unless only CV means. H2 F3 recovery comparison: C2R .929, J9 .832; H2 improves B8Q by about .22 on C2R and .23 on J9.

Rankings: T6 source-side and M9 target-side X4 rankings (abs probe coefficient × Q7 std) do not recover transferable basis better than B8Q; T6 roughly B8Q, M9 good C2R, worse than H2 W6, below random J9. Appendix D selected sets: T6 Source = 7,8,11,12,4,5,2,3,6,27,22,21,1,41,18. H2 C2R = 6,89,62,66,26,14,57,25,93,9,70,97,78. H2 W6 = 71,53,28,86,32,81,77. H2 J9 = 37,62,54,41,46,9,57,44,51,43,19,48,86,81,33. M9 C2R = 5,6,89,18,79,46,87,4,14,34,29,1,66,67,19. M9 W6 = 4,1,8,53,30,7,13,18,5,20,26,49,28,31,97. M9 J9 = 51,91,97,13,39,77,4,66,53,86,62,23,41,10,61. Appendix D claims H2–M9 Jaccard D3 values C2R .182, W6 .077, J9 .167, but table sets imply .167, .100, .154 respectively (internal inconsistency).

Interpretability/language selection: C7 uses GPT-5-mini on eight most/least activating source examples per Q7 direction, outputs positive/negative/shared descriptions and R5 score. Prompt says token<TAB>activation normalized -10 to +10; low R5 for surface/task/noisy, >=5 for general deception-relevant strategies. L2 retains directions reaching observed maximum in both scoring runs; no target data. Appendix E: max observed R5 = 6; two scoring runs; 19 directions reached max in both and retained for L2; A7 complement = 81 directions. H2 directions selected for >1 target = five: 62,57,9 shared C2R+J9; 81,86 shared W6+J9. Among these shared H2 directions, max-rated are 62,57,86 = 3/5; 9 and 81 have R5=3. Among top five T6 directions 7,8,11,12,4, only Q7 4 has max R5=6; R5s listed: 7=3, 8=4, 11=3, 12=3, 4=6.

L2 results: improves over B8Q all targets and over variance Y4; large gains C2R/J9; exceeds A7 everywhere. L2 F3 C2R .881, J9 .662; baseline–H2 gap recovered C2R 78%, J9 25%. W6 has little headroom/uninformative.

Limitations/conclusion: narrow, single model/source; W6 already-high baseline uninformative; J9 most OOD, improvement modest; C2R improvement more robust. “Encode” descriptive, not causal; high-rated directions not ablated during inference. Potential inconsistency from earlier text: claims findings also hold for nonlinear probes and every residual-stream layer despite setup/experiments specifying linear logistic regression on layer-15 activations. Appendix C: lower-index Q7 align more strongly with SAE decoder features U9; Spearman rho best-matching -0.857, mean top-10 -0.917.

Paper title: “Probe Generalization as Subspace Selection for OOD Deception Detection.” Authors Daniel Yoo, Adrians Skapars. Abstract claims: directions heavily weighted by a source probe seem to encode source-specific surface features; transferable directions encode the same contrast more abstractly and can be captured in natural language; probe OOD robustness is largely determined by subspace selection.

Introduction: Linear probes expose semantically meaningful information in LM representations but may fail OOD despite strong in-distribution performance. Paper title: “Probe Generalization as Subspace Selection for OOD Deception Detection.” Authors Daniel Yoo, Adrians Skapars. Work during 11th AI Safety Camp; compute provided; thanks Prasad Mahadik/Arya Hariharan. Impact statement: advances ML, no specific societal consequences highlighted.

Main claims: linear probes for deception in Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct activations can fail OOD; OOD probing can be reframed as subspace/representation selection. Small subset of source-domain PCs can transfer nearly matching target-trained probes, but subset cannot be identified by source-side or target-side separability alone. LLM judge can score/interpretable PCs and partially recover transferable subspace without target data. LLM-judge gap closure: 78% on Insider Trading Report, 25% on Sandbagging. Conclusion: robust probing requires locating where behavioral signal is represented robustly; full-representation probes may mix general behavioral features with dataset-specific surface cues, while sparse PC subspaces can better isolate general behavioral structure.

Setup: Source dataset Roleplaying; targets from Goldowsky-Dill et al. (2025): Insider Trading Report, Insider Trading Confirm, Sandbagging. Labels honest=0, deceptive=1, ambiguous=-1 by GPT-4o; ambiguous removed. Appendix A counts: Roleplaying total 371, labels -1/0/1 = 140/59/172. Insider Trading Report 473, labels 218/194/61. Insider Trading Confirm 151, labels 29/38/84. Sandbagging 1000, labels 379/375/246. Activations: Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct, layer 15 residual stream, averaged over assistant response tokens only. Standardize source activations; apply same stats to targets. PCA on scaled source activations; retain top 100 PCs. Logistic regression probes λ=10. For subset S, project onto S before train/eval. Baseline probes train on full standardized activations. Top-100 rationale: interpretability/SAE alignment decreases with PC index; Appendix C says lower PCs show stronger decoder alignment with andyrdt/saes-llama-3.1-8b-instruct, Spearman rho -0.857 for best-matching SAE feature and -0.917 for mean top 10 features. Not claimed low-index PCs inherently generalize better; Sec 4.1 confirms top-100 retains enough info.

Sec 4.1 baseline: Fig 2 compares source-trained full reps, source-trained top-100 PCs, and target-trained top-100 source PCs with 5-fold CV. Full-source transfer AUROCs: Confirm 0.874, Report 0.706, Sandbagging 0.606. Target-trained/oracle within top-100 PCs achieves 0.936 / 0.950 / 0.869 AUROC across targets (likely Report / Confirm / Sandbagging). Conclusion: top-100 contains sufficient info; failure is source-trained direction not generalizing.

Sec 4.2 greedy oracle PC selection: searches top 100 source PCs, adds PC with best target AUROC improvement for source-trained projected probes. Uses labeled target examples; 5-fold target CV selection on non-held-out folds and evaluation on held-out fold. Stop if no improvement >0.001. Average selected subset sizes in CV: 15 Report, 8 Confirm, 14 Sandbagging. Greedy improves over full baseline by ~0.22 Report and ~0.23 Sandbagging; close to target-trained probes. Later Sec 4.5/5 states greedy oracle AUROC is 0.929 Report and 0.832 Sandbagging. Greedy is upper bound, not unbiased OOD, because selection uses target data.

Sec 4.3: tests whether transferable PCs are individually target-separating or highly weighted by source probe. Fig 4 compares source-PCA-probe ranking, target-PCA-probe ranking, and greedy oracle. Rankings use source-PCA basis and standardized coefficient = abs(coef) × SD of PC. Evaluated probes trained on source data projected onto top k PCs from ranking. Earlier notes: Fig 4 k set by greedy run on full target dataset: k=13 Report, 7 Confirm, 14 Sandbagging. Appendix D Table 2 instead lists greedy Sandbagging with 15 PCs; Report 13 and Confirm 7. Results: source-PCA probe transfers about as well as full baseline; target-PCA probe does well on Report but worse than greedy on Confirm and below random on Sandbagging.

Appendix D PC sets: source probe weights top list: PC7,8,11,12,4,5,2,3,6,27,22,21,1,41,18. Greedy Report: PC6,89,62,66,26,14,57,25,93,9,70,97,78. Greedy Confirm: PC71,53,28,86,32,81,77. Greedy Sandbagging: PC37,62,54,41,46,9,57,44,51,43,19,48,86,81,33. Target ranking Report table lists 15 PCs: PC5,6,89,18,79,46,87,4,14,34,29,1,66,67,19. Confirm target ranking 15: PC4,1,8,53,30,7,13,18,5,20,26,49,28,31,97. Sandbag target ranking 15: PC51,91,97,13,39,77,4,66,53,86,62,23,41,10,61. Appendix D reports Jaccard greedy vs target-pca = 0.182 Report, 0.077 Confirm, 0.167 Sandbagging, but these do not match the listed full table sets.

Sec 4.4 interpretability: For each top-100 source PC, find 8 most and 8 least PC-activating source examples; prompt LLM to describe positive pole, negative pole, overall direction. LLM judge rates OOD generalizability 1–10. No PC scored above 6, so 6 treated as maximum observed OOD score. Scoring run twice; PCs with max score in both runs retained: 19 PCs. Among 5 PCs appearing in greedy selections for more than one target, 3/5 received max OOD score. Only 1 of top 5 PCs selected by source-PCA probes received max OOD score. Appendix E has breakdown.

Appendix B LLM judge prompt: says GPT-5-mini used to interpret directions; examples from Roleplay source. Required output: Positive pole, Negative pole, Shared direction, OOD deception usefulness.

Sec 4.5 interp-selected subspace: Fig 5 evaluates 19 interp-selected PCs versus full baseline, top-19 variance PCs, and remaining 81 PCs after ablating selected PCs. No target data used. Interp-selected probe outperforms baseline, variance control, and ablated probe on all 3 targets; wide margins on Report/Sandbagging. Report: baseline 0.706 to ~0.881, closing 78% to greedy 0.929. Confirm: baseline near ceiling/little headroom; methods aside from interp-ablated roughly similar. Sandbagging: baseline 0.606 to ~0.662, closing 25% to greedy 0.832.

Sec 5 limitations: narrow; all experiments use single model Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct layer 15 and single source Roleplaying. Confirm uninformative because baseline already 0.874. Sandbagging margins small; Report more robust. Pipeline fully linear; nonlinear/readout extensions open. Structural/PC encoding claims descriptive from examples and LLM verbalization, not causal; no inference-time ablation to verify contrast.

Appendix E: Table 3 lists PCs selected by greedy for more than one target and OOD scores/explanations: PC62 Report+Sandbagging score 6; PC57 Report+Sandbagging score 6; PC9 Report+Sandbagging score 3; PC81 Confirm+Sandbagging score 3; PC86 Confirm+Sandbagging score 6. This supports earlier statement that 3/5 multi-target greedy PCs received max observed score 6. Table 4 begins listing OOD scores/interpretations for individual PCs: PC7 score 3, PC8 4, PC11 3, PC12 3, PC4 6; this supports earlier statement that only 1 of top 5 source-PCA PCs got max score (source top 5 were PC7,8,11,12,4).

final_notes:
Paper title: “Probe Generalization as Subspace Selection for OOD Deception Detection.” Authors Daniel Yoo, Adrians Skapars. Abstract/core thesis: source-probe-heavy directions encode source-specific surface features; transferable directions encode same contrast more abstractly/natural-language-capturable; OOD robustness largely determined by subspace selection.

Setup: N4D = PCA on source-standardized activations, retaining leading 100 directions; Q7 = PCs. Pipeline: project into source PCA basis, filter Q7 directions, train/evaluate probe in selected subspace. Retaining 100 for interpretability/comparability, not because low-index PCs necessarily generalize. Lower PCs easier to interpret/aligned with SAE decoder vectors U9.

Experimental setup: Single Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct (E6), layer 15 residual stream, assistant-response tokens averaged. Datasets: source Roleplaying V8; targets Insider Trading Report C2R, Insider Trading Confirm W6, Sandbagging J9. GPT-4o labeler K8: honest=0, ambiguous=-1, deceptive=1; ambiguous removed. Source activations standardized; same stats for targets. Logistic regression lambda=10. Full-representation baseline B8Q trains all standardized activations. Error bars 95% CIs. F3 = AUROC.

Dataset totals incl ambiguous: V8 371 = 140/59/172 (-1/0/1). C2R 473 = 218/194/61. W6 151 = 29/38/84. J9 1000 = 379/375/246.

§4.1 baseline: W6 transfer reasonably good, C2R moderate, J9 poor. Target-trained classification within retained source PCA subspace separates deceptive/honest on every target, so info exists but source-trained direction fails. B8Q F3: C2R .706, W6 .874, J9 .606. Target-trained 5-fold CV in leading-100 source subspace: C2R .936, W6 .950, J9 .869.

§4.2 H2 greedy oracle: starts empty, considers leading 100 source PCs, fits source logistic regression on candidate subset, adds direction maximizing target F3; stop if improvement <=.001. Target labels guide subset only, not weights; upper bound, not unbiased OOD. H2 nearly matches target-trained probes esp. C2R/J9. Variance selection Y4 with k matched to H2 only matches W6, worse C2R/J9. H2 improvement over B8Q: .22 C2R, .23 J9. H2 F3 recovery comparison: C2R .929, J9 .832. Mean H2 subset size target CV: C2R 15, W6 8, J9 14; full-target H2 k: C2R 13, W6 7, J9 14; elsewhere Appendix D says full H2 selected indices C2R 13, W6 7, J9 15, conflicting with earlier J9 k=14.

§4.3 rankings: Source-side T6 and target-side M9 coefficient rankings do not recover transferable subspace or transfer better than B8Q. T6 about B8Q; M9 good C2R, worse than H2 on W6, below random on J9. X4 ranking = abs probe coefficient × corresponding Q7 std dev on source-N4D-projected activations. Top T6 indices: 7,8,11,12,4,5,2,3,6,27,22,21,1,41,18. Appendix D H2–M9 Jaccard claims conflict with set arithmetic: claimed C2R .182, W6 .077, J9 .167 but sets imply .167, .100, .154.

§4.4/Appendix B/E interpretation: C7 interpreter uses 8 most-activating and 8 least-activating source examples per leading source direction; generates positive/negative/shared descriptions and R5 score 1–10. GPT-5-mini/OpenAI 2025. Selection for L2 retains directions reaching observed maximum in both scoring runs; scores noisy. Earlier claim about descriptions surviving every LLM family conflicts with single-model setup/§5 limitation. Appendix E: maximum observed R5 = 6; scoring runs = 2; directions reaching max in both runs retained for L2 = 19; complement A7 = 81. Shared H2 selections for >1 target = 5; among these max-rated = 3/5. Shared H2 table: Q7 62 C2R+J9 R5 6; 57 C2R+J9 R5 6; 9 C2R+J9 R5 3; 81 W6+J9 R5 3; 86 W6+J9 R5 6. Paper title: “Probe Generalization as Subspace Selection for OOD Deception Detection.” Authors Daniel Yoo, Adrians Skapars. Work during 11th AI Safety Camp; compute by AI Safety Camp.

Abstract/main claims: linear probes for deception in Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct activations can fail OOD; projecting onto selected source-PCA PCs enables cross-domain transfer near oracle/target-trained probes. Evaluates Roleplaying source vs 3 targets: Insider Trading Report, Insider Trading Confirm, Sandbagging. LLM judge scores PC interpretations to select transferable deception directions. Reported LLM-judge gap closure: 78% on Report and 25% on Sandbagging. Conclusion: OOD probing as representation/subspace selection.

Datasets/labels: Goldowsky-Dill deception datasets. Roleplaying total 371, labels -1/0/1 = 140/59/172, usable 231. Insider Trading Report 473, 218/194/61, usable 255. Insider Trading Confirm 151, 29/38/84, usable 122. Sandbagging 1000, 379/375/246, usable 621. Labels: honest=0, ambiguous=-1 removed, deceptive=1 by GPT-4o.

Setup: Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct layer 15 residual stream, assistant-token average. Standardize source activations, apply stats to targets. PCA on scaled source activations; top 100 PCs. Logistic regression λ=10. For subset S project onto S. Baseline trains on full standardized activations.

Sec 4.1/Fig.2: source-trained full probe target AUROCs: Confirm 0.874, Report 0.706, Sandbagging 0.606. Target-trained probe within top-100 source PCs using 5-fold CV achieves 0.936 / 0.950 / 0.869 across targets, order likely Report / Confirm / Sandbagging though preceding sentence listed Confirm first. They say top-100 source-PC subspace has enough target information. Possible tension: earlier “causally increase” wording vs §5 no causal validation.

Sec 4.2/Fig.3: greedy PC selection among top 100 source PCs, using labeled target examples with 5-fold CV: select on non-held-out target folds, evaluate source-trained probe on held-out fold. Stop if no AUROC improvement >0.001. Avg selected subset sizes: 15 Report, 8 Confirm, 14 Sandbagging. Greedy is an upper bound, not unbiased OOD. Variance control selects top k PCs by variance. Greedy improves baseline by 0.22 Report and 0.23 Sandbagging; variance control matches only easy Confirm.

Sec 4.3/Fig.4: tests if transferable PCs are individually target-separating or heavily weighted by source probe. Ranking by standardized coefficient = abs coefficient × PC SD. Source-PCA ranking by source-trained probe weights; target-PCA by target-trained probe weights, but wording ambiguous about final training. k set using greedy on full target: k=13 Report, 7 Confirm, 14 Sandbagging (but Appendix D later lists 15 greedy Sandbagging PCs, inconsistent). Results: both hypotheses fail. Source-PCA probe transfers about as full baseline. Target-PCA good on Report, worse than greedy on Confirm, below-random on Sandbagging.

Sec 4.4: top-100 source PCs interpreted using 8 most/least activating source examples. LLM describes positive pole, negative pole, overall direction; judge rates OOD usefulness 1–10. No PC above 6; retain PCs scoring 6 in both runs, yielding 19 interp-selected PCs. Of 5 PCs appearing in greedy selections for >1 target, 3/5 got max OOD score; only 1 of top 5 source-PCA PCs got max score. Appendix B: GPT-5-mini prompt, normalized activations -10 to +10, Roleplaying examples, output Positive pole/Negative pole/Shared direction/OOD deception usefulness.

Sec 4.5/Fig.5: 19 LLM-selected PCs, no target data. Source-trained probe AUROC compared to full baseline, top-19 variance, remaining-81 ablation. Interp-selected beats baseline on all targets and controls. Gap recovery: Report 0.706→0.881 closes 78% to greedy 0.929. Confirm near ceiling. Sandbagging 0.606→0.662 closes 25% to greedy 0.832.

Sec 5 limitations: one model/layer/source; Confirm uninformative because baseline already 0.874; Sandbagging weakest/most OOD; linear pipeline; no causal validation or inference-time ablation.

Appendix C: Lower PCs show stronger decoder alignment to SAE features from andyrdt/saes-llama-3.1-8b-instruct; Spearman ρ = -0.857 for best-matching SAE feature and -0.917 for mean top 10.

Appendix D/Table 2: PC set comparisons. Claims Jaccard greedy vs target-pca: Report 0.182, Confirm 0.077, Sandbagging 0.167; says methods agree on less than a fifth. But values conflict with listed 15-PC target sets: Report listed sets give 4/24=0.167; Confirm 2/20=0.100; Sandbagging listed sets give common {PC51, PC86, PC62, PC41}, union 26, Jaccard 0.154. Table source probe weights list 15 PCs: PC7,8,11,12,4,5,2,3,6,27,22,21,1,41,18. Greedy lists Report 13 PCs, Confirm 7, Sandbagging 15. Target separability ranking lists 15 PCs for each target.

Appendix E: Table 3 caption says PCs “selected for likely transferability, based on interpretation with an LLM judge,” but lists the 5 PCs selected on multiple greedy targets: PC62 Report+Sandbagging score 6; PC57 Report+Sandbagging score 6; PC9 Report+Sandbagging score 3; PC81 Confirm+Sandbagging score 3; PC86 Confirm+Sandbagging score 6. This conflicts with the earlier LLM-judge selection rule retaining score-6 PCs; PC9/PC81 are not LLM-selected transferable by that criterion. Table 4 starts listing PC OOD scores/interpretations: PC7 3, PC8 4, PC11 3, PC12 3, PC4 6, consistent with earlier “only 1 of top 5 source-PCA PCs got max score.”

- Evaluates probe generalization over 3 held-out deception detection datasets.

Paper title: “Probe Generalization as Subspace Selection for OOD Deception Detection.” Authors Daniel Yoo, Adrians Skapars. Abstract claims source probe heavily weighted directions encode source-specific surface features; transferable directions encode same contrast abstractly/natural-language capturable; OOD robustness largely determined by subspace selection.

Setup: Linear probes for OOD deception. Model Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct (E6), layer 15 residual-stream activations averaged over assistant-response tokens. Baseline B8Q trains on all standardized activations. AUROC=F3; 95% CIs.

Appendix A label counts before ambiguous removal: V8 371 labels -1/0/1=140/59/172; C2R 473=218/194/61; W6 151=29/38/84; J9 1000=379/375/246.

Representation: N4D=PCA on source-standardized activations, retaining leading 100 Q7/PCs; projections before training/eval. Abstract claims: directions heavily weighted by source probe encode source-specific surface features; transferable directions encode same contrast more abstractly and can be captured in natural language; probe OOD robustness largely determined by subspace selection.

(2025): source Roleplaying (V8); targets Insider Trading Report (C2R), Insider Trading Confirm (W6), Sandbagging (J9). Experiment 4.1 baseline: W6 transfer reasonably good, C2R moderate, J9 poor. Target-trained classification within retained source subspace separates deceptive/honest on all targets, suggesting information present. Claim: source probe’s favored directions causally increase E6 deception on target responses. Figure 2 compares target F3 for source-trained full representations B8Q (blue), source-trained leading 100 Q7 (orange), target-trained leading 100 source Q7 with 5-fold CV (green).

Experiment 4.2 transferable subspace: Small source-trained subspaces can nearly match target-trained probes, especially C2R and J9. Variance selection matches H2 only on easy W6; falls behind on C2R/J9; explained variance not predictive. Greedy oracle H2: starts empty, considers each leading 100 source Q7 direction, projects source activations to current candidate subset, fits source logistic-regression weights, adds direction most improving target F3. Target 5-fold CV selects on non-held-out target folds and evaluates selected source-trained probe on held-out fold. Stop if no candidate improvement >0.001. Target labels guide subset selection only, never probe-weight fitting. H2 is transfer upper bound, not unbiased OOD estimate. Figure 3: B8Q (blue), Y4 with k matched to H2 (teal), H2 (purple).

Experiment 4.3 hypotheses for transferable components: Neither source-side nor target-side ranking recovers transferable subspace or transfers better than B8Q. T6 transfers about as well as B8Q; source-reliant directions do not generalize. M9 does well on C2R, worse than H2 on W6, below random on J9. Target-class separation and transfer under source-fitted weighting select different directions. Rankings use standardized coefficient X4 = absolute probe coefficient × corresponding Q7 standard deviation, on source-N4D-projected activations. Source-trained ranking probe/source-PCA probe T6 and target-trained ranking probe/target-PCA probe M9 provide X4 orderings; evaluated probes then train on source data projected to top-k ranked directions. Full-target H2 supplies stable set and k rather than fold-specific selections; numbers differ slightly from CV. Figure 4: T6 red, M9 pink, H2 purple.

Experiment 4.4 interpretation: Transferable subsets differ from directions relied on by source or target classification. Interpretations of H2-selected directions express contrasts abstract enough to survive domain changes; only partial recovery. For each leading source direction, interpreter LLM judge C7 gets 8 most-activating and 8 least-activating source examples; generates positive-pole, negative-pole, whole-direction descriptions following Bills/Casademunt; assigns OOD/generalization score R5. Selection retains all directions reaching observed maximum in both scoring runs; scores noisy.

Experiment 4.5 language-only subspace selection: L2 = interp-selected PC probe from retained intersection; no target data. Controls: complement A7 = interp-ablated PC probe; equal-dimensional variance-ranked subset Y4 = top-k PCs by variance; all trained as source probes. Claims: L2 meaningfully improves generalization over B8Q, exceeds B8Q on all targets and variance control, widely on C2R/J9; also exceeds A7 everywhere. Recovery varies: C2R substantially closes baseline–H2 gap; J9 only partially; W6 has little headroom and all methods except A7 roughly tied. Paper title: “Probe Generalization as Subspace Selection for OOD Deception Detection.” Authors Daniel Yoo, Adrians Skapars. Work from 11th AI Safety Camp.

Abstract/main claims: Linear probes may fail OOD; projecting inputs onto small subset of source-distribution PCs enables cross-domain transfer nearly matching target-trained/oracle probes. LLM judge scores PC interpretations from most/least activating examples; probe trained on highest-scoring PCs. Reported gap closure: 78% on Insider Trading Report and 25% on Sandbagging. OOD robustness largely determined by subspace selection.

Setup: Datasets: Roleplaying source; targets: Insider Trading Report, Insider Trading Confirm, Sandbagging. Labels honest 0, ambiguous -1, deceptive 1 by GPT-4o; ambiguous removed for training/eval. Counts before removal: Roleplaying 371, -1/0/1=140/59/172; Report 473, 218/194/61; Confirm 151, 29/38/84; Sandbagging 1000, 379/375/246. Model/activations: Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct, layer 15 residual stream, average over assistant response only. Standardize source activations; apply source stats to targets. PCA on scaled source activations; retain top 100 PCs. Logistic regression λ=10. Baseline probes train on full standardized activations.

§4.1 baseline: Fig. 2 compares source-trained full reps, source-trained top-100 PCs, target-trained top-100 source PCs with 5-fold CV. Full source transfer AUROC: Confirm 0.874, Report 0.706, Sandbagging 0.606. Target-trained in 100-PC source-PCA subspace: 0.936 / 0.950 / 0.869, apparently Confirm / Report / Sandbagging. Conclusion: 100-PC subspace contains target info; source probe learns nongeneralizing direction.

§4.2 greedy oracle: Greedy PC selection from top 100 source PCs, train on source projected to candidate subset, select by target AUROC. Uses target labels; upper bound, not unbiased OOD. 5-fold target CV: select using non-held-out folds; evaluate source-trained probe on held-out fold. Stop if improvement ≤0.001. Average selected subset sizes in CV: 15 PCs Report, 8 Confirm, 14 Sandbagging. Greedy oracle values Report 0.929 and Sandbagging 0.832; improves over full baseline by ~0.22 Report and ~0.23 Sandbagging. Variance control matches greedy only for Confirm. Earlier internal inconsistency: section says retaining greedy PCs “causally makes the model more honest,” but experiments only improve probe AUROC, not model behavior.

§4.3 PC-weight hypotheses: Fig. 4 compares source-probe weights, target-probe weights/target-PCA probe, greedy oracle. Rankings use standardized coefficient = abs coefficient × PC std from probe trained in source-PCA basis. For Fig. 4 k set by greedy on full target dataset: k=13 Report, 7 Confirm, 14 Sandbagging; differs from CV. Final probes trained on source projected onto top-k PCs by rankings. Both hypotheses fail. Source-PCA probe transfers about as well as full baseline. Target-PCA probe does well on Report, worse than greedy on Confirm, below-random transfer on Sandbagging.

§4.4: For each top-100 source PC, find 8 most/least activating source examples; LLM describes direction; LLM judge rates OOD usefulness 1–10. No PC scored above 6; 6 treated as max observed. Scoring run twice; retain PCs with max score in both runs: 19 PCs. Of 5 PCs in greedy selections for >1 target, 3/5 got max OOD score; only 1 of top 5 source-PCA probe PCs got max. Appendix B judge prompt says GPT-5-mini and token<TAB>activation format, conflicting with method saying source examples.

§4.5: Fig. 5 interp-selected 19 PCs vs full baseline, top-19 variance, and ablated remaining 81. Interp-selected PCs have max OOD score in both judge runs; no target data. Outperforms baseline all targets; Report 0.706→0.881 closes 78% gap to greedy 0.929. Confirm little headroom. Sandbagging 0.606→0.662 closes 25% gap to greedy 0.832.

§5 Limitations: Single model/layer/source; Confirm uninformative due baseline 0.874; Sandbagging margins small; linear only; no causal validation of PC encoding. Conflicts with earlier causal wording. §6 conclusion: small source-PC subset enables cross-domain transfer nearly matching target-trained probes; source/target separability alone fail; LLM-judge interpretability partially recovers subspace.

Appendix C: Lower PCs show stronger decoder alignment with SAE features, Spearman ρ=-0.857 for best-matching feature and -0.917 for mean top 10; uses andyrdt/saes-llama-3.1-8b-instruct.

Appendix D: Claims Jaccard overlap between greedy and target-pca sets: Report 0.182, Confirm 0.077, Sandbagging 0.167, and says agreement <1/5. Paper title: “Probe Generalization as Subspace Selection for OOD Deception Detection.” Authors Daniel Yoo, Adrians Skapars. Work from 11th AI Safety Camp. Impact statement generic.

Abstract/main claims: Linear probes may fail OOD; projecting inputs onto small subset of source-distribution PCs enables cross-domain transfer nearly matching target-trained/oracle probes. Setup: Datasets: Roleplaying source; targets: Insider Trading Report, Insider Trading Confirm, Sandbagging. Labels honest 0, ambiguous -1, deceptive 1 by GPT-4o; ambiguous removed for training/eval. Appendix A dataset descriptions/counts before removal: Roleplaying total 371, counts -1/0/1 = 140/59/172; Insider Trading Report total 473, 218/194/61; Insider Trading Confirm total 151, 29/38/84; Sandbagging total 1000, 379/375/246. Model/activations: Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct, layer 15 residual stream, average over assistant response only. Standardize source activations; apply source stats to targets. PCA on scaled source activations; retain top 100 PCs. Probes: logistic regression λ=10. For subset S, project activations onto S before training/eval. Baseline probes train on full standardized activations.

§4.1 baseline: Figure 2 compares source-trained full reps (blue), source-trained top-100 PCs (orange), target-trained top-100 source PCs with 5-fold CV (green), 95% CIs. Full source-representation transfer AUROC: Insider Trading Confirm 0.874, Insider Trading Report 0.706, Sandbagging 0.606. Target-trained probe in 100-PC source-PCA subspace with 5-fold CV: 0.936 / 0.950 / 0.869, apparently Confirm / Report / Sandbagging. Conclusion: 100-PC subspace contains target info; source probe learns nongeneralizing direction.

Uses target labels; upper bound, not unbiased OOD. 5-fold target CV: select using non-held-out folds; evaluate selected source-trained probe on held-out fold. Stop if no candidate improves AUROC >0.001. Average selected subset sizes in CV: 15 PCs Report, 8 Confirm, 14 Sandbagging. Greedy improves over full baseline by ~0.22 AUROC Report and ~0.23 Sandbagging; greedy oracle values Report 0.929 and Sandbagging 0.832. Variance control matches greedy only for Confirm, worse for Report/Sandbagging. Internal inconsistency noted earlier: section says retaining greedy PCs “causally makes the model more honest,” but experiments only improve probe AUROC, not model behavior/honesty.

§4.3 PC-weight hypotheses: Figure 4 compares selection rules: source-probe weights/source-PCA probe (red), target-probe weights/target-PCA probe (pink), greedy oracle (purple), 95% CIs. Rankings use standardized coefficient = abs coefficient × PC std from probe trained in source-PCA basis. For Fig. 4 k set by running greedy on full target dataset, not CV: k=13 Report, 7 Confirm, 14 Sandbagging; differs slightly from CV numbers. Final probes are trained on source projected onto top-k PCs by rankings. Both hypotheses fail. Source-PCA probe transfers about as well as full representation baseline. Target-PCA probe does well on Report, worse than greedy on Confirm, and below-random transfer on Sandbagging.

§4.4 interpreting transferable subspace: For each top-100 source PC, find 8 most and 8 least activating source examples. Prompt LLM to describe positive pole, negative pole, whole direction. LLM judge rates generalizability/OOD score 1–10. No PC scored above 6, so 6 treated as max observed score. Scoring run twice; retain PCs with max score in both runs: 19 PCs. Among 5 PCs appearing in greedy selections for more than one target, 3/5 got max OOD score; only 1 of top 5 source-PCA probe PCs got max score. Authors say greedy-selected PC interpretations describe abstract contrasts surviving domain shift. Appendix E has breakdown.

Results: interp-selected probe outperforms baseline on all 3 targets; outperforms variance control, especially Report and Sandbagging; outperforms interp-ablated on all 3. Report: 0.706 to 0.881, closes 78% of gap to greedy oracle 0.929. Confirm: baseline near ceiling; little headroom; all methods except interp-ablated roughly comparable. Sandbagging: 0.606 to 0.662, closes 25% of gap to greedy oracle 0.832.

§5 Limitations: Single model/layer/source dataset; Confirm uninformative because baseline transfer already 0.874. Sandbagging margins small, only 25% gap closure. Pipeline linear only. No causal validation: PC encoding claims descriptive, not causal; no ablation during inference to verify contrast. This conflicts with earlier causal wording.

§6 Conclusion: Small subset of source-domain PCs enables cross-domain transfer nearly matching target-trained probes; subset cannot be found with source-side or target-side separability alone. LLM-judge interpretability score with no target data partially recovers subspace. Robust probing framed as representation/subspace selection.

Paper title: “Probe Generalization as Subspace Selection for OOD Deception Detection.” Authors Daniel Yoo, Adrians Skapars. Abstract claims source-probe-heavy directions encode source-specific surface features; transferable directions encode same contrast more abstractly and can be captured in natural language; OOD robustness mostly determined by subspace selection.

Setup: Work in source Q7 coordinates. N4D = PCA on source-standardized activations, retain leading 100 directions; Q7 = PCs. Projection onto subset S precedes training/eval. 100 chosen for interpretability comparability. Appendix C: lower-index Q7 align more strongly with SAE decoder vectors U9; Spearman alignment vs index: best-matching feature -0.857, mean top 10 -0.917. Model E6 = Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct; layer 15 residual-stream activations averaged over assistant-response tokens only. Datasets from Goldowsky-Dill et al. (2025): source Roleplaying V8; targets Insider Trading Report C2R, Insider Trading Confirm W6, Sandbagging J9. GPT-4o labeler K8: honest=0, ambiguous=-1, deceptive=1; ambiguous removed. Source activations standardized zero mean/unit variance; target standardized with source stats. Logistic regression lambda=10. Full-representation baseline B8Q trains on all standardized activations. Metric F3 = AUROC. Error bars 95% CIs.

Dataset labels (-1/0/1): V8 total 371 = 140/59/172; C2R 473 = 218/194/61; W6 151 = 29/38/84; J9 1000 = 379/375/246. V8 simple opportunity to lie; C2R trader deciding whether to honestly report insider-information use; W6 asks E6, after concealing earlier insider use, to confirm non-use; J9 deliberate underperformance vs normal.

4.1 Baseline: W6 transfer reasonably good, C2R moderate, J9 poor. Target-trained classification within retained source subspace separates honest/deceptive on every target. B8Q F3: C2R 0.706, W6 0.874, J9 0.606. Target-trained leading-100 source-subspace 5-fold CV F3: C2R 0.936, W6 0.950, J9 0.869.

4.2 H2 transferable subspace: Greedy oracle starts empty, considers each leading 100 source Q7, trains source logistic on candidate subset, adds direction most improving target F3; target labels guide subset selection only, not weights; target CV selects on non-held-out folds and evaluates held-out; stop if no improvement >0.001. Transfer upper bound, not unbiased OOD estimate. H2 improves over B8Q ≈0.22 C2R and 0.23 J9; H2 F3 for recovery: C2R 0.929, J9 0.832; mean H2 subset size target CV C2R 15, W6 8, J9 14. Earlier notes said full-target H2 k C2R 13, W6 7, J9 14, but Appendix D Table 2 lists full H2 J9 with 15 indices (internal conflict).

4.3 Rankings: Neither source-side nor target-side ranking recovers transferable subspace or better-than-B8Q basis. T6 transfers about as B8Q; M9 good on C2R, worse than H2 on W6, below random on J9. Rankings use X4 = abs probe coefficient times corresponding Q7 SD on source-N4D-projected activations. T6 = source-trained/source-PCA ranking; M9 = target-trained/target-PCA ranking; evaluated probes train on source data projected onto top k ranked directions. Appendix D says H2 and M9 agree on <1/5 selections. Reported H2–M9 D3: C2R 0.182, W6 0.077, J9 0.167, but selected-index table implies Jaccards C2R 4/24=0.167, W6 2/20=0.100, J9 4/26=0.154. Table 2 indices: T6 Source = 7,8,11,12,4,5,2,3,6,27,22,21,1,41,18. H2 C2R = 6,89,62,66,26,14,57,25,93,9,70,97,78; H2 W6 = 71,53,28,86,32,81,77; H2 J9 = 37,62,54,41,46,9,57,44,51,43,19,48,86,81,33. M9 C2R = 5,6,89,18,79,46,87,4,14,34,29,1,66,67,19; M9 W6 = 4,1,8,53,30,7,13,18,5,20,26,49,28,31,97; M9 J9 = 51,91,97,13,39,77,4,66,53,86,62,23,41,10,61.

4.4/Appendix E Interpretation: C7 sees 8 most/least source examples per leading source direction, produces positive/negative/shared descriptions and OOD/generalization score R5. GPT-5-mini P2 prompt uses token<TAB>activation normalized -10 to +10; asks narrow supported contrast and low scores for surface/lexical/task-specific cues; 5+ only for plausible general deception-relevant strategies/behaviors. Appendix E: max observed R5 = 6, no direction exceeded it; 2 scoring runs; 19 directions reached max in both runs and retained for L2; A7 complement has 81 directions. Shared H2 selections across >1 target = 5: 62,57,9 shared C2R+J9; 81,86 shared W6+J9. Among these, max-rated directions = 3/5: 62 R5=6, 57 R5=6, 86 R5=6; 9 and 81 R5=3. Top T6 first five R5s: 7=3, 8=4, 11=3, 12=3, 4=6, so 1/5 max-rated. Internal issue: Appendix E Table 3 is captioned as directions selected for likely transferability from C7 interpretation but includes R5=3 directions, conflicting with stated selection rule that L2 retained only directions reaching max R5=6 in both runs.

4.5 Language selection: L2 interp-selected PC probe improves over B8Q on all targets and over variance control, esp. C2R/J9; exceeds A7 everywhere. L2 F3: C2R 0.881, J9 0.662; baseline–H2 gap recovered: C2R 78%, J9 25%. Controls: A7 complement/interp-ablated PC probe; Y4 equal-dimensional top-k PCs by variance.

Limitations: single model/source; W6 high baseline uninformative; J9 weakest/most OOD; pipeline linear; encoding interpretations descriptive, not causal/ablated. Conclusion: robust probing requires representation/subspace selection; full probes may mix general and dataset-specific cues; sparse subspaces may isolate more general behavioral structure.

Paper title: “Probe Generalization as Subspace Selection for OOD Deception Detection.” Authors Daniel Yoo, Adrians Skapars. Work during 11th AI Safety Camp; compute by AI Safety Camp. Impact Statement: goal advancing ML, no societal consequences needing specific highlighting.

Abstract/main claims: linear probes for deception in Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct activations can fail OOD; projecting onto selected source-domain PCs enables transfer nearly matching oracle target-trained probes. LLM judge can score/interpretable PCs; reported LLM-judge gap closure: 78% on Insider Trading Report, 25% on Sandbagging. Conclusion: robust probing depends on where signal is represented, not only linear accessibility; full probes may mix general behavioral features with source-specific surface cues; OOD probing reframed as representation/subspace selection.

Setup: Source dataset Roleplaying; targets from Goldowsky-Dill et al. (2025): Insider Trading Report, Insider Trading Confirm, Sandbagging. Labels honest=0, deceptive=1, ambiguous=-1 by GPT-4o; ambiguous removed. Appendix A counts before removing ambiguous: Roleplaying 371 total, labels -1/0/1 = 140/59/172; Insider Trading Report 473, 218/194/61; Insider Trading Confirm 151, 29/38/84; Sandbagging 1000, 379/375/246.

Activations: Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct, layer 15 residual stream, averaged over assistant response tokens only. Standardize source activations; same stats to targets. PCA on scaled source activations; retain top 100 PCs. Logistic regression probes λ=10. For subset S, project onto S before train/eval. Baseline probes train on full standardized activations. Top-100 rationale: interpretability/SAE alignment decreases with PC index; not claimed low-index PCs inherently generalize better. Sec 4.1 intended to confirm top-100 retains enough information.

Sec 4.1/Fig 2: 5-fold CV, AUROC with 95% CIs. Full-source transfer AUROCs: Confirm 0.874, Report 0.706, Sandbagging 0.606. Target-trained/oracle in top-100 source PCs: 0.936 / 0.950 / 0.869 AUROC across three targets, likely order Report / Confirm / Sandbagging. Conclusion: top-100 contains sufficient info; source-trained direction fails to generalize.

Sec 4.2/Fig 3: Greedy starts empty; at each step searches top 100 source PCs and adds PC giving best target AUROC improvement. Probes trained on source projections; subset choice uses labeled target examples. 5-fold CV over target: select PCs on non-held-out target folds, evaluate source-trained probe on held-out target fold. Stop if no candidate improves AUROC >0.001. Average selected subset sizes: 15 Report, 8 Confirm, 14 Sandbagging. Greedy is upper bound, not unbiased OOD. Improves over full baseline by 0.22 AUROC on Report and 0.23 Sandbagging, close to target-trained probes. Variance control matches greedy only Confirm, poor Report/Sandbagging.

Sec 4.3/Fig 4: source-weighted and target-separating PC rankings fail. Standardized coefficient = absolute probe coefficient × SD of PC. Evaluate source-trained probes on top k PCs, k from greedy full target dataset: k=13 Report, 7 Confirm, 14 Sandbagging. Source-PCA probe about full baseline. Target-PCA probe good Report but worse than greedy Confirm and below random Sandbagging. Subset cannot be found by source-side or target-side separability alone.

Sec 4.4: LLM interprets each top-100 source PC from 8 most/least activating source examples and rates OOD generalizability 1–10. No PC >6; max observed treated as 6. Run twice; PCs scoring max both times retained: 19 PCs. Of 5 PCs in greedy selections for >1 target, 3/5 got max OOD score; only 1 of top 5 source-PCA-selected PCs got max.

Appendix B LLM Judge Prompt: uses GPT-5-mini. Prompt says PC direction is bipolar; positive/negative activations are opposite poles and magnitude indicates stronger match. Examples from Roleplaying source setup. Potential inconsistency: prompt says lines are formatted as “token<TAB>activation” although methods use example-level activations averaged over assistant response tokens and Sec 4.4 describes most/least activating examples.

Sec 4.5/Fig 5: 19 interp-selected PCs. Source-trained probe in this subspace compared with full baseline, top-19 variance PCs, and complement/ablation remaining 81 PCs. Confirm baseline 0.874 near ceiling/uninformative. Sandbagging: 0.606→0.662, closes 25% gap to greedy 0.832. Earlier inconsistency: Sec 4.5 reportedly says selection “causally reduces the model’s deceptive behavior,” but methods/results only improve probe detection/generalization.

Sec 5 limitations: narrow claims. Single model/source; Confirm uninformative due baseline 0.874; Sandbagging margins small; Report more robust. Linear pipeline only. No causal validation: PC encoding claims descriptive, not causal; high-scoring PCs not ablated during model inference. Conflicts with any earlier causal-reduction wording.

Sec 6 conclusion: repeats small source-PC subsets enable cross-domain transfer nearly matching target-trained probes; source/target separability alone cannot find them; LLM judge with no target data partially recovers subspace.

Appendix C: Lower PCs show stronger decoder alignment to SAE features, Spearman ρ=-0.857 best feature and -0.917 mean top 10; SAE used andyrdt/saes-llama-3.1-8b-instruct.

Table greedy sets: Report 13 PCs; Confirm 7; Sandbagging 15, conflicting with earlier Sec 4.3 k=14 Sandbagging. Table source probe weights lists 15 PCs.

Appendix E: Table 3 caption says PCs “selected for likely transferability, based on interpretation with an LLM judge,” but lists five multi-target greedy PCs: PC62 score 6, PC57 score 6, PC9 score 3, PC81 score 3, PC86 score 6. This matches earlier statement that 3/5 repeatedly greedy-selected PCs got max score, but conflicts with caption if interpreted as LLM-selected transferable PCs because two score only 3 and are described as brittle/domain-specific. Table 4 gives some PC scores/explanations: PC7=3, PC8=4, PC11=3, PC12=3, PC4=6.
