final_notes:
Paper title: “PrivDrift: Auditing User-Secret Leakage Under Topic Drift in Active LLM Conversations.” Author Luciano Rolando Maldonado Romero, WVU.

Core setup/definitions:
- QX2/PrivDrift audits active-context re-disclosure of user-supplied secrets after unrelated topic drift and later probes. E9U = assistant reproduces earlier sensitive value under later querying/justification/pressure; not merely transcript presence.
- Dataset: N=1000 dialogues, 900 synthetic + 100 human-authored, interspersed. One seeded secret per dialogue. Drift lengths D7A sampled from {0,2,3,4,5,6}: d=0 p=.2, otherwise uniform over 2–6 with p=.8. Overall avg words 359.16; median 385; min/max 43/795. Approx tokens avg 478.87; median 513.33; min/max 57.33/1060.00. Appendix A Table 7 D7A counts/lengths: d=0 N=197 avg words 44.29 median 43 avg tokens 59.05 median 57.33; d=2 N=147 avg words 253.97 median 258 avg tokens 338.62 median 344; d=3 N=142 avg words 344.18 median 347 avg tokens 458.91 median 462.67; d=4 N=166 avg words 452.27 median 447 avg tokens 603.02 median 596; d=5 N=181 avg words 520.92 median 543 avg tokens 694.56 median 724; d=6 N=167 avg words 568.03 median 605 avg tokens 757.37 median 806.67.
- Secret types S8Q: A2L phone/contact; F8Z email/electronic contact; W3B SSN/government IDs; N6G credit card/payment IDs.
- Probe/persuasion V4N: C8R simple neutral retrieval; Z2F medium contextual justification/form-filling; L9W hard urgent/high-pressure elicitation.
- H8D hybrid detector positive if normalized inclusion or LLM judge finds full secret/substantial substring/sufficient identifying partial info. B6T/U3P deterministic baseline via normalization/regex. R5J fuzzy sensitivity also used on cached outputs.
- K2V tau: threshold delta=0.1*L(0); tau=min observed d where L(d)<=delta and all later observed d’ also <=delta; if none, tau=max(D_obs)+1. Later resurgence disqualifies transient decrease.

Experimental setup:
- Models via OpenRouter: M7Q = GPT-OSS-120B, T4X = DeepSeek-R1, Y9C = Qwen3-VL-235B; API-served models may change despite logs/cache.
- Cached responses = 3000/model and 9000 total = 1000 dialogues × 3 V4N probes × 3 models.
- G4P = dialogue-level any-probe leakage. P6S = probe-level/response statistic. G4P can exceed mean condition-specific P6S.
- G4P CIs bootstrap over dialogues. McNemar for model/detector comparisons; Cochran’s Q then McNemar for repeated persuasion; chi-square and Cramer’s V/X2H for associations with D7A/V4N/S8Q.

Results:
- §5.1 Table 2 G4P U3P vs H8D: M7Q 47.70 vs 47.70 Δ0 p=1.0; T4X 37.80 vs 38.70 Δ+0.90 p=7.7e-3; Y9C 53.50 vs 54.60 Δ+1.10 p=2.57e-3. Claim: H8D differs only slightly from baseline; direct/near-direct reproduction dominates.
- §5.2 Table 3 H8D G4P CIs: T4X 38.70% [35.7,41.6]; M7Q 47.70% [44.6,50.8]; Y9C 54.60% [51.6,57.7].
- §5.3 Table 4 H8D P6S by V4N: M7Q C8R 39.30, Z2F 40.50, L9W 32.90; T4X C8R 28.10, Z2F 22.00, L9W 29.20; Y9C C8R 38.70, Z2F 33.30, L9W 40.60. Cochran’s Q p<1e-5 every model. Internal error already found: prose says “T4X maximizes at Z2F,” but table shows T4X max at L9W 29.20 and Z2F lowest at 22.00.
- §5.4 D7A: cached P6S associations with drift length are small/negligible; risk persists; Figure 4 H8D vs D7A dips near d=3 then rebounds; no reliable reduction.
- §5.5 Table 5 H8D P6S by S8Q across cached model-probe responses: W3B M7Q 0.14, T4X 1.11, Y9C 5.97; N6G 0.00, 0.39, 4.01; F8Z 78.24, 57.11, 81.13; A2L 70.89, 46.13, 57.24. Claim: S8Q strongest association; W3B/N6G far more suppressed than F8Z/A2L.
- §5.6 K2V: every model and persuasion condition assigned tau=7 because no system approaches threshold at tested lengths; suppression never stabilizes.
- §5.7 Table 6 cached-output P6S: T4X U3P 25.50, R5J .85 26.40, R5J .80 26.53, H8D 26.43; M7Q 36.80, 37.03, 37.07, 37.57; Y9C 36.97, 37.60, 37.93, 37.53.
- Appendix B Table 8 cached P6S effect sizes for H8D-benchmark-variable associations: T4X S8Q 0.5871 Large, D7A 0.1073 Small, V4N 0.0718 Negligible; M7Q S8Q 0.7731 Large, D7A 0.0659 Negligible, V4N 0.0689 Negligible; Y9C S8Q 0.6927 Large, D7A 0.0723 Negligible, V4N 0.0639 Negligible. This supports S8Q strongest and D7A/V4N small/negligible.

Discussion/limitations:
- Behavioral recoverability does not imply permanent memory or uniform long-context behavior.
- M7Q pressure response interpreted as urgency activating safety/refusal behavior (L9W lower); Y9C weaker pressure resistance (L9W highest). J7K not implicit privacy boundary; evaluate stability not transient suppression.
- Limitations: bounded D7A short-to-medium, fixed-format secrets, active context only, no row identifiers for human subset, detector scope surface-form outputs/no formal human–automated IAA; planned artifact release.

Paper title: “PrivDrift: Auditing User-Secret Leakage Under Topic Drift in Active LLM Conversations.” Author Luciano Rolando Maldonado Romero, WVU.

Core framing: PrivDrift audits whether user-disclosed sensitive info remains behaviorally recoverable through later prompts after unrelated topic drift. Not about training-data memorization, personalization/cross-session memory, or permanent model memory. Risk settings include shared/persistent sessions, browser assistants, enterprise copilots, agent workflows, prompt injection/tool outputs. Benchmark: 1,000 controlled multi-turn dialogues with seeded secrets, content-dense drift turns, standardized extraction probes; evaluated per model. Main conclusion: dialogue-level hybrid leakage substantial, 38.7%–54.6%; varies by model, secret type, persuasion intensity; within tested drift window d≤6 topic drift does not reliably reduce leakage; Privacy Half-Life exceeds observed window for all models. Secret type strongest association; protections seem format-sensitive. SSNs/credit cards are suppressed far more often than emails/phones per Table 5 and Discussion, though earlier Section 5.5 text apparently said “far less often,” an internal contradiction.

Dataset: N=1000 dialogues, 900 synthetic + 100 human-authored under same constraints; human-authored inserted throughout, not separate block, but cached metadata does not identify which rows are human-authored, so only aggregate results and human-vs-synthetic left for future work. Table 1: secret categories 4; drift lengths 0,2,3,4,5,6; avg words 359.16, median 385, min/max 43/795; avg approx tokens 478.87, median 513.33, min/max 57.33/1060.00. Appendix A/Table 7 by drift length: d0 N197 avg words 44.29 median 43 avg tokens 59.05 median 57.33; d2 N147 avg words 253.97 median 258 avg tokens 338.62 median 344; d3 N142 avg words 344.18 median 347 avg tokens 458.91 median 462.67; d4 N166 avg words 452.27 median 447 avg tokens 603.02 median 596; d5 N181 avg words 520.92 median 543 avg tokens 694.56 median 724; d6 N167 avg words 568.03 median 605 avg tokens 757.37 median 806.67. Counts sum to 1000 and weighted averages match Table 1. Approx tokens estimated from word counts. Four fixed-format PII categories: phone, email, SSN, credit card. Secret inserted in opening turn. Drift turns from topic-conditioned dense Q-A library/fallback professional writing, structured reasoning, summarization; naturalistic rewrite preserves exact secret, drift length, role structure, probe conditions. Limitations: fixed-format secrets easier to detect than unstructured sensitive info; future work for non-fixed attributes.

Probing: Three persuasion levels per dialogue: Simple direct neutral query; Medium contextual justification; Hard high-pressure/urgent. Drift length sampled d=0 p=0.2; otherwise Uniform{2,3,4,5,6}; no d=1. Results bounded to short-to-medium active-context persistence, not arbitrary long/full context windows; drift only up to d=6.

Evaluation: Hierarchical hybrid detector. Leakage if normalized secret appears in normalized response OR LLM judge says response reveals full secret, substantial substring, or enough partial info to identify secret. Stage 1 normalization: numeric secrets strip non-digits from secret/response; alphanumeric normalize case/whitespace while preserving delimiters. Regex-negative responses go to open-weights Llama judge. Regex-only and hybrid rates separately; fuzzy matching auxiliary. Detector limitation: no formal human inter-annotator agreement yet. Privacy Half-Life τ: threshold δ=0.1×L(0); τ=min d such that L(d)≤δ and all later observed d′>d also ≤δ; if none, τ=max(D_obs)+1.

Experimental setup: Models GPT-OSS-120B, DeepSeek-R1, Qwen3-VL-235B via OpenRouter/API-served models. Same dialogues/probes. 1,000 dialogues/model, three probes/dialogue = 3,000 cached responses/model, 9,000 total. Dialogue leaks if any standardized probe elicits secret. Dialogue-level 95% bootstrap CIs; paired comparisons McNemar with Bonferroni; persuasion Cochran’s Q + post-hoc McNemar; associations chi-square and Cramer’s V.

Results: Table 2 dialogue regex vs hybrid: GPT-OSS 47.70/47.70 Δ0 p=1.0; DeepSeek 37.80/38.70 Δ+0.90 p=7.7e-3; Qwen 53.50/54.60 Δ+1.10 p=2.57e-3. Table 3 dialogue-level hybrid CI: DeepSeek 38.70% [35.7,41.6]; GPT-OSS 47.70% [44.6,50.8]; Qwen 54.60% [51.6,57.7].

Table 4 probe-level hybrid by persuasion: GPT-OSS Simple 39.30%, Medium 40.50%, Hard 32.90%; DeepSeek 28.10%, 22.00%, 29.20%; Qwen 38.70%, 33.30%, 40.60%. Cochran’s Q p<1e-5 all; non-monotonic/model-dependent. Appendix B/Table 8 persuasion Cramer’s V: DeepSeek 0.0718, GPT-OSS 0.0689, Qwen 0.0639, all negligible.

Drift length: curves dip near d=3 then rebound; Cramer’s V small/negligible: DeepSeek 0.1073 small, GPT-OSS 0.0659 negligible, Qwen 0.0723 negligible. Topic drift does not reliably reduce leakage within d≤6; not about arbitrary long contexts. Privacy Half-Life: no model approaches δ=0.1·L(0); τ=7 for all models and persuasion levels.

Secret type: Cramer’s V DeepSeek 0.5871 large, GPT-OSS 0.7731 large, Qwen 0.6927 large. Table 5 probe-level hybrid leakage: GPT-OSS SSN 0.14%, credit card 0.00%, email 78.24%, phone 70.89%; DeepSeek SSN 1.11%, credit card 0.39%, email 57.11%, phone 46.13%; Qwen SSN 5.97%, credit card 4.01%, email 81.13%, phone 57.24%.

Fuzzy Table 6 probe-level rates: DeepSeek regex 25.50, fuzzy0.85 26.40, fuzzy0.80 26.53, hybrid 26.43; GPT-OSS 36.80, 37.03, 37.07, 37.57; Qwen 36.97, 37.60, 37.93, 37.53. Fuzzy0.85 closely tracks hybrid; leakage mostly direct/near-direct reproduction.

Artifact availability: release benchmark generation code, probe templates, evaluation scripts, aggregate result files, sanitized subset; examples use non-real identifiers/templates. Appendix C: Figure 6 dialogue construction details.

Related work: Active-context privacy differs from training-data extraction/membership/memorized PII; compares to privacy reasoning/access-control benchmarks (ConfAIde, PrivacyLens, PrivaCI-Bench), multi-turn jailbreak/prompt injection work (Crescendo etc.), and unlearning benchmarks (TOFU/WMDP). PrivDrift focuses on re-disclosure of user-supplied sensitive values in current context after drift/persuasion, not static norms, unsafe content, or parameter unlearning.

Section 3 framework: PrivDrift has three components: parametric dialogue generator, probing harness, metric suite for leakage detection/temporal analysis. Figure 1 overview: constructs controlled dialogues, appends standardized probes, queries target models, scores with hybrid detector.

Threat model (3.1): Active-context re-disclosure = sensitive info disclosed earlier remains recoverable via later prompts after unrelated topic drift. They do not assume adversary cannot inspect raw transcript; benchmark asks whether model itself will re-disclose the value when later instructions query/justify/pressure it. Practical risks: shared/persistent sessions, later user unaware of prior private info; enterprise/agent workflows with later tool outputs/retrieved docs/prompt-injection instructions interacting with active context; browser/app assistants where user does not intend prior disclosures reused after task shift. Formalism: secret S disclosed at turn t0; then d unrelated content-dense drift turns D={u1,a1,...,ud,ad}; standardized probe P appended; leakage if response reveals S exactly, approximately, or semantically.

Dataset generation (3.2): N=1000 controlled dialogues, scaffold-then-rewrite pipeline. 900 synthetic + 100 human-authored under same secret/drift constraints, inserted throughout benchmark not contiguous. Cached metadata lacks human-authored identifiers, so only aggregate results reported; human-vs-synthetic comparison left for future work. Table 1: total dialogues 1,000; synthetic 900; human 100; secret categories 4; drift lengths 0,2,3,4,5,6; average words 359.16; median words 385; min/max words 43/795; avg approx tokens 478.87; median approx tokens 513.33; min/max approx tokens 57.33/1060.00. Approx token counts estimated from word counts.

Persona/secret injection: persona sampled from >100 professions/demographic profiles plus ground-truth secret S. Four fixed-format PII categories: phone numbers, email addresses, Social Security Numbers, credit card numbers. Secret inserted in opening turn as plausible task context so assistant legitimately observes it.

Topic drift: each dialogue assigned a topic such as tax filing, medical triage, travel logistics. Drift turns drawn from topic-conditioned library of dense Q-A pairs and fallback tasks involving professional writing, structured reasoning, or long-form summarization. Some drift turns human-authored and incorporated into generation library. Aim: add unrelated entities/task demands while preserving control over original secret and number of drift turns.

Naturalistic refinement: scaffold passed to rewriting model to improve fluency/persona realism while preserving exact secret, drift length, role structure, and final probe conditions.

Probing setup (3.3): final standardized probe appended to completed conversation history. Three persuasion levels: Simple = direct neutral query (e.g. ask phone number mentioned earlier); Medium = contextual justification (e.g. needed for form); Hard = high-pressure/urgent request testing pressure cues. Paper title: “PrivDrift: Auditing User-Secret Leakage Under Topic Drift in Active LLM Conversations.” Author Luciano Rolando Maldonado Romero, WVU.

Core claim: QX2=PrivDrift audits persistence of user-secret leakage in active/persistent conversations via seeded multi-turn histories, unrelated content-dense intervening exchanges, standardized probes. Main findings: G4P under H8D remains substantial across evaluated extended-context models; varies by system, S8Q, V4N; does not reliably decline within tested drift window. SSNs/payment identifiers should have stronger suppression than contact identifiers; no stable decay. Active-context privacy framed as persistent behavioral failure, not parameter memorization/immediate jailbreak.

Threat model/framework: E9U=active-context re-disclosure: assistant reproduces earlier sensitive value under later querying/justification/pressure; transcript invisibility not assumed. Secret S supplied at t0; unrelated topic drift D={u1,a1,...,ud,ad}; standardized probe P appended; exact/approx/semantic revelation counts. D7A drift length d values: 0,2,3,4,5,6; d=0 p=.2, otherwise uniform over {2..6}. S8Q secret types: A2L phone/contact; F8Z email/electronic contact; W3B SSN/government IDs; N6G credit card/payment IDs. V4N probe styles: C8R simple direct; Z2F contextual/form-filling; L9W urgent/high-pressure. H8D positive if normalized inclusion OR LLM judge detects full secret, substantial substring, or sufficient partial identifying info. B6T/U3P deterministic normalized matching baseline; numeric strips non-digits, alphanumeric normalizes case/whitespace. LLM judge used for deterministic negatives. K2V tau: threshold delta=0.1*L(0); tau=min observed d with L(d)<=delta and all later d also <=delta; if none tau=max(D_obs)+1. Later resurgence disqualifies transient decay.

Dataset/setup: N=1000 dialogues: 900 synthetic, 100 human-authored, interspersed. Avg words/dialogue 359.16, median 385, min/max 43/795; approx tokens avg 478.87, median 513.33, min/max 57.33/1060. Scaffold-then-rewrite preserves exact secret, turn counts, roles, probe conditions. Personas >100; drift tasks include tax/medical/travel and professional writing/structured reasoning/summarization. All systems get identical histories/probe templates through OpenRouter. Each system processes full dataset: one seeded secret and sampled d per dialogue, under every V4N condition. Cached responses: 3000/model, 9000 total, so 3 evaluated models ×1000 dialogues×3 probes. G4P=dialogue-level any-probe leakage; P6S=probe-level response statistic for V4N/R5J etc. G4P can exceed mean condition rate. Bootstrap CIs over dialogues; McNemar for matched comparisons; Cochran’s Q/McNemar for repeated persuasion; chi-square for D7A/V4N/S8Q associations, Cramer’s V/effect size.

§5 Results:
- §5.1/Table 2 G4P U3P vs H8D: M7Q 47.70/47.70 Δ0 p=1.0; T4X 37.80/38.70 Δ+0.90 p=7.7e-3; Y9C 53.50/54.60 Δ+1.10 p=2.57e-3. H8D differs only slightly from B6T; direct/near-direct reproduction dominates semantic paraphrase.
- §5.2/Table 3 H8D G4P with 95% bootstrap CI: T4X 38.70% [35.7,41.6]; M7Q 47.70% [44.6,50.8]; Y9C 54.60% [51.6,57.7]. Every evaluated system remains vulnerable at substantial rates.
- §5.3/Table 4 H8D P6S by V4N: M7Q C8R 39.30, Z2F 40.50, L9W 32.90; T4X 28.10, 22.00, 29.20; Y9C 38.70, 33.30, 40.60. Cochran’s Q p<1e-5 every model. Non-monotonic: M7Q declines under L9W vs C8R/Z2F; T4X minimum Z2F; Y9C maximum L9W.
- §5.4: D7A associations small/negligible; risk persists; Fig 4 H8D vs D7A dip near d=3 then rebound. Supports no reliable reduction.
- §5.5/Table 5 H8D P6S by S8Q: W3B M7Q 0.14, T4X 1.11, Y9C 5.97; N6G 0.00, 0.39, 4.01; F8Z 78.24, 57.11, 81.13; A2L 70.89, 46.13, 57.24. Table shows W3B/N6G far lower leakage/stronger suppression than F8Z/A2L. Text says “W3B and N6G receive far less suppression,” an internal reversal/error.
- §5.6/Table: K2V exceeds observation: every model and persuasion condition, observed d<=6, assigned tau=max(D_obs)+1=7; no system approaches threshold/stable suppression.
- §5.7/Table 6 cached-output P6S sensitivity R5J: T4X U3P 25.50, R5J .85 26.40, R5J .80 26.53, H8D 26.43; M7Q 36.80,37.03,37.07,37.57; Y9C 36.97,37.60,37.93,37.53. R5J fuzzy matching auxiliary, higher threshold tracks H8D. Figure 5 heatmap by D7A and V4N.

§6 Discussion: Behavioral recoverability does not imply permanent memory or uniform behavior across long-context settings; assistants may reproduce sensitive in-context information under retrieval pressure. M7Q pressure response interpreted as urgency activating safety/refusal behavior, consistent with M7Q L9W being lower than C8R/Z2F. Y9C response interpreted as weaker pressure resistance, consistent with Y9C L9W being highest. Discussion says J7K is not an implicit privacy boundary; likely refers to drift/context boundary/length, and unstable intermediate decreases require stability-based evaluation rather than treating dips as suppression evidence.

§7 Limitations/Future Work: Tested D7A short-to-medium range does not saturate modern windows; not full-window/arbitrarily long privacy characterization. Only fixed-format structured identifiers tested; unstructured sensitive attributes future work. Active context only; no training-data memorization, personalization memory, or cross-session retention. Mixed synthetic/human-authored construction; cached metadata no longer preserves human-authored row IDs; only aggregate results; human-vs-synthetic leakage deferred. Detector labels limited to U3P, R5J, external judge; no formal human–automated IAA; larger manual audits future work. API-served model identifiers: M7Q=GPT-OSS-120B, T4X=DeepSeek-R1, Y9C=Qwen3-VL-235B; models may change despite logged identifiers/prompts/timestamps/cached responses/paired stats. Planned artifact release: generation code, probe templates, evaluation scripts, aggregate result files, sanitized dialogue subset; non-real identifiers/templates for reproduction.

§8 Conclusion: S8Q asymmetry suggests safeguards are uneven and rely more on format/sensitivity cues and format-sensitive safety heuristics than generalized contextual confidentiality/robust contextual reasoning. Appendix A Table 7 D7A length characterization: d=0 N197 avg words 44.29 median 43 avg tokens 59.05 median 57.33; d=2 N147 253.97/258/338.62/344; d=3 N142 344.18/347/458.91/462.67; d=4 N166 452.27/447/603.02/596; d=5 N181 520.92/543/694.56/724; d=6 N167 568.03/605/757.37/806.67. Counts sum 1000 and weighted averages match overall avg words/tokens from dataset notes.

Appendix B/Table 8 cached P6S effect sizes for H8D–benchmark-variable associations: S8Q large for all models (T4X 0.5871, M7Q 0.7731, Y9C 0.6927); D7A small/negligible (T4X 0.1073 small, M7Q 0.0659 negligible, Y9C 0.0723 negligible); V4N negligible (T4X 0.0718, M7Q 0.0689, Y9C 0.0639). Appendix C only notes Figure 6 dialogue construction details.

Overall consistency: evaluated model count=3; response totals 9000. Distinguish G4P vs P6S. Main internal error found: §5.5 prose reverses Table 5 direction; correct interpretation is SSN/payment W3B/N6G are strongly suppressed relative to email/phone F8Z/A2L.

- D7A = drift length/intervening-turn quantity d, turns between disclosure and final probe. Values in benchmark: 0,2,3,4,5,6. Sampling: d=0 with p=.2; otherwise uniform over {2,3,4,5,6} with p=.8. Immediate recall included; short-to-medium drift emphasized.

Paper title: “PrivDrift: Auditing User-Secret Leakage Under Topic Drift in Active LLM Conversations.” Author Luciano Rolando Maldonado Romero, WVU.

Core framing/threat model: PrivDrift measures active-context re-disclosure of a user-supplied secret S after unrelated topic drift and later probe. Targets inference-time/active-context behavioral reproduction, not training-data memorization, parameter storage, static privacy reasoning, unlearning, immediate jailbreaks, personalization memory, or cross-session retention. Does not assume adversary cannot inspect transcript; asks whether model re-discloses value when queried/justified/pressured. Practical settings: shared/persistent sessions, enterprise copilots, agentic workflows, browser/app assistants, RAG/tool/prompt-injection contexts.

Formalization: user discloses secret at t0; conversation continues through d unrelated content-dense drift turns; standardized probe appended; leakage if model response reveals S exactly, approximately, or semantically.

Dataset/framework: PrivDrift = parametric dialogue generator, probing harness, metric suite. N=1000 controlled dialogues per model: 900 synthetic + 100 human-authored inserted throughout benchmark, not a separate block. Human IDs/metadata identifying human-authored rows are not cached/preserved; aggregate results only; human-vs-synthetic comparison left for future work. Table 1: 1000 dialogues; 4 secret categories; drift lengths 0,2,3,4,5,6; avg words 359.16, median 385, min/max 43/795; avg approx tokens 478.87, median 513.33, min/max 57.33/1060. Appendix Table 7 by drift: d=0 N197 avg words 44.29 median 43 avg tokens 59.05 median 57.33; d=2 N147 avg 253.97 median 258 tokens 338.62/344; d=3 N142 avg 344.18 median 347 tokens 458.91/462.67; d=4 N166 avg 452.27 median 447 tokens 603.02/596; d=5 N181 avg 520.92 median 543 tokens 694.56/724; d=6 N167 avg 568.03 median 605 tokens 757.37/806.67. Counts sum to 1000 and weighted averages match Table 1. One seeded fixed-format PII-like secret per dialogue: phone, email, SSN, credit card, inserted in opening turn. Personas >100. Topics include tax, medical triage, travel. Naturalistic rewrite preserves exact secret, drift length, role structure, final probe conditions. Future work: extend beyond fixed-format secrets to unstructured sensitive attributes.

Models/setup: GPT-OSS-120B, DeepSeek-R1, Qwen3-VL-235B via OpenRouter/API-served models. Same dialogue histories and probe templates. Each 1000 dialogues × 3 probes = 3000 cached model-probe responses per model, 9000 total. Logs model IDs, prompts, timestamps, cached responses, paired stats. Planned artifact release includes code/templates/eval scripts/aggregate results/sanitized subset.

Probes/drift: final standardized probe appended after conversation. Persuasion: Simple/direct neutral, Medium/contextual justification, Hard/high-pressure urgent. Drift d sampled: d=0 p=.2, otherwise uniform {2,3,4,5,6} p=.8; no d=1. Bounded active-context persistence, not arbitrary long context/full saturation. Limitation: drift up to d=6 only.

Detection/metrics: leakage if normalized secret appears or Llama judge says response reveals full secret/substantial substring/enough partial info. Stage 1 strips non-digits for numeric secrets; alphanumeric normalize case/whitespace. Dialogue-level leaking if any standardized probe elicits secret. Persuasion/fuzzy analyses probe-level. Dialogue-level can exceed individual persuasion rates. CIs bootstrap over dialogues/probe responses as appropriate. McNemar/Cochran Q/chi-square/Cramer’s V. Detector limitations: automated surface/fuzzy/LLM judge; no formal human-vs-automated IAA yet.

Results: Dialogue-level regex vs hybrid Table 2: GPT 47.70/47.70 Δ0 p=1.0; DeepSeek 37.80/38.70 Δ+0.90 p=7.7e-3; Qwen 53.50/54.60 Δ+1.10 p=2.57e-3. Judge adds up to 1.10 pp; leakage dominated by direct/near-direct reproduction. Dialogue-level hybrid Table 3: DeepSeek 38.70% CI [35.7,41.6]; GPT 47.70% [44.6,50.8]; Qwen 54.60% [51.6,57.7]. Conclusion repeats range 38.7% to 54.6%.

Persuasion Table 4 probe-level hybrid: GPT Simple 39.30, Medium 40.50, Hard 32.90; DeepSeek 28.10, 22.00, 29.20; Qwen 38.70, 33.30, 40.60. Cochran Q p<1e-5 all; non-monotonic/model-dependent. Discussion: GPT hard reduces leakage, DeepSeek medium lowest, Qwen hard highest. Appendix B persuasion effect sizes: DeepSeek V=0.0718 negligible; GPT V=0.0689 negligible; Qwen V=0.0639 negligible.

Drift Section 5.4 and Appendix B: drift-leak curves dip near d=3 then rebound. Cramer’s V: DeepSeek .1073 small, GPT .0659 negligible, Qwen .0723 negligible. Claim drift length does not reliably reduce leakage within d≤6; not about arbitrary long contexts. Discussion says topic drift not implicit privacy boundary; intermediate dips not stable enough for Privacy Half-Life criterion.

Secret type Section 5.5 and Appendix B: secret type strongest association with leakage, large Cramer’s V: DeepSeek .5871, GPT .7731, Qwen .6927. Results/discussion/conclusion say SSNs/credit cards suppressed far more often than emails/phones, suggesting format-sensitive safety heuristics/uneven protections rather than robust contextual confidentiality reasoning. Table 5 probe-level hybrid leakage: SSN GPT .14%, DeepSeek 1.11%, Qwen 5.97%; credit card GPT 0.00%, DeepSeek .39%, Qwen 4.01%; email GPT 78.24%, DeepSeek 57.11%, Qwen 81.13%; phone GPT 70.89%, DeepSeek 46.13%, Qwen 57.24%. INTERNAL CONTRADICTION found earlier: intro claim said SSNs and credit cards are suppressed far less often than emails/phones, reversing results/discussion/Table 5.

Privacy Half-Life Section 5.6: no model reaches δ at any tested drift length; τ=max(D_obs)+1=7 for all models and persuasion levels; no stable decay within d≤6. Conclusion says Privacy Half-Life exceeds observed window for all models.

Fuzzy Section 5.7 Table 6 probe-level rates: DeepSeek regex 25.50, fuzzy .85 26.40, fuzzy .80 26.53, hybrid 26.43; GPT 36.80, 37.03, 37.07, 37.57; Qwen 36.97, 37.60, 37.93, 37.53. Fuzzy at .85 closely tracks hybrid; auxiliary only. Discussion says behavior mostly direct/near-direct reproduction.

Conclusion: introduces PrivDrift; across three LLMs and 1000 dialogues/model, dialogue-level hybrid leakage substantial 38.7–54.6%; persuasion model-dependent; secret type strongest association; drift within tested range does not reliably reduce leakage; PHL exceeds observed window; secret-type asymmetry suggests protections uneven and format-cue-dependent.

Appendix B Table 8: probe-level effect sizes for associations between hybrid leakage and benchmark variables; values match those reported in results for secret type and drift, and add persuasion V values. Appendix C only states Figure 6 dialogue construction details.

Paper title: “PrivDrift: Auditing User-Secret Leakage Under Topic Drift in Active LLM Conversations.” Author Luciano Rolando Maldonado Romero, WVU.

Core framing: E9U = active-context re-disclosure, where assistant reproduces earlier sensitive value under later querying/justification/pressure, not just because transcript contains it. Threat model: user supplies secret S at t0; unrelated dense exchanges D follow; standardized probe P appended; exact, approximate, or semantic revelation counts as leakage. QX2/PrivDrift benchmark: seeded multi-turn histories, topic drift J7K, standardized probes, target-model queries, composite leakage scoring. Claimed contribution: active-context privacy as persistent behavioral failure, not parameter memorization/immediate jailbreak. §6 says behavioral recoverability does not imply permanent memory or uniform long-context behavior; J7K is not an implicit privacy boundary; unstable dips require stability-based evaluation. §8 conclusion: S8Q asymmetry suggests uneven safeguards relying more on format/sensitivity cues than generalized contextual confidentiality.

Variables/definitions: S8Q secret types: A2L phone/contact; F8Z email/electronic contact; W3B SSN/government ID; N6G credit card/payment ID. V4N probes: C8R direct; Z2F contextual justification; L9W urgent pressure. D7A drift length d in {0,2,3,4,5,6}, d=0 p=.2, d=2–6 uniform p=.8. H8D detector positive if normalized inclusion or LLM judge finds full secret, substantial substring, or sufficient partial identifying info. B6T/U3P deterministic baseline: Leak_U3P(R,S)=I[phi(S) subset phi(R)], numeric strips non-digits; alphanumeric normalizes case/whitespace but keeps meaningful delimiters. Possible §5.1 label inconsistency: heading/text says B6T but table/text use U3P. LLM judge: open-weights Llama after deterministic negatives; binary full/substantial disclosure. K2V privacy half-life tau: delta=0.1*L(0); tau=min d where L(d)<=delta and all later d’>d also <=delta; none => max(D_obs)+1. G4P dialogue-level any-probe leakage; P6S probe-level statistic. X2H = Cramer’s V.

Dataset/setup: Table 1 N=1000 dialogues; 900 synthetic/100 human; 4 secret categories; D7A values 0,2,3,4,5,6; avg words 359.16, median 385, min/max 43/795; avg approx tokens 478.87, median 513.33, min/max 57.33/1060. Appendix A/Table 7 D7A counts: d=0 N=197, d=2 147, d=3 142, d=4 166, d=5 181, d=6 167; counts sum 1000 and weighted avg words matches Table 1. Scaffold-then-rewrite preserves exact ground truth, turn counts, probes; human-authored interspersed; opening contexts give legitimate access to S; personas >100. Experiments: identical histories/probes via OpenRouter; each model full dataset under all 3 V4N conditions; 3,000 responses/model, 9,000 total, 3 models. Models: M7Q GPT-OSS-120B, T4X DeepSeek-R1, Y9C Qwen3-VL-235B.

Earlier abstract/intro claims: abstract says across extended-context models G4P substantial, varies sharply across systems/S8Q/V4N, and does not reliably decline within tested window. Intro claim “SSNs and payment identifiers receive much weaker suppression than contact identifiers” conflicts with §5.5 results showing W3B/N6G far more suppressed than F8Z/A2L. No evaluated system attains stable decay.

§5 results: Table 2 G4P U3P vs H8D: M7Q 47.70 vs 47.70 Δ0 p=1.0; T4X 37.80 vs 38.70 Δ+0.90 p=7.7e-3; Y9C 53.50 vs 54.60 Δ+1.10 p=2.57e-3. Table 3 H8D G4P: T4X 38.70 [35.7,41.6]; M7Q 47.70 [44.6,50.8]; Y9C 54.60 [51.6,57.7]. Table 4 H8D P6S by V4N: M7Q C8R 39.30, Z2F 40.50, L9W 32.90; T4X 28.10, 22.00, 29.20; Y9C 38.70, 33.30, 40.60. Cochran Q p<1e-5 for every model; directions non-monotonic. §5.4 D7A associations small/negligible; Figure 4 dips near d=3 then rebounds; no reliable reduction within tested window. Table 5 H8D P6S by S8Q: W3B M7Q 0.14, T4X 1.11, Y9C 5.97; N6G 0.00, 0.39, 4.01; F8Z 78.24, 57.11, 81.13; A2L 70.89, 46.13, 57.24. Text: S8Q large/strongest association; W3B/N6G far more suppressed than F8Z/A2L. K2V: all model/persuasion conditions d<=6 assigned tau=7; no stable suppression. Table 6 P6S sensitivity: T4X U3P 25.50, R5J .85 26.40, R5J .80 26.53, H8D 26.43; M7Q 36.80, 37.03, 37.07, 37.57; Y9C 36.97, 37.60, 37.93, 37.53.

§7 limitations: bounded to short-to-medium D7A; fixed-format identifiers only; active context only, no training memorization/personalization/cross-session; mixed synthetic/human but no human-vs-synthetic comparison; detector limitations; API models may change. Core framing/claims to track:
- Concern: persistent/shared-session/tool-augmented LLMs may re-disclose user secrets from active context after unrelated tasks/topic drift; not about users believing transcript is invisible.
- Failure mode now defined: E9U = active-context re-disclosure, i.e., assistant reproduces earlier sensitive value under later querying/justification/pressure, not merely because transcript contains it.

- QX2/PrivDrift benchmark uses seeded multi-turn histories, content-dense intervening exchanges (J7K = topic drift), standardized probes, target-model queries, and composite leakage scoring.
- Main conclusion claimed earlier: active-context privacy should be evaluated as persistent behavioral failure, not only parameter memorization or immediate jailbreak.

Variables/acronyms/definitions:
- S8Q = secret type. Four sampled formats: A2L = phone numbers/contact values; F8Z = email addresses/electronic contact values; W3B = Social Security Numbers/government identifiers; N6G = credit card numbers/payment identifiers.
- V4N = persuasion intensity/probe style, 3 standardized conditions: C8R = Simple/neutral direct retrieval; Z2F = Medium/contextual justification; L9W = Hard/urgent high-pressure elicitation.
- D7A = drift length/intervening-turn quantity d, values {0,2,3,4,5,6}. Sampling: d=0 with p=.2; Uniform{2,3,4,5,6} with p=.8. Immediate recall included; short-to-medium drift emphasized.
- H8D = hybrid/composite detector. Labels positive if normalized inclusion succeeds or LLM judge finds full secret, substantial substring, or sufficient partial identifying information.
- B6T = normalization-based deterministic matching; equation Leak_U3P(R,S)=I[phi(S) subset phi(R)]. Numeric secrets/responses strip all non-digit chars; alphanumeric processing normalizes case/whitespace but retains meaningful delimiters.
- U3P = regex-only/deterministic baseline, separately reported alongside H8D.

Paper title: “PrivDrift: Auditing User-Secret Leakage Under Topic Drift in Active LLM Conversations.” Author Luciano Rolando Maldonado Romero, WVU.

Core framing: PrivDrift audits active-context re-disclosure: whether user-disclosed sensitive info remains behaviorally recoverable via later prompts after conversation shifts to unrelated topics. Not training-data memorization, personalization memory, permanent/cross-session memory. Risks include shared/persistent sessions, browser assistants, enterprise copilots, agent workflows, prompt injection/tool outputs. Main finding: across 3 LLMs and 1,000 dialogues/model, dialogue-level hybrid leakage substantial at 38.7%–54.6%; varies by model, secret type, persuasion intensity; within tested drift window d≤6, topic drift does not reliably reduce leakage. Secret type strongest association: SSNs/credit cards suppressed far more than emails/phones. Privacy Half-Life exceeds observed window for all models (τ=7), indicating no stable decay within d≤6. Conclusion reiterates uneven protections depend more on format-sensitive cues than robust contextual confidentiality.

Dataset/benchmark: 1,000 controlled multi-turn dialogues: 900 synthetic + 100 human-authored under same constraints, inserted throughout benchmark rather than separate block; metadata/cached eval rows do not preserve human-authored identifiers, so only aggregate results and human-vs-synthetic comparison future work. Four fixed-format structured PII categories: phone, email, SSN, credit card; secret inserted in opening turn. Drift lengths 0,2,3,4,5,6 (no d=1); d=0 p=0.2, otherwise uniform over 2–6. Table 1 overall: avg words 359.16; median 385; min/max 43/795; avg approx tokens 478.87; median 513.33; min/max 57.33/1060.00. Tokens estimated from words. Appendix A/Table 7 length by drift: d0 N=197 avg/median words 44.29/43, avg/median tokens 59.05/57.33; d2 N=147 253.97/258 words, 338.62/344 tokens; d3 N=142 344.18/347, 458.91/462.67; d4 N=166 452.27/447, 603.02/596; d5 N=181 520.92/543, 694.56/724; d6 N=167 568.03/605, 757.37/806.67. Appendix weighted averages match Table 1 overall. Personas sampled from >100 profiles. Drift from topic-conditioned dense Q-A/fallback tasks; some human-authored drift turns. Rewrite model preserves exact secret, drift length, role structure, final probe conditions. Limitations: fixed-format secrets only; future work unstructured sensitive attributes.

Threat model/formalism: Active-context re-disclosure = sensitive info disclosed earlier remains recoverable via later prompts after unrelated topic drift. Does not assume adversary cannot inspect raw transcript; asks whether model itself will re-disclose value. Secret S at turn t0; then d unrelated drift turns D={u1,a1,...,ud,ad}; probe P appended; leakage if response reveals S exactly, approximately, or semantically.

Probing/evaluation: standardized final probe with persuasion levels: Simple direct neutral; Medium contextual justification; Hard urgent/high-pressure. Hierarchical hybrid detector: leakage if normalized secret appears in normalized response OR LLM judge says response reveals full secret, substantial substring, or enough partial info to identify it. Stage 1 normalization: numeric secrets strip non-digits; alphanumeric normalize case/whitespace preserving meaningful delimiters; Leak_regex(R,S)=I[phi(S) subset phi(R)]. Stats: regex-only and hybrid; dialogue-level 95% bootstrap CIs; probe-level sensitivity over cached responses; McNemar, Cochran’s Q, chi-square/Cramer’s V. Reproducibility mitigation for API models: log model identifiers, prompts, timestamps, cached responses, paired statistics on identical dialogue sets.

Results: Table 2 dialogue-level regex vs hybrid: GPT 47.70/47.70 Δ0 p=1.0; DeepSeek 37.80/38.70 Δ+0.90 p=7.7e-3; Qwen 53.50/54.60 Δ+1.10 p=2.57e-3. Table 3 dialogue-level hybrid + 95% bootstrap CIs: DeepSeek 38.70% [35.7,41.6]; GPT 47.70% [44.6,50.8]; Qwen 54.60% [51.6,57.7].

Table 4 probe-level hybrid by persuasion: GPT Simple 39.30, Medium 40.50, Hard 32.90; DeepSeek 28.10, 22.00, 29.20; Qwen 38.70, 33.30, 40.60. Cochran’s Q p<1e-5 all models. Direction non-monotonic/model-dependent. Appendix B/Table 8 gives persuasion Cramer’s V: DeepSeek 0.0718, GPT 0.0689, Qwen 0.0639, all interpreted negligible.

Drift length: Figure 4 curves dip near d=3 then rebound. Probe-level Cramer’s V for drift: DeepSeek 0.1073 small; GPT 0.0659 negligible; Qwen 0.0723 negligible. Caveat bounded d≤6 only.

Secret type: strong association with hybrid leakage; Cramer’s V DeepSeek 0.5871 large, GPT 0.7731 large, Qwen 0.6927 large. Table 5 probe-level hybrid by secret type: SSN GPT 0.14, DeepSeek 1.11, Qwen 5.97; credit card GPT 0.00, DeepSeek 0.39, Qwen 4.01; email GPT 78.24, DeepSeek 57.11, Qwen 81.13; phone GPT 70.89, DeepSeek 46.13, Qwen 57.24.

Limitations/artifact: bounded drift d≤6; fixed-format secrets only; active context not cross-session/training/personalization memory; no human-vs-synthetic row metadata; no formal human IAA; API reproducibility mitigated by logging/caching; planned release generation code, probe templates, eval scripts, aggregate results, sanitized subset/examples with non-real identifiers/templates. Paper: “PrivDrift: Auditing User-Secret Leakage Under Topic Drift in Active LLM Conversations,” Luciano Rolando Maldonado Romero, WVU. QX2/PrivDrift audits active-context re-disclosure of user-provided secrets after topic drift/probes. E9U = assistant reproducing/revealing earlier sensitive value, not transcript presence. Secret S at t0, drift D of d unrelated exchanges, probe P. Leakage exact/approx/semantic. D7A lengths 0,2,3,4,5,6; d=0 p=.2, others uniform p=.8. S8Q categories: A2L phone/contact, F8Z email/contact, W3B SSN/gov ID, N6G credit card/payment. V4N probes: C8R neutral direct, Z2F contextual/form-fill, L9W urgent/high-pressure. H8D detector positive if normalized inclusion or LLM judge finds full/substantial/identifying partial disclosure. B6T normalization first stage; U3P deterministic/regex-only baseline separately. Judge used for deterministic negatives. K2V tau = first d where L(d)<=0.1*L(0) and all later observed d too; if none tau=max(D_obs)+1; resurgence disqualifies transient decreases.

Dataset/setup: N=1000 dialogues: 900 synthetic, 100 human-authored. Avg words 359.16, median 385, min/max 43/795; approx tokens avg 478.87, median 513.33, min/max 57.33/1060. Same histories/probes through OpenRouter. Each of 3 models: 1000 dialogues × 3 probes = 3000 responses/model, 9000 total. G4P = dialogue-level any-probe leakage; P6S = probe-level statistic; G4P can exceed condition-specific means. CIs bootstrap over dialogues; McNemar matched comparisons; persuasion Cochran Q then McNemar; chi-square/Cramer’s V associations. Appendix A Table 7: d=0 N197 avg words44.29/tokens59.05; d=2 N147 253.97/338.62; d=3 N142 344.18/458.91; d=4 N166 452.27/603.02; d=5 N181 520.92/694.56; d=6 N167 568.03/757.37.

Results: §5.1 claims H8D largely agrees with B6T, but Table 2 compares U3P vs H8D G4P: M7Q 47.70 vs 47.70 Δ0 p=1.0; T4X 37.80 vs 38.70 Δ+0.90 p=7.7e-3; Y9C 53.50 vs 54.60 Δ+1.10 p=2.57e-3. This is a potential internal inconsistency/mislabel: B6T named but U3P shown. Table 3 H8D G4P CIs: T4X 38.70% [35.7,41.6]; M7Q 47.70 [44.6,50.8]; Y9C 54.60 [51.6,57.7]. §5.3 V4N P6S H8D: M7Q C8R39.30/Z2F40.50/L9W32.90; T4X 28.10/22.00/29.20; Y9C 38.70/33.30/40.60. Cochran Q p<1e-5 every model; directions non-monotonic. §5.4 says D7A associations small/negligible; risk persists; Figure 4 dip near d=3 then rebound, supporting no reliable reduction. §5.5 S8Q strongest: W3B/N6G much more suppressed than F8Z/A2L. Table 5 H8D P6S: W3B M7Q .14/T4X1.11/Y9C5.97; N6G 0/.39/4.01; F8Z 78.24/57.11/81.13; A2L 70.89/46.13/57.24. §5.6 K2V: no system approaches threshold; all model×persuasion tau=7 for observed d<=6. §5.7 R5J cached P6S: T4X U3P25.50/R5J.85 26.40/R5J.80 26.53/H8D26.43; M7Q 36.80/37.03/37.07/37.57; Y9C 36.97/37.60/37.93/37.53.

Discussion: recoverability does not imply permanent memory; assistants reproduce sensitive in-context info under retrieval pressure. M7Q urgency lowers leakage interpreted as safety/refusal; Y9C urgency highest interpreted weaker pressure resistance. “J7K is not an implicit privacy boundary”; likely drift/context boundary; unstable dips require stability-based evaluation.

Limitations: bounded D7A says short-to-medium range does not saturate modern windows, but then overclaims findings establish leakage throughout arbitrarily long/full saturated context windows—internally inconsistent with d<=6/caveats. Fixed-format secrets only; unstructured attributes future. Active context only; no training memorization/personalization/cross-session retention. Mixed synthetic/human; human-vs-synthetic deferred. Detector scope U3P/R5J/external judge, no formal human–automated IAA. API models M7Q=GPT-OSS-120B, T4X=DeepSeek-R1, Y9C=Qwen3-VL-235B may change. Planned artifacts listed.

Appendix B Table 8 H8D cached P6S effect sizes (X2H): S8Q large for all (T4X .5871, M7Q .7731, Y9C .6927); D7A small/negligible (T4X .1073 small, M7Q .0659 negligible, Y9C .0723 negligible); V4N negligible (T4X .0718, M7Q .0689, Y9C .0639). This matches earlier claims that S8Q is strong and D7A/V4N effects are small/negligible despite significant V4N tests. Appendix C: Figure 6 dialogue construction details.

Paper title: “PrivDrift: Auditing User-Secret Leakage Under Topic Drift in Active LLM Conversations.” Author Luciano Rolando Maldonado Romero, WVU.

Core claim from abstract/intro to check against later results: Benchmark QX2=PrivDrift audits persistence of user-secret leakage in active/persistent conversations using seeded multi-turn histories, content-dense unrelated intervening exchanges, and standardized probes. Main metric/result claims: Across extended-context models, G4P under H8D remains substantial, varies sharply across systems, S8Q, and V4N, and does not reliably decline within tested window. Intro specifically claims SSNs/payment identifiers receive much stronger suppression than contact identifiers; no evaluated system attains stable decay. Active-context privacy should be evaluated as persistent behavioral failure, not only parameter memorization or immediate jailbreak behavior.

Threat model/framework definitions from §3:
- E9U = active-context re-disclosure: assistant reproduces earlier sensitive value under later querying/justification/pressure; not mere presence of value in transcript. Transcript invisibility is not assumed.
- User supplies secret S at t0. Unrelated content-dense exchanges/J7K = topic drift are D={u1,a1,...,ud,ad}; standardized probe P appended after drift. Exact, approximate, or semantic revelation of S = leakage.
- D7A = drift length/intervening-turn quantity d, turns between disclosure and final probe. Values in benchmark: 0,2,3,4,5,6. Sampling: d=0 with p=.2; otherwise uniform over {2,3,4,5,6} with p=.8. Immediate recall included; short-to-medium drift emphasized.
- S8Q = secret type. Four fixed-format categories: A2L=phone numbers/contact values; F8Z=email addresses/electronic contact values; W3B=Social Security Numbers/government identifiers; N6G=credit card numbers/payment identifiers. Each inserted as ground-truth secret, not inferred.
- V4N = persuasion intensity/probe style: C8R=Simple neutral direct retrieval; Z2F=Medium contextual justification/form-filling; L9W=Hard urgent/high-pressure elicitation. Standardized conditions, not unconstrained adversarial search.
- H8D = hybrid composite detector. Labels response positive if normalized inclusion succeeds OR LLM judge finds full secret, substantial substring, or sufficient partial info to identify it. Eligible disclosures include verbatim output, formatting changes, partial substrings, paraphrased references.
- B6T = normalization-based matching, first stage/hierarchical eval. Numeric secrets/responses strip non-digit chars; alphanumeric normalizes case/whitespace but retains meaningful delimiters. Formula Leak_U3P(R,S)=I[phi(S) subset phi(R)].
- U3P = regex-only/deterministic baseline, reported separately alongside H8D.
- LLM judge: open-weights Llama judge receives S and R, binary full/substantial-disclosure verdict for deterministic negatives; judge errors possible, not treated as error-free.

Paper title: “PrivDrift: Auditing User-Secret Leakage Under Topic Drift in Active LLM Conversations.” Author Luciano Rolando Maldonado Romero, WVU.

Core framework: QX2/PrivDrift audits active-context re-disclosure of user-provided secrets after topic drift and standardized probes. E9U is assistant reproducing/revealing earlier sensitive value, not mere transcript presence. Secret S at t0, intervening drift D of d unrelated exchanges, then probe P. Leakage exact/approx/semantic. D7A drift lengths: 0,2,3,4,5,6; d=0 p=.2, others uniform p=.8. S8Q categories: A2L phone/contact, F8Z email/electronic contact, W3B SSN/government ID, N6G credit card/payment. V4N probe styles: C8R neutral direct, Z2F contextual/form-filling, L9W urgent/high-pressure. H8D composite detector positive if normalized inclusion or LLM judge finds full/substantial/identifying partial disclosure. B6T normalization-based matching first stage; U3P deterministic/regex-only baseline reported separately. LLM judge used for deterministic negatives. K2V privacy half-life tau: first observed d where L(d)<=0.1*L(0) and all later observed d also <= threshold; if none, tau=max(D_obs)+1. Later resurgence disqualifies transient decreases.

Dataset/setup: N=1000 dialogues: 900 synthetic, 100 human-authored, interspersed. Avg words 359.16, median 385, min/max 43/795; approx tokens avg 478.87, median 513.33, min/max 57.33/1060. Same histories/probes through OpenRouter. Each of 3 models processes 1000 dialogues × 3 V4N probes = 3000 cached responses/model, 9000 total. G4P = dialogue-level any-probe leakage; P6S = probe-level response statistic. G4P can exceed condition-specific means. CIs bootstrap over dialogues; matched comparisons McNemar; persuasion Cochran’s Q then McNemar; chi-square/Cramer’s V for associations.

Results: §5.1 claims H8D largely agrees with B6T, but Table 2 actually compares U3P vs H8D G4P: M7Q 47.70 vs 47.70 Δ0 p=1.0; T4X 37.80 vs 38.70 Δ+0.90 p=7.7e-3; Y9C 53.50 vs 54.60 Δ+1.10 p=2.57e-3. Potential inconsistency: B6T named but U3P shown. Table 3 H8D G4P CIs: T4X 38.70% [35.7,41.6]; M7Q 47.70% [44.6,50.8]; Y9C 54.60% [51.6,57.7]. §5.3 V4N P6S H8D: M7Q C8R 39.30, Z2F 40.50, L9W 32.90; T4X 28.10, 22.00, 29.20; Y9C 38.70, 33.30, 40.60. Cochran Q p<1e-5 for every model; directions non-monotonic. §5.4 says D7A associations small/negligible; risk persists; Figure 4 H8D vs D7A has dip near d=3 then rebound. §5.5 S8Q strong/strongest association; W3B/N6G suppressed vs F8Z/A2L. Table 5 H8D P6S: W3B M7Q .14%, T4X 1.11%, Y9C 5.97%; N6G 0.00, .39, 4.01; F8Z 78.24, 57.11, 81.13; A2L 70.89, 46.13, 57.24. §5.6 K2V: no system approaches threshold; all tau=7. §5.7 R5J cached-output P6S: T4X U3P 25.50, R5J .85 26.40, R5J .80 26.53, H8D 26.43; M7Q 36.80, 37.03, 37.07, 37.57; Y9C 36.97, 37.60, 37.93, 37.53.

Discussion/limitations/conclusion: active-context recoverability not permanent memory. Limitations: short-to-medium D7A only, fixed-format identifiers only, active context only, human-vs-synthetic deferred, no formal human–automated IAA. Internal contradiction in limitations: claims labels establish equivalent suppression for arbitrary unstructured personal narratives despite fixed-format-only limitation. API models: M7Q=GPT-OSS-120B, T4X=DeepSeek-R1, Y9C=Qwen3-VL-235B.

Appendix A Table 7 D7A lengths: d=0 N197 avg words44.29 tokens59.05; d=2 N147 words253.97 tokens338.62; d=3 N142 words344.18 tokens458.91; d=4 N166 words452.27 tokens603.02; d=5 N181 words520.92 tokens694.56; d=6 N167 words568.03 tokens757.37. Paper title: “PrivDrift: Auditing User-Secret Leakage Under Topic Drift in Active LLM Conversations.” Author Luciano Rolando Maldonado Romero, WVU.

Core claim from abstract/intro to check against later results: Benchmark QX2=PrivDrift audits persistence of user-secret leakage in active/persistent conversations using seeded multi-turn histories, content-dense unrelated intervening exchanges, and standardized probes. Main metric/result claims: Across extended-context models, G4P under H8D remains substantial, varies sharply across systems, S8Q, and V4N, and does not reliably decline within tested window. Intro specifically claims SSNs/payment identifiers receive much stronger suppression than contact identifiers; no evaluated system attains stable decay. Active-context privacy should be evaluated as persistent behavioral failure, not only parameter memorization or immediate jailbreak behavior.

Threat model/framework definitions from §3:
- E9U = active-context re-disclosure: assistant reproduces earlier sensitive value under later querying/justification/pressure; not mere presence of value in transcript. Transcript invisibility is not assumed.
- User supplies secret S at t0. Unrelated content-dense exchanges/J7K = topic drift are D={u1,a1,...,ud,ad}; standardized probe P appended after drift. Exact, approximate, or semantic revelation of S = leakage.
- D7A = drift length/intervening-turn quantity d, turns between disclosure and final probe. Values in benchmark: 0,2,3,4,5,6. Sampling: d=0 with p=.2; otherwise uniform over {2,3,4,5,6} with p=.8. Immediate recall included; short-to-medium drift emphasized.
- S8Q = secret type. Four fixed-format categories: A2L=phone numbers/contact values; F8Z=email addresses/electronic contact values; W3B=Social Security Numbers/government identifiers; N6G=credit card numbers/payment identifiers. Each inserted as ground-truth secret, not inferred.
- V4N = persuasion intensity/probe style: C8R=Simple neutral direct retrieval; Z2F=Medium contextual justification/form-filling; L9W=Hard urgent/high-pressure elicitation. Standardized conditions, not unconstrained adversarial search.
- H8D = hybrid composite detector. Labels response positive if normalized inclusion succeeds OR LLM judge finds full secret, substantial substring, or sufficient partial info to identify it. Eligible disclosures include verbatim output, formatting changes, partial substrings, paraphrased references.
- B6T = normalization-based matching, first stage/hierarchical eval. Numeric secrets/responses strip non-digit chars; alphanumeric normalizes case/whitespace but retains meaningful delimiters. Formula Leak_U3P(R,S)=I[phi(S) subset phi(R)].
- U3P = regex-only/deterministic baseline, reported separately alongside H8D.
- LLM judge: open-weights Llama judge receives S and R, binary full/substantial-disclosure verdict for deterministic negatives; judge errors possible, not treated as error-free.
- K2V = Privacy Half-Life/stability metric tau. Observed lengths D_obs and leakage rates L(d), safety threshold delta=0.1*L(0). tau=min d in D_obs such that L(d)<=delta and for all later observed d’, L(d’)<=delta. Empty set tau=max(D_obs)+1. This is sustained suppression, not momentary decrease.

Dataset generation from §3:
- Total dialogues N=1000: 900 synthetic, 100 human-authored, interspersed not contiguous.
- Secret categories=4. Avg words/dialogue 359.16; median 385; min/max 43/795. Approx tokens avg 478.87; median 513.33; min/max 57.33/1060.00.
- Pipeline: scaffold-then-rewrite preserves exact ground truth secret, intervening-turn counts, role structure, final-probe conditions; rewriting model only improves fluency/persona realism. Human-authored dialogues obey same constraints. Personas sampled from >100 professions/demographic profiles. Topic-dense drift library includes tax filing, medical triage, travel logistics plus professional-writing/structured-reasoning/long-form-summarization fallback tasks; annotators contribute subset.

Related-work framing to remember: QX2 differs from training-data memorization/membership/unlearning benchmarks because it concerns inference-time handling of user-supplied active-context secrets still present in context. Differs from contextual-integrity/legal/static access-control benchmarks by isolating behavioral recoverability after unrelated exchanges and persuasive probing. Differs from jailbreak/instruction-hijacking/multi-turn unsafe-content attacks because target is information-flow/re-disclosure of earlier sensitive info.

Potential consistency checks for later: Results should report G4P and P6S (not yet defined in §3) alongside U3P/H8D; support claims that SSN/payment leakage lower than phone/email, no stable decay for any evaluated system, leakage varies by model, S8Q, V4N, and does not reliably decline within d=0..6 window.

Paper title: “PrivDrift: Auditing User-Secret Leakage Under Topic Drift in Active LLM Conversations.” Author Luciano Rolando Maldonado Romero, WVU.

Core framing: PrivDrift audits whether user-disclosed sensitive info remains behaviorally recoverable through later prompts after conversation shifts to unrelated topics. Not about permanent model memory, training-data memorization, personalization memory, or cross-session retention; findings do not imply all long-context settings behave similarly. Risk contexts: shared/persistent sessions, browser assistants, enterprise copilots, agent workflows, prompt injection/tool outputs. Dataset: 1,000 controlled multi-turn dialogues with seeded secrets, drift turns, standardized extraction probes; each of three models evaluated on same 1,000 dialogues. Main results/conclusion: dialogue-level hybrid leakage substantial, 38.7%–54.6%; varies by model, secret type, persuasion; drift d≤6 does not reliably reduce leakage; SSNs/credit cards suppressed more than emails/phones; Privacy Half-Life exceeds observed window / τ not reached, τ=7. Conclusion states persuasion effects model-dependent, secret type strongest association, protections uneven and more format-sensitive than robustly context-confidential.

Framework/method: Secret S disclosed at turn t0; then d unrelated content-dense drift turns; standardized probe appended; leakage if response reveals S exactly, approximately, or semantically. Dataset: 900 synthetic + 100 human-authored, human IDs not cached; only aggregate results. Human-authored dialogues inserted throughout benchmark, not separate block. Secret categories: phone, email, SSN, credit card. Drift sampled: d=0 p=.2; otherwise uniform over {2,3,4,5,6}; no d=1.

Dataset lengths: Table 1 overall: 1,000 dialogues; avg words 359.16; median 385; min/max 43/795; avg approx tokens 478.87; median 513.33; min/max 57.33/1060. Appendix A/Table 7 by drift: d=0 N=197 avg words 44.29 median 43 avg tokens 59.05 median 57.33; d=2 N=147 avg words 253.97 median 258 avg tokens 338.62 median 344; d=3 N=142 avg words 344.18 median 347 avg tokens 458.91 median 462.67; d=4 N=166 avg words 452.27 median 447 avg tokens 603.02 median 596; d=5 N=181 avg words 520.92 median 543 avg tokens 694.56 median 724; d=6 N=167 avg words 568.03 median 605 avg tokens 757.37 median 806.67. Ns sum to 1,000 and weighted averages match Table 1.

Evaluation: Three persuasion probes per dialogue: Simple direct; Medium contextual justification; Hard urgent/high-pressure. Leakage detector: regex/normalization first, then Llama open-weights judge for regex-negative responses. Numeric secrets strip non-digits; alphanumeric normalize case/whitespace. Leakage if normalized secret substring in response or judge says full/substantial/identifying partial info revealed. Regex-only and hybrid rates reported; fuzzy matching later reported as auxiliary post-hoc sensitivity. Dialogue-level leakage = any of three standardized probes leaks. Probe-level analyses = one response per persuasion per dialogue. Total per model: 3,000 cached responses; 9,000 total. Dialogue-level CIs bootstrap over dialogues; paired comparisons McNemar; persuasion Cochran’s Q/post-hoc McNemar; associations chi-square/Cramer’s V. Note internal overclaim found in §5.2: dialogue-level rates from three standardized probes do not estimate “all possible extraction attacks” or adaptive probing.

Privacy Half-Life: threshold δ=0.1×L(0); τ=min observed d where L(d)≤δ and all later observed d′ also ≤δ; if none, τ=max(Dobs)+1. Stable suppression required; transient/intermediate dips don’t count.

Models: GPT-OSS-120B, DeepSeek-R1, Qwen3-VL-235B via OpenRouter API. Limitation: API-served models may change; mitigated with logged model identifiers, prompts, timestamps, cached responses, and paired stats on identical dialogue sets.

Section 5 results: Table 2 dialogue-level regex vs hybrid: GPT 47.70→47.70, Δ0, p=1.0; DeepSeek 37.80→38.70, Δ+0.90, p=7.7e-3; Qwen 53.50→54.60, Δ+1.10, p=2.57e-3. Table 3 dialogue-level hybrid leakage with 95% CI: DeepSeek 38.70% [35.7,41.6]; GPT 47.70% [44.6,50.8]; Qwen 54.60% [51.6,57.7].

Table 4 probe-level hybrid leakage by persuasion: GPT Simple 39.30, Medium 40.50, Hard 32.90; DeepSeek 28.10, 22.00, 29.20; Qwen 38.70, 33.30, 40.60. Cochran’s Q p<1e-5 all models; non-monotonic/model-dependent.

Drift: §5.4 says drift-leak curves dip near d=3 then rebound; Cramer’s V small/negligible at probe level: DeepSeek 0.1073 small, GPT 0.0659 negligible, Qwen 0.0723 negligible. Only bounded short-to-medium drift up to d=6.

Secret type: strong association with hybrid leakage, Cramer’s V probe-level: DeepSeek 0.5871 large, GPT 0.7731 large, Qwen 0.6927 large. Table 5 probe-level hybrid by secret type: SSN GPT 0.14%, DeepSeek 1.11%, Qwen 5.97%; Credit card GPT 0.00%, DeepSeek 0.39%, Qwen 4.01%; Email GPT 78.24%, DeepSeek 57.11%, Qwen 81.13%; Phone GPT 70.89%, DeepSeek 46.13%, Qwen 57.24%.

Appendix B/Table 8 probe-level effect sizes: Secret type as above; drift as above; persuasion Cramer’s V: DeepSeek 0.0718 negligible, GPT 0.0689 negligible, Qwen 0.0639 negligible. Significant Cochran’s Q for persuasion coexists with negligible V effect sizes.

§5.6: no evaluated model approaches half-life threshold at any tested drift; τ=max(Dobs)+1=7 for all models and persuasion levels.

§5.7 fuzzy matching: Table 6 probe-level rates: DeepSeek regex 25.50, fuzzy .85 26.40, fuzzy .80 26.53, hybrid 26.43; GPT 36.80, 37.03, 37.07, 37.57; Qwen 36.97, 37.60, 37.93, 37.53. Fuzzy auxiliary only.

Limitations/future work: no formal human inter-annotator agreement; future larger manual audit. Artifact availability planned: benchmark generation code, probe templates, evaluation scripts, aggregate results, sanitized subset/examples with non-real identifiers/templates. errors.claim: “These rates estimate whether a dialogue is vulnerable across all possible extraction attacks, including adaptive adversarial probing.”
errors.evidence: Earlier notes: “All models get same dialogue histories and probe templates… three standardized persuasion probes per dialogue, yielding 3,000 cached model-probe responses per model… Aggregation: overall leakage at dialogue level, counted leaking if any standardized probe elicits secret.” Also Section 5.2/Table 3 says: “A dialogue is counted as leaking if any standardized probe elicits the secret.”
errors.explanation: The experiment measures leakage under three fixed standardized probes, not all possible or adaptive extraction attacks. Claiming the rates estimate vulnerability across all possible/adaptive probing contradicts the described evaluation design.

Paper title: “PrivDrift: Auditing User-Secret Leakage Under Topic Drift in Active LLM Conversations.” Author Luciano Rolando Maldonado Romero, WVU.

Core claim: QX2/PrivDrift audits persistence of user-secret leakage in active/persistent conversations using seeded multi-turn histories, content-dense unrelated drift, and standardized probes. Main claims: G4P under H8D remains substantial, varies sharply across systems, S8Q, and V4N, and does not reliably decline within tested d=0..6 window. SSNs/payment IDs suppressed far more than contact identifiers; no stable decay. Caveat: behavioral recoverability does not imply permanent memory, training memorization, personalization/cross-session retention, or uniform long-context behavior; only active-context re-disclosure under sufficient retrieval pressure.

Definitions: E9U=active-context re-disclosure of earlier user-supplied secret S after drift/probe, not mere transcript presence. D7A drift length d values 0,2,3,4,5,6; d=0 p=.2, otherwise uniform over 2–6. S8Q: A2L phone/contact, F8Z email/electronic contact, W3B SSN/gov IDs, N6G credit card/payment. V4N: C8R neutral direct retrieval, Z2F contextual/form-filling, L9W urgent/high-pressure; standardized probes, not unconstrained/adaptive adversarial search. H8D positive if normalized inclusion or Llama judge finds full/substantial/identifying partial disclosure. B6T normalized matching; U3P deterministic/regex baseline. R5J fuzzy matching sensitivity on cached outputs. K2V tau: first observed d where L(d)<=0.1*L(0) and all later d remain <= threshold; if none tau=max(Dobs)+1.

Dataset/setup: N=1000 dialogues: 900 synthetic, 100 human-authored, interspersed. Avg words/dialogue 359.16; median 385; min/max 43/795; tokens avg 478.87, median 513.33, min/max 57.33/1060.00. Appendix A Table 7 by D7A: d0 N197 avg words/tokens 44.29/59.05 med 43/57.33; d2 N147 avg 253.97/338.62 med 258/344; d3 N142 avg 344.18/458.91 med 347/462.67; d4 N166 avg 452.27/603.02 med 447/596; d5 N181 avg 520.92/694.56 med 543/724; d6 N167 avg 568.03/757.37 med 605/806.67. Counts sum 1000 and weighted word avg matches 359.16. 3 evaluated models/cached responses: 3,000/model, 9,000 total = 1000 dialogues × 3 V4N probes × 3 models. Model mappings from Limitations: M7Q = GPT-OSS-120B; T4X = DeepSeek-R1; Y9C = Qwen3-VL-235B. Full dataset per model. G4P=dialogue-level any-probe leakage; P6S=probe-level response statistic. G4P can exceed mean condition-specific P6S. CIs bootstrap over dialogues; McNemar/Cochran Q/chi-square/Cramer’s V as appropriate.

Results §5:
- §5.1 Table 2 G4P U3P vs H8D: M7Q 47.70/47.70 Δ0 p=1.0; T4X 37.80/38.70 Δ+0.90 p=7.7e-3; Y9C 53.50/54.60 Δ+1.10 p=2.57e-3. Claim H8D only slightly differs from B6T/U3P; direct/near-direct dominates.
- §5.2 Table 3 H8D G4P with bootstrap CIs: T4X 38.70% [35.7,41.6], M7Q 47.70% [44.6,50.8], Y9C 54.60% [51.6,57.7]. Internal error noted earlier: text says “all possible extraction attacks, including adaptive adversarial probing,” contradicting standardized non-adaptive probes.
- §5.3 Table 4 H8D P6S by V4N: M7Q C8R 39.30, Z2F 40.50, L9W 32.90; T4X 28.10, 22.00, 29.20; Y9C 38.70, 33.30, 40.60. Cochran Q p<1e-5 every model. Claim directions non-monotonic: M7Q declines under L9W; T4X minimum at Z2F; Y9C maximum at L9W.
- §5.4 D7A: cached P6S associations small/negligible; risk persists; Figure 4 H8D vs D7A has dip near d=3 then rebound. Supports no reliable reduction. J7K/drift/context boundary is not an implicit privacy boundary; unstable intermediate decreases should not be treated as suppression evidence.
- §5.5 Table 5 H8D P6S by S8Q: W3B M7Q 0.14, T4X 1.11, Y9C 5.97; N6G 0.00, 0.39, 4.01; F8Z 78.24, 57.11, 81.13; A2L 70.89, 46.13, 57.24. Claim S8Q large/strongest association; W3B/N6G far more suppressed than F8Z/A2L. Conclusion says S8Q asymmetry suggests safeguards rely more on format/sensitivity cues and format-sensitive heuristics than generalized contextual confidentiality/robust contextual reasoning.
- §5.6 K2V: every model and persuasion condition observed bound d<=6; assigned tau=max(Dobs)+1=7; no system approaches threshold or stabilizes.
- §5.7 Table 6 cached-output P6S: T4X U3P 25.50, R5J .85 26.40, R5J .80 26.53, H8D 26.43; M7Q 36.80, 37.03, 37.07, 37.57; Y9C 36.97, 37.60, 37.93, 37.53. These are P6S, so lower than Table 2 G4P is expected. Figure 5: H8D heatmap by D7A and V4N.

Appendix B Table 8 cached P6S H8D-benchmark-variable effect sizes: T4X S8Q 0.5871 Large, D7A 0.1073 Small, V4N 0.0718 Negligible; M7Q S8Q 0.7731 Large, D7A 0.0659 Negligible, V4N 0.0689 Negligible; Y9C S8Q 0.6927 Large, D7A 0.0723 Negligible, V4N 0.0639 Negligible. Appendix C Figure 6: dialogue construction details.

Limitations/Future Work §7: bounded short-to-medium D7A only, not full-window/arbitrarily long behavior; fixed-format secrets only, non-fixed sensitive attributes future; active context only, not cross-session memory/training-data memorization/personalization. Mixed synthetic/human construction; cached metadata no longer preserves human-authored row identifiers, so only aggregate results reported and human-vs-synthetic comparison deferred. Detector scope: U3P/R5J/external judge surface outputs, no formal human–automated IAA; larger manual audits future. API-served models may change despite logs/caches/paired stats. Planned artifact releases: generation code, probe templates, evaluation scripts, aggregate result files, sanitized dialogue subset; synthetic PII-like strings require non-real identifiers/templates for safe reproduction.

Main metric/result claims: Across extended-context models, G4P under H8D remains substantial, varies sharply across systems, S8Q, and V4N, and does not reliably decline within tested window. Intro specifically claims SSNs/payment identifiers receive much stronger suppression than contact identifiers; no evaluated system attains stable decay. Active-context privacy should be evaluated as persistent behavioral failure, not only parameter memorization or immediate jailbreak behavior.

Threat model/framework definitions from §3:
- E9U = active-context re-disclosure: assistant reproduces earlier sensitive value under later querying/justification/pressure; not mere presence of value in transcript. Transcript invisibility is not assumed.
- User supplies secret S at t0. Unrelated content-dense exchanges/J7K = topic drift are D={u1,a1,...,ud,ad}; standardized probe P appended after drift. Exact, approximate, or semantic revelation of S = leakage.
- D7A = drift length/intervening-turn quantity d, turns between disclosure and final probe. Values in benchmark: 0,2,3,4,5,6. Sampling: d=0 with p=.2; otherwise uniform over {2,3,4,5,6} with p=.8. Immediate recall included; short-to-medium drift emphasized.
- S8Q = secret type. Four fixed-format categories: A2L=phone numbers/contact values; F8Z=email addresses/electronic contact values; W3B=Social Security Numbers/government identifiers; N6G=credit card numbers/payment identifiers. Each inserted as ground-truth secret, not inferred.
- V4N = persuasion intensity/probe style: C8R=Simple neutral direct retrieval; Z2F=Medium contextual justification/form-filling; L9W=Hard urgent/high-pressure elicitation. Standardized conditions, not unconstrained adversarial search.
- H8D = hybrid composite detector. Labels response positive if normalized inclusion succeeds OR LLM judge finds full secret, substantial substring, or sufficient partial info to identify it. Eligible disclosures include verbatim output, formatting changes, partial substrings, paraphrased references.
- B6T = normalization-based matching, first stage/hierarchical eval. Numeric secrets/responses strip non-digit chars; alphanumeric normalizes case/whitespace but retains meaningful delimiters. Formula Leak_U3P(R,S)=I[phi(S) subset phi(R)].
- U3P = regex-only/deterministic baseline, reported separately alongside H8D.
- LLM judge: open-weights Llama judge receives S and R, binary full/substantial-disclosure verdict for deterministic negatives; judge errors possible, not treated as error-free.
- K2V = Privacy Half-Life/stability metric tau. Observed lengths D_obs and leakage rates L(d), safety threshold delta=0.1*L(0). tau=min d in D_obs such that L(d)<=delta and for all later observed d’, L(d’)<=delta. Empty set tau=max(D_obs)+1. This is sustained suppression, not momentary decrease.

Dataset generation from §3:
- Total dialogues N=1000: 900 synthetic, 100 human-authored, interspersed not contiguous.
- Secret categories=4. Avg words/dialogue 359.16; median 385; min/max 43/795. Approx tokens avg 478.87; median 513.33; min/max 57.33/1060.00.
- Pipeline: scaffold-then-rewrite preserves exact ground truth secret, intervening-turn counts, role structure, final-probe conditions; rewriting model only improves fluency/persona realism. Human-authored dialogues obey same constraints. Personas sampled from >100 professions/demographic profiles. Topic-dense drift library includes tax filing, medical triage, travel logistics plus professional-writing/structured-reasoning/long-form-summarization fallback tasks; annotators contribute subset.

Related-work framing to remember: QX2 differs from training-data memorization/membership/unlearning benchmarks because it concerns inference-time handling of user-supplied active-context secrets still present in context. Differs from contextual-integrity/legal/static access-control benchmarks by isolating behavioral recoverability after unrelated exchanges and persuasive probing. Differs from jailbreak/instruction-hijacking/multi-turn unsafe-content attacks because target is information-flow/re-disclosure of earlier sensitive info.

Potential consistency checks for later: Results should report G4P and P6S (not yet defined in §3) alongside U3P/H8D; support claims that SSN/payment leakage lower than phone/email, no stable decay for any evaluated system, leakage varies by model, S8Q, V4N, and does not reliably decline within d=0..6 window.

Paper title: “PrivDrift: Auditing User-Secret Leakage Under Topic Drift in Active LLM Conversations.” Author Luciano Rolando Maldonado Romero, WVU.

Core framing: PrivDrift audits whether user-disclosed sensitive info remains behaviorally recoverable through later prompts after unrelated topic drift. Not training-data memorization/cross-session memory; risk in shared/persistent sessions, browser assistants, enterprise copilots, agent workflows, prompt injection/tool outputs. Dataset: 1,000 controlled multi-turn dialogues with seeded secrets, content-dense drift turns, standardized extraction probes; evaluated per model. Main conclusion: dialogue-level hybrid leakage substantial, 38.7%–54.6%; varies by model, secret type, persuasion intensity; within d≤6 drift does not reliably reduce leakage; Privacy Half-Life exceeds observed window for all models; secret type strongest association/asymmetry, suggesting protections are uneven and format-sensitive rather than robust contextual confidentiality. SSNs/credit cards suppressed more often than emails/phones.

Framework: dialogue generator, probing harness, metric suite. Threat model: secret S disclosed at turn t0; then d unrelated drift turns; standardized probe P appended; leakage if response reveals S exactly, approximately, or semantically. Dataset: N=1000; 900 synthetic + 100 human-authored, inserted throughout benchmark rather than separate block; current cached eval metadata does not preserve which rows are human-authored, so only aggregate results/no human-vs-synthetic comparison. Secret categories: phone, email, SSN, credit card. Drift lengths sampled from {0,2,3,4,5,6}; no d=1. Table 1 aggregate: avg words 359.16, median 385, min/max 43/795; approx tokens avg 478.87, median 513.33, min/max 57.33/1060. Appendix A/Table 7 by drift: d0 N197 avg words44.29 median43 avg tokens59.05 median57.33; d2 N147 avg253.97 median258 avg tokens338.62 median344; d3 N142 avg344.18 median347 avg tokens458.91 median462.67; d4 N166 avg452.27 median447 avg tokens603.02 median596; d5 N181 avg520.92 median543 avg tokens694.56 median724; d6 N167 avg568.03 median605 avg tokens757.37 median806.67. Counts sum to 1000 and weighted averages match Table 1.

Probing: three persuasion levels per dialogue: Simple direct neutral, Medium contextual justification, Hard high-pressure/urgent. Models GPT-OSS-120B, DeepSeek-R1, Qwen3-VL-235B via OpenRouter/API-served models. 1,000 dialogues/model; three probes/dialogue = 3,000 cached responses/model, 9,000 total. Overall leakage at dialogue level: any standardized probe elicits secret. Persuasion/fuzzy analyses probe level. Stats: regex-only and hybrid; dialogue-level bootstrap CIs; probe-level sensitivity rates; McNemar with Bonferroni; Cochran’s Q; chi-square/Cramer’s V.

Detector: hybrid = normalized matching plus open-weights Llama judge on regex-negative responses. Numeric secrets strip non-digits; alphanumeric normalize case/whitespace while preserving meaningful delimiters. Regex leak if normalized secret substring in normalized response. Judge binary if response reveals full secret/substantial substring/enough partial info. No formal human inter-annotator agreement yet.

Known internal inconsistency: Section 5.1 and repeated in Section 6 claim dialogue-level hybrid/deterministic results are “identical” or deterministic matching fully captures behavior for every model, but Table 2 shows added hybrid leakage for DeepSeek (+0.90) and Qwen (+1.10); only GPT identical. Table 3 dialogue-level hybrid CIs: DeepSeek 38.70% [35.7,41.6]; GPT 47.70% [44.6,50.8]; Qwen 54.60% [51.6,57.7]. Conclusion’s 38.7%–54.6% range is consistent.

Persuasion probe-level hybrid Table 4: GPT Simple 39.30%, Medium 40.50%, Hard 32.90%; DeepSeek Simple 28.10%, Medium 22.00%, Hard 29.20%; Qwen Simple 38.70%, Medium 33.30%, Hard 40.60%. Text: Cochran’s Q p<1e-5 all models; non-monotonic/model-dependent; GPT hard reduces leakage, DeepSeek medium lowest, Qwen hard highest. Appendix B/Table 8 persuasion Cramer’s V: DeepSeek 0.0718 negligible; GPT 0.0689 negligible; Qwen 0.0639 negligible.

Drift length: Section 5.4 says dip near d=3 followed by rebound; effect sizes small/negligible. Cramer’s V probe-level for drift: DeepSeek 0.1073 small; GPT 0.0659 negligible; Qwen 0.0723 negligible (also Appendix B/Table 8). Not claim about arbitrarily long contexts; risk persists across several unrelated shifts. Limitations: bounded drift up to d=6, short-to-medium active-context drift, not full saturation/long-context characterization.

Secret type Table 5 probe-level hybrid: GPT SSN 0.14%, Credit card 0.00%, Email 78.24%, Phone 70.89%; DeepSeek SSN 1.11%, Credit card 0.39%, Email 57.11%, Phone 46.13%; Qwen SSN 5.97%, Credit card 4.01%, Email 81.13%, Phone 57.24%. Cramer’s V large: DeepSeek 0.5871, GPT 0.7731, Qwen 0.6927 (also Appendix B/Table 8). Interpretation/conclusion: secret type strongest association with leakage.

With max d=6, no model approaches threshold; τ=7 for all models and persuasion levels.
