Paper title: “Explanation Multiplicity: Circuit-Level Interpretability”; claim: “Evidence Does Not Survive Defensible Analytic Variation.” Author Ajay Pravin Mahale, date 12 Aug 2026.

Regulatory framing: EU AI Act high-risk documentation. Annex IV 2(b) “general logic… algorithms”; 2(e) “technical measures needed to facilitate interpretation”; Article 86(1) right to “clear and meaningful explanations…” for certain automated decisions. Claim map has φ_overseer based on Annex IV 2(e), 3, Article 14(4)(c), keyed by dominant layer band, size class, ranked input segment; φ_affected based on Article 86(1), leading with input segment. Three nested granularities.

Premise/RQ: audit value requires two analysts to reach compatible conclusions. Tests whether mechanistic/circuit evidence survives “two competent analysts, same system, same tool, different defensible settings.” Scope: GPT-2 small and IOI only; no scaling claim. Graph separates Q/K/V inputs, |E|=32,491; circuits touch 144 attention heads and 12 MLPs=156 components.

Grid: seven objectives, seven ablations, four corruptions nested within five operators, four metrics, three thresholds, two prompts, five seeds. Pre-registered: 1,540 discovery cells / 18,480 specifications. One objective fails: all 220 cells runtime error from MSE against integral target; not repaired. Realised: six objectives, 1,320 cells / 15,840 specs. Thresholds fixed 6 Aug 2026 and not revisited.

Stats/protocol: no p-values across specs. Bootstrap resamples specifications, B=10,000; intervals quantify grid uncertainty only. F = 1 − [Σc nc(nc−1)]/[N(N−1)] = probability two draws without replacement differ. π*=modal share. Filable at tolerance α iff π*≥1−α. Nine-class ceiling F≤0.8889; observed 0.7316 =82.3% ceiling. Section 8 filability protocol: declare defensible S; deterministic published non-LLM claim map φ; compute π*, F; filable iff π*≥1−α; report π*, F, discard rate per axis level, within-group decomposition. Filing without π* “has not been audited.”

Main results: threshold admits no circuit for 8,279/15,840 specs (52.3% discarded), uneven by metric. Kept: comprehensiveness 3,947, KL 1,467, logit diff 1,270, sufficiency 877; total 7,561. Surviving pool 52% comprehensiveness vs 25% design.

Claim map fixed in pre-registration, deterministic code, published, not LLM-generated. Size bins from committed calibration rule. Size-binning sensitivity: committed F=.7316; ×0.5 .7448, ×0.8 .7435, ×0.9 .7394, ×1.1 .7289, ×1.25 .7314, ×1.5 .7308, ×2 .7232, equal thirds .7018, deciles .7719, no size/COARSE .5733.

Section 7/Table 3: P0 Jbar .1396 [.1377,.1418]. H2 F>0.20: .7316 [.7247,.7380], confirmed. H3 “not separated from random null”: rejected; separated. H4 F−(1−agreement)>0.10: .3344 [.3297,.3394], supported.

Jbar=.1396 over 28,580,580 pairs among 7,561 specs; 3,218 distinct circuits. D quantiles: 1% .196, 25% .788, median .960, 75% .998; median pair shares 4% edges; 1% pairs Jaccard >.8. Median circuit size 200; random line .0031; observed mean overlap ~45× chance.

F=.7316, π*=.4109; not filable at 0.95/0.90/0.80. Overseer MEDIUM nine classes: early/distributed 3,107 (.4109); late/sparse 2,153 (.2848); late/moderate 657; late/distributed 489; early/sparse 477; middle/moderate 283; middle/sparse 269; middle/distributed 90; early/moderate 36. Aggregated layer: early 47.9%/COARSE modal .4788, late 43.6%, middle 8.5%. Top two claims early vs late contradict.

All addressee-granularity combos fail filability α=.20: affected COARSE F=.3950 π=.7291; affected MEDIUM .6597 π=.4875; affected FINE .6744 π=.4786; overseer COARSE .5733 π=.4788; overseer MEDIUM .7316 π=.4109; overseer FINE .7681 π=.4109.

Standardising axes residual F/removes: metric .5939/.1377; ablation .7014/.0302; objective .7018/.0298; threshold .7070/.0246; corruption .7092/.0224; prompt .7232/.0084; seed .7307/.0009. Metric largest but insufficient. REML log10 circuit size: ablation-corruption interaction 78.8%, residual 11.5%, ablation 4.4%, threshold 4.1%, metric .7%. Maximum pressure remove circuit size, dominant layer only, hold size fixed: F=.2706 [.2550,.2859], above prereg threshold.

Random baseline: pooled discovered less stable than size-matched random null: .7316 vs .6774, intervals disjoint; H3 rejected. Direction not reported due size artefact. Holding size fixed reverses: discovered .2746 vs null .4230 medium; .2706 vs .3822 coarse. Internal inconsistency already noted: Table 7 medium by size includes 2000 n312 F=.5714, while earlier text says instability lives entirely below 2,000 edges.

Functional agreement: per-example agreement .6028; instability .3972; gap .3344 [.3297,.3394]. Cohen κ=.0146; raw 60% mostly both right same fraction, not same examples. κ .016–.047 at every size while raw agreement .52 to .92, tracking accuracy .51 to .95. H4 pooled supported, but gap fails .10 at 6/10 sizes and negative at 5; pooled carried by 500–2,000 edge band.

Limitations/discussion: one model/task; larger models may change F. Second-model replication pre-registered/not run: Pythia-160m, 924-cell grid, same axes except seed has 3 levels not 5; second task designed/not run. Circuit size is outcome not axis; threshold-chosen size distorted F, null comparison direction, functional gap sign; fixing size drops F .7316→.2746, larger than standardising any preregistered axis; report pooled stats with within-size decomposition. Multiverse only as wide as library; optimal ablation not implemented; measured F lower bound vs full defensible choices. Discard rate high/uneven: 52.3%, metric imbalance. Bootstrap invalid for one reported family where conditioning groups have only 2–5 specs; those quantities point estimates with diagnostic; no post hoc bias-corrected estimator. Discussion says failed objective is not headline, but tooling maturity observation; regulator takeaway: interpretability evidence is not worthless, but evidentiary weight should be measured cheaply relative to original sweep.

Reproducibility: pre-registration is timestamped commit tagged prereg-p1-confirmatory before confirmatory sweep. Reported numbers trace to config, seed, environment fingerprint. Confirmatory sweep ran under single environment across all 1,320 cells, verified from archive; code commit recovered by content-addressed comparison, 22/22 files identical. Analysis layer runs without GPU. Verification recomputes headline quantities from raw results: 36 checks, 0 failures, F derived three ways including brute-force pairwise. Second script checks numeric tokens match stored results; tables emitted directly from results; test suite has 343 tests.

Paper title: “Explanation Multiplicity: Circuit-Level Interpretability”; subtitle/claim: “Evidence Does Not Survive Defensible Analytic Variation.” Author Ajay Pravin Mahale, date 12 Aug 2026.

Abstract key claims to track:
- Context: EU AI Act requires providers of high-risk systems to file technical documentation describing how system reaches decisions. Mechanistic interpretability, especially circuit discovery, is framed as source of such evidence.
- Research question: whether evidence survives when “two competent analysts, the same system, the same tool, different defensible settings.”
- Design: pre-registered crossed grid of seven analytic axes; every level taken from a published implementation. Each discovered circuit mapped through a deterministic claim map to a structured Annex IV statement.
- Scope/model/task: GPT-2 small and indirect object identification (IOI) task. Study covers one model and one task; scaling untested.
- Main numbers: 15,840 pre-registered specifications; 7,561 produced a claim. Derived statement flips across 73.2% of specification pairs, 95% CI 0.725–0.738. Modal claim commands 41.1% of the space. Evidence fails a filability criterion at every plausibly acceptable conformity-assessment tolerance.
- Sensitivity/ablation claims: Standardising the single most influential choice, the evaluation metric, leaves flip rate 59.4%. Removing circuit size from the claim entirely and holding it fixed leaves 27.1% flip rate, 95% CI 0.255–0.286, still above pre-registered threshold.
- Circuit similarity/function claims: circuits underlying claims structurally near-disjoint, median pairwise Jaccard overlap 4%; functionally uncorrelated at Cohen’s kappa 0.015. Therefore instability is not just one mechanism described in different words.
- Protocol/contribution: gives filability criterion as standalone protocol.
- Additional reported issue: one of seven documented discovery objectives does not execute at all on the library’s own canonical task.

Paper title: “Explanation Multiplicity: Circuit-Level Interpretability / Evidence Does Not Survive Defensible Analytic Variation” by Ajay Pravin Mahale, dated 12 Aug 2026.

Abstract key claims/results to check later:
- Context: EU AI Act requires high-risk AI providers to file technical documentation describing how systems reach decisions. Mechanistic interpretability/circuit discovery is framed as likely evidence source.
- Research question: whether circuit-discovery evidence survives “two competent analysts, same system, same tool, different defensible settings.”
- Study design: pre-registered crossed grid of seven analytic axes; every level taken from a published implementation. Each discovered circuit mapped through a deterministic claim map to a structured Annex IV statement.
- Setting: GPT-2 small and indirect object identification (IOI) task; one model and one task only.
- Total specifications: 15,840 pre-registered specifications. Of these, 7,561 produced a claim.
- Main result: derived statement flips across 73.2% of specification pairs, 95% CI 0.725 to 0.738. Modal claim covers/commands 41.1% of the space.
- Conclusion: evidence fails a “filability criterion” at every tolerance plausibly acceptable to a conformity assessment body.
- Sensitivity/robustness claims:
  - Standardising the single most influential choice, the evaluation metric, leaves flip rate at 59.4%.
  - Removing circuit size from the claim entirely and holding it fixed leaves 27.1% flip rate, 95% CI 0.255 to 0.286; still above pre-registered threshold.
- Circuit similarity results: circuits underlying claims are structurally near-disjoint, median pairwise Jaccard overlap 4%; functionally uncorrelated at Cohen’s kappa 0.015. Therefore instability is not merely one mechanism described in different words.
- Additional contribution: filability criterion given as standalone protocol.
- Execution failure: one of the seven documented discovery objectives does not execute at all on the library’s own canonical task.
- Caveat: conclusion at scale untested; study covers one model and one task.

Related work (Part 3):
- Non-identifiability: cites Méloux et al. [6], premise that unique explanation need not exist; contribution is measuring downstream cost when explanation is filed rather than published.

Current Part 9: Table 6 residual flip after standardising each axis: metric F=.5939 CI .5803-.6063 removes .1377; ablation .7014 removes .0302; objective .7018 removes .0298; threshold .7070 removes .0246; corruption .7092 removes .0224; prompt .7232 removes .0084; seed .7307 removes .0009. It claims group sizes 1,512-2,520, but this conflicts with 7,561 specs and two prompt variants. Metric largest lever but insufficient. REML on log10 selected circuit size: 78.8% structural variance from ablation-corruption interaction, 11.5% residual, 4.4% ablation, 4.1% threshold, 0.7% metric; metric largest claim-variance driver.

Maximum pressure: strip size from claim to dominant layer band and hold circuit size fixed: F=0.2706 [0.2550,0.2859], above prereg threshold.

Random baseline: pooled discovered less stable than size-matched random null, .7316 vs .6774, intervals disjoint; H3 rejected. Direction not reported as finding because size distribution artefact. With size fixed ordering reverses: discovered .2746 vs null .4230 at medium, and .2706 vs .3822 at coarse; discovered more stable than random but not stable enough. Table 7 size bins sum to N=7,561: 10 n2492 F .4543 null .7331; 20 n489 F .3380 null .6622; 50 n519 F .4639 null .7310; 100 n242 F .5792 null .6584; 200 n199 F .5122 null .6366; 500 n236 F .4258 null .1421; 1000 n380 F .5133 null 0; 2000 n312 F .5714 null 0; 5000 n625 F 0; 10000 n2067 F 0. Cohen kappa .0146; raw agreement mostly due both circuits being right at same fraction, not same examples. Final notes. Paper title: “Explanation Multiplicity: Circuit-Level Interpretability”. Subtitle/claim: “Evidence Does Not Survive Defensible Analytic Variation.” Author Ajay Pravin Mahale, dated 12 Aug 2026.

Core thesis: regulatory circuit evidence fails Y3W throughout plausible conformity-assessment tolerances; competent analysts using same system/tool get incompatible statements under defensible settings; standardisation and size controls do not remove failure; structural and functional disagreement rule out “same mechanism reworded”; no claim beyond one model/task. Legal basis: EU AI Act/Reg. 2024/1689 Annex IV 2(b), 2(e), Art 86(1), amended by Reg. 2026/1744. No improved discovery method proposed.

Found internal inconsistencies: (1) §2 says “seven-axis regulatory propagation,” but §4 formalism defines 8 axes: s=(o,a,d,m,τ,P,r,g). (2) Part 5 sensitivity row says “Across factor-four binnings: 0.70 to 0.77,” but threshold ×0.5–×2 range is .7232–.7448; .7018/.7719 are equal-thirds/deciles. (3) Part 9 says “instability lives entirely below 2,000 edges,” but Table 7 has size 2,000 with discovered F=.5714 and 3 classes.

Formalism: Q7V factorised graph |E|=32,491; 144 attention heads + 12 MLPs = 156 components. D=1-Jaccard; J-bar mean Jaccard. F=1-[Σc nc(nc-1)]/[N(N-1)]. Conditional F_within(G)=1-[ΣgΣc n_gc(n_gc-1)]/[Σg ng(ng-1)]. Y3W ceiling for 9 classes .8889; observed fraction 82.3%.

Y3W protocol: For circuit-derived filed claim c, declare S, deterministic φ, compute π*=max_c n_c/N over S and F, pass at tolerance α iff π*≥1−α, report π*, F, discard rate per axis level, and within-group decomposition of every pooled statistic. Filing unable to state π* is asserted, not audited.

Claim mapping: D9P overseer grounded Annex IV 2(e), 3 and Art 14(4)(c), ordered by dominant layer band, size class, ranked input segment. L3X affected grounded Art 86(1), leads with input segment/right of decision subject. Resolutions E7R/K8Z/V2H coarse/medium/fine designed so refinement cannot contradict coarser statement. Size bins committed on measured node-count curve. Table 1 F values include committed .7316; no size term/E7R .5733; threshold variants .7232–.7448; equal thirds .7018; deciles .7719.

Method: Q7V=GPT-2 small; Z4K=IOI. Grid: 7 objectives, 7 operators, 4 corruption distributions nested within 5 operators, 4 metrics, 3 thresholds, 2 prompts, 5 seeds. Per objective 22 operator/corruption combos; total discovery cells 1,540; specs 18,480. One objective failed due to MSE/integral target runtime error; realised objectives 6, cells 1,320, specs 15,840. Discarded 8,279 (52.3%); kept 7,561. Metric retention: T9V 3,947 kept, H2W 1,467, N6C 1,270, U4J 877. Bootstrap resamples specifications, B=10,000; no spec-level p-values; intervals condition on grid.

Registered outcomes: J6D J-bar .1396 [0.1377,.1418], premise holds; X4R F>.20 .7316 [.7247,.7380], confirmed; Q2F “not separated from random null” rejected because separated/disjoint; Z8N functional gap .3344 [.3297,.3394], supported. Two outcomes require within-size qualifications.

Structural results: 7,561 claim specs; 3,218 distinct circuits; all pairs 28,580,580. D quantiles: 1% .196, 25% .788, median .960, 75% .998. Median shared-edge fraction 4%; pairs Jaccard>0.8 only 1%; median size 200 edges. Random overlap at median size .0031; observed/chance ~45×.

Regulatory claim results: D9P K8Z shares: early distributed .4109; late sparse .2848; late moderate .0869; late distributed .0647; early sparse .0631; middle moderate .0374; middle sparse .0356; middle distributed .0119; early moderate .0048. Pair disagreement 73.2%; CI .725–.738; required .95/.90/.80 fail; size-aggregated early/late/middle 47.9/43.6/8.5. Table 5 all addressee/resolution at α=.20 fail: L3X E7R F .3950 pi .7291; L3X K8Z .6597 pi .4875; L3X V2H .6744 pi .4786; D9P E7R .5733 pi .4788; D9P K8Z .7316 pi .4109; D9P V2H .7681 pi .4109.

Standardisation: residual F/removes: metric .5939/.1377; ablation .7014/.0302; objective .7018/.0298; threshold .7070/.0246; corruption .7092/.0224; prompt .7232/.0084; seed .7307/.0009. REML log10 size: ablation-corruption interaction 78.8%, residual 11.5, ablation 4.4, threshold 4.1, metric .7. Metric-standardised disagreement 59.4%.

Size/null/functional: size-free claim fixed size F=.2706 CI .2550-.2859. Pooled discovered F .7316 vs A6N .6774; fixed-size reverses: K8Z discovered .2746 vs A6N .4230, E7R .2706 vs A6N .3822. Table 7 includes size 2000 discovered F .5714; sizes 5000/10000 F=0. Functional pooled agreement .6028; instability .3972; smallest-circuit instability .4777; kappa .0146; kappa range every size .016-.047; raw agreement .52-.92; accuracy .51-.95; sizes failing gap threshold 6/10; negative gap 5; band carrying pooled gap 500-2000 edges.

Limitations: one model/task; larger models unclear. Second-model M9B Pythia-160m plan unrun: same task, 924-cell grid with 3 not 5 seed levels; second task unrun. Circuit size outcome not axis; threshold-selected size distorts F, null direction, functional-gap sign; every pooled statistic reportedly has within-size decomposition. Multiverse limited to library not literature; unsupported C4Y optimal ablation excluded, so measured F lower bound relative to full field. Discard high/uneven; retained metric imbalance not adjusted; threshold fixed. Bootstrap invalid for one family: groups with 2–5 specs have dominating self-pairs; intervals replaced by point estimates/diagnostics.

Reproducibility (§11): public timestamped commit tagged prereg-p1-confirmatory; archive verifies one environment across all 1,320 confirmatory cells; 22/22 files identical; analysis needs no GPU. One script recomputes headlines and asserts 36 checks, 0 failures, F via three routes including brute-force pairs. Numeric tokens checked against stored derivations; tables emitted directly; suite has 343 tests.

errors.claim: “seven-axis regulatory propagation”
errors.evidence: Later formalism defines the setting as an 8-tuple: “s=(o,a,d,m,τ,P,r,g)” with axes objective, operator/ablation, corruption distribution, metric, threshold, prompt, seed, and granularity/resolution.
errors.explanation: The paper describes the propagation as seven-axis in one place but formalises eight axes later.

errors.claim: “Across factor-four binnings: 0.70 to 0.77”
errors.evidence: The threshold ×0.5–×2 range is .7232–.7448; the .7018 and .7719 values correspond to equal-thirds and deciles, not factor-four threshold binnings.
errors.explanation: The stated 0.70–0.77 range is attributed to factor-four binnings, but those endpoints come from different binning schemes.

errors.claim: “instability lives entirely below 2,000 edges”
errors.evidence: Table 7 includes size 2,000 with discovered F=.5714 and 3 classes.
errors.explanation: If size 2,000 still has nonzero discovered instability, the instability does not live entirely below 2,000 edges.

errors.claim: The paper expands prior single-axis findings to “seven-axis regulatory propagation.”
errors.evidence: This part defines a specification as s=(o,a,d,m,τ,P,r,g), “respectively discovery objective, ablation operator, corruption distribution, evaluation metric, size threshold, prompt variant, seed, granularity.”
errors.explanation: The formalism lists eight axes, not seven. Unless one of these is later excluded from the regulatory-propagation design, this contradicts the earlier characterization as seven-axis.

errors.claim: “Across factor-four binnings | 0.70 to 0.77”
errors.evidence: The factor-four threshold binnings listed appear to be “all thresholds × 0.5” through “all thresholds × 2”, with F values 0.7448, 0.7435, 0.7394, 0.7289, 0.7314, 0.7308, and 0.7232. The 0.70 and 0.77 endpoints come from “equal thirds” = 0.7018 and “deciles” = 0.7719, not from factor-four threshold binnings.
errors.explanation: The stated range for factor-four binnings does not match the rows that are factor-four threshold scalings. It instead matches the broader set including non-factor-four alternatives.

errors.claim: “The grid yields ‘18,480 pre-registered specifications.’”
errors.evidence: Earlier Section 4 defined a specification as s=(o,a,d,m,τ,P,r,g), including granularity g. Earlier notes record three resolutions/granularities: E7R=COARSE, K8Z=MEDIUM, V2H=FINE. The current part’s count is 1,540 discovery cells × 4 metrics × 3 thresholds = 18,480, with no factor for the three granularity levels.
errors.explanation: If granularity g is part of the specification, as Section 4 stated, the fully crossed pre-registered specification count should include the three g levels, i.e. 55,440 rather than 18,480, unless the paper explicitly excludes g from the grid count. The current count conflicts with the earlier definition of specification.

errors.claim: “Claim-producing specifications | 7,561” while reporting multiple “Addressee | Granularity” combinations, including E7R/K8Z/V2H.
errors.evidence: Earlier formalism defined a specification as including granularity: “s=(o,a,d,m,τ,P,r,g)” with three resolutions E7R, K8Z, V2H. errors.explanation: If granularity g is part of each specification as defined, then the number of claim-producing specifications should reflect the three granularity levels, or the paper should redefine granularity as a reporting view rather than a crossed specification axis. errors.explanation: A6N degeneracy is shown to occur at 1,000 edges, not only above 1,000 edges.

Paper title: “Explanation Multiplicity: Circuit-Level Interpretability”. Main claim: circuit-derived regulatory evidence fails Y3W across defensible analytic variation; same model/task/tool can yield incompatible Annex IV statements. Scope caveat: no broad generalisation beyond one model/task unless qualified. Audit premise is commissioning requirement, not ML definition. EU AI Act refs: Annex IV 2(b), 2(e), Article 86(1), consolidated text amended by Reg. 2026/1744, CELEX 02024R1689-20260727, read 11 Aug 2026.

Key standing internal inconsistency: formal spec in §4 is s=(o,a,d,m,τ,P,r,g), including granularity g with levels E7R/K8Z/V2H, but §6 counts specs as 1,540 discovery cells ×4 metrics×3 thresholds=18,480, omitting g; realised specs 15,840; kept/claim-producing 7,561. §7 reports “claim-producing specifications 7,561” while Table 5 varies granularity across E7R/K8Z/V2H, so either g is not a spec axis or counts are undercounted by factor 3. Other possible earlier error: §5 row/prose “Across factor-four binnings 0.70 to 0.77” conflicts with threshold factor-four rows, which range about 0.7232–0.7448; 0.70/0.77 comes from equal thirds/deciles.

Definitions/protocol: Q7V graph |E|=32,491. Components: 144 attention heads +12 MLPs=156; output receives all 157 non-terminal sources. D=1−Jaccard. Jbar mean Jaccard over unordered pairs. Claim instability F=1−Σc nc(nc−1)/[N(N−1)]. Conditional Fwithin pair-weighted. Y3W ceiling observed classes=9, ceiling=0.8889; observed fraction 82.3%; observed F≈0.7315. §8 Y3W protocol for filed circuit claim: declare analytic space S with cited axes/levels; declare deterministic published φ, not LM; compute pi*=max_c n_c/N and F; passes at tolerance α iff pi*≥1−α; report pi*, F, discard rate per axis level, and within-group decomposition of every pooled statistic. Filing unable to state pi* is asserted, not audited; implementability only needs declared space and measured agreement, not regulatory adjudication.

G7U mappings: D9P overseer grounded in Annex IV 2(e), 3 and Art.14(4)(c): dominant layer band, size class, ranked input segment. L3X affected grounded in Art.86(1): leads with input segment. Resolutions: E7R coarse, K8Z medium, V2H fine; refinement cannot contradict coarser. φ deterministic, pre-registered, code, not LLM output. Size bins committed; Table 1 committed F=0.7316; no size term F=0.5733; alternatives mostly similar.

§6 method: GPT-2 small Q7V, task IOI Z4K. Grid: 7 objectives, 7 operators, 4 corruptions nested within 5 operators; 2 operators ignore corruption; effective op-corruption combos 22. Discovery cells 7×22×2 prompts×5 seeds=1,540. One objective failed before circuits; no repair. Realised objectives 6; discovery cells/confirmatory cells 1,320. Realised specs 15,840; no-circuit/discarded specs 8,279; kept 7,561. Discard rate 52.3%. Designed T9V composition 25%; surviving T9V 52%. Metric kept/discarded: T9V 3947/13; H2W 1467/2493; N6C 1270/2690; U4J 877/3083. Bootstrap specs B=10,000; CIs condition on grid.

§7 outcomes Table 3: J6D Jbar=0.1396 [0.1377,0.1418], premise holds. X4R F=0.7316 [0.7247,0.7380], confirmed. Q2F random-comparison separated from random null, intervals disjoint, hypothesis rejected. Z8N pooled functional gap F−(1−agreement)=0.3344 [0.3297,0.3394], supported. §7 says two outcomes need within-size qualifications.

§7.1 structural: specs 7,561; distinct circuits 3,218; pairs 28,580,580. D quantiles: 1%=0.196, 25%=0.788, median=0.960, 75%=0.998. Median shared-edge fraction 4%; 1% pairs Jaccard>0.8. Median circuit size 200 edges. Random line k/(2|E|−k); median size 0.0031; observed/chance overlap about 45×; expected random overlap for 500-edge circuit 0.008.

§7.2 claim frequencies D9P K8Z over 7,561: early/distributed 3107 .4109; late/sparse 2153 .2848; late/moderate 657 .0869; late/distributed 489 .0647; early/sparse 477 .0631; middle/moderate 283 .0374; middle/sparse 269 .0356; middle/distributed 90 .0119; early/moderate 36 .0048. Pair disagreement 73.2%, CI .725–.738. Required shares .95/.90/.80. Size-aggregated early/late/middle 47.9/43.6/8.5. Table 5 all fail Y3W at loosest α=.20: L3X E7R F=.3950 pi*=.7291; L3X K8Z .6597 pi*=.4875; L3X V2H .6744 pi*=.4786; D9P E7R .5733 pi*=.4788; D9P K8Z .7316 pi*=.4109; D9P V2H .7681 pi*=.4109.

§7.3 no analytic axis rescues filing; metric dominates single-axis claim control but insufficient. Table 6 residual F after standardisation: metric .5939 removes .1377; ablation .7014; objective .7018; threshold .7070; corruption .7092; prompt .7232; seed .7307. Structural variance log10 size: ablation-corruption interaction 78.8%, residual 11.5%, ablation 4.4%, threshold 4.1%, metric 0.7%. Metric-standardised percentage disagreement 59.4%. §10 reiterates complete metric standardisation exceeds conformity expectations, no single knob suffices, and declaring resolution after one-axis standardisation would be mistaken.

§7.4 maximum pressure: size absent and conditioned out; dominant-layer attribution still clears registered instability threshold. Size-free fixed-size F=.2706, CI .2550–.2859; discussion precision 27%.

§7.5 random baseline: pooled discovered F=.7316 vs A6N .6774; fixed-size reverses ordering, discovered more stable but still fails Y3W: K8Z .2746 vs A6N .4230; E7R .2706 vs .3822. A6N R=1,000. Internal errors in §7.5: says degeneracy occurs above 1,000, but Table 7/prose show A6N collapses at 1,000; says instability entirely below 2,000, but Table 7 has discovered F=.5714/classes 3 at size 2,000. Table 7 K8Z sizes 10/20/50/100/200/500/1000/2000/5000/10000 n=2492/489/519/242/199/236/380/312/625/2067; discovered F=.4543/.3380/.4639/.5792/.5122/.4258/.5133/.5714/0/0; A6N F=.7331/.6622/.7310/.6584/.6366/.1421/0/0/0/0. 5k+10k n sum 2692 no flips.

§7.6 functional: per-example agreement .6028; functional instability .3972; smallest-circuit functional instability .4777; kappa .0146/abstract .015; raw agreement 60%; kappa range every size .016–.047; raw-agreement climb .52–.92; accuracy .51–.95; sizes failing gap threshold 6/10; sizes with negative gap 5; pooled gap carried by 500–2,000 edges. Z8N holds only pooled, not under size conditioning.

§9 limitations: one model/task; larger models may change F. Committed second-model plan M9B Pythia-160m, same task, 924-cell grid identical except 3 not 5 seeds, unrun; second task designed but unrun. Size is outcome, not axis; threshold-selected size distorts F, null-comparison direction, and functional-gap sign; conditioning on size reduces claim instability more than standardising any registered axis; every pooled statistic reportedly has within-size decomposition. Multiverse limited to library, not whole literature: unsupported C4Y optimal ablation excluded, so measured F lower bound relative to full defensible field. Discard rate high/uneven; retained metric imbalance reported not adjusted; threshold fixed; no failed item repaired. Bootstrap invalid for one reported family: conditioning groups with 2–5 specs have dominating self-pairs; unusable intervals replaced by point estimates with diagnostics; no post hoc bias-corrected estimator.

§10 discussion: failed objective publicly exported/documented but cannot execute on library canonical task; this and discard rate framed as evidence of tooling maturity, not headline or criticism of authors. Regulator takeaway: interpretability evidence is not worthless; evidentiary weight is measurable and cheap relative to sweep producing circuit.

§11 reproducibility: public timestamped commit tagged prereg-p1-confirmatory. Every reported number said to trace to config/seed/environment fingerprint. Archive verification says one environment across all 1,320 confirmatory cells; content-addressed comparison recovers code commit, 22/22 files identical. Analysis needs no GPU. One script recomputes headline quantities from raw results and asserts 36 checks, 0 failures, including F via three routes and brute-force pairs. Another checks every manuscript numeric token against stored-result derivations. Tables emitted directly, never transcribed; suite has 343 tests.

errors.claim: “A specification is a tuple of analytic choices $s=(o,a,d,m,\tau,P,r,g)$ ...”
errors.evidence: Earlier notes: “Pre-registered multiverse/crossed grid over seven analytic axes of circuit discovery.” The tuple in this part lists eight analytic choices: objective, ablation operator, corruption distribution, evaluation metric, size threshold, prompt variant, seed, and granularity.
errors.explanation: The paper previously described the design as crossing seven analytic axes, but the formal specification here defines eight analytic-choice axes. Unless one of these is not intended to count as an axis, the counts conflict.

errors.claim: “six alternatives give a higher F, including halving every threshold.”
errors.evidence: Table 1 lists committed bins F = 0.7316. Alternatives higher than this are: all thresholds ×0.5 = 0.7448, ×0.8 = 0.7435, ×0.9 = 0.7394, and deciles = 0.7719. The remaining listed alternatives are lower: ×1.1 = 0.7289, ×1.25 = 0.7314, ×1.5 = 0.7308, ×2 = 0.7232, equal thirds = 0.7018, no size term = 0.5733.
errors.explanation: Only four alternatives in the table have F greater than the committed-bin value, not six.

errors.claim: “removing the size term from the claim entirely still leaves 0.5733.”
errors.evidence: Earlier notes record: “Removing circuit size from claim entirely and holding it fixed leaves 27.1% flip rate, 95% CI 0.255–0.286.”
errors.explanation: The paper appears to report two different flip rates for removing circuit size from the claim: 0.5733 here versus 0.271 earlier. This is an inconsistency unless the earlier additional condition, “holding it fixed,” is meant to define a different analysis.

errors.claim: “Seven discovery objectives… five seeds: 1,540 discovery cells and 18,480 specifications as pre-registered.”
errors.evidence: Earlier notes record the paper’s main number as: “15,840 pre-registered specifications; 7,561 produced a claim.” This part instead says the pre-registered grid had 18,480 specifications, with “realised grid” of 15,840 after one objective failed.

final_notes: Paper title: “Explanation Multipity: Circuit-Level Interpretability”; claim: “Evidence Does Not Survive Defensible Analytic Variation.” Author Ajay Pravin Mahale, 12 Aug 2026. Regulatory framing: EU AI Act / Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 high-risk providers must file technical documentation. Intro quotes Annex IV 2(b) “general logic”; 2(e) “assessment of technical measures needed to facilitate interpretation”; Article 86(1) right to “clear and meaningful explanations…” for certain automated decisions. Quotes from consolidated text as amended by Regulation (EU) 2026/1744, CELEX 02024R1689-20260727, read 11 Aug 2026. Premise/RQ: audit value requires two analysts to reach compatible conclusions. Mechanistic interpretability/circuit discovery candidate technical content for filings. Tests whether evidence survives “two competent analysts, same system, same tool, different defensible settings.” Pre-registered multiverse/crossed grid over analytic axes; formalism defines eight choices: objective, ablation, corruption distribution, metric, threshold, prompt variant, seed, granularity. Scope/model/task: GPT-2 small on IOI; no scale claims. Edge count enables size-matched random baseline. Grid/method: Sec 6 says seven objectives, seven ablations, four corruption distributions nested within five ablations, four metrics, three thresholds, two prompt variants, five seeds. 1,540 discovery cells and 18,480 specifications pre-registered; one objective failed (all 220 cells runtime error from MSE against integral target in library code), not repaired. Realised grid: six objectives, 1,320 cells, 15,840 specifications. Discovery uses edge attribution patching/integrated edge gradients in Miller et al. library; lineage Conmy et al.; corruption levels from Wang et al. Discussion reiterates one of seven documented/publicly exported objectives does not run on library canonical task; reported as discard/rate and tooling-maturity observation, not headline or library criticism. Pre-reg/stats: plan tagged before confirmatory sweep; both abstracts drafted in advance; deviations append-only. No p-values across specs; specs are designed grid, not independent. Bootstrap resamples specifications (not pairs), B=10,000; F and J-bar are U-statistics over dependent pairs. Eq. 3 used for residual flip after standardising/holding axes or size. Reproducibility section: pre-registration timestamped commit tagged prereg-p1-confirmatory before sweep; all 1,320 cells ran under one verified environment; uploaded archive matched git tree 22/22 files; analysis layer no GPU. Verification script recomputes headline quantities from raw results: 36 checks, 0 failures; F derived three ways including brute force. Another script checks every numeric token matches stored results; tables emitted directly; test suite 343 tests. Exclusions/discards: threshold admits no circuit for 8,279/15,840 specs (52.3% discard), uneven by metric. Table 2: comprehensiveness kept 3,947 discarded 13 rate .003; KL kept 1,467 discarded 2,493 rate .630; logit diff kept 1,270 discarded 2,690 rate .679; sufficiency kept 877 discarded 3,083 rate .779. Total kept 7,561, discarded 8,279. Surviving pool 52% comprehensiveness vs 25% by design. Formalism/model graph: C(s)⊆E. GPT-2 small factorised graph with separate Q/K/V inputs, |E|=32,491. Circuits touch 144 attention heads and 12 MLPs=156. D=1−Jaccard; J-bar mean Jaccard similarity. Main results: 7,561 specs produced a claim. Exact pairs = 28,580,580. Table 3: P0 J-bar 0.1396 [0.1377,0.1418], premise holds; H2 F>0.20 lower CI above, F=0.7316 [0.7247,0.7380], confirmed; H3 “not separated from random null” rejected because separated/intervals disjoint; H4 F−(1−agreement)>0.10 result 0.3344 [0.3297,0.3394], supported. Claim flip across 73.16% pairs; modal share π*=0.4109. Not filable at tolerances requiring modal share .95, .90, .80. Circuit overlap: 3,218 distinct circuits among 7,561 specs. Pairwise D quantiles: 1% .196, 25% .788, median .960, 75% .998. Median pair shares 4% edges; only 1% pairs exceed Jaccard .8. Median circuit size 200; random line k/(2|E|−k)=.0031; observed mean overlap about 45× chance, but authors say still not much. Claim map/results: φ fixed pre-registration, deterministic code. Overseer addressee based on Annex IV 2(e), 3 and Art 14(4)(c), keyed on dominant layer band, size class, ranked input segment; affected based on Art 86(1), leads with input segment. Three granularities nested. Medium overseer nine classes Table 4 counts/shares: early distributed 3107 .4109; late sparse 2153 .2848; late moderate 657 .0869; late distributed 489 .0647; early sparse 477 .0631; middle moderate 283 .0374; middle sparse 269 .0356; middle distributed 90 .0119; early moderate 36 .0048. Aggregating over size: early 47.9%, late 43.6%, middle 8.5%; coarse overseer modal share .4788. Text says top two claims (early vs late) are contradictory, not emphases. All six addressee-granularity combos fail α=.20 filability (need π*≥.80): affected coarse 2 classes F .3950 π .7291; affected medium 4 F .6597 π .4875; affected fine 8 F .6744 π .4786; overseer coarse 3 F .5733 π .4788; overseer medium 9 F .7316 π .4109; overseer fine 12 F .7681 π .4109. Sensitivity/controls: Table 6 residual F standardising one axis: metric .5939 CI .5803-.6063 removes .1377; ablation .7014; objective .7018; threshold .7070; corruption .7092; prompt .7232; seed .7307 removes .0009. Text/discussion: metric biggest lever but not enough; no single knob, standardising one axis cannot solve problem. REML on log10 circuit size: 78.8% structural variance ablation-corruption interaction, 11.5% residual, 4.4% ablation, 4.1% threshold, 0.7% metric; metric largest driver of claim variance. Removing size from claim and holding size fixed gives F=.2706; size-fixed medium discovered F=.2746. Random baseline: pooled discovered less stable than size-matched random null, .7316 vs .6774, intervals disjoint; H3 rejected/separated. Authors do not treat pooled direction as finding due to size distribution. With size fixed ordering reverses: discovered .2746 vs null .4230 at medium granularity, and .2706 vs .3822 at coarse; discovered more stable than random but still not stable enough. Table 7 size rows sum to 7,561: 10 n2492 discovered F .4543 null .7331; 20 n489 F .3380 null .6622; 50 n519 F .4639 null .7310; 100 n242 F .5792 null .6584; 200 n199 F .5122 null .6366; 500 n236 F .4258 null .1421; 1000 n380 F .5133 null 0; 2000 n312 F .5714 null 0; 5000 n625 F 0 null 0; 10000 n2067 F 0 null 0. Null collapses to one class at/above 1000; discovered collapses at 5000 and 10000 (2692 specs no flips). Known possible error to watch: saying instability lives entirely below 2000 conflicts with 2000 row nonzero. Functional instability: per-example functional agreement .6028, instability .3972; gap to claim flip .3344 CI .3297-.3394 threshold .10, so H4 supported on pre-registered pooled quantity. Gap does not survive holding size fixed; fails 0.10 threshold at 6 of 10 sizes and is negative at 5. At both ends mechanisms differ more than filings; pooled H4 figure carried by 500–2,000 edge band alone. Agreement from per-example correct/incorrect verdicts using Bayat Makou et al. Cohen’s kappa .0146; raw agreement ~60% mostly due to both circuits being right about same fraction, not same examples. Kappa between .016 and .047 at every circuit size while raw agreement rises .52 to .92 tracking accuracy .51 to .95. Authors argue not behaviorally identical subgraphs. Known possible internal error from earlier: earlier text claimed six size-binning alternatives higher than committed F, but table shows four. Section 8 filability protocol: for a filed claim derived from a circuit, declare specification space S (analytic axes/defensible levels with citations); declare deterministic published-code claim map φ (not LLM); compute π*=max_c n_c/N over S and F by Eq. 2; claim filable at tolerance α iff π*≥1−α; report π*, F, discard rate per axis level, and within-group decomposition of any pooled statistic. Protocol says a filing unable to state π* is asserted, not audited; regulator need not decide which analytic choice is correct, only require declaration of space and agreement across it. Limitations: One model/task; larger models may change F. Second-model replication pre-registered but not run: 924-cell Pythia-160m grid, same task, identical axes except seed has 3 not 5 levels (matches 1540/5*3=924); criteria committed before running; second task designed/not run. Circuit size is outcome chosen by threshold and distorted F, null-comparison direction, and functional-gap sign; fixing size drops F from .7316 to .2746, larger reduction than standardising any pre-registered axis; authors say pooled stats should include within-size decomposition. Multiverse limited to implemented library, not full literature; optimal ablation defensible but absent, so authors call measured F a lower bound wrt full defensible choices. Discard rate high/uneven; fixed threshold, no repairs. Bootstrap invalid for one reported family where conditioning groups have only 2–5 specifications; retained self-pairs dominate, intervals unusable, reported as point estimates with diagnostic; no post hoc bias-corrected

Paper title: “Explanation Multiplicity: Circuit-Level Interpretability”; subtitle/claim: “Evidence Does Not Survive Defensible Analytic Variation.” Author Ajay Pravin Mahale, date 12 Aug 2026.

Abstract key claims to track:
- Context: EU AI Act requires providers of high-risk systems to file technical documentation describing how system reaches decisions. Mechanistic interpretability, especially circuit discovery, is framed as source of such evidence.
- Research question: whether evidence survives when “two competent analysts, the same system, the same tool, different defensible settings.”
- Design: pre-registered crossed grid of seven analytic axes; every level taken from a published implementation. Each discovered circuit mapped through a deterministic claim map to a structured Annex IV statement.
- Scope/model/task: GPT-2 small and indirect object identification (IOI) task. Study covers one model and one task; scaling untested.
- Main numbers: 15,840 pre-registered specifications; 7,561 produced a claim. Derived statement flips across 73.2% of specification pairs, 95% CI 0.725–0.738. Modal claim commands 41.1% of the space. Evidence fails a filability criterion at every plausibly acceptable conformity-assessment tolerance.
- Sensitivity/ablation claims: Standardising the single most influential choice, the evaluation metric, leaves flip rate 59.4%. Removing circuit size from the claim entirely and holding it fixed leaves 27.1% flip rate, 95% CI 0.255–0.286, still above pre-registered threshold.
- Circuit similarity/function claims: circuits underlying claims structurally near-disjoint, median pairwise Jaccard overlap 4%; functionally uncorrelated at Cohen’s kappa 0.015. Therefore instability is not just one mechanism described in different words.
- Protocol/contribution: gives filability criterion as standalone protocol.
- Additional reported issue: one of seven documented discovery objectives does not execute at all on the library’s own canonical task.

Related work / positioning:
- Non-identifiability: Méloux et al. [6] show unique explanations need not exist under MI criteria; this paper takes that premise and measures downstream filing cost.
- Faithfulness metric sensitivity: Miller et al. [8] found ablation-based faithfulness methods highly sensitive to design choices; this paper crosses seven axes and propagates to regulatory statements. - Structure versus function: Bayat Makou et al. [1] found structurally distinct circuits can implement same computation (“phantom specialisation”). [9] argue comparison across methods requires standardised evaluation, adjacent to this paper’s standardised-specification argument.

Two of this paper’s four evaluation metrics are sufficiency and comprehensiveness; this motivates reporting discard rate per metric rather than silently pooling.

Scope/model/task: GPT-2 small and indirect object identification (IOI) task. One model, one task; scaling untested. Section 3 reiterates “nothing at all about scale.”

grade.reason: Review item 2 directly challenges the planted claim about six alternatives raising F by citing Table 1 and showing only four alternatives have higher F, matching the planted-error explanation.

errors.claim: “A specification is s=(o,a,d,m,τ,P,r,g), respectively discovery objective, ablation operator, corruption distribution, evaluation metric, size threshold, prompt variant, seed, granularity. Every axis level comes from a published implementation...”
errors.evidence: Earlier notes record the paper’s related-work/method framing as: “this paper expands single-axis finding into ‘seven-axis regulatory propagation’; ... Need later design to have seven axes.”
errors.explanation: The formalism defines eight specification axes, not seven. Unless one listed element is not intended as an axis, this conflicts with the earlier claim that the design/propagation is seven-axis.

errors.claim: “Six alternatives exceed the committed result, including halving thresholds”
errors.evidence: Table 1 gives committed bins F=0.7316. Alternatives above this are: all thresholds ×0.5 = 0.7448, ×0.8 = 0.7435, ×0.9 = 0.7394, and deciles = 0.7719. The other listed alternatives are ≤0.7316: ×1.1 = 0.7289, ×1.25 = 0.7314, ×1.5 = 0.7308, ×2 = 0.7232, equal thirds = 0.7018, no size term = 0.5733.
errors.explanation: Only four listed alternatives exceed the committed result, not six.

errors.claim: “Across factor-four binnings | 0.70 to 0.77”
errors.evidence: The factor-four threshold binnings appear to be the threshold multipliers from ×0.5 through ×2, whose F values range from 0.7232 to 0.7448. The 0.70 and 0.77 endpoints correspond instead to equal thirds = 0.7018 and deciles = 0.7719, not threshold multipliers spanning a factor of four.
errors.explanation: The stated sensitivity range for factor-four binnings does not match the rows that constitute factor-four threshold binnings in the same table.

errors.claim: “Thus 2,692 of 7,561 specifications contribute no flips; instability lives entirely below 2,000 edges.”
errors.evidence: Table 7 reports for size 2,000: n=312, Discovered F=0.5714, Classes=3.
errors.explanation: A nonzero F with 3 classes at exactly 2,000 edges means instability is present at 2,000 edges, not entirely below 2,000 edges. The preceding sentence only says discovery collapses at 5,000 and 10,000, which is consistent with the table, but the “below 2,000” summary is not.

errors.claim: “Another checks every manuscript numeric token against stored-result derivations.”
errors.evidence: Earlier notes record numeric-token inconsistencies: “text said six alternative size binnings exceed committed F=.7316, but only four do” and “‘Across factor-four binnings 0.70 to 0.77’ conflicts with threshold ×0.5–×2 range .7232–.7448.”

Paper title: “Explanation Multiplicity: Circuit-Level Interpretability”. Main thesis: circuit-derived regulatory evidence fails Y3W across plausible tolerances; competent analysts using same model/tool get incompatible Annex IV/Art 86-style statements under defensible settings. Scope: one model/task only: Q7V GPT-2 small on Z4K IOI; no scale claim. Limitations explicitly say larger models may change F unpredictably. Unrun second-model plan M9B: Pythia-160m, same task, different architecture, 924-cell grid identical except 3 not 5 seed levels; replication/refutation criteria pre-fixed; second task designed but unrun.

Key formalism: specification s=(o,a,d,m,τ,P,r,g), 8 axes (conflicts with earlier “seven-axis” wording). Q7V graph |E|=32,491; components 144 heads + 12 MLPs. D=1-Jaccard; J-bar mean pairwise Jaccard. Claim instability F=1-[Σc nc(nc-1)]/[N(N-1)], pair-weighted; within-axis conditioning pair-weighted.

G7U claim maps deterministic, not LLM. D9P overseer: dominant layer band, size class, ranked input segment. L3X affected-person: input segment/right subject. Granularities E7R coarse, K8Z medium, V2H fine nested so refinement cannot contradict coarser.

Grid/method: 7 objectives, 7 operators, nested corruptions; metrics T9V/H2W/N6C/U4J; 3 thresholds, 2 prompts, 5 seeds. One objective failed as preregistered, leaving 1,320 discovery/confirmatory cells and 15,840 specs. No-circuit/discarded 8,279; kept 7,561. Metric kept/discarded: T9V 3,947/13; H2W 1,467/2,493; N6C 1,270/2,690; U4J 877/3,083. T9V 52% of kept despite 25% designed. High uneven discard rate acknowledged; retained metric imbalance is reported-set property, threshold fixed, no failed item repaired. C4Y optimal ablation is defensible but unsupported/excluded, so measured F lower bound relative to full literature. Discussion says failed objective is documented/publicly exported yet cannot execute on library’s canonical task; records tooling maturity, not headline/criticism of authors.

Y3W protocol: declare defensible analytic space S and deterministic published code φ; compute π*=max_c nc/N and F over S; pass α iff π*≥1−α; report π*, F, discard rate per axis level, and within-group decomposition of every pooled statistic. Filing unable to state π* is asserted not audited. Bootstrap resamples specs, not pairs; intervals conditional on grid. Limitation: bootstrap invalid for one reported family where conditioning groups have only 2–5 specs and self-pairs dominate; unusable intervals replaced by point estimates/diagnostics; no bias-corrected estimator after naive intervals disagreed.

Earlier internal errors noted: (1) text said six alternative size binnings exceed committed F=.7316, but only four do; (2) “Across factor-four binnings 0.70 to 0.77” conflicts with threshold ×0.5–×2 range .7232–.7448; (3) “instability lives entirely below 2,000 edges” conflicts with Table 7 showing size 2,000 discovered F=.5714 with 3 classes. Current reproducibility section’s broad claims that every numeric token is checked and 36 checks have 0 failures conflict with these recorded internal numeric/result inconsistencies if those manuscript claims are included.

Registered results: J6D J-bar=.1396 [0.1377,.1418]. X4R F=.7316 [.7247,.7380]. Q2F random-comparison rejected. Z8N functional-gap supported pooled: F-(1-agreement)=.3344 [.3297,.3394]. Intro says decision rules fixed/tagged before sweep; two outcomes need within-size qualifications.

Structural: kept specs 7,561; distinct circuits 3,218; spec pairs 28,580,580. D quantiles: 1%=.196, 25%=.788, median=.960, 75%=.998. Median shared-edge fraction 4%; only 1% pairs Jaccard>0.8. Median circuit size 200. Random line k/(2|E|-k); median size .0031; observed/chance overlap ~45×. Expected random overlap for 500-edge circuit .008.

Claim Table 4 D9P/K8Z counts/shares: early distributed 3107/.4109; late sparse 2153/.2848; late moderate 657/.0869; late distributed 489/.0647; early sparse 477/.0631; middle moderate 283/.0374; middle sparse 269/.0356; middle distributed 90/.0119; early moderate 36/.0048. Pair disagreement 73.2%, CI .725–.738. Modal share .411; required .95/.90/.80. Aggregated early/late/middle 47.9%/43.6%/8.5%.

Table 5 all addressee/granularity fail α=.20. L3X: E7R F=.3950 π*=.7291; K8Z F=.6597 π*=.4875; V2H F=.6744 π*=.4786. D9P: E7R F=.5733 π*=.4788; K8Z F=.7316 π*=.4109; V2H F=.7681 π*=.4109.

Table 6 residual F after standardising: metric .5939; ablation .7014; objective .7018; threshold .7070; corruption .7092; prompt .7232; seed .7307. Discussion says complete metric standardisation exceeds what conformity procedure could demand, no single knob suffices, and declaring resolution after standardising one axis would be mistaken. Conditioning on circuit size reduces F more than standardising any registered axis; limitations say threshold-selected size distorts F, null-comparison direction, functional-gap sign, and every pooled statistic has within-size decomposition. Max pressure size-free/fixed-size dominant-layer F=.2706 [.2550,.2859]. Random baseline: pooled discovered .7316 vs A6N .6774; fixed-size K8Z .2746 vs .4230; fixed-size E7R .2706 vs .3822. Table 7 size F includes 2000: .5714/3 classes; 5000 and 10000 F=0. Functional: pooled agreement .6028; instability .3972; kappa .0146; size-conditioned gaps vary, pooled gap carried by 500–2,000 edges. Discussion: interpretability evidence not worthless; evidentiary weight measurable rather than presumed and cheap relative to circuit-producing sweep.

Reproducibility section: public timestamped commit tagged prereg-p1-confirmatory; one environment across all 1,320 confirmatory cells; archive/git comparison 22/22 files identical; no GPU needed. Script recomputes headline quantities and asserts reported values: 36 checks, 0 failures, F through three routes including brute-force pairs. Another script allegedly checks every manuscript numeric token against stored-result derivations. Tables emitted directly; suite has 343 tests.

final_notes:
Paper title: “Explanation Multiplicity: Circuit-Level Interpretability”. Main claim: evidence does not survive defensible analytic variation; regulatory circuit evidence fails Y3W across plausible conformity-assessment tolerances; competent analysts get incompatible statements under defensible settings; standardisation/size controls do not remove failure; structural/functional disagreement rule out “same mechanism reworded”; no scale claim beyond tested model/task. Discussion adds: standardising one axis, even metric standardisation, is not enough; failed objective/tooling maturity is documented but not headline or author criticism; interpretability evidence can have measurable evidentiary weight.

Internal errors found: (1) §2 said “seven-axis regulatory propagation,” but §4 formalism defines 8 axes s=(o,a,d,m,τ,P,r,g). (2) Part 5 sensitivity row says “Across factor-four binnings: 0.70 to 0.77,” but threshold ×0.5–×2 range is .7232–.7448; .7018/.7719 are equal-thirds/deciles, not factor-four threshold binnings. (3) §7.5 says “2,792 of 7,561 specifications contribute no flips,” but Table 7 no-flip discovered rows are 5,000 n=625 and 10,000 n=2,067, totaling 2,692. (4) §7.5 says “instability lives entirely below 2,000 edges,” but Table 7 has size 2,000: n=312, Discovered F=.5714, Classes=3. (5) §11 says every manuscript numeric token is checked against stored-result derivations, conflicting with the above manuscript numeric inconsistencies.

Definitions/formalism: Q7V factorised graph |E|=32,491; 144 attention heads + 12 MLPs = 156 components. D=1-|Ci∩Cj|/|Ci∪Cj|; J-bar mean Jaccard. F=1-[Σc nc(nc-1)]/[N(N-1)]. Paper title: “Explanation Multiplicity: Circuit-Level Interpretability — Evidence Does Not Survive Defensible Analytic Variation” by Ajay Pravin Mahale, dated 12 Aug 2026.

Core claims/results:
- EU AI Act high-risk systems require technical documentation explaining decision logic; circuit discovery considered possible evidence source.
- RQ: whether circuit-discovery evidence survives variation between two competent analysts using same system/tool but different defensible settings.
- Setting: GPT-2 small, IOI task; no scale claim. Factorised graph with separate Q/K/V inputs has |E|=32,491; components 144 attention heads + 12 MLPs = 156.
- Main result: overseer MEDIUM claim flip rate F=0.7316, CI 0.7247–0.7380; modal share π*=0.4109. Filable at tolerance α iff π* ≥ 1−α; fails α=.05,.10,.20.
- Table 6/Sec.10: standardising evaluation metric leaves residual F=0.5939 [0.5803,0.6063], removes 0.1377 of 0.7316; no single axis solves problem. Earlier text/notes said standardising evaluation metric leaves flip rate 49.4%: internal conflict if that earlier claim appears in final text.
- Maximum pressure/no-size claim + size fixed: F=0.2706 [0.2550,0.2859], still above prereg threshold; Section 7 fixed-size medium discovered F=0.2746 vs size-matched random null 0.4230. Section 9 says fixing size drops F from 0.7316 to 0.2746.
- Size-bin sensitivity Table 1: committed bins 0.7316; thresholds ×0.5 0.7448; ×0.8 0.7435; ×0.9 0.7394; ×1.1 0.7289; ×1.25 0.7314; ×1.5 0.7308; ×2 0.7232; equal thirds 0.7018; deciles 0.7719; no size term/COARSE 0.5733.
- Circuits structurally near-disjoint but above random: P0 mean Jbar=0.1396 [0.1377,0.1418] over 28,580,580 pairs; 7,561 specs, 3,218 distinct circuits. Pairwise D quantiles: 1%=0.196, 25%=0.788, median=0.960, 75%=0.998; median Jaccard 4%; only 1% pairs J>0.8. Median circuit size 200; random line k/(2|E|-k)=0.0031, observed overlap about 45× chance.
- Functionally uncorrelated: Cohen’s κ≈0.0146/0.015. Functional agreement 0.6028, instability 0.3972; H4 gap to claim flip rate 0.3344 [0.3297,0.3394]. Kappa 0.016–0.047 at every circuit size while raw agreement climbs 0.52–0.92, accuracy 0.51–0.95.
- H4 supported only on pre-registered pooled quantity. Gap does not survive holding size fixed: fails 0.10 threshold at 6/10 sizes, negative at 5; pooled figure carried by 500–2,000 edge band alone.
- Random seeds select sampled prompts/evaluation-set variability, not nondeterminism.

Formalism/protocol:
- Specification tuple earlier defined as s=(o,a,d,m,τ,P,r,g): objective, ablation, corruption, metric, threshold, prompt, seed, granularity. Recurring inconsistency: paper also says “7 axes.”
- Circuit C(s)⊆E. Instability D=1−Jaccard. Claim instability φ maps circuit to structured Annex IV statement. Flip rate F=1−Σc nc(nc−1)/[N(N−1)]. Ceiling with nine observed classes 0.8889; observed 0.7316 is 82.3% of ceiling.
- φ fixed/pre-registered, deterministic, published, not LLM-generated. Overseer claim keyed on dominant layer band, size class, ranked input segment; affected claim leads with input segment. Three granularities nested.
- Section 8 filability protocol: declare specification space S, deterministic claim map φ, compute π* and F; filable at α iff π*≥1−α; report π*, F, discard rate per axis level, and within-group decomposition.

Section 6 Method:
- Grid: 7 objectives, 7 ablation operators, 4 corruption distributions nested within 5 operators that read them, 4 metrics, 3 thresholds, 2 prompt variants, 5 seeds = 1,540 discovery cells and 18,480 specs “as pre-registered.” Earlier tuple included granularity; this grid omits it.
- Exclusion fixed before circuits: one objective fails in all 220 cells due to MSE against integral target in library code. Realised grid: 6 objectives, 1,320 cells, 15,840 specs.
- Threshold rule admits no circuit for 8,279/15,840 specs, discard 52.3%; surviving claims 7,561. Surviving pool 52% comprehensiveness vs 25% design.
- Table 2 metric discards: comprehensiveness kept 3,947 discarded 13; KL kept 1,467 discarded 2,493; logit diff kept 1,270 discarded 2,690; sufficiency kept 877 discarded 3,083.

Section 7:
- Table 3 prereg outcomes: P0 Jbar 0.1396 premise holds; H2 F>0.20 confirmed at 0.7316; H3 “not separated from random null” rejected because separated/disjoint intervals; H4 supported, value 0.3344 [0.3297,0.3394].
- Table 4 nine overseer MEDIUM counts/shares: early distributed 3107 .4109; late sparse 2153 .2848; late moderate 657 .0869; late distributed 489 .0647; early sparse 477 .0631; middle moderate 283 .0374; middle sparse 269 .0356; middle distributed 90 .0119; early moderate 36 .0048.
- Table 5: affected COARSE F .3950 π* .7291; affected MEDIUM F .6597 π* .4875; affected FINE F .6744 π* .4786; overseer COARSE F .5733 π* .4788; overseer MEDIUM F .7316 π* .4109; overseer FINE F .7681 π* .4109. All fail α=.20.
- Table 6 residual F by standardised axis: metric .5939; ablation .7014; objective .7018; threshold .7070; corruption .7092; prompt .7232; seed .7307. REML log10 size variance: ablation-corruption interaction 78.8%, residual 11.5%, ablation 4.4%, threshold 4.1%, metric 0.7%; metric largest driver of claim variance.
- Random baseline: pooled discovered less stable than size-matched random null: 0.7316 vs 0.6774; fixed-size ordering reverses: discovered 0.2746 vs null 0.4230 medium, 0.2706 vs 0.3822 coarse. Table 7 has nonzero F at 2,000 (0.5714) despite text saying instability entirely below 2,000 edges.

Section 9/10/legal:
- One model/task; second-model replication preregistered but not run: Pythia-160m, 924-cell grid, same task, seed 3 not 5 levels. Second task designed but not run.
- Circuit size is outcome chosen by threshold, not an axis; distorted F, null-comparison direction, and sign of functional gap. Authors say every pooled statistic reported with within-size decomposition.
- Multiverse limited to implemented library; optimal ablation omitted, so measured F called lower bound relative to full defensible field.
- Discard rate high/uneven; no failed item repaired.
- Bootstrap invalid for one reported family with conditioning groups only 2–5 specs; intervals unusable, point estimates only.
- Sec.10: regulator should infer not worthlessness, but measurable evidentiary weight; one of seven documented/publicly exported discovery objectives fails on canonical task, reported as tooling maturity observation.

Section 11 reproducibility:
- Pre-registration is timestamped commit tagged prereg-p1-confirmatory before confirmatory sweep. Every reported number traces to config, seed, environment fingerprint.
- Confirmatory sweep ran under single environment across all 1,320 cells, verified from archive; code commit recovered by content-addressed comparison, 22/22 files identical. Analysis layer runs without GPU.
- Verification script recomputes every headline quantity from raw results: 36 checks, 0 failures; F derived three ways incl. brute-force pairwise. Second script checks every numeric token matches stored result. Tables emitted directly from results. Test suite 343 tests.

Paper title: “Explanation Multiplicity: Circuit-Level Interpretability”. Subtitle/claim: “Evidence Does Not Survive Defensible Analytic Variation.” Ajay Pravin Mahale, 12 Aug 2026. Core claim: regulatory circuit evidence fails Y3W across plausible conformity-assessment tolerances; competent analysts using same system/tool get incompatible statements under defensible settings; standardisation/size controls do not remove failure; structural and functional disagreement rule out “same mechanism reworded”; beyond one model/task untested/no scale claim. Audit: “two auditors to reach same conclusion.” Legal basis: EU AI Act/Reg. 2024/1689 Annex IV 2(b),2(e), Art 86(1), amended by Reg. 2026/1744. No improved discovery method proposed.

Internal errors found: §2 says “seven-axis regulatory propagation,” but §4 formalism defines 8 axes s=(o,a,d,m,τ,P,r,g). Part 5 sensitivity row says “Across factor-four binnings: 0.70 to 0.77,” but threshold ×0.5–×2 range is .7232–.7448; .7018/.7719 are equal-thirds/deciles, not factor-four threshold binnings. §7.5 text says A6N degeneracy occurs above 1000, but table and next sentence show at/above 1000. §7.5 also says instability lives entirely below 2000 despite 2000 row F .5714. §11 says every manuscript numeric token is checked against stored-result derivations, conflicting with those manuscript numeric/range errors.

Formalism/Y3W: Q7V graph |E|=32,491; 144 attention heads + 12 MLPs =156 components. D=1-Jaccard; F=1-[Σc nc(nc-1)]/[N(N-1)], conditional F_within(G)=1-[ΣgΣc n_gc(n_gc-1)]/[Σg ng(ng-1)]. Y3W ceiling for 9 classes .8889; observed fraction 82.3%. Y3W protocol: declare defensible axes/levels; declare deterministic published φ, not LLM; compute π*=max_c n_c/N and F over S; pass at tolerance α iff π*≥1−α; report π*, F, discard rate by axis level, within-group decomposition. Filing unable to state own π* is asserted not audited.

Claim mapping: D9P overseer grounded Annex IV 2(e),3 and Art 14(4)(c), ordered by dominant layer band, size class, ranked input segment. L3X affected grounded Art 86(1), leads with input segment/right of decision subject. Resolutions E7R coarse, K8Z medium, V2H fine; refinement cannot contradict coarse. φ deterministic/preregistered/published code. Size bins committed on node-count curve.

Method: GPT-2 small/Q7V on IOI/Z4K. Grid: 7 objectives, 7 operators, corruption distributions nested in 5 operators, 4 metrics, 3 thresholds, 2 prompts, 5 seeds. Total discovery cells 1,540; one objective failed, realised 6 objectives, discovery cells 1,320, specs 15,840. Discarded 8,279; kept 7,561. Retention by metric: T9V 3,947 kept/13 discarded; H2W 1,467/2,493; N6C 1,270/2,690; U4J 877/3,083. Bootstrap resamples specs B=10,000; intervals condition on grid.

Registered outcomes Table 3: J6D J-bar .1396 [.1377,.1418] premise holds; X4R F .7316 [.7247,.7380] confirmed; Q2F random-null separation rejected because separated/disjoint; Z8N gap .3344 [.3297,.3394] supported. Two outcomes need within-size qualifications.

Key results: 7,561 specs; 3,218 distinct circuits; all pairs 28,580,580. D quantiles 1% .196, 25% .788, median .960, 75% .998. Jaccard>0.8 only 1%; median circuit size 200; random overlap .0031; observed/chance ≈45×. D9P K8Z shares: modal early distributed .4109, second late sparse .2848; pair disagreement 73.2%; early/late/middle 47.9/43.6/8.5. All Table 5 addressee/resolution fail α=.20: L3X E7R F .3950 pi .7291; L3X K8Z .6597 pi .4875; L3X V2H .6744 pi .4786; D9P E7R .5733 pi .4788; D9P K8Z .7316 pi .4109; D9P V2H .7681 pi .4109.

Standardisation: fixing metric residual F .5939 removes .1377; ablation .7014 removes .0302; objective .7018; threshold .7070; corruption .7092; prompt .7232; seed .7307. REML structural variance: ablation-corruption interaction 78.8%, residual 11.5%, ablation 4.4%, threshold 4.1%, metric 0.7%. Metric-standardised disagreement 49.4%. Discussion §10 says complete metric standardisation exceeds what conformity procedure could demand; no single knob suffices; declaring resolution after one-axis standardisation would be substantially mistaken.

Size/threshold sensitivity Table 1: committed .7316; ×0.5 .7448; ×0.8 .7435; ×0.9 .7394; ×1.1 .7289; ×1.25 .7314; ×1.5 .7308; ×2 .7232; equal thirds .7018; deciles .7719; no size term/E7R .5733. Maximum pressure fixed size/size-free F .2706 CI .2550-.2859, abstract precision 27.1%, discussion 27%; dominant-layer still unstable. Random baseline: pooled discovered F .7316 vs A6N .6774; fixed size K8Z discovered .2746 vs A6N .4230; fixed size E7R .2706 vs A6N .3822. Table 7 size rows include 1000 and 2000 A6N .0000/c1, 5000/10000 both discovered and A6N .0000/c1.

Functional: pooled agreement .6028; instability .3972; smallest-circuit functional instability .4777; Cohen κ .0146 (abstract .015); raw agreement 60%; kappa by size .016-.047; raw agreement .52-.92; accuracy .51-.95; sizes failing gap threshold 6/10; sizes with negative gap 5; pooled gap carried by 500-2000 band. Z8N holds pooled, not size-conditioned.

Limitations (§9): one model/task; larger models may change F direction unclear. Timestamped unrun M9B Pythia-160m second-model plan: same task, different architecture, 924-cell grid identical except 3 not 5 seed levels, preregistered criteria; second task designed but unrun. Circuit size is outcome not axis; threshold-selected size distorts F, null-comparison direction, functional-gap sign; conditioning reduces instability more than registered-axis standardisation; every pooled statistic reported with within-size decomposition. Multiverse only as wide as library, not literature; unsupported C4Y optimal ablation never in instrument, so F lower bound vs field. Discard rate high/uneven; retained metric imbalance reported not adjusted; threshold fixed; no failed item repaired. Bootstrap invalid for one reported family: groups with 2–5 specs retain dominating self-pairs; unusable intervals replaced by point estimates/diagnostics; no bias-corrected estimator after naive intervals disagreed.

Discussion §10: failed objective is documented/publicly exported but cannot execute on the library’s own canonical task; its discard rate reflects tooling maturity below prospective regulatory evidence, but is neither headline nor criticism of authors requesting improvements. Regulator takeaway: interpretability evidence not worthless; evidentiary weight should be measured, cheaply relative to sweep producing circuit.

Reproducibility §11: public timestamped commit tagged prereg-p1-confirmatory; reported numbers trace to config/seed/environment fingerprint. Archive verification says one environment across all 1,320 confirmatory cells; code commit recovered, 22/22 files identical; analysis needs no GPU. One script recomputes headline quantities and asserts reported values: 36 checks, 0 failures, F via three routes including brute-force pairs. Another checks every manuscript numeric token against stored-result derivations. Tables emitted directly; suite has 343 tests.

errors.evidence: Earlier notes record numeric claims that conflict with the paper’s own tables/results: e.g. “Part 5 sensitivity row says ‘Across factor-four binnings: 0.70 to 0.77,’ but threshold ×0.5–×2 range is .7232–.7448; .7018/.7719 are equal-thirds/deciles, not factor-four threshold binnings.” Also §7.5 text says A6N degeneracy occurs “above 1000,” while the table and next sentence show at/above 1000.
errors.explanation: If every manuscript numeric token were checked against stored-result derivations, these manuscript numeric/range statements should not disagree with the stored/table-derived values. grade.reason: None of the reviewer's reported errors mention the metric-standardised percentage disagreement or the mismatch between the 49.4% claim and Table 6's 0.5939 (59.4%).

errors.claim: “A specification is a tuple of analytic choices $s=(o,a,d,m,\tau,P,r,g)$ ...”
errors.evidence: Earlier notes: “Pre-registered multiverse/crossed grid over seven analytic axes of circuit discovery.” The tuple in this part lists eight analytic choices: objective, ablation operator, corruption distribution, evaluation metric, size threshold, prompt variant, seed, and granularity.
errors.explanation: The paper previously described the design as crossing seven analytic axes, but the formal specification here defines eight analytic-choice axes. Unless one of these is not intended to count as an axis, the counts conflict.

errors.claim: “Seven discovery objectives, seven ablation operators, four corruption distributions nested within the five operators that read them, four metrics, three thresholds, two prompt variants, five seeds: 1,540 discovery cells and 18,480 specifications as pre-registered.”
errors.evidence: Earlier notes record: “Main numbers: 15,840 pre-registered specifications; 7,561 produced a claim.”
errors.explanation: This part says the pre-registered grid had 18,480 specifications, later reduced to a realised grid of 15,840 after one objective failed. errors.evidence: Table 7 reports for size 2,000: n = 312, Discovered F = 0.5714, Classes = 3.
errors.explanation: If the 2,000-edge bin has nonzero discovered flip rate and three claim classes, instability does not live entirely below 2,000 edges. It lives below 5,000 edges, or at and below 2,000 edges.

Paper title: “Explanation Multiplicity: Circuit-Level Interpretability”; claim: “Evidence Does Not Survive Defensible Analytic Variation.” Author Ajay Pravin Mahale, date 12 Aug 2026.

Regulatory framing: EU AI Act high-risk documentation. Annex IV 2(b) “general logic… algorithms”; 2(e) “technical measures needed to facilitate interpretation”; Article 86(1) right to “clear and meaningful explanations…” for certain automated decisions. Claim map: φ_overseer based on Annex IV 2(e), 3, Article 14(4)(c), keyed by dominant layer band, size class, ranked input segment; φ_affected based on Article 86(1), leading with input segment. Three nested granularities.

Premise/RQ: audit value requires two analysts to reach compatible conclusions. Tests whether mechanistic/circuit evidence survives “two competent analysts, same system, same tool, different defensible settings.” Scope: GPT-2 small and IOI only; no scaling claim. Graph separates Q/K/V inputs, |E|=32,491; circuits touch 144 attention heads and 12 MLPs=156 components.

Grid: seven objectives, seven ablations, four corruptions nested within five operators, four metrics, three thresholds, two prompts, five seeds. Pre-registered: 1,540 discovery cells / 18,480 specifications. One objective fails: all 220 cells runtime error from MSE against integral target; not repaired. Realised: six objectives, 1,320 cells / 15,840 specs. Thresholds fixed 6 Aug 2026 and not revisited.

Stats/protocol: no p-values across specs. Bootstrap resamples specifications, B=10,000; intervals quantify grid uncertainty only. F = 1 − [Σc nc(nc−1)]/[N(N−1)] = probability two draws without replacement differ. π*=modal share. Filable at tolerance α iff π*≥1−α. Nine-class ceiling F≤0.8889; observed 0.7316 =82.3% ceiling. Section 8 filability protocol: declare defensible S; deterministic published non-LLM claim map φ; compute π*, F; filable iff π*≥1−α; report π*, F, discard rate per axis level, within-group decomposition. Filing without π* “has not been audited.”

Main results: threshold admits no circuit for 8,279/15,840 specs (52.3% discarded), uneven by metric. Kept: comprehensiveness 3,947, KL 1,467, logit diff 1,270, sufficiency 877; total 7,561. Surviving pool 52% comprehensiveness vs 25% design.

Claim map fixed in pre-registration, deterministic code, published, not LLM-generated. Size bins from committed calibration rule. Size-binning sensitivity: committed F=.7316; ×0.5 .7448, ×0.8 .7435, ×0.9 .7394, ×1.1 .7289, ×1.25 .7314, ×1.5 .7308, ×2 .7232, equal thirds .7018, deciles .7719, no size/COARSE .5733.

Section 7/Table 3: P0 Jbar .1396 [.1377,.1418]. H2 F>0.20: .7316 [.7247,.7380], confirmed. H3 “not separated from random null”: rejected; separated. H4 F−(1−agreement)>0.10: .3344 [.3297,.3394], supported.

Jbar=.1396 over 28,580,580 pairs among 7,561 specs; 3,218 distinct circuits. D quantiles: 1% .196, 25% .788, median .960, 75% .998; median pair shares 4% edges; 1% pairs Jaccard >.8. Median circuit size 200; random line .0031; observed mean overlap ~45× chance.

F=.7316, π*=.4109; not filable at 0.95/0.90/0.80. Overseer MEDIUM nine classes: early/distributed 3,107 (.4109); late/sparse 2,153 (.2848); late/moderate 657; late/distributed 489; early/sparse 477; middle/moderate 283; middle/sparse 269; middle/distributed 90; early/moderate 36. Paper title: “Explanation Multiplicity: Circuit-Level Interpretability”; subtitle/claim: “Evidence Does Not Survive Defensible Analytic Variation.” Author Ajay Pravin Mahale, date 12 Aug 2026.

Abstract key claims to track:
- Context: EU AI Act requires providers of high-risk systems to file technical documentation describing how system reaches decisions. Mechanistic interpretability, especially circuit discovery, is framed as source of such evidence.
- Research question: whether evidence survives when “two competent analysts, the same system, the same tool, different defensible settings.”
- Design: pre-registered crossed grid of seven analytic axes; every level taken from a published implementation. Each discovered circuit mapped through a deterministic claim map to a structured Annex IV statement.
- Scope/model/task: GPT-2 small and indirect object identification (IOI) task. Study covers one model and one task; scaling untested.
- Main numbers: 15,840 pre-registered specifications; 7,561 produced a claim. Derived statement flips across 73.2% of specification pairs, 95% CI 0.725–0.738. Modal claim commands 41.1% of the space. Evidence fails a filability criterion at every plausibly acceptable conformity-assessment tolerance.
- Sensitivity/ablation claims: Standardising the single most influential choice, the evaluation metric, leaves flip rate 59.4%. Removing circuit size from the claim entirely and holding it fixed leaves 27.1% flip rate, 95% CI 0.255–0.286, still above pre-registered threshold.
- Circuit similarity/function claims: circuits underlying claims structurally near-disjoint, median pairwise Jaccard overlap 4%; functionally uncorrelated at Cohen’s kappa 0.015. Therefore instability is not just one mechanism described in different words.
- Protocol/contribution: gives filability criterion as standalone protocol.
- Additional reported issue: one of seven documented discovery objectives does not execute at all on the library’s own canonical task.

Paper title: “Explanation Multiplicity: Circuit-Level Interpretability”. Subtitle/claim: “Evidence Does Not Survive Defensible Analytic Variation.” Author Ajay Pravin Mahale, dated 12 Aug 2026.

Key claims: regulatory circuit evidence fails Y3W throughout plausible conformity-assessment tolerances; competent analysts using same system/tool get incompatible statements under defensible settings; standardisation and size controls do not remove failure; structural and functional disagreement rule out “same mechanism reworded”; beyond one model/task untested/no scale claim. Legal basis: EU AI Act/Reg. 2024/1689 Annex IV 2(b), 2(e), Art 86(1), amended by Reg. 2026/1744. No improved discovery method proposed. Discussion says interpretability evidence is not worthless; evidentiary weight is measurable and cheap relative to sweep producing circuit.

Found inconsistencies: §2 said “seven-axis regulatory propagation,” but §4 formalism defines 8 axes: s=(o,a,d,m,τ,P,r,g). Part 5 sensitivity row says “Across factor-four binnings: 0.70 to 0.77,” but threshold ×0.5–×2 range is .7232–.7448; .7018/.7719 are equal-thirds/deciles, not factor-four threshold binnings. Part 9 says “instability lives entirely below 2,000 edges,” but Table 7 has size 2,000 with discovered F=.5714 and 3 classes. §11 says verification establishes one environment across all 1,540 confirmatory cells, conflicting with earlier statement that one objective failed and only 1,320 cells were realised.

Formalism: Q7V factorised graph |E|=32,491; 144 attention heads + 12 MLPs = 156 components. D=1-Jaccard; J-bar mean Jaccard. F=1-[Σc nc(nc-1)]/[N(N-1)]. Conditional F_within(G)=1-[ΣgΣc n_gc(n_gc-1)]/[Σg ng(ng-1)]. Y3W ceiling for 9 classes .8889; observed fraction 82.3%.

Y3W protocol: For circuit-derived filed claim c, declare S, deterministic φ, compute π*=max_c n_c/N over S and F, pass at tolerance α iff π*≥1−α, report π*, F, discard rate per axis level, and within-group decomposition of every pooled statistic. Filing unable to state π* is asserted, not audited.

Claim mapping: D9P overseer grounded Annex IV 2(e), 3 and Art 14(4)(c), ordered by dominant layer band, size class, ranked input segment. L3X affected grounded Art 86(1), leads with input segment/right of decision subject. Resolutions E7R/K8Z/V2H COARSE/MEDIUM/FINE designed so refinement cannot contradict coarser statement. Size bins committed on measured node-count curve. Table 1 F values include committed .7316; no size term/E7R .5733; threshold variants .7232–.7448; equal thirds .7018; deciles .7719.

Method: Q7V=GPT-2 small; Z4K=IOI. Grid: 7 objectives, 7 operators, 4 corruption distributions nested within 5 operators, 4 metrics, 3 thresholds, 2 prompts, 5 seeds. Per objective 22 operator/corruption combos; total discovery cells 1,540; specs 18,480. One objective failed due to MSE/integral target runtime error; realised objectives 6, cells 1,320, specs 15,840. Discarded 8,279 (52.3%); kept 7,561. Metric retention: T9V 3,947 kept, H2W 1,467, N6C 1,270, U4J 877. Bootstrap resamples specifications, B=10,000; no spec-level p-values; intervals condition on grid.

Structural results: 7,561 claim specs; 3,218 distinct circuits; all pairs 28,580,580. D quantiles: 1% .196, 25% .788, median .960, 75% .998. Median shared-edge fraction 4%; pairs Jaccard>0.8 only 1%; median size 200 edges. Random overlap at median size .0031; observed/chance ~45×.
