Pair disagreement 73.2%; CI .725–.738; required .95/.90/.80 fail; size-aggregated early/late/middle 47.9/43.6/8.5. Table 5 all addressee/resolution at α=.20 fail: L3X E7R F .3950 pi .7291; L3X K8Z .6597 pi .4875; L3X V2H .6744 pi .4786; D9P E7R .5733 pi .4788; D9P K8Z .7316 pi .4109; D9P V2H .7681 pi .4109.

Standardisation: residual F/removes: metric .5939/.1377; ablation .7014/.0302; objective .7018/.0298; threshold .7070/.0246; corruption .7092/.0224; prompt .7232/.0084; seed .7307/.0009. REML log10 size: ablation-corruption interaction 78.8%, residual 11.5, ablation 4.4, threshold 4.1, metric .7. Metric-standardised disagreement 59.4%.

Size/null/functional: size-free fixed size F=.2706 CI .2550-.2859, still above threshold. Pooled discovered F .7316 vs A6N .6774; fixed-size reverses: K8Z discovered .2746 vs A6N .4230, E7R .2706 vs A6N .3822. Table 7 includes size 2000 discovered F .5714; sizes 5000/10000 F=0. errors.claim: “Archive verification establishes one environment across all 1,540 confirmatory cells.”
errors.evidence: Earlier methods state: “One objective failed due to MSE/integral target runtime error; realised objectives 6, cells 1,320, specs 15,840.”
errors.explanation: The paper previously says only 1,320 cells were realised because one of seven objectives failed. Describing verification across all 1,540 confirmatory cells conflicts with the earlier realised-cell count unless the failed cells are not meant as realised confirmatory cells.

grade.reason: Yes — the reviewer flags the reproducibility claim that verification covered 1,540 confirmatory cells and cites the paper's earlier statement that one objective failed, leaving only 1,320 realised confirmatory cells, which contradicts the planted claim.

errors.claim: “A specification is a tuple of analytic choices $s=(o,a,d,m,\tau,P,r,g)$ ...”
errors.evidence: Earlier notes: “Pre-registered multiverse/crossed grid over seven analytic axes of circuit discovery.” The tuple in this part lists eight analytic choices: objective, ablation operator, corruption distribution, evaluation metric, size threshold, prompt variant, seed, and granularity.
errors.explanation: The paper previously described the design as crossing seven analytic axes, but the formal specification here defines eight analytic-choice axes. Unless one of these is not intended to count as an axis, the counts conflict.

errors.claim: “Seven discovery objectives, seven ablation operators, four corruption distributions nested within the five operators that read them, four metrics, three thresholds, two prompt variants, five seeds: 1,540 discovery cells and 18,480 specifications as pre-registered.”
errors.evidence: Earlier notes record: “Main numbers: 15,840 pre-registered specifications; 7,561 produced a claim.”
errors.explanation: This part says the pre-registered grid had 18,480 specifications, later reduced to a realised grid of 15,840 after one objective failed. Earlier parts characterized 15,840 itself as the pre-registered specification count, which conflicts with the current distinction between pre-registered and realised specifications.

errors.claim: “The discovered multiverse also collapses at 5,000 and 10,000 edges, so 2,692 of 7,561 specifications contribute no flips at all and the instability lives entirely below 2,000 edges.”
errors.evidence: Table 7 reports for size 2,000: n = 312, Discovered F = 0.5714, Classes = 3.
errors.explanation: If the 2,000-edge bin has nonzero discovered flip rate and three claim classes, instability does not live entirely below 2,000 edges. It lives below 5,000 edges, or at and below 2,000 edges.

errors.claim: “Coarse overseer filings are more stable than coarse affected-person filings.”
errors.evidence: Earlier Table 5 notes: “affected COARSE F=.3950 π*=.7291; … overseer COARSE .5733 π*=.4788.” Filability/stability protocol defines filable by higher modal share: “filable at tolerance α iff π* ≥ 1−α,” and F is probability two draws differ, so lower F is more stable.
errors.explanation: By the paper’s own stability measures, coarse affected-person claims are more stable than coarse overseer claims: affected COARSE has higher π* and lower F. The current sentence reverses that comparison.

Paper title: “Explanation Multiplicity: Circuit-Level Interpretability”; subtitle/claim: “Evidence Does Not Survive Defensible Analytic Variation.” Author Ajay Pravin Mahale, 12 Aug 2026.

Regulatory framing: EU AI Act / Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 high-risk providers technical documentation. Intro quotes Annex IV 2(b) “general logic...algorithms”; 2(e) “assessment of technical measures needed to facilitate interpretation”; Article 86(1) right to “clear and meaningful explanations…” for certain automated decisions. Consolidated text as amended by Regulation (EU) 2026/1744, CELEX 02024R1689-20260727, read 11 Aug 2026. Claim map: φ_overseer keyed by dominant layer band, size class, ranked input segment; φ_affected leads with input segment. Three nested granularities.

Premise/RQ: audit value requires two auditors/analysts to reach compatible/same conclusions; test if evidence survives when “two competent analysts, same system, same tool, different defensible settings.” Scope GPT-2 small and IOI only; no scaling claim. Graph separate Q/K/V inputs, |E|=32,491. Circuits touch 144 attention heads + 12 MLPs = 156 total. Instability D=1−|Ci∩Cj|/|Ci∪Cj|; J-bar mean Jaccard.

Grid: seven objectives, seven ablations, four corruptions nested in five operators, four metrics, three thresholds, two prompts, five seeds. States 1,540 discovery cells and 18,480 specs pre-registered; one objective fails: all 220 cells runtime error from MSE against integral target; exactly that arm by digest, not repaired. Realised grid six objectives, 1,320 cells, 15,840 specs. Beware if later calls “15,840 pre-registered specs.” Pre-registration/tag before confirmatory sweep; both abstracts drafted in advance; deviations append-only. Thresholds fixed 6 Aug 2026 and not revisited.

Stats: no p-values across specs. Bootstrap resamples specifications, not pairs, B=10,000; intervals grid uncertainty only. F = 1 − [Σc nc(nc−1)]/[N(N−1)], unbiased Gini–Simpson / probability two draws without replacement differ; modal share π*=maxc nc/N. Filable at tolerance α iff π* ≥ 1−α. With nine classes ceiling F≤0.8889; observed 0.7316 is 82.3% ceiling.

Main results: threshold rule admits no circuit for 8,279/15,840 realised specs (52.3% discarded), uneven by metric. Kept totals: comprehensiveness 3,947, KL 1,467, logit diff 1,270, sufficiency 877; kept total 7,561. Discarded: 13, 2,493, 2,690, 3,083. Surviving pool 52% comprehensiveness vs 25% design.

Claim map fixed in pre-registration, deterministic code, published, not LLM-generated. Size bins from committed calibration rule. Size-binning sensitivity: committed F=.7316; ×0.5 .7448, ×0.8 .7435, ×0.9 .7394, ×1.1 .7289, ×1.25 .7314, ×1.5 .7308, ×2 .7232, equal thirds .7018, deciles .7719, no size term/COARSE .5733.

Section 7/Table 3: P0 Jbar .1396 [.1377,.1418]. H2 F>0.20: .7316 [.7247,.7380], confirmed. H3 “not separated from random null”: rejected; separated. H4 F−(1−agreement)>0.10: .3344 [.3297,.3394], supported.

7.1: Jbar=.1396 exact over 28,580,580 pairs among 7,561 specs; 3,218 distinct circuits. Pairwise D quantiles: 1% .196, 25% .788, median .960, 75% .998; median pair shares 4% edges; only 1% pairs have Jaccard >.8. Median circuit size 200; random line k/(2|E|−k)=.0031; observed mean overlap ~45× chance.

7.2: F=.7316, π*=.4109; not filable at .95/.90/.80. Table 4 overseer MEDIUM nine classes: early/distributed 3,107 (.4109); late/sparse 2,153 (.2848); late/moderate 657; late/distributed 489; early/sparse 477; middle/moderate 283; middle/sparse 269; middle/distributed 90; early/moderate 36. Aggregated layer: early 47.9% / COARSE modal .4788, late 43.6%, middle 8.5%; top two claims early vs late contradict.

Table 5 all addressee-granularity combos fail filability at α=.20: affected COARSE F=.3950 π*=.7291; affected MEDIUM .6597 π*=.4875; affected FINE .6744 π*=.4786; overseer COARSE .5733 π*=.4788; overseer MEDIUM .7316 π*=.4109; overseer FINE .7681 π*=.4109. Therefore affected COARSE is more stable than overseer COARSE by both higher π* and lower F; Section 8 says reverse = internal error.

Table 6: standardising axes residual F/removes: metric .5939/.1377; ablation .7014/.0302; objective .7018/.0298; threshold .7070/.0246; corruption .7092/.0224; prompt .7232/.0084; seed .7307/.0009. Metric largest but insufficient. REML log10 selected circuit size: ablation-corruption interaction 78.8%, residual 11.5%, ablation 4.4%, threshold 4.1%, metric 0.7%; structural and claim axes differ. Max pressure: remove circuit size, dominant layer only, hold size fixed: F=.2706 [.2550,.2859], above prereg threshold.

Random baseline: pooled discovered less stable than size-matched random null: .7316 vs .6774, intervals disjoint; H3 rejected. Direction not reported due size artefact. Holding size fixed reverses: discovered .2746 vs null .4230 medium; .2706 vs .3822 coarse. Table 7 medium by size includes 2000 n312 F=.5714; earlier text says instability lives entirely below 2,000 edges, conflicting with this row.

Functional agreement: per-example agreement .6028; functional instability .3972; gap to claim flip rate .3344 [.3297,.3394] vs threshold .10. Cohen’s κ .0146; raw 60% agreement mostly both-right fraction, not same examples. κ .016–.047 at every size while raw agreement climbs .52 to .92, tracking accuracy .51 to .95. H4 supported pooled, but gap fails holding size fixed at 6/10 sizes and negative at 5; mechanisms differ more than filings at both ends; pooled carried by 500–2,000 edge band.

Section 8 protocol: for a filed claim, declare specification space S and defensible levels with citations; deterministic published claim map φ, not LLM; compute π* and F; filable iff π* ≥ 1−α; report π*, F, discard rate per axis level, and within-group decomposition. Regulator need not adjudicate correct analytic choice.

Section 9 limitations: one model/task; larger models may change F unpredictably. Second-model replication pre-registered but not run: 924-cell Pythia-160m grid, same task, seed 3 not 5; to report in revision. Second task designed not run. Circuit size is threshold-selected outcome, not axis; distorted pooled F, null direction, functional gap sign; fixing size drops F .7316 to .2746. Multiverse limited to implemented library; absent optimal ablation means measured F lower bound relative to full field choices. Discard rate high/uneven. Bootstrap invalid for small conditioning groups (2–5 specs); point estimates with diagnostic only.

Section 10 discussion: standardising one axis buys less than appears; metric biggest lever removes .1377 of .7316 flip rate, no single knob solves. One of seven documented publicly exported discovery objectives does not run on library canonical task; reported as discard and tooling-maturity observation, not headline or library criticism. Regulator takeaway: interpretability evidence not worthless; evidentiary weight is measurable and cheap relative to producing circuit sweep.

Section 11 reproducibility: preregistration is timestamped commit tagged prereg-p1-confirmatory before confirmatory sweep. Reported numbers trace to config, seed, environment fingerprint. Confirmatory sweep ran under one environment across all 1,320 realised cells; archive verified, code commit recovered by content-addressed comparison, 22/22 files identical. Analysis layer no GPU. Verification script recomputes headline quantities: 36 checks, 0 failures; F derived three ways including brute-force pairwise. Second script checks numeric tokens against stored results. Tables emitted directly from results. Test suite 343 tests.

Paper title: “Explanation Multiplicity: Circuit-Level Interpretability”; subtitle/claim: “Evidence Does Not Survive Defensible Analytic Variation.” Author Ajay Pravin Mahale, date 12 Aug 2026.

Abstract key claims to track:
- Context: EU AI Act requires providers of high-risk systems to file technical documentation describing how system reaches decisions. Mechanistic interpretability, especially circuit discovery, is framed as source of such evidence.
- Research question: whether evidence survives when “two competent analysts, the same system, the same tool, different defensible settings.”
- Design: pre-registered crossed grid of seven analytic axes; every level taken from a published implementation. Each discovered circuit mapped through a deterministic claim map to a structured Annex IV statement.
- Scope/model/task: GPT-2 small and indirect object identification (IOI) task. Study covers one model and one task; scaling untested.

grade.reason: Review item 5 identifies the exact planted claim and shows Table 5’s values (overseer F higher, π* lower) contradict the paper’s statement, demonstrating the claim is reversed.

errors.claim: “A specification is s=(o,a,d,m,τ,P,r,g), respectively discovery objective, ablation operator, corruption distribution, evaluation metric, size threshold, prompt variant, seed, granularity. Every axis level comes from a published implementation...”
errors.evidence: Earlier notes record the paper’s related-work/method framing as: “this paper expands single-axis finding into ‘seven-axis regulatory propagation’; ... Need later design to have seven axes.”
errors.explanation: The formalism defines eight specification axes, not seven. Unless one listed element is not intended as an axis, this conflicts with the earlier claim that the design/propagation is seven-axis.

errors.claim: “Across factor-four binnings | 0.70 to 0.77”
errors.evidence: The factor-four threshold binnings shown are all thresholds ×0.5 through ×2, with F values 0.7448, 0.7435, 0.7394, 0.7289, 0.7314, 0.7308, and 0.7232.
errors.explanation: Those rows range from 0.7232 to 0.7448, not 0.70 to 0.77. The 0.70 and 0.77 endpoints appear to come from “equal thirds” and “deciles,” which are not factor-four threshold binnings.

errors.claim: “Thus 2,692 of 7,561 specifications contribute no flips; instability lives entirely below 2,000 edges.”
errors.evidence: Table 7 reports at size 2,000: n = 312, Discovered F = 0.5714, Classes = 3.
errors.explanation: A nonzero F with three classes at exactly 2,000 edges means there are flips/instability at 2,000 edges, not entirely below 2,000 edges. The statement would only fit “at or below 2,000” or “below 5,000.”

errors.claim: “E7R D9P filings are more stable than E7R L3X filings: a measurable advantage.”
errors.evidence: Earlier Table 5 notes: “L3X E7R F .3950 pi .7291; ... D9P E7R .5733 pi .4788.” Under §8, evidence passes/stability is based on higher \(\pi^*\) and lower disagreement \(F\).
errors.explanation: The recorded results show E7R L3X has higher majority share and lower pair disagreement than E7R D9P, so L3X is more stable, not D9P.

Paper title: “Explanation Multiplicity: Circuit-Level Interpretability”. Subtitle/claim: “Evidence Does Not Survive Defensible Analytic Variation.” Author Ajay Pravin Mahale, dated 12 Aug 2026.

Main claims: regulatory circuit evidence fails Y3W throughout plausible conformity-assessment tolerances; competent analysts using same system/tool get incompatible statements under defensible settings; standardisation and size controls do not remove failure; structural and functional disagreement rule out “same mechanism reworded”; beyond one model/task untested/no scale claim. Audit commissioning uses “two auditors to reach same conclusion” meaning. Legal basis: EU AI Act/Reg. 2024/1689 Annex IV 2(b), 2(e), Art 86(1), amended by Reg. 2026/1744. No improved discovery method proposed. Discussion §10 says one-axis standardisation insufficient; full metric standardisation exceeds plausible conformity demands; failed objective/discard rate indicate tooling maturity limits but are not headline or author criticism; interpretability evidence not worthless and evidentiary weight is measurable.

Found internal inconsistencies: (1) §2 said “seven-axis regulatory propagation,” but §4 formalism defines 8 axes: s=(o,a,d,m,τ,P,r,g). (2) Part 5 sensitivity row says “Across factor-four binnings: 0.70 to 0.77,” but threshold ×0.5–×2 range is .7232–.7448; .7018/.7719 are equal-thirds/deciles, not factor-four threshold binnings. (3) Part 9 says “instability lives entirely below 2,000 edges,” but Table 7 has size 2,000 with discovered F=.5714 and 3 classes. (4) §8 says “E7R D9P filings are more stable than E7R L3X filings,” but Table 5 shows L3X E7R F=.3950, pi*=.7291 vs D9P E7R F=.5733, pi*=.4788, so D9P is less stable.

Definitions/formalism: Q7V factorised graph |E|=32,491; 144 attention heads + 12 MLPs = 156 components. D=1-|Ci∩Cj|/|Ci∪Cj|; J-bar mean Jaccard. F=1-[Σc nc(nc-1)]/[N(N-1)] unbiased pair disagreement. Conditional F_within(G)=1-[ΣgΣc n_gc(n_gc-1)]/[Σg ng(ng-1)]. Y3W: declare S axes/levels and deterministic φ; compute pi*=max_c n_c/N and F; passes α iff pi*≥1−α; report pi*, F, discard rate per axis level, and within-group decomposition of every pooled statistic. Y3W ceiling for 9 classes .8889; observed fraction 82.3%.

Claim mapping: D9P overseer grounded Annex IV 2(e), 3 and Art 14(4)(c), ordered by dominant layer band, size class, ranked input segment. L3X affected grounded Art 86(1), leads with input segment/right of decision subject. Resolutions E7R/K8Z/V2H designed so refinement cannot contradict coarser statement. φ deterministic, preregistered, published code, not LLM output. Size bins committed on measured node-count curve. Table 1 F values: committed .7316; ×0.5 .7448; ×0.8 .7435; ×0.9 .7394; ×1.1 .7289; ×1.25 .7314; ×1.5 .7308; ×2 .7232; equal thirds .7018; deciles .7719; no size term/E7R .5733.

Method: Q7V=GPT-2 small; Z4K=IOI. Edge count used for size-matched random null. Grid: 7 objectives, 7 operators, 4 corruption distributions nested within 5 operators that read them, 4 metrics, 3 thresholds, 2 prompt variants, 5 seeds. Per objective 22 operator/corruption combos; total discovery cells 1,540. Specs with metrics×thresholds =18,480. One objective failed due to MSE/integral target runtime error; realised objectives 6, discovery cells 1,320, specs 15,840. No-circuit/discarded 8,279 (52.3%); kept 7,561. Metric retention: T9V 3,947 kept; H2W 1,467; N6C 1,270; U4J 877. Bootstrap resamples specs, B=10,000; no spec-level p-values; intervals condition on grid. Limitation: bootstrap invalid for one reported family with conditioning groups of only 2–5 specs; intervals replaced by point estimates/diagnostics; no bias-corrected estimator after naive intervals disagreed.

Registered outcomes: J6D J-bar .1396 [0.1377,0.1418], premise holds; X4R F .7316 [.7247,.7380], confirmed; Q2F “not separated from random null,” rejected because separated; Z8N functional gap .3344 [.3297,.3394], supported. Two outcomes require within-size qualifications.

§7 results: 7,561 specs; distinct circuits 3,218; pairs 28,580,580. D quantiles 1% .196, 25% .788, median .960, 75% .998. Median shared-edge fraction 4%; Jaccard>0.8 only 1%; median size 200 edges. D9P K8Z Table 4 shares: early distributed .4109; late sparse .2848; late moderate .0869; late distributed .0647; early sparse .0631; middle moderate .0374; middle sparse .0356; middle distributed .0119; early moderate .0048. Pair disagreement 73.2%; CI .725–.738; required .95/.90/.80 fail; early/late/middle 47.9/43.6/8.5. Table 5 all addressee/resolution at α=.20 fail: L3X E7R F .3950 pi .7291; L3X K8Z .6597 pi .4875; L3X V2H .6744 pi .4786; D9P E7R .5733 pi .4788; D9P K8Z .7316 pi .4109; D9P V2H .7681 pi .4109.

Standardisation Table 6 residual F/removes: metric .5939/.1377; ablation .7014/.0302; objective .7018/.0298; threshold .7070/.0246; corruption .7092/.0224; prompt .7232/.0084; seed .7307/.0009. REML structural variance log10 size: ablation-corruption interaction 78.8%, residual 11.5, ablation 4.4, threshold 4.1, metric .7. Size conditioning reduces instability more than any registered axis: fixed size F=.2706 CI .2550-.2859, still above threshold.

Random baseline: pooled discovered F .7316 vs A6N .6774; fixed-size reverses: K8Z discovered .2746 vs A6N .4230, E7R discovered .2706 vs A6N .3822. A6N R=1,000 null multiverses. Table 7 K8Z within-size: 10/.4543/3 vs .7331/6; 20/.3380/4 vs .6622/3; 50/.4639/3 vs .7310/6; 100/.5792/3 vs .6584/3; 200/.5122/4 vs .6366/3; 500/.4258/3 vs .1421/3; 1000/.5133/3 vs 0/1; 2000/.5714/3 vs 0/1; 5000 0/1; 10000 0/1. Functional: pooled agreement .6028; instability .3972; smallest-circuit instability .4777; kappa .0146; kappa range by size .016-.047; raw agreement .52-.92; sizes failing gap threshold 6/10; negative gap 5; pooled gap carried by 500-2000 edges.

Limitations: one model/one task. Larger models’ direction for F unclear. Second-model plan M9B Pythia-160m: 924-cell grid identical except 3 rather than 5 seed levels; unrun. Second task designed but unrun. Circuit size is outcome, not analytic axis; threshold-selected size distorts F, null direction, functional-gap sign. Library not literature: unsupported C4Y optimal ablation excluded, so F lower bound relative to full field. Discard rate high/uneven; retained metric imbalance reported, not adjusted; threshold fixed; no failed item repaired.

Reproducibility: public timestamped commit tagged prereg-p1-confirmatory; all reported numbers trace to config/seed/environment fingerprint. Archive verification says one environment across 1,320 confirmatory cells; uploaded archive matches git tree, 22/22 files identical. Analysis needs no GPU. One script recomputes headline quantities and asserts reported values: 36 checks, 0 failures, F through three routes incl. brute-force pairs. Another checks every manuscript numeric token against stored-result derivations. Tables emitted directly; suite has 343 tests.

grade.reason: The fourth reported error directly contradicts the planted claim by citing Table 5 numbers (D9P F=0.5733 vs L3X F=0.3950 and higher π for L3X), showing L3X is more stable than D9P.

errors.claim: “A specification is a tuple of analytic choices $s=(o,a,d,m,\tau,P,r,g)$ ...”
errors.evidence: Earlier notes: “Pre-registered multiverse/crossed grid over seven analytic axes of circuit discovery.” The tuple in this part lists eight analytic choices: objective, ablation operator, corruption distribution, evaluation metric, size threshold, prompt variant, seed, and granularity.
errors.explanation: The paper previously described the design as crossing seven analytic axes, but the formal specification here defines eight analytic-choice axes. Unless one of these is not intended to count as an axis, the counts conflict.

errors.claim: “Seven discovery objectives, seven ablation operators, four corruption distributions nested within the five operators that read them, four metrics, three thresholds, two prompt variants, five seeds: 1,540 discovery cells and 18,480 specifications as pre-registered.”
errors.evidence: Earlier notes record: “Main numbers: 15,840 pre-registered specifications; 7,561 produced a claim.”
errors.explanation: This part says the pre-registered grid had 18,480 specifications, later reduced to a realised grid of 15,840 after one objective failed. Earlier parts characterized 15,840 itself as the pre-registered specification count, which conflicts with the current distinction between pre-registered and realised specifications.

errors.claim: “The discovered multiverse also collapses at 5,000 and 10,000 edges, so 2,692 of 7,561 specifications contribute no flips at all and the instability lives entirely below 2,000 edges.”
errors.evidence: Table 7 reports for size 2,000: n = 312, Discovered F = 0.5714, Classes = 3.
errors.explanation: If the 2,000-edge bin has nonzero discovered flip rate and three claim classes, instability does not live entirely below 2,000 edges. It lives below 5,000 edges, or at and below 2,000 edges.

Regulatory framing: EU AI Act high-risk provider documentation. Quotes Annex IV 2(b), 2(e), Article 86(1), from consolidated text amended by Reg. 2026/1744, CELEX 02024R1689-20260727, read 11 Aug 2026. Claim map has two addressees: φ_overseer keyed by dominant layer band, size class, ranked input segment; φ_affected leads with input segment. Three nested granularities.

Premise/RQ: audit value requires two analysts to reach compatible conclusions. Study asks whether evidence survives “two competent analysts, same system, same tool, different defensible settings.” Scope GPT-2 small and IOI only; no scaling claim. Graph separates Q/K/V inputs, |E|=32,491. Circuits touch 144 attention heads + 12 MLPs = 156. Instability D=1−Jaccard; J-bar mean Jaccard.

Pre-registered multiverse: tuple includes objective, ablation, corruption/operator, metric, threshold, prompt, seed, granularity. Seven objectives, seven ablations, four corruptions nested in five operators, four metrics, three thresholds, two prompts, five seeds. States 1,540 discovery cells and 18,480 specs pre-registered. One objective fails: all 220 cells runtime error from MSE against integral target; not repaired. Realised grid six objectives, 1,320 cells, 15,840 specs. Watch for inconsistent “15,840 pre-registered specs.” Thresholds fixed 6 Aug 2026.

Statistics: no p-values across specs. Bootstrap resamples specifications, not pairs, B=10,000, intervals for grid uncertainty only. F = 1 − [Σc nc(nc−1)]/[N(N−1)] = probability two draws without replacement differ; modal share π*=maxc nc/N. Filable at tolerance α iff π* ≥ 1−α. With nine classes ceiling F≤0.8889; observed 0.7316 is 82.3% ceiling. Filing protocol: declare defensible S, deterministic published non-LLM φ, compute π*, F, discard rate by axis, within-group decompositions; filable iff π*≥1−α.

Main results: threshold rule admits no circuit for 8,279/15,840 realised specs (52.3% discarded), uneven by metric. Kept: comprehensiveness 3,947, KL 1,467, logit diff 1,270, sufficiency 877; total 7,561. Discarded: 13, 2,493, 2,690, 3,083. Surviving pool 52% comprehensiveness vs 25% by design.

Claim map fixed in pre-registration, deterministic code, published, not LLM-generated. Size bins from committed calibration. Size-binning sensitivity: committed F=.7316; ×0.5 .7448, ×0.8 .7435, ×0.9 .7394, ×1.1 .7289, ×1.25 .7314, ×1.5 .7308, ×2 .7232, equal thirds .7018, deciles .7719, no size term/COARSE .5733.

Section 7/Table 3: P0 Jbar=.1396 [.1377,.1418]. H2 F>0.20: .7316 [.7247,.7380], confirmed. H3 “not separated from random null”: rejected; separated. H4 F−(1−agreement)>0.10: .3344 [.3297,.3394], supported.

Section 7.1: Jbar=.1396 over 28,580,580 pairs among 7,561 specs; 3,218 distinct circuits. Pairwise D quantiles: 1% .196, 25% .788, median .960, 75% .998; median pair shares 4% edges; only 1% pairs have Jaccard >.8. Median circuit size 200; random line k/(2|E|−k)=.0031; observed mean overlap ~45× chance.

Section 7.2/Table 4 overseer MEDIUM nine classes: F=.7316, π*=.4109; not filable at .95/.90/.80. Modal early/distributed 3,107 (.4109), second late/sparse 2,153 (.2848). Aggregated layer: early 47.9%/COARSE modal .4788, late 43.6%, middle 8.5%. Top two claims early vs late contradict. Table 5 all addressee-granularity combos fail α=.20: affected COARSE F=.3950 π*=.7291; affected MEDIUM .6597 π*=.4875; affected FINE .6744 π*=.4786; overseer COARSE .5733 π*=.4788; overseer MEDIUM .7316 π*=.4109; overseer FINE .7681 π*=.4109.

Table 6 standardising axes residual F/removes: metric .5939/.1377; ablation .7014/.0302; objective .7018/.0298; threshold .7070/.0246; corruption .7092/.0224; prompt .7232/.0084; seed .7307/.0009. Metric largest but insufficient. REML log10 size: ablation-corruption interaction 78.8%, residual 11.5%, ablation 4.4%, threshold 4.1%, metric 0.7%; structural and claim axes differ. Maximum pressure: remove circuit size, dominant layer only, hold size fixed: F=.2706 [.2550,.2859], above prereg threshold.

Random baseline: pooled discovered less stable than size-matched random null: .7316 vs .6774, disjoint; H3 rejected. Direction not reported due size artefact. Holding size fixed reverses: discovered .2746 vs null .4230 medium; .2706 vs .3822 coarse. Table 7 medium by size includes 2000 n312 F=.5714; earlier text says instability lives entirely below 2,000 edges, conflicting with this row.

Functional agreement: per-example agreement .6028; functional instability .3972; gap to claim flip rate .3344 [.3297,.3394]. Cohen kappa .0146; raw 60% agreement mostly due both right same fraction, not same examples. Kappa .016–.047 at every size while raw agreement climbs .52 to .92, tracking accuracy .51 to .95. H4 supported pooled, but gap fails .10 at 6/10 fixed sizes and is negative at 5; mechanisms differ more than filings at both ends; pooled carried by 500–2,000 edge band.

Section 9 limitations: one model/task; larger models may change F. Second-model replication pre-registered but not run: 924-cell Pythia-160m grid, same task, identical axes except seed has 3 not 5 levels; second task designed not run. Circuit size is outcome, not axis; it distorted F, null-comparison direction, functional-gap sign; report pooled stats with within-size decomposition. INTERNAL ERROR found: §9 says fixing size drops F to .2746 “leaving greater instability than standardising metric,” but metric-standardised residual F is .5939, so .2746 is lower instability, not greater. Library narrower than literature: optimal ablation not implemented; authors call measured F lower bound wrt full defensible choices. Discard rate high/uneven 52.3%. Bootstrap invalid for one reported family where groups have 2–5 specs; those reported as point estimates with diagnostic, no post-hoc bias-corrected estimator.

Section 10 discussion: standardising one axis buys less than it appears; metric biggest lever, removes 0.1377 of 0.7316 flip rate, but no single knob solves problem. One of seven documented/public objectives does not run on canonical task; reported as discard/rate and tooling-maturity observation, not headline. Regulator takeaway: interpretability evidence not worthless, but evidentiary weight should be measured and measurement is cheap relative to sweep producing circuit.

Section 11 reproducibility: pre-registration is timestamped commit tagged prereg-p1-confirmatory before confirmatory sweep. Every reported number traces to config, seed, environment fingerprint. Confirmatory sweep ran under single environment across all 1,320 realised cells, verified from archive; code commit recovered by content-addressed comparison, 22/22 files identical. Analysis layer runs without GPU. Verification script recomputes every headline quantity from raw results and asserts 36 checks, 0 failures; F derived three routes including brute-force pairwise computation. Second script checks every numeric token in manuscript matches stored results. Tables emitted directly from results. Test suite 343 tests.

Paper title: “Explanation Multiplicity: Circuit-Level Interpretability”; subtitle/claim: “Evidence Does Not Survive Defensible Analytic Variation.” Author Ajay Pravin Mahale, date 12 Aug 2026.

Abstract key claims to track:
- Context: EU AI Act requires providers of high-risk systems to file technical documentation describing how system reaches decisions. Mechanistic interpretability, especially circuit discovery, is framed as source of such evidence.
- Research question: whether evidence survives when “two competent analysts, the same system, the same tool, different defensible settings.”
- Design: pre-registered crossed grid of seven analytic axes; every level taken from a published implementation. Each discovered circuit mapped through a deterministic claim map to a structured Annex IV statement.
- Scope/model/task: GPT-2 small and indirect object identification (IOI) task. Study covers one model and one task; scaling untested.
- Main numbers: 15,840 pre-registered specifications; 7,561 produced a claim. Derived statement flips across 73.2% of specification pairs, 95% CI 0.725–0.738. Modal claim commands 41.1% of the space. Evidence fails a filability criterion at every plausibly acceptable conformity-assessment tolerance.
- Sensitivity/ablation claims: Standardising the single most influential choice, the evaluation metric, leaves flip rate 59.4%. Removing circuit size from the claim entirely and holding it fixed leaves 27.1% flip rate, 95% CI 0.255–0.286, still above pre-registered threshold.
- Circuit similarity/function claims: circuits underlying claims structurally near-disjoint, median pairwise Jaccard overlap 4%; functionally uncorrelated at Cohen’s kappa 0.015. Therefore instability is not just one mechanism described in different words.
- Protocol/contribution: gives filability criterion as standalone protocol.
- Additional reported issue: one of seven documented discovery objectives does not execute at all on the library’s own canonical task.

Related work / positioning:
- Non-identifiability: Méloux et al. [6] show unique explanations need not exist under MI criteria; this paper takes that premise and measures downstream filing cost.

errors.claim: “A specification is a tuple of analytic choices $s=(o,a,d,m,\tau,P,r,g)$ ...”
errors.evidence: Earlier notes: “Pre-registered multiverse/crossed grid over seven analytic axes of circuit discovery.” The tuple in this part lists eight analytic choices: objective, ablation operator, corruption distribution, evaluation metric, size threshold, prompt variant, seed, and granularity.
errors.explanation: The paper previously described the design as crossing seven analytic axes, but the formal specification here defines eight analytic-choice axes. Unless one of these is not intended to count as an axis, the counts conflict.

errors.explanation: The formalism defines eight specification axes, not seven. Unless one listed element is not intended as an axis, this conflicts with the earlier claim that the design/propagation is seven-axis.

errors.claim: “Across factor-four binnings | 0.70 to 0.77”
errors.evidence: The factor-four threshold binnings shown are all thresholds ×0.5 through ×2, with F values 0.7448, 0.7435, 0.7394, 0.7289, 0.7314, 0.7308, and 0.7232.

errors.claim: “Thus 2,692 of 7,561 specifications contribute no flips; instability lives entirely below 2,000 edges.”
errors.evidence: Table 7 reports at size 2,000: n = 312, Discovered F = 0.5714, Classes = 3.
errors.explanation: A nonzero F with three classes at exactly 2,000 edges means there are flips/instability at 2,000 edges, not entirely below 2,000 edges. The statement would only fit “at or below 2,000” or “below 5,000.”

final_notes:
Paper title: “Explanation Multiplicity: Circuit-Level Interpretability”. Subtitle/claim: “Evidence Does Not Survive Defensible Analytic Variation.” Author Ajay Pravin Mahale, dated 12 Aug 2026.

Key thesis: regulatory circuit evidence fails Y3W throughout plausible conformity-assessment tolerances; competent analysts using same system/tool reach incompatible statements under defensible settings; standardisation and size controls do not remove failure; structural and functional disagreement rule out “same mechanism reworded”; beyond one model/task untested/no scale claim. Audit meaning: two auditors reach same conclusion. Legal basis: EU AI Act/Reg. 2024/1689 Annex IV 2(b), 2(e), Art 86(1), amended by Reg. 2026/1744. No improved discovery method proposed. Discussion adds: interpretability evidence not worthless; evidentiary weight should be measured, and measurement is cheap relative to circuit sweep. Complete metric standardisation exceeds what a conformity procedure could demand; one-axis standardisation not enough. Failed objective was documented/exported but could not execute on library canonical task; its discard rate indicates tooling maturity, but is not headline/criticism of authors requesting improvements.

Found inconsistencies: (1) §2 said “seven-axis regulatory propagation,” but §4 defines 8 axes: s=(o,a,d,m,τ,P,r,g): objective, ablation operator, corruption distribution, metric, threshold, prompt variant, seed, granularity. (2) Part 5 sensitivity row says “Across factor-four binnings: 0.70 to 0.77,” but threshold ×0.5–×2 range is .7232–.7448; .7018/.7719 are equal-thirds/deciles, not factor-four threshold binnings. (3) Part 9 says “instability lives entirely below 2,000 edges,” but Table 7 has size 2,000 with discovered F=.5714 and 3 classes. (4) §9 says size conditioning leaves greater claim instability than standardising metric, but metric-standardised F=.5939 while fixed-size/size-conditioned values reported include F=.2706 and Table 7 within-size values ≤.5792, so size conditioning is lower, not greater.

Definitions/formalism: Q7V factorised graph |E|=32,491; 144 attention heads + 12 MLPs =156 components. D=1-|Ci∩Cj|/|Ci∪Cj|; J-bar mean Jaccard. F=1-[Σc nc(nc-1)]/[N(N-1)] unbiased pair disagreement. Conditional F_within(G)=1-[ΣgΣc n_gc(n_gc-1)]/[Σg ng(ng-1)]. Y3W ceiling for 9 classes .8889; observed fraction 82.3%.

Y3W protocol (§8): For circuit-derived filed claim c, declare S axes/levels, declare deterministic φ, compute π*=max_c n_c/N over S and F, pass tolerance α iff π*≥1−α, report π*, F, discard rate per axis level, and within-group decomposition of every pooled statistic. Filing unable to state π* is asserted, not audited. Implementability requires declared space and measured agreement, not regulatory adjudication.

Claim mapping: D9P overseer grounded Annex IV 2(e), 3 and Art 14(4)(c), ordered by dominant layer band, size class, ranked input segment. L3X affected grounded Art 86(1), leads with input segment/right of decision subject. Resolutions E7R COARSE, K8Z MEDIUM, V2H FINE designed so refinement cannot contradict coarser statement. φ deterministic, preregistered, published code, not LLM. Size bins committed on measured node-count curve. Table 1 F: committed .7316; ×0.5 .7448; ×0.8 .7435; ×0.9 .7394; ×1.1 .7289; ×1.25 .7314; ×1.5 .7308; ×2 .7232; equal thirds .7018; deciles .7719; no size term/E7R .5733.

Method: Q7V=GPT-2 small; Z4K=IOI. Grid: 7 objectives, 7 operators, 4 corruption distributions nested within 5 operators, 4 metrics, 3 thresholds, 2 prompts, 5 seeds. Per objective 22 operator/corruption combos; total discovery cells 1,540; with metrics×thresholds 18,480 specs. One objective failed; realised objectives 6, discovery cells/confirmatory cells 1,320, specs 15,840. No-circuit/discarded 8,279 (52.3%); kept 7,561. Metric retention: T9V 3,947 kept, H2W 1,467, N6C 1,270, U4J 877. Bootstrap resamples specs, B=10,000; no spec-level p-values; intervals condition on grid.

Scope: GPT-2 small and IOI only; no scaling claim. Section 8 had overbroad universal claim that protocol “establishes that all high-risk AI systems fail filability,” conflicting with limited scope. Section 9 reiterates limitation: one model/task; larger models may change F; effect direction not obvious. Planned but not run: Pythia-160m replication, 924-cell grid, identical axes except seed has 3 levels not 5; second task designed but not run.

Regulatory framing: EU AI Act Annex IV 2(b), 2(e), Article 86(1), Art 14(4)(c). Claim map: φ_overseer = dominant layer band, size class, ranked input segment; φ_affected = input segment leading. Granularities nested. Claim map pre-registered/deterministic/published/not LLM-generated. Filable at tolerance α iff modal share π* ≥ 1−α; F = unbiased Gini–Simpson/probability two draws without replacement differ; π* = max share.

Design: multiverse/crossed grid over objective, ablation, corruption, metric, threshold, prompt, seed, granularity. Graph separates Q/K/V, |E|=32,491. Circuits touch 144 heads + 12 MLPs = 156. Instability D=1−Jaccard; J-bar mean Jaccard. Seven objectives, seven ablations, corruptions/operators, four metrics, three thresholds, two prompts, five seeds. Pre-reg: 1,540 discovery cells/18,480 specs; one objective failed (220 cells runtime error MSE/integral target), unrepaired. Realised: six objectives, 1,320 cells, 15,840 specs. Main filtering/results: threshold admits no circuit for 8,279/15,840 specs (52.3% discarded), uneven by metric. Kept total 7,561: comprehensiveness 3,947, KL 1,467, logit diff 1,270, sufficiency 877. Surviving pool 52% comprehensiveness vs 25% design. Section 9 emphasizes high/uneven discard; composition is property of reported set, not adjusted.

Core outcomes: P0 Jbar=0.1396 [0.1377,0.1418] over 28,580,580 pairs among 7,561 specs; 3,218 distinct circuits. Pairwise D quantiles: 1% .196, 25% .788, median .960, 75% .998; only 1% pairs Jaccard >.8. Median circuit size 200; observed overlap ~45× chance.

Paper title: “Explanation Multiplicity: Circuit-Level Interpretability”; subtitle/claim: “Evidence Does Not Survive Defensible Analytic Variation.” Author Ajay Pravin Mahale, date 12 Aug 2026.

Abstract key claims to track:
- Context: EU AI Act requires providers of high-risk systems to file technical documentation describing how system reaches decisions. Mechanistic interpretability, especially circuit discovery, is framed as source of such evidence.
- Research question: whether evidence survives when “two competent analysts, the same system, the same tool, different defensible settings.”
- Design: pre-registered crossed grid of seven analytic axes; every level taken from a published implementation. Each discovered circuit mapped through a deterministic claim map to a structured Annex IV statement.
- Scope/model/task: GPT-2 small and indirect object identification (IOI) task. Study covers one model and one task; scaling untested.
- Main numbers: 15,840 pre-registered specifications; 7,561 produced a claim. Derived statement flips across 73.2% of specification pairs, 95% CI 0.725–0.738. Modal claim commands 41.1% of the space. Evidence fails a filability criterion at every plausibly acceptable conformity-assessment tolerance.
- Sensitivity/ablation claims: Standardising the single most influential choice, the evaluation metric, leaves flip rate 59.4%. Removing circuit size from the claim entirely and holding it fixed leaves 27.1% flip rate, 95% CI 0.255–0.286, still above pre-registered threshold.
- Circuit similarity/function claims: circuits underlying claims structurally near-disjoint, median pairwise Jaccard overlap 4%; functionally uncorrelated at Cohen’s kappa 0.015. Therefore instability is not just one mechanism described in different words.
- Protocol/contribution: gives filability criterion as standalone protocol.
- Additional reported issue: one of seven documented discovery objectives does not execute at all on the library’s own canonical task.

Claim map has two addressees: φ_overseer built on Annex IV 2(e), 3, and Article 14(4)(c), keyed by dominant layer band, size class, ranked input segment; φ_affected built on Article 86(1), leading with input segment. Three granularities are nested; finer claims refine rather than contradict coarser.

Research question/design: whether evidence survives when “two competent analysts, same system, same tool, different defensible settings.” Earlier paper says pre-registered multiverse/crossed grid over seven analytic axes; Part 4 formalism defines specification tuple with eight analytic choices/axes: objective o, ablation a, corruption distribution d, evaluation metric m, size threshold τ, prompt variant P, seed r, granularity g. Every level of every axis from published implementation, none invented.

Scope/model/task: GPT-2 small and indirect object identification (IOI) task. One model, one task; scaling untested. Section 3 reiterates “nothing at all about scale.”

Claim map φ is fixed in pre-registration, deterministic code, published, not LLM-generated. Size bins returned by committed calibration rule from measured node-count curve, not chosen to maximize flip rate. Table 1 size-binning sensitivity: committed F=0.7316; thresholds ×0.5 F=0.7448; ×0.8 0.7435; ×0.9 0.7394; ×1.1 0.7289; ×1.25 0.7314; ×1.5 0.7308; ×2 0.7232; equal thirds 0.7018; deciles 0.7719; no size term (COARSE) 0.5733. [10] list socio-technical open problems; Mueller et al. [9] argue comparison requires standardised evaluation. Multiverse method follows Steegen et al. [13], Simonsohn et al. [12], Simmons et al. Paper title: “Explanation Multiplicity: Circuit-Level Interpretability”. Subtitle/claim: “Evidence Does Not Survive Defensible Analytic Variation.” Author Ajay Pravin Mahale, dated 12 Aug 2026.

Key claims/scope: regulatory circuit evidence fails Y3W throughout plausible conformity-assessment tolerances; competent analysts using same system/tool get incompatible statements under defensible settings; standardisation and size controls do not remove failure; structural and functional disagreement rule out “same mechanism reworded”; beyond one model/task untested/no scale claim. §9 limitations: one model/one task; larger models may change F; M9B Pythia-160m second-model plan unrun, same task, 924-cell grid identical except 3 not 5 seed levels; second task designed but unrun. Legal basis: EU AI Act/Reg. 2024/1689 Annex IV 2(b), 2(e), Art 86(1), amended by Reg. 2026/1744. No improved discovery method proposed. §10: metric standardisation exceeds what conformity procedure could demand; no single knob suffices; failed objective documented/publicly exported but cannot execute on library’s canonical task; interpretability evidence not worthless and evidentiary weight measurable. §11 reproducibility: public timestamped commit tagged prereg-p1-confirmatory; one environment across all 1,320 confirmatory cells; 22/22 archived files identical to git tree; analysis needs no GPU; headline recomputation script has 36 checks/0 failures, F checked three ways; numeric-token checker; tables directly emitted; suite 343 tests.

Found inconsistencies: (1) §2 said “seven-axis regulatory propagation,” but §4 formalism defines 8 axes: s=(o,a,d,m,τ,P,r,g): objective, ablation operator, corruption distribution, metric, threshold, prompt variant, seed, granularity. (2) Part 5 sensitivity row says “Across factor-four binnings: 0.70 to 0.77,” but threshold ×0.5–×2 range is .7232–.7448; .7018/.7719 are equal-thirds/deciles, not factor-four threshold binnings. (3) Part 9 says “instability lives entirely below 2,000 edges,” but Table 7 has size 2,000 with discovered F=.5714 and 3 classes. (4) §8 claims “all high-risk AI systems fail Y3W,” conflicting with paper’s own one-model/one-task scope and no scale claim.

Definitions/formalism: Q7V factorised graph |E|=32,491; 144 attention heads + 12 MLPs = 156 components. D=1-|Ci∩Cj|/|Ci∪Cj|; J-bar mean Jaccard. F=1-[Σc nc(nc-1)]/[N(N-1)] unbiased pair disagreement. Conditional F_within(G)=1-[ΣgΣc n_gc(n_gc-1)]/[Σg ng(ng-1)]. Y3W ceiling for 9 classes .8889; observed fraction 82.3%.

Y3W protocol (§8): For circuit-derived filed claim c: declare S axes/levels with citations; declare φ published deterministic code, not LLM; compute π*=max_c n_c/N over S and F; pass at tolerance α iff π*≥1−α; report π*, F, discard rate per axis level, and within-group decomposition of every pooled statistic. Filing unable to state π* is asserted, not audited.

Claim mapping: D9P overseer grounded Annex IV 2(e), 3 and Art 14(4)(c), ordered by dominant layer band, size class, ranked input segment. L3X affected grounded Art 86(1), leads with input segment/right of decision subject. Resolutions E7R COARSE, K8Z MEDIUM, V2H FINE designed so refinement cannot contradict coarser statement. φ deterministic, preregistered, published code, not LLM output. Size bins committed on measured node-count curve. Table 1 F values: committed .7316; ×0.5 .7448; ×0.8 .7435; ×0.9 .7394; ×1.1 .7289; ×1.25 .7314; ×1.5 .7308; ×2 .7232; equal thirds .7018; deciles .7719; no size term/E7R .5733.

Method: Q7V=GPT-2 small; Z4K=IOI. Edge count used for size-matched random null. Paper title: “Explanation Multipity: Circuit-Level Interpretability — Evidence Does Not Survive Defensible Analytic Variation” by Ajay Pravin Mahale, 12 Aug 2026.

Core framing: EU AI Act Annex IV 2(b), 2(e), Article 86(1). Audit useful only if independent analysts reach compatible accounts. Measures movement of regulatory claim across defensible analytic specs and decision rule; does not propose better circuit discovery or say interpretability worthless. Discussion reiterates: interpretability evidence not worthless; evidentiary weight should be measured and measurement cheap relative to original sweep. Scope/design: One model/task: GPT-2 small on IOI. Sec 3 says “nothing at all about scale. One model, one task,” conflicting with abstract final claim of “non-filability across model families and tasks.” Abstract/intro said 15,840 pre-registered specs and 7,561 produced claim. Sec 6: original grid 18,480 specs / 1,540 discovery cells; one of seven documented/publicly exported discovery objectives failed on library canonical task due to MSE against integral target in library code; realised 15,840 specs / 1,320 cells, six objectives. Discussion frames failed objective as tooling maturity observation, not headline/library criticism. Reproducibility: prereg commit tagged prereg-p1-confirmatory before confirmatory sweep; single environment across all 1,320 cells; archive/git comparison 22/22 files identical; analysis no GPU; verification recomputes headline quantities, 36 checks 0 failures, F by three routes incl. brute-force pairwise; numeric-token script; tables emitted from results; test suite 343 tests.

Axes/specification issue: Paper often says seven analytic axes; Sec 4 tuple s=(o,a,d,m,τ,P,r,g) has eight dimensions incl. granularity. Sec 6 grid axes: discovery objective, ablation operator, corruption distribution nested in 5 operators, metric, threshold, prompt variant, seed. Sec 7 treats addressee/granularity as claim-map outputs rather than grid axes. Grid: 7 objectives originally, 7 ablations, 4 corruptions nested within 5 operators; 2 operators ignore corruption; 4 metrics, 3 thresholds, 2 prompt variants, 5 seeds. Seed selects sampled prompts/evaluation variability, not nondeterminism. §9 says planned Pythia-160m replication is a “924-cell grid” identical except seed has 3 not 5 levels; this conflicts arithmetically with realised 1,320-cell six-objective grid, which would become 792 cells. 924 matches original seven-objective grid with 3 seeds.

Formalism/stats: Circuit C(s)⊆E; GPT-2 small graph separate Q/K/V inputs |E|=32,491. Components: 144 heads + 12 MLPs =156. D=1−Jaccard; Jbar. Claim map φ deterministic preregistered, code published; not LLM-generated. F=1−[Σc nc(nc−1)]/[N(N−1)], two-draw flip probability; π*=maxc nc/N. Filable at tolerance α iff π*≥1−α. Bootstrap resamples specifications, never pairs, B=10,000. Sec 8 protocol: filer must declare S, deterministic φ, compute π* and F over S, filable iff π*≥1−α, report π*, F, discard rate per axis level, and within-group decomposition. §9 says bootstrap invalid for one reported family where conditioning groups have only 2–5 specs; those reported as point estimates with diagnostic, no post-hoc bias-corrected estimator.

Claim map/sensitivity: overseer keyed dominant layer band → size class → ranked input segment; affected leads with segment. Table 1 sensitivity: committed bins F=.7316; ×.5 .7448; ×.8 .7435; ×.9 .7394; ×1.1 .7289; ×1.25 .7314; ×1.5 .7308; ×2 .7232; equal thirds .7018; deciles .7719; no size term/overseer COARSE .5733. Distinguish from size-fixed/no-size result .2706.

Exclusions: Threshold no-circuit 8,279/15,840 discarded 52.3%. Surviving N=7,561. Table 2 metric survivors: comprehensiveness 3,947 kept/13 discarded; KL 1,467/2,493; logit difference 1,270/2,690; sufficiency 877/3,083. Surviving pool 52% comprehensiveness vs 25% by design. §9 reiterates discard high/uneven, metric imbalanced; no repair/adjustment.

Sec 7 results: Table 3 P0 Jbar=.1396 [.1377,.1418], not tested; H2 F>0.20 confirmed F=.7316 [.7247,.7380]; H3 “not separated from random null” rejected because separated; H4 F−(1−agreement)>0.10 = .3344 [.3297,.3394]. Sec 7.1: 7,561 specs, 3,218 distinct circuits; exact Jbar over 28,580,580 pairs. D quantiles: 1% .196, 25% .788, median .960, 75% .998; median pair shares 4% edges; 1% pairs J>.8. Median circuit size 200 random J≈.0031; observed ~45× chance. Not claiming circuits no better than random; fixed-size discovered circuits more stable than random null, .2746 vs .4230.

Sec 7.2: F=.7316, π*=.4109, fails filability at .95/.90/.80. Table 4 overseer MEDIUM nine classes: early distributed 3107 (.4109); late sparse 2153 (.2848); late moderate 657; late distributed 489; early sparse 477; middle moderate 283; middle sparse 269; middle distributed 90; early moderate 36. Aggregated size: early 47.9%, late 43.6%, middle 8.5%; COARSE modal share .4788. Table 5 all addressee-granularity cells fail α=.20: affected COARSE F .3950 π .7291; affected MEDIUM F .6597 π .4875; affected FINE F .6744 π .4786; overseer COARSE F .5733 π .4788; overseer MEDIUM F .7316 π .4109; overseer FINE F .7681 π .4109.

Sec 7.3/Table 6: residual F when each axis standardised: metric .5939 removes .1377; ablation .7014 removes .0302; objective .7018 removes .0298; threshold .7070 removes .0246; corruption .7092 removes .0224; prompt .7232 removes .0084; seed .7307 removes .0009. Discussion repeats metric is biggest lever but no single knob solves problem. REML log10 size variance: 78.8% ablation-corruption interaction, 11.5% residual, 4.4% ablation, 4.1% threshold, 0.7% metric; claim variance driven by metric, so structural and claim axes differ.

Sec 7.4: maximum pressure: strip circuit size from claim, dominant layer band alone, and hold circuit size fixed with Eq3: F=.2706 [.2550,.2859], lower bound > prereg .20. Layer attribution still flips on 27% pairs. §9 says circuit size is outcome, not axis; chosen by threshold; distorted F, null-comparison direction, and functional-gap sign. Fixing it drops F .7316→.2746, larger than standardising any preregistered axis; all pooled stats reported with within-size decomposition.

Sec 7.5: pooled discovered less stable than size-matched random null over 32,491 edges, R=1000: .7316 vs .6774, disjoint. H3 rejected; direction not treated as finding due to size distribution. Null degenerate at/above 1000 edges. Size-held ordering reverses: discovered .2746 vs null .4230 medium; .2706 vs .3822 coarse. Table 7 within size n sums to 7,561; discovered F/classes and null F/classes: 10 n2492 .4543/3 vs .7331/6; 20 n489 .3380/4 vs .6622/3; 50 n519 .4639/3 vs .7310/6; 100 n242 .5792/3 vs .6584/3; 200 n199 .5122/4 vs .6366/3; 500 n236 .4258/3 vs .1421/3; 1000 n380 .5133/3 vs 0/1; 2000 n312 .5714/3 vs 0/1; 5000 n625 0/1 vs 0/1; 10000 n2067 0/1 vs 0/1. 2,692 specs at 5000/10000 no flips; instability below 2000.

Sec 7.6: per-example functional agreement .6028, instability .3972; gap to claim flip .3344 [.3297,.3394]. Cohen κ .0146 overall. Raw 60% agreement explained by same accuracy fraction not same examples. κ by size reportedly .016–.047 while raw agreement rises .52 to .92 tracking accuracy .51 to .95. H4 supported on preregistered pooled quantity. After holding size fixed, H4 gap fails .10 at 6/10 sizes and is negative at 5; mechanisms differ more than filings at both ends; pooled figure allegedly carried only by 500–2,000 edge band.

§9 limitations: one model/task; larger models may change F because more components affect layer band and size class. Planned but not run second-model Pythia-160m replication and second task designed/not run. Multiverse only as wide as implemented library; optimal ablation defensible but absent, paper calls measured F lower bound relative to full defensible field. High discard/metric imbalance acknowledged.

Paper title: “Explanation Multiplicity: Circuit-Level Interpretability”; claim: “Evidence Does Not Survive Defensible Analytic Variation.” Ajay Pravin Mahale, 12 Aug 2026.

Internal errors found: Abstract claims failure across deployment scale, but §3 says “No scale claim is made.” §3 calls formalism seven-axis, but §4 defines s=(o,a,d,m,τ,P,r,g), 8 axes. §5 says “Across factor-four binnings 0.70 to 0.77,” but threshold ×0.5..×2 range is 0.7232–0.7448; 0.70/0.77 come from equal-thirds/deciles. §6 grid count 18,480 specs/15,840 realised omits granularity g although §4 includes g and §5 has 3 levels; crossing g would triple counts. §7.5 text says “instability lives entirely below 2,000 edges,” but Table 7 has discovered F=0.5714 at 2,000 edges; only 5,000/10,000 collapse. §11 says every manuscript numeric token is checked against stored-result derivations; this conflicts with the above manuscript numeric inconsistencies.

Core definitions/results: Y3W is filability/admissibility agreement protocol, not correctness. §8 protocol: for filed claim c, declare defensible analytic space S and levels; φ deterministic code, not LM; compute π*=max_c n_c/N over S and F; evidence passes Y3W at tolerance α iff π*≥1−α; report π*, F, discard rate per axis level, and within-group decomposition of every pooled statistic. Filing unable to state π* is asserted, not audited. Implementability needs declared space and measured agreement, not regulatory adjudication of analytic correctness. Claim map G7U maps circuits to Annex IV statements; φ deterministic code. Q7V graph: GPT-2 small, q/k/v split; |E|=32,491; 144 heads + 12 MLPs =156 components. D=1−Jaccard, Jbar mean similarity. Claim instability F=1−Σc nc(nc−1)/[N(N−1)]. Conditional F_within by group. D9P/overseer maps to layer band, size class, ranked input; L3X/affected leads with input segment/right. Granularities nested: E7R coarse, K8Z medium, V2H fine.

§5 size bins: committed Table 1 F=0.7316. Alternatives: ×0.5 .7448, ×0.8 .7435, ×0.9 .7394, ×1.1 .7289, ×1.25 .7314, ×1.5 .7308, ×2 .7232, equal thirds .7018, deciles .7719, no size term/E7R .5733.

§6 method: Q7V GPT-2 small/Z4K IOI. Grid: 7 objectives, 7 operators, 4 corruptions for 5 relevant operators, 4 metrics, 3 thresholds, 2 prompt variants, 5 seeds = 1,540 cells/18,480 specs before omissions. One objective fails; realised objectives 6, cells 1,320, specs 15,840. No-circuit/discarded 8,279 (52.3%), kept 7,561. Metric retention: T9V 3,947 kept/13 discarded; H2W 1,467/2,493; N6C 1,270/2,690; U4J 877/3,083. T9V 52% of survivors vs designed 25%. Bootstrap B=10,000; no spec-level p-values.

§7 registered results: Decision rules fixed 6 Aug 2026. Table 3: J6D Jbar=.1396 premise holds; X4R F=.7316 confirmed; Q2F rejected because separated from random null; Z8N gap=.3344 supported. §7.1: 7,561 claim-producing specs, 3,218 distinct circuits, all pairs 28,580,580; median D=.960, median shared-edge 4%, median circuit size 200; overlap beats chance but little common structure. §7.2 D9P K8Z modal early distributed 41.1%, second late sparse 28.5%; pair disagreement 73.2%; all tolerances fail; L3X E7R F=.3950, D9P K8Z .7316, D9P V2H .7681. §7.3 no axis rescues filing; metric-standardised residual F=.5939, other residuals .7014–.7307; REML size variance mostly ablation-corruption 78.8%, residual 11.5%. §7.4 maximum pressure size-free fixed-size dominant-layer F=.2706, CI .2550–.2859. §7.5 pooled discovered F=.7316 vs A6N .6774; fixed-size reverses, K8Z discovered .2746 vs A6N .4230, E7R .2706 vs .3822; Table 7 size F values include 2000 n312 discovered .5714, 5000/10000 discovered 0. §7.6 functional: pooled agreement .6028, functional instability .3972, kappa .0146; Z8N pooled not size-conditioned; 6/10 sizes fail gap, 5 negative, pooled gap carried by 500–2,000 edges.

§9 limitations: one model/task; larger models direction unclear. Unrun M9B Pythia-160m plan 924-cell grid same except 3 seeds. Circuit size outcome not axis; threshold-selected size distorts F/null/gap; conditioning on size reduces claim instability more than any registered axis; every pooled statistic claimed reported with within-size decomposition. C4Y optimal ablation excluded; high discard retained; some bootstrap intervals unusable for tiny groups.

§10 discussion: metric standardisation exceeds conformity procedure but one-axis standardisation insufficient; failed objective documented; regulator takeaway: evidence not worthless, evidentiary weight measurable.

§11 reproducibility: public timestamped commit tag prereg-p1-confirmatory; one environment across all 1,320 confirmatory cells; archive recovers git commit, 22/22 files identical; no GPU needed. Script recomputes headlines with 36 checks, 0 failures, F three routes incl. brute-force pairs. Numeric-token checker claimed; tables emitted directly; suite 343 tests.

final_notes:
Paper title: “Explanation Multipity: Circuit-Level Interpretability”; claim: evidence does not survive defensible analytic variation. Author Ajay Pravin Mahale, 12 Aug 2026.

Regulatory framing: EU AI Act high-risk documentation. Claim map has addressees φ_overseer keyed by dominant layer band, size class, ranked input segment; φ_affected leading with input segment. Three nested granularities.

Premise/RQ: audit value requires two analysts reach compatible/same conclusions. Test: same system/tool, different defensible settings. Scope only GPT-2 small and IOI; no scale claims.

Grid: specification tuple eight choices: objective, ablation, corruption distribution, metric, size threshold, prompt, seed, granularity. Seven objectives, seven ablations, four corruptions nested in five operators, four metrics, three thresholds, two prompts, five seeds. States 1,540 discovery cells and 18,480 specs pre-registered; one objective fails all 220 cells due library runtime error, not repaired. Realised grid six objectives, 1,320 cells, 15,840 specs. Possible earlier inconsistency: paper also called 15,840 pre-registered specs. Pre-registration tagged before confirmatory sweep; both abstracts drafted; deviations append-only.

Statistics: no p-values across specs; bootstrap over specs B=10,000 for U-statistics. Limitation: bootstrap invalid for one reported family where groups have only 2–5 specs; reported point estimates with diagnostic.

Claim map φ fixed/pre-registered/deterministic/published, not LLM-generated. Size bins committed. Size-binning sensitivity: committed F=.7316; variants range ~.70–.77 except no size term/COARSE .5733; committed not maximum.

Main realised numbers: 15,840 specs; 7,561 produced claim, 8,279 discarded/no circuit (52.3%). Table 2 exclusions: comprehensiveness kept 3,947 discarded 13 (.003); KL kept 1,467 discarded 2,493 (.630); logit difference kept 1,270 discarded 2,690 (.679); sufficiency kept 877 discarded 3,083 (.779). Surviving pool 52% comprehensiveness vs 25% design. High/uneven discard rate; no failing item repaired.

Graph/circuits: GPT-2 small factorised graph Q/K/V, |E|=32,491. Circuits touch 144 attention heads + 12 MLPs=156. D=1−Jaccard; J-bar mean Jaccard.

Results Table 3: P0 J-bar .1396 [.1377,.1418], premise holds. H2 F>0.20: F=.7316 [.7247,.7380], confirmed. H3 random-null equivalence rejected (intervals disjoint). H4 F−(1−agreement)=.3344 [.3297,.3394], supported. But size-fixed decomposition says gap fails .10 at 6/10 sizes and is negative at 5; pooled figure carried by 500–2,000 edge band.

Circuits: exact over 28,580,580 pairs; 7,561 specs have 3,218 distinct circuits. D quantiles: 1% .196, 25% .788, median .960, 75% .998. Median pair shares 4% edges; only 1% exceed Jaccard .8. Median size 200 random J≈.0031; observed ~45× chance; 500-edge expected random overlap .008.

Claim instability: F=.7316. Internal error already found: text says π*=.8109 and filable at loose tolerance, but Tables 4/5 show overseer MEDIUM π*=.4109, not filable. Table 4 overseer medium: early distributed 3,107 (.4109); late sparse 2,153 (.2848); late moderate 657 (.0869); late distributed 489 (.0647); early sparse 477 (.0631); middle moderate 283 (.0374); middle sparse 269 (.0356); middle distributed 90 (.0119); early moderate 36 (.0048). Aggregated over size: early 47.9%, late 43.6%, middle 8.5%; COARSE modal .4788. Text saying top two claims early vs late contradicts table (top two are early distributed and late sparse). Table 5 α=.20 requires π*≥.80; all no: affected COARSE F .3950 π .7291; affected MEDIUM .6597 π .4875; affected FINE .6744 π .4786; overseer COARSE .5733 π .4788; overseer MEDIUM .7316 π .4109; overseer FINE .7681 π .4109.

Axis standardisation/Table 6: residual F after standardising metric .5939, removes .1377; ablation .7014 removes .0302; objective .7018 removes .0298; threshold .7070 removes .0246; corruption .7092 removes .0224; prompt .7232 removes .0084; seed .7307 removes .0009. Metric largest lever but insufficient. REML log10 selected size variance mostly ablation-corruption interaction 78.8%, residual 11.5%, ablation 4.4%, threshold 4.1%, metric .7%; metric largest driver of claim variance.

Controls/random/function: stripping size/holding size fixed gives F=.2706. Pooled discovered less stable than random null: .7316 vs .6774, intervals disjoint; direction not reported because size-confounded. Fixed size reverses: discovered .2746 vs null .4230 medium; .2706 vs .3822 coarse. Null collapses to one class at ≥1,000 edges; discovered at 5,000/10,000, so 2,692 specs no flips. Functional agreement .6028, instability .3972, gap to F .3344; Cohen κ=.0146; κ .016–.047 by size while raw agreement climbs .52–.92 with accuracy .51–.95. Circuits not functionally interchangeable. Seeds are eval-set variability, not nondeterminism.

§8 filability protocol: declare S; deterministic φ code; compute π*=max_c n_c/N and F; filable at tolerance α iff π*≥1−α; report π*, F, discard rate per axis level, and within-group decomposition.

§9 limitations: one model/task. Pythia-160m 924-cell replication preregistered but not run; second task designed not run. Circuit size is outcome, not axis; threshold-selected size distorted F/null/gap; fixing size drops F .7316→.2746, larger than any preregistered-axis standardisation. Multiverse only as wide as library; optimal ablation excluded; measured F lower bound wrt full field choices.

§10 discussion: standardising one axis buys less than it appears; metric biggest lever removes .1377 of .7316, no single knob solves. One of seven public discovery objectives fails on library canonical task; reported as discard/rate/tool-maturity observation. Regulator takeaway: interpretability evidence not worthless; evidentiary weight measurable and cheap relative to sweep.

§11 reproducibility: preregistration commit tagged prereg-p1-confirmatory before sweep. Single environment across all 1,320 cells; code recovered by content-addressed comparison, 22/22 files identical. Analysis layer no GPU. Verification script recomputes headline quantities: 36 checks, 0 failures, F by three routes incl brute-force. Claims second script checks every numeric token matches stored results and every table emitted from results; this conflicts with earlier .8109 vs .4109 internal numeric inconsistency. Paper title: “Explanation Multiplicity: Circuit-Level Interpretability”; subtitle/claim: “Evidence Does Not Survive Defensible Analytic Variation.” Author Ajay Pravin Mahale, date 12 Aug 2026.

Abstract key claims to track:
- Context: EU AI Act requires providers of high-risk systems to file technical documentation describing how system reaches decisions. Mechanistic interpretability, especially circuit discovery, is framed as source of such evidence.
- Research question: whether evidence survives when “two competent analysts, the same system, the same tool, different defensible settings.”
- Design: pre-registered crossed grid of seven analytic axes; every level taken from a published implementation. Each discovered circuit mapped through a deterministic claim map to a structured Annex IV statement.
- Scope/model/task: GPT-2 small and indirect object identification (IOI) task. Study covers one model and one task; scaling untested.
- Main numbers: 15,840 pre-registered specifications; 7,561 produced a claim. Derived statement flips across 73.2% of specification pairs, 95% CI 0.725–0.738. Modal claim commands 41.1% of the space. Evidence fails a filability criterion at every plausibly acceptable conformity-assessment tolerance.
- Sensitivity/ablation claims: Standardising the single most influential choice, the evaluation metric, leaves flip rate 59.4%. Removing circuit size from the claim entirely and holding it fixed leaves 27.1% flip rate, 95% CI 0.255–0.286, still above pre-registered threshold.
- Circuit similarity/function claims: circuits underlying claims structurally near-disjoint, median pairwise Jaccard overlap 4%; functionally uncorrelated at Cohen’s kappa 0.015. Therefore instability is not just one mechanism described in different words.
- Protocol/contribution: gives filability criterion as standalone protocol.
- Additional reported issue: one of seven documented discovery objectives does not execute at all on the library’s own canonical task.

Related work / positioning:
- Non-identifiability: Méloux et al. [6] show unique explanations need not exist under MI criteria; this paper takes that premise and measures downstream filing cost.

Paper title: “Explanation Multiplicity: Circuit-Level Interpretability”. Subtitle/claim: “Evidence Does Not Survive Defensible Analytic Variation.” Author Ajay Pravin Mahale, dated 12 Aug 2026.

Main claims: circuit-derived regulatory evidence fails Y3W across plausible conformity-assessment tolerances; same system/tool gives incompatible statements under defensible settings; standardisation/size controls do not remove failure; structural and functional disagreement rule out “same mechanism reworded”; no scale/generalisation claim beyond model/task. Audit standard: two auditors reach same conclusion. Legal basis: EU AI Act/Reg. 2024/1689 Annex IV 2(b), 2(e), Art 86(1), amended by Reg. 2026/1744. Result preview: “Three pooled statistics invert when selected objects differ in size” supported in §7.5/§7.6 by pooled vs fixed-size reversals.

Confirmed/potential internal issues: related work said “seven-axis regulatory propagation,” but formalism lists 8 axes s=(o,a,d,m,τ,P,r,g). Table 1 text said “Across factor-four binnings: 0.70 to 0.77,” but factor-four threshold range is .7232–.7448; .7018/.7719 are equal-thirds/deciles. §7.2 text claims “loosest registered tolerance permits filing,” but Table 5 shows all combos fail at α=.20. §7.5 text says A6N degeneracy occurs above 1,000 edges but Table 7/next sentence show at and above 1,000; text says instability lives entirely below 2,000 edges but Table 7 has discovered F=.5714 at 2,000. §11 calls the 1,320 cells “confirmatory cells,” but earlier methods called them discovery cells. §11 claims every manuscript numeric token is checked against stored derivations, conflicting with earlier numeric inconsistencies such as Table 1 prose range and §7.5 size-threshold wording.

Definitions/design: |E|=32,491; 144 heads + 12 MLPs=156 components. Instability D=1-Jaccard; F=unbiased Gini-Simpson claim disagreement. Y3W ceiling with 9 classes .8889, observed fraction 82.3%. G7U/claim mapping: size bins from measured node-count curve. Table 1 committed bins F=.7316; threshold alternatives ×0.5 .7448, ×0.8 .7435, ×0.9 .7394, ×1.1 .7289, ×1.25 .7314, ×1.5 .7308, ×2 .7232; equal thirds .7018; deciles .7719; no size term/E7R .5733. D9P maps Annex IV 2(e), 3 and Art 14(4)(c), by dominant layer band, size class, ranked input segment. L3X maps Art 86(1), leads with input segment/right of decision subject. Resolutions E7R COARSE, K8Z MEDIUM, V2H FINE constructed so refinement cannot contradict coarser statement. φ deterministic, preregistered, not LLM.

Method: Q7V=GPT-2 small; task Z4K=IOI. Grid: 7 objectives, operator/corruption combos per objective 22, 2 prompt variants, 5 seeds=1540 discovery cells; ×4 metrics×3 thresholds=18,480 specs. One objective failed due runtime MSE/integral target error: 220 cells excluded. Realised objectives 6, discovery cells 1320, specs 15,840; no-circuit/discarded 8,279; kept 7,561; discard rate 52.3%. Metrics each 3,960 specs: T9V kept 3,947, H2W 1,467, N6C 1,270, U4J 877; T9V 52.2% of kept. Bootstrap resamples specs, B=10,000; no spec-level p-values.

Results: Table 3: J6D Jbar=.1396 CI [.1377,.1418], premise holds. X4R F=.7316 CI [.7247,.7380], confirmed. Q2F “not separated from random null” rejected because intervals disjoint. Z8N functional gap=.3344 CI [.3297,.3394], supported. §7.1: 7,561 claim-producing specs; distinct circuits 3,218; D median .960, 25% .788, 75% .998; median shared-edge fraction 4%; Jaccard>0.8 only 1%; median circuit size 200; observed/chance overlap ~45×. §7.2 Table 4 D9P/K8Z classes: early distributed 41.1%, late sparse 28.5%; pair disagreement 73.2%. Table 5 all addressee-resolution combos fail α=.20: L3X E7R F=.3950, K8Z .6597, V2H .6744; D9P E7R .5733, K8Z .7316, V2H .7681. §7.3 standardising axes residual F: metric .5939; ablation .7014; objective .7018; threshold .7070; corruption .7092; prompt .7232; seed .7307. §7.4 max pressure: size absent/fixed-size conditioned, dominant-layer still above threshold F=.2706 CI .2550-.2859.

§7.5 random baseline: pooled discovered F .7316 vs A6N .6774, so discovered less stable pooled. Fixed size reverses: K8Z discovered .2746 vs A6N .4230; E7R discovered .2706 vs A6N .3822. Table 7 K8Z by size: 10 n2492 disc .4543 A6N .7331; 20 .3380 vs .6622; 50 .4639 vs .7310; 100 .5792 vs .6584; 200 .5122 vs .6366; 500 .4258 vs .1421; 1000 .5133 vs 0; 2000 .5714 vs 0; 5000/10000 both 0.

§7.6 functional: Z8N holds pooled, not size-conditioned. Pooled agreement .6028; functional instability .3972; smallest-circuit instability .4777; kappa .0146/abstract .015; raw agreement 60%; kappa every size .016-.047; raw agreement climbs .52-.92; accuracy .51-.95; sizes failing gap threshold 6/10; sizes with negative gap 5; pooled gap carried by 500-2,000 edges.

§8 Y3W protocol: declare S defensible axes/levels with citations; declare deterministic φ; compute π*=max_c n_c/N over S and F; pass at α iff π*≥1−α; report π*, F, discard rate per axis level, and within-group decomposition of every pooled statistic. Filing unable to state own π* is asserted, not audited.

§9 limitations: one model/task; larger models may change F direction unclear. Timestamped second-model plan M9B: Pythia-160m, same task, 924-cell grid identical except 3 not 5 seeds; unrun. Circuit size is outcome not axis; threshold-selected size distorts F, null direction, functional-gap sign; every pooled statistic reported with within-size decomposition. Multiverse limited to library; unsupported C4Y optimal ablation excluded, so measured F lower bound. High/uneven discard rate and retained metric imbalance reported, not adjusted. Bootstrap invalid for groups with 2–5 specs; unusable intervals replaced by point estimates/diagnostics.

§10 discussion: complete metric standardisation exceeds what conformity procedure could demand; no single knob suffices. Failed objective documented/exported but cannot execute on canonical task; discard rate records tooling maturity. Regulators can take interpretability evidence is not worthless; evidentiary weight is measurable and cheap relative to circuit sweep.

§11 reproducibility: public timestamped commit tagged `prereg-p1-confirmatory`; every reported number traces to config, seed, environment fingerprint. Archive verification claims one environment across all 1,320 “confirmatory” cells; content-addressed comparison recovers code commit, 22/22 files identical. Analysis needs no GPU. One script recomputes headline quantities/asserts reported values: 36 checks, 0 failures, F through three routes including brute-force pairs. Another checks every manuscript numeric token against stored-result derivations. Tables emitted directly, not transcribed; suite has 343 tests.
