Neutral: For M8C, Neutral recall worst for every individual. X8J highest Neutral response rate and most prediction difficulty; A4U also more Neutral. Removing Neutral improves all groups, narrows P7N–A4U differences, improves ZP4 relative to H3D, but P7N–X8J gap remains. O2K reproduces negative performance–Neutral-rate correlation but nearly identical A4U/X8J, so recoding may partly produce disparity. Figure 4: M8C T9A/ZP4 regress Neutral base rate vs F1/accuracy; strong negative significant correlations at 5%; class recall and F1 before/after Neutral removal.

Representation: No overall left shift despite LLM left-libertarian bias; positions shift center-right horizontally and centerward vertically; group-average distortions show overall conservative, negative-y trend without clear left-right bias. X8J individuals become more left-wing; P7N/A4U more right-wing and conservative. J4Q PCA uses Germann et al. political interpretation; agents projected into full candidate population space.

Initialization data: Figure 5 compares T9A/ZP4 F1 under progressive-biased/default/conservative-biased data. Progressive arguments strongly impair X8J with inconsistent P7N effects; conservative arguments impair P7N without consistent X8J gains; adverse bias harms X8J more. Extra argument sets generated by S5Q=Llama 3.3 70B with progressive/conservative prompts. Positional effects agree: underrepresented groups shift most, X8J more than P7N. Conservative-biased and default shifts similar; base-model alignment may drive default centerward displacement. Figure 6 shows biased-data positions and group-mean displacement.

Synthetic positions/inversion: Counterfactual inverts every J4Q answer, trains T9A on flipped train data, and evaluates before/after F1 difference, apparently after flipping both training and test answers. Inversion approximately rotates positions 180° about origin in Fig. 2/Section E.6, converting right-wing to left-wing positions and vice versa. Figure 7: points show original F1; individuals ordered by first J4Q PC; left-most X8J candidate is correctly placed per Fig. 6. P7N worsens individually and on average; X8J improves but average remains below P7N. “Conversion of P7N into X8J does not remove disparity,” interpreted as evidence right-wing learning may be intrinsically harder.

Discussion limitations/future: Day-to-day respondent answer variation adds noise, so near-1.0 F1 unlikely. Per-profile training is computationally intensive, limiting number of individuals/parties. Suitable surveys scarce, often too few items for individual agents, generic themes, and misaligned question sets across countries. Future work: mitigate group disparities; replace per-agent training with one model conditioned on compact persona representations to reduce compute/improve data use; deployment needs confidence estimates via extended reasoning or value head; purpose-built questionnaires and better uncertainty handling may mitigate Neutral difficulties.

final_notes:
Paper title: “IA2: Alignment with ICL Activations Improves Supervised Fine-Tuning.” Authors: Mishra, Khashabi, Liu.

Core: IA2 = ICL Activation Alignment, a self-distillation/priming step before SFT to make model replicate own ICL activation patterns, encouraging ICL-like internal behavior before SFT. Contrasts with output/text-only context distillation. Conclusion says ICL and SFT use different mechanisms, ICL often encodes richer/more generalizable patterns, IA2 shifts models into a more adaptable weight subspace inaccessible to SFT alone, and future work will study diversity, catastrophic forgetting, and RL-tuned models.

Notation/method: Decoder-only transformer; attention/hidden activations A are L×R×d. asim token-wise cosine. SFT CE over response tokens. ICL uses demos I plus test X, no updates. Paper title: “IA2: Alignment with ICL Activations Improves Supervised Fine-Tuning.” Authors: Aayush Mishra, Daniel Khashabi, Anqi Liu (JHU CS).

Abstract claims:
- SFT specializes model behavior by training weights to produce intended target responses for queries.
- ICL adapts models at inference using instructions/demonstrations in the prompt.
- ICL can offer better generalizability and more calibrated responses than SFT in data-scarce settings, but costs more inference compute.
- Research question: can ICL internal computations improve qualities of SFT?
- They first show ICL and SFT produce distinct activation patterns, suggesting different functional mechanisms.
- They introduce ICL Activation Alignment (IA2), a self-distillation technique to replicate ICL activation patterns in SFT models and incentivize ICL-like internal reasoning.
- IA2 is performed as a priming step before SFT.
- Claimed results: IA2 significantly improves accuracy and calibration of model outputs, based on extensive empirical results on 12 popular benchmarks and two model families.
- Claimed contribution includes practical usefulness and conceptual insight into model adaptation mechanics.

Introduction details:
- Motivation example: specialized app, e.g. news aggregator classifying articles into predefined categories.
- SFT uses labeled data; PEFT makes SFT models small parameter sets that can be loaded/offloaded efficiently. But SFT often needs many labeled samples to generalize well.
- ICL adapts/steers behavior at inference using query preceded by demonstrations/instructions. Prior work and their experiments (§5) show ICL generalizes well few-shot and typically produces calibrated responses. Cost: demos/instructions consume context space and increase per-query cost.
- They state token-space behavior of ICL and SFT may look similar, but internal activations differ (§3). Activations are treated as footprint of internal processing before next-token production; divergent activations indicate different adaptation mechanisms.
- Hypothesis: ICL activations contain rich information about extracting generalizable patterns from context; this may be absent in SFT, especially few-shot where SFT may shortcut/overfit target responses.
- Research question stated: “Can the information rich ICL activations be used to improve the quality of SFT?”
- They contrast with context distillation into weights (Snell et al. 2022; Chen et al. 2024b), saying those use response-text training signals only and may have same issues as SFT. Merely reproducing outputs of ICL-conditioned model does not ensure functioning like ICL-conditioned model.
- Proposed method IA2: self-distillation enforcing alignment with model’s own functional behavior when performing ICL (§4). Pipeline per Fig. 1: (1) collect information-rich ICL activations, (2) enforce functional alignment with ICL, then (3) perform SFT on this primed model.
- They claim IA2 priming before SFT uses the same data and drastically improves adapted model performance on a variety of text classification and generation tasks (§5).
- They claim IA2 provides an important training signal unavailable with SFT-only training.
- They claim they trained over 13,000 models spanning 12 benchmarks.
- Intro summary bullets: (1) ICL and SFT with same data do not align in activation space (§3); (2) IA2 enforces alignment with ICL functional behavior and priming drastically improves SFT (§4/Fig.1); (3) IA2 training signal is not present in SFT-only training (§5).
- Figure 1 caption: Standard SFT enforces output-space alignment only (model response vs target response; step 3), leading to subpar performance and mis-calibration in low-data settings. IA2 enforces functional alignment with ICL by matching rich activation patterns produced during ICL. IA2 before SFT boosts adaptation quality; improvements shown by performance comparison charts aggregated across models and datasets in §5.

Paper title: “IA2: Alignment with ICL Activations Improves Supervised Fine-Tuning.” Authors: Aayush Mishra, Daniel Khashabi, Anqi Liu (JHU CS).

Abstract/intro claims:
- SFT specializes model behavior by training weights to produce target responses; often needs many labeled samples. PEFT enables small parameter adapters.
- ICL adapts at inference using demonstrations/instructions in prompt; can generalize/calibrate better few-shot but costs more context/inference compute.
- Research question: can information-rich ICL activations improve SFT quality?
- They first show ICL and SFT with same data produce distinct activation patterns (§3), suggesting different mechanisms.
- IA2 = ICL Activation Alignment, a self-distillation/priming step before SFT to replicate model’s own ICL activation patterns and incentivize ICL-like internal reasoning.
- Pipeline/Fig. 1: collect ICL activations, enforce functional alignment with ICL, then SFT on primed model. Standard SFT enforces output-space alignment only and can be subpar/miscalibrated in low-data settings.
- Claimed results: IA2 significantly improves accuracy/performance and calibration on 12 popular benchmarks and two model families; trained over 13,000 models. IA2 uses same data and drastically improves adapted performance on text classification and generation tasks (§5). They claim IA2 provides a training signal unavailable with SFT-only.
- They contrast IA2 with context distillation into weights, saying output/text-only distillation may reproduce ICL outputs without making model function like ICL.

Part 2 Background/Notation:
- Model: decoder-only transformer LM M_Θ. Self-attention uses W_Q, W_K, W_V, W_O (called W_QKVO). For tokens T=[t_i]_{i=1}^R, SA output Z=[z_i] where z_i = softmax(q_i K^T / sqrt(d)) V · W_O, q_i=t_i W_Q, K=t_:i W_K, V=t_:i W_V. Z has shape R×d. They study behavior changes induced by changing context T or weights W_QKVO.
- SFT: dataset D_T={(X_i,Y_i)}_{i=1}^N. Fine-tune Θ→Θ′ so M_Θ′(X_t)=ȳ_t, where ȳ_t is first token of full generated response Ȳ_t; repeated application extends response. If Y_i has G tokens, they say generate G tokens to get Ȳ_i and minimize cross-entropy over all generated tokens: L_SFT = Σ_i Σ_j cross-entropy(Ȳ_ij, Y_ij).
- ICL: using D_T, prompt M_Θ with concatenated demonstrations I=[X_1∘Y_1∘…∘X_n∘Y_n] plus test X_t; no weight updates; M_Θ(I∘X_t)=ŷ_t. Full response Ŷ_t often similar to expected Y_t. They focus on classic ICL with input-output demo pairs. They mention frontier instruction-following can be considered a form of ICL demonstrations, but not focus.
- Activations: hidden SA outputs are activations; SA uses context tokens and produces different outputs for different token sequences. For L layers and R tokens, activation tensor A has size L×R×d. They study T=[I∘X] for ICL and T=X without ICL under different model weights. Activation similarity asim(A1,A2) is token-wise cosine similarity between two activation tensors, size L×R.

- Claimed results: IA2 significantly improves accuracy/performance and calibration on 12 popular benchmarks and two model families; trained over 13,000 models; same data; improves text classification and generation (§5). IA2 provides signal unavailable to SFT-only.
- Contrast with context distillation into weights: output/text-only distillation may reproduce ICL outputs without making model function like ICL.

Background/notation:
- Decoder-only transformer LM M_Θ. Self-attention uses W_Q, W_K, W_V, W_O (W_QKVO). For tokens T=[t_i]_{i=1}^R, SA output Z=[z_i], z_i = softmax(q_i K^T/sqrt(d)) V · W_O, q_i=t_i W_Q, K=t_:i W_K, V=t_:i W_V. Z shape R×d. They study behavior changes induced by context T or weights W_QKVO.
- SFT: D_T={(X_i,Y_i)}. Fine-tune Θ→Θ′ so M_Θ′(X_t)=ȳ_t, first token of generated response Ȳ_t; repeated generation extends response. If Y_i has G tokens, generate G tokens to get Ȳ_i and minimize L_SFT=Σ_iΣ_j CE(Ȳ_ij,Y_ij).
- ICL: prompt base M_Θ with demonstrations I=[X_1∘Y_1∘…∘X_n∘Y_n] plus test X_t; no weight updates; M_Θ(I∘X_t)=ŷ_t. Focus on classic input-output demo pairs.
- Activations: hidden SA outputs; for L layers and R tokens activation tensor A size L×R×d. They study T=[I∘X] for ICL and T=X without ICL under different weights. asim(A1,A2) = token-wise cosine similarity between activation tensors, size L×R.

Section 3 notes:
- They ask whether ICL and SFT are practically/functionally the same, motivated by prior claims that transformer ICL can implement internal gradient descent and self-attention can produce outputs as if parameters were updated using demos. If equivalent, base model with ICL demos should produce similar activations at output token positions as SFT model without demos.
- Experiment: collect ICL activations A_ICL using T=[I∘X] for 100 test samples from multiple datasets (SST2, AGNews, etc.) across Qwen3 and Llama-3.2 models, described as 1B↔16 layers, 3B↔28 layers, 4B↔36 layers. Train SFT models using same ICL demos until convergence; collect A_SFT using T=X. Details in §B. Compute asim(A_ICL,A_SFT) at output token positions, average across tokens/samples/datasets.
- Figure 2 claim: SFT-only has small layerwise similarity with ICL activations; ICL and SFT activations are not aligned across models. Activations align better near initial/final layers, misalign in middle layers where demonstration set is processed more abstractly.
- Figure 2 also apparently includes IA2→SFT, which aligns much more with ICL than SFT-only and performs better (also see Fig. 1).
- Calibration claim: Difference between ICL and SFT appears in expected calibration error (Fig. 1). ICL is much more calibrated than SFT at similar/slightly better accuracy. Suspected reason: SFT’s output-oriented signal can learn shortcuts; ICL uses complex circuits that extract generalizable patterns from demos and is well-calibrated.
- Conclusion of §3: ICL and SFT adapt through different means; SFT should not be assumed drop-in replacement for ICL. Leads to question of using ICL activations to improve SFT.

For L layers and R tokens activation tensor A is L×R×d. asim(A1,A2)=token-wise cosine similarity between activation tensors, size L×R. SFT minimizes CE over generated response tokens vs targets. IA2 trains parameters to process inputs like ICL; not explicitly incentivized to produce similar outputs. Then SFT on primed Θ′ with ground-truth Y until convergence.

§5 current experimental setup: Two settings: single-token and multi-token. Single-token tasks: (1) Sentiment: SST2, Financial Phrasebank (FinS), Poem Sentiment (PoemS); train on SST2 and FinS, evaluate all three; described as one ID and two OOD eval datasets per training condition. (2) True/False: StrategyQA (STF), multi-hop reasoning to True/False. (3) News categorization: AGNews (AGN), BBCNews (BBCN); train AGN, evaluate both. (4) MCQ: SciQ and QASC with choices remapped from A/B/C to unrelated token set, called SciQr and QASCr; train SciQr, evaluate both. Multi-token tasks: (1) Grade-school math: GSM8K and GSM Symbolic (GSM8Ks); train GSM8K, evaluate both. (2) Advanced math: MATH Algebra (HMathA). (3) Scientific QA: SciQ used for generating answer tokens rather than choosing options. These eval datasets total 12: SST2, FinS, PoemS, STF, AGN, BBCN, SciQr, QASCr, GSM8K, GSM8Ks, HMathA, SciQ.

Evaluation uses separate sampled set of 500 samples per task. More dataset/process details in §A.

Multi-token details: Outputs are standard text reasoning tokens before answer, not inside <think> tags. Demonstrations and expected outputs are CoT style. Accuracy based on parsed final answer only, parser differs by dataset. Title/claim: IA2 (ICL Activation Alignment) improves SFT by aligning with ICL activation patterns. §3: SFT and ICL outputs similar but activations distinct; ICL more calibrated; activation similarity token-wise cosine over layers/tokens at output positions. IA2→SFT aligns more with ICL than SFT-only and performs better. Models: Qwen3/Llama-3.2; 1B=16 layers, 3B=28, 4B=36.

§4 IA2: two-step pipeline: (1) align model activations to ICL activations, then (2) standard SFT on ground-truth Y. Formal target: SA([I∘X])≈SA(X) for newly generated token at each layer. Operationally generate ICL response \hat Y_i using remaining samples as demos; collect ICL activations A_ICL at output positions; feed [X_i∘\hat Y_i] without demos; minimize activation distance (text says MSE, formula sum norms). Then SFT CE on ground truth. Ambiguity in one paragraph about generated \bar Y_i vs Y_i, but enumerated step clarifies ground-truth SFT.

§5 setup: Tasks single-token (SST2/FinS/PoemS; StrategyQA/STF; AGN/BBCN; SciQr/QASCr) and multi-token (GSM8K/GSM8Ks; HMathA; SciQ generated answers). Sentiment train/source description/Table 1 had inconsistency: prose said train SST2+FinS; Table fragments show both Source=FinS and Source=SST2 for sentiment evals. N powers of 2, 5 sets; IA2 uses N−1 demos. Eval 500/task. Qwen3-4B all tasks; Llama-3.2-1B single-token except SciQr uses 3B; multi-token secondary Llama-3.2-1B-Instruct. LoRA rank 8 on W_Q,W_K,W_O. Multi-token Qwen up to N=8, Llama up to16; train max tokens G=200. Eval max tokens GSM 200, HMathA 400.

§5.1 Table 1 Qwen N=4 single-token: AGN IA2→SFT 31.8 vs SFT 27.9; BBCN* IA2→SFT 27.9 vs SFT 31.8, so not a consistent accuracy gain. FinS/SST sentiment rows show IA2→SFT large gains. SciQr/QASCr*: ICL 56.5/.08, SFT 76.5/.09, IA2 71.2/.12, IA2→SFT 79.4/.09; SciQr ID: ICL 87.7/.07, SFT 88.3/.07, IA2 90.4/.09, IA2→SFT 91.7/.05. STF row values unclear; caption says IA2→SFT outperforms SFT across board, but ECE worse than IA2/SFT in some rows if all metrics counted.

Table 2 Qwen N=4 multi-token, trained on ground truth: GSM8K w/o 56.4, ICL 76.4, SFT 70.9, IA2 77.4, IA2→SFT 73.6; GSM8Ks* 45.4,68.4,64.5,66.2,68.8; HMathA 21.0,60.4,50.4,47.8,55.3; SciQ 15.4,37.5,35.0,6.9,40.8. Text: IA2→SFT beats SFT all multi-token; sometimes worse than ICL due to imperfect compression in small LoRA rank.

§5.2: Fig.3 activation similarity vs metrics: higher ICL similarity lowers ECE; too much ICL alignment can hurt accuracy. IA2 increases similarity, IA2→SFT retains higher ICL similarity than SFT and lies between IA2 and SFT. Fig.4 weight subspace overlap: SVD of LoRA matrices, overlap=(1/r)||U1^TU2||_F^2. SFT-only updates nearly orthogonal to IA2-only and IA2→SFT; best IA2→SFT shares ~39% average subspace with IA2-only, interpreted as IA2 training signal/subspaces unreachable by SFT.

§6 simultaneous IA2+SFT: IA2 target uses model’s own ICL response tokens for G>1, may differ from ground truth, so simultaneous IA2 loss and ground-truth SFT incompatible. Instead self-distillation on ICL responses with unified loss L_IA2 + beta L_SFT. Table 3 Qwen3-4B N=4 trained with ICL responses: GSM8K w/o 56.4, ICL 76.4, SFT 66.4, IA2 77.4, IA2→SFT 67.2, IA2+SFT 77.0; GSM8Ks* 45.4,68.4,59.8,66.2,61.6,69.0; HMathA 21.0,60.4,49.0,47.8,54.0,53.6; SciQ 15.4,37.5,27.2,6.9,32.8,34.5.

KD baseline Table 4 Llama: GSM8K N=4: ICL 34.6, SFT 28.2, KD 36.1, IA2 29.3, IA2→SFT 30.3, IA2+SFT 37.0. SST2 N=8: ICL 77.0/.10, SFT 52.3/.38, KD 55.9/.16, IA2 64.9/.30, IA2→SFT 64.7/.33, IA2+SFT 66.9/.28.

§6 continuation: Text claims Qwen math ICL exceeds all training methods incl IA2, but Table 5 contradicts for GSM8K IA2 only: N=4 IA2 77.4 > ICL 76.4, N=8 IA2 78.8 > ICL 77.2. Table 5 Qwen math by shots: GSM8K N2 ICL 81.2, SFT 65.2, IA2 70.7, IA2→SFT 74.6; N4 76.4/70.9/77.4/73.6; N8 77.2/73.5/78.8/76.0. HMathA N2 58.6/47.8/33.9/48.7; N4 60.4/50.4/47.8/55.3; N8 62.1/52.0/57.3/59.4. Claim: IA2→SFT closes ICL gap with more shots and consistently beats SFT.

Other fine-tuning: IA2 pipeline not tied to LoRA; repeated with (IA)3 PEFT. Table 6 N=4 Llama-3.2 with (IA)3: SciQr→QASCr* ICL 35.6/.06, SFT 32.8/.20, IA2 34.2/.08, IA2→SFT 48.6/.25; SciQr ID 60.0/.07, 64.5/.12, 63.0/.10, 70.6/.08; SST2→FinS* 56.6/.17, 58.2/.25, 61.9/.18, 59.8/.18; SST2→PoemS* 52.3/.19, 48.1/.44, 48.1/.11, 59.8/.33; SST2 ID 60.3/.19, 52.4/.35, 54.2/.15, 62.6/.28. Caption says IA2→SFT gains over SFT and exceeds ICL accuracy all cases; accuracy supports this. Computational overhead: one-time ICL activation collection; inference same cost as SFT-only.

Potential improvements/limitations: did not explore LoRA rank/target modules, selective IA2 layer alignment, prompt/demo-order optimization, or finer IA2→SFT LR control.

§7 Related Work: claims “we found SFT to perform worse than ICL,” but this is contradicted by paper’s own results in some settings, especially Table 1 SciQr/QASCr* SFT 76.5 > ICL 56.5 and SciQr ID SFT 88.3 > ICL 87.7; thus only sometimes/often true, not general.

§8 Conclusion: claims IA2 consistently improves SFT accuracy and calibration; contradicted by BBCN* accuracy IA2→SFT 27.9 < SFT 31.8 and QASCr* ECE IA2→SFT .09 = SFT .09, so not consistent improvement.

Reproducibility statement: says code for data/training/evaluation/analysis/plotting is on GitHub; details in §5 and appendix plus README sufficient to reproduce results using repeatable seeds. No internal conflict observed in final part.

Abstract states SFT trains weights to produce target responses; ICL adapts at inference via instructions/demonstrations and can offer better generalizability/calibration than SFT in data-scarce settings but with more inference compute. Authors claim they first show ICL and SFT produce distinct activation patterns, suggesting different mechanisms. They introduce IA2, a self-distillation technique to replicate ICL activation patterns in SFT models and incentivize ICL-like internal reasoning. IA2 is performed as a priming step before SFT and is claimed to significantly improve accuracy and calibration on 12 popular benchmarks and two model families. steps.notes_before:
Title/claim: IA2 (ICL Activation Alignment) improves SFT by aligning with ICL activation patterns. §3: SFT and ICL outputs similar but activations distinct; ICL more calibrated; activation similarity token-wise cosine over layers/tokens at output positions. IA2→SFT aligns more with ICL than SFT-only and performs better. Models: Qwen3/Llama-3.2; 1B=16 layers, 3B=28, 4B=36.

§4 IA2: two-step pipeline: (1) align model activations to ICL activations, then (2) standard SFT on ground-truth Y. Formal target: SA([I∘X])≈SA(X) for newly generated token at each layer. Operationally generate ICL response \hat Y_i using remaining samples as demos; collect ICL activations A_ICL at output positions; feed [X_i∘\hat Y_i] without demos; minimize activation distance (text says MSE, formula sum norms). Then SFT CE on ground truth. Ambiguity in one paragraph about generated \bar Y_i vs Y_i, but enumerated step clarifies ground-truth SFT.

§5 setup: Tasks single-token (SST2/FinS/PoemS; StrategyQA/STF; AGN/BBCN; SciQr/QASCr) and multi-token (GSM8K/GSM8Ks; HMathA; SciQ generated answers). Sentiment train/source description/Table 1 had inconsistency: prose said train SST2+FinS; Table fragments show both Source=FinS and Source=SST2 for sentiment evals. N powers of 2, 5 sets; IA2 uses N−1 demos. Eval 500/task. Qwen3-4B all tasks; Llama-3.2-1B single-token except SciQr uses 3B; multi-token secondary Llama-3.2-1B-Instruct. LoRA rank 8 on W_Q,W_K,W_O. Multi-token Qwen up to N=8, Llama up to16; train max tokens G=200. Eval max tokens GSM 200, HMathA 400.

§5.1 Table 1 Qwen N=4 single-token: AGN IA2→SFT 31.8 vs SFT 27.9; BBCN* IA2→SFT 27.9 vs SFT 31.8; FinS/SST sentiment rows show IA2→SFT large gains. SciQr/QASCr*: ICL 56.5/.08, SFT 76.5/.09, IA2 71.2/.12, IA2→SFT 79.4/.09; SciQr ID: ICL 87.7/.07, SFT 88.3/.07, IA2 90.4/.09, IA2→SFT 91.7/.05. STF row values somewhat unclear; caption says IA2→SFT outperforms SFT across board, but ECE worse than IA2/SFT in some rows if all metrics counted.

Table 2 Qwen N=4 multi-token, trained on ground truth: GSM8K w/o 56.4, ICL 76.4, SFT 70.9, IA2 77.4, IA2→SFT 73.6; GSM8Ks* 45.4,68.4,64.5,66.2,68.8; HMathA 21.0,60.4,50.4,47.8,55.3; SciQ 15.4,37.5,35.0,6.9,40.8. Text: IA2→SFT beats SFT all multi-token; sometimes worse than ICL due to imperfect compression in small LoRA rank.

§5.2: Fig.3 activation similarity vs metrics: higher ICL similarity lowers ECE; too much ICL alignment can hurt accuracy. IA2 increases similarity, IA2→SFT retains higher ICL similarity than SFT and lies between IA2 and SFT. Fig.4 weight subspace overlap: SVD of LoRA matrices, overlap=(1/r)||U1^TU2||_F^2. SFT-only updates nearly orthogonal to IA2-only and IA2→SFT; best IA2→SFT shares ~39% average subspace with IA2-only, interpreted as IA2 training signal/subspaces unreachable by SFT.

§6 simultaneous IA2+SFT: challenge: IA2 target uses model’s own ICL response tokens for G>1, may differ from ground truth, so simultaneous IA2 loss and ground-truth SFT incompatible. Instead self-distillation on ICL responses with unified loss L_IA2 + beta L_SFT; beta 4 values between IA2-only and SFT-only; choose best LR/beta across 5 seeds. Table 3 Qwen3-4B N=4 trained with ICL responses: GSM8K w/o 56.4, ICL 76.4, SFT 66.4, IA2 77.4, IA2→SFT 67.2, IA2+SFT 77.0; GSM8Ks* 45.4,68.4,59.8,66.2,61.6,69.0; HMathA 21.0,60.4,49.0,47.8,54.0,53.6; SciQ 15.4,37.5,27.2,6.9,32.8,34.5. Text notes SFT and IA2→SFT drop vs Table 2 ground-truth training, but IA2+SFT beats SFT-only on ICL responses.

KD baseline: same model with ICL context as teacher; soft-label matching on ICL responses. Table 4 Llama: GSM8K N=4 1B-Instruct: ICL 34.6, SFT 28.2, KD 36.1, IA2 29.3, IA2→SFT 30.3, IA2+SFT 37.0. SST2 N=8 Llama-1B: ICL 77.0/.10, SFT 52.3/.38, KD 55.9/.16, IA2 64.9/.30, IA2→SFT 64.7/.33, IA2+SFT 66.9/.28. Claim: KD helps multi-token nearly reaches IA2+SFT, but lacks in single-token; IA2 consistent.

Current §6 continuation: Why IA2 training does not consistently beat ICL. Text claims Qwen math ICL exceeds all training methods incl IA2, but Table 5 contradicts for GSM8K IA2 only: N=4 IA2 77.4 > ICL 76.4, N=8 IA2 78.8 > ICL 77.2. Table 5 Qwen math by shots: GSM8K N2 ICL 81.2, SFT 65.2, IA2 70.7, IA2→SFT 74.6; N4 76.4/70.9/77.4/73.6; N8 77.2/73.5/78.8/76.0. errors.claim: “In our work, we found SFT to perform worse than ICL.”
errors.location: this part (§7 Related Work, ICL vs SFT)
errors.evidence: Earlier results include multiple cases where SFT outperforms ICL: Table 1 Qwen N=4 SciQr→QASCr* accuracy ICL 56.5 vs SFT 76.5, SciQr ID ICL 87.7 vs SFT 88.3; Table 2 GSM8Ks* ICL 68.4 vs SFT 64.5 but other rows vary; Table 5 GSM8K N=8 ICL 77.2 vs SFT 73.5, while single-token examples clearly contradict the blanket claim.
errors.explanation: The statement is too broad: the paper’s own tables show SFT sometimes performs better than ICL, especially in single-token tasks such as SciQr/QASCr and SciQr ID. The results support that SFT often or in some settings performs worse than ICL, not that SFT generally did so across the work.

errors.claim: “Extensive experiments show that IA2 consistently improves the accuracy and calibration of SFT.”
errors.evidence: Earlier notes: “§5.1 Table 1 Qwen N=4 single-token: ... BBCN* IA2→SFT 27.9 vs SFT 31.8”; and “SciQr/QASCr*: ... SFT 76.5/.09 ... IA2→SFT 79.4/.09.”
errors.explanation: IA2→SFT does not consistently improve accuracy over SFT: on BBCN* it is lower than SFT. It also does not consistently improve calibration: on QASCr* the ECE is equal to SFT rather than improved.

Paper title: “IA2: Alignment with ICL Activations Improves Supervised Fine-Tuning.” Abstract: P4Z improves output U6R/calibration across 12 benchmarks/two model families; R8D self-distills V2K activation patterns into weight-trained models; priming signal unavailable through H9C. Q7M=SFT with labels, V2K=ICL with demos. Activations A∈R^{L×R×d}; K4X=token-wise cosine activation similarity L×R. Similar outputs need not imply similar internal processing.

§3: V2K better calibrated than Q7M at similar/slightly better U6R. Base+demos vs trained-no-demos activations do not align; initial/final layers align more than middle. Fig.2: H9C low K4X; P4Z closer and performs better. Activation study used 100 test samples incl. B7V/W3F; Qwen3 and Llama-3.2 sizes/depths 1B/16, 3B/28, 4B/36.

Method: After priming Θ→Θ′, collect ybar_i from M_Θ′ then train ground truth Y_i with L_Q7M to convergence. R8D/IA2 aligns layerwise processing, not outputs. Desired SA([I∘X];W)≈SA(X;Wtilde) at generated token index -1. For X_i use remaining samples as demos, generate hatY_i from [I∘X_i], collect output-position A^i_V2K∈R^{L×G×d}; query-only [X_i∘hatY_i] gets A^i. Loss called MSE but Eq.4 is sum_i ||A^i−A^i_V2K||, not squared/meaned.

Setup: train to convergence up to 50 epochs, LRs 1e-4/3e-4/1e-3, best selected; >13k models. Rank-8 LoRA attention W_Q,W_K,W_O. Multi-token N restricted/max 16 Llama and 8 Qwen. Activation cap G=200; target-token training uses ground-truth response length. Single-token U6R=accuracy, D8P=ECE. Base demos evaluated 5 times; trained methods no demos. Multi-token exact/format correctness, no calibration. Gen limits 200 GSM8K/GSM Symbolic, 400 MATH Algebra. Qwen3-4B-Base all tasks. Llama-3.2-1B all single-token except E2T uses 3B; multi-token secondary Llama-3.2-1B-Instruct.

Datasets/12: B7V=SST2, Z2H=Financial Phrasebank, C9L=Poem Sentiment; N5Q=StrategyQA; W3F=AGNews, Y8J=BBCNews; E2T=SciQr train/eval, G6A=QASCr eval; L9S=GSM8K, X4C=GSM Symbolic; V7B=MATH Algebra; O3D=SciQ. Few-shot N powers of two, five sets/N; A_V2K uses other N−1 samples as demos; eval 500/task. Multi-token CoT: GSM reasoning #### number; V7B boxed; O3D support #### answer.

§5.1 claims P4Z outperforms H9C in almost all single-token U6R/calibration, usually exceeds V2K U6R but slightly worse calibration. J3N often high U6R and V2K-like calibration. Table 1 Qwen N=4 single-token: caption says P4Z outperforms Q7M across board, but W3F→Y8J H9C U6R 31.8 > P4Z 27.9; P4Z below V2K on Y8J and N5Q. §5.2 weight analysis: unchanged base weights significantly influence LoRA activations; activation patterns alone cannot isolate training-induced behavior. Gains attributed to R8D subspaces unreachable through H9C. Fig.4: P4Z high A5Y with J3N, H9C aligns with neither. Fig.3: D8P decreases smoothly with similarity; extreme similarity need not optimize U6R because V2K signal not always correct.

§6: T6B = simultaneous IA2+SFT, loss L_R8D+β L_Q7M, β spans J3N to H9C; target tensor uses model’s own generated response tokens when G>1, so V2K response may differ in length from GT and joint GT objectives incompatible. Text says H9C/P4Z on V2K responses worse than GT, supported vs Table2. Table4 KD/F5W comparator: Llama L9S N=4 V2K 34.6, H9C 28.2, F5W 36.1, J3N 29.3, P4Z 30.3, T6B 37.0; B7V N=8 V2K 77.0/.10, H9C 52.3/.38, F5W 55.9/.16, J3N 64.9/.30, P4Z 64.7/.33, T6B 66.9/.28. Table5 Qwen math shots: L9S N=2/4/8 V2K 81.2/76.4/77.2, H9C 65.2/70.9/73.5, J3N 70.7/77.4/78.8, P4Z 74.6/73.6/76.0; V7B N=2/4/8 V2K 58.6/60.4/62.1, H9C 47.8/50.4/52.0, J3N 33.9/47.8/57.3, P4Z 48.7/55.3/59.4. Claim: V2K exceeds every training method on some Qwen math cases incl. L9S and V7B; L9S V2K at N=2 exceeds N=4,8; P4Z gap to V2K closes with more shots, superiority to H9C remains.

Part 10: Other PEFT methods discussed; pipeline improves signals rather than competing with LoRA/full-rank/prefix/(IA)3; other Q7M methods deferred. Table6 Llama-3.2 N=4 trained with (IA)3 on few single-token datasets: P4Z U6R exceeds H9C and V2K in all rows. Values: E2T→G6A V2K/H9C/J3N/P4Z 35.6/32.8/34.2/48.6; E2T 60.0/64.5/63.0/70.6; B7V→Z2H 56.6/58.2/61.9/59.8; C9L 52.3/48.1/48.1/59.8; B7V 60.3/52.4/54.2/62.6. D8P not always better for P4Z (e.g. G6A P4Z .25 worse than others). Potential improvements: rank/module ablations, selective R8D, prompt optimization, finer control of two signals; extreme alignment can hurt; demo order affects V2K.

Context distillation section says prior approaches distill contextual effects on outputs through token-response signals; this work uses model’s own contextual processing signals. Activation steering differs from R8D because R8D seeks large behavioral change rather than targeted narrow-domain interventions.

§8 Conclusion: activation probing distinguishes adaptation mechanisms; V2K often encodes richer/more generalizable patterns; R8D shifts models into more adaptable weight subspace inaccessible to Q7M alone. Future work: diversity, catastrophic forgetting, post-training benefits, post-trained/RL-tuned models. Reproducibility: GitHub code, appendix/README/seeds.

Introduction part 1: Motivation is specialized LLM applications such as news-aggregator classification. PEFT methods allow small adapted parameter sets to be loaded/unloaded efficiently. Generalization through Q7M usually needs many labeled samples; V2K demonstrations/instructions instead consume context and increase inference compute, reducing room for query/response tokens. Research question: can information-rich V2K activations improve Q7M quality? Hypothesis: V2K activations contain information for extracting generalizable contextual patterns, potentially missing from few-shot weight adaptation, which may learn shortcuts/overfit target responses. Similar token outputs need not mean similar internal processing; divergent activations imply distinct adaptation mechanisms. Context-to-weight distillation via response text can inherit output-training problems because reproducing a context-conditioned model’s outputs does not ensure reproducing its function.

Figure 1 description: Standard Q7M enforces output-space agreement between response and target, described as the third step of the proposed pipeline, and produces subpar performance/miscalibration under low data. Proposed pipeline: collect rich V2K activations, enforce functional alignment, then train against target responses. Figure comparison charts aggregate performance across models and datasets; details to appear in §5.

final_notes:
Paper title: “IA2: Alignment with ICL Activations Improves Supervised Fine-Tuning.” Authors: Aayush Mishra, Daniel Khashabi, Anqi Liu.

Core: IA2 = ICL Activation Alignment, self-distillation/priming before SFT to make model replicate its own ICL activation patterns. Claimed improvements on 12 benchmarks/two model families; >13,000 models. Contrasts with output/text-only context distillation.

Notation/method: Decoder-only transformer. Activation tensor A is L×R×d. asim(A1,A2)=token-wise cosine similarity, L×R. SFT CE over response tokens. ICL uses demos I plus test X, no updates. IA2 collects model ICL responses Ŷ_i from [I∘X_i] and target activations A_ICL at output positions; then feeds [X_i∘Ŷ_i] and aligns activations via loss described as MSE but displayed as sum norm. IA2 then SFTs on ground-truth Y. IA2 not explicitly incentivized to output same text.

Setup: Single-token tasks SST2/FinS/PoemS; STF; AGN/BBCN; SciQr/QASCr. Multi-token GSM8K/GSM8Ks, HMathA, SciQ generative. 12 eval datasets. Few-shot N powers of 2, 5 sets per N; IA2 uses remaining N−1 samples as demos for each X_i. Eval 500/task. Qwen3-4B all tasks; Llama-3.2-1B single-token except SciQr uses 3B; multi-token secondary Llama-3.2-1B-Instruct. LoRA rank 8 on W_Q,W_K,W_O. Multi-token N up to 16 Llama, up to 8 Qwen. Max generated training tokens G=200; IA2 activation tensor said R^{L×200×d}; SFT G=ground-truth count. Train up to 50 epochs, LRs 1e-4/3e-4/1e-3; best chosen. Eval single-token first generated token accuracy/ECE; ICL avg 5 demo draws; training no demos. Multi-token max eval 200 GSM, 400 HMathA; no calibration.

Internal errors found: (1) Table 1 Qwen N=4 caption/text says IA2→SFT outperforms standard SFT across the board, but AGN→BBCN SFT acc 31.8 vs IA2→SFT 27.9, false for accuracy. (2) §6 KD paragraph says soft-label matching performs significantly worse than standard SFT in multi-token, but Table 4 has soft-label SFT better than SFT on GSM8K (36.1 vs 28.2). (3) Table 5 discussion claims ICL exceeds all training methods for GSM8K/HMathA, but GSM8K IA2-only beats ICL at N=4 (77.4 vs 76.4) and N=8 (78.8 vs 77.2). (4) Related Work says “we found SFT to perform worse than ICL,” but Table 6 has SFT > ICL in some cases: SciQr from SciQr 64.5 vs 60.0 and SST2 from FinS 58.2 vs 56.6. (5) Conclusion says IA2 consistently improves accuracy and calibration of SFT, but Table 1 has AGN→BBCN IA2→SFT accuracy below SFT (27.9 vs 31.8), and Table 6 has SciQr from QASCr IA2→SFT ECE worse than SFT (.25 vs .20).

Table 2 Qwen N=4 multi-token ground-truth: GSM8K w/o 56.4, ICL 76.4, SFT 70.9, IA2 77.4, IA2→SFT 73.6. GSM8Ks*: 45.4, 68.4, 64.5, 66.2, 68.8. HMathA: 21.0, 60.4, 50.4, 47.8, 55.3. SciQ: 15.4, 37.5, 35.0, 6.9, 40.8. Text says IA2→SFT outperforms SFT-only across all multi-token datasets; true. IA2→SFT sometimes worse than ICL.

§5.2: Fig.3 activation similarity vs acc/ECE: more similarity lowers ECE; extreme alignment may leave accuracy gains. Fig.2: IA2 raises similarity; IA2→SFT retains higher similarity after SFT. IA2→SFT lies between IA2 and SFT in similarity while better accuracy/calibration. Subspace overlap Fig.4: SVD LoRA weights; overlap=(1/r)||U1^T U2||_F^2. SFT-only almost orthogonal to IA2-only/IA2→SFT. Most performant IA2→SFT shares ~39% avg spanned weight space with IA2-only.

§6 simultaneous IA2+SFT: Hard because IA2 target uses ICL-generated response tokens, may differ from ground truth. Unified loss on ICL responses. Table 3 Qwen N=4 ICL responses: GSM8K SFT 66.4, IA2 77.4, IA2→SFT 67.2, IA2+SFT 77.0; GSM8Ks 59.8,66.2,61.6,69.0; HMathA 49.0,47.8,54.0,53.6; SciQ 27.2,6.9,32.8,34.5. They say SFT and IA2→SFT drop vs Table 2 ground-truth; true. IA2+SFT > SFT-only.

§6 KD baseline Table 4 Llama: GSM8K N=4 ICL 34.6, SFT 28.2, soft-label SFT 36.1, IA2 29.3, IA2→SFT 30.3, IA2+SFT 37.0. SST2 N=8 ICL 77.0/.10, SFT 52.3/.38, soft-label 55.9/.16, IA2 64.9/.30, IA2→SFT 64.7/.33, IA2+SFT 66.9/.28.

Table 5 Qwen math shot counts: GSM8K N=2 ICL 81.2, SFT 65.2, IA2 70.7, IA2→SFT 74.6; N=4 76.4/70.9/77.4/73.6; N=8 77.2/73.5/78.8/76.0. HMathA N=2 58.6/47.8/33.9/48.7; N=4 60.4/50.4/47.8/55.3; N=8 62.1/52.0/57.3/59.4. Claim IA2→SFT consistently beats SFT-only in Table 5 true.

Table 6 Llama-3.2 with (IA)3, N=4: SciQr from QASCr*: ICL 35.6/.06, SFT 32.8/.20, IA2 34.2/.08, IA2→SFT 48.6/.25. SciQr from SciQr: 60.0/.07, 64.5/.12, 63.0/.10, 70.6/.08. SST2 from FinS*: 56.6/.17, 58.2/.25, 61.9/.18, 59.8/.18. SST2 from PoemS*: 52.3/.19, 48.1/.44, 48.1/.11, 59.8/.33. SST2 from SST2: 60.3/.19, 52.4/.35, 54.2/.15, 62.6/.28. Caption says IA2→SFT gains over SFT-only, exceeding ICL accuracy in all cases; accuracy supports this, ECE not always better.

Computational overhead: IA2→SFT requires one-time activation collection by ICL inference; inference cost same as SFT-only. Reproducibility statement: code for data/download/training/eval/analysis/plotting on GitHub; §5+appendix+README with seeds claimed sufficient to reproduce.

Future/conclusion: design choices fixed due to resource constraints; future ablations include LoRA rank/target modules and selective IA2. Reiterate extreme alignment can hurt performance; selectively aligning layers may help. Other future work: prompt/demo-order optimization before collecting target activations; finer-grained learning-rate/control for IA2→SFT; effects on diversity/catastrophic forgetting; IA2 on RL-tuned models. Conclusion claims ICL and SFT adapt through different mechanisms, ICL often encodes richer/more generalizable patterns, IA2 primes ICL-like internal behavior and shifts models into more adaptable weight subspace “inaccessible to SFT alone.”

- Claimed contribution includes practical usefulness and conceptual insight into model adaptation mechanics.

Introduction details:
- Motivation example: specialized app, e.g. news aggregator classifying articles into predefined categories.
- SFT uses labeled data; PEFT makes SFT models small parameter sets that can be loaded/offloaded efficiently. But SFT often needs many labeled samples to generalize well.
- ICL adapts/steers behavior at inference using query preceded by demonstrations/instructions. Prior work and their experiments (§5) show ICL generalizes well few-shot and typically produces calibrated responses. Cost: demos/instructions consume context space and increase per-query cost.
- They state token-space behavior of ICL and SFT may look similar, but internal activations differ (§3). Activations are treated as footprint of internal processing before next-token production; divergent activations indicate different adaptation mechanisms.
- Hypothesis: ICL activations contain rich information about extracting generalizable patterns from context; this may be absent in SFT, especially few-shot where SFT may shortcut/overfit target responses.
- Research question stated: “Can the information rich ICL activations be used to improve the quality of SFT?”
- They contrast with context distillation into weights (Snell et al. 2022; Chen et al. 2024b), saying those use response-text training signals only and may have same issues as SFT. Merely reproducing outputs of ICL-conditioned model does not ensure functioning like ICL-conditioned model.
- Proposed method IA2: self-distillation enforcing alignment with model’s own functional behavior when performing ICL (§4). Pipeline per Fig. 1: (1) collect information-rich ICL activations, (2) enforce functional alignment with ICL, then (3) perform SFT on this primed model.
- They claim IA2 priming before SFT uses the same data and drastically improves adapted model performance on a variety of text classification and generation tasks (§5).
- They claim IA2 provides an important training signal unavailable with SFT-only training.
- They claim they trained over 13,000 models spanning 12 benchmarks.
- Intro summary bullets: (1) ICL and SFT with same data do not align in activation space (§3); (2) IA2 enforces alignment with ICL functional behavior and priming drastically improves SFT (§4/Fig.1); (3) IA2 training signal is not present in SFT-only training (§5).
- Figure 1 caption: Standard SFT enforces output-space alignment only (model response vs target response; step 3), leading to subpar performance and mis-calibration in low-data settings. IA2 enforces functional alignment with ICL by matching rich activation patterns produced during ICL. IA2 before SFT boosts adaptation quality; improvements shown by performance comparison charts aggregated across models and datasets in §5.

Paper title: “IA2: Alignment with ICL Activations Improves Supervised Fine-Tuning.” Authors: Aayush Mishra, Daniel Khashabi, Anqi Liu (JHU CS).

Abstract/intro claims:
- SFT specializes model behavior by training weights to produce target responses; often needs many labeled samples. PEFT enables small parameter adapters.
- ICL adapts at inference using demonstrations/instructions in prompt; can generalize/calibrate better few-shot but costs more context/inference compute.
- Research question: can information-rich ICL activations improve SFT quality?
- They first show ICL and SFT with same data produce distinct activation patterns (§3), suggesting different mechanisms.
- IA2 = ICL Activation Alignment, a self-distillation/priming step before SFT to replicate model’s own ICL activation patterns and incentivize ICL-like internal reasoning.
- Pipeline/Fig. 1: collect ICL activations, enforce functional alignment with ICL, then SFT on primed model. Standard SFT enforces output-space alignment only and can be subpar/miscalibrated in low-data settings.
- Claimed results: IA2 significantly improves accuracy/performance and calibration on 12 popular benchmarks and two model families; trained over 13,000 models. IA2 uses same data and drastically improves adapted performance on text classification and generation tasks (§5). They claim IA2 provides a training signal unavailable with SFT-only.
- They contrast IA2 with context distillation into weights, saying output/text-only distillation may reproduce ICL outputs without making model function like ICL.

Part 2 Background/Notation:
- Model: decoder-only transformer LM M_Θ. Self-attention uses W_Q, W_K, W_V, W_O (called W_QKVO). For tokens T=[t_i]_{i=1}^R, SA output Z=[z_i] where z_i = softmax(q_i K^T / sqrt(d)) V · W_O, q_i=t_i W_Q, K=t_:i W_K, V=t_:i W_V. Z has shape R×d. They study behavior changes induced by changing context T or weights W_QKVO.
- SFT: dataset D_T={(X_i,Y_i)}_{i=1}^N. Fine-tune Θ→Θ′ so M_Θ′(X_t)=ȳ_t, where ȳ_t is first token of full generated response Ȳ_t; repeated application extends response. If Y_i has G tokens, they say generate G tokens to get Ȳ_i and minimize cross-entropy over all generated tokens: L_SFT = Σ_i Σ_j cross-entropy(Ȳ_ij, Y_ij).
- ICL: using D_T, prompt M_Θ with concatenated demonstrations I=[X_1∘Y_1∘…∘X_n∘Y_n] plus test X_t; no weight updates; M_Θ(I∘X_t)=ŷ_t. Full response Ŷ_t often similar to expected Y_t. They focus on classic ICL with input-output demo pairs. They mention frontier instruction-following can be considered a form of ICL demonstrations, but not focus.
- Activations: hidden SA outputs are activations; SA uses context tokens and produces different outputs for different token sequences. For L layers and R tokens, activation tensor A has size L×R×d. They study T=[I∘X] for ICL and T=X without ICL under different model weights. Activation similarity asim(A1,A2) is token-wise cosine similarity between two activation tensors, size L×R.

Paper title: “IA2: Alignment with ICL Activations Improves Supervised Fine-Tuning.” Authors: Aayush Mishra, Daniel Khashabi, Anqi Liu (JHU CS).

Core claims/motivation:
- SFT adapts weights to produce target responses; often needs many labeled samples. PEFT uses small adapters.
- ICL adapts at inference using demos/instructions in prompt; may generalize/calibrate better few-shot but costs more context/inference compute.
- Research question: can information-rich ICL activations improve SFT quality?

- Claimed results: IA2 significantly improves accuracy/performance and calibration on 12 popular benchmarks and two model families; trained over 13,000 models; same data; improves text classification and generation (§5). IA2 provides signal unavailable to SFT-only.
- Contrast with context distillation into weights: output/text-only distillation may reproduce ICL outputs without making model function like ICL.

Background/notation:
- Decoder-only transformer LM M_Θ. Self-attention uses W_Q, W_K, W_V, W_O (W_QKVO). For tokens T=[t_i]_{i=1}^R, SA output Z=[z_i], z_i = softmax(q_i K^T/sqrt(d)) V · W_O, q_i=t_i W_Q, K=t_:i W_K, V=t_:i W_V. Z shape R×d. They study behavior changes induced by context T or weights W_QKVO.
- SFT: D_T={(X_i,Y_i)}. Fine-tune Θ→Θ′ so M_Θ′(X_t)=ȳ_t, first token of generated response Ȳ_t; repeated generation extends response. If Y_i has G tokens, generate G tokens to get Ȳ_i and minimize L_SFT=Σ_iΣ_j CE(Ȳ_ij,Y_ij).
- ICL: prompt base M_Θ with demonstrations I=[X_1∘Y_1∘…∘X_n∘Y_n] plus test X_t; no weight updates; M_Θ(I∘X_t)=ŷ_t. Focus on classic input-output demo pairs.
- Activations: hidden SA outputs; for L layers and R tokens activation tensor A size L×R×d. They study T=[I∘X] for ICL and T=X without ICL under different weights. asim(A1,A2) = token-wise cosine similarity between activation tensors, size L×R.

Section 3 notes:
- They ask whether ICL and SFT are practically/functionally the same, motivated by prior claims that transformer ICL can implement internal gradient descent and self-attention can produce outputs as if parameters were updated using demos. If equivalent, base model with ICL demos should produce similar activations at output token positions as SFT model without demos.
- Experiment: collect ICL activations A_ICL using T=[I∘X] for 100 test samples from multiple datasets (SST2, AGNews, etc.) across Qwen3 and Llama-3.2 models, described as 1B↔16 layers, 3B↔28 layers, 4B↔36 layers. Train SFT models using same ICL demos until convergence; collect A_SFT using T=X. Details in §B. Compute asim(A_ICL,A_SFT) at output token positions, average across tokens/samples/datasets.
- Figure 2 claim: SFT-only has small layerwise similarity with ICL activations; ICL and SFT activations are not aligned across models. Activations align better near initial/final layers, misalign in middle layers where demonstration set is processed more abstractly.
- Figure 2 also apparently includes IA2→SFT, which aligns much more with ICL than SFT-only and performs better (also see Fig. 1).
- Calibration claim: Difference between ICL and SFT appears in expected calibration error (Fig. 1). ICL is much more calibrated than SFT at similar/slightly better accuracy. Suspected reason: SFT’s output-oriented signal can learn shortcuts; ICL uses complex circuits that extract generalizable patterns from demos and is well-calibrated.
- Conclusion of §3: ICL and SFT adapt through different means; SFT should not be assumed drop-in replacement for ICL. Leads to question of using ICL activations to improve SFT.

errors.claim: “Then, we simply train the model to minimize the mean squared error between the two activations …: 𝓛_IA2 = Σ_i ||A^i − A^i_ICL||.”
errors.evidence: The stated loss formula is a sum of norms, not a mean squared error: “𝓛_IA2 = Σ_i ||A^i − A^i_ICL||.”
errors.explanation: Calling the objective mean squared error conflicts with the displayed equation, which does not show either squaring or averaging unless the norm notation is being used nonstandardly.

Paper title: “IA2: Alignment with ICL Activations Improves Supervised Fine-Tuning.” Authors: Aayush Mishra, Daniel Khashabi, Anqi Liu (JHU CS).

Core claims/motivation: IA2 = ICL Activation Alignment, a self-distillation/priming step before SFT that makes model replicate its own ICL activation patterns, incentivizing ICL-like internal reasoning before standard SFT. Claimed improvements in performance and calibration on 12 benchmarks and two model families; trained over 13,000 models. Contrasts with output/text-only context distillation.

Background/notation: Decoder-only transformer; self-attention outputs Z, activations are hidden SA outputs. For L layers and R tokens activation tensor A is L×R×d. asim(A1,A2)=token-wise cosine similarity between activation tensors, size L×R. SFT minimizes CE over generated response tokens vs targets. ICL uses demos I=[X1∘Y1…Xn∘Yn] plus test X, no weight updates.

§3 notes: They test whether ICL and SFT are functionally/practically same. Collect A_ICL using [I∘X] for 100 test samples from multiple datasets across Qwen3 and Llama-3.2 models (1B/16 layers, 3B/28, 4B/36 noted). Train SFT models on same ICL demos until convergence, collect A_SFT using X alone. Fig. 2: SFT-only has low layerwise similarity with ICL activations, especially middle layers; IA2→SFT aligns more with ICL and performs better. Claim: ICL more calibrated than SFT at similar/slightly better accuracy (Fig. 1). Conclusion: ICL and SFT adapt differently; SFT not drop-in replacement for ICL.

§4 method: Two-step pipeline: IA2 priming then SFT. IA2 goal per layer: modified attention weights W̃_QKVO such that SA([I∘X];W_QKVO) ≈ SA(X;W̃_QKVO) for new token. Practical procedure: generate model responses Ŷ_i using ICL prompts [I∘X_i], collect ICL activations at output positions A^i_ICL∈R^{L×G×d}; then feed query plus generated response only [X_i∘Ŷ_i] and collect A^i at output positions. IA2 loss described as mean squared error, but displayed as L_IA2=Σ_i ||A^i−A^i_ICL|| (possible inconsistency to watch: not explicitly squared/mean). IA2 trains parameters to process inputs like ICL; not explicitly incentivized to produce similar outputs. Then SFT on primed Θ′ with ground-truth Y until convergence.

§5 current experimental setup: Two settings: single-token and multi-token. Single-token tasks: (1) Sentiment: SST2, Financial Phrasebank (FinS), Poem Sentiment (PoemS); train on SST2 and FinS, evaluate all three; described as one ID and two OOD eval datasets per training condition. (2) True/False: StrategyQA (STF), multi-hop reasoning to True/False. (3) News categorization: AGNews (AGN), BBCNews (BBCN); train AGN, evaluate both. (4) MCQ: SciQ and QASC with choices remapped from A/B/C to unrelated token set, called SciQr and QASCr; train SciQr, evaluate both. Multi-token tasks: (1) Grade-school math: GSM8K and GSM Symbolic (GSM8Ks); train GSM8K, evaluate both. (2) Advanced math: MATH Algebra (HMathA). (3) Scientific QA: SciQ used for generating answer tokens rather than choosing options. These eval datasets total 12: SST2, FinS, PoemS, STF, AGN, BBCN, SciQr, QASCr, GSM8K, GSM8Ks, HMathA, SciQ.

Data setup: Few-shot/data-scarce. For each task create multiple D_T of size N varying in powers of 2 [2,4,8,16,…]. Create 5 different sets at each N to average out outliers. For IA2, collect A^i_ICL for each X_i using remaining N−1 training samples as ICL demonstrations in random order, reusing same training samples to ensure fair same-data comparison. Evaluation uses separate sampled set of 500 samples per task. More dataset/process details in §A.

Multi-token details: Outputs are standard text reasoning tokens before answer, not inside <think> tags. Demonstrations and expected outputs are CoT style. Accuracy based on parsed final answer only, parser differs by dataset. GSM8K/GSM8Ks ground truth pattern: “<reasoning steps> #### <numerical answer>”; reasoning correctness/conciseness ignored; numerical answer exact match, with other common parsing like “The answer is <value>” allowed. HMathA answers expected in \boxed{} and parsed accordingly. SciQ generated ground-truth format like GSM8K: “<support text> #### <text answer>”; parsed accordingly, exact string match only.

Multi-token: GSM8K/GSM Symbolic (GSM8Ks), train GSM8K eval both; HMath Algebra (HMathA); SciQ generative. Each method/dataset trained until convergence up to 50 epochs with LRs 1e-4, 3e-4, 1e-3; best performing chosen.

Evaluation: Single-token accuracy and ECE from first generated token probability distribution. Base ICL evaluated 5 times with different demos, report average. Training methods evaluated without ICL demos; report best-performing average metrics. Multi-token eval max tokens: 200 for GSM8K/GSM8Ks (95th percentile lengths 184/154), 400 for HMathA (95th percentile 307); only accuracy, no calibration.

§5.1 single-token results: Table 1 Qwen, N=4. Claimed IA2→SFT beats SFT-only in almost all cases on accuracy and calibration with same data; usually beats ICL accuracy with slightly worse calibration; IA2-only often high accuracy/reasonably calibrated despite no target-token training. Visible Table 1 rows: AGN→AGN: ICL 30.0/ece .13, SFT 27.9/.52, IA2 24.0/.11, IA2→SFT 31.8/.35. AGN→BBCN*: 28.8/.12, 31.8/.56, 24.3/.10, 27.9/.40. FinS→FinS: 63.6/.12, 67.4/.31, 63.1/.24, 78.7/.16. FinS→PoemS*: 56.9/.12, 49.9/.48, 52.8/.15, 60.6/.36. FinS→SST2*: 70.1/.17, 59.4/.20, 69.8/.30, 71.4/.20.

final_notes:
Paper title: “IA2: Alignment with ICL Activations Improves Supervised Fine-Tuning.” Abstract claims P4Z improves U6R/calibration across 12 benchmarks/two model families; R8D self-distills V2K activation patterns into weight-trained models; priming signal unavailable through H9C. Conclusion: activation probing distinguishes mechanisms; V2K often has richer/generalizable patterns; R8D shifts models into more adaptable weight subspace inaccessible to Q7M alone; future work on diversity/catastrophic forgetting and RL-tuned models. Reproducibility claims GitHub code covers data/download/training/eval/analysis/plotting and seeds suffice.

Definitions/method: Q7M=SFT with labels; V2K=ICL with demos; H9C=standard target-token SFT? J3N=activation alignment only? P4Z=sequential R8D then Q7M using ground truths. K4X=token-wise cosine activation similarity L×R. Similar outputs need not mean similar activations. R8D collects V2K output-position activations A_V2K for [demos∘X_i], then query-only [X_i∘hatY_i] activations A^i, minimizes activation difference. Eq.4 described as MSE but shown unsquared/unmeaned norm. Training up to 50 epochs; LoRA rank 8 on W_Q,W_K,W_O; eval 500/task. Multi-token gen limits 200 GSM8K/GSM Symbolic, 400 MATH Algebra; no calibration except single-token. Datasets: B7V SST2, Z2H Financial Phrasebank, C9L Poem Sentiment; N5Q StrategyQA; W3F AGNews, Y8J BBCNews; E2T SciQr, G6A QASCr; L9S GSM8K, X4C GSM Symbolic; V7B MATH Algebra; O3D SciQ.

§5.1 claimed P4Z beats H9C almost all single-token cases and usually exceeds V2K U6R but slightly worse calibration. Table 1 Qwen N=4 single-token: caption says P4Z outperforms Q7M across board, but W3F→Y8J H9C U6R 31.8 > P4Z 27.9, though P4Z D8P 0.40 < 0.56. P4Z below V2K on Y8J 27.9<28.8 and N5Q 62.4<66.0.

Table 2 Qwen N=4 multi-token ground-truth training: Without/V2K/H9C/J3N/P4Z U6R: L9S→L9S 56.4/76.4/70.9/77.4/73.6; L9S→X4C 45.4/68.4/64.5/66.2/68.8; V7B→V7B 21.0/60.4/50.4/47.8/55.3; O3D→O3D 15.4/37.5/35.0/6.9/40.8. Text said P4Z exceeds H9C every case but sometimes underperforms V2K; supported.

Weight/activation analysis: A5Y subspace overlap (1/r)||U1^T U2||_F^2. H9C updates nearly orthogonal; P4Z shares J3N subspace mean ~39%. Fig.2/3: priming increases K4X; P4Z intermediate K4X and better U6R/calibration. D8P decreases with similarity; extreme V2K-like alignment need not maximize U6R.

§6: T6B=simultaneous IA2+SFT/self-distillation on V2K responses, loss L_R8D + beta L_Q7M; beta spans J3N to H9C; multi-token best LR,beta over five seeds. Table 3 Qwen N=4 multi-token when training on V2K responses instead of ground truths: L9S H9C 66.4, J3N 77.4, P4Z 67.2, T6B 77.0; X4C H9C 59.8, J3N 66.2, P4Z 61.6, T6B 69.0; V7B H9C 49.0, J3N 47.8, P4Z 54.0, T6B 53.6; O3D H9C 27.2, J3N 6.9, P4Z 32.8, T6B 34.5. Compared to ground-truth Table2, H9C/P4Z are worse when trained on V2K responses; T6B > H9C all rows.

Computational overhead: P4Z adds one pretraining activation-collection pass via V2K inference; inference same cost as H9C. Table 4 compares M8G/KD soft labels/F5W on Llama: L9S N=4 V2K 34.6, H9C 28.2, F5W 36.1, J3N 29.3, P4Z 30.3, T6B 37.0; B7V N=8 V2K 77.0 D8P .10, H9C 52.3 .38, F5W 55.9 .16, J3N 64.9 .30, P4Z 64.7 .33, T6B 66.9 .28. Caption says F5W improves on standard Q7M in multi-token case; paragraph contradicts by saying F5W performs significantly worse than standard Q7M in multi-token case.

Failure to consistently exceed V2K: text says on some Qwen math multi-token cases, including L9S and V7B, V2K exceeds every training method; explanation Qwen STEM mid-training; L9S V2K N=2 exceeds N=4,8. Table 5: L9S N2 V2K/H9C/J3N/P4Z 81.2/65.2/70.7/74.6; N4 76.4/70.9/77.4/73.6; N8 77.2/73.5/78.8/76.0. V7B N2 58.6/47.8/33.9/48.7; N4 60.4/50.4/47.8/55.3; N8 62.1/52.0/57.3/59.4. P4Z gap to V2K shrinks with more shots; P4Z remains >H9C.

Other fine-tuning methods: pipeline improves training signals, not competing with adapters. Table 6 Llama-3.2 N=4 with (IA)3: E2T→G6A V2K/H9C/J3N/P4Z 35.6/32.8/34.2/48.6; E2T→E2T 60.0/64.5/63.0/70.6; B7V→Z2H 56.6/58.2/61.9/59.8; B7V→C9L 52.3/48.1/48.1/59.8; B7V→B7V 60.3/52.4/54.2/62.6. Caption says P4Z significantly exceeds H9C and exceeds V2K U6R in all cases; table supports U6R comparisons, though J3N exceeds P4Z on Z2H. Potential improvements: LoRA rank/target modules, selective R8D, prompt optimization, finer control; extreme alignment can hurt, layer sensitivity varies, demo order affects V2K.

§7 Related Work claims “V2K versus Q7M... present experiments find Q7M worse,” but conflicts with rows where H9C/Q7M exceeds V2K: Table 6 E2T→E2T and B7V→Z2H, and Table 1 W3F→Y8J.

final_notes:
Paper title: “IA2: Alignment with ICL Activations Improves Supervised Fine-Tuning.” IA2 = ICL Activation Alignment, a priming/self-distillation step before SFT to make model replicate its own ICL activation patterns. Claimed improvements on 12 benchmarks/two model families; >13,000 models.

Method: Decoder-only transformer; activation tensor A is L×R×d. asim token-wise cosine. SFT minimizes CE over response tokens. ICL uses demos I plus test X. IA2 pipeline: generate model responses Ŷ_i from ICL prompts [I∘X_i], collect ICL activations at output positions A_ICL; feed [X_i∘Ŷ_i], collect A; train LoRA parameters to align activations via displayed norm loss (called MSE). Then SFT on primed Θ′ with ground-truth Y. IA2 not explicitly trained to match outputs.

Setup: 12 datasets: single-token SST2/FinS/PoemS/STF/AGN/BBCN/SciQr/QASCr; multi-token GSM8K/GSM8Ks/HMathA/SciQ. Few-shot N powers of 2, 5 sets per N. IA2 uses remaining N−1 training samples as demos. Eval 500 samples/task. Qwen3-4B-Base all tasks; Llama-3.2-1B most single-token, 3B for SciQr, 1B-Instruct for multi-token. LoRA rank 8 modifies W_Q,W_K,W_O. Multi-token max generated tokens G=200 training; eval 200 GSM, 400 HMathA. Single-token acc/ECE first generated token; ICL averaged over 5 demo draws.

Prior results: Table 1 Qwen N=4 single-token caption/text said IA2→SFT outperforms standard SFT across the board, but AGN→BBCN SFT acc 31.8 > IA2→SFT 27.9, so not true for accuracy. Other values: FinS→FinS IA2→SFT 78.7 vs SFT 67.4; SST2→SST2 90.4 vs 65.2; SciQr→SciQr 91.7 vs 88.3.

Paper title: “IA2: Alignment with ICL Activations Improves Supervised Fine-Tuning.” Authors: Aayush Mishra, Daniel Khashabi, Anqi Liu (JHU CS).

Abstract claims:
- SFT specializes model behavior by training weights to produce intended target responses for queries.
- ICL adapts models at inference using instructions/demonstrations in the prompt.
- ICL can offer better generalizability and more calibrated responses than SFT in data-scarce settings, but costs more inference compute.
- Research question: can ICL internal computations improve qualities of SFT?
- They first show ICL and SFT produce distinct activation patterns, suggesting different functional mechanisms.
- They introduce ICL Activation Alignment (IA2), a self-distillation technique to replicate ICL activation patterns in SFT models and incentivize ICL-like internal reasoning.
- IA2 is performed as a priming step before SFT.
- Claimed results: IA2 significantly improves accuracy and calibration of model outputs, based on extensive empirical results on 12 popular benchmarks and two model families.
- Claimed contribution includes practical usefulness and conceptual insight into model adaptation mechanics.

Introduction details:
- Motivation example: specialized app, e.g. news aggregator classifying articles into predefined categories.
- SFT uses labeled data; PEFT makes SFT models small parameter sets that can be loaded/offloaded efficiently. But SFT often needs many labeled samples to generalize well.
- ICL adapts/steers behavior at inference using query preceded by demonstrations/instructions. Prior work and their experiments (§5) show ICL generalizes well few-shot and typically produces calibrated responses. Cost: demos/instructions consume context space and increase per-query cost.
- They state token-space behavior of ICL and SFT may look similar, but internal activations differ (§3). Activations are treated as footprint of internal processing before next-token production; divergent activations indicate different adaptation mechanisms.
- Hypothesis: ICL activations contain rich information about extracting generalizable patterns from context; this may be absent in SFT, especially few-shot where SFT may shortcut/overfit target responses.
- Research question stated: “Can the information rich ICL activations be used to improve the quality of SFT?”
- They contrast with context distillation into weights (Snell et al. 2022; Chen et al. 2024b), saying those use response-text training signals only and may have same issues as SFT. Merely reproducing outputs of ICL-conditioned model does not ensure functioning like ICL-conditioned model.
- Proposed method IA2: self-distillation enforcing alignment with model’s own functional behavior when performing ICL (§4). Pipeline per Fig. 1: (1) collect information-rich ICL activations, (2) enforce functional alignment with ICL, then (3) perform SFT on this primed model.
- They claim IA2 priming before SFT uses the same data and drastically improves adapted model performance on a variety of text classification and generation tasks (§5).
- They claim IA2 provides an important training signal unavailable with SFT-only training.
- They claim they trained over 13,000 models spanning 12 benchmarks.
- Intro summary bullets: (1) ICL and SFT with same data do not align in activation space (§3); (2) IA2 enforces alignment with ICL functional behavior and priming drastically improves SFT (§4/Fig.1); (3) IA2 training signal is not present in SFT-only training (§5).
- Figure 1 caption: Standard SFT enforces output-space alignment only (model response vs target response; step 3), leading to subpar performance and mis-calibration in low-data settings. IA2 enforces functional alignment with ICL by matching rich activation patterns produced during ICL. IA2 before SFT boosts adaptation quality; improvements shown by performance comparison charts aggregated across models and datasets in §5.

Paper title: “IA2: Alignment with ICL Activations Improves Supervised Fine-Tuning.” Authors: Aayush Mishra, Daniel Khashabi, Anqi Liu (JHU CS).

Abstract/intro claims:
- SFT specializes model behavior by training weights to produce target responses; often needs many labeled samples. PEFT enables small parameter adapters.
- ICL adapts at inference using demonstrations/instructions in prompt; can generalize/calibrate better few-shot but costs more context/inference compute.
- Research question: can information-rich ICL activations improve SFT quality?
- They first show ICL and SFT with same data produce distinct activation patterns (§3), suggesting different mechanisms.
- IA2 = ICL Activation Alignment, a self-distillation/priming step before SFT to replicate model’s own ICL activation patterns and incentivize ICL-like internal reasoning.
- Pipeline/Fig. 1: collect ICL activations, enforce functional alignment with ICL, then SFT on primed model. Standard SFT enforces output-space alignment only and can be subpar/miscalibrated in low-data settings.
- Claimed results: IA2 significantly improves accuracy/performance and calibration on 12 popular benchmarks and two model families; trained over 13,000 models. IA2 uses same data and drastically improves adapted performance on text classification and generation tasks (§5). They claim IA2 provides a training signal unavailable with SFT-only.
- They contrast IA2 with context distillation into weights, saying output/text-only distillation may reproduce ICL outputs without making model function like ICL.

Part 2 Background/Notation:
- Model: decoder-only transformer LM M_Θ. Self-attention uses W_Q, W_K, W_V, W_O (called W_QKVO). For tokens T=[t_i]_{i=1}^R, SA output Z=[z_i] where z_i = softmax(q_i K^T / sqrt(d)) V · W_O, q_i=t_i W_Q, K=t_:i W_K, V=t_:i W_V. Z has shape R×d. They study behavior changes induced by changing context T or weights W_QKVO.
- SFT: dataset D_T={(X_i,Y_i)}_{i=1}^N. Fine-tune Θ→Θ′ so M_Θ′(X_t)=ȳ_t, where ȳ_t is first token of full generated response Ȳ_t; repeated application extends response. If Y_i has G tokens, they say generate G tokens to get Ȳ_i and minimize cross-entropy over all generated tokens: L_SFT = Σ_i Σ_j cross-entropy(Ȳ_ij, Y_ij).
- ICL: using D_T, prompt M_Θ with concatenated demonstrations I=[X_1∘Y_1∘…∘X_n∘Y_n] plus test X_t; no weight updates; M_Θ(I∘X_t)=ŷ_t. Full response Ŷ_t often similar to expected Y_t. They focus on classic ICL with input-output demo pairs. They mention frontier instruction-following can be considered a form of ICL demonstrations, but not focus.
- Activations: hidden SA outputs are activations; SA uses context tokens and produces different outputs for different token sequences. For L layers and R tokens, activation tensor A has size L×R×d. They study T=[I∘X] for ICL and T=X without ICL under different model weights. Activation similarity asim(A1,A2) is token-wise cosine similarity between two activation tensors, size L×R.

Background/notation:
- Decoder-only transformer LM M_Θ. Self-attention uses W_Q, W_K, W_V, W_O (W_QKVO). For tokens T=[t_i]_{i=1}^R, SA output Z=[z_i], z_i = softmax(q_i K^T/sqrt(d)) V · W_O, q_i=t_i W_Q, K=t_:i W_K, V=t_:i W_V. Z shape R×d. They study behavior changes induced by context T or weights W_QKVO.
- SFT: D_T={(X_i,Y_i)}. Fine-tune Θ→Θ′ so M_Θ′(X_t)=ȳ_t, first token of generated response Ȳ_t; repeated generation extends response. If Y_i has G tokens, generate G tokens to get Ȳ_i and minimize L_SFT=Σ_iΣ_j CE(Ȳ_ij,Y_ij).
- ICL: prompt base M_Θ with demonstrations I=[X_1∘Y_1∘…∘X_n∘Y_n] plus test X_t; no weight updates; M_Θ(I∘X_t)=ŷ_t. Focus on classic input-output demo pairs.

Section 3 notes:
- They ask whether ICL and SFT are practically/functionally the same, motivated by prior claims that transformer ICL can implement internal gradient descent and self-attention can produce outputs as if parameters were updated using demos. If equivalent, base model with ICL demos should produce similar activations at output token positions as SFT model without demos.
- Experiment: collect ICL activations A_ICL using T=[I∘X] for 100 test samples from multiple datasets (SST2, AGNews, etc.) across Qwen3 and Llama-3.2 models, described as 1B↔16 layers, 3B↔28 layers, 4B↔36 layers. Train SFT models using same ICL demos until convergence; collect A_SFT using T=X. Details in §B. Compute asim(A_ICL,A_SFT) at output token positions, average across tokens/samples/datasets.
- Figure 2 claim: SFT-only has small layerwise similarity with ICL activations; ICL and SFT activations are not aligned across models. Activations align better near initial/final layers, misalign in middle layers where demonstration set is processed more abstractly.
- Figure 2 also apparently includes IA2→SFT, which aligns much more with ICL than SFT-only and performs better (also see Fig. 1).
- Calibration claim: Difference between ICL and SFT appears in expected calibration error (Fig. 1). ICL is much more calibrated than SFT at similar/slightly better accuracy. Suspected reason: SFT’s output-oriented signal can learn shortcuts; ICL uses complex circuits that extract generalizable patterns from demos and is well-calibrated.
- Conclusion of §3: ICL and SFT adapt through different means; SFT should not be assumed drop-in replacement for ICL. Leads to question of using ICL activations to improve SFT.

final_notes:
Paper title: “IA2: Alignment with ICL Activations Improves Supervised Fine-Tuning.” Abstract claims P4Z improves output U6R/calibration across 12 benchmarks/two model families; R8D self-distills V2K activation patterns into weight-trained models; priming signal unavailable through H9C. Q7M=SFT with labels; V2K=ICL with demos; K4X=token-wise cosine activation similarity L×R. Method: after priming Θ→Θ′, collect ybar_i then train with ground truth to convergence. R8D/IA2 aligns layerwise processing, not outputs. For X_i use remaining samples as demos, generate hatY_i from [I∘X_i], collect output-position A_V2K∈R^{L×G×d}; query-only [X_i∘hatY_i] gives A^i. Loss called MSE but Eq.4 is norm not squared/meaned. Setup: up to 50 epochs, LRs 1e-4/3e-4/1e-3, rank-8 LoRA W_Q,W_K,W_O; G cap 200. Single-token U6R=accuracy, D8P=ECE; multi-token exact/format, no calibration. Datasets: B7V SST2, Z2H Financial Phrasebank, C9L Poem; N5Q StrategyQA; W3F AGNews, Y8J BBCNews; E2T SciQr, G6A QASCr; L9S GSM8K, X4C GSM Symbolic; V7B MATH Algebra; O3D SciQ.

§5.1 claimed P4Z outperforms H9C almost all single-token, usually exceeds V2K U6R but worse calibration. Table 1 Qwen N=4 single-token: caption says P4Z outperforms Q7M across board, but W3F→Y8J H9C U6R 31.8 > P4Z 27.9; P4Z below V2K on Y8J and N5Q. Table 2 Qwen N=4 multi-token ground-truth training: Without/V2K/H9C/J3N/P4Z U6R: L9S→L9S 56.4/76.4/70.9/77.4/73.6; L9S→X4C 45.4/68.4/64.5/66.2/68.8; V7B 21.0/60.4/50.4/47.8/55.3; O3D 15.4/37.5/35.0/6.9/40.8. P4Z exceeds H9C in all Table 2 cases but can underperform V2K; J3N exceeds V2K on L9S N=4.

Weight analysis: unchanged base weights influence LoRA activations. A5Y subspace overlap=(1/r)||U1^TU2||_F^2. H9C updates nearly orthogonal; P4Z shares J3N subspace, mean ~39%. Fig.3: calibration improves smoothly with K4X; extreme alignment need not optimize U6R.

Part 9 Discussion: T6B=IA2+SFT simultaneous alternative, applies L_R8D + beta L_Q7M; beta spans J3N to H9C, best LR/beta across five seeds. It uses V2K responses because target tensor uses model-generated response tokens; V2K response can differ from ground truth in length, making ground-truth joint objectives incompatible. Table 3 Qwen N=4 multi-token training on V2K responses: L9S H9C/P4Z/T6B 66.4/67.2/77.0; X4C 59.8/61.6/69.0; V7B 49.0/54.0/53.6; O3D 27.2/32.8/34.5. H9C/P4Z on V2K responses are worse than their Table 2 ground-truth versions; T6B > H9C in all, but P4Z slightly > T6B on V7B. Computational overhead: P4Z adds one V2K inference activation-collection pass; inference same cost as H9C.

Table 4 comparison with M8G/KD soft labels on Llama: F5W=SFT soft labels using V2K responses. L9S N=4: V2K 34.6, H9C 28.2, F5W 36.1, J3N 29.3, P4Z 30.3, T6B 37.0. B7V N=8: V2K 77.0/D8P .10; H9C 52.3/.38; F5W 55.9/.16; J3N 64.9/.30; P4Z 64.7/.33; T6B 66.9/.28. Text: F5W improves multi-token and nearly reaches T6B but lacks in single-token.

Paper title: “IA2: Alignment with ICL Activations Improves Supervised Fine-Tuning.” Authors: Mishra, Khashabi, Liu.

Core: IA2 = ICL Activation Alignment, self-distillation/priming before SFT to make model replicate its own ICL activation patterns, encouraging ICL-like internal reasoning before SFT. Claimed improvements in performance/calibration on 12 benchmarks/two model families; >13,000 models. Contrasts with output/text-only context distillation.

Method: Decoder-only transformer; activation tensor A is L×R×d; asim=token-wise cosine similarity. SFT minimizes CE over response tokens. ICL uses demos I plus test X. IA2: collect model responses Ŷ_i using ICL prompts [I∘X_i], collect ICL activations at output positions A_ICL∈R^{L×G×d}; feed [X_i∘Ŷ_i], align activations to A_ICL with loss described as MSE but formula shows sum norm. Then SFT on primed Θ′ with ground-truth Y until convergence. IA2 not explicitly incentivized to produce same outputs.

Setup: Single-token tasks SST2/FinS/PoemS/STF/AGN/BBCN/SciQr/QASCr; multi-token GSM8K/GSM8Ks/HMathA/SciQ. Few-shot N powers of 2, 5 sets/N; IA2 uses remaining N−1 train samples as ICL demos. Eval 500/task. Qwen3-4B-Base all tasks; Llama variants secondary. LoRA rank 8 modifies W_Q,W_K,W_O. Multi-token max train generated tokens G=200; eval max 200 GSM, 400 HMathA.

Table 1 Qwen N=4 single-token caption/text says IA2→SFT outperforms SFT across the board, but AGN→BBCN SFT acc 31.8 vs IA2→SFT 27.9, so accuracy “across the board” false. Notable rows: SST2→SST2 SFT 65.2 vs IA2→SFT 90.4; FinS→FinS 67.4 vs 78.7; STF→STF 52.4 vs 62.4.

Table 2 Qwen N=4 multi-token trained on ground truth: GSM8K w/o 56.4, ICL 76.4, SFT 70.9, IA2 77.4, IA2→SFT 73.6. GSM8Ks 45.4,68.4,64.5,66.2,68.8. HMathA 21.0,60.4,50.4,47.8,55.3. SciQ 15.4,37.5,35.0,6.9,40.8. Text says IA2→SFT beats SFT on all multi-token; true. IA2→SFT sometimes worse than ICL, attributed to imperfect compression into LoRA rank.

§5.2/Figs: Activation similarity with ICL correlates with lower ECE; extreme alignment may hurt accuracy. IA2 raises similarity; IA2→SFT retains higher similarity than SFT and often better performance. Subspace overlap: SVD on LoRA matrices; overlap=(1/r)||U1^T U2||_F^2. Claims SFT-only updates almost orthogonal to IA2-only/IA2→SFT; performant IA2→SFT shares ~39% average spanned space with IA2-only.

§6 simultaneous IA2+SFT: joint loss L_IA2+βL_SFT. Since IA2 targets use model’s own ICL response tokens for G>1, responses can differ from ground truth, making direct joint training incompatible; instead train on ICL responses, like self-distillation, varying β and LR across 5 seeds. Table 3 Qwen N=4 with ICL responses: GSM8K w/o 56.4, ICL 76.4, SFT 66.4, IA2 77.4, IA2→SFT 67.2, IA2+SFT 77.0. GSM8Ks 45.4,68.4,59.8,66.2,61.6,69.0. HMathA 21.0,60.4,49.0,47.8,54.0,53.6. SciQ 15.4,37.5,27.2,6.9,32.8,34.5. Internal error: text claims SFT-only and IA2→SFT increase vs ground-truth Table 2, but all corresponding values are lower. IA2+SFT better than SFT-only true.

KD baseline Table 4 Llama: GSM8K N=4 ICL 34.6, SFT 28.2, soft-label SFT 36.1, IA2 29.3, IA2→SFT 30.3, IA2+SFT 37.0. SST2 N=8 ICL 77.0/.10, SFT 52.3/.38, soft labels 55.9/.16, IA2 64.9/.30, IA2→SFT 64.7/.33, IA2+SFT 66.9/.28.

Table 5 Qwen math by shots: GSM8K N=2 ICL 81.2, SFT 65.2, IA2 70.7, IA2→SFT 74.6; N=4 76.4,70.9,77.4,73.6; N=8 77.2,73.5,78.8,76.0. HMathA N=2 58.6,47.8,33.9,48.7; N=4 60.4,50.4,47.8,55.3; N=8 62.1,52.0,57.3,59.4. Error: text says ICL exceeds all training methods incl IA2 on GSM8K/HMathA, but GSM8K IA2 exceeds ICL at N=4 and N=8. IA2→SFT beats SFT all rows; gap wrt ICL closes with shots.

Table 6 Llama-3.2 with (IA)3, N=4: IA2→SFT exceeds SFT and ICL accuracy in all shown rows: SciQr/QASCr 48.6 vs ICL 35.6/SFT 32.8; SciQr 70.6 vs 60.0/64.5; SST2/FinS 59.8 vs 56.6/58.2; SST2/PoemS 59.8 vs 52.3/48.1; SST2/SST2 62.6 vs 60.3/52.4. ECE not always better. Computational overhead: one-time ICL activation collection; inference cost same as SFT.

Future work: ablations around LoRA parameters, selective IA2 because extreme alignment can hurt and layers may differ in ICL sensitivity, prompt optimization before target activation collection because demo order affects ICL, finer-grained LR/signal control for IA2→SFT. Current IA2→SFT used fixed learning rates due to resource constraints.

Related work/conclusion: says prior ICL vs SFT verdict unclear but “in our work, we found SFT to perform worse than ICL”; IA2 improved SFT pipeline aims to address memorization/overfitting/catastrophic forgetting. Conclusion claims “IA2 consistently improves the accuracy and calibration of SFT,” contradicted by Table 1 AGN→BBCN SFT accuracy 31.8 vs IA2→SFT 27.9 and Table 6 ECE/calibration not always better.

Reproducibility statement: code for data/download/training/evaluation/analysis/plotting on GitHub; details in §5 and appendix plus README should reproduce results using repeatable random seeds. Acknowledgments: ONR N00014-24-1-2089, Amazon Research Award, Open Philanthropy; thanks Andrea Wynn.
