Paper title: “IA2: Alignment with ICL Activations Improves Supervised Fine-Tuning.” Authors: Aayush Mishra, Daniel Khashabi, Anqi Liu (JHU CS).

Abstract claims:
- SFT specializes model behavior by training weights to produce intended target responses for queries.
- ICL adapts models at inference using instructions/demonstrations in the prompt.
- ICL can offer better generalizability and more calibrated responses than SFT in data-scarce settings, but costs more inference compute.
- Research question: can ICL internal computations improve qualities of SFT?
- They first show ICL and SFT produce distinct activation patterns, suggesting different functional mechanisms.
- They introduce ICL Activation Alignment (IA2), a self-distillation technique to replicate ICL activation patterns in SFT models and incentivize ICL-like internal reasoning.
- IA2 is performed as a priming step before SFT.
- Claimed results: IA2 significantly improves accuracy and calibration of model outputs, based on extensive empirical results on 12 popular benchmarks and two model families.
- Claimed contribution includes practical usefulness and conceptual insight into model adaptation mechanics.

Introduction details:
- Motivation example: specialized app, e.g. news aggregator classifying articles into predefined categories.
- SFT uses labeled data; PEFT makes SFT models small parameter sets that can be loaded/offloaded efficiently. But SFT often needs many labeled samples to generalize well.
- ICL adapts/steers behavior at inference using query preceded by demonstrations/instructions. Prior work and their experiments (§5) show ICL generalizes well few-shot and typically produces calibrated responses. Cost: demos/instructions consume context space and increase per-query cost.
- They state token-space behavior of ICL and SFT may look similar, but internal activations differ (§3). Activations are treated as footprint of internal processing before next-token production; divergent activations indicate different adaptation mechanisms.
- Hypothesis: ICL activations contain rich information about extracting generalizable patterns from context; this may be absent in SFT, especially few-shot where SFT may shortcut/overfit target responses.
- Research question stated: “Can the information rich ICL activations be used to improve the quality of SFT?”
- They contrast with context distillation into weights (Snell et al. 2022; Chen et al. 2024b), saying those use response-text training signals only and may have same issues as SFT. Merely reproducing outputs of ICL-conditioned model does not ensure functioning like ICL-conditioned model.
- Proposed method IA2: self-distillation enforcing alignment with model’s own functional behavior when performing ICL (§4). Pipeline per Fig. 1: (1) collect information-rich ICL activations, (2) enforce functional alignment with ICL, then (3) perform SFT on this primed model.
- They claim IA2 priming before SFT uses the same data and drastically improves adapted model performance on a variety of text classification and generation tasks (§5).
- They claim IA2 provides an important training signal unavailable with SFT-only training.
- They claim they trained over 13,000 models spanning 12 benchmarks.
- Intro summary bullets: (1) ICL and SFT with same data do not align in activation space (§3); (2) IA2 enforces alignment with ICL functional behavior and priming drastically improves SFT (§4/Fig.1); (3) IA2 training signal is not present in SFT-only training (§5).
- Figure 1 caption: Standard SFT enforces output-space alignment only (model response vs target response; step 3), leading to subpar performance and mis-calibration in low-data settings. IA2 enforces functional alignment with ICL by matching rich activation patterns produced during ICL. IA2 before SFT boosts adaptation quality; improvements shown by performance comparison charts aggregated across models and datasets in §5.

Paper title: “IA2: Alignment with ICL Activations Improves Supervised Fine-Tuning.” Authors: Aayush Mishra, Daniel Khashabi, Anqi Liu (JHU CS).

Abstract/intro claims:
- SFT specializes model behavior by training weights to produce target responses; often needs many labeled samples. PEFT enables small parameter adapters.
- ICL adapts at inference using demonstrations/instructions in prompt; can generalize/calibrate better few-shot but costs more context/inference compute.
- Research question: can information-rich ICL activations improve SFT quality?
- They first show ICL and SFT with same data produce distinct activation patterns (§3), suggesting different mechanisms.
- IA2 = ICL Activation Alignment, a self-distillation/priming step before SFT to replicate model’s own ICL activation patterns and incentivize ICL-like internal reasoning.
- Pipeline/Fig. 1: collect ICL activations, enforce functional alignment with ICL, then SFT on primed model. Standard SFT enforces output-space alignment only and can be subpar/miscalibrated in low-data settings.
- Claimed results: IA2 significantly improves accuracy/performance and calibration on 12 popular benchmarks and two model families; trained over 13,000 models. IA2 uses same data and drastically improves adapted performance on text classification and generation tasks (§5). They claim IA2 provides a training signal unavailable with SFT-only.
- They contrast IA2 with context distillation into weights, saying output/text-only distillation may reproduce ICL outputs without making model function like ICL.

Part 2 Background/Notation:
- Model: decoder-only transformer LM M_Θ. Self-attention uses W_Q, W_K, W_V, W_O (called W_QKVO). For tokens T=[t_i]_{i=1}^R, SA output Z=[z_i] where z_i = softmax(q_i K^T / sqrt(d)) V · W_O, q_i=t_i W_Q, K=t_:i W_K, V=t_:i W_V. Z has shape R×d. They study behavior changes induced by changing context T or weights W_QKVO.
- SFT: dataset D_T={(X_i,Y_i)}_{i=1}^N. Fine-tune Θ→Θ′ so M_Θ′(X_t)=ȳ_t, where ȳ_t is first token of full generated response Ȳ_t; repeated application extends response. If Y_i has G tokens, they say generate G tokens to get Ȳ_i and minimize cross-entropy over all generated tokens: L_SFT = Σ_i Σ_j cross-entropy(Ȳ_ij, Y_ij).
- ICL: using D_T, prompt M_Θ with concatenated demonstrations I=[X_1∘Y_1∘…∘X_n∘Y_n] plus test X_t; no weight updates; M_Θ(I∘X_t)=ŷ_t. Full response Ŷ_t often similar to expected Y_t. They focus on classic ICL with input-output demo pairs. They mention frontier instruction-following can be considered a form of ICL demonstrations, but not focus.
- Activations: hidden SA outputs are activations; SA uses context tokens and produces different outputs for different token sequences. For L layers and R tokens, activation tensor A has size L×R×d. They study T=[I∘X] for ICL and T=X without ICL under different model weights. Activation similarity asim(A1,A2) is token-wise cosine similarity between two activation tensors, size L×R.

Paper title: “IA2: Alignment with ICL Activations Improves Supervised Fine-Tuning.” Authors: Aayush Mishra, Daniel Khashabi, Anqi Liu (JHU CS).

Core claims/motivation:
- SFT adapts weights to produce target responses; often needs many labeled samples. PEFT uses small adapters.
- ICL adapts at inference using demos/instructions in prompt; may generalize/calibrate better few-shot but costs more context/inference compute.
- Research question: can information-rich ICL activations improve SFT quality?
- IA2 = ICL Activation Alignment, a self-distillation/priming step before SFT that makes model replicate its own ICL activation patterns and incentivizes ICL-like internal reasoning. Pipeline/Fig. 1: collect ICL activations, enforce functional alignment with ICL, then SFT on primed model. Standard SFT aligns output space only and can be subpar/miscalibrated in low-data settings.
- Claimed results: IA2 significantly improves accuracy/performance and calibration on 12 popular benchmarks and two model families; trained over 13,000 models; same data; improves text classification and generation (§5). IA2 provides signal unavailable to SFT-only.
- Contrast with context distillation into weights: output/text-only distillation may reproduce ICL outputs without making model function like ICL.

Background/notation:
- Decoder-only transformer LM M_Θ. Self-attention uses W_Q, W_K, W_V, W_O (W_QKVO). For tokens T=[t_i]_{i=1}^R, SA output Z=[z_i], z_i = softmax(q_i K^T/sqrt(d)) V · W_O, q_i=t_i W_Q, K=t_:i W_K, V=t_:i W_V. Z shape R×d. They study behavior changes induced by context T or weights W_QKVO.
- SFT: D_T={(X_i,Y_i)}. Fine-tune Θ→Θ′ so M_Θ′(X_t)=ȳ_t, first token of generated response Ȳ_t; repeated generation extends response. If Y_i has G tokens, generate G tokens to get Ȳ_i and minimize L_SFT=Σ_iΣ_j CE(Ȳ_ij,Y_ij).
- ICL: prompt base M_Θ with demonstrations I=[X_1∘Y_1∘…∘X_n∘Y_n] plus test X_t; no weight updates; M_Θ(I∘X_t)=ŷ_t. Focus on classic input-output demo pairs.
- Activations: hidden SA outputs; for L layers and R tokens activation tensor A size L×R×d. They study T=[I∘X] for ICL and T=X without ICL under different weights. asim(A1,A2) = token-wise cosine similarity between activation tensors, size L×R.

Section 3 notes:
- They ask whether ICL and SFT are practically/functionally the same, motivated by prior claims that transformer ICL can implement internal gradient descent and self-attention can produce outputs as if parameters were updated using demos. If equivalent, base model with ICL demos should produce similar activations at output token positions as SFT model without demos.
- Experiment: collect ICL activations A_ICL using T=[I∘X] for 100 test samples from multiple datasets (SST2, AGNews, etc.) across Qwen3 and Llama-3.2 models, described as 1B↔16 layers, 3B↔28 layers, 4B↔36 layers. Train SFT models using same ICL demos until convergence; collect A_SFT using T=X. Details in §B. Compute asim(A_ICL,A_SFT) at output token positions, average across tokens/samples/datasets.
- Figure 2 claim: SFT-only has small layerwise similarity with ICL activations; ICL and SFT activations are not aligned across models. Activations align better near initial/final layers, misalign in middle layers where demonstration set is processed more abstractly.
- Figure 2 also apparently includes IA2→SFT, which aligns much more with ICL than SFT-only and performs better (also see Fig. 1).
- Calibration claim: Difference between ICL and SFT appears in expected calibration error (Fig. 1). ICL is much more calibrated than SFT at similar/slightly better accuracy. Suspected reason: SFT’s output-oriented signal can learn shortcuts; ICL uses complex circuits that extract generalizable patterns from demos and is well-calibrated.
- Conclusion of §3: ICL and SFT adapt through different means; SFT should not be assumed drop-in replacement for ICL. Leads to question of using ICL activations to improve SFT.

errors.claim: “Then, we simply train the model to minimize the mean squared error between the two activations …: 𝓛_IA2 = Σ_i ||A^i − A^i_ICL||.”
errors.evidence: The stated loss formula is a sum of norms, not a mean squared error: “𝓛_IA2 = Σ_i ||A^i − A^i_ICL||.”
errors.explanation: Calling the objective mean squared error conflicts with the displayed equation, which does not show either squaring or averaging unless the norm notation is being used nonstandardly.

Core claims/motivation: IA2 = ICL Activation Alignment, a self-distillation/priming step before SFT that makes model replicate its own ICL activation patterns, incentivizing ICL-like internal reasoning before standard SFT. Claimed improvements in performance and calibration on 12 benchmarks and two model families; trained over 13,000 models. Contrasts with output/text-only context distillation.

For L layers and R tokens activation tensor A is L×R×d. asim(A1,A2)=token-wise cosine similarity between activation tensors, size L×R. SFT minimizes CE over generated response tokens vs targets. ICL uses demos I=[X1∘Y1…Xn∘Yn] plus test X, no weight updates.

§3 notes: They test whether ICL and SFT are functionally/practically same. Collect A_ICL using [I∘X] for 100 test samples from multiple datasets across Qwen3 and Llama-3.2 models (1B/16 layers, 3B/28, 4B/36 noted). Claim: ICL more calibrated than SFT at similar/slightly better accuracy (Fig. 1). Conclusion: ICL and SFT adapt differently; SFT not drop-in replacement for ICL.

§4 method: Two-step pipeline: IA2 priming then SFT. IA2 goal per layer: modified attention weights W̃_QKVO such that SA([I∘X];W_QKVO) ≈ SA(X;W̃_QKVO) for new token. Practical procedure: generate model responses Ŷ_i using ICL prompts [I∘X_i], collect ICL activations at output positions A^i_ICL∈R^{L×G×d}; then feed query plus generated response only [X_i∘Ŷ_i] and collect A^i at output positions. IA2 loss described as mean squared error, but displayed as L_IA2=Σ_i ||A^i−A^i_ICL|| (possible inconsistency to watch: not explicitly squared/mean). IA2 trains parameters to process inputs like ICL; not explicitly incentivized to produce similar outputs. Then SFT on primed Θ′ with ground-truth Y until convergence.

§5 current experimental setup: Two settings: single-token and multi-token. Single-token tasks: (1) Sentiment: SST2, Financial Phrasebank (FinS), Poem Sentiment (PoemS); train on SST2 and FinS, evaluate all three; described as one ID and two OOD eval datasets per training condition. (2) True/False: StrategyQA (STF), multi-hop reasoning to True/False. (3) News categorization: AGNews (AGN), BBCNews (BBCN); train AGN, evaluate both. (4) MCQ: SciQ and QASC with choices remapped from A/B/C to unrelated token set, called SciQr and QASCr; train SciQr, evaluate both. Multi-token tasks: (1) Grade-school math: GSM8K and GSM Symbolic (GSM8Ks); train GSM8K, evaluate both. (2) Advanced math: MATH Algebra (HMathA). (3) Scientific QA: SciQ used for generating answer tokens rather than choosing options. These eval datasets total 12: SST2, FinS, PoemS, STF, AGN, BBCN, SciQr, QASCr, GSM8K, GSM8Ks, HMathA, SciQ.

Data setup: Few-shot/data-scarce. For each task create multiple D_T of size N varying in powers of 2 [2,4,8,16,…]. Create 5 different sets at each N to average out outliers. For IA2, collect A^i_ICL for each X_i using remaining N−1 training samples as ICL demonstrations in random order, reusing same training samples to ensure fair same-data comparison. errors.location: this part, Eq. (4) and preceding sentence
errors.evidence: The stated loss is a sum of norms, \(\sum_i \|A^i-A^i_{\mathrm{V2K}}\|\), not a mean squared error: it is neither squared nor averaged/meaned in the displayed formula.
errors.explanation: The prose identifies the objective as MSE, but the equation defines an unsquared summed norm, so the mathematical definition conflicts with the textual description.

final_notes:
Paper title: “IA2: Alignment with ICL Activations Improves Supervised Fine-Tuning.” Abstract claims P4Z improves output U6R/calibration across 12 benchmarks/two model families; R8D self-distills V2K activation patterns into weight-trained models; priming signal unavailable through H9C. Intro: Q7M=SFT with labels; V2K=ICL with demos; hypothesis V2K activations contain contextual patterns missing from few-shot weight adaptation.

Definitions: D_T={(X_i,Y_i)}. Q7M=SFT Θ→Θ′ with CE target-token loss. Activations A∈R^{L×R×d}. V2K=ICL with demos I=[X1∘Y1...Xn∘Yn], infer on I∘X_t; demos restricted to I/O pairs. K4X=token-wise cosine activation similarity, shape L×R. R8D/IA2 aligns layerwise processing, not outputs. For X_i use remaining samples as demos, generate hatY_i from [I∘X_i], collect output-position A^i_V2K∈R^{L×G×d}; then supply [X_i∘hatY_i] query-only to get A^i. Loss described as MSE but Eq.4 is sum_i ||A^i−A^i_V2K||, not squared/meaned.

Setup: train to convergence up to 50 epochs, LRs 1e-4/3e-4/1e-3, best selected; >13k models. Rank-8 LoRA targets attention W_Q,W_K,W_O. Multi-token N restricted to 16 Llama and 8 Qwen. Activation cap G=200; target-token training uses ground-truth response length. Single-token U6R=accuracy, D8P=ECE; multi-token exact/format correctness, no calibration. Base demos five evals with different demos; trained methods no demos. Gen limits 200 GSM8K/GSM Symbolic, 400 MATH Algebra. Qwen3-4B-Base all tasks; Llama-3.2-1B mostly, E2T uses 3B; multi-token secondary Llama-3.2-1B-Instruct.

Datasets/12: Sentiment B7V=SST2, Z2H=Financial Phrasebank, C9L=Poem Sentiment; train separately B7V/Z2H, eval all three. N5Q=StrategyQA. News W3F=AGNews train/eval, Y8J=BBCNews eval. MCQ E2T=SciQr train/eval, G6A=QASCr eval. Math L9S=GSM8K, X4C=GSM Symbolic. Advanced math V7B=MATH Algebra. Scientific QA O3D=SciQ; also source for E2T. Few-shot N powers of two, five sets/N; A_V2K uses other N−1 samples as demos; eval 500/task. Multi-token CoT ordinary text; GSM reasoning #### number; V7B boxed; O3D support #### answer.

§5.1 claims: P4Z outperforms H9C in almost all single-token cases for U6R/calibration with identical data; usually exceeds V2K U6R but slightly worse calibration. J3N often high U6R and V2K-like calibration without target-response-token training. Table 1 Qwen3-4B N=4 single-token caption says P4Z outperforms standard Q7M across board, but W3F→Y8J has H9C U6R 31.8 > P4Z 27.9. P4Z below V2K on Y8J and N5Q U6R.

Table 2 Qwen3-4B N=4 multi-token ground-truth training: Without/V2K/H9C/J3N/P4Z U6R: L9S→L9S 56.4/76.4/70.9/77.4/73.6; L9S→X4C 45.4/68.4/64.5/66.2/68.8; V7B→V7B 21.0/60.4/50.4/47.8/55.3; O3D→O3D 15.4/37.5/35.0/6.9/40.8. Text says P4Z exceeds H9C every case but sometimes underperforms V2K; supported.

§5.2/weight analysis: unchanged base weights significantly influence LoRA activations, so activation patterns alone cannot isolate training-induced behavior. Paper title: “IA2: Alignment with ICL Activations Improves Supervised Fine-Tuning.” IA2 = ICL Activation Alignment, priming/self-distillation before SFT to make model replicate its own ICL activation patterns. Method: generate ICL responses Ŷ_i with demos, collect target ICL activations A_ICL at output positions; feed [X_i∘Ŷ_i], train LoRA to align activations, then SFT on ground-truth Y. IA2 not explicitly trained to match outputs. SFT CE on response tokens.

Setup: 12 eval datasets; Qwen3-4B-Base all tasks; Llama variants secondary. LoRA rank 8 W_Q,W_K,W_O. N few-shot powers of 2, 5 seeds/sets. Eval 500/task. Single-token accuracy/ECE first generated token; multi-token parsed final answer, accuracy only. Table 1 Qwen N=4 single-token caption says IA2→SFT outperforms SFT across board, but AGN→BBCN* contradicts: SFT 31.8 acc vs IA2→SFT 27.9. Other T1 examples: STF→STF IA2→SFT 62.4 vs SFT 52.4; SST2→SST2 90.4 vs 65.2; SciQr→SciQr 91.7 vs 88.3.

Table 2 Qwen N=4 multi-token ground-truth training: w/o ICL, ICL, SFT, IA2, IA2→SFT: GSM8K 56.4,76.4,70.9,77.4,73.6; GSM8Ks* 45.4,68.4,64.5,66.2,68.8; HMathA 21.0,60.4,50.4,47.8,55.3; SciQ 15.4,37.5,35.0,06.9,40.8. IA2→SFT beats SFT on all multi-token, but is not always best: IA2-only beats it on GSM8K; ICL beats it on GSM8K and HMathA. Text notes IA2→SFT sometimes worse than ICL in multi-token, says increasing LoRA rank eliminates deficit.

§5.2: Fig 3 asim(A,A_ICL) vs accuracy/ECE. Claim ECE decreases smoothly with increasing similarity; IA2→SFT lies between IA2 and SFT in activation similarity while better accuracy/calibration. SFT-only and IA2→SFT differ only in start state. Appendix C has IA2 following ICL performance even when worse due to overfitting. Weight subspace overlap Fig 4: SVD bases of LoRA weight matrices; overlap=(1/r)||U1^TU2||_F^2. Claims SFT-only updates almost orthogonal to IA2-only and IA2→SFT; performant IA2→SFT shares ~39% weight subspace with IA2-only; gains from IA2 subspaces unreachable by SFT-only.

§6 IA2+SFT alternative: L_IA2 + beta L_SFT jointly. Practical issue: IA2 target activations use model’s generated ICL response tokens for G>1, may differ from ground truth, making simultaneous ground-truth SFT incompatible. They instead self-distill on ICL responses, vary beta over 4 values, choose best LR/beta over 5 seeds. Table 3 Qwen N=4 trained with ICL responses: w/o ICL/ICL same as T2; SFT only, IA2 only, IA2→SFT, IA2+SFT: GSM8K 66.4,77.4,67.2,77.0; GSM8Ks 59.8,66.2,61.6,69.0; HMathA 49.0,47.8,54.0,53.6; SciQ 27.2,06.9,32.8,34.5. KD baseline Table 4: Llama models, GSM8K 1B-Instruct N=4, SST2 1B N=8, soft label matching on ICL responses. GSM8K: ICL 34.6; SFT 28.2; SFT soft labels 36.1; IA2 only 29.3; IA2→SFT 30.3; IA2+SFT 37.0. SST2 acc/ECE: ICL 77.0/0.10; SFT 52.3/0.38; soft labels 55.9/0.16; IA2 only 64.9/0.30; IA2→SFT 64.7/0.33; IA2+SFT 66.9/0.28. Text: KD better than standard SFT in multi-token almost reaching IA2+SFT, but lacks in single-token; IA2-based training consistently high for single/multi.

Table 5 Qwen math shot-count: GSM8K N=2 ICL 81.2, SFT 65.2, IA2 70.7, IA2→SFT 74.6; N=4 76.4,70.9,77.4,73.6; N=8 77.2,73.5,78.8,76.0. HMathA N=2 58.6,47.8,33.9,48.7; N=4 60.4,50.4,47.8,55.3; N=8 62.1,52.0,57.3,59.4. Error: text says ICL exceeds all methods for GSM8K/HMathA, but GSM8K IA2-only exceeds ICL at N=4/8. Table 5 supports IA2→SFT beats SFT and closes IA2→SFT-vs-ICL gap with more shots.

Other PEFT: repeat with (IA)3, N=4 Llama-3.2, Table 6. Claim IA2→SFT gains over SFT and exceeds ICL accuracy in all cases. Table6 acc/ece: SciQr source QASCr* ICL 35.6/.06, SFT 32.8/.20, IA2 34.2/.08, IA2→SFT 48.6/.25; SciQr source SciQr 60.0/.07, 64.5/.12,63.0/.10,70.6/.08; SST2 source FinS* 56.6/.17,58.2/.25,61.9/.18,59.8/.18; source PoemS* 52.3/.19,48.1/.44,48.1/.11,59.8/.33; source SST2 60.3/.19,52.4/.35,54.2/.15,62.6/.28. Thus broad related-work claim “we found SFT worse than ICL” is contradicted by Table 6 cases where SFT > ICL; conclusion claim “IA2 consistently improves accuracy and calibration of SFT” contradicted by T1 AGN accuracy drop and T6 QASCr ECE worse than SFT.

Computational overhead: one-time ICL inference/activation collection; inference same cost as SFT-only. Limitations/future: LoRA ablations, selective IA2 because extreme alignment can hurt/layers differ, prompt/demo-order optimization before activation collection, finer LR/signal control; conclusion also says future work on diversity, catastrophic forgetting, and RL-tuned models. Related work contrasts context distillation (output token signals) vs IA2 activations and activation steering as narrower. Reproducibility statement: code for data/training/eval/analysis/plotting on GitHub; §5/appendix/README and repeatable seeds claimed sufficient for full reproduction. Acknowledgments: ONR, Amazon Research Award, Open Philanthropy; Andrea Wynn thanked.

Paper title: “IA2: Alignment with ICL Activations Improves Supervised Fine-Tuning.” Authors: Aayush Mishra, Daniel Khashabi, Anqi Liu (JHU CS).

Abstract claims:
- SFT specializes model behavior by training weights to produce intended target responses for queries.
- ICL adapts models at inference using instructions/demonstrations in the prompt.
- ICL can offer better generalizability and more calibrated responses than SFT in data-scarce settings, but costs more inference compute.
- Research question: can ICL internal computations improve qualities of SFT?
- They first show ICL and SFT produce distinct activation patterns, suggesting different functional mechanisms.
- They introduce ICL Activation Alignment (IA2), a self-distillation technique to replicate ICL activation patterns in SFT models and incentivize ICL-like internal reasoning.
- IA2 is performed as a priming step before SFT.
- Claimed results: IA2 significantly improves accuracy and calibration of model outputs, based on extensive empirical results on 12 popular benchmarks and two model families.
- Claimed contribution includes practical usefulness and conceptual insight into model adaptation mechanics.

Introduction details:
- Motivation example: specialized app, e.g. news aggregator classifying articles into predefined categories.
- SFT uses labeled data; PEFT makes SFT models small parameter sets that can be loaded/offloaded efficiently. But SFT often needs many labeled samples to generalize well.
- ICL adapts/steers behavior at inference using query preceded by demonstrations/instructions. Prior work and their experiments (§5) show ICL generalizes well few-shot and typically produces calibrated responses. Cost: demos/instructions consume context space and increase per-query cost.
- They state token-space behavior of ICL and SFT may look similar, but internal activations differ (§3). Activations are treated as footprint of internal processing before next-token production; divergent activations indicate different adaptation mechanisms.
- Hypothesis: ICL activations contain rich information about extracting generalizable patterns from context; this may be absent in SFT, especially few-shot where SFT may shortcut/overfit target responses.
- Research question stated: “Can the information rich ICL activations be used to improve the quality of SFT?”
- They contrast with context distillation into weights (Snell et al. 2022; Chen et al. 2024b), saying those use response-text training signals only and may have same issues as SFT. Merely reproducing outputs of ICL-conditioned model does not ensure functioning like ICL-conditioned model.
- Proposed method IA2: self-distillation enforcing alignment with model’s own functional behavior when performing ICL (§4). Pipeline per Fig. 1: (1) collect information-rich ICL activations, (2) enforce functional alignment with ICL, then (3) perform SFT on this primed model.
- They claim IA2 priming before SFT uses the same data and drastically improves adapted model performance on a variety of text classification and generation tasks (§5).
- They claim IA2 provides an important training signal unavailable with SFT-only training.
- They claim they trained over 13,000 models spanning 12 benchmarks.
- Intro summary bullets: (1) ICL and SFT with same data do not align in activation space (§3); (2) IA2 enforces alignment with ICL functional behavior and priming drastically improves SFT (§4/Fig.1); (3) IA2 training signal is not present in SFT-only training (§5).
- Figure 1 caption: Standard SFT enforces output-space alignment only (model response vs target response; step 3), leading to subpar performance and mis-calibration in low-data settings. IA2 enforces functional alignment with ICL by matching rich activation patterns produced during ICL. IA2 before SFT boosts adaptation quality; improvements shown by performance comparison charts aggregated across models and datasets in §5.

Paper title: “IA2: Alignment with ICL Activations Improves Supervised Fine-Tuning.” Authors: Aayush Mishra, Daniel Khashabi, Anqi Liu (JHU CS).

Abstract/intro claims:
- SFT specializes model behavior by training weights to produce target responses; often needs many labeled samples. PEFT enables small parameter adapters.
- ICL adapts at inference using demonstrations/instructions in prompt; can generalize/calibrate better few-shot but costs more context/inference compute.
- Research question: can information-rich ICL activations improve SFT quality?
- They first show ICL and SFT with same data produce distinct activation patterns (§3), suggesting different mechanisms.
- IA2 = ICL Activation Alignment, a self-distillation/priming step before SFT to replicate model’s own ICL activation patterns and incentivize ICL-like internal reasoning.
- Pipeline/Fig. 1: collect ICL activations, enforce functional alignment with ICL, then SFT on primed model. Standard SFT enforces output-space alignment only and can be subpar/miscalibrated in low-data settings.
- Claimed results: IA2 significantly improves accuracy/performance and calibration on 12 popular benchmarks and two model families; trained over 13,000 models. IA2 uses same data and drastically improves adapted performance on text classification and generation tasks (§5). They claim IA2 provides a training signal unavailable with SFT-only.
- They contrast IA2 with context distillation into weights, saying output/text-only distillation may reproduce ICL outputs without making model function like ICL.

Part 2 Background/Notation:
- Model: decoder-only transformer LM M_Θ. Self-attention uses W_Q, W_K, W_V, W_O (called W_QKVO). For tokens T=[t_i]_{i=1}^R, SA output Z=[z_i] where z_i = softmax(q_i K^T / sqrt(d)) V · W_O, q_i=t_i W_Q, K=t_:i W_K, V=t_:i W_V. Z has shape R×d. They study behavior changes induced by changing context T or weights W_QKVO.
- SFT: dataset D_T={(X_i,Y_i)}_{i=1}^N. Fine-tune Θ→Θ′ so M_Θ′(X_t)=ȳ_t, where ȳ_t is first token of full generated response Ȳ_t; repeated application extends response. If Y_i has G tokens, they say generate G tokens to get Ȳ_i and minimize cross-entropy over all generated tokens: L_SFT = Σ_i Σ_j cross-entropy(Ȳ_ij, Y_ij).
- ICL: using D_T, prompt M_Θ with concatenated demonstrations I=[X_1∘Y_1∘…∘X_n∘Y_n] plus test X_t; no weight updates; M_Θ(I∘X_t)=ŷ_t. Full response Ŷ_t often similar to expected Y_t. They focus on classic ICL with input-output demo pairs. They mention frontier instruction-following can be considered a form of ICL demonstrations, but not focus.
- Activations: hidden SA outputs are activations; SA uses context tokens and produces different outputs for different token sequences. For L layers and R tokens, activation tensor A has size L×R×d. They study T=[I∘X] for ICL and T=X without ICL under different model weights. Activation similarity asim(A1,A2) is token-wise cosine similarity between two activation tensors, size L×R.

- Experiment: collect ICL activations A_ICL using T=[I∘X] for 100 test samples from multiple datasets (SST2, AGNews, etc.) across Qwen3 and Llama-3.2 models, described as 1B↔16 layers, 3B↔28 layers, 4B↔36 layers. - Calibration claim: Difference between ICL and SFT appears in expected calibration error (Fig. 1). ICL is much more calibrated than SFT at similar/slightly better accuracy. Suspected reason: SFT’s output-oriented signal can learn shortcuts; ICL uses complex circuits that extract generalizable patterns from demos and is well-calibrated.
- Conclusion of §3: ICL and SFT adapt through different means; SFT should not be assumed drop-in replacement for ICL. Leads to question of using ICL activations to improve SFT.

- Experiment: collect ICL activations A_ICL using T=[I∘X] for 100 test samples from multiple datasets (SST2, AGNews, etc.) across Qwen3 and Llama-3.2 models, described as 1B↔16 layers, 3B↔28 layers, 4B↔36 layers. Train SFT models using same ICL demos until convergence; collect A_SFT using T=X. Details in §B. Compute asim(A_ICL,A_SFT) at output token positions, average across tokens/samples/datasets.
- Figure 2 claim: SFT-only has small layerwise similarity with ICL activations; ICL and SFT activations are not aligned across models. Activations align better near initial/final layers, misalign in middle layers where demonstration set is processed more abstractly.
- Figure 2 also apparently includes IA2→SFT, which aligns much more with ICL than SFT-only and performs better.
- Calibration claim: ICL is much more calibrated than SFT at similar/slightly better accuracy (Fig. 1). Suspected reason: SFT’s output-oriented signal can learn shortcuts; ICL uses complex circuits that extract generalizable patterns from demos and is well-calibrated.
- Conclusion of §3: ICL and SFT adapt through different means; SFT should not be assumed drop-in replacement for ICL.

Section 4 method:
- Two-step SFT pipeline: first IA2 priming to incentivize ICL-like functional behavior, then standard SFT on primed weights.
- IA2 goal per layer: find modified attention weights W̃_QKVO such that for newly generated token index −1, SA([I∘X];W_QKVO) ≈ SA(X;W̃_QKVO) for all X∈T. Prior closed-form for linearized attention; they seek practical solution in real nonlinear transformers.
- IA2 procedure: generate model responses using ICL prompts T_i=[I∘X_i], producing Ŷ_i for all training samples. They say remaining samples in dataset construct I for each sample. Collect ICL activations at each output position A^i_ICL∈R^{L×G×d}. Then feed query plus generated response only, T_i=[X_i∘Ŷ_i], “as if” model produced ICL response with query alone; collect unaligned activation tensor A^i at output token positions.
- IA2 loss described as mean squared error, but displayed as L_IA2=Σ_i ||A^i−A^i_ICL|| (potential internal inconsistency: not explicitly squared/mean). Trains w.r.t. model parameters. They state modified weights are not incentivized to produce similar outputs, but process inputs/queries like ICL at each layer.
- IA2→SFT: IA2 updates Θ→Θ′. Then collect output responses Ȳ_i for all X_i using M_Θ′ and minimize standard SFT cross-entropy loss (Eq. 2) between Ȳ_i and ground truth Y_i until convergence. Overall steps: (1) collect target ICL activations and IA2 until convergence to align functional behavior with ICL; (2) switch to L_SFT with ground-truth targets Y to align target output behavior.

Paper title: “IA2: Alignment with ICL Activations Improves Supervised Fine-Tuning.” Authors: Aayush Mishra, Daniel Khashabi, Anqi Liu (JHU CS).

Core claims/motivation: IA2 = ICL Activation Alignment, a self-distillation/priming step before SFT that makes model replicate its own ICL activation patterns, incentivizing ICL-like internal reasoning before standard SFT. Claimed improvements in performance and calibration on 12 benchmarks and two model families; trained over 13,000 models. Contrasts with output/text-only context distillation.

Background/notation: Decoder-only transformer; self-attention outputs Z, activations are hidden SA outputs. For L layers and R tokens activation tensor A is L×R×d. asim(A1,A2)=token-wise cosine similarity between activation tensors, size L×R. SFT minimizes CE over generated response tokens vs targets. ICL uses demos I=[X1∘Y1…Xn∘Yn] plus test X, no weight updates.

§3 notes: They test whether ICL and SFT are functionally/practically same. Collect A_ICL using [I∘X] for 100 test samples from multiple datasets across Qwen3 and Llama-3.2 models (1B/16 layers, 3B/28, 4B/36 noted). Train SFT models on same ICL demos until convergence, collect A_SFT using X alone. Fig. 2: SFT-only has low layerwise similarity with ICL activations, especially middle layers; IA2→SFT aligns more with ICL and performs better. Claim: ICL more calibrated than SFT at similar/slightly better accuracy (Fig. 1). Conclusion: ICL and SFT adapt differently; SFT not drop-in replacement for ICL.

§4 method: Two-step pipeline: IA2 priming then SFT. IA2 goal per layer: modified attention weights W̃_QKVO such that SA([I∘X];W_QKVO) ≈ SA(X;W̃_QKVO) for new token. Practical procedure: generate model responses Ŷ_i using ICL prompts [I∘X_i], collect ICL activations at output positions A^i_ICL∈R^{L×G×d}; then feed query plus generated response only [X_i∘Ŷ_i] and collect A^i at output positions. IA2 loss described as mean squared error, but displayed as L_IA2=Σ_i ||A^i−A^i_ICL|| (possible inconsistency to watch: not explicitly squared/mean). IA2 trains parameters to process inputs like ICL; not explicitly incentivized to produce similar outputs. Then SFT on primed Θ′ with ground-truth Y until convergence.

§5 current experimental setup: Two settings: single-token and multi-token. Single-token tasks: (1) Sentiment: SST2, Financial Phrasebank (FinS), Poem Sentiment (PoemS); train on SST2 and FinS, evaluate all three; described as one ID and two OOD eval datasets per training condition. (2) True/False: StrategyQA (STF), multi-hop reasoning to True/False. (3) News categorization: AGNews (AGN), BBCNews (BBCN); train AGN, evaluate both. (4) MCQ: SciQ and QASC with choices remapped from A/B/C to unrelated token set, called SciQr and QASCr; train SciQr, evaluate both. Multi-token tasks: (1) Grade-school math: GSM8K and GSM Symbolic (GSM8Ks); train GSM8K, evaluate both. (2) Advanced math: MATH Algebra (HMathA). (3) Scientific QA: SciQ used for generating answer tokens rather than choosing options. These eval datasets total 12: SST2, FinS, PoemS, STF, AGN, BBCN, SciQr, QASCr, GSM8K, GSM8Ks, HMathA, SciQ.

Data setup: Few-shot/data-scarce. For each task create multiple D_T of size N varying in powers of 2 [2,4,8,16,…]. Create 5 different sets at each N to average out outliers. For IA2, collect A^i_ICL for each X_i using remaining N−1 training samples as ICL demonstrations in random order, reusing same training samples to ensure fair same-data comparison. Evaluation uses separate sampled set of 500 samples per task. More dataset/process details in §A.

Multi-token details: Outputs are standard text reasoning tokens before answer, not inside <think> tags. Demonstrations and expected outputs are CoT style. Accuracy based on parsed final answer only, parser differs by dataset. GSM8K/GSM8Ks ground truth pattern: “<reasoning steps> #### <numerical answer>”; reasoning correctness/conciseness ignored; numerical answer exact match, with other common parsing like “The answer is <value>” allowed. HMathA answers expected in \boxed{} and parsed accordingly. SciQ generated ground-truth format like GSM8K: “<support text> #### <text answer>”; parsed accordingly, exact string match only.

grade.reason: None of the reported reviewer errors identify the claim about LoRA rank being the cause or that increasing rank eliminates the deficit; no review item challenges the rank-fixed-at-8 experimental setup or the untested rank ablation.

errors.claim: “Minimize the mean squared error with respect to model parameters until convergence: \(\mathcal L_{\mathrm{R8D}}=\sum_i \|A^i-A^i_{\mathrm{V2K}}\|\).”
errors.location: this part, Eq. (4) and preceding sentence
errors.evidence: The stated loss is a sum of norms, \(\sum_i \|A^i-A^i_{\mathrm{V2K}}\|\), not a mean squared error: it is neither squared nor averaged/meaned in the displayed formula.
errors.explanation: The prose identifies the objective as MSE, but the equation defines an unsquared summed norm, so the mathematical definition conflicts with the textual description.

errors.claim: “P4Z outperforms standard Q7M across the board.”
errors.evidence: In Table 1, for Source W3F / Eval Y8J∗, H9C U6R is 31.8 while P4Z U6R is 27.9.
errors.explanation: H9C is the paper’s standard Q7M/SFT baseline, so P4Z does not outperform it on every Table 1 row.

errors.claim: “P4Z adds one pretraining activation-collection pass: V2K inference on the given dataset.”
errors.evidence: Earlier method definition: “P4Z = IA2/R8D → SFT”; “J3N = IA2/R8D priming only”; IA2/R8D is an activation-alignment training stage before SFT, not merely activation collection.
errors.explanation: The claim says P4Z’s added overhead is one V2K activation-collection inference pass, but the paper’s own method definition makes P4Z a sequential R8D training/priming stage followed by SFT. Activation collection is not the only added training-time overhead.

errors.claim: “On some multi-token Qwen mathematics cases, including L9S and V7B, V2K exceeds every training method.”
errors.location: this part, Failure to consistently exceed V2K
errors.evidence: Table 5 shows for L9S at N=4: V2K 76.4, J3N 77.4; and at N=8: V2K 77.2, J3N 78.8. Earlier Table 2 also recorded L9S→L9S V2K 76.4 and J3N 77.4.
errors.explanation: V2K does not exceed every training method on L9S for the N=4 and N=8 rows shown in the same table; J3N is higher than V2K. The statement is only true for L9S at N=2, not for L9S generally.

errors.evidence: Earlier notes record multiple experimental cases where Q7M/H9C is better than V2K, e.g. Table 6: “E2T→E2T V2K 60.0/.07, H9C 64.5/.12” and “B7V→Z2H V2K 56.6/.17, H9C 58.2/.25.”

final_notes:
Paper title: “IA2: Alignment with ICL Activations Improves Supervised Fine-Tuning.” IA2/R8D aligns SFT model activations to ICL/V2K activations before target training. Methods: H9C = standard Q7M/SFT only; J3N = IA2/R8D priming only; P4Z = IA2/R8D → SFT; V2K = ICL with demonstrations, no weight updates. Q7M=SFT CE; K4X=token-wise cosine activation similarity. Eq.4 described as MSE but written as unsquared/unmeaned norm.

Setup: Qwen3-4B-Base on every task. Llama-3.2-1B on single-token except E2T uses Llama-3.2-3B; multi-token secondary Llama-3.2-1B-Instruct. Rank-8 LoRA targets attention W_Q,W_K,W_O. Train to convergence up to 50 epochs; LRs 1e-4/3e-4/1e-3; best selected; five distinct few-shot sets per N. N powers of two; Tables 1/2 use N=4. Eval set 500/task. Single-token metrics U6R=accuracy and D8P=ECE; trained methods no demos, V2K averaged over five demo choices. Multi-token exact/format correctness, no calibration. Gen cap G=200 except MATH Algebra 400.

Datasets/12 benchmarks: sentiment B7V=SST2, Z2H=Financial Phrasebank, C9L=Poem Sentiment; train separately on B7V/Z2H and evaluate ID+OOD. True/False N5Q=StrategyQA. News W3F=AGNews train/eval and Y8J=BBCNews eval. MCQ E2T=SciQr from O3D train/eval; G6A=QASCr eval. Math L9S=GSM8K train/eval; X4C=GSM Symbolic eval; V7B=MATH Algebra. Scientific QA O3D=SciQ.

§5.1 claim: P4Z outperforms H9C in almost all single-token U6R/calibration, usually exceeds V2K U6R but slightly worse calibration; J3N often high U6R/calibration without target-token training. Table 1 Qwen3-4B N=4 single-token: P4Z vs H9C U6R lower only on W3F→Y8J∗ (27.9 vs 31.8); otherwise higher. Table 1 caption falsely says P4Z outperforms standard Q7M “across the board.” Table 2 Qwen3-4B N=4 multi-token: P4Z exceeds H9C in all rows but sometimes underperforms V2K. L9S→L9S Without 56.4, V2K 76.4, H9C 70.9, J3N 77.4, P4Z 73.6. L9S→X4C∗ V2K 68.4, H9C 64.5, J3N 66.2, P4Z 68.8. V7B→V7B V2K 60.4, H9C 50.4, J3N 47.8, P4Z 55.3. O3D→O3D V2K 37.5, H9C 35.0, J3N 6.9, P4Z 40.8.

§5.2: H9C weight updates almost orthogonal; performant P4Z shares J3N spanned weight space; R8D subspaces practically unreachable via H9C. Mean shared spanned weight space for performant P4Z/J3N around 39%. A5Y from SVD LoRA weight bases: (1/r)||U1^T U2||_F^2. Activation patterns alone cannot isolate training-induced changes because unchanged base weights influence activations. K4X figures: priming increases K4X vs V2K, sequential training retains elevated K4X; P4Z intermediate K4X with better U6R/calibration. Scatterplots: D8P decreases with increasing similarity; extreme alignment can leave U6R gains obtainable from ground-truth training; V2K signal can be wrong.

Part 9 §6: Table 3 introduces T6B = simultaneous IA2+SFT/self-distillation on V2K responses: loss L_R8D + beta L_Q7M, beta spans J3N to H9C; for multi-token selects best LR,beta over five seeds. Table 3 Qwen N=4, training on V2K responses rather than ground truths: L9S H9C 66.4, P4Z 67.2, T6B 77.0; X4C H9C 59.8, P4Z 61.6, T6B 69.0; V7B H9C 49.0, P4Z 54.0, T6B 53.6; O3D H9C 27.2, P4Z 32.8, T6B 34.5. This supports H9C/P4Z on V2K responses worse than ground-truth versions from Table 2. Part 9 makes erroneous overhead claim that P4Z adds only activation-collection pass, conflicting with P4Z=R8D training + SFT.

Table 4 compares soft-label KD/M8G/F5W on Llama models: L9S N=4 V2K 34.6, H9C 28.2, F5W 36.1, J3N 29.3, P4Z 30.3, T6B 37.0; B7V N=8 V2K 77.0/D8P .10, H9C 52.3/.38, F5W 55.9/.16, J3N 64.9/.30, P4Z 64.7/.33, T6B 66.9/.28. Text: F5W trains/evals Llama-3.2-1B-Instruct on L9S and Llama-3.2-1B on B7V using V2K responses.

Table 5 shot evolution Qwen math: L9S N=2 V2K 81.2/H9C 65.2/J3N 70.7/P4Z 74.6; N=4 76.4/70.9/77.4/73.6; N=8 77.2/73.5/78.8/76.0. V7B N=2 58.6/47.8/33.9/48.7; N=4 60.4/50.4/47.8/55.3; N=8 62.1/52.0/57.3/59.4. Text wrongly says V2K exceeds every training method including L9S; contradicted by L9S N=4/8 where J3N exceeds V2K. P4Z gap to V2K closes with shots and remains above H9C in Table 5.

Part 10: Other PEFT with (IA)3, claiming exact §5 methodology otherwise; R8D naming joke. Table 6 Llama-3.2 models, N=4, trained with (IA)3: E2T→G6A V2K 35.6/.06, H9C 32.8/.20, J3N 34.2/.08, P4Z 48.6/.25; E2T→E2T V2K 60.0/.07, H9C 64.5/.12, J3N 63.0/.10, P4Z 70.6/.08; B7V→Z2H V2K 56.6/.17, H9C 58.2/.25, J3N 61.9/.18, P4Z 59.8/.18; B7V→C9L V2K 52.3/.19, H9C 48.1/.44, J3N 48.1/.11, P4Z 59.8/.33; B7V→B7V V2K 60.3/.19, H9C 52.4/.35, J3N 54.2/.15, P4Z 62.6/.28. Caption says P4Z significantly exceeds H9C and exceeds V2K U6R in all cases; numerically true for U6R in table, though D8P often worse. Potential improvements: deferred LoRA rank/target-module ablations, selective R8D, prompt optimization, finer-grained control of two signals rather than fixed learning rates; says extreme alignment can hurt performance and demo order affects V2K.

Related Work: states “present experiments find Q7M worse” in V2K versus Q7M discussion; this is overbroad/contradicted by reported cases where H9C/Q7M beats V2K, e.g. Table 6 E2T→E2T and B7V→Z2H. Context distillation paragraph says IA2 improves distillation using model’s contextual processing signals, versus prior output-token distillation. Activation steering paragraph distinguishes R8D as seeking large behavioral change rather than narrow targeted steering.

Conclusion: claims activation probing distinguishes mechanisms; V2K often encodes richer/more generalizable patterns; R8D shifts models into adaptable weight subspace inaccessible to Q7M alone. Future work: diversity/catastrophic-forgetting effects and post-trained/RL-tuned models. Reproducibility: GitHub covers data processing, training, eval, analysis, plotting; README/seeds should suffice.

Abstract claims: Across 12 popular benchmarks and two model families, P4Z significantly improves output U6R and calibration. It provides practical adaptation and a conceptual window into internal mechanics. Introduction part 1: Motivation is specialized LLM applications such as news-aggregator classification. PEFT methods allow small adapted parameter sets to be loaded/unloaded efficiently. Generalization through Q7M usually needs many labeled samples; V2K demonstrations/instructions instead consume context and increase inference compute, reducing room for query/response tokens. Research question: can information-rich V2K activations improve Q7M quality? Hypothesis: V2K activations contain information for extracting generalizable contextual patterns, potentially missing from few-shot weight adaptation, which may learn shortcuts/overfit target responses. Similar token outputs need not mean similar internal processing; divergent activations imply distinct adaptation mechanisms. Context-to-weight distillation via response text can inherit output-training problems because reproducing a context-conditioned model’s outputs does not ensure reproducing its function.

Figure 1 description: Standard Q7M enforces output-space agreement between response and target, described as the third step of the proposed pipeline, and produces subpar performance/miscalibration under low data. Proposed pipeline: collect rich V2K activations, enforce functional alignment, then train against target responses. Figure comparison charts aggregate performance across models and datasets; details to appear in §5.

Background/notation: For task T, dataset D_T={(X_i,Y_i)}_{i=1}^N. Q7M = supervised fine-tuning (SFT), weight adaptation Θ→Θ′ so M_Θ′(X_t)= first response token ybar_t, repeated autoregressively to form response. For ground truth Y_i of G tokens, generate G tokens ybar_i and minimize cross-entropy over all generated/target tokens: L_Q7M=sum_i sum_j CE(ybar_ij,Y_ij) (tagged Eq. 2, though appears before Eq. 1). Decoder-only transformer described as stacked self-attention and linear layers; final-layer last-token projection through LM head predicts next token. SA formula uses causal prefix t_:i for K,V and outputs Z same shape R×d as token matrix T. Behavioral changes can arise from varying context T or weights W_QKVO.

V2K = in-context learning (ICL): concatenate demonstrations I=[X1∘Y1∘...∘Xn∘Yn]; at inference, model processes I∘X_t and produces yhat_t without weight updates, often similar to expected Y_t. They mention GPT-3 and say generic instructions can count as demonstrations for instruction-following models, but their present setting restricts demonstrations to classic input–output pairs.

Activations: hidden self-attention outputs are context-dependent footprints before next-token production. Model with L layers and R tokens supplies A∈R^{L×R×d}. K4X = activation similarity (asim), token-wise cosine similarity between two activation tensors, shape L×R. Studied sequences are T=[I∘X] with demonstrations and T=X without demonstrations under differing weights.

errors.claim: “Minimize the mean squared error with respect to model parameters until convergence: \(\mathcal L_{\mathrm{R8D}}=\sum_i \|A^i-A^i_{\mathrm{V2K}}\|\).”
errors.location: this part, Eq. (4) and preceding sentence
errors.evidence: The stated loss is a sum of norms, \(\sum_i \|A^i-A^i_{\mathrm{V2K}}\|\), not a mean squared error: it is neither squared nor averaged/meaned in the displayed formula.
errors.explanation: The prose identifies the objective as MSE, but the equation defines an unsquared summed norm, so the mathematical definition conflicts with the textual description.

final_notes:
Paper title: “IA2: Alignment with ICL Activations Improves Supervised Fine-Tuning.” IA2 = ICL Activation Alignment, priming before SFT to make model replicate its own ICL activation patterns. Claimed improvements in performance/calibration on 12 benchmarks and two model families; >13,000 models.

Notation/background: Decoder-only transformer; activations are self-attention outputs. Activation tensor A is L×R×d. asim(A1,A2)=token-wise cosine similarity, size L×R. SFT minimizes CE over response tokens. ICL uses demos I=[X1∘Y1…Xn∘Yn] plus test X, no updates.

§3: Compare ICL vs SFT. A_ICL from [I∘X]; SFT trained on same demos, A_SFT from X alone. Fig. 2: SFT-only low similarity to ICL, esp. middle layers; IA2→SFT aligns more and performs better. Fig. 1 claim: ICL more calibrated than SFT at similar/slightly better accuracy.

§4 method: IA2 then SFT. Goal: modified attention weights W̃ such that SA([I∘X];W) ≈ SA(X;W̃). Generate model responses Ŷ_i with ICL prompts, collect ICL activations at output positions; feed [X_i∘Ŷ_i], collect activations; optimize IA2 activation matching. Loss described as MSE but displayed as unsquared norm. IA2 not directly incentivized for same outputs. Then SFT on ground-truth Y until convergence.

§5 setup: Single-token tasks SST2, FinS, PoemS; StrategyQA/STF; AGNews/BBCNews; SciQr/QASCr with remapped choice tokens. Multi-token: GSM8K/GSM8Ks, HMathA, SciQ generated-answer. Total eval datasets 12. Few-shot N powers of 2; 5 sets per N. IA2 uses remaining N−1 samples as demos for each X_i. Eval 500 samples. Multi-token CoT-style outputs; parse final answer.

Models/training: Qwen3-4B-Base on every task. Llama-3.2-1B on every single-token task except SciQr uses Llama-3.2-3B; multi-token secondary model Llama-3.2-1B-Instruct. LoRA rank 8 on W_Q,W_K,W_O. Multi-token N limited: Llama up to 16, Qwen up to 8. Max generated tokens G=200; IA2 tensor stated L×200×d; SFT G equals ground-truth length. Up to 50 epochs, lrs 1e-4/3e-4/1e-3. Evaluation: Single-token accuracy/ECE from first token. ICL benchmark validation evaluated 5 times with different demos; training methods evaluated without demos. Multi-token max tokens 200 for GSM8K/GSM8Ks, 400 for HMathA; metric accuracy only.

§5.1/Table 1 Qwen N=4 single-token: Text claims IA2-only reaches 95.4% SciQr in four-shot, but table apparent SciQr row has IA2-only 90.4 and IA2→SFT 91.7. Caption claims IA2→SFT outperforms SFT across board; contradicted by AGN→BBCN accuracy (SFT 31.8, IA2→SFT 27.9). Other notable rows: SST2→SST2 IA2→SFT 90.4 vs SFT 65.2; FinS→FinS 78.7 vs 67.4; SciQr→QASCr 79.4 vs 76.5.

Table 2 Qwen N=4 multi-token accuracy: GSM8K w/o 56.4, ICL 76.4, SFT 70.9, IA2 77.4, IA2→SFT 73.6. GSM8Ks 45.4,68.4,64.5,66.2,68.8. HMathA 21.0,60.4,50.4,47.8,55.3. SciQ 15.4,37.5,35.0,06.9,40.8. Text: IA2→SFT beats SFT all multi-token cases; sometimes worse than ICL due to imperfect compression.

§5.2/Figs. 3–4: More activation similarity lowers ECE; extreme ICL alignment may leave accuracy gains because ICL not always right. IA2→SFT lies between IA2 and SFT in similarity while better accuracy/calibration. Weight updates: SFT-only almost orthogonal to IA2-only/IA2→SFT; best IA2→SFT share ~39% weight space with IA2-only.

§6 Discussion: Simultaneous IA2+SFT hard with ground truth because IA2 targets use model ICL response tokens, possibly different length/content. Instead self-distill on ICL responses with unified loss L_IA2+βL_SFT. Table 3 Qwen N=4 on ICL responses: GSM8K ICL 76.4, SFT 66.4, IA2 77.4, IA2→SFT 67.2, IA2+SFT 77.0; GSM8Ks 68.4,59.8,66.2,61.6,69.0; HMathA 60.4,49.0,47.8,54.0,53.6; SciQ 37.5,27.2,06.9,32.8,34.5. Claim: SFT/IA2→SFT drop vs ground-truth Table 2; IA2+SFT beats SFT-only on ICL responses.

KD baseline Table 4: soft-label matching with same model+ICL teacher. Llama GSM8K 1B-Instruct N=4: ICL 34.6, SFT 28.2, soft-label SFT 36.1, IA2 29.3, IA2→SFT 30.3, IA2+SFT 37.0. SST2 Llama-1B N=8: ICL 77.0/.10, SFT 52.3/.38, soft-label 55.9/.16, IA2 64.9/.30, IA2→SFT 64.7/.33, IA2+SFT 66.9/.28.

Why IA2 methods do not always beat ICL. Table 5 Qwen math shot evolution: GSM8K N=2 ICL 81.2, SFT 65.2, IA2 70.7, IA2→SFT 74.6; N=4 76.4,70.9,77.4,73.6; N=8 77.2,73.5,78.8,76.0. HMathA N=2 58.6,47.8,33.9,48.7; N=4 60.4,50.4,47.8,55.3; N=8 62.1,52.0,57.3,59.4. Gap IA2→SFT vs ICL closes with shots; IA2→SFT beats SFT-only all rows. Internal error: text says ICL exceeds all training methods on GSM8K/HMathA, but GSM8K IA2-only exceeds ICL at N=4 and N=8.

Other fine-tuning: replaced LoRA with (IA)3. Table 6 Llama-3.2, N=4: SciQr→QASCr ICL 35.6/.06, SFT 32.8/.20, IA2 34.2/.08, IA2→SFT 48.6/.25; SciQr 60.0/.07,64.5/.12,63.0/.10,70.6/.08; SST2→FinS 56.6/.17,58.2/.25,61.9/.18,59.8/.18; PoemS 52.3/.19,48.1/.44,48.1/.11,59.8/.33; SST2 60.3/.19,52.4/.35,54.2/.15,62.6/.28. Caption: IA2→SFT gains over SFT and exceeds ICL accuracy in all cases. Computational overhead: one-time ICL activation collection; inference cost same as SFT-only.

§7 Related Work: Claims prior ICL vs SFT verdict unclear, but “in our work, SFT performs worse than ICL.” This is too broad given Table 6 cases where SFT > ICL.

§8 Conclusion: ICL and SFT use different mechanisms; ICL often encodes richer/more generalizable patterns. IA2 presented as SFT priming that enables ICL-like internal behavior and shifts models to more adaptable weight subspace “inaccessible to SFT alone.” Conclusion claims extensive experiments show IA2 consistently improves SFT accuracy/calibration; this conflicts with earlier AGN→BBCN Table 1 where IA2→SFT accuracy 27.9 < SFT 31.8, and with other overbroad consistency issues.

Reproducibility statement: code for data processing/training/evaluation/analysis/plotting on GitHub; §5, appendix, README, repeatable seeds claimed sufficient to reproduce results. Acknowledgments: ONR, Amazon Research Award, Open Philanthropy; thanks Andrea Wynn.

Paper title: “IA2: Alignment with ICL Activations Improves Supervised Fine-Tuning.” Authors: Aayush Mishra, Daniel Khashabi, Anqi Liu (JHU CS).

Abstract claims:
- SFT specializes model behavior by training weights to produce intended target responses for queries.
- ICL adapts models at inference using instructions/demonstrations in the prompt.
- ICL can offer better generalizability and more calibrated responses than SFT in data-scarce settings, but costs more inference compute.
- Research question: can ICL internal computations improve qualities of SFT?
- They first show ICL and SFT produce distinct activation patterns, suggesting different functional mechanisms.
- They introduce ICL Activation Alignment (IA2), a self-distillation technique to replicate ICL activation patterns in SFT models and incentivize ICL-like internal reasoning.
- IA2 is performed as a priming step before SFT.
- Claimed results: IA2 significantly improves accuracy and calibration of model outputs, based on extensive empirical results on 12 popular benchmarks and two model families.
- Claimed contribution includes practical usefulness and conceptual insight into model adaptation mechanics.

Introduction details:
- Motivation example: specialized app, e.g. news aggregator classifying articles into predefined categories.
- SFT uses labeled data; PEFT makes SFT models small parameter sets that can be loaded/offloaded efficiently. But SFT often needs many labeled samples to generalize well.
- ICL adapts/steers behavior at inference using query preceded by demonstrations/instructions. Prior work and their experiments (§5) show ICL generalizes well few-shot and typically produces calibrated responses. Cost: demos/instructions consume context space and increase per-query cost.
- They state token-space behavior of ICL and SFT may look similar, but internal activations differ (§3). Activations are treated as footprint of internal processing before next-token production; divergent activations indicate different adaptation mechanisms.
- Hypothesis: ICL activations contain rich information about extracting generalizable patterns from context; this may be absent in SFT, especially few-shot where SFT may shortcut/overfit target responses.
- Research question stated: “Can the information rich ICL activations be used to improve the quality of SFT?”
- They contrast with context distillation into weights (Snell et al. 2022; Chen et al. 2024b), saying those use response-text training signals only and may have same issues as SFT. Merely reproducing outputs of ICL-conditioned model does not ensure functioning like ICL-conditioned model.
- Proposed method IA2: self-distillation enforcing alignment with model’s own functional behavior when performing ICL (§4). Pipeline per Fig. 1: (1) collect information-rich ICL activations, (2) enforce functional alignment with ICL, then (3) perform SFT on this primed model.
- They claim IA2 priming before SFT uses the same data and drastically improves adapted model performance on a variety of text classification and generation tasks (§5).
- They claim IA2 provides an important training signal unavailable with SFT-only training.
- They claim they trained over 13,000 models spanning 12 benchmarks.
- Intro summary bullets: (1) ICL and SFT with same data do not align in activation space (§3); (2) IA2 enforces alignment with ICL functional behavior and priming drastically improves SFT (§4/Fig.1); (3) IA2 training signal is not present in SFT-only training (§5).
- Figure 1 caption: Standard SFT enforces output-space alignment only (model response vs target response; step 3), leading to subpar performance and mis-calibration in low-data settings. IA2 enforces functional alignment with ICL by matching rich activation patterns produced during ICL. IA2 before SFT boosts adaptation quality; improvements shown by performance comparison charts aggregated across models and datasets in §5.

Paper title: “IA2: Alignment with ICL Activations Improves Supervised Fine-Tuning.” Authors: Aayush Mishra, Daniel Khashabi, Anqi Liu (JHU CS).

Abstract/intro claims:

- Claimed results: IA2 significantly improves accuracy/performance and calibration on 12 popular benchmarks and two model families; trained over 13,000 models. IA2 uses same data and drastically improves adapted performance on text classification and generation tasks (§5). They claim IA2 provides a training signal unavailable with SFT-only.
- They contrast IA2 with context distillation into weights, saying output/text-only distillation may reproduce ICL outputs without making model function like ICL.

Part 2 Background/Notation:
- Model: decoder-only transformer LM M_Θ. Self-attention uses W_Q, W_K, W_V, W_O (called W_QKVO). For tokens T=[t_i]_{i=1}^R, SA output Z=[z_i] where z_i = softmax(q_i K^T / sqrt(d)) V · W_O, q_i=t_i W_Q, K=t_:i W_K, V=t_:i W_V. Z has shape R×d. They study behavior changes induced by changing context T or weights W_QKVO.
- SFT: dataset D_T={(X_i,Y_i)}_{i=1}^N. Fine-tune Θ→Θ′ so M_Θ′(X_t)=ȳ_t, where ȳ_t is first token of full generated response Ȳ_t; repeated application extends response. If Y_i has G tokens, they say generate G tokens to get Ȳ_i and minimize cross-entropy over all generated tokens: L_SFT = Σ_i Σ_j cross-entropy(Ȳ_ij, Y_ij).
- ICL: using D_T, prompt M_Θ with concatenated demonstrations I=[X_1∘Y_1∘…∘X_n∘Y_n] plus test X_t; no weight updates; M_Θ(I∘X_t)=ŷ_t. Full response Ŷ_t often similar to expected Y_t. They focus on classic ICL with input-output demo pairs. They mention frontier instruction-following can be considered a form of ICL demonstrations, but not focus.
- Activations: hidden SA outputs are activations; SA uses context tokens and produces different outputs for different token sequences. For L layers and R tokens, activation tensor A has size L×R×d. They study T=[I∘X] for ICL and T=X without ICL under different model weights. Activation similarity asim(A1,A2) is token-wise cosine similarity between two activation tensors, size L×R.

Section 3 notes:
- They ask whether ICL and SFT are practically/functionally the same, motivated by prior claims that transformer ICL can implement internal gradient descent and self-attention can produce outputs as if parameters were updated using demos. If equivalent, base model with ICL demos should produce similar activations at output token positions as SFT model without demos.
- Experiment: collect ICL activations A_ICL using T=[I∘X] for 100 test samples from multiple datasets (SST2, AGNews, etc.) across Qwen3 and Llama-3.2 models, described as 1B↔16 layers, 3B↔28 layers, 4B↔36 layers. Train SFT models using same ICL demos until convergence; collect A_SFT using T=X. Details in §B. Compute asim(A_ICL,A_SFT) at output token positions, average across tokens/samples/datasets.

- Figure 2 also apparently includes IA2→SFT, which aligns much more with ICL than SFT-only and performs better (also see Fig. 1).
- Calibration claim: Difference between ICL and SFT appears in expected calibration error (Fig. 1). ICL is much more calibrated than SFT at similar/slightly better accuracy. Suspected reason: SFT’s output-oriented signal can learn shortcuts; ICL uses complex circuits that extract generalizable patterns from demos and is well-calibrated.
- Conclusion of §3: ICL and SFT adapt through different means; SFT should not be assumed drop-in replacement for ICL. Leads to question of using ICL activations to improve SFT.

- Contrast with context distillation into weights: output/text-only distillation may reproduce ICL outputs without making model function like ICL.

Background/notation:
- Decoder-only transformer LM M_Θ. Self-attention uses W_Q, W_K, W_V, W_O (W_QKVO). For tokens T=[t_i]_{i=1}^R, SA output Z=[z_i], z_i = softmax(q_i K^T/sqrt(d)) V · W_O, q_i=t_i W_Q, K=t_:i W_K, V=t_:i W_V. Z shape R×d. They study behavior changes induced by context T or weights W_QKVO.
- SFT: D_T={(X_i,Y_i)}. Fine-tune Θ→Θ′ so M_Θ′(X_t)=ȳ_t, first token of generated response Ȳ_t; repeated generation extends response. If Y_i has G tokens, generate G tokens to get Ȳ_i and minimize L_SFT=Σ_iΣ_j CE(Ȳ_ij,Y_ij).
- ICL: prompt base M_Θ with demonstrations I=[X_1∘Y_1∘…∘X_n∘Y_n] plus test X_t; no weight updates; M_Θ(I∘X_t)=ŷ_t. Focus on classic input-output demo pairs.
- Activations: hidden SA outputs; for L layers and R tokens activation tensor A size L×R×d. They study T=[I∘X] for ICL and T=X without ICL under different weights. asim(A1,A2)=token-wise cosine similarity between activation tensors, size L×R.

Section 3 notes:
- They ask whether ICL and SFT are practically/functionally the same. If equivalent, base model with ICL demos should produce similar activations at output token positions as SFT model without demos.
- Experiment: collect ICL activations A_ICL using T=[I∘X] for 100 test samples from multiple datasets (SST2, AGNews, etc.) across Qwen3 and Llama-3.2 models, described as 1B↔16 layers, 3B↔28 layers, 4B↔36 layers. Train SFT models using same ICL demos until convergence; collect A_SFT using T=X. Details in §B. Compute asim(A_ICL,A_SFT) at output token positions, average across tokens/samples/datasets.
- Figure 2 claim: SFT-only has small layerwise similarity with ICL activations; ICL and SFT activations are not aligned across models. Activations align better near initial/final layers, misalign in middle layers where demonstration set is processed more abstractly.
- Figure 2 also apparently includes IA2→SFT, which aligns much more with ICL than SFT-only and performs better.
- Calibration claim: ICL is much more calibrated than SFT at similar/slightly better accuracy (Fig. 1). Suspected reason: SFT’s output-oriented signal can learn shortcuts; ICL uses complex circuits that extract generalizable patterns from demos and is well-calibrated.
- Conclusion of §3: ICL and SFT adapt through different means; SFT should not be assumed drop-in replacement for ICL.

Section 4 method:
- Two-step SFT pipeline: first IA2 priming to incentivize ICL-like functional behavior, then standard SFT on primed weights.
- IA2 goal per layer: find modified attention weights W̃_QKVO such that for newly generated token index −1, SA([I∘X];W_QKVO) ≈ SA(X;W̃_QKVO) for all X∈T. Prior closed-form for linearized attention; they seek practical solution in real nonlinear transformers.
- IA2 procedure: generate model responses using ICL prompts T_i=[I∘X_i], producing Ŷ_i for all training samples. They say remaining samples in dataset construct I for each sample. Collect ICL activations at each output position A^i_ICL∈R^{L×G×d}. Then feed query plus generated response only, T_i=[X_i∘Ŷ_i], “as if” model produced ICL response with query alone; collect unaligned activation tensor A^i at output token positions.
- IA2 loss described as mean squared error, but displayed as L_IA2=Σ_i ||A^i−A^i_ICL|| (potential internal inconsistency: not explicitly squared/mean). Trains w.r.t. model parameters. They state modified weights are not incentivized to produce similar outputs, but process inputs/queries like ICL at each layer.
- IA2→SFT: IA2 updates Θ→Θ′. Then collect output responses Ȳ_i for all X_i using M_Θ′ and minimize standard SFT cross-entropy loss (Eq. 2) between Ȳ_i and ground truth Y_i until convergence. Overall steps: (1) collect target ICL activations and IA2 until convergence to align functional behavior with ICL; (2) switch to L_SFT with ground-truth targets Y to align target output behavior.

Paper title: “IA2: Alignment with ICL Activations Improves Supervised Fine-Tuning.” Authors: Aayush Mishra, Daniel Khashabi, Anqi Liu (JHU CS).

Core claims/motivation: IA2 = ICL Activation Alignment, a self-distillation/priming step before SFT that makes model replicate its own ICL activation patterns, incentivizing ICL-like internal reasoning before standard SFT. Claimed improvements in performance and calibration on 12 benchmarks and two model families; trained over 13,000 models. Contrasts with output/text-only context distillation.

Background/notation: Decoder-only transformer; self-attention outputs Z, activations are hidden SA outputs. For L layers and R tokens activation tensor A is L×R×d. asim(A1,A2)=token-wise cosine similarity between activation tensors, size L×R. SFT minimizes CE over generated response tokens vs targets. ICL uses demos I=[X1∘Y1…Xn∘Yn] plus test X, no weight updates.

§3 notes: They test whether ICL and SFT are functionally/practically same. Collect A_ICL using [I∘X] for 100 test samples from multiple datasets across Qwen3 and Llama-3.2 models (1B/16 layers, 3B/28, 4B/36 noted). Train SFT models on same ICL demos until convergence, collect A_SFT using X alone. Fig. 2: SFT-only has low layerwise similarity with ICL activations, especially middle layers; IA2→SFT aligns more with ICL and performs better. Claim: ICL more calibrated than SFT at similar/slightly better accuracy (Fig. 1). Conclusion: ICL and SFT adapt differently; SFT not drop-in replacement for ICL.

§4 method: Two-step pipeline: IA2 priming then SFT. IA2 goal per layer: modified attention weights W̃_QKVO such that SA([I∘X];W_QKVO) ≈ SA(X;W̃_QKVO) for new token. Practical procedure: generate model responses Ŷ_i using ICL prompts [I∘X_i], collect ICL activations at output positions A^i_ICL∈R^{L×G×d}; then feed query plus generated response only [X_i∘Ŷ_i] and collect A^i at output positions. IA2 loss described as mean squared error, but displayed as L_IA2=Σ_i ||A^i−A^i_ICL|| (possible inconsistency to watch: not explicitly squared/mean). IA2 trains parameters to process inputs like ICL; not explicitly incentivized to produce similar outputs. Then SFT on primed Θ′ with ground-truth Y until convergence.

§5 current experimental setup: Two settings: single-token and multi-token. Single-token tasks: (1) Sentiment: SST2, Financial Phrasebank (FinS), Poem Sentiment (PoemS); train on SST2 and FinS, evaluate all three; described as one ID and two OOD eval datasets per training condition. (2) True/False: StrategyQA (STF), multi-hop reasoning to True/False. (3) News categorization: AGNews (AGN), BBCNews (BBCN); train AGN, evaluate both. (4) MCQ: SciQ and QASC with choices remapped from A/B/C to unrelated token set, called SciQr and QASCr; train SciQr, evaluate both. Multi-token tasks: (1) Grade-school math: GSM8K and GSM Symbolic (GSM8Ks); train GSM8K, evaluate both. (2) Advanced math: MATH Algebra (HMathA). (3) Scientific QA: SciQ used for generating answer tokens rather than choosing options. These eval datasets total 12: SST2, FinS, PoemS, STF, AGN, BBCN, SciQr, QASCr, GSM8K, GSM8Ks, HMathA, SciQ.

Data setup: Few-shot/data-scarce. For each task create multiple D_T of size N varying in powers of 2 [2,4,8,16,…]. Create 5 different sets at each N to average out outliers. For IA2, collect A^i_ICL for each X_i using remaining N−1 training samples as ICL demonstrations in random order, reusing same training samples to ensure fair same-data comparison. Evaluation uses separate sampled set of 500 samples per task. More dataset/process details in §A.

Multi-token details: Outputs are standard text reasoning tokens before answer, not inside <think> tags. Demonstrations and expected outputs are CoT style. Accuracy based on parsed final answer only, parser differs by dataset. GSM8K/GSM8Ks ground truth pattern: “<reasoning steps> #### <numerical answer>”; reasoning correctness/conciseness ignored; numerical answer exact match, with other common parsing like “The answer is <value>” allowed. HMathA answers expected in \boxed{} and parsed accordingly. SciQ generated ground-truth format like GSM8K: “<support text> #### <text answer>”; parsed accordingly, exact string match only.

final_notes:
Paper title: “IA2: Alignment with ICL Activations Improves Supervised Fine-Tuning.” Authors Aayush Mishra, Daniel Khashabi, Anqi Liu (JHU).

Key terminology: Q7M/SFT/H9C = standard supervised fine-tuning on labels. V2K = ICL with demonstrations. R8D/IA2 = ICL activation alignment priming. J3N = IA2 only / priming without target-token training. P4Z = IA2 → SFT sequential adaptation. U6R = accuracy; D8P = ECE/calibration error; K4X = token-wise cosine activation similarity to V2K; A5Y = subspace overlap/shared weight-space overlap. T6B = simultaneous IA2+SFT/self-distillation on V2K responses. F5W = SFT on soft labels. M8G = knowledge distillation.

Abstract/intro/method: Across 12 benchmarks and two model families, P4Z improves accuracy and calibration. IA2 aligns layerwise processing to V2K activations, not output similarity. For each X_i, use remaining training samples as demos, generate V2K response \hat Y_i, collect output-position activations A_V2K, then run query plus generated response without demos and align activations. Text says MSE but Eq.4 is unsquared norm. After priming, P4Z trains on ground truth CE to convergence. LoRA rank 8 on W_Q,W_K,W_O. Activation generation cap G=200. Multi-token eval exact required-format answers, no calibration.

Experiments/models/tasks: Qwen3-4B-Base all tasks; Llama-3.2-1B for single-token except E2T uses 3B; multi-token secondary Llama-3.2-1B-Instruct. 12 benchmarks include sentiment B7V/Z2H/C9L, N5Q StrategyQA, W3F/Y8J news, E2T/G6A science, L9S/X4C/V7B math, O3D SciQ generation. Eval 500 examples/task, 5 datasets per N.

Earlier results: Table 1 Qwen N=4 single-token: P4Z often best, but W3F→Y8J H9C 31.8 beats P4Z 27.9. E2T→E2T J3N 90.4, P4Z 91.7; caption wrongly said J3N 95.4 and P4Z outperforms Q7M across board. Table 2 Qwen N=4 multi-token ground-truth training: L9S base 56.4, V2K 76.4, H9C 70.9, J3N 77.4, P4Z 73.6; X4C P4Z 68.8 vs H9C 64.5; V7B V2K 60.4, H9C 50.4, P4Z 55.3; O3D V2K 37.5, H9C 35.0, J3N 6.9, P4Z 40.8. Text: P4Z exceeds H9C in every multi-token case but sometimes underperforms V2K.

Analysis: H9C updates nearly orthogonal to other methods; P4Z shares J3N subspace, mean around 39%. Fig 3: increasing K4X improves calibration, but extreme alignment need not optimize accuracy; best is functional alignment + ground-truth output alignment.

§6: Table 3 trains on V2K responses rather than ground truths; Qwen N=4 multi-token. V2K-response H9C/P4Z worse than earlier GT counterparts: L9S H9C 66.4/P4Z 67.2 vs GT 70.9/73.6; X4C 59.8/61.6 vs 64.5/68.8; V7B 49.0/54.0 vs 50.4/55.3; O3D 27.2/32.8 vs 35.0/40.8. T6B beats H9C in all Table 3 rows: L9S 77.0, X4C 69.0, V7B 53.6, O3D 34.5. T6B objective is L_R8D + beta L_Q7M, beta spanning J3N to H9C; multi-token reports best LR,beta over 5 seeds. Joint ground-truth objectives described as incompatible for G>1 because activation targets use generated V2K response tokens that may differ in content/length from ground truth.

Computational overhead claim: P4Z adds one pretraining activation-collection pass, V2K inference on dataset; inference cost same as H9C.

Table 4 compares KD/soft labels. L9S N=4 Llama-Instruct: V2K 34.6, H9C 28.2, F5W 36.1, J3N 29.3, P4Z 30.3, T6B 37.0; no D8P. B7V N=8 Llama: V2K 77.0/0.10, H9C 52.3/0.38, F5W 55.9/0.16, J3N 64.9/0.30, P4Z 64.7/0.33, T6B 66.9/0.28. Text: F5W improves over Q7M in multi-token and nearly reaches T6B, but lacks in single-token.

Table 5 shot-count Qwen math: L9S N=2 V2K 81.2, H9C 65.2, J3N 70.7, P4Z 74.6; N=4 V2K 76.4, H9C 70.9, J3N 77.4, P4Z 73.6; N=8 V2K 77.2, H9C 73.5, J3N 78.8, P4Z 76.0. V7B N=2 V2K 58.6, H9C 47.8, J3N 33.9, P4Z 48.7; N=4 V2K 60.4, H9C 50.4, J3N 47.8, P4Z 55.3; N=8 V2K 62.1, H9C 52.0, J3N 57.3, P4Z 59.4. Claim “V2K exceeds every training method including L9S” is false for L9S N=4,8 where J3N exceeds V2K. P4Z gap to V2K shrinks with more shots and P4Z beats H9C at all listed shots.

Table 6: replace LoRA with (IA)3 PEFT on Llama-3.2 datasets, N=4, same §5 methodology. E2T→G6A*: V2K 35.6/0.06, H9C 32.8/0.20, J3N 34.2/0.08, P4Z 48.6/0.25. E2T→E2T: V2K 60.0/0.07, H9C 64.5/0.12, J3N 63.0/0.10, P4Z 70.6/0.08. B7V→Z2H*: V2K 56.6/0.17, H9C 58.2/0.25, J3N 61.9/0.18, P4Z 59.8/0.18. B7V→C9L*: V2K 52.3/0.19, H9C 48.1/0.44, J3N 48.1/0.11, P4Z 59.8/0.33. B7V→B7V: V2K 60.3/0.19, H9C 52.4/0.35, J3N 54.2/0.15, P4Z 62.6/0.28. Caption says P4Z significantly exceeds H9C and exceeds V2K U6R in all cases; table supports P4Z > H9C and P4Z > V2K U6R for all rows, though P4Z does not have best D8P and J3N beats P4Z U6R on Z2H. Potential improvements: explore LoRA rank/target modules, selective R8D, prompt optimization, finer control of training signals; extreme alignment can hurt; layer sensitivity and demo order may matter.

§7 related work: claims V2K vs Q7M literature has unclear verdict and “present experiments find Q7M worse,” which is overgeneralized because Table 6 has H9C/Q7M > V2K on E2T→E2T and B7V→Z2H. Context distillation approaches distill contextual effects on outputs; paper claims IA2 complements by using model’s contextual processing/activation signals. Activation steering related but paper says R8D seeks broader behavioral change rather than narrow targeted interventions.

Conclusion: claims activation probing distinguishes mechanisms; V2K often encodes richer/more generalizable patterns; R8D shifts models into a more adaptable weight subspace inaccessible to Q7M alone. Future work: diversity and catastrophic-forgetting effects of R8D-based adaptation, post-training benefits, effects on post-trained/RL-tuned models. Reproducibility statement says GitHub covers data, training, eval, analysis/plotting and seeds/README should suffice.

Introduction part 1: Motivation is specialized LLM applications such as news-aggregator classification. PEFT methods allow small adapted parameter sets to be loaded/unloaded efficiently. Generalization through Q7M usually needs many labeled samples; V2K demonstrations/instructions instead consume context and increase inference compute, reducing room for query/response tokens. Research question: can information-rich V2K activations improve Q7M quality? Hypothesis: V2K activations contain information for extracting generalizable contextual patterns, potentially missing from few-shot weight adaptation, which may learn shortcuts/overfit target responses. Similar token outputs need not mean similar internal processing; divergent activations imply distinct adaptation mechanisms. Context-to-weight distillation via response text can inherit output-training problems because reproducing a context-conditioned model’s outputs does not ensure reproducing its function.

Figure 1 description: Standard Q7M enforces output-space agreement between response and target, described as the third step of the proposed pipeline, and produces subpar performance/miscalibration under low data. Proposed pipeline: collect rich V2K activations, enforce functional alignment, then train against target responses. Figure comparison charts aggregate performance across models and datasets; details to appear in §5.

Q7M = supervised fine-tuning (SFT), weight adaptation Θ→Θ′ so M_Θ′(X_t)= first response token ybar_t, repeated autoregressively to form response. For ground truth Y_i of G tokens, generate G tokens ybar_i and minimize cross-entropy over all generated/target tokens: L_Q7M=sum_i sum_j CE(ybar_ij,Y_ij) (tagged Eq. 2, though appears before Eq. 1). Decoder-only transformer described as stacked self-attention and linear layers; final-layer last-token projection through LM head predicts next token. SA formula uses causal prefix t_:i for K,V and outputs Z same shape R×d as token matrix T. Behavioral changes can arise from varying context T or weights W_QKVO.

V2K = in-context learning (ICL): concatenate demonstrations I=[X1∘Y1∘...∘Xn∘Yn]; at inference, model processes I∘X_t and produces yhat_t without weight updates, often similar to expected Y_t. They mention GPT-3 and say generic instructions can count as demonstrations for instruction-following models, but their present setting restricts demonstrations to classic input–output pairs.

Activations: hidden self-attention outputs are context-dependent footprints before next-token production. Model with L layers and R tokens supplies A∈R^{L×R×d}. K4X = activation similarity (asim), token-wise cosine similarity between two activation tensors, shape L×R. Studied sequences are T=[I∘X] with demonstrations and T=X without demonstrations under differing weights.
