final_notes:
Paper title: “Some Robustness Properties of Label Cleaning” by Chen Cheng and John Duchi.

Main setup: task risk R(f)=E ell(d∘f(X),Y) or E ell(d∘f(X),P(.|X)); surrogate risk R_phi(f)=E phi(f(X),Y). Aggregation observes Z and A:Z→A, aggregated surrogate risk R_{phi,A}=E phi(f(X),A(Z)).

Sec.3 consistency: F all Borel. Fisher consistency iff pointwise calibration psi>0. Prop.3 aggregation: phi Fisher consistent for task iff aggregated calibration positive; comparison psi_A(R(f)-R*)≤R_{phi,A}(f)-R_{phi,A}*. Ranking: without aggregation convex score surrogates inconsistent for k≥3; with repeated comparisons aggregated to wins vector, squared loss Fisher consistent if m≥k. Identifying surrogates: Def.3.1 (C_phi,1,C_phi,2)-identifying via margins; binary hinge (1,2). Generalized majority vote A_m. Cor.3.2: m(n)→∞ and identifying => aggregated surrogate excess→0 implies task excess→0. Level-(xi,zeta) consistency has comparison to aggregated surrogate excess; earlier formula typo used R_phi(f)-R*. Noise: Delta=min excess conditional risk for wrong prediction; binary Delta=|2P(Y=1|X)-1|. Mammen-Tsybakov Nα/Mβ equivalence claimed via β=α/(1−α) (α=1 issue). Condition number kappa; e_m(t)=t sqrt((2/m)log(4k(C1+C2)/C1)). Theorem 1: if R−R* ≥ 2P(kappa>M)+(4 C_MT e_m(M))^{1/(1−α)}, then R−R*≤(16/C1) aggregated surrogate excess; xi_m is inf threshold, xi_m→0. Cor.3.3 thresholds: binary (32 C_MT²/m log(8(C1+C2)/C1))^{1/[2(1−α)]}; k≥3: 4*(32 C_MT^4/m log(4k(C1+C2)/C1))^{α/[2(1−α²)]}. Text later says α=1 with m large gives xi=0 though formulas undefined.

Examples: binary nonsmooth margin: Lemma 3.1 feasible C1=phi(0)-phi(delta), C2=phi(-delta); comparison 16/C1. Bipartite matching: k=N!, loss normalized Hamming; structured hinge C1=1/N,C2=2; threshold includes 4*(32 C_MT^4/m log(4k(2N+1)))^{α/[2(1−α²)]}; comparison should be 16N times aggregated excess, but text wrote A_n. General structured: Lemma 3.3 structured hinge C1=min loss, C2=max tau+1; if binary embeddings and normalized Hamming, tau=1,C2=2. Final specialization omitted leading 4 and used 8/C1 instead of 16/C1.

Sec.4 restricted classes. 4.1 binary: Y={±1}, zero-one ell=1{ys≤0}, margin varphi(s,y)=phi(sy), phi convex. All-measurable Fisher iff phi'(0)<0. Linear F={f_theta=<theta,x>}. Optimally predictable along theta*: sign matches Bayes sign. Prop.4: for any eps and nonzero theta*, ∃P optimally predictable along theta* such that all surrogate minimizers have larger task risk than theta* and |cos angle|≤eps. Notation issue: proposition uses E[phi(f_theta(X),Y)] although phi unary. Aggregation A_m majority: epsilon_m-argmin E[phi(A_m(Ys) f_theta(X))] yields R→R* and cos(theta_m,theta*)→1.

4.2 multiclass: Y=[k], zero-one, decoder argmax_y s_y. F linear cone with f^T1=0 and closed under positive scaling. Surrogate varphi Fisher consistent and limiting loss condition (13): varphi(s,y)→0 if s_y−s_j→∞ for all j≠y. Examples: multiclass logistic and pairwise margin losses with phi convex nonincreasing, phi'(0)<0, inf phi=0. Zhang theorem: such losses consistent over all measurable centered scores; binary margin included via f=(g,-g). Linear multiclass functions with sum_i theta_i=0 form convex cone. New definition: F optimally predicts P if ∃f∈F whose argmax lies in argmax of conditional class probabilities for all x. Theorem 2: if F cone optimally predicts P, P(Delta>0)=1, majority vote A_m, epsilon_m→0, then any epsilon_m-argmin of aggregated surrogate risk has R(f_m)→R*. Text says this gives asymptotic consistency by aggregation and contrasts Prop.4.

4.3 finite-dimensional multiclass. X=R^d,Y=[k], linear predictors Θ=[θ1…θ_{k−1}], θ_k=0 convention. True categorical p_Θ(x) from link σ(t) with σ_k=1−1^Tσ and consistency condition (14): t_y=max_i t_i iff σ_y(t)=max_i σ_i(t), with t_k=0. Logistic link example. With repeated labels and majority vote Y_i^+, distribution p_{Θ,m} via ρ_m; text says ρ_m satisfies (14). Logistic loss (15), gradient, population L_m minimizer satisfies E[X(σ_lr(Θ_m^T X)−ρ_m(Θ*^T X))^T]=0. Claims for k=2 and Gaussian X, mis-specified link gives Θ_m=t_mΘ*, hence classification consistent for all m. For k≥3 slight misspecification causes failure. Defines T_ε of Lebesgue measure ε and σ^ε(t)=σ_lr(t) outside T_ε, uniform inside T_ε; prose incorrectly reverses this. Also claim σ^ε clearly satisfies (14) is false for t in T_ε unless ties. Defines L_{m,ε}, Θ_m(ε), notes Θ_1(0)=Θ*. Prop.5: for k≥3, Σ=I, assuming linear map M↦DM=E[Z(∇σ_lr(Θ*^T Z)MZ)^T] for Z~N(0,I_{k−1}) is invertible, ∃ε0>0 such that for any ε∈(0,ε0), ∃T_ε of Lebesgue measure ≤ε with Θ_1(ε)/||Θ_1(ε)|| ≠ Θ*/||Θ*||; proof in App.E.1. Then majority vote addresses inconsistency as m→∞ for any true link σ satisfying (14): define L_{m,σ}, Θ_m=argmin. Theorem3: if Θ*=U*T* with U*∈R^{d×(k−1)} orthogonal and T* nonsingular, then ∃T_m with Θ_m=U*T_m for every m, ||T_m||→∞ and T_m/||T_m||→T*/||T*||. Claimed as evidence of robustness/asymptotic consistency in misspecified models, contrasting Prop.5.

Sec.5 numerics. Experiment 1: binary truncated quadratic phi(δ)=max{1−δ,0}²; cites Bartlett calibration psi(ε)=ε². With majority vote and Lemma 3.1 δ=1, no low-noise α=0,C_MT=1: psi_m(ε)=1/16(ε−sqrt(32/m log 40))_+. This matches C1=phi(0)-phi(1)=1 and C2=phi(-1)=4. Figure 1 compares psi vs psi_m for m=2^16,…,2^32 and says aggregation moves quadratic toward linear, though theorem bound conservative. Experiment 2: logistic Sec.4.3 k=3,d=2 with corrupted link tildeσ(t)=σ_lr(t)1{||t||≤r}+σ_lr(αt)1{||t||>r}, r=3, α=0.1, θ1*=(0,1)^T, θ2*=(1,1)^T. Claims Fig.2 shows asymptotic consistency as m→∞. Caption gives erroneous classification error formula || ||T_m|| − T*/||T*|| ||, inconsistent with Theorem3 convergence T_m/||T_m||→T*/||T*||. Left: n=10000 multilabeled observations for each m. Right: n=640000/m so total labels fixed. 95% error bars over T=100 trials.

Sec.6 discussion: future work. Says many consistency results rely on m→∞; ranking Sec.3.1 has finite-m guarantees. Notes κ(X) captures multiclass comparison difficulty; binary κ=1; low Mammen-Tsybakov noise α≈1 need not control κ in multiclass. Says Sec.4.3/misspecified-model results require optimal predictability (12), i.e. Bayes-optimal classifier in F; classical surrogate consistency may fail even then, while aggregation can succeed. Suggests extending comparison inequalities with aggregation to restricted classes/H-consistency; cites smooth convex loss quadratic psi growth as rate optimal.

Paper title: “Some Robustness Properties of Label Cleaning” by Chen Cheng and John Duchi.

Abstract claims:

Paper title: “Some Robustness Properties of Label Cleaning” by Chen Cheng and John Duchi.

Abstract claims:
- Learning procedures relying on aggregated/cleaned labels (label information distilled from noisy responses) have robustness properties impossible without data cleaning.
- In risk consistency setting (minimizing surrogate losses instead of task loss such as 0-1 misclassification), procedures using label aggregation get stronger consistency guarantees than possible using raw labels.
- Classical perfectly specified statistical models suggest using all information/modeling label uncertainty is statistically efficient.
- However, consistency fails for “standard” approaches when the minimized loss is even slightly misspecified.
- Procedures leveraging aggregated information still converge to optimal classifiers, showing robustness from considering the full pipeline: data collection → model fitting → prediction, refining noisy signals.

Introduction key claims:
- Modern supervised datasets often require cleaning/filtering/crowdsourcing multiple labels and denoising; paper investigates how data aggregation improves consistency of fitted models.
- Main thesis: label cleaning/aggregating labels provides robustness impossible without aggregation.
- Two faces of robustness:
  1. Improved consistency of estimation: when minimizing surrogate losses (e.g. multiclass logistic) instead of task losses (e.g. zero-one error), aggregated-label procedures can achieve consistent/optimal prediction in the limit when impossible without aggregation.
  2. Even in finite-dimensional statistical problems, aggregation can provide consistent classifiers when standard methods fail.
- Motivating questions: whether aggregation is needed for surrogate consistency, and if it helps, in what sense.
- Paper proposes concrete examples in ranking and binary/multiclass classification with linear estimators where estimators using only pairs (X,Y) necessarily fail but label aggregation yields consistency.
- Develops new notions/theory for surrogate consistency with data aggregation.
- In fully nonparametric scenarios, shows how number of aggregated samples combines with noise conditions to improve consistency.
- Claims aggregation permits surrogate risk consistency under only weak conditions on the surrogate loss; losses using aggregated labels admit approximate linear comparison inequalities.
- Unlike conventional risk consistency theory requiring hypothesis class F of all measurable functions, paper will show classification results where aggregating labels guarantees consistency even over restricted hypothesis classes, which may fail without aggregation.

Background mentioned:
- Surrogate risk consistency literature: Bartlett/Jordan/McAuliffe characterized binary convex surrogate consistency for zero-one error; further work in multilabel, ranking, structured prediction, ordinal regression, restricted classes, general theory.
- Existing analyses typically assume standard supervised pairs (X,Y) and do not address aggregation machinery.

errors.claim: “we investigate (2), whose minimizers frequently coincide with the original problem (2)”
errors.evidence: The paper first defines the original task risk as equation (1): “the goal is to minimize the task risk… (1)”. It then introduces the conditional-distribution version as equation (2): “we investigate … (2)”.
errors.explanation: The phrase says equation (2) coincides with the original problem (2), but the original problem was numbered (1). This is an internal numbering/reference inconsistency.

errors.claim: “letting m_{ij}=\sum_{y\in\mathcal{Y}^{m}}1\!\left\{y=(i,j)\right\}”
errors.evidence: The same paragraph defines the observed aggregate object as “multiple independent pairwise comparisons Z=(Y_1,\ldots,Y_m)” and then says “Regressing directly on A(Z) when A(Z)\neq\star yields consistency.”
errors.explanation: As written, the summation variable y ranges over m-tuples in \mathcal{Y}^m, so y cannot equal the single pair (i,j). Thus all m_{ij} would be zero, forcing m_j=0 and A(Z)=\star always, which conflicts with the later use of cases where A(Z)\neq\star. The definition appears internally inconsistent with its intended role as counts/frequencies of observed comparisons in Z.

errors.claim: “the pointwise and uniform calibration functions ... \(\overline{\psi}_{A}(\epsilon)\coloneqq\inf_{s\in\mathbb{R}^{d}}\overline{\psi}_{A}(\epsilon,x)\)”
errors.evidence: Immediately before, \(\overline{\psi}_{A}(\epsilon,x)\) is already defined as an infimum over \(s\): \(\overline{\psi}_{A}(\epsilon,x)\coloneqq\inf_{s\in\mathbb{R}^{d}}\{\delta_{\varphi,A}(s,x)\mid\delta_{\ell}(s,x)\geq\epsilon\}\). Earlier notes for Corollary 3.1 also record the uniform calibration as an infimum over \(x\): “overline psi=inf_x psi.”
errors.explanation: The stated ‘uniform’ calibration function takes an infimum over \(s\) of a quantity that no longer depends on \(s\), while leaving \(x\) free. This conflicts with both the immediately preceding pointwise definition and the earlier standard definition, where the uniform function is obtained by infimizing over \(x\), not over \(s\).

errors.claim: “the aggregation strategy (7) allows an explicitly improved comparison inequality ψ(R(f)-R*) ≤ R_φ(f) − R*”
errors.evidence: Definition 3.2 in this same part defines the aggregated comparison inequality as “ψ(R(f)−R*) ≤ R_{φ,A}(f) − R^*_{φ,A}.” Earlier notes also define aggregated surrogate risk R_{φ,A} and its optimum R^*_{φ,A}.
errors.explanation: The opening formula subtracts the task optimum R* from the surrogate risk R_φ(f), mixing task and surrogate risks, and omits the aggregator A. This conflicts with the paper’s own definition of the comparison inequality for aggregated surrogates.

errors.claim: “In the bipartite matching specialization: one has R(f)-R^* ≤ 16N(R_{φ,A_n}(f)-R_{φ,A_n}^*).”
errors.evidence: Throughout the theorem/corollary and the immediately preceding condition the aggregation level is denoted m: “once m, the number of aggregated labels…” and “for all measurable f … such that [condition involving 1/m]”. Earlier notes: Theorem 1/Corollary 3.3 compare against R_{φ,A_m}(f)-R^*_{φ,A_m}.

Earlier thesis: label cleaning/aggregation gives robustness unavailable without cleaning; aggregation yields stronger risk consistency, esp. misspecified/finite-dimensional settings. Setup: task risk R(f)=E ell(d∘f(X),Y), generalized R(f)=E ell(d∘f(X),P(.|X)); surrogate risk; aggregation observes repeated/noisy Z and A(Z). A_m often empirical task-loss minimizer/majority vote.

Sec3 calibration: Prop3 Fisher consistency iff pointwise aggregated calibration positive; biconjugate comparison ψ_A(R−R*)≤aggregated surrogate excess. Ranking: no convex Fisher-consistent surrogate for k≥3 without aggregation; aggregated comparison counts + squared loss is Fisher consistent if m≥k. Identifying surrogates Def3.1 constants C1,C2; Cor3.2: if m(n)→∞ and identifying surrogate, A_m surrogate excess→0 implies task excess→0. Def3.2 level-(ξ,ζ) consistency. Noise: Δ minimal conditional excess; Nα/Mβ; κ. Theorem1: identifying, majority vote, bounded loss, Nα: above threshold gives R−R*≤16/C1 aggregated surrogate excess. Cor3.3 thresholds: binary and multiclass; α=1 gives uniform linear comparison for m=O(log k). Examples: binary margin identifying; bipartite matching structured hinge C1=1/N,C2=2; some printed inconsistencies noted earlier (A_n vs A_m; missing factors in application).

Sec4 restricted-model consistency. 4.1 binary: zero-one, margin surrogate φ convex nonnegative; classical all-measurable consistency iff φ′(0)<0. Linear class F={fθ=<θ,x>}. Optimally predictable along θ*: sign(<θ*,x>)=Bayes sign. Prop4: for any ε>0, nonzero θ*, exists distribution optimally predictable along θ* such that every surrogate minimizer has higher task risk than θ* and can be nearly orthogonal. Aggregation: repeated labels, majority vote; Cor4.1 from Thm2: if P optimally predictable along θ*, ε_m→0, then R(fθm)→R(fθ*) and cos angle→1.

4.2 multiclass restricted classes: Y=[k], F linear cone with f^T1=0 and tf∈F. Zero-one argmax. Surrogate Fisher consistent and limiting loss condition (13). Logistic and pairwise margin examples. Define multiclass optimal predictability: exists f∈F with argmax f_y(x) in argmax conditional class probabilities for all x. Theorem2: If F cone optimally predicts P, P(Δ>0)=1, ε_m→0, A_m majority vote on m labels, any ε_m-argmin of aggregated surrogate risk over F has R(f_m)→R*.

4.3 finite-dimensional multiclass. X=R^d,Y=[k], linear Θ=[θ1…θ_{k−1}], θ_k=0. Conditional p_Θ(x) via link σ with link consistency (14): t_y=max_i t_i iff σ_y(t)=max_i σ_i(t). Logistic link. Repeated labels; majority vote probabilities p_{Θ,m} using ρ_m; text says ρ_m satisfies (14). Fit logistic loss; gradient condition. Binary k=2 with Gaussian X and misspecified link: Θ_m=t_mΘ*, classification consistent any m. For k≥3, slight misspecification breaks consistency without aggregation. Defines T_ε and σ^ε; prose incorrectly reverses inside/outside, and uniform region violates (14) despite text saying clearly satisfies it. Prop5: for k≥3, Σ=I, Z~N(0,I_{k−1}), invertibility assumption, ∃ small ε and T_ε measure≤ε with Θ_1(ε) direction different from Θ*. Then majority vote addresses inconsistency as m→∞ for any true link σ satisfying (14). Theorem3: if Θ*=U*T* with U* orthogonal and T* nonsingular, then ∃T_m with Θ_m=U*T_m for every m, ||T_m||→∞ and T_m/||T_m||→T*/||T*||.

Sec5 numerical illustrations. Exp1: binary squared hinge/truncated quadratic φ(δ)=max{1−δ,0}^2; Bartlett ψ(ε)=ε^2. With majority vote, Lemma3.1 δ=1, no low-noise α=0,C_MT=1 gives ψ_m(ε)=1/16(ε−sqrt((32/m)log40))_+. Claims aggregated curve transitions from quadratic toward linear as m→∞, but ψ_m conservative. Exp2: k=3,d=2 logistic loss with corrupted link \tildeσ(t)=σ^lr(t)1{||t||≤r}+σ^lr(αt)1{||t||>r}; θ1*=(0,1), θ2*=(1,1), r=3, α=0.1, m∈{1,4,16,64,256,1024}; n=10000 fixed or n=640000/m fixed label budget, 100 trials 95% bars. Caption inconsistency: reports error || ||T_m|| − T*/||T*|| ||, conflicting with Theorem3’s T_m/||T_m||→T*/||T*|| and dimensionally invalid.

Sec6 discussion: cites debate: unaggregated all labels may be statistically efficient if model can represent uncertainty, while cleaning robust otherwise; paper claims evidence for limits of uncleaned/unaggregated labels and robustness from cleaning. Future work: finite-m theory (only explicit finite-m consistency in ranking Sec3.1); characterize when label cleaning needed. Noise condition number κ: binary κ=1; multiclass κ can be large even with low Mammen–Tsybakov noise α≈1; need loss/surrogate-dependent difficulty and failure modes. Mis-specified models: results esp Sec4.3 rely on optimal predictability/Bayes-optimal classifier in F; methods with aggregation can succeed where classical surrogate consistency fails; beyond this remains open. Restricted-class comparison inequalities: current paper gives nonparametric comparison inequalities and parametric statistical consistency; future extend H-consistency/restricted-class comparison inequalities, possibly aggregation upgrading quadratic ψ behavior for smooth convex losses.

Part 1 (Abstract): Paper claims label-cleaning/aggregation methods have robustness properties unavailable without cleaning. In risk consistency with surrogate losses for task losses (e.g., 0-1 classification error), procedures using label aggregation get stronger consistency guarantees than possible using raw labels. It also claims that in perfectly specified classical statistical models, modeling uncertainty in labels / using all information can be statistically efficient, but consistency of “standard” approaches fails when the minimized loss is even slightly misspecified. Part 1 (Abstract): Paper claims label-cleaning/aggregation methods have robustness properties unavailable without cleaning. In risk consistency with surrogate losses for task losses (e.g., 0-1 classification error), procedures using label aggregation get stronger consistency guarantees than possible using raw labels. It also claims that in perfectly specified classical statistical models, modeling uncertainty in labels / using all information can be statistically efficient, but consistency of “standard” approaches fails when the minimized loss is even slightly misspecified. In contrast, procedures using aggregated information still converge to optimal classifiers. Overall thesis: considering full pipeline (collection, model fitting, prediction) and refining noisy signals via aggregation yields more robust methodology.

Part 2 (Introduction): Reiterates that modern supervised datasets often involve cleaning/filtering/crowdsourcing multiple labels and denoising. Main thesis: label cleaning/aggregation provides robustness impossible without aggregation. Two robustness aspects: (1) improved consistency when minimizing surrogate loss (e.g., multiclass logistic) instead of task loss (e.g., zero-one error); aggregated-label procedures can be consistent/optimal in limits where non-aggregated procedures cannot. (2) Even finite-dimensional statistical problems: aggregation can provide consistent classifiers when standard methods fail. Existing surrogate-risk consistency theory mostly assumes standard (X,Y) pairs and does not address aggregation. Main questions: whether aggregation is needed, and if so how it helps consistency. Paper says it will give concrete examples in ranking, binary classification, and multiclass classification with linear estimators where estimators using only (X,Y) necessarily fail but label aggregation yields consistency. It will develop notions/theory for surrogate consistency with aggregation. In fully nonparametric scenarios, it will show how number of samples aggregated combines with noise conditions to improve consistency. It claims aggregation allows surrogate risk consistency under only weak conditions on the surrogate loss; losses using aggregated labels admit approximate linear comparison inequalities. It also claims that unlike conventional risk consistency theory requiring hypothesis class F of all measurable functions, aggregation can guarantee consistency over restricted hypothesis classes in classification problems, while consistency may fail without aggregation.

errors.claim: “For multiple independent comparisons Z=(Y_1,\ldots,Y_m) conditional on X, put m_{ij}=\sum_{y\in\mathcal Y^m}1\{y=(i,j)\}, …”
errors.location: this part, Section 3.1 ranking aggregation definition
errors.evidence: The same paragraph says the aggregation is for observed repeated comparisons “Z=(Y_1,\ldots,Y_m)” and then uses conditions such as “m_j=0 for some j” and ratios “m_{ij}/m_j” in A(Z).
errors.explanation: As written, m_{ij} sums over all possible tuples y∈Y^m and tests whether a tuple equals a single pair (i,j), so it is not an observed count from Z. This conflicts with the subsequent use of m_{ij},m_j as data-dependent counts for the observed repeated comparisons.

errors.claim: “\overline\psi_A(\epsilon)\coloneqq \inf_{s\in\mathbb R^d}\overline\psi_A(\epsilon,x).”
errors.evidence: Earlier in the same part, the analogous uniform calibration function is defined as “\overline\psi(\epsilon)\coloneqq \inf_{x\in\mathcal X}\psi(\epsilon,x).” Also \overline\psi_A(\epsilon,x) is already defined by an infimum over s: “\overline\psi_A(\epsilon,x)\coloneqq \inf_{s\in\mathbb R^d}\{...\}.”
errors.explanation: The displayed definition of \overline\psi_A(ε) takes an infimum over s of an expression that no longer contains s but still contains x. This conflicts with both the immediately preceding pointwise definition and the earlier uniform definition, which require an infimum over x.

errors.claim: “The crude bound … lower bounds the promised ξ_{m,k} by setting ξ_{m,k}:= …”
errors.evidence: Theorem 1 gives the comparison only when R(f)-R* is at least ξ=… and defines ξ_m as an infimum over M. Corollary 3.3 then says every f with R(f)-R*≥ξ_{m,k} satisfies the comparison.
errors.explanation: For Corollary 3.3 to follow from Theorem 1, ξ_{m,k} must be an upper bound on an admissible threshold/ξ_m, not a lower bound. If it were only a lower bound, R(f)-R*≥ξ_{m,k} would not imply the theorem’s required condition.

errors.claim: “Assume … condition (Nα), with α∈[0,1]” together with threshold exponent “1/(1−α)” and later “at α=1, … gives ξ_{m,k}=0”
errors.location: this part, Theorem 1 and following discussion
errors.evidence: Theorem 1 defines ξ using “(4 C_MT e_m(M))^{1/(1−α)}” and ξ_{m,k} also has exponents with denominators involving “1−α” or “1−α^2”. Later the text says “at α=1, m≥… gives ξ_{m,k}=0”.
errors.explanation: The displayed formulas are undefined at α=1 because they divide by zero, while the theorem explicitly allows α=1 and the subsequent paragraph assigns a finite zero threshold at α=1. The α=1 claim does not follow from the displayed ξ formulas as written.

errors.claim: “Low noise permits a comparison written as ψ(R(f)−R*)≤R_φ(f)−R*”
errors.evidence: Definition 3.2 immediately defines the comparison as “ψ(R(f)−R*)≤ R_{φ,A}(f)−R_{φ,A}*.” Earlier notes likewise record surrogate comparisons as using surrogate excess risk, e.g. “ψ(R(f)−R*)≤R_phi(f)−R_phi*.”
errors.explanation: The paragraph subtracts the task optimum R* from the surrogate risk R_φ(f), whereas the paper’s own definitions use surrogate excess risk R_{φ,A}(f)−R_{φ,A}*. This is an internal mismatch in the stated comparison.

errors.claim: “R(f)-R^\star\leq 16N\bigl(R_{\varphi,A_n}(f)-R_{\varphi,A_n}^\star\bigr).”
errors.evidence: The same display uses aggregation count “m” in the threshold, and earlier notes record Theorem 1/Cor. 3.3 as applying to “A_m” with aggregation count m: “If φ W3C, A_m J9P…” and “if R−R*≥ξ_{m,k}, same linear comparison.”

errors.claim: “every measurable f … satisfying [threshold without a leading 4] also satisfies …”
errors.location: this part, structured prediction consistency after Lemma 3.3
errors.evidence: Earlier notes record Cor. 3.3 for k≥3 as using a threshold with a leading factor 4: “otherwise 4*(32 C_MT^4/m log(4k(C1+C2)/C1))^{α/[2(1−α^2)]}.” The matching specialization in this same part also has “4·(32 C_MT^4/m log(...))^{...}.”

errors.claim: “R(f)-R^\star\leq \frac8{\min_{\hat y\neq y}\ell(\hat y,y)}\bigl(R_{\varphi,A_m}(f)-R_{\varphi,A_m}^\star\bigr).”

errors.claim: “As a corollary to Theorem 2 ... the aggregated approximate minimizers satisfy ... cos angle(theta_m, theta*) -> 1.”

errors.explanation: The theorem concerns convergence of the normalized matrix/vector \(T_m/\|T_m\|\) to \(T^*/\|T^*\|\). final_notes:
Paper title: “Some Robustness Properties of Label Cleaning” by Chen Cheng and John Duchi.

Framework: iid (X,Y). Scores f:X→R^d decoded by d; task risk R(f)=E ell(d∘f(X),Y). Aggregated surrogate R_{φ,A}(f)=E φ(f(X),A(Z)); repeated labels Z=(Y1,...,Ym) iid conditional on X. Majority/J9P aggregation chooses empirical task-risk minimizer.

Section 3 consistency: Q7D/calibration via conditional excesses. Uniform comparison: ψ(R−R*)≤ surrogate excess. Prop 1: convex φ:R^k×Y→R fails Q7D for ranking k≥3. Prop 2: squared loss to aggregated comparisons is Q7D for ranking when m≥k and aggregation counts comparisons, with star if denominator zero; possible formula issue: m_ij summed over y∈Y^m rather than observed comparisons. Prop 3: φ Q7D iff overlineψ_A(ε,x)>0; ψ_A=(overlineψ_A)** comparison; possible bad formula for uniform overlineψ_A.

W3C/J9P: finite label space card(Y)=k. J9P parameters a_y output empirical task-risk minimizer; empirical argmin eventually subset of population minimizers. W3C constants 0<C1≤C2 with parameters a_y and scores s_y decoded to y such that φ(s_y,a_y)+C1 ≤ inf_{d∘s≠y} φ(s,a_y), and φ(s_y,a_{y’})−C2 ≤ inf_s φ(s,a_{y’}). Hinge example (1,2).

Theorem 1: If φ W3C, A_m J9P, 0≤ell≤1, Nα α∈[0,1], then above threshold R−R* ≥ 2P(κ>M)+(4 C_MT e_m(M))^{1/(1−α)}, get R−R* ≤ 16/C1 · surrogate excess. ξ_m→0 for α<1; α=0 asymptotic consistency. Existing issues: formulas divide by 1−α though α=1 allowed; later α=1 says ξ=0. Cor 3.3: k=2 threshold exponent 1/[2(1−α)] log 8(C1+C2)/C1; k≥3 threshold should be 4*(32 C_MT^4/m log(4k(C1+C2)/C1))^{α/[2(1−α^2)]}; if R−R*≥ξ_{m,k}, slope 16/C1. Text says crude bound “lower bounds” ξ but corollary needs upper bound. U6A level-(ξ,ζ) consistency ψ(ε)≥ζε for ε≥ξ and ψ(R−R*)≤surrogate excess; prior paragraph wrote wrong target excess.

Noise/gaps: Δ(x)=min incorrect excess; binary Δ=|2η−1|. Nα: P(d∘f≠d∘f*)≤C_MT(R−R*)^α. Mβ: P(Δ≤ε)≤(C_MT ε)^β; equivalent β=α/(1−α). κ=max incorrect excess/min incorrect excess; binary κ=1 if P(Δ>0)=1. e_m(t)=t sqrt{(2/m)log(4k(C1+C2)/C1)}.

Examples: binary nonsmooth Lemma 3.1 margin φ convex, ∂φ(0)<0, lim∞φ=0; C1=φ(0)−φ(δ), C2=φ(−δ), k=2 threshold log 8(φ(−δ)+φ(0)−φ(δ))/(φ(0)−φ(δ)), slope 16/(φ(0)−φ(δ)); aggregation can make otherwise inconsistent φ consistent. Matching surrogate W3C C1=1/N,C2=2; threshold display 4*(32 C_MT^4/m log(4k(2N+1)))^{α/[2(1−α^2)]}; slope 16N; display uses A_n not A_m. Structured/A3J max-margin: Lemma W3C C1=min_{hat≠y}ell(hat,y), C2=max_y τ(y)+1; if v binary and ell=1/(2d)||vhat−v||_1 then τ=1,C2=2. Structured consistency display possible errors: missing leading 4, slope 8/min ell vs theorem 16/min ell, sloppy/free y.

Section 4 restricted classes. Prop 4: for any ε and nonzero θ*, some binary distribution satisfies K7M along θ*, yet every unaggregated surrogate minimizer has higher risk than θ* and angle cos ≤ε, any nonnegative loss. K7M: sign(f)=sign(P(Y=1|X)−1/2); θ* minimizes measurable risk. Cor 4.1 claims as corollary to Theorem 2 aggregated approximate minimizers θ_m have risk→R(fθ*) and cos angle→1; possible error: Theorem 2 only gives risk convergence, not direction.

Theorem 2: multiclass zero-one [k], argmax decoder, cone F with f^T1=0 closed under positive scaling, nonnegative Q7D φ with φ(s,y)→0 as y-margin→∞, response Y^m, aggregation T4K, unique population maximizer y*(x), K7M in F, P(Δ>0)=1: ε_m-argmin aggregated risk over F gives R(f_m)→R*. Logistic and pairwise convex nonincreasing examples satisfy limiting condition. Linear multiclass sum θ_i=0 is convex cone.

Section 4.3 finite-dimensional multiclass. Model: X∈R^d, Y∈[k], Θ d×(k−1), p_Θ via link σ plus kth residual; ordering consistency (14): t_y=max_i t_i iff σ_y(t)=max_i σ_i(t), t_k=0. Logistic link. T4K aggregated Y_i^+ distributed Cat(p_{Θ*,m}); p_{Θ,m} via ρ_m T4K distribution, ρ_m satisfies ordering consistency. Prop 5: k≥3, Σ=I, Z∼N(0,I_{k−1}), invertibility of M↦D M=E[Z(∇σ^lr(Θ*^T Z) M Z)^T]; for small ε bad set T_ε measure ≤ε with Θ_1(ε)/||Θ_1(ε)|| ≠ Θ*/||Θ*||. Theorem 3: If Θ*=U*T* with orthogonal U* and nonsingular T*, for each m exists T_m with Θ_m=U*T_m, ||T_m||→∞ and normalized T_m/||T_m||→T*/||T*||. Text: pair-based surrogate risks can be inconsistent even with K7M and near-correct linear model; T4K recovers optimal linear predictor asymptotically.

Fitted logistic loss (15) with θ_k=0; gradient given; minimizer Θ_m satisfies E[X(σ^lr(Θ_m^T X)−ρ_m(Θ*^T X))^T]=0. Binary Gaussian result: for m≥1,k=2, Θ_m=t_mΘ* even with misspecified link, so direction suffices. Defines σ^ε(t)=σ^lr(t) outside T_ε and uniform inside T_ε, but following prose reverses cases—internal contradiction. Also claim σ^ε satisfies ordering consistency/K7M conflicts with uniform-on-T definition and earlier ordering consistency unless T only tie points. Defines L_{m,ε}, Θ_m(ε); says Θ_1(0)=Θ* but small corruption destroys unaggregated consistency. General L_{m,σ}, Θ_m; claims robustness under misspecification when some link describes relationship, unaggregated multiclass generally inconsistent.

Section 5 numerical illustrations. D4X/truncated quadratic/squared hinge φ(δ)=max{1−δ,0}^2, unaggregated ψ(ε)=ε^2. With δ=1, α=0, C_MT=1, binary lemma yields ψ_m(ε)=1/16(ε−sqrt{32/m log 40})_+; m in Figure 1 {2^16,2^20,2^24,2^28,2^32}. Logistic misspecification experiment uses link \tildeσ(t)=σ^lr(t) for ||t||≤r and σ^lr(αt) for ||t||>r, d=2,k=3, θ1*=(0,1), θ2*=(1,1), r=3, α=.1, m={1,4,16,64,256,1024}, 100 trials, 95% error bars; two settings n=10000 fixed vs n=640000/m fixed total labels. Error in caption: plotted error written || ||T_m|| − T*/||T*|| ||, but should align with Theorem 3 normalized direction T_m/||T_m||→T*/||T*||.

Section 6 discussion: says many consistency results require m→∞; ranking has explicit finite-m guarantees; open theory depending jointly on (ell, φ, m). Notes κ large beyond binary even with low noise α≈1; binary κ=1. Mis-specified-model results require K7M/Bayes-optimal classifier in F; classical surrogate consistency can fail even there while aggregation succeeds. Suggests H-consistency/restricted-class aggregation comparisons as future work.

errors.claim: “Its minimizers frequently coincide with the original problem (2)”
errors.evidence: Equation (2) is the distribution-dependent criterion just introduced: “The distribution-dependent task criterion is … R(f) := … (2).” The instantaneous/original formulation is introduced later as equation (1): “The instantaneous formulation … R(f):= … (1).”
errors.explanation: The text says minimizers of equation (2) coincide with the original problem ‘(2),’ but equation (2) is the same criterion, not a separate original problem. Within this section, the intended comparison appears to be with the instantaneous formulation labeled equation (1), so the cross-reference is internally inconsistent.

errors.claim: “The regime is finite card(Y)=k<∞ and instantaneous task loss R(f)=E[ell(f(X),Y)]. The ranking construction belongs to this regime … card(Y)=k(k−1).”
errors.evidence: Earlier in this same part, the ranking risk is defined using the conditional/population aggregation matrix, not the observed pairwise label: “For each x, population aggregation transforms p_ij=P(Y=(i,j)|x) into an ordering” and “R(f) := P(f(X) and C_X 1 order differently).” The loss is also written as ell(s,C), depending on C, not on Y.
errors.explanation: The ranking construction described in §3.1 is distribution-dependent through C_X, whereas §3.2.2 claims it is an instantaneous task-loss problem of the form E[ell(f(X),Y)] over observed labels Y. These are not the same formulation.

errors.claim: “Assume … condition (Nα), with α∈[0,1]” and later formulas use exponents such as “1/(1−α)” and “1/[2(1−α)]”; later, “at α=1, … gives ξ_{m,k}=0”.
errors.evidence: Theorem 1 defines the threshold term as “(4 C_MT e_m(M))^{1/(1−α)}”; ξ_{m,k} for k=2 has exponent “1/(2(1−α))” and for k>2 has denominator “2(1−α^2)”. These are undefined at α=1, but the text explicitly includes α=1 and then claims a finite sample bound at α=1 gives ξ_{m,k}=0.
errors.explanation: The stated formulas do not make sense at α=1 because they divide by zero, yet the paper treats α=1 as included and derives a conclusion from the same comparison. A special α=1 case may be intended, but it is not what the displayed formulas state.

errors.claim: “Low noise permits a comparison written as ψ(R(f)−R*)≤R_φ(f)−R* …”
errors.evidence: Earlier in the same part and notes, comparison inequalities are between task excess and surrogate excess: Theorem 1 uses “R(f)−R*≤(16/Cφ,1)(R_{φ,A_m}(f)−R_{φ,A_m}*)”, and Definition 3.2 requires “ψ(R(f)−R*)≤R_{φ,A}(f)−R_{φ,A}*”. Earlier notes also record Cor. 3.1/Prop. 3 comparison as ψ(R−R*)≤R_φ−R_φ* or R_{φ,A}−R_{φ,A}*.
errors.explanation: The quoted sentence subtracts the task optimum R* from a surrogate risk R_φ(f), unlike the paper’s own definitions and the surrounding theorem/definition, which subtract the optimal surrogate risk. This is an internal mismatch in the comparison quantity.

errors.claim: “R(f)-R^\star\leq 16N\bigl(R_{\varphi,A_n}(f)-R_{\varphi,A_n}^\star\bigr).”
errors.evidence: The same displayed result is stated in terms of aggregation count m: “aggregation yields consistency once its count exceeds O(N\log N)” and the preceding threshold is “.../m...”. Earlier notation in the paper uses A_m for m repeated labels/aggregation, e.g. notes: “Cor 3.2: for m(n)→∞ ... R_{φ,A_m}” and “Theorem 1 ... R_{φ,A_m}(f)−R_{φ,A_m}*.”
errors.explanation: The conclusion switches from A_m to A_n although the result’s aggregation count and threshold are m; no n is defined for this bound. This conflicts with both the surrounding statement and the paper’s earlier aggregation notation.

errors.claim: “As a corollary to Theorem 2, if P satisfies K7M along θ⋆ and ε_m→0 … R(f_{θ_m})→R(f_{θ⋆}), cos angle(θ_m,θ⋆)→1.”
errors.evidence: Theorem 2 states: “Let a cone F satisfy K7M for P, and assume P(Δ(X)>0)=1. For ε_m… every sequence … satisfies R(f_m)→R⋆.”
errors.explanation: Corollary 4.1 is said to follow from Theorem 2 but omits Theorem 2’s explicit assumption P(Δ(X)>0)=1. It also attributes convergence of the parameter angle to Theorem 2, while Theorem 2 only concludes risk convergence R(f_m)→R⋆.

final_notes:
Paper title: “Some Robustness Properties of Label Cleaning” by Chen Cheng and John Duchi.

Core setup: label aggregation/cleaning improves robustness; surrogate minimization on cleaned labels gives stronger task-risk consistency than raw labels; finite-dimensional classifiers stay consistent under loss misspecification whereas standard uncertainty modeling can fail. Data iid (X,Y)~P. Scores f:X→R^d decoded by d. Task risk instantaneous or distribution-dependent. Aggregated surrogate risk R_{φ,A}(f)=E[φ(f(X),A(Z))]. Repeated labeling Z=(Y_1,…,Y_m), A_m/T4K=majority/argmin empirical task loss.

Detected internal errors: §3.2.2 called pairwise ranking finite instantaneous task loss with card(Y)=k(k−1), conflicting with §3.1 where ranking risk depends on conditional C_X. Theorem 1/Cor 3.3 formulas include α=1 despite division by zero and text says α=1 sample O(log k) gives ξ=0. Paragraph says ψ(R−R*)≤R_φ(f)−R* but formal comparisons use surrogate excess. In structured matching §3.3.3, opening uses A_n instead of A_m; opening bound has leading 4 and comparison 16N, while Lemma 3.3 general bound stated without leading 4 and comparison 8/min ell. §4 Cor 4.1 cites Theorem 2 for angle convergence though Theorem 2 only gives risk convergence and assumes P(Δ>0)=1. σ^ε formula/prose reversal and claims ordering consistency despite uniform-on-T_ε corruption. §5 Figure 2 says plotted error is || ||T_m|| − T*/||T*|| ||, conflicting with Theorem 3’s T_m/||T_m||→T*/||T*|| and ||T_m||→∞.

Section 3 reminders: Calibration ψ, Q7D; Prop 3 aggregation comparison ψ_A(R−R*)≤surrogate excess. W3C constants Cφ1,Cφ2 via scores s_y/a_y; binary hinge constants (1,2). Theorem 1 for zero-one finite labels under Nα gives threshold ξ_{m,k}; comparison factor 16/Cφ1. Level-(ξ,ζ) consistency. Nα: P(d∘f≠d∘f*)≤C_MT excess^α. Mβ low-noise. κ=max wrong δ/min wrong δ; binary κ=1 if P(Δ>0)=1. Binary nonsmooth margin surrogate W3C constants C1=ϕ(0)−ϕ(δ), C2=ϕ(−δ). Structured hinge/A3J generally inconsistent except low-noise; W3C with C1=min nonzero loss, C2=max τ+1; matching labels N!, loss normalized Hamming, C1=1/N,C2=2.

§4 Restricted/parametric F. Prop 4: for every ε>0 and nonzero θ*∈R^d, some P satisfies K7M along θ*, yet every unaggregated surrogate minimizer θ_φ of E[φ(fθ(X),Y)] has higher task risk than θ* and is essentially orthogonal: |cos angle(θ_φ,θ*)|≤ε, for any nonnegative loss φ. Binary setup: Y={±1}, zero-one ell(d(s),y)=1{ys≤0}, margin surrogate varphi(s,y)=φ(sy), X=R^d, F={x↦<θ,x>}. K7M/optimal predictability means sign(<θ*,x>)=sign(P(Y=1|x)−1/2), so fθ* is globally Bayes optimal.

Cor 4.1: if P satisfies K7M along θ* and ε_m→0, aggregated approximate minimizers θ_m of E[φ(A_m(Y_1,…,Y_m)fθ(X))] satisfy risk →R(fθ*) and cos angle→1, but cited Theorem 2 only proves risk convergence and also assumes P(Δ>0)=1.

Theorem 2: multiclass zero-one labels [k], argmax decoder, linear-cone conditions f^T1=0 and closure under positive scaling. Nonnegative surrogate varphi:R^k×[k]→R_+ is Q7D and tends to 0 when true score margin →∞. Response Z=Y^m, aggregation T4K, unique population maximizer y*(x). If cone F satisfies K7M and P(Δ(X)>0)=1, any ε_m-argmin over F of aggregated risk has task risk →R*. Examples: multiclass logistic; pairwise convex nonincreasing φ with φ'(0)<0, inf φ=0. Linear multiclass f_i=<θ_i,x>, Σθ_i=0 convex cone.

§4.3 finite-dimensional multiclass: Logistic loss with θ_k=0. Model: X=R^d,Y=[k], Θ=[θ_1…θ_{k−1}], Y|X=x~Cat(p_Θ(x)); p has σ(<θ_i,x>) and residual class k. Link σ satisfies 1^Tσ≤1 and ordering consistency. Logistic σ_i^lr=e^{t_i}/(1+Σe^{t_j}). Repeated labels iid; aggregated Y_i^+=A_m has distribution ρ_m/T4K. Proposition 5: k≥3, Σ=I, invertibility of M↦DM=E[Z(∇σ^lr(Θ*^T Z)MZ)^T]; then for small ε exists bad set T_ε of Lebesgue measure ≤ε with Θ_1(ε)/||Θ_1(ε)||≠Θ*/||Θ*||. Defines corrupted σ^ε as logistic outside T_ε and uniform inside. Theorem 3: if Θ*=U*T* with U* orthogonal d×(k−1), T* nonsingular, then for each m exists T_m, Θ_m=U*T_m, ||T_m||→∞ and T_m/||T_m||→T*/||T*||.

§5 numerical illustrations: D4X/truncated quadratic defined φ(δ)=max{1−δ,0}^2, exact unaggregated ψ(ε)=ε^2. With δ=1, α=0, C_MT=1: ψ_m(ε)=1/16(ε−sqrt((32/m)log40))_+. Figure 1 m={2^16,2^20,2^24,2^28,2^32}. Mis-specified logistic experiment uses link \tildeσ(t)=σ^lr(t) for ||t||≤r and σ^lr(αt) outside. Settings d=2,k=3, θ1*=(0,1), θ2*=(1,1), r=3, α=0.1, m={1,4,16,64,256,1024}, 100 trials, 95% bars. Experiment (i) n=10000 for each m; (ii) n=640000/m constant total labels.

§6 discussion: claims many consistency results require m→∞; ranking has explicit finite-m guarantees; open theory depending jointly on (ell,varphi,m), including higher-order item comparisons and powers C_x^p. Says beyond binary classification κ(X) can remain large even with low noise α≈1; binary κ=1. Mis-specified-model results require K7M/Bayes-optimal classifier in F; classical surrogate consistency can fail even there while aggregation succeeds. Future directions: restricted-class aggregation comparison/H-consistency; Mao et al. rate-optimal quadratic ψ growth for smooth convex loss.

final_notes:
Paper title: “Some Robustness Properties of Label Cleaning” by Chen Cheng and John Duchi.

Setup/results: Task risk R and surrogate R_phi; aggregated surrogate R_{phi,A}. Fisher iff pointwise psi>0; aggregated Fisher iff overline psi_A>0; comparison psi_A(R−R*)≤aggregated surrogate excess. Identifying surrogates: finite Y, Def.3.1 (C1,C2)-identifying with a_y,s_y and margins; binary hinge (1,2). Majority vote A_m. Cor.3.2: m(n)→∞ and identifying phi: small aggregated surrogate excess ⇒ task excess→0. Level-(xi,zeta) consistency defined using aggregated surrogate excess; earlier shorthand incorrectly used R_phi(f)−R*.

Noise: Delta=min conditional excess for wrong prediction; binary |2P(Y=1|X)−1|. Nα: P(d∘f≠d∘f*)≤C_MT(R−R*)^α. Mβ: P(Delta≤eps)≤(C_MT eps)^β. Paper claimed α=1/2 gives β=2, but equivalence β=α/(1−α) gives β=1. kappa=max incorrect delta/min incorrect delta; binary kappa=1 if P(Delta>0)=1. Final discussion says “trivially κ(X)=1” in binary, omitting/conflicting with this caveat. e_m(t)=t sqrt((2/m) log(4k(C1+C2)/C1)). Theorem 1: if R−R* ≥ 2P(kappa>M)+(4C_MT e_m(M))^{1/(1−α)}, then R−R*≤16/C1 aggregated surrogate excess. Formula undefined for α=1. Cor.3.3 thresholds: k=2: (32 C_MT^2/m log(8(C1+C2)/C1))^{1/[2(1−α)]}; k≥3: 4*(32 C_MT^4/m log(4k(C1+C2)/C1))^{α/[2(1−α²)]}. Text later says as α→1 less m needed and α=1 xi=0 if m large, conflicting with formulas unless separate.

Examples: binary margin convex phi identifying with C1=phi(0)−phi(delta)>0, C2=phi(−delta). Bipartite matching structured hinge identifying C1=1/N,C2=2; comparison should be 16N; text wrote A_n instead of A_m. General structured prediction Lemma 3.3 C1=min loss (notation issue), C2=max tau+1; if v binary/tau=1 then C2=2. Later application omitted leading 4 in k≥3 threshold and used comparison 8/min ell instead of 16/min ell.

Section 4 restricted classes. Binary Y={±1}, zero-one ell=1{ys≤0}, margin surrogate phi(sy). All-measurable Fisher/uniform iff phi'(0)<0. Linear fθ=<θ,x>. Optimally predictable along θ*: sign(<θ*,x>)=sign(P(Y=1|x)−1/2), so fθ* Bayes. Proposition 4: for any ε>0, nonzero θ*, any nonnegative φ, ∃P optimally predictable along θ* such that every surrogate minimizer θφ has R(fθφ)>R(fθ*) and |cos angle(θφ,θ*)|≤ε. Internal false for φ≡0: all θ minimizers incl. θ*, so strict risk inequality fails. Aggregation: majority vote A_m; θ_m ε_m-argmin E[φ(A_m(Ys)fθ(X))]. Cor.4.1: if optimally predictable and ε_m→0, R(fθm)→R(fθ*) and cos angle→1.

Multiclass restricted: Y=[k], F linear cone with f(x)^T1=0, closed under positive scaling. Zero-one argmax. φ nonnegative, Fisher consistent, limiting loss φ→0 when correct margin→∞. Examples multiclass logistic and sums of binary φ. Zhang Thm 8 consistency all measurable. Optimal predictability: ∃f∈F whose argmax is Bayes argmax. Theorem 2: cone optimally predicts P, unique Bayes label P(Δ>0)=1, ε_m→0 ⇒ ε_m-argmin of aggregated majority surrogate over F has R(f_m)→R*.

Introduction key claims:
- Modern supervised datasets often require cleaning/filtering/crowdsourcing multiple labels and denoising; paper investigates how data aggregation improves consistency of fitted models.
- Main thesis: label cleaning/aggregating labels provides robustness impossible without aggregation.
- Two faces of robustness:
  1. Improved consistency of estimation: when minimizing surrogate losses (e.g. multiclass logistic) instead of task losses (e.g. zero-one error), aggregated-label procedures can achieve consistent/optimal prediction in the limit when impossible without aggregation.
  2. Even in finite-dimensional statistical problems, aggregation can provide consistent classifiers when standard methods fail.
- Motivating questions: whether aggregation is needed for surrogate consistency, and if it helps, in what sense.
- Paper proposes concrete examples in ranking and binary/multiclass classification with linear estimators where estimators using only pairs (X,Y) necessarily fail but label aggregation yields consistency.
- Develops new notions/theory for surrogate consistency with data aggregation.
- In fully nonparametric scenarios, shows how number of aggregated samples combines with noise conditions to improve consistency.
- Claims aggregation permits surrogate risk consistency under only weak conditions on the surrogate loss; losses using aggregated labels admit approximate linear comparison inequalities.

Background mentioned:
- Surrogate risk consistency literature: Bartlett/Jordan/McAuliffe characterized binary convex surrogate consistency for zero-one error; further work in multilabel, ranking, structured prediction, ordinal regression, restricted classes, general theory.

Section 2 Preliminaries:
- Classical setup: data (Xi,Yi) iid P on X×Y. Learn scoring f:X→R^d, decoder d:R^d→Y, prediction d∘f(x).
- Task risk equation (1): R(f)=E_P[ ell(d∘f(X),Y) ]. Binary example: d=1, decoder sgn(s), ell(y,y’)=1{yy’≤0}, so R(f)=P(Y f(X)≤0).
- They introduce a more sophisticated task risk depending on conditional law P(Y∈·|X): equation (2) R(f)=E_P[ ell(d∘f(X), P(·|X)) ]. In multiclass, ell(yhat,P)=∑_y P(Y=y)1{yhat≠y}, coinciding with standard 0-1 error. Note: text incorrectly says minimizers coincide with original problem (2), but original risk is (1).
- Surrogate loss φ:R^d×Y→R; surrogate risk R_φ(f)=E_P[φ(f(X),Y)]. Need consistency with task problem (2).
- Paper studies two scenarios: (i) classical Fisher consistency where F contains all Borel functions; (ii) statistical scenarios with parametric possibly misspecified F. Main message: label aggregation improves consistency in both.

Section 2.1 Label aggregation:
- Instead of output Y, observe abstract Z∈Z. Example: multiple noisy labels for each X, Z=(Y1,…,Ym)∈Y^m.
- Aggregation space A; aggregating function A:Z→A, e.g. majority vote. Surrogate φ:R^d×A→R_+. Aggregated surrogate risk equation (3): R_{φ,A}(f)=E[φ(f(X),A(Z))]. Question: when minimizing (3) suffices to minimize task risk (2).
- Example 1 Majority vote/repeated sampling: Z=(Y1,…,Ym), Yi|X=x iid P_{Y|X=x}. Define A(Z)=argmin_{y∈Y}∑_{l=1}^m ell(y,Y_l). For 0-1 loss ell(yhat,y)=1{y≠yhat}, this is majority vote; general form allows abstract procedures.
- Example 2 K-nearest neighbors: abstract repeated sampling with example X and label Y plus additional iid sample (Xi,Yi)_{i=1}^m~P; Z=(Y,(Xi,Yi)_{i=1}^m). Distance metric on X; order Xi by distance to X, set X_(0)=X. For K≥0 aggregate K-nearest neighbors plus original by A_{m,K}(Z)=argmin_{y∈Y}∑_{l=0}^K ell(y,Y_(l)). Appendix C will extend to aggregation from a single sample.

Consistency notions for all P: (i) Fisher consistency: R_phi(f_n)→R_phi* implies R(f_n)→R*. (ii) Uniform comparison: nondecreasing psi with psi(eps)>0 for eps>0 and psi(R(f)-R*)≤R_phi(f)-R_phi*. Paper title: “Some Robustness Properties of Label Cleaning” by Chen Cheng and John Duchi.

Framework: iid (X,Y). Scores f:X→R^d decoded by d; task risk R(f)=E ell(d∘f(X),Y) or distribution-dependent risk. Binary sign/0-1. Aggregated surrogate risk R_{phi,A}(f)=E phi(f(X),A(Z)); repeated labels Z=(Y1,...,Ym) iid conditional on X; A_m=argmin_y sum_l ell(y,Y_l), majority vote/T4K for 0-1.

Section 3 consistency: Standard surrogate consistency over all Borel f; comparison inequality ψ(R−R*)≤R_phi−R_phi* stronger but coincides with consistency for convex binary margin losses. Conditional calibration ψ(ε,x)=inf_s{δ_phi:δ_l≥ε}; Q7D iff positive pointwise calibration. For ranking k≥3 every convex φ:R^k×Y→R fails Q7D. Prop 2 squared ranking surrogate Q7D with aggregation m≥k; possible formula error in m_ij. Prop 3 aggregation extension possible typo in uniform overlineψ_A.

W3C/J9P: Cor 3.2 says for m(n)→∞ and W3C φ, surrogate excess for A_m going to 0 implies task excess to 0. J9P generalized majority vote: parameters a_y; A_m outputs parameter of empirical-risk-minimizing label; eventual empirical argmin subset of population minimizers. W3C constants C1,C2 via (6a)(6b); binary hinge W3C (1,2).

Theorem 1: If φ W3C, A_m J9P, 0≤ell≤1, Nα, α∈[0,1], then for f with R−R* ≥ 2P(κ>M)+(4 C_MT e_m(M))^{1/(1−α)}, get R−R* ≤ 16/C1 · surrogate excess. ξ_m=inf_M{...}→0. Internal issues: formulas divide by 1−α although α=1 included; later α=1 separately claimed ξ=0. Text says explicit ξ_{m,k} “lower bounds” promised ξ, but corollary needs upper bound. Explicit ξ_{m,k}: k=2, [(32 C_MT²/m) log(8(C1+C2)/C1)]^{1/[2(1−α)]}; otherwise 4[(32 C_MT⁴/m) log(4k(C1+C2)/C1)]^{α/[2(1−α²)]}. Cor 3.3 if R−R*≥ξ_{m,k}, same comparison. At α=1 claims m≥32 max{C_MT²,C_MT⁴} log(4k(C1+C2)/C1)=O(log k) gives ξ=0 and linear R2V.

Noise/gaps: Δ(x)=min_{d(s)∉y*(x)} δ_l(s,x), binary |2P(Y=1|X=x)−1|. Nα: P(d∘f≠d∘f*)≤C_MT(R(f)−R*)^α. Mβ: P(Δ≤ε)≤(C_MT ε)^β. Text inconsistency: says α=1/2 gives β=2 but equivalence β=α/(1−α) gives β=1. κ=max incorrect δ_l/min incorrect δ_l; binary κ=1 if P(Δ>0)=1. e_m(t)=t sqrt[(2/m) log(4k(C1+C2)/C1)].

Examples: Lemma 3.1 binary nonsmooth margin surrogate W3C with C1=ϕ(0)−ϕ(δ), C2=ϕ(−δ). Lemma 3.2 bipartite matching W3C C1=1/N, C2=2; threshold uses 4[(32 C_MT^4/m) log(4k(2N+1))]^{α/[2(1−α²)]}; conclusion printed A_n not A_m—internal inconsistency. Lemma 3.3 structured hinge W3C C1=min_{\hat y≠y} ell(\hat y,y), C2=max_y τ(y)+1; comparison threshold omitted factor 4 relative to corollary/Lemma 3.2; slope printed 8/min loss though Theorem 1 gives 16/C1.

Section 4 restricted/parametric F. Prop 4: for every ε>0 and nonzero θ*, some P satisfies K7M along θ*, but every unaggregated surrogate minimizer θ_φ has R(f_θφ)>R(f_θ*) and |cos angle(θφ,θ*)|≤ε. Cor 4.1 claims as corollary to Theorem 2: if P satisfies K7M along θ* and ε_m→0, then R(f_θm)→R(f_θ*) and cos angle(θ_m,θ*)→1; internal issue: Theorem 2 only states risk convergence, not angle convergence.

Theorem 2: cone F satisfies K7M, P(Δ>0)=1, ε_m→0; every ε_m-argmin of aggregated surrogate risk over F has R(f_m)→R*. Multiclass zero-one, decoder argmax, centered cone; nonnegative Q7D surrogate with limit φ(s,y)→0 as correct margin→∞. Unique population maximizer y*(x). K7M: argmax f_y(x) in argmax P(Y=y|X=x). Logistic and pairwise convex examples.

Section 4.3: Prop 5 k≥3, Gaussian cov I, invertibility condition; small corruption set T_ε can make unaggregated Θ_1 direction differ from Θ*. Theorem 3: If Θ*=U*T* with U* orthogonal and T* nonsingular, for each m exists T_m with Θ_m=U*T_m, ||T_m||→∞ and T_m/||T_m||→T*/||T*||. Earlier link definition contradiction: σ^ε logistic outside Tε and uniform inside, then text said samples logistic inside Tε and uniform otherwise.

Section 5 numerics: D4X/squared hinge φ(δ)=max{1−δ,0}², unaggregated ψ(ε)=ε². With δ=1, α=0, C_MT=1, aggregated lower curve ψ_m(ε)=1/16(ε−sqrt((32/m)log40))_+. Fig.1 uses m=2^16,...,2^32. Mis-specified logistic simulation link \tildeσ(t)=σlr(t) for ||t||≤r and σlr(αt) for ||t||>r; d=2,k=3, θ1*=(0,1), θ2*=(1,1), r=3, α=0.1, m={1,4,16,64,256,1024}, 100 trials. Two regimes: n=10000 fixed; or n=640000/m fixed total labels. Internal error: Fig.2 says classification-rule error is || ||T_m|| − T*/||T*|| ||, conflicting with Theorem 3’s direction convergence T_m/||T_m||→T*/||T*||.

Section 6 discussion: claims collection debate: unaggregated labels more efficient if models represent all uncertainty, cleaning more robust otherwise; current results show limitations of uncleaned labels and robustness gains. Says many consistency results require m→∞; ranking has explicit finite-m guarantees; joint theory in (ell,φ,m) open, including higher-order item comparisons/powers C_x^p. Says beyond binary κ may remain large even with low Nα/noise α≈1; claims binary κ=1 unconditionally, conflicting with earlier caveat P(Δ>0)=1. Mis-specified-model discussion: results require K7M/Bayes-optimal classifier in F; classical surrogate consistency can fail even there while aggregation succeeds. Restricted-class comparison: H-consistency may extend aggregation comparisons; Mao et al. rate-optimal quadratic ψ growth for smooth convex loss; aggregation-based H-consistency upgrades remain open.

final_notes:
Paper title: “Some Robustness Properties of Label Cleaning” by Chen Cheng and John Duchi.

Main setup: task risk R(f)=E ell(d∘f(X),Y) or E ell(d∘f(X),P(.|X)); surrogate risk R_phi(f)=E phi(f(X),Y). Aggregation observes Z and A:Z→A, aggregated surrogate risk R_{phi,A}=E phi(f(X),A(Z)).

Sec.3 consistency: F all Borel. Fisher consistency iff pointwise calibration psi>0. Prop.3 aggregation: phi Fisher consistent iff aggregated calibration positive; comparison psi_A(R(f)-R*)≤R_{phi,A}(f)-R_{phi,A}*. Ranking: convex score surrogates inconsistent for k≥3 without aggregation; repeated comparisons aggregated to wins vector make squared loss Fisher consistent if m≥k. Identifying surrogates: Def.3.1 (C_phi,1,C_phi,2)-identifying via margins; binary hinge (1,2). Generalized majority vote A_m. Cor.3.2: m(n)→∞ and identifying => aggregated surrogate excess→0 implies task excess→0. Level-(xi,zeta) consistency has comparison to aggregated surrogate excess; earlier formula typo used R_phi(f)-R*. Noise: Delta=min excess conditional risk for wrong prediction; binary Delta=|2P(Y=1|X)-1|. Mammen-Tsybakov Nα/Mβ equivalence claimed via β=α/(1−α) (α=1 issue). Condition number kappa; e_m(t)=t sqrt((2/m)log(4k(C1+C2)/C1)). Theorem 1: if R−R* ≥ 2P(kappa>M)+(4 C_MT e_m(M))^{1/(1−α)}, then R−R*≤(16/C1) aggregated surrogate excess; xi_m is inf threshold, xi_m→0. Cor.3.3 thresholds: binary (32 C_MT²/m log(8(C1+C2)/C1))^{1/[2(1−α)]}; k≥3: 4*(32 C_MT^4/m log(4k(C1+C2)/C1))^{α/[2(1−α²)]}. Text later says α=1 with m large gives xi=0 though formulas undefined.

Examples: binary nonsmooth margin: Lemma 3.1 feasible C1=phi(0)-phi(delta), C2=phi(-delta); comparison 16/C1. Bipartite matching: k=N!, normalized Hamming; structured hinge C1=1/N,C2=2; threshold includes 4*(32 C_MT^4/m log(4k(2N+1)))^{α/[2(1−α²)]}; comparison should be 16N times aggregated excess, but text wrote A_n. General structured: Lemma 3.3 structured hinge C1=min loss, C2=max tau+1; if binary embeddings and normalized Hamming, tau=1,C2=2. Final specialization omitted leading 4 and used 8/C1 instead of 16/C1.

Sec.4 restricted classes. 4.1 binary: zero-one ell=1{ys≤0}, margin varphi(s,y)=phi(sy), phi convex. All-measurable Fisher iff phi'(0)<0. Linear F. Optimally predictable along theta*: sign matches Bayes sign. Prop.4: for any eps and nonzero theta*, ∃P optimally predictable along theta* such that all surrogate minimizers have larger task risk than theta* and |cos angle|≤eps. Aggregation A_m majority: epsilon_m-argmin E[phi(A_m(Ys) f_theta(X))] yields R→R* and cos(theta_m,theta*)→1.

4.2 multiclass: Y=[k], zero-one, decoder argmax. F linear cone centered and closed under positive scaling. Surrogate varphi Fisher consistent and limiting loss condition (13): varphi(s,y)→0 if correct margin→∞. Logistic and pairwise margin examples. Theorem 2: if F cone optimally predicts P, P(Delta>0)=1, majority vote A_m, epsilon_m→0, then any epsilon_m-argmin aggregated surrogate has R(f_m)→R*.

4.3 finite-dimensional multiclass: X=R^d,Y=[k], linear Θ=[θ1…θ_{k−1}], θ_k=0. True categorical p_Θ from link σ satisfying (14): t_y=max iff σ_y(t)=max. Logistic link example. Majority vote distribution p_{Θ,m} via ρ_m; text says ρ_m satisfies (14). Logistic loss (15); population minimizer solves E[X(σ_lr(Θ_m^T X)−ρ_m(Θ*^T X))^T]=0. Claims k=2 Gaussian and misspecified link gives Θ_m=t_mΘ*, classification consistent. For k≥3 slight misspecification causes failure. σ^ε prose reversed formula; claim σ^ε clearly satisfies (14) false on uniform region unless ties. Prop.5: for k≥3, Σ=I, invertible D map, ∃ small ε and T_ε measure≤ε with Θ_1(ε)/||Θ_1(ε)|| ≠ Θ*/||Θ*||. Theorem3: if Θ*=U*T* with U* orthogonal and T* nonsingular, then ∃T_m with Θ_m=U*T_m, ||T_m||→∞ and T_m/||T_m||→T*/||T*||.

Sec.5 numerical illustrations. Truncated quadratic binary phi(δ)=max{1−δ,0}²; non-aggregated calibration ψ(ε)=ε². For majority vote m, Lemma 3.1 with δ=1 gives C1=1,C2=4 and ψ_m(ε)=1/16(ε−sqrt((32/m)log40))_+. Part incorrectly states threshold 1/4 requires m≥128 log40; displayed formula implies m≥512 log40. Fig.1 uses m∈{2^16,2^20,2^24,2^28,2^32}; claims aggregated curve transitions quadratic to linear and ψ_m conservative. Second experiment: logistic regression Sec.4.3, k=3,d=2, corrupted link tildeσ(t)=σ_lr(t)1{||t||≤r}+σ_lr(αt)1{||t||>r}, with θ1*=(0,1), θ2*=(1,1), r=3, α=0.1. Fig.2 m∈{1,4,16,64,256,1024}; left n=10000 for each m; right n=640000/m; 95% error bars over T=100 trials. Caption’s written error metric appears malformed: || ||T_m|| − T*/||T*|| ||, whereas theorem predicts T_m/||T_m||→T*/||T*||.

Sec.6 discussion: situates work in debate on using noisy/all labels vs cleaned labels; says non-aggregated data may be statistically efficient when models fully represent uncertainty, but cleaning more robust otherwise. Future directions: finite-m consistency/results beyond asymptotic m→∞; ranking has explicit finite-m guarantees, asks about higher-order comparisons. Noise condition number kappa important for multiclass; binary trivially kappa=1; low MT noise α≈1 may still have large kappa. Mis-specified models discussion says Sec.4.3 and related results require optimal predictability/Bayes classifier in F; wants beyond restricted scenarios. Also proposes restricted-class comparison inequalities with aggregation, connecting to H-consistency and rate-optimal quadratic ψ for smooth convex losses.

Paper title: “Some Robustness Properties of Label Cleaning” by Chen Cheng and John Duchi.

Abstract claims:
- Learning procedures relying on aggregated/cleaned labels (label information distilled from noisy responses) have robustness properties impossible without data cleaning.
- In risk consistency setting (minimizing surrogate losses instead of task loss such as 0-1 misclassification), procedures using label aggregation get stronger consistency guarantees than possible using raw labels.
- Classical perfectly specified statistical models suggest using all information/modeling label uncertainty is statistically efficient.
- However, consistency fails for “standard” approaches when the minimized loss is even slightly misspecified.
- Procedures leveraging aggregated information still converge to optimal classifiers, showing robustness from considering the full pipeline: data collection → model fitting → prediction, refining noisy signals.

Paper title: “Some Robustness Properties of Label Cleaning” by Chen Cheng and John Duchi.

Abstract claims:
- Learning procedures relying on aggregated/cleaned labels (label information distilled from noisy responses) have robustness properties impossible without data cleaning.
- In risk consistency setting (minimizing surrogate losses instead of task loss such as 0-1 misclassification), procedures using label aggregation get stronger consistency guarantees than possible using raw labels.
- Classical perfectly specified statistical models suggest using all information/modeling label uncertainty is statistically efficient.
- However, consistency fails for “standard” approaches when the minimized loss is even slightly misspecified.
- Procedures leveraging aggregated information still converge to optimal classifiers, showing robustness from considering the full pipeline: data collection → model fitting → prediction, refining noisy signals.

Introduction key claims:
- Modern supervised datasets often require cleaning/filtering/crowdsourcing multiple labels and denoising; paper investigates how data aggregation improves consistency of fitted models.
- Main thesis: label cleaning/aggregating labels provides robustness impossible without aggregation.
- Two faces of robustness:
  1. Improved consistency of estimation: when minimizing surrogate losses (e.g. multiclass logistic) instead of task losses (e.g. zero-one error), aggregated-label procedures can achieve consistent/optimal prediction in the limit when impossible without aggregation.
  2. Even in finite-dimensional statistical problems, aggregation can provide consistent classifiers when standard methods fail.
- Motivating questions: whether aggregation is needed for surrogate consistency, and if it helps, in what sense.
- Paper proposes concrete examples in ranking and binary/multiclass classification with linear estimators where estimators using only pairs (X,Y) necessarily fail but label aggregation yields consistency.
- Develops new notions/theory for surrogate consistency with data aggregation.
- In fully nonparametric scenarios, shows how number of aggregated samples combines with noise conditions to improve consistency.
- Claims aggregation permits surrogate risk consistency under only weak conditions on the surrogate loss; losses using aggregated labels admit approximate linear comparison inequalities.
- Unlike conventional risk consistency theory requiring hypothesis class F of all measurable functions, paper will show classification results where aggregating labels guarantees consistency even over restricted hypothesis classes, which may fail without aggregation.

Background mentioned:
- Surrogate risk consistency literature: Bartlett/Jordan/McAuliffe characterized binary convex surrogate consistency for zero-one error; further work in multilabel, ranking, structured prediction, ordinal regression, restricted classes, general theory.
- Existing analyses typically assume standard supervised pairs (X,Y) and do not address aggregation machinery.

errors.claim: “For multiple independent comparisons Z=(Y_1,\ldots,Y_m) conditional on X, put m_{ij}=\sum_{y\in\mathcal Y^m}1\{y=(i,j)\}, …”
errors.location: this part, Section 3.1 ranking aggregation definition
errors.evidence: The same paragraph says the aggregation is for observed repeated comparisons “Z=(Y_1,\ldots,Y_m)” and then uses conditions such as “m_j=0 for some j” and ratios “m_{ij}/m_j” in A(Z).
errors.explanation: As written, m_{ij} sums over all possible tuples y∈Y^m and tests whether a tuple equals a single pair (i,j), so it is not an observed count from Z. This conflicts with the subsequent use of m_{ij},m_j as data-dependent counts for the observed repeated comparisons.

errors.claim: “\overline\psi_A(\epsilon)\coloneqq \inf_{s\in\mathbb R^d}\overline\psi_A(\epsilon,x).”
errors.evidence: Earlier in the same part, the analogous uniform calibration function is defined as “\overline\psi(\epsilon)\coloneqq \inf_{x\in\mathcal X}\psi(\epsilon,x).” Also \overline\psi_A(\epsilon,x) is already defined by an infimum over s: “\overline\psi_A(\epsilon,x)\coloneqq \inf_{s\in\mathbb R^d}\{...\}.”
errors.explanation: The displayed definition of \overline\psi_A(ε) takes an infimum over s of an expression that no longer contains s but still contains x. This conflicts with both the immediately preceding pointwise definition and the earlier uniform definition, which require an infimum over x.

errors.claim: “The crude bound … lower bounds the promised ξ_{m,k} by setting ξ_{m,k}:= …”
errors.evidence: Theorem 1 gives the comparison only when R(f)-R* is at least ξ=… and defines ξ_m as an infimum over M. Corollary 3.3 then says every f with R(f)-R*≥ξ_{m,k} satisfies the comparison.
errors.explanation: For Corollary 3.3 to follow from Theorem 1, ξ_{m,k} must be an upper bound on an admissible threshold/ξ_m, not a lower bound. If it were only a lower bound, R(f)-R*≥ξ_{m,k} would not imply the theorem’s required condition.

errors.explanation: The displayed formulas are undefined at α=1 because they divide by zero, while the theorem explicitly allows α=1 and the subsequent paragraph assigns a finite zero threshold at α=1. The α=1 claim does not follow from the displayed ξ formulas as written.

errors.claim: “Low noise permits a comparison written as ψ(R(f)−R*)≤R_φ(f)−R*”

errors.claim: “R(f)-R^\star\leq 16N\bigl(R_{\varphi,A_n}(f)-R_{\varphi,A_n}^\star\bigr).”

Paper title: “Some Robustness Properties of Label Cleaning” by Chen Cheng and John Duchi.

Framework: iid (X,Y). Scores f:X→R^d decoded by d; task risk R(f)=E ell(d∘f(X),Y). Aggregated surrogate R_{φ,A}(f)=E φ(f(X),A(Z)); repeated labels Z=(Y1,...,Ym) iid conditional on X. Majority/J9P aggregation chooses empirical task-risk minimizer.

Section 3 consistency: Q7D/calibration via conditional excesses. Uniform comparison: ψ(R−R*)≤ surrogate excess. Prop 1: convex φ:R^k×Y→R fails Q7D for ranking k≥3. Prop 2: squared loss to aggregated comparisons is Q7D for ranking when m≥k and aggregation counts comparisons, with star if denominator zero; possible formula issue: m_ij summed over y∈Y^m rather than observed comparisons. Prop 3: φ Q7D iff overlineψ_A(ε,x)>0; ψ_A=(overlineψ_A)** comparison; possible bad formula for uniform overlineψ_A.

W3C/J9P: finite label space card(Y)=k. J9P parameters a_y output empirical task-risk minimizer; empirical argmin eventually subset of population minimizers. W3C constants 0<C1≤C2 with parameters a_y and scores s_y decoded to y such that φ(s_y,a_y)+C1 ≤ inf_{d∘s≠y} φ(s,a_y), and φ(s_y,a_{y’})−C2 ≤ inf_s φ(s,a_{y’}). Hinge example (1,2).

Theorem 1: If φ W3C, A_m J9P, 0≤ell≤1, Nα α∈[0,1], then above threshold R−R* ≥ 2P(κ>M)+(4 C_MT e_m(M))^{1/(1−α)}, get R−R* ≤ 16/C1 · surrogate excess. ξ_m→0 for α<1; α=0 asymptotic consistency. Existing issues: formulas divide by 1−α though α=1 allowed; later α=1 says ξ=0. Cor 3.3: k=2 threshold exponent 1/[2(1−α)] log 8(C1+C2)/C1; k≥3 threshold should be 4*(32 C_MT^4/m log(4k(C1+C2)/C1))^{α/[2(1−α^2)]}; if R−R*≥ξ_{m,k}, slope 16/C1. Text says crude bound “lower bounds” ξ but corollary needs upper bound. U6A level-(ξ,ζ) consistency ψ(ε)≥ζε for ε≥ξ and ψ(R−R*)≤surrogate excess; prior paragraph wrote wrong target excess.

Noise/gaps: Δ(x)=min incorrect excess; binary Δ=|2η−1|. Nα: P(d∘f≠d∘f*)≤C_MT(R−R*)^α. Mβ: P(Δ≤ε)≤(C_MT ε)^β; equivalent β=α/(1−α). κ=max incorrect excess/min incorrect excess; binary κ=1 if P(Δ>0)=1. e_m(t)=t sqrt{(2/m)log(4k(C1+C2)/C1)}.

Examples: binary nonsmooth Lemma 3.1 margin φ convex, ∂φ(0)<0, lim∞φ=0; C1=φ(0)−φ(δ), C2=φ(−δ), k=2 threshold log 8(φ(−δ)+φ(0)−φ(δ))/(φ(0)−φ(δ)), slope 16/(φ(0)−φ(δ)); aggregation can make otherwise inconsistent φ consistent. Matching surrogate W3C C1=1/N,C2=2; threshold display 4*(32 C_MT^4/m log(4k(2N+1)))^{α/[2(1−α^2)]}; slope 16N; display uses A_n not A_m. Structured/A3J max-margin: Lemma W3C C1=min_{hat≠y}ell(hat,y), C2=max_y τ(y)+1; if v binary and ell=1/(2d)||vhat−v||_1 then τ=1,C2=2. Structured consistency display possible errors: missing leading 4, slope 8/min ell vs theorem 16/min ell, sloppy/free y.

Section 4 restricted classes. Prop 4: for any ε and nonzero θ*, some binary distribution satisfies K7M along θ*, yet every unaggregated surrogate minimizer has higher risk than θ* and angle cos ≤ε, any nonnegative loss. K7M: sign(f)=sign(P(Y=1|X)−1/2); θ* minimizes measurable risk. Cor 4.1 claims as corollary to Theorem 2 aggregated approximate minimizers θ_m have risk→R(fθ*) and cos angle→1; possible error: Theorem 2 only gives risk convergence, not direction.

Theorem 2: multiclass zero-one [k], argmax decoder, cone F with f^T1=0 closed under positive scaling, nonnegative Q7D φ with φ(s,y)→0 as y-margin→∞, response Y^m, aggregation T4K, unique population maximizer y*(x), K7M in F, P(Δ>0)=1: ε_m-argmin aggregated risk over F gives R(f_m)→R*. Logistic and pairwise convex nonincreasing examples satisfy limiting condition. Linear multiclass sum θ_i=0 is convex cone.

Section 4.3 finite-dimensional multiclass. Model: X∈R^d, Y∈[k], Θ d×(k−1), p_Θ via link σ plus kth residual; ordering consistency (14): t_y=max_i t_i iff σ_y(t)=max_i σ_i(t), t_k=0. Logistic link. T4K aggregated Y_i^+ distributed Cat(p_{Θ*,m}); p_{Θ,m} via ρ_m T4K distribution, ρ_m satisfies ordering consistency. Prop 5: k≥3, Σ=I, Z∼N(0,I_{k−1}), invertibility of M↦D M=E[Z(∇σ^lr(Θ*^T Z) M Z)^T]; for small ε bad set T_ε measure ≤ε with Θ_1(ε)/||Θ_1(ε)|| ≠ Θ*/||Θ*||. Theorem 3: If Θ*=U*T* with orthogonal U* and nonsingular T*, for each m exists T_m with Θ_m=U*T_m, ||T_m||→∞ and normalized T_m→T*/||T*||. Text: pair-based surrogate risks can be inconsistent even with K7M and near-correct linear model; T4K recovers optimal linear predictor asymptotically.

Fitted logistic loss (15) with θ_k=0; gradient; minimizer Θ_m satisfies E[X(σ^lr(Θ_m^T X)−ρ_m(Θ*^T X))^T]=0. Binary Gaussian result: for m≥1,k=2, Θ_m=t_mΘ* even with misspecified link, so direction suffices. Defines σ^ε(t)=σ^lr(t) outside T_ε and uniform inside T_ε, but following prose reverses cases—internal contradiction. Also claim σ^ε satisfies ordering consistency/K7M conflicts with uniform-on-T definition and earlier ordering consistency unless T only tie points. Defines L_{m,ε}, Θ_m(ε); says Θ_1(0)=Θ* but small corruption destroys unaggregated consistency. General L_{m,σ}, Θ_m; claims robustness under misspecification when some link describes relationship, unaggregated multiclass generally inconsistent.

Section 5 numerical illustrations. D4X/squared hinge φ(δ)=max{1−δ,0}^2; unaggregated ψ(ε)=ε^2. For δ=1, φ(0)=1, φ(1)=0, φ(−1)=4, so displayed aggregated curve ψ_m(ε)=1/16(ε−sqrt(32/m log40))_+. Part incorrectly says m≥128 log40 gives threshold 1/4; actual threshold then 1/2, and 1/4 needs 512 log40. Figure 1 uses m∈{2^16,2^20,2^24,2^28,2^32}. Mis-specified logistic numerical link: σ~(t)=σ^lr(t) for ||t||≤r, σ^lr(αt) for ||t||>r, with d=2,k=3, θ1*=(0,1), θ2*=(1,1), r=3, α=.1, m∈{1,4,16,64,256,1024}, 100 trials. Two sampling regimes n=10000 fixed or n=640000/m fixed total labels. Figure 2 says plotted error is || ||T_m||−T*/||T*|| ||, conflicting with Theorem 3’s normalized T_m/||T_m||→T*/||T*|| and dimensionally wrong.

Section 6 discussion: claims consistency often needs m→∞; ranking has explicit finite-m guarantees; future theory should depend jointly on task loss ell, surrogate φ, and count m. Notes binary κ=1, while beyond binary κ may be large even under low noise/α≈1. Mis-specified-model discussion says results require K7M/Bayes-optimal classifier in F; unaggregated surrogate consistency can fail even there while aggregation succeeds. Mentions H-consistency as future direction for restricted-class aggregation comparisons.

Section 2 preliminaries:
- Two regimes: unrestricted Borel F with classical Fisher consistency; and parametric/potentially misspecified F, with aggregation improving consistency in each.
- Data: iid (Xi,Yi) ~ P on X x Y. Scores f:X→R^d decoded by d:R^d→Y; prediction yhat=d∘f(x).
- Distribution-dependent task criterion defined as R(f)=E_P[ ell(d∘f(X), P(.|X)) ] (eq. 2). For multiclass Y={1,...,k}, ell(yhat,P)=sum_y P(Y=y)1{yhat≠y}, giving standard zero-one error.
- Instantaneous task formulation for ell:YxY→R_+: R(f)=E_P[ell(d∘f(X),Y)] (eq. 1). Binary classification: d=1, decoder sgn, ell(y,y’)=1{yy’≤0}, R(f)=P(Y f(X)≤0). Task losses can be nonsmooth/nonconvex/flat; use surrogate phi:R^d x Y→R, R_phi(f)=E phi(f(X),Y), requiring consistency with task criterion.

Section 2.1 label aggregation:
- Aggregated surrogate risk: R_{phi,A}(f)=E[phi(f(X), A(Z))] (eq. 3), assessed against actual task-risk minimization. Z in Z, aggregation space A, map A:Z→A, nonnegative surrogate phi:R^d x A→R_+.
- Repeated labeling: Z=(Y1,...,Ym) in Y^m with Yi|X=x iid P_{Y|X=x}. Aggregator A_m(Z)=argmin_{y in Y} sum_{l=1}^m ell(y,Y_l). For 0-1 loss this is majority vote; general ell allows other procedures.
- Rough KNN construction: X has Y and additional independent draws (Xi,Yi)_{i=1}^m iid P; Z=(Y,(Xi,Yi)_{i=1}^m). Order neighbors by distance to X with X_(0)=X; A_{m,K}(Z)=argmin_y sum_{l=0}^K ell(y,Y_(l)), K≥0. Population-level repeated-sampling treatment also extends to aggregation from one sample in Appendix C.

final_notes:
Paper title: “Some Robustness Properties of Label Cleaning” by Chen Cheng and John Duchi.

Core setup: task risk R(f)=E ell(d∘f(X),Y) or E ell(d∘f(X),P(.|X)); surrogate risk R_phi(f)=E phi(f(X),Y). Aggregation observes Z and A:Z→A, aggregated surrogate risk R_{phi,A}=E phi(f(X),A(Z)).

Sec.3 consistency: F all Borel. Fisher consistency iff pointwise calibration psi>0. Uniform comparison via psi/biconjugate. Prop.3 aggregation: phi Fisher consistent for task iff pointwise aggregated calibration positive; comparison should be psi_A(R(f)-R*)≤R_{phi,A}(f)-R_{phi,A}*. Earlier text defined uniform calibration likely with inf_s typo instead of inf_x.

Ranking: without aggregation, k≥3 any convex score surrogate inconsistent for ranking risk (Prop.1). With repeated pairwise comparisons and aggregation to empirical normalized wins vector (or star if missing), squared loss phi(s,q)=||s−q||², phi(s,star)=0 is Fisher consistent for ranking if m≥k (Prop.2). Discussion later says finite-m explicit consistency guarantees exist for ranking and asks for broader finite-m theory.

Identifying surrogates: finite label space k. Def.3.1 phi is (C1,C2)-identifying if ∃a_y and scores s_y with d(s_y)=y satisfying margin inequalities (6a),(6b). Binary hinge is (1,2)-identifying. Generalized majority vote A_m(y_1,…,y_m)=a_hat y, hat y minimizes empirical task loss. Cor.3.2: if m(n)→∞ and phi identifying, aggregated surrogate excess→0 implies task excess→0.

Level-(xi,zeta) consistency: ∃psi with psi(eps)≥zeta eps for eps≥xi and psi(R(f)-R*)≤R_{phi,A}(f)-R_{phi,A}*. Opening paragraph had inconsistent formula using R_phi(f)-R* instead of aggregated surrogate excess.

Noise: Delta=min wrong conditional excess; binary Delta=|2P(Y=1|X)-1|. Mammen-Tsybakov (Nα) and (Mβ), claimed equivalent β=α/(1−α), problematic at α=1. Theorem 1: phi identifying, A_m majority, 0≤ell≤1, P satisfies (Nα), α∈[0,1]. If R−R* ≥ 2P(kappa>M)+(4C_MT e_m(M))^{1/(1−α)}, then R−R* ≤ (16/C1)(aggregated surrogate excess). α=1 allowed but formulas undefined. xi_m→0. Cor.3.3 explicit xi formulas also undefined at α=1; text “lower bound xi” logically wrong; claims α=1, xi=0 conflict with formulas. Discussion says noise condition number kappa(X) characterizes multiclass comparison inequalities; binary kappa(X)=1; kappa can be large even with low-noise α≈1 beyond binary.

Examples: binary nonsmooth margin surrogate identifying with C1=phi(0)-phi(δ), C2=phi(-δ). Matching: loss=1/(2N)||v1−v2||_1=1/(2N)||.||²; structured hinge identifying C1=1/N,C2=2; comparison should 16N times excess, but text writes A_n. General structured prediction: Lemma 3.3 C1=min_{hat y≠y} ell(hat y,y) (likely should min over y too), C2=max tau+1; binary embeddings normalized l1 loss tau=1,C2=2. Applying Cor.3.3 should have factor 4 in threshold and comparison 16/C1; text omitted 4 and gave 8/C1.

Sec.4 restricted classes. 4.1 binary classification: zero-one loss with d(s) sign, margin surrogate convex; all measurable Fisher/uniform iff φ′(0)<0. Linear F. Optimally predictable along θ*: sign(<θ*,x>) matches Bayes sign. Prop.4: for any ε>0 and nonzero θ*, exists P optimally predictable along θ* such that every surrogate minimizer θ_φ has higher task risk than θ* and |cos angle(θ_φ,θ*)|≤ε. Aggregation with majority vote: θ_m ε_m-argmin aggregated surrogate. Cor.4.1: if P optimally predictable along θ*, ε_m→0, then R(f_{θ_m})→R(f_{θ*}) and cos angle(θ_m,θ*)→1.

4.2 multiclass restricted classes: Y=[k], F linear cone zero-sum scores, decoder argmax. Surrogate Fisher consistent and limiting loss condition (13). Multiclass optimal predictability: ∃f∈F selecting Bayes label. Theorem 2: If F cone optimally predicts P, P(Delta>0)=1, majority aggregation, ε_m→0, f_m ε_m-argmin aggregated surrogate, then R(f_m)→R*.

4.3 finite-dimensional multiclass: X=R^d,Y=[k], linear Θ=[θ_1…θ_{k−1}], θ_k=0; categorical p_Θ via link σ. Link consistency (14): t_y=max_i t_i iff σ_y(t)=max_i σ_i(t). Logistic link/loss. For k=2 Gaussian, Θ_m=t_mΘ* even misspecified; binary classification consistent all m. For k≥3 slight misspecification can fail. σ^ε formula defined logistic outside T_ε, uniform inside; prose immediately reverses it (logistic inside, uniform outside), contradiction. Also claim σ^ε clearly satisfies (14), but uniform region generally violates iff unless all t tied. Proposition 5: for k≥3, Σ=I, assuming linear map D M=E[Z(∇σ^lr(Θ*^T Z) M Z)^T] invertible, there exists ε0>0 such that for any ε∈(0,ε0), some set T_ε of Lebesgue measure ≤ε yields unaggregated Θ_1(ε)/||Θ_1(ε)|| ≠ Θ*/||Θ*||. Theorem 3: for majority vote and true link σ satisfying (14), with Θ*=U*T* (U* orthogonal, T* nonsingular), Θ_m=U*T_m for every m and ||T_m||→∞, T_m/||T_m||→T*/||T*||. Text says this gives asymptotic consistency under misspecification and contrasts Prop.5. Discussion says these misspecified-model results require optimal predictability (12), i.e. Bayes-optimal classifier in F.

Sec.5 numerical illustrations. Experiment 1: binary margin truncated quadratic/squared hinge φ(δ)=max{1−δ,0}², optimal nonaggregated calibration ψ(ε)=ε². Majority aggregation with m labels, no low-noise α=0,C_MT=1, δ=1 gives ψ_m(ε)=1/16(ε−sqrt((32/m)log 40))_+. Claims curves transition from quadratic to linear as m→∞, conservative due to Theorem 1. Experiment 2: k=3,d=2 logistic loss with corrupted link \tildeσ(t)=σ^lr(t)1{||t||≤r}+σ^lr(αt)1{||t||>r}, matches softmax near origin and shrinks scores outside radius r. Parameters θ1*=(0,1), θ2*=(1,1), r=3, α=0.1. Fig.2 claims asymptotic consistency as m increases. Caption states error as || ||T_m||−T*/||T*|| ||, conflicting with Theorem 3’s convergence quantity T_m/||T_m||→T*/||T*||.

Discussion/future work: emphasizes nonaggregated data can be statistically efficient with fully expressive uncertainty models but cleaning more robust under misspecification/restricted classes. Future work: finite-m theory depending on (ell,phi) and m; limits of kappa/noise condition; beyond optimal predictability in misspecified models; restricted-class comparison inequalities/H-consistency with aggregation.

Paper title: “Some Robustness Properties of Label Cleaning” by Chen Cheng and John Duchi.

Abstract claims:
- Learning procedures relying on aggregated/cleaned labels (label information distilled from noisy responses) have robustness properties impossible without data cleaning.
- In risk consistency setting (minimizing surrogate losses instead of task loss such as 0-1 misclassification), procedures using label aggregation get stronger consistency guarantees than possible using raw labels.
- Classical perfectly specified statistical models suggest using all information/modeling label uncertainty is statistically efficient.
- However, consistency fails for “standard” approaches when the minimized loss is even slightly misspecified.
- Procedures leveraging aggregated information still converge to optimal classifiers, showing robustness from considering the full pipeline: data collection → model fitting → prediction, refining noisy signals.

Paper title: “Some Robustness Properties of Label Cleaning” by Chen Cheng and John Duchi.

Abstract claims:
- Learning procedures relying on aggregated/cleaned labels (label information distilled from noisy responses) have robustness properties impossible without data cleaning.
- In risk consistency setting (minimizing surrogate losses instead of task loss such as 0-1 misclassification), procedures using label aggregation get stronger consistency guarantees than possible using raw labels.
