- However, consistency fails for “standard” approaches when the minimized loss is even slightly misspecified.
- Procedures leveraging aggregated information still converge to optimal classifiers, showing robustness from considering the full pipeline: data collection → model fitting → prediction, refining noisy signals.

Introduction key claims:
- Modern supervised datasets often require cleaning/filtering/crowdsourcing multiple labels and denoising; paper investigates how data aggregation improves consistency of fitted models.
- Main thesis: label cleaning/aggregating labels provides robustness impossible without aggregation.
- Two faces of robustness:
  1. Improved consistency of estimation: when minimizing surrogate losses (e.g. multiclass logistic) instead of task losses (e.g. zero-one error), aggregated-label procedures can achieve consistent/optimal prediction in the limit when impossible without aggregation.
  2. Even in finite-dimensional statistical problems, aggregation can provide consistent classifiers when standard methods fail.
- Motivating questions: whether aggregation is needed for surrogate consistency, and if it helps, in what sense.
- Paper proposes concrete examples in ranking and binary/multiclass classification with linear estimators where estimators using only pairs (X,Y) necessarily fail but label aggregation yields consistency.
- Develops new notions/theory for surrogate consistency with data aggregation.
- In fully nonparametric scenarios, shows how number of aggregated samples combines with noise conditions to improve consistency.
- Claims aggregation permits surrogate risk consistency under only weak conditions on the surrogate loss; losses using aggregated labels admit approximate linear comparison inequalities.
- Unlike conventional risk consistency theory requiring hypothesis class F of all measurable functions, paper will show classification results where aggregating labels guarantees consistency even over restricted hypothesis classes, which may fail without aggregation.

Background mentioned:
- Surrogate risk consistency literature: Bartlett/Jordan/McAuliffe characterized binary convex surrogate consistency for zero-one error; further work in multilabel, ranking, structured prediction, ordinal regression, restricted classes, general theory.
- Existing analyses typically assume standard supervised pairs (X,Y) and do not address aggregation machinery.

Section 2 Preliminaries:
- Classical setup: data (Xi,Yi) iid P on X×Y. Learn scoring f:X→R^d, decoder d:R^d→Y, prediction d∘f(x).
- Task risk equation (1): R(f)=E_P[ ell(d∘f(X),Y) ]. Binary example: d=1, decoder sgn(s), ell(y,y’)=1{yy’≤0}, so R(f)=P(Y f(X)≤0).
- They introduce a more sophisticated task risk depending on conditional law P(Y∈·|X): equation (2) R(f)=E_P[ ell(d∘f(X), P(·|X)) ]. In multiclass, ell(yhat,P)=∑_y P(Y=y)1{yhat≠y}, coinciding with standard 0-1 error. Note: text incorrectly says minimizers coincide with original problem (2), but original risk is (1).
- Surrogate loss φ:R^d×Y→R; surrogate risk R_φ(f)=E_P[φ(f(X),Y)]. Need consistency with task problem (2).
- Paper studies two scenarios: (i) classical Fisher consistency where F contains all Borel functions; (ii) statistical scenarios with parametric possibly misspecified F. Main message: label aggregation improves consistency in both.

Section 2.1 Label aggregation:
- Instead of output Y, observe abstract Z∈Z. Example: multiple noisy labels for each X, Z=(Y1,…,Ym)∈Y^m.
- Aggregation space A; aggregating function A:Z→A, e.g. majority vote. Surrogate φ:R^d×A→R_+. Aggregated surrogate risk equation (3): R_{φ,A}(f)=E[φ(f(X),A(Z))]. Question: when minimizing (3) suffices to minimize task risk (2).
- Example 1 Majority vote/repeated sampling: Z=(Y1,…,Ym), Yi|X=x iid P_{Y|X=x}. Define A(Z)=argmin_{y∈Y}∑_{l=1}^m ell(y,Y_l). For 0-1 loss ell(yhat,y)=1{y≠yhat}, this is majority vote; general form allows abstract procedures.
- Example 2 K-nearest neighbors: abstract repeated sampling with example X and label Y plus additional iid sample (Xi,Yi)_{i=1}^m~P; Z=(Y,(Xi,Yi)_{i=1}^m). Distance metric on X; order Xi by distance to X, set X_(0)=X. For K≥0 aggregate K-nearest neighbors plus original by A_{m,K}(Z)=argmin_{y∈Y}∑_{l=0}^K ell(y,Y_(l)). Appendix C will extend to aggregation from a single sample.

Paper title: “Some Robustness Properties of Label Cleaning” by Chen Cheng and John Duchi.

Earlier notes: Main claims: label aggregation/cleaning can yield robustness/consistency impossible with raw labels; aggregated-label procedures can get stronger consistency/optimal prediction guarantees than raw-label procedures, including ranking and classification examples. Classical setup: data (X,Y), score f:X→R^d, decoder d, task risk (1) E ell(d∘f(X),Y). More general task risk (2): R(f)=E[ell(d∘f(X), P(.|X))], e.g. multiclass conditional 0-1. Surrogate risk R_phi(f)=E phi(f(X),Y). Aggregation: observe Z, aggregate A:Z→A, aggregated surrogate risk (3) E phi(f(X),A(Z)). Examples: repeated labels with majority-vote/general empirical task minimizer; KNN aggregation.

Section 3 Surrogate consistency: Standard framework assumes F all Borel functions f:X→R^d. Conditional task risk R(s|x)=ell(d∘s, P(Y|X=x)); conditional surrogate R_phi(s|x)=E[phi(s,Y)|X=x]. Pointwise excess risks delta_l and delta_phi defined relative to inf over s’∈R^d. Minimal risks R*=inf_F R(f), R_phi*=inf_F R_phi(f). Consistency notions for all P: (i) Fisher consistency: R_phi(f_n)→R_phi* implies R(f_n)→R*. (ii) Uniform comparison: nondecreasing psi with psi(eps)>0 for eps>0 and psi(R(f)-R*)≤R_phi(f)-R_phi*. In binary margin-based convex case, notions coincide. Calibration functions: psi(eps,x)=inf{delta_phi(s,x): delta_l(s,x)≥eps}, overline psi(eps)=inf_x psi(eps,x). Corollary 3.1: phi Fisher consistent iff psi(eps,x)>0 for all x, eps>0. Let psi be Fenchel biconjugate of overline psi; overline psi(eps)>0 iff psi(eps)>0, and comparison inequality holds for all measurable f.

Text says for general risk minimization (2), a Fisher-consistent surrogate from single pairs (X,Y) would allow ordinary empirical process tools and simpler data collection, but such results are generally impossible; motivates aggregation theory in Sec. 3.2.

grade.reason: The reviewer flagged issues about formulas being undefined or contradictory at α=1, but did not identify the planted monotonicity error that increasing α (toward 1) can decrease the required sample size due to the exponent 1/[2(1−α)].

errors.claim: “For multiple independent comparisons Z=(Y_1,\ldots,Y_m) conditional on X, put m_{ij}=\sum_{y\in\mathcal Y^m}1\{y=(i,j)\}, …”
errors.location: this part, Section 3.1 ranking aggregation definition
errors.evidence: The same paragraph says the aggregation is for observed repeated comparisons “Z=(Y_1,\ldots,Y_m)” and then uses conditions such as “m_j=0 for some j” and ratios “m_{ij}/m_j” in A(Z).
errors.explanation: As written, m_{ij} sums over all possible tuples y∈Y^m and tests whether a tuple equals a single pair (i,j), so it is not an observed count from Z. This conflicts with the subsequent use of m_{ij},m_j as data-dependent counts for the observed repeated comparisons.

errors.claim: “\overline\psi_A(\epsilon)\coloneqq \inf_{s\in\mathbb R^d}\overline\psi_A(\epsilon,x).”
errors.evidence: Earlier in the same part, the analogous uniform calibration function is defined as “\overline\psi(\epsilon)\coloneqq \inf_{x\in\mathcal X}\psi(\epsilon,x).” Also \overline\psi_A(\epsilon,x) is already defined by an infimum over s: “\overline\psi_A(\epsilon,x)\coloneqq \inf_{s\in\mathbb R^d}\{...\}.”
errors.explanation: The displayed definition of \overline\psi_A(ε) takes an infimum over s of an expression that no longer contains s but still contains x. This conflicts with both the immediately preceding pointwise definition and the earlier uniform definition, which require an infimum over x.

errors.claim: “Assume ... condition (Nα), with α∈[0,1]” in Theorem 1, followed by thresholds containing powers 1/(1−α), e.g. “(4 C_MT e_m(M))^{1/(1−α)}”.
errors.evidence: The theorem allows α=1, but its displayed condition and ξ definition use the exponent 1/(1−α), which is undefined at α=1. Later the text also separately says “at α=1, m≥... gives ξ_{m,k}=0,” confirming α=1 is intended to be included.
errors.explanation: The theorem’s stated α range includes a value for which the theorem’s own formulas are not defined.

errors.claim: “Low noise permits a comparison written as ψ(R(f)−R*)≤R_φ(f)−R* ...”
errors.evidence: Theorem 1 and Definition 3.2 use surrogate excess risk: “R_{φ,A_m}(f)−R_{φ,A_m}^*” and “ψ(R(f)−R*)≤R_{φ,A}(f)−R_{φ,A}^*.”
errors.explanation: The informal comparison subtracts the task optimum R* from the surrogate risk R_φ(f), while the surrounding theorem and formal definition subtract the surrogate optimum. These are different quantities.

errors.claim: “The crude bound ... lower bounds the promised ξ_{m,k} by setting ξ_{m,k}:= ...” followed by Corollary 3.3: “every f with R(f)−R*≥ξ_{m,k} satisfies ...”
errors.location: this part, after Theorem 1 and Corollary 3.3
errors.evidence: Theorem 1 gives the comparison only for functions above the threshold ξ = 2P(κ(X)>M)+(4C_MT e_m(M))^{1/(1−α)}, and ξ_m is the infimum of such thresholds. To use ξ_{m,k} as a sufficient threshold in Corollary 3.3, ξ_{m,k} must be at least an available theorem threshold, not a lower bound on it.
errors.explanation: A lower bound on the required threshold would not justify applying the theorem to all f above that lower value. The statement of “lower bounds” conflicts with the use of ξ_{m,k} as a valid sufficient threshold.

errors.claim: “On 2N vertices, the matching surrogate is W3C with C_{φ,1}=1/N.”
errors.evidence: Later in this part, Lemma 3.3 states for A3J that “C_{φ,1}=min_{ŷ≠y} ℓ(ŷ,y),” and the matching loss is defined as ℓ(y1,y2)=1/(2N)||v(y1)-v(y2)||_1. For two distinct perfect matchings, the smallest symmetric difference is two edges removed and two added, so ||v(y1)-v(y2)||_1=4 and min ℓ=2/N.
errors.explanation: The stated matching constant 1/N does not agree with the later formula for C_{φ,1} applied to the matching loss defined in the same part.

errors.claim: The structured prediction bound says “R(f)-R* ≤ 8/min_{ŷ≠y}ℓ(ŷ,y) · (R_{φ,A_m}(f)-R_{φ,A_m}*)”.
errors.evidence: Earlier notes record Theorem 1: if φ is W3C, then for functions above the threshold, “R−R*≤16/C1 (R_{φ,A_m}−R_{φ,A_m}*)”. Lemma 3.3 in this part identifies C1=min_{ŷ≠y}ℓ(ŷ,y).
errors.explanation: The coefficient should match the general theorem’s 16/C1, but this part gives 8/C1. This also conflicts with the matching bound in the same part, which uses 16N from C1=1/N.

errors.claim: The structured prediction threshold is written without a leading factor 4: “R(f)-R* ≥ (32 C_MT^4/m log(...))^{α/[2(1−α^2)]}”.
errors.evidence: Earlier notes record the explicit Theorem 1 threshold for k>2 as “4*(32 C_MT^4/m log(4k(C1+C2)/C1))^{α/[2(1−α²)]}”. The matching specialization earlier in this same part also includes the leading factor: “R(f)-R* ≥ 4·(32 C_MT^4/m log(...))^{α/[2(1−α²)]}”.
errors.explanation: The general structured bound drops the factor 4 even though it is present in the earlier theorem and in the immediately preceding matching specialization.

errors.claim: The matching bound concludes with “R(f)-R* ≤ 16N(R_{φ,A_n}(f)-R_{φ,A_n}*)”.
errors.evidence: The same paragraph says aggregation consistency is controlled by a count m and states the threshold using m: “once its count exceeds O(N log N)” and “32 C_MT^4/m”. Earlier notation in the notes consistently uses A_m for aggregation over m labels.
errors.explanation: The conclusion switches from A_m to A_n, but no n is defined as the aggregation count here; this conflicts with the notation and formulas using m.

errors.claim: “The conditional distribution ... samples Y∼σ^lr(t) if t∈Tε and uniformly otherwise.”
errors.evidence: Immediately before, the paper defines σ^ε(t)=σ^lr(t)1{t∉Tε} + (1/k)1 1{t∈Tε}.
errors.explanation: The displayed definition says the model is logistic outside Tε and uniform inside Tε, while the prose says the opposite.

errors.claim: “The link satisfies ordering consistency...”
errors.evidence: The notes define ordering consistency/link condition (14): t_y=max_i t_i iff σ_y(t)=max_i σ_i(t). But this part defines σ^ε(t)=(1/k)1 on t∈Tε.
errors.explanation: On any point t∈Tε with non-tied coordinates, σ^ε makes all classes tied for maximum probability, so σ_y(t)=max_i σ_i(t) for every y, not only those with maximal t_y. Thus the displayed σ^ε generally violates the paper’s own ordering-consistency condition.

errors.claim: “plotted classification-rule error is \(\left\|\|T_m\|-T^\star/\|T^\star\|\right\|\) against label count.”
errors.evidence: Earlier theorem statement in notes: “Theorem 3: ... \(\|T_m\|\to\infty\) and direction \(T_m/\|T_m\|\to T^\star/\|T^\star\|\).”
errors.explanation: The caption’s expression subtracts a normalized matrix/vector from the scalar norm \(\|T_m\|\), which is not the directional error described by the theorem. It should be comparing normalized directions, e.g. \(\|T_m/\|T_m\|-T^\star/\|T^\star\|\|\).

final_notes:
Paper title: “Some Robustness Properties of Label Cleaning” by Chen Cheng and John Duchi.

Framework: iid (X,Y). Scores f:X→R^d decoded by d; task risk R(f)=E ell(d∘f(X),Y) or distribution-dependent R(f)=E ell(d∘f(X),P(.|X)). Binary sign/0-1. Aggregated surrogate risk R_{φ,A}(f)=E φ(f(X),A(Z)); repeated labels Z=(Y1,...,Ym) iid conditional on X; A_m=argmin_y sum_l ell(y,Y_l), majority vote/T4K for 0-1.

Section 3 surrogate consistency: Q7D/calibration with conditional excesses δ_l,δ_φ; ψ(ε,x)=inf_s{δ_φ(s,x):δ_l(s,x)≥ε}; uniform overlineψ. Positivity ⇔ Q7D; biconjugate comparison. Pair-only generally impossible. Prop 1: k≥3, every convex φ:R^k×Y→R fails Q7D for ranking/pairwise comparisons. Prop 2: squared φ(s,q)=||s−q||² with aggregation over m≥k comparisons Q7D. Section 2 preliminaries:
- Two regimes: unrestricted Borel F with classical Fisher consistency; and parametric/potentially misspecified F, with aggregation improving consistency in each.
- Data: iid (Xi,Yi) ~ P on X x Y. Scores f:X→R^d decoded by d:R^d→Y; prediction yhat=d∘f(x).
- Distribution-dependent task criterion defined as R(f)=E_P[ ell(d∘f(X), P(.|X)) ] (eq. 2). For multiclass Y={1,...,k}, ell(yhat,P)=sum_y P(Y=y)1{yhat≠y}, giving standard zero-one error.
- Instantaneous task formulation for ell:YxY→R_+: R(f)=E_P[ell(d∘f(X),Y)] (eq. 1). Binary classification: d=1, decoder sgn, ell(y,y’)=1{yy’≤0}, R(f)=P(Y f(X)≤0). Section 2.1 label aggregation:
- Aggregated surrogate risk: R_{phi,A}(f)=E[phi(f(X), A(Z))] (eq. 3), assessed against actual task-risk minimization. Z in Z, aggregation space A, map A:Z→A, nonnegative surrogate phi:R^d x A→R_+.
- Repeated labeling: Z=(Y1,...,Ym) in Y^m with Yi|X=x iid P_{Y|X=x}. Aggregator A_m(Z)=argmin_{y in Y} sum_{l=1}^m ell(y,Y_l). For 0-1 loss this is majority vote; general ell allows other procedures.
- Rough KNN construction: X has Y and additional independent draws (Xi,Yi)_{i=1}^m iid P; Z=(Y,(Xi,Yi)_{i=1}^m). Order neighbors by distance to X with X_(0)=X; A_{m,K}(Z)=argmin_y sum_{l=0}^K ell(y,Y_(l)), K≥0. errors.claim: “The link satisfies ordering consistency...”

errors.explanation: On any point t∈Tε with non-tied coordinates, σ^ε makes all classes tied for maximum probability, so σ_y(t)=max_i σ_i(t) for every y, not only those with maximal t_y. Thus the displayed σ^ε generally violates the paper’s own ordering-consistency condition.

Paper title: “Some Robustness Properties of Label Cleaning” by Chen Cheng and John Duchi.

Main setup: task risk R(f)=E ell(d∘f(X),Y) or E ell(d∘f(X),P(.|X)); surrogate risk R_phi(f)=E phi(f(X),Y). Aggregation observes Z and A:Z→A, aggregated surrogate risk R_{phi,A}=E phi(f(X),A(Z)).

Sec.3 consistency: F all Borel. Fisher consistency iff pointwise calibration psi>0. Prop.3 aggregation: phi Fisher consistent for task iff aggregated calibration positive; comparison psi_A(R(f)-R*)≤R_{phi,A}(f)-R_{phi,A}*. Ranking: without aggregation convex score surrogates inconsistent for k≥3; with repeated comparisons aggregated to wins vector, squared loss Fisher consistent if m≥k. Identifying surrogates: Def.3.1 (C_phi,1,C_phi,2)-identifying via margins; binary hinge (1,2). Generalized majority vote A_m. Cor.3.2: m(n)→∞ and identifying => aggregated surrogate excess→0 implies task excess→0. Level-(xi,zeta) consistency has comparison to aggregated surrogate excess; earlier formula typo used R_phi(f)-R*. Noise: Delta=min excess conditional risk for wrong prediction; binary Delta=|2P(Y=1|X)-1|. Mammen-Tsybakov Nα/Mβ equivalence claimed via β=α/(1−α) (α=1 issue). Condition number kappa; e_m(t)=t sqrt((2/m)log(4k(C1+C2)/C1)). Theorem 1: if R−R* ≥ 2P(kappa>M)+(4 C_MT e_m(M))^{1/(1−α)}, then R−R*≤(16/C1) aggregated surrogate excess; xi_m is inf threshold, xi_m→0. Cor.3.3 thresholds: binary (32 C_MT²/m log(8(C1+C2)/C1))^{1/[2(1−α)]}; k≥3: 4*(32 C_MT^4/m log(4k(C1+C2)/C1))^{α/[2(1−α²)]}. Text later says α=1 with m large gives xi=0 though formulas undefined.

Examples: binary nonsmooth margin: Lemma 3.1 feasible C1=phi(0)-phi(delta), C2=phi(-delta); comparison 16/C1. Bipartite matching: k=N!, loss normalized Hamming; structured hinge C1=1/N,C2=2; threshold includes 4*(32 C_MT^4/m log(4k(2N+1)))^{α/[2(1−α²)]}; comparison should be 16N times aggregated excess, but text wrote A_n. General structured: Lemma 3.3 structured hinge C1=min loss, C2=max tau+1; if binary embeddings and normalized Hamming, tau=1,C2=2. Final specialization omitted leading 4 and used 8/C1 instead of 16/C1.

Sec.4 restricted classes. 4.1 binary: Y={±1}, zero-one ell=1{ys≤0}, margin varphi(s,y)=phi(sy), phi convex. All-measurable Fisher iff phi'(0)<0. Linear F={f_theta=<theta,x>}. Optimally predictable along theta*: sign matches Bayes sign. Prop.4: for any eps and nonzero theta*, ∃P optimally predictable along theta* such that all surrogate minimizers have larger task risk than theta* and |cos angle|≤eps. Notation issue: proposition uses E[phi(f_theta(X),Y)] although phi unary. Aggregation A_m majority: epsilon_m-argmin E[phi(A_m(Ys) f_theta(X))] yields R→R* and cos(theta_m,theta*)→1.

4.2 multiclass: Y=[k], zero-one, decoder argmax_y s_y. F linear cone with f^T1=0 and closed under positive scaling. Surrogate varphi Fisher consistent and limiting loss condition (13): varphi(s,y)→0 if s_y−s_j→∞ for all j≠y. Examples: multiclass logistic and pairwise margin losses with phi convex nonincreasing, phi'(0)<0, inf phi=0. Zhang theorem: such losses consistent over all measurable centered scores; binary margin included via f=(g,-g). Linear multiclass functions with sum_i theta_i=0 form convex cone. New definition: F optimally predicts P if ∃f∈F whose argmax lies in argmax of conditional class probabilities for all x. Theorem 2: if F cone optimally predicts P, P(Delta>0)=1, majority vote A_m, epsilon_m→0, then any epsilon_m-argmin of aggregated surrogate risk has R(f_m)→R*. Text says this gives asymptotic consistency by aggregation and contrasts Prop.4.

4.3 finite-dimensional multiclass. X=R^d,Y=[k], linear predictors Θ=[θ1…θ_{k−1}], θ_k=0 convention. True categorical p_Θ(x) from link σ(t) with σ_k=1−1^Tσ and consistency condition (14): t_y=max_i t_i iff σ_y(t)=max_i σ_i(t), with t_k=0. Logistic link example. With repeated labels and majority vote Y_i^+, distribution p_{Θ,m} via ρ_m; text says ρ_m satisfies (14). Logistic loss (15), gradient, population L_m minimizer satisfies E[X(σ_lr(Θ_m^T X)−ρ_m(Θ*^T X))^T]=0. Claims for k=2 and Gaussian X, mis-specified link gives Θ_m=t_mΘ*, hence classification consistent for all m. For k≥3 slight misspecification causes failure. Defines T_ε of Lebesgue measure ε and σ^ε(t)=σ_lr(t) outside T_ε, uniform inside T_ε; prose incorrectly reverses this. Also claim σ^ε clearly satisfies (14) is false for t in T_ε unless ties. Defines L_{m,ε}, Θ_m(ε), notes Θ_1(0)=Θ*. Prop.5: for k≥3, Σ=I, assuming linear map M↦DM=E[Z(∇σ_lr(Θ*^T Z)MZ)^T] for Z~N(0,I_{k−1}) is invertible, ∃ε0>0 such that for any ε∈(0,ε0), ∃T_ε of Lebesgue measure ≤ε with Θ_1(ε)/||Θ_1(ε)|| ≠ Θ*/||Θ*||; proof in App.E.1. Then majority vote addresses inconsistency as m→∞ for any true link σ satisfying (14): define L_{m,σ}, Θ_m=argmin. Theorem3: if Θ*=U*T* with U*∈R^{d×(k−1)} orthogonal and T* nonsingular, then ∃T_m with Θ_m=U*T_m for every m, ||T_m||→∞ and T_m/||T_m||→T*/||T*||. Claimed as evidence of robustness/asymptotic consistency in misspecified models, contrasting Prop.5.

Sec.5 numerics. Experiment 1: binary truncated quadratic phi(δ)=max{1−δ,0}²; cites Bartlett calibration psi(ε)=ε². With majority vote and Lemma 3.1 δ=1, no low-noise α=0,C_MT=1: psi_m(ε)=1/16(ε−sqrt(32/m log 40))_+. This matches C1=phi(0)-phi(1)=1 and C2=phi(-1)=4. Figure 1 compares psi vs psi_m for m=2^16,…,2^32 and says aggregation moves quadratic toward linear, though theorem bound conservative. Experiment 2: logistic Sec.4.3 k=3,d=2 with corrupted link tildeσ(t)=σ_lr(t)1{||t||≤r}+σ_lr(αt)1{||t||>r}, r=3, α=0.1, θ1*=(0,1)^T, θ2*=(1,1)^T. Claims Fig.2 shows asymptotic consistency as m→∞. Caption gives erroneous classification error formula || ||T_m|| − T*/||T*|| ||, inconsistent with Theorem3 convergence T_m/||T_m||→T*/||T*||. Left: n=10000 multilabeled observations for each m. Right: n=640000/m so total labels fixed. 95% error bars over T=100 trials.

Sec.6 discussion: positions paper in debate over using all noisy labels vs cleaned labels; says aggregation can improve robustness but many questions remain. Notes many consistency results take m→∞; ranking Sec.3.1 has explicit finite-m guarantees, but broader finite-m surrogate consistency theory is future work. Discussion of noise condition number: says κ(X) characterizes comparison inequalities for multiclass and binary has trivially κ=1; then claims κ is “smaller than in binary” beyond binary even when α≈1, which conflicts with κ as a difficulty/condition-number measure and binary κ=1. Mis-specified model discussion says Sec.4.3 results require optimal predictability/Bayes optimal classifier in F; beyond this is future work. Final future work: extend aggregation comparison inequalities to restricted hypothesis classes/H-consistency; mentions smooth convex losses have rate-optimal quadratic growth of ψ and asks whether aggregation can upgrade consistency.

Paper title: “Some Robustness Properties of Label Cleaning” by Chen Cheng and John Duchi.

Abstract claims:
- Learning procedures relying on aggregated/cleaned labels (label information distilled from noisy responses) have robustness properties impossible without data cleaning.
- In risk consistency setting (minimizing surrogate losses instead of task loss such as 0-1 misclassification), procedures using label aggregation get stronger consistency guarantees than possible using raw labels.
- Classical perfectly specified statistical models suggest using all information/modeling label uncertainty is statistically efficient.
- However, consistency fails for “standard” approaches when the minimized loss is even slightly misspecified.
- Procedures leveraging aggregated information still converge to optimal classifiers, showing robustness from considering the full pipeline: data collection → model fitting → prediction, refining noisy signals.

Introduction key claims:

- Main thesis: label cleaning/aggregating labels provides robustness impossible without aggregation.
- Two faces of robustness:
  1. Improved consistency of estimation: when minimizing surrogate losses (e.g. multiclass logistic) instead of task losses (e.g. zero-one error), aggregated-label procedures can achieve consistent/optimal prediction in the limit when impossible without aggregation.
  2. Even in finite-dimensional statistical problems, aggregation can provide consistent classifiers when standard methods fail.
- Motivating questions: whether aggregation is needed for surrogate consistency, and if it helps, in what sense.
- Paper proposes concrete examples in ranking and binary/multiclass classification with linear estimators where estimators using only pairs (X,Y) necessarily fail but label aggregation yields consistency.
- Develops new notions/theory for surrogate consistency with data aggregation.

- Claims aggregation permits surrogate risk consistency under only weak conditions on the surrogate loss; losses using aggregated labels admit approximate linear comparison inequalities.
- Unlike conventional risk consistency theory requiring hypothesis class F of all measurable functions, paper will show classification results where aggregating labels guarantees consistency even over restricted hypothesis classes, which may fail without aggregation.

- Surrogate risk consistency literature: Bartlett/Jordan/McAuliffe characterized binary convex surrogate consistency for zero-one error; further work in multilabel, ranking, structured prediction, ordinal regression, restricted classes, general theory.

Section 2 Preliminaries:
- Classical setup: data (Xi,Yi) iid P on X×Y. Learn scoring f:X→R^d, decoder d:R^d→Y, prediction d∘f(x).
- Task risk equation (1): R(f)=E_P[ ell(d∘f(X),Y) ]. Binary example: d=1, decoder sgn(s), ell(y,y’)=1{yy’≤0}, so R(f)=P(Y f(X)≤0).
- They introduce a more sophisticated task risk depending on conditional law P(Y∈·|X): equation (2) R(f)=E_P[ ell(d∘f(X), P(·|X)) ]. In multiclass, ell(yhat,P)=∑_y P(Y=y)1{yhat≠y}, coinciding with standard 0-1 error. Note: text incorrectly says minimizers coincide with original problem (2), but original risk is (1).
- Surrogate loss φ:R^d×Y→R; surrogate risk R_φ(f)=E_P[φ(f(X),Y)]. Need consistency with task problem (2).
- Paper studies two scenarios: (i) classical Fisher consistency where F contains all Borel functions; (ii) statistical scenarios with parametric possibly misspecified F. Main message: label aggregation improves consistency in both.

Section 2.1 Label aggregation:
- Instead of output Y, observe abstract Z∈Z. Example: multiple noisy labels for each X, Z=(Y1,…,Ym)∈Y^m.
- Aggregation space A; aggregating function A:Z→A, e.g. majority vote. Surrogate φ:R^d×A→R_+. Aggregated surrogate risk equation (3): R_{φ,A}(f)=E[φ(f(X),A(Z))]. Question: when minimizing (3) suffices to minimize task risk (2).
- Example 1 Majority vote/repeated sampling: Z=(Y1,…,Ym), Yi|X=x iid P_{Y|X=x}. Define A(Z)=argmin_{y∈Y}∑_{l=1}^m ell(y,Y_l). For 0-1 loss ell(yhat,y)=1{y≠yhat}, this is majority vote; general form allows abstract procedures.
- Example 2 K-nearest neighbors: abstract repeated sampling with example X and label Y plus additional iid sample (Xi,Yi)_{i=1}^m~P; Z=(Y,(Xi,Yi)_{i=1}^m). Distance metric on X; order Xi by distance to X, set X_(0)=X. For K≥0 aggregate K-nearest neighbors plus original by A_{m,K}(Z)=argmin_{y∈Y}∑_{l=0}^K ell(y,Y_(l)). Appendix C will extend to aggregation from a single sample.

Paper title: “Some Robustness Properties of Label Cleaning” by Chen Cheng and John Duchi.

Earlier notes: Main claims: label aggregation/cleaning can yield robustness/consistency impossible with raw labels; aggregated-label procedures can get stronger consistency/optimal prediction guarantees than raw-label procedures, including ranking and classification examples. Classical setup: data (X,Y), score f:X→R^d, decoder d, task risk (1) E ell(d∘f(X),Y). More general task risk (2): R(f)=E[ell(d∘f(X), P(.|X))], e.g. multiclass conditional 0-1. Surrogate risk R_phi(f)=E phi(f(X),Y). Aggregation: observe Z, aggregate A:Z→A, aggregated surrogate risk (3) E phi(f(X),A(Z)). Examples: repeated labels with majority-vote/general empirical task minimizer; KNN aggregation.

Section 3 Surrogate consistency: Standard framework assumes F all Borel functions f:X→R^d. Conditional task risk R(s|x)=ell(d∘s, P(Y|X=x)); conditional surrogate R_phi(s|x)=E[phi(s,Y)|X=x]. Pointwise excess risks delta_l and delta_phi defined relative to inf over s’∈R^d. Minimal risks R*=inf_F R(f), R_phi*=inf_F R_phi(f). Consistency notions for all P: (i) Fisher consistency: R_phi(f_n)→R_phi* implies R(f_n)→R*. (ii) Uniform comparison: nondecreasing psi with psi(eps)>0 for eps>0 and psi(R(f)-R*)≤R_phi(f)-R_phi*. In binary margin-based convex case, notions coincide. Calibration functions: psi(eps,x)=inf{delta_phi(s,x): delta_l(s,x)≥eps}, overline psi(eps)=inf_x psi(eps,x). Corollary 3.1: phi Fisher consistent iff psi(eps,x)>0 for all x, eps>0. Let psi be Fenchel biconjugate of overline psi; overline psi(eps)>0 iff psi(eps)>0, and comparison inequality holds for all measurable f.

Text says for general risk minimization (2), a Fisher-consistent surrogate from single pairs (X,Y) would allow ordinary empirical process tools and simpler data collection, but such results are generally impossible; motivates aggregation theory in Sec. 3.2.

errors.claim: “The condition number is smaller than in binary classification even when the Mammen-Tsybakov noise level (Nα) is low—i.e. α≈1—in cases beyond binary classification.”
errors.location: this part, ‘Fundamental limits of the noise condition number’
errors.evidence: The same paragraph says the noise condition number characterizes “the difficulty beyond binary classification, where trivially κ(X)=1.” Earlier results also use κ as a condition number in comparison bounds, with binary treated as the trivial κ=1 case.
errors.explanation: If binary classification has trivially κ(X)=1 and κ is a condition number measuring difficulty, saying multiclass κ is “smaller than in binary classification” conflicts with the surrounding claim that κ captures additional difficulty beyond binary. The statement appears internally inconsistent; it likely should say larger/worse rather than smaller.

grade.reason: The reviewer’s last reported error identifies the claim that the multiclass condition number is smaller than in binary, noting this conflicts with earlier statements that binary has κ(X)=1 and that κ is at least 1 (so multiclass cannot be smaller), which matches the planted error's core contradiction.

errors.claim: “For multiple independent comparisons Z=(Y_1,\ldots,Y_m) conditional on X, put m_{ij}=\sum_{y\in\mathcal Y^m}1\{y=(i,j)\}, …”
errors.location: this part, Section 3.1 ranking aggregation definition
errors.evidence: The same paragraph says the aggregation is for observed repeated comparisons “Z=(Y_1,\ldots,Y_m)” and then uses conditions such as “m_j=0 for some j” and ratios “m_{ij}/m_j” in A(Z).
errors.explanation: As written, m_{ij} sums over all possible tuples y∈Y^m and tests whether a tuple equals a single pair (i,j), so it is not an observed count from Z. This conflicts with the subsequent use of m_{ij},m_j as data-dependent counts for the observed repeated comparisons.

errors.claim: “\overline\psi_A(\epsilon)\coloneqq \inf_{s\in\mathbb R^d}\overline\psi_A(\epsilon,x).”

errors.explanation: The displayed definition of \overline\psi_A(ε) takes an infimum over s of an expression that no longer contains s but still contains x. This conflicts with both the immediately preceding pointwise definition and the earlier uniform definition, which require an infimum over x.

errors.claim: “The crude bound … lower bounds the promised ξ_{m,k} by setting ξ_{m,k}:= …”

Prop 2: squared loss to aggregated comparisons is Q7D for ranking when m≥k and aggregation counts comparisons, with star if denominator zero; possible formula issue: m_ij summed over y∈Y^m rather than observed comparisons. Cor 3.3: k=2 threshold exponent 1/[2(1−α)] log 8(C1+C2)/C1; k≥3 threshold should be 4*(32 C_MT^4/m log(4k(C1+C2)/C1))^{α/[2(1−α^2)]}; if R−R*≥ξ_{m,k}, slope 16/C1. Prop 4: for any ε and nonzero θ*, some binary distribution satisfies K7M along θ*, yet every unaggregated surrogate minimizer has higher risk than θ* and angle cos ≤ε, any nonnegative loss. Theorem 2: multiclass zero-one [k], argmax decoder, cone F with f^T1=0 closed under positive scaling, nonnegative Q7D φ with φ(s,y)→0 as y-margin→∞, response Y^m, aggregation T4K, unique population maximizer y*(x), K7M in F, P(Δ>0)=1: ε_m-argmin aggregated risk over F gives R(f_m)→R*. Section 6 discussion: claims uncleaned supervised-label information has fundamental limitations and cleaning gives robustness gains. Section 2 preliminaries:
- Two regimes: unrestricted Borel F with classical Fisher consistency; and parametric/potentially misspecified F, with aggregation improving consistency in each.
- Data: iid (Xi,Yi) ~ P on X x Y. Scores f:X→R^d decoded by d:R^d→Y; prediction yhat=d∘f(x).
- Distribution-dependent task criterion defined as R(f)=E_P[ ell(d∘f(X), P(.|X)) ] (eq. 2). For multiclass Y={1,...,k}, ell(yhat,P)=sum_y P(Y=y)1{yhat≠y}, giving standard zero-one error.
- Instantaneous task formulation for ell:YxY→R_+: R(f)=E_P[ell(d∘f(X),Y)] (eq. 1). Binary classification: d=1, decoder sgn, ell(y,y’)=1{yy’≤0}, R(f)=P(Y f(X)≤0). Task losses can be nonsmooth/nonconvex/flat; use surrogate phi:R^d x Y→R, R_phi(f)=E phi(f(X),Y), requiring consistency with task criterion.

Section 2.1 label aggregation:
- Aggregated surrogate risk: R_{phi,A}(f)=E[phi(f(X), A(Z))] (eq. 3), assessed against actual task-risk minimization. Z in Z, aggregation space A, map A:Z→A, nonnegative surrogate phi:R^d x A→R_+.
- Repeated labeling: Z=(Y1,...,Ym) in Y^m with Yi|X=x iid P_{Y|X=x}. Aggregator A_m(Z)=argmin_{y in Y} sum_{l=1}^m ell(y,Y_l). For 0-1 loss this is majority vote; general ell allows other procedures.
- Rough KNN construction: X has Y and additional independent draws (Xi,Yi)_{i=1}^m iid P; Z=(Y,(Xi,Yi)_{i=1}^m). Order neighbors by distance to X with X_(0)=X; A_{m,K}(Z)=argmin_y sum_{l=0}^K ell(y,Y_(l)), K≥0. Population-level repeated-sampling treatment also extends to aggregation from one sample in Appendix C.

Paper title: “Some Robustness Properties of Label Cleaning” by Chen Cheng and John Duchi.

Main setup: task risk R(f)=E ell(d∘f(X),Y) or E ell(d∘f(X),P(.|X)); surrogate risk R_phi(f)=E phi(f(X),Y). Aggregation observes Z and A:Z→A, aggregated surrogate risk R_{phi,A}=E phi(f(X),A(Z)).

Sec.3 consistency: F all Borel. Fisher consistency iff pointwise calibration psi>0. Prop.3 aggregation: phi Fisher consistent iff pointwise aggregated calibration positive; comparison psi_A(R(f)-R*)≤R_{phi,A}(f)-R_{phi,A}*. Ranking: convex score surrogates inconsistent for k≥3 without aggregation; with repeated comparisons and empirical wins, squared loss Fisher consistent if m≥k. Identifying surrogates: Def.3.1 margin inequalities; binary hinge (1,2)-identifying. Majority vote A_m chooses label minimizing empirical task loss. Cor.3.2: if m(n)→∞ and phi identifying, aggregated surrogate excess→0 implies task excess→0. Level-(xi,zeta) consistency uses aggregated surrogate excess; opening paragraph had inconsistent nonaggregated formula.

Noise: Delta(x)=min excess conditional risk for incorrect prediction; binary Delta=|2P(Y=1|X=x)-1|. Mammen-Tsybakov (Nα)/(Mβ), β=α/(1−α) with α=1 issue. Condition number kappa; e_m(t)=t sqrt((2/m)log(4k(C1+C2)/C1)). Theorem 1: identifying phi, majority A_m, bounded loss, (Nα). If R−R* ≥ 2P(kappa>M)+(4C_MT e_m(M))^{1/(1−α)}, then R−R*≤(16/C1)(aggregated surrogate excess). xi_m inf threshold →0. Cor.3.3 explicit xi: binary (32 C_MT²/m log(8(C1+C2)/C1))^{1/[2(1−α)]}; k≥3: 4*(32 C_MT^4/m log(4k(C1+C2)/C1))^{α/[2(1−α²)]}. Wording “lower bound xi” likely wrong; formulas undefined at α=1 but text claims xi=0 if m large O(log k).

Examples: Binary nonsmooth margin surrogate with C1=phi(0)-phi(delta), C2=phi(-delta), comparison 16/C1. Bipartite matching: k=N!, loss normalized Hamming; structured hinge C1=1/N,C2=2; comparison should be 16N times aggregated excess, but text wrote A_n. General structured prediction: structured hinge C1=min loss, C2=max tau+1; if binary embeddings normalized Hamming then C2=2. Final specialization omitted leading 4 in threshold and used 8/C1 instead of 16/C1.

Sec.4 restricted classes. 4.1 binary: Y={±1}, zero-one ell=1{ys≤0}; margin surrogate varphi(s,y)=phi(sy), phi convex. All-measurable consistency iff phi'(0)<0. Linear class f_theta=<theta,x>. Optimally predictable along theta*: sign matches Bayes. Prop.4: for any eps and nonzero theta*, some P optimally predictable along theta* such that all surrogate minimizers have worse task risk and angle nearly orthogonal. Notation issue: proposition uses E[phi(f_theta(X),Y)] though phi unary. Aggregation majority A_m; epsilon_m-argmin E[phi(A_m(Ys) f_theta(X))]. Cor.4.1: if optimally predictable, R(f_theta_m)→R(f_theta*) and cosine→1.

4.2 multiclass: Y=[k], zero-one, decoder argmax. F linear cone with scores sum zero and closed under positive scaling. Surrogate varphi Fisher consistent and limiting loss condition (13): varphi(s,y)→0 when y margin→∞. Examples logistic and pairwise margin losses. Zhang result: convex nonincreasing phi with phi'(0)<0, inf phi=0 gives consistency over all measurable sum-zero F; binary setting via f=(g,-g). Linear multiclass with sum theta_i=0 is convex cone. Optimal predictability extended: ∃f∈F with argmax f_y(x) in argmax P(Y=y|X=x) for all x. Theorem 2: If F is a cone, optimally predicts P, P(Delta>0)=1, and epsilon_m→0, then any epsilon_m-argmin of aggregated surrogate risk with majority A_m has R(f_m)→R*. Text after theorem incorrectly says “arbitrary compact F” although theorem assumes cone.

4.3 finite-dimensional multiclass: X=R^d,Y=[k], linear predictors Theta=[theta_1...theta_{k-1}], theta_k=0. True conditional p_Theta uses link sigma with consistency (14): score maximizers iff probability maximizers. Logistic link example. Repeated labels, majority Y_i^+ has link rho_m; claimed rho_m satisfies (14). Fit logistic loss (15); L_m gradient condition E[X( sigma^lr(Theta_m^T X)-rho_m(Theta*^T X))^T]=0. For k=2, Gaussian X and mis-specified link, prior result gives Theta_m=t_m Theta*, so classification consistent for any m. For k≥3 slight mis-specification: define T_epsilon of Lebesgue measure epsilon and sigma^epsilon formula logistic outside T_epsilon, uniform inside; prose says opposite (internal contradiction). Claim sigma^epsilon clearly satisfies link consistency (14), but uniform part violates iff for non-tied scores. Prop.5/current: for k≥3, Sigma=I, and invertibility of linear map M↦DM=E[Z(∇sigma^lr(Theta*^T Z)MZ)^T], exists eps0 such that for any eps∈(0,eps0) there is T_eps with Lebesgue measure ≤eps and normalized unaggregated minimizer Theta_1(eps)/||Theta_1(eps)|| differs from Theta*/||Theta*||. Theorem 3/current: for general true link sigma satisfying (14), with L_{m,sigma}, Theta_m=argmin, and Theta*=U*T* with U* orthogonal and T* nonsingular, ∃T_m such that Theta_m=U*T_m for every m, ||T_m||→∞ and T_m/||T_m||→T*/||T*||. Text says majority aggregation gives asymptotic consistency in mis-specified models, contrasting Prop.5 inconsistency without aggregation for k≥3.

Sec.5 numerical illustrations: claims two experiments support theory. Binary truncated quadratic/squared hinge phi(delta)=max{1−delta,0}^2, nonaggregated calibration psi(eps)=eps^2. For majority vote, with delta=1, alpha=0,C_MT=1, gives psi_m(eps)=1/16 (eps − sqrt(32/m log 40))_+, comparing psi(R−R*)≤surrogate excess and psi_m(R−R*)≤aggregated surrogate excess. Says curves become more linear as m→∞. Multiclass k=3,d=2 logistic mis-specification: corrupted link tilde sigma(t)=softmax(t) for ||t||≤r and softmax(alpha t) for ||t||>r; r=3, alpha=.1, theta1*=(0,1), theta2*=(1,1). Claims Fig.2 shows asymptotic consistency as m→∞. Caption’s plotted error formula incorrectly uses || ||T_m|| − T*/||T*|| ||, conflicting with Theorem 3’s normalized direction T_m/||T_m||→T*/||T*||.

Sec.6 discussion: frames contribution as evidence of limits of uncleaned/unaggregated labels and robustness from cleaning. Notes many consistency results take m→∞; finite-m guarantees exist for ranking Sec.3.1, more finite-m surrogate theory proposed. Says noise condition number kappa characterizes multiclass comparison inequalities; binary has kappa=1, but multiclass kappa can be large even with alpha≈1. Says mis-specified-model results, especially Sec.4.3, require optimal predictability (Bayes-optimal classifier in F); moving beyond is future work. Suggests extending aggregation comparison inequalities to restricted hypothesis classes/H-consistency; cites smooth convex loss quadratic growth of psi rate optimal.

Introduction key claims:
- Modern supervised datasets often require cleaning/filtering/crowdsourcing multiple labels and denoising; paper investigates how data aggregation improves consistency of fitted models.
- Main thesis: label cleaning/aggregating labels provides robustness impossible without aggregation.
- Two faces of robustness:
  1. Improved consistency of estimation: when minimizing surrogate losses (e.g. multiclass logistic) instead of task losses (e.g. zero-one error), aggregated-label procedures can achieve consistent/optimal prediction in the limit when impossible without aggregation.
  2. Even in finite-dimensional statistical problems, aggregation can provide consistent classifiers when standard methods fail.
- Motivating questions: whether aggregation is needed for surrogate consistency, and if it helps, in what sense.
- Paper proposes concrete examples in ranking and binary/multiclass classification with linear estimators where estimators using only pairs (X,Y) necessarily fail but label aggregation yields consistency.
- Develops new notions/theory for surrogate consistency with data aggregation.
- In fully nonparametric scenarios, shows how number of aggregated samples combines with noise conditions to improve consistency.
- Claims aggregation permits surrogate risk consistency under only weak conditions on the surrogate loss; losses using aggregated labels admit approximate linear comparison inequalities.
- Unlike conventional risk consistency theory requiring hypothesis class F of all measurable functions, paper will show classification results where aggregating labels guarantees consistency even over restricted hypothesis classes, which may fail without aggregation.

Background mentioned:
- Surrogate risk consistency literature: Bartlett/Jordan/McAuliffe characterized binary convex surrogate consistency for zero-one error; further work in multilabel, ranking, structured prediction, ordinal regression, restricted classes, general theory.
- Existing analyses typically assume standard supervised pairs (X,Y) and do not address aggregation machinery.

Section 2.1 Label aggregation:
- Instead of output Y, observe abstract Z∈Z. Example: multiple noisy labels for each X, Z=(Y1,…,Ym)∈Y^m.

- Example 1 Majority vote/repeated sampling: Z=(Y1,…,Ym), Yi|X=x iid P_{Y|X=x}. Define A(Z)=argmin_{y∈Y}∑_{l=1}^m ell(y,Y_l). For 0-1 loss ell(yhat,y)=1{y≠yhat}, this is majority vote; general form allows abstract procedures.

grade.reason: Yes — report 9 points out the same issue: Theorem 2’s assumptions require F to be a cone, so the paper’s claim that it holds for an arbitrary compact hypothesis class is incorrect.

errors.claim: “For multiple independent comparisons Z=(Y_1,\ldots,Y_m) conditional on X, put m_{ij}=\sum_{y\in\mathcal Y^m}1\{y=(i,j)\}, …”
errors.location: this part, Section 3.1 ranking aggregation definition
errors.evidence: The same paragraph says the aggregation is for observed repeated comparisons “Z=(Y_1,\ldots,Y_m)” and then uses conditions such as “m_j=0 for some j” and ratios “m_{ij}/m_j” in A(Z).
errors.explanation: As written, m_{ij} sums over all possible tuples y∈Y^m and tests whether a tuple equals a single pair (i,j), so it is not an observed count from Z. This conflicts with the subsequent use of m_{ij},m_j as data-dependent counts for the observed repeated comparisons.

errors.claim: “\overline\psi_A(\epsilon)\coloneqq \inf_{s\in\mathbb R^d}\overline\psi_A(\epsilon,x).”
errors.evidence: Earlier in the same part, the analogous uniform calibration function is defined as “\overline\psi(\epsilon)\coloneqq \inf_{x\in\mathcal X}\psi(\epsilon,x).” Also \overline\psi_A(\epsilon,x) is already defined by an infimum over s: “\overline\psi_A(\epsilon,x)\coloneqq \inf_{s\in\mathbb R^d}\{...\}.”
errors.explanation: The displayed definition of \overline\psi_A(ε) takes an infimum over s of an expression that no longer contains s but still contains x. This conflicts with both the immediately preceding pointwise definition and the earlier uniform definition, which require an infimum over x.

errors.claim: “The crude bound … lower bounds the promised ξ_{m,k} by setting ξ_{m,k}:= …”
errors.evidence: Theorem 1 gives the comparison only when R(f)-R* is at least ξ=… and defines ξ_m as an infimum over M. Corollary 3.3 then says every f with R(f)-R*≥ξ_{m,k} satisfies the comparison.
errors.explanation: For Corollary 3.3 to follow from Theorem 1, ξ_{m,k} must be an upper bound on an admissible threshold/ξ_m, not a lower bound. If it were only a lower bound, R(f)-R*≥ξ_{m,k} would not imply the theorem’s required condition.

errors.claim: “Assume … condition (Nα), with α∈[0,1]” together with threshold exponent “1/(1−α)” and later “at α=1, … gives ξ_{m,k}=0”
errors.location: this part, Theorem 1 and following discussion
errors.evidence: Theorem 1 defines ξ using “(4 C_MT e_m(M))^{1/(1−α)}” and ξ_{m,k} also has exponents with denominators involving “1−α” or “1−α^2”. Later the text says “at α=1, m≥… gives ξ_{m,k}=0”.
errors.explanation: The displayed formulas are undefined at α=1 because they divide by zero, while the theorem explicitly allows α=1 and the subsequent paragraph assigns a finite zero threshold at α=1. The α=1 claim does not follow from the displayed ξ formulas as written.

errors.claim: “Low noise permits a comparison written as ψ(R(f)−R*)≤R_φ(f)−R*”
errors.evidence: Definition 3.2 immediately defines the comparison as “ψ(R(f)−R*)≤ R_{φ,A}(f)−R_{φ,A}*.” Earlier notes likewise record surrogate comparisons as using surrogate excess risk, e.g. “ψ(R(f)−R*)≤R_phi(f)−R_phi*.”
errors.explanation: The paragraph subtracts the task optimum R* from the surrogate risk R_φ(f), whereas the paper’s own definitions use surrogate excess risk R_{φ,A}(f)−R_{φ,A}*. This is an internal mismatch in the stated comparison.

errors.claim: “R(f)-R^\star\leq 16N\bigl(R_{\varphi,A_n}(f)-R_{\varphi,A_n}^\star\bigr).”
errors.evidence: The same display uses aggregation count “m” in the threshold, and earlier notes record Theorem 1/Cor. 3.3 as applying to “A_m” with aggregation count m: “If φ W3C, A_m J9P…” and “if R−R*≥ξ_{m,k}, same linear comparison.”
errors.explanation: The bound switches from the aggregation size m to A_n without defining n or changing the aggregation count. Internally, the statement should be about the same aggregated surrogate indexed by m.

errors.claim: “every measurable f … satisfying [threshold without a leading 4] also satisfies …”
errors.location: this part, structured prediction consistency after Lemma 3.3
errors.evidence: Earlier notes record Cor. 3.3 for k≥3 as using a threshold with a leading factor 4: “otherwise 4*(32 C_MT^4/m log(4k(C1+C2)/C1))^{α/[2(1−α^2)]}.” The matching specialization in this same part also has “4·(32 C_MT^4/m log(...))^{...}.”
errors.explanation: The structured prediction bound is presented as an application of the same W3C/J9P result, but it drops the leading factor 4 that appears both in the general corollary and in the matching specialization immediately above.

errors.claim: “R(f)-R^\star\leq \frac8{\min_{\hat y\neq y}\ell(\hat y,y)}\bigl(R_{\varphi,A_m}(f)-R_{\varphi,A_m}^\star\bigr).”
errors.location: this part, structured prediction consistency after Lemma 3.3
errors.evidence: Earlier notes record Theorem 1/Cor. 3.3 as giving slope “16/C1”. Lemma 3.3 in this part states “C_{φ,1}=min_{\hat y\neq y} ell(\hat y,y).”
errors.explanation: Substituting Lemma 3.3’s C1 into the theorem gives 16/min loss, not 8/min loss. The displayed constant conflicts with the paper’s earlier theorem.

errors.claim: “The conditional distribution on Y… samples Y∼σ^lr(t) if t∈T_ε and uniformly otherwise.”
errors.evidence: Immediately before, the paper defines σ^ε(t)=σ^lr(t)1{t∉T_ε}+(1/k)1·1{t∈T_ε}.
errors.explanation: The formula says the distribution is logistic outside T_ε and uniform inside T_ε, but the prose states the reverse.

errors.claim: “The link satisfies ordering consistency and K7M.”
errors.evidence: The same part defines σ^ε(t)=σ^lr(t) outside T_ε and uniform on T_ε. Earlier notes define ordering consistency as: with t_k=0, t_y=max_i t_i iff σ_y(t)=max_i σ_i(t).
errors.explanation: On T_ε the link is uniform, so every class has maximal probability regardless of which coordinate(s) of t are maximal. Thus the stated ordering-consistency condition fails for any t∈T_ε with a non-tied maximum.

errors.claim: “plotted classification-rule error is $\left\|\|T_m\|-T^\star/\|T^\star\|\right\|$ against label count.”

final_notes:
Paper title: “Some Robustness Properties of Label Cleaning” by Chen Cheng and John Duchi.

Framework: iid (X,Y). Scores f:X→R^d decoded by d; task risk R(f)=E ell(d∘f(X),Y). Aggregated surrogate R_{φ,A}(f)=E φ(f(X),A(Z)); repeated labels Z=(Y1,...,Ym) iid conditional on X. Majority/T4K aggregation chooses empirical task-risk minimizer/plurality.

Section 3 consistency: Q7D/calibration via conditional excesses. Uniform comparison: ψ(R−R*)≤ surrogate excess. Prop 1: convex φ:R^k×Y→R fails Q7D for ranking k≥3. Prop 2: squared loss to aggregated comparisons Q7D for ranking when m≥k; possible formula error for m_ij. Prop 3: φ Q7D iff overlineψ_A(ε,x)>0; ψ_A=(overlineψ_A)** comparison; possible bad formula for uniform overlineψ_A.

W3C/J9P: finite labels card(Y)=k. J9P outputs empirical task-risk minimizer; eventually empirical argmin subset of population minimizers. W3C constants C1,C2. Theorem 1: If φ W3C, A_m J9P, 0≤ell≤1, Nα, then above threshold get R−R* ≤ 16/C1 surrogate excess. ξ_m→0 for α<1; α=0 asymptotic consistency. Existing issue: formulas divide by 1−α though α=1 allowed; later α=1 says ξ=0. Cor 3.3 threshold for k=2 and k≥3; slope 16/C1. Existing issue: text says crude bound “lower bounds” ξ but corollary needs upper bound. U6A level-(ξ,ζ) consistency: ψ(ε)≥ζε for ε≥ξ and ψ(R−R*)≤surrogate excess; earlier paragraph had wrong target excess.

Noise/gaps: Δ=min incorrect excess; binary Δ=|2η−1|. Nα: P(d∘f≠d∘f*)≤C_MT(R−R*)^α. Mβ: P(Δ≤ε)≤(C_MT ε)^β. κ=max/min incorrect excess; binary κ=1 if P(Δ>0)=1. e_m(t)=t sqrt{(2/m)log(4k(C1+C2)/C1)}.

Examples: binary nonsmooth Lemma 3.1 W3C constants C1=φ(0)−φ(δ), C2=φ(−δ). Matching: W3C C1=1/N,C2=2, k=N!, threshold log 4k(2N+1), slope 16N; display used A_n instead of A_m (inconsistency). Structured A3J max-margin: Lemma 3.3 W3C with C1=min ell(hat,y), C2=max τ(y)+1; binary embedding and loss gives C2=2. Structured consistency display possible errors: threshold lacks leading 4; slope 8/min ell though theorem gives 16/min ell; sloppy/free y in max/min.

Section 4 restricted/parametric models. Proposition 4: for every ε>0 and nonzero θ*, some distribution P on (X,Y) satisfies K7M along θ*, yet every unaggregated surrogate minimizer θ_φ has strictly higher task risk than θ* and is nearly orthogonal: |cos angle(θ_φ,θ*)|≤ε; holds for any nonnegative loss φ. Binary setting: Y={±1}, ell(d(s),y)=1{ys≤0}, margin surrogate φ(s,y)=φ(sy) for convex nonnegative scalar φ, X=R^d, F={x↦<θ,x>}. K7M/optimal predictability: sign(<θ*,x>)=sign(P(Y=1|x)−1/2), so f_{θ*} minimizes task risk over all measurable functions. Cor 4.1 says, as corollary to Theorem 2, if P satisfies K7M along θ* and ε_m→0, then aggregated approximate minimizers satisfy risk convergence and cos angle(θ_m,θ*)→1. Note: theorem statement only explicitly gives risk convergence, so angle convergence may rely on binary linear proof/unstated uniqueness.

Theorem 2: Let cone F satisfy K7M for P and P(Δ(X)>0)=1. For ε_m→0, every aggregated surrogate ε_m-argmin over F satisfies R(f_m)→R*. Multiclass setup: Y=[k], zero-one loss, decoder argmax_y s_y; F cone with f(x)^T1=0 and closed under positive scaling. Surrogate nonnegative, Q7D, and limiting condition φ(s,y)→0 if s_y−s_j→+∞ for all j≠y. Aggregation T4K; population maximizer y*(x)=argmax_y P(Y=y|x) unique. Multiclass K7M requires argmax f_y(x) in population argmax for every x. Examples satisfying limiting condition: multiclass logistic and pairwise convex nonincreasing losses with inf φ=0.

Section 4.3 finite-dimensional multiclass. Proposition 5: k≥3, Σ=I, Gaussian Z, small corruption set T_ε of Lebesgue measure ≤ε can make Θ_1(ε)/||Θ_1(ε)|| ≠ Θ*/||Θ*||. Paper title: “Some Robustness Properties of Label Cleaning” by Chen Cheng and John Duchi. Thesis: label aggregation/cleaning can give robustness/consistency unavailable from raw labels.

Core setup/results: task risk R Eq.1, generalized risk Eq.2, surrogate R_φ, aggregation A(Z) risk R_{φ,A} Eq.3. Consistency/calibration for all measurable f: Fisher and uniform comparison via pointwise ψ/overlineψ. Ranking: no convex pairwise-label φ Fisher consistent for k≥3, but aggregation with enough comparisons+squared loss is Fisher consistent. Prop.3: φ Fisher consistent iff pointwise aggregated calibration positive; comparison if biconjugate positive. Eq.(5) likely typo: uniform defined as inf_s overlineψ_A(ε,x), should be inf_x.

Identifying finite-label surrogates: Def.3.1 constants C1,C2 and labels satisfying (6a),(6b). Binary hinge (1,2)-identifying. Generalized majority A_m; Cor.3.2: m(n)→∞ and identifying φ gives task consistency from aggregated surrogate optimality. Level-(ξ,ζ) consistency; opening paragraph had inconsistent ψ≤R_φ(f)−R* instead of surrogate excess. Noise Nα/Mβ, κ, e_m. Theorem 1: identifying φ, A_m, bounded loss, Nα: above threshold, R−R*≤(16/C1)(aggregated surrogate excess), ξ_m→0. Cor.3.3 gives ξ_{m,k}; α=1 and m=O(log k) gives ξ=0 and linear comparison. Examples: binary margin Lemma 3.1 C1=φ(0)−φ(δ), C2=φ(−δ); matching structured hinge C1=1/N,C2=2, comparison constant 16N, text printed A_n likely should be A_m; structured prediction Lemma 3.3 C1 should be global min loss, C2=max τ+1; final specialization omitted factor 4 and printed 8/min ell instead of Cor.3.3’s 16/C1.

Section 4 restricted classes. 4.1 binary: Y={±1}, zero-one ell(d(s),y)=1{ys≤0}; convex margin φ. All measurable consistency iff φ′(0)<0. Linear f_θ. Optimally predictable along θ*: sign(<θ*,x>)=sign(P(Y=1|x)−1/2), then θ* is Bayes. Prop.4: for any ε>0 and nonzero θ*, ∃P optimally predictable along θ* such that every surrogate minimizer has higher task risk than θ* and |cos angle(θ_φ,θ*)|≤ε. Aggregation remedy: majority A_m; Cor.4.1: if optimally predictable and θ_m ε_m-argmin aggregated risk, then R(f_{θ_m})→R(f_{θ*}) and cos→1.

4.2 multiclass: F cone, sum-zero scores, zero-one/argmax. Surrogate φ Fisher consistent and limiting condition (13). Logistic and pairwise margins examples. Define F optimally predicts P if some f∈F predicts a Bayes label pointwise. Theorem 2: if F cone optimally predicts P and unique best label a.s., ε_m-argmins of aggregated majority-vote surrogate have R(f_m)→R*.

4.3 finite-dimensional multiclass linear models: X=R^d, Y=[k], θ_k=0. True Cat(p_Θ(x)) with link σ satisfying consistency (14): t_y=max_i t_i iff σ_y(t)=max_i σ_i(t). Logistic link example. Majority labels induce ρ_m; claims ρ_m satisfies (14). Logistic loss (15), gradient; majority logistic minimizer satisfies moment equation. Prior: binary Gaussian misspecification still Θ_m=t_mΘ*. For k≥3 slight misspecification causes inconsistency. Defines T_ε and σ^ε formula logistic outside T_ε, uniform inside; prose immediately reverses cases—internal error. Claim σ^ε satisfies (14) conflicts with uniform region. Prop.5: for k≥3, Gaussian, invertible map D, ∃ small ε and T_ε with measure≤ε such that Θ_1(ε) direction differs from Θ*. Theorem 3: for true link satisfying (14), if Θ*=U*T* with U* orthogonal and T* nonsingular, then ∃T_m with Θ_m=U*T_m, ||T_m||→∞, and T_m/||T_m||→T*/||T*||. Claims aggregation yields asymptotic robustness under misspecification; no aggregation generally inconsistent for k≥3.

Section 5 experiments. Exp1: binary truncated quadratic φ=max{1−δ,0}^2; nonaggregated ψ=ε^2. Majority aggregation with δ=1, no low-noise α=0,C_MT=1 gives ψ_m(ε)=1/16(ε−sqrt((32/m)log40))_+; compares ψ(R−R*)≤surrogate excess and ψ_m(R−R*)≤aggregated surrogate excess. Fig.1 m=2^16…2^32; aggregation transitions quadratic to linear; ψ_m conservative. Exp2: k=3,d=2 logistic regression with corrupted link logistic inside ||t||≤r and logistic(αt) outside, r=3, α=.1, Θ*: θ1=(0,1), θ2=(1,1). Fig.2 m={1,4,16,64,256,1024}; left n=10000 multilabeled obs per m, right n=640000/m, 100 trials. Fig.2 caption internal error: error shown as || ||T_m|| − T*/||T*|| ||, conflicting with theorem’s directional convergence T_m/||T_m||→T*/||T*||.

Section 6 discussion/future work: cites debate on noisy vs cleaned labels. Says many consistency results take m→∞; finite-m guarantees exist for ranking Sec.3.1, future work should characterize dependence on loss/surrogate and label count m, including higher-order comparisons. Notes κ in (9) characterizes comparison inequalities for multiclass; binary κ=1, but κ may be large even when Nα low (α≈1). Says mis-specified model results, especially 4.3, rely on optimal predictability/Bayes classifier in F; classical surrogate consistency can fail even then, aggregation can succeed. Future: beyond restricted scenarios; representation-learning surrogate forms. Also proposes restricted-class comparison inequalities with aggregation, linking nonparametric comparison and parametric consistency; H-consistency and whether aggregation can improve quadratic-growth limits for smooth convex losses.

Paper title: “Some Robustness Properties of Label Cleaning” by Chen Cheng and John Duchi.

Abstract claims:
- Learning procedures relying on aggregated/cleaned labels (label information distilled from noisy responses) have robustness properties impossible without data cleaning.
- In risk consistency with surrogate losses for task losses (e.g., convex surrogate instead of 0-1 misclassification), procedures using label aggregation obtain stronger consistency guarantees than possible using raw labels.
- Classical perfectly specified statistical models suggest using all information/modeling label uncertainty is statistically efficient, but consistency fails for “standard” approaches when the minimized loss is even slightly misspecified.
- Procedures leveraging aggregated information still converge to optimal classifiers with every fixed label count.
- Overall thesis: considering full pipeline from data collection to model fitting to prediction can yield more robust methodology by refining noisy signals.

Paper title: “Some Robustness Properties of Label Cleaning” by Chen Cheng and John Duchi.

Abstract + Introduction main thesis:
- Label cleaning/aggregation (distilling multiple noisy responses into label information/gold-standard labels) provides robustness impossible without aggregation.
- Two robustness aspects: (1) improved consistency for estimation when minimizing surrogate losses (e.g., multiclass logistic/convex surrogate) instead of task losses (e.g., 0-1 error); aggregated-label procedures can be consistent/optimal where raw-pair methods cannot. (2) In finite-dimensional statistical problems, aggregation can provide consistent classifiers when standard methods fail.
- Classical correctly specified models may suggest using all information/modeling label uncertainty is efficient, but consistency can fail for standard approaches when minimized loss is slightly misspecified; aggregation still converges to optimal classifiers with every fixed label count (from abstract).

Intro context and questions:
- Standard supervised theory assumes pairs (X,Y), with mature empirical process/surrogate consistency theory (Bartlett et al., etc.), but does not address modern data aggregation/crowdsourcing/denoising pipelines.
- Paper asks whether aggregation is needed, whether it helps consistency, and in what sense.

Claims about contributions/results to check later:
- Concrete examples in ranking and binary/multiclass classification with linear estimators where estimators using only pairs (X,Y) necessarily fail, but label aggregation methods yield consistency.
- Develops new notions/theory for surrogate consistency with data aggregation.
- In fully nonparametric scenarios, shows how number of aggregated samples combines with noise conditions to improve consistency.
- Aggregation allows surrogate risk consistency under only weak conditions on the surrogate loss; losses using aggregated labels admit approximate linear comparison inequalities.
- Unlike conventional risk consistency theory requiring hypothesis class F of all measurable functions, aggregation can guarantee consistency even over restricted hypothesis classes, which may fail without aggregation.

Paper title: “Some Robustness Properties of Label Cleaning” by Chen Cheng and John Duchi.

Main thesis from abstract/introduction:
- Label cleaning/aggregation (distilling multiple noisy responses into label information/gold-standard labels) gives robustness unavailable without aggregation.
- Two robustness aspects: (1) better consistency for estimation when minimizing surrogate losses (e.g. multiclass logistic/convex surrogate) instead of task losses; aggregated-label procedures can be consistent/optimal where raw-pair methods cannot. (2) In finite-dimensional statistical problems, aggregation can provide consistent classifiers when standard methods fail.
- Classical correctly specified models may suggest using all information/modeling label uncertainty is efficient, but consistency can fail for standard approaches when minimized loss is slightly misspecified; aggregation still converges to optimal classifiers with every fixed label count (abstract).
- Claimed contributions include concrete examples in ranking and binary/multiclass classification with linear estimators where pair-only estimators fail but aggregation succeeds; new notions/theory for surrogate consistency with aggregation; nonparametric scenarios showing aggregated samples plus noise conditions improve consistency; aggregated-label losses admit approximate linear comparison inequalities; aggregation can ensure consistency over restricted hypothesis classes where conventional theory often requires all measurable functions.

Section 2 preliminaries:
- Classical setup: i.i.d. pairs (X_i,Y_i)~P, scoring f:X→R^d, decoder d:R^d→Y, prediction yhat=d∘f(x). Task risk initially R(f)=E[ell(d∘f(X),Y)] (Eq. 1).
- Binary example: d=1, decoder sgn(s), loss ell(y,y’)=1{yy’≤0}, giving R(f)=P(Y f(X)≤0).
- They generalize task risk to allow loss depending on conditional distribution P(Y|X): R(f)=E[ell(d∘f(X), P(·|X))] (Eq. 2). Example multiclass: ell(yhat,P)=Σ_y P(Y=y)1{yhat≠y}, which equals standard 0-1 error.
- Surrogate loss without aggregation: φ:R^d×Y→R, surrogate risk R_φ(f)=E[φ(f(X),Y)]. Paper studies when minimizing surrogate is consistent with task risk (Eq. 2), in (i) Fisher consistency with F all Borel functions and (ii) parametric/statistical scenarios where F may be misspecified. Main message restated: label aggregation improves consistency in both.

Section 2.1 label aggregation:
- Instead of pair output Y, use abstract variable Z∈Z. Example repeated labels: Z=(Y_1,…,Y_m)∈Y^m. Aggregation space A (calligraphic), aggregating function A:Z→A (e.g. majority vote), surrogate φ:R^d×A→R_+. Aggregated surrogate risk R_{φ,A}(f)=E[φ(f(X),A(Z))] (Eq. 3). Question: when minimizing Eq. 3 suffices to minimize actual task risk Eq. 2.
- Example 1 Majority vote/repeated sampling: Z=(Y_1,…,Y_m), Y_i|X=x iid~P_{Y|X=x}. Define A_m(Z)=argmin_{y∈Y} Σ_{l=1}^m ell(y,Y_l). For 0-1 loss ell(yhat,y)=1{y≠yhat}, this is majority vote; more general form allows abstract procedures.
- Example 2 K-nearest-neighbor aggregation (rough population-level version): an example X comes with label Y plus additional iid draws (X_i,Y_i)_{i=1}^m~P, so Z=(Y,(X_i,Y_i)_{i=1}^m). Order X_i by distance to X as X_(1),…,X_(m), with X_(0)=X. For K≥0 aggregate K nearest neighbors plus the original point via A_{m,K}(Z)=argmin_{y∈Y} Σ_{l=0}^K ell(y,Y_(l)). Appendix C later extends to aggregation from a single sample (X_i,Y_i)_{i=1}^n.

Paper title: “Some Robustness Properties of Label Cleaning” by Chen Cheng and John Duchi.

Main thesis: Label aggregation/cleaning can provide robustness/consistency unavailable from raw paired labels, including surrogate consistency and finite-dimensional statistical consistency under misspecification. Aggregation may be consistent/optimal where raw-pair methods fail.

Section 2 preliminaries:
- Classical iid pairs (X,Y), score f:X→R^d, decoder d, task risk R(f)=E[ell(d∘f(X),Y)] (Eq.1). Binary example R(f)=P(Y f(X)≤0).
- Generalized task risk allows loss depending on conditional distribution: R(f)=E[ell(d∘f(X),P(·|X))] (Eq.2). Multiclass 0-1 example.
- Surrogate without aggregation: φ:R^d×Y→R, R_φ(f)=E[φ(f(X),Y)]. Study consistency for Eq.2 both in all-measurable Fisher setting and restricted/statistical settings.

Section 2.1 aggregation:
- Abstract output Z, aggregation space A, aggregator A:Z→A, surrogate φ:R^d×A→R_+, aggregated surrogate risk R_{φ,A}(f)=E[φ(f(X),A(Z))] (Eq.3).
- Example 1 repeated labels: Z=(Y_1,…,Y_m), conditionally iid; A_m(Z)=argmin_y Σ_l ell(y,Y_l), majority vote for 0-1.
- Example 2 KNN aggregation population version: Z=(Y,(X_i,Y_i)_{i=1}^m), order neighbors of X with X_(0)=X; A_{m,K}=argmin_y Σ_{l=0}^K ell(y,Y_(l)). Appendix C handles single-sample aggregation.

Section 3 surrogate consistency:
- Standard framework assumes F all Borel f:X→R^d. Conditional task risk R(s|x)=ell(d∘s,P(Y∈·|X=x)); conditional surrogate R_φ(s|x)=E[φ(s,Y)|X=x]. Pointwise excess δ_ell, δ_φ defined vs inf over s′∈R^d. Minimal risks R*=inf_F R, R_φ*=inf_F R_φ.
- Consistency notions for all distributions: (i) Fisher: R_φ(f_n)→R_φ* implies R(f_n)→R*. (ii) Uniform comparison: nondecreasing ψ with ψ(ε)>0 for ε>0 and ψ(R(f)-R*)≤R_φ(f)-R_φ* for all f. For binary margin convex, notions coincide. Strong guarantee may not always hold.
- Calibration: ψ(ε,x)=inf_s{δ_φ(s,x):δ_ell(s,x)≥ε}; overlineψ(ε)=inf_x ψ(ε,x). Cor.3.1: φ Fisher consistent iff ψ(ε,x)>0 for all x,ε>0. If ψ is Fenchel biconjugate of overlineψ, overlineψ(ε)>0 iff ψ(ε)>0, and comparison inequality holds for all measurable f.
- Authors say paired-observation consistency generally impossible; aggregation theory needed in Sec.3.2.

Section 3.1 ranking failure without aggregation:
- Ranking k items from pairwise comparisons Y={(i,j):i≠j,1≤i,j≤k}, where (i,j)=item i ranked higher than j. For each x probabilities p_ij=P(Y=(i,j)|x).
- Define normalized transition matrix C_x∈R_+^{k×k}: diagonal 0; for i≠j, (C_x)_ij=p_ij/Σ_{l≠j}p_lj, with 0/0=1/(k-1), so C_x^T 1=1. Rank items by C_x 1 (row sums), interpreted as how often an item is preferred.
- Task loss (decoder incorporated): ell(s,C)=max_{i<j}1{(s_i-s_j)(e_i-e_j)^T C1≤0, (e_i-e_j)^T C1≠0}, penalizing misordered scores. Population task risk Eq.(4): R(f)=P(f(X) and C_X 1 order differently).
- For convex surrogate φ:R^k×Y→R, restrict scores to s^T1=0 (ordering invariant). Proposition 1: for k≥3, no convex φ in first argument is Fisher consistent for ranking task risk (4). Proof in Appendix A.1.
- Aggregation can restore consistency if number of collected pairwise comparisons m≥k. Assume Z=(Y_1,…,Y_m) conditionally iid. Define counts m_ij and m_j=Σ_i m_ij; aggregator A(Z)=star if any m_j=0, otherwise vector over i: (m_i1/m_1 + m_i2/m_2 + … + m_ik/m_k). Text says regress scores f(x) on frequencies of label orderings and Proposition 2 will show consistency (proof Appendix A.2). Note possible formula issue: part writes m_ij=Σ_{y∈Y^m}1{y=(i,j)}, which seems not to depend on Z; likely intended count among components Y_l.

Theorem 2: if F cone optimally predicts P, P(Δ(X)>0)=1 (unique best label), ε_m→0, then any ε_m-argmin of aggregated majority-vote surrogate risk has R(f_m)→R*. Used to justify Cor.4.1.

Repeated labels, majority Y_i^+=A_m, induces p_{Θ,m} via ρ_m; claims ρ_m satisfies (14). Logistic loss (15); gradient −x(1{y=i}−σ_i^lr). Population majority logistic minimizer Θ_m satisfies E[X(σ^lr(Θ_m^TX)−ρ_m(Θ*^TX))^T]=0. Prior result: for k=2 Gaussian X, even misspecified link gives Θ_m=t_mΘ*, so binary classification consistent regardless of aggregation. For k≥3 slight misspecification causes inconsistency. Paper title: “Some Robustness Properties of Label Cleaning” by Chen Cheng and John Duchi.

Main claims: label aggregation/cleaning gives robustness; convex/typical surrogate losses with cleaned labels yield stronger task-risk consistency than raw labels; finite-dimensional classifiers remain consistent under loss misspecification where uncertainty-modeling fails; if perfectly specified, all info is more efficient but slight misspecification destroys standard consistency; aggregation retains convergence for fixed label count; constructions in ranking/binary/multiclass separate pair-only from aggregation; nonparametric results combine aggregation counts/noise conditions and allow approximate linear comparison inequalities.

Section 2: Data iid (X,Y). Scores f:X→R^d decoded by d:R^d→Y. Task risk instantaneous or distribution-dependent. Aggregated surrogate risk R_{φ,A}(f)=E φ(f(X),A(Z)), evaluated against original task risk. Repeated labels Z=(Y_1,…,Y_m), aggregation A_m empirical risk minimizer/majority vote. Rough KNN aggregation includes original Y and K neighbors.

Section 3: Conditional risks/excesses/calibration ψ. Q7D positivity gives consistency; Fenchel-biconjugate comparison ψ(R−R*)≤surrogate excess for measurable f. Pair-only Q7D generally impossible. Ranking Prop 1: k≥3 outcomes, every convex φ:R^k×Y→R fails Q7D. Prop 2: squared regression with aggregation and m≥k is Q7D. Earlier internal error: m_ij definition sums over y∈Y^m rather than observed labels. Prop 3: if integrable b bounds δ_ell, φ Q7D iff aggregated calibration positive for every x,ε; ψ_A comparison. Eq.(5) printed global overlineψ_A(ε)=inf_s overlineψ_A(ε,x) inconsistent with earlier uniform inf_x. Cor 3.2: if m(n)→∞ and φ W3C, aggregated surrogate excess→0 implies task excess→0.

Finite label space card(Y)=k. J9P generalized majority vote: A_m returns a_{ŷ}, empirical task-risk minimizer, arbitrary ties. W3C identifying surrogate: constants C1,C2, parameters a_y and scores s_y with d(s_y)=y and separation conditions; no convexity/unaggregated consistency/argmax decoder required. Binary hinge constants (1,2). Theorem 1: for W3C φ, J9P A_m, bounded ell, noise Nα, if task excess ≥ 2P(κ>M)+(4 C_MT e_m(M))^{1/(1−α)}, then task excess ≤16/C1 times aggregated surrogate excess. Potential errors: formulas divide by zero at α=1 but later claims α=1 gives ξ=0; explicit ξ_{m,k} called lower bound despite being used as sufficient threshold. Cor 3.3: every f with excess≥ξ_{m,k} satisfies comparison; α=1 stated ξ=0 under m=O(log k). Definition 3.2 U6A: level-(ξ,ζ) consistency; sentence before incorrectly writes ψ(R−R*)≤R_φ(f)−R* rather than aggregated surrogate excess.

Noise/gaps: Δ(x)=min nonoptimal conditional task regret; binary |2P(Y=1|X=x)−1|. Nα: P(d∘f≠d∘f*)≤C_MT(R−R*)^α. Mβ: P(Δ≤ε)≤(C_MT ε)^β; equivalent β=α/(1−α). κ=max incorrect δ/min incorrect δ; binary κ=1 if P(Δ>0)=1. e_m(t)=t sqrt[2/m log(4k(C1+C2)/C1)]. Discussion later reiterates binary κ=1 and beyond binary κ can be large even under low noise/α≈1.

Examples: Lemma 3.1 binary nonsmooth/margin surrogate W3C constants C1=φ(0)−φ(δ), C2=φ(−δ). Matching: W3C C1=1/N,C2=2; labels perfect matchings k=N!, consistency count O(N log N); printed risk uses A_n though aggregation count m/A_m elsewhere. Structured hinge A3J W3C C1=min ell, C2=max τ+1; if v∈{0,1}^d and ell normalized Hamming then C2=2. Structured consequence prints threshold without theorem’s leading 4 and slope 8/min ell, inconsistent with theorem/corollary requiring prefactor 4 and slope 16/C1.

Section 4 restricted/parametric. Prop 4: for any ε>0 and nonzero θ*, some binary linear P satisfies K7M along θ*, but every unaggregated surrogate minimizer has higher task risk than θ* and nearly orthogonal. Theorem 2: cone F satisfying K7M and P(Δ>0)=1; ε_m-argmins of aggregated risk with T4K satisfy R(f_m)→R*. Cor 4.1 internally overclaims cos angle(θ_m,θ*)→1; Theorem 2 only supports risk convergence.

Section 4.3 multiclass finite-dimensional. Model: X∈R^d, Y=[k], Θ d×(k−1), θ_k=0; p_Θ(x)=[σ(<θ_1,x>,…,<θ_{k−1},x>);1−1^Tσ]. Ordering consistency: t_y maximal iff σ_y(t) maximal. Logistic link σ_i^lr=e^{t_i}/(1+Σ_{j<k}e^{t_j}). Prop 5: k≥3, Gaussian X, under invertibility, for arbitrarily small perturbation set T_ε measure ≤ε, unaggregated logistic minimizer direction Θ_1(ε)/||Θ_1(ε)|| differs from Θ*/||Θ*||. Theorem 3: if Θ*=U*T*, for each m exists T_m with Θ_m=U*T_m, ||T_m||→∞ and T_m/||T_m||→T*/||T*||; aggregation recovers optimal linear predictor asymptotically under ordering consistency.

Part 9 numerical illustrations. D4X/squared hinge φ(δ)=max{1−δ,0}^2 has unaggregated ψ(ε)=ε^2. With δ=1, α=0, C_MT=1, binary lemma gives aggregated ψ_m(ε)=1/16(ε−sqrt((32/m)log40))_+. Figure 1 uses m={2^16,2^20,2^24,2^28,2^32}. Mis-specified logistic experiment: corrupted link \tildeσ(t)=softmax(t) for ||t||≤r and softmax(αt) outside; n=10000 fixed in one experiment, n=640000/m in constant total-label experiment; d=2,k=3, θ1*=(0,1), θ2*=(1,1), r=3, α=.1, m={1,4,16,64,256,1024}, 100 trials. New internal error: Figure 2 says plotted classification-rule error is || ||T_m|| − T*/||T*|| ||, but earlier theorem and consistency claim require comparing normalized directions T_m/||T_m|| to T*/||T*||.

Discussion/future work: notes collection debate—uncleaned labels more statistically efficient if uncertainty model correct; cleaning robust under misspecification. Open issues: finite-m theory beyond current ranking guarantees; fundamental limits of B2Z/κ for multiclass; mis-specified-model results require K7M/Bayes-optimal classifier in F; extend aggregation comparisons to restricted-class/H-consistency settings.

final_notes:
Paper title: “Some Robustness Properties of Label Cleaning” by Chen Cheng and John Duchi.

Main setup: task risk R(f)=E ell(d∘f(X),Y) or E ell(d∘f(X),P(.|X)); surrogate risk R_phi(f)=E phi(f(X),Y). Aggregation observes Z and A:Z→A, aggregated surrogate risk R_{phi,A}=E phi(f(X),A(Z)).

Sec.3 consistency: F all Borel. Fisher consistency iff pointwise calibration psi>0. Prop.3 aggregation: phi Fisher consistent for task iff aggregated calibration positive; comparison psi_A(R(f)-R*)≤R_{phi,A}(f)-R_{phi,A}*. Ranking: without aggregation convex score surrogates inconsistent for k≥3; with repeated comparisons aggregated to wins vector, squared loss Fisher consistent if m≥k. Identifying surrogates: Def.3.1 (C_phi,1,C_phi,2)-identifying via margins; binary hinge (1,2). Generalized majority vote A_m. Cor.3.2: m(n)→∞ and identifying => aggregated surrogate excess→0 implies task excess→0. Level-(xi,zeta) consistency has comparison to aggregated surrogate excess; earlier formula typo used R_phi(f)-R*. Noise: Delta=min excess conditional risk for wrong prediction; binary Delta=|2P(Y=1|X)-1|. Mammen-Tsybakov Nα/Mβ equivalence claimed via β=α/(1−α) (α=1 issue). Condition number kappa; e_m(t)=t sqrt((2/m)log(4k(C1+C2)/C1)). Theorem 1: if R−R* ≥ 2P(kappa>M)+(4 C_MT e_m(M))^{1/(1−α)}, then R−R*≤(16/C1) aggregated surrogate excess; xi_m is inf threshold, xi_m→0. κ is defined independently of m; m reduces e_m/threshold, not κ itself. Cor.3.3 thresholds: binary (32 C_MT²/m log(8(C1+C2)/C1))^{1/[2(1−α)]}; k≥3: 4*(32 C_MT^4/m log(4k(C1+C2)/C1))^{α/[2(1−α²)]}. Text later says α=1 with m large gives xi=0 though formulas undefined.

Examples: binary nonsmooth margin: Lemma 3.1 feasible C1=phi(0)-phi(delta), C2=phi(-delta); comparison 16/C1. Bipartite matching: k=N!, loss normalized Hamming; structured hinge C1=1/N,C2=2; threshold includes 4*(32 C_MT^4/m log(4k(2N+1)))^{α/[2(1−α²)]}; comparison should be 16N times aggregated excess, but text wrote A_n. General structured: Lemma 3.3 structured hinge C1=min loss, C2=max tau+1; if binary embeddings and normalized Hamming, tau=1,C2=2. Final specialization omitted leading 4 and used 8/C1 instead of 16/C1.

Sec.4 restricted classes. 4.1 binary: Y={±1}, zero-one ell=1{ys≤0}, margin varphi(s,y)=phi(sy), phi convex. All-measurable Fisher iff phi'(0)<0. Linear F={f_theta=<theta,x>}. Optimally predictable along theta*: sign matches Bayes sign. Prop.4: for any eps and nonzero theta*, ∃P optimally predictable along theta* such that all surrogate minimizers have larger task risk than theta* and |cos angle|≤eps. Notation issue: proposition uses E[phi(f_theta(X),Y)] although phi unary. Aggregation A_m majority: epsilon_m-argmin E[phi(A_m(Ys) f_theta(X))] yields R→R* and cos(theta_m,theta*)→1.

4.2 multiclass: Y=[k], zero-one, decoder argmax_y s_y. F linear cone with f^T1=0 and closed under positive scaling. Surrogate varphi Fisher consistent and limiting loss condition (13): varphi(s,y)→0 if s_y−s_j→∞ for all j≠y. Examples: multiclass logistic and pairwise margin losses with phi convex nonincreasing, phi'(0)<0, inf phi=0. Zhang theorem: such losses consistent over all measurable centered scores; binary margin included via f=(g,-g). Linear multiclass functions with sum_i theta_i=0 form convex cone. New definition: F optimally predicts P if ∃f∈F whose argmax lies in argmax of conditional class probabilities for all x. Theorem 2: if F cone optimally predicts P, P(Delta>0)=1, majority vote A_m, epsilon_m→0, then any epsilon_m-argmin of aggregated surrogate risk has R(f_m)→R*.
