Notation issue: proposition uses E[phi(f_theta(X),Y)] although phi unary. Aggregation A_m majority: epsilon_m-argmin E[phi(A_m(Ys) f_theta(X))] yields R→R* and cos(theta_m,theta*)→1.

4.2 multiclass: Y=[k], zero-one, decoder argmax_y s_y. F linear cone with f^T1=0 and closed under positive scaling. Surrogate varphi Fisher consistent and limiting loss condition (13): varphi(s,y)→0 if s_y−s_j→∞ for all j≠y. Examples: multiclass logistic and pairwise margin losses with phi convex nonincreasing, phi'(0)<0, inf phi=0. Zhang theorem: such losses consistent over all measurable centered scores; binary margin included via f=(g,-g). Linear multiclass functions with sum_i theta_i=0 form convex cone. New definition: F optimally predicts P if ∃f∈F whose argmax lies in argmax of conditional class probabilities for all x. Theorem 2: if F cone optimally predicts P, P(Delta>0)=1, majority vote A_m, epsilon_m→0, then any epsilon_m-argmin of aggregated surrogate risk has R(f_m)→R*. Text says this gives asymptotic consistency by aggregation and contrasts Prop.4.

4.3 finite-dimensional multiclass. X=R^d,Y=[k], linear predictors Θ=[θ1…θ_{k−1}], θ_k=0 convention. True categorical p_Θ(x) from link σ(t) with σ_k=1−1^Tσ and consistency condition (14): t_y=max_i t_i iff σ_y(t)=max_i σ_i(t), with t_k=0. Logistic link example. With repeated labels and majority vote Y_i^+, distribution p_{Θ,m} via ρ_m; text says ρ_m satisfies (14). Logistic loss (15), gradient, population L_m minimizer satisfies E[X(σ_lr(Θ_m^T X)−ρ_m(Θ*^T X))^T]=0. Claims for k=2 and Gaussian X, mis-specified link gives Θ_m=t_mΘ*, hence classification consistent for all m. For k≥3 slight misspecification causes failure. Defines T_ε of Lebesgue measure ε and σ^ε(t)=σ_lr(t) outside T_ε, uniform inside T_ε; prose incorrectly reverses this. Also claim σ^ε clearly satisfies (14) is false for t in T_ε unless ties. Defines L_{m,ε}, Θ_m(ε), notes Θ_1(0)=Θ*. Prop.5: for k≥3, Σ=I, assuming linear map M↦DM=E[Z(∇σ_lr(Θ*^T Z)MZ)^T] for Z~N(0,I_{k−1}) is invertible, ∃ε0>0 such that for any ε∈(0,ε0), ∃T_ε of Lebesgue measure ≤ε with Θ_1(ε)/||Θ_1(ε)|| ≠ Θ*/||Θ*||; proof in App.E.1. Then majority vote addresses inconsistency as m→∞ for any true link σ satisfying (14): define L_{m,σ}, Θ_m=argmin. Theorem3: if Θ*=U*T* with U*∈R^{d×(k−1)} orthogonal and T* nonsingular, then ∃T_m with Θ_m=U*T_m for every m, ||T_m||→∞ and T_m/||T_m||→T*/||T*||. Claimed as evidence of robustness/asymptotic consistency in misspecified models, contrasting Prop.5.

Sec.5 numerics. Experiment 1: binary truncated quadratic phi(δ)=max{1−δ,0}²; cites Bartlett calibration psi(ε)=ε². With majority vote and Lemma 3.1 δ=1, no low-noise α=0,C_MT=1: psi_m(ε)=1/16(ε−sqrt(32/m log 40))_+. This matches C1=phi(0)-phi(1)=1 and C2=phi(-1)=4. Figure 1 compares psi vs psi_m for m=2^16,…,2^32 and says aggregation moves quadratic toward linear, though theorem bound conservative. Experiment 2: logistic Sec.4.3 k=3,d=2 with corrupted link tildeσ(t)=σ_lr(t)1{||t||≤r}+σ_lr(αt)1{||t||>r}, r=3, α=0.1, θ1*=(0,1)^T, θ2*=(1,1)^T. Claims Fig.2 shows asymptotic consistency as m→∞. Caption gives erroneous classification error formula || ||T_m|| − T*/||T*|| ||, inconsistent with Theorem3 convergence T_m/||T_m||→T*/||T*||. Left: n=10000 multilabeled observations for each m. Right: n=640000/m so total labels fixed. 95% error bars over T=100 trials.

errors.claim: “This shows that increasing aggregation causally reduces the noise condition number in our setting”
errors.location: this part, Fundamental limits of the noise condition number
errors.evidence: Earlier notes: “Noise: ... Condition number kappa; ... Theorem 1: if R−R* ≥ 2P(kappa>M)+(4 C_MT e_m(M))^{1/(1−α)}, then ...; xi_m→0.” The notes record κ as a property used in the threshold, while the dependence on the number of aggregated labels m enters through e_m(t)=t sqrt((2/m)log(...)), not through κ itself.
errors.explanation: Within the paper’s earlier definitions/results, κ(X) is an intrinsic noise condition number of the multiclass problem and is not defined as changing with m. Increasing m reduces the aggregation error term e_m and hence the threshold xi_m, but the paper’s own theorem does not show that aggregation reduces κ(X).

grade.reason: The final reported error directly points out that the paper's theorem/definitions treat the noise condition number kappa as intrinsic and independent of aggregation m, and that increasing m only affects the aggregation error term e_m rather than kappa itself.

errors.claim: “For multiple independent comparisons Z=(Y_1,\ldots,Y_m) conditional on X, put m_{ij}=\sum_{y\in\mathcal Y^m}1\{y=(i,j)\}, …”
errors.location: this part, Section 3.1 ranking aggregation definition
errors.evidence: The same paragraph says the aggregation is for observed repeated comparisons “Z=(Y_1,\ldots,Y_m)” and then uses conditions such as “m_j=0 for some j” and ratios “m_{ij}/m_j” in A(Z).
errors.explanation: As written, m_{ij} sums over all possible tuples y∈Y^m and tests whether a tuple equals a single pair (i,j), so it is not an observed count from Z. This conflicts with the subsequent use of m_{ij},m_j as data-dependent counts for the observed repeated comparisons.

errors.claim: “\overline\psi_A(\epsilon)\coloneqq \inf_{s\in\mathbb R^d}\overline\psi_A(\epsilon,x).”
errors.evidence: Earlier in the same part, the analogous uniform calibration function is defined as “\overline\psi(\epsilon)\coloneqq \inf_{x\in\mathcal X}\psi(\epsilon,x).” Also \overline\psi_A(\epsilon,x) is already defined by an infimum over s: “\overline\psi_A(\epsilon,x)\coloneqq \inf_{s\in\mathbb R^d}\{...\}.”
errors.explanation: The displayed definition of \overline\psi_A(ε) takes an infimum over s of an expression that no longer contains s but still contains x. This conflicts with both the immediately preceding pointwise definition and the earlier uniform definition, which require an infimum over x.

errors.claim: “The crude bound … lower bounds the promised ξ_{m,k} by setting ξ_{m,k}:= …”
errors.evidence: Theorem 1 gives the comparison only when R(f)-R* is at least ξ=… and defines ξ_m as an infimum over M. Corollary 3.3 then says every f with R(f)-R*≥ξ_{m,k} satisfies the comparison.
errors.explanation: For Corollary 3.3 to follow from Theorem 1, ξ_{m,k} must be an upper bound on an admissible threshold/ξ_m, not a lower bound. If it were only a lower bound, R(f)-R*≥ξ_{m,k} would not imply the theorem’s required condition.

errors.claim: “Assume … condition (Nα), with α∈[0,1]” together with threshold exponent “1/(1−α)” and later “at α=1, … gives ξ_{m,k}=0”
errors.location: this part, Theorem 1 and following discussion
errors.evidence: Theorem 1 defines ξ using “(4 C_MT e_m(M))^{1/(1−α)}” and ξ_{m,k} also has exponents with denominators involving “1−α” or “1−α^2”. Later the text says “at α=1, m≥… gives ξ_{m,k}=0”.
errors.explanation: The displayed formulas are undefined at α=1 because they divide by zero, while the theorem explicitly allows α=1 and the subsequent paragraph assigns a finite zero threshold at α=1. The α=1 claim does not follow from the displayed ξ formulas as written.

errors.claim: “Low noise permits a comparison written as ψ(R(f)−R*)≤R_φ(f)−R*”
errors.evidence: Definition 3.2 immediately defines the comparison as “ψ(R(f)−R*)≤ R_{φ,A}(f)−R_{φ,A}*.” Earlier notes likewise record surrogate comparisons as using surrogate excess risk, e.g. “ψ(R(f)−R*)≤R_phi(f)−R_phi*.”
errors.explanation: The paragraph subtracts the task optimum R* from the surrogate risk R_φ(f), whereas the paper’s own definitions use surrogate excess risk R_{φ,A}(f)−R_{φ,A}*. This is an internal mismatch in the stated comparison.

errors.claim: “R(f)-R^\star\leq 16N\bigl(R_{\varphi,A_n}(f)-R_{\varphi,A_n}^\star\bigr).”
errors.evidence: The same display uses aggregation count “m” in the threshold, and earlier notes record Theorem 1/Cor. 3.3 as applying to “A_m” with aggregation count m: “If φ W3C, A_m J9P…” and “if R−R*≥ξ_{m,k}, same linear comparison.”
errors.explanation: The bound switches from the aggregation size m to A_n without defining n or changing the aggregation count. Internally, the statement should be about the same aggregated surrogate indexed by m.

errors.claim: “every measurable f … satisfying [threshold without a leading 4] also satisfies …”
errors.location: this part, structured prediction consistency after Lemma 3.3
errors.evidence: Earlier notes record Cor. 3.3 for k≥3 as using a threshold with a leading factor 4: “otherwise 4*(32 C_MT^4/m log(4k(C1+C2)/C1))^{α/[2(1−α^2)]}.” The matching specialization in this same part also has “4·(32 C_MT^4/m log(...))^{...}.”
errors.explanation: The structured prediction bound is presented as an application of the same W3C/J9P result, but it drops the leading factor 4 that appears both in the general corollary and in the matching specialization immediately above.

errors.claim: “R(f)-R^\star\leq \frac8{\min_{\hat y\neq y}\ell(\hat y,y)}\bigl(R_{\varphi,A_m}(f)-R_{\varphi,A_m}^\star\bigr).”
errors.location: this part, structured prediction consistency after Lemma 3.3
errors.evidence: Earlier notes record Theorem 1/Cor. 3.3 as giving slope “16/C1”. Lemma 3.3 in this part states “C_{φ,1}=min_{\hat y\neq y} ell(\hat y,y).”
errors.explanation: Substituting Lemma 3.3’s C1 into the theorem gives 16/min loss, not 8/min loss. The displayed constant conflicts with the paper’s earlier theorem.

errors.claim: “As a corollary to Theorem 2 ... the aggregated approximate minimizers satisfy ... cos angle(theta_m, theta*) -> 1.”
errors.evidence: Theorem 2 in this part concludes only that every aggregated approximate minimizer sequence “satisfies R(f_m) -> R^*.” It does not state convergence of parameters or directions.
errors.explanation: The directional conclusion is presented as following from Theorem 2, but the theorem as stated only gives risk consistency. The added claim that the cosine angle tends to 1 is not supported by, and overstates, the stated theorem.

errors.claim: “The conditional distribution on Y samples Y∼σ^lr(t) if t∈T_ε and uniformly otherwise.”
errors.evidence: Immediately before, the paper defines σ^ε(t)=σ^lr(t)1{t∉T_ε}+(1/k)1 1{t∈T_ε}.
errors.explanation: The displayed definition says the model is logistic outside T_ε and uniform inside T_ε, while the following sentence reverses these cases.

errors.claim: “The link satisfies ordering consistency and K7M.”
errors.evidence: The defined link is σ^ε(t)=σ^lr(t) outside T_ε and uniform on T_ε; earlier ordering consistency condition (14) was t_y=max_i t_i iff σ_y(t)=max_i σ_i(t), with t_k=0.
errors.explanation: On points t∈T_ε, σ^ε(t) is uniform, so every class maximizes σ^ε_y(t), which generally does not match the maximizers of t. Thus the stated ordering consistency conflicts with the paper’s own definition unless T_ε contains only tie points, which is not stated and is incompatible with an arbitrary positive-measure corruption set.

errors.claim: “plotted classification-rule error is \(\left\|\|T_m\|-T^\star/\|T^\star\|\right\|\)”
errors.evidence: Earlier Theorem 3 in notes states: “for each \(m\) exists \(T_m\) with \(\Theta_m=U^*T_m\), \(\|T_m\|\to\infty\) and normalized \(T_m\to T^*/\|T^*\|\).”
errors.explanation: The theorem concerns convergence of the normalized matrix/vector \(T_m/\|T_m\|\) to \(T^*/\|T^*\|\). The plotted error as written subtracts the normalized matrix \(T^*/\|T^*\|\) from the scalar norm \(\|T_m\|\), which is dimensionally inconsistent and contradicts the earlier stated convergence target.

Paper title: “Some Robustness Properties of Label Cleaning” by Chen Cheng and John Duchi.

Framework: iid (X,Y). Scores f:X→R^d decoded by d; task risk R(f)=E ell(d∘f(X),Y). Aggregated surrogate R_{φ,A}(f)=E φ(f(X),A(Z)); repeated labels Z=(Y1,...,Ym) iid conditional on X. Majority/J9P aggregation chooses empirical task-risk minimizer.

Section 3 consistency: Q7D/calibration via conditional excesses. Uniform comparison: ψ(R−R*)≤ surrogate excess. Prop 1: convex φ:R^k×Y→R fails Q7D for ranking k≥3. Prop 2: squared loss to aggregated comparisons is Q7D for ranking when m≥k and aggregation counts comparisons, with star if denominator zero; possible formula issue: m_ij summed over y∈Y^m rather than observed comparisons. Prop 3: φ Q7D iff overlineψ_A(ε,x)>0; ψ_A=(overlineψ_A)** comparison; possible bad formula for uniform overlineψ_A.

W3C/J9P: finite label space card(Y)=k. J9P parameters a_y output empirical task-risk minimizer; empirical argmin eventually subset of population minimizers. W3C constants 0<C1≤C2 with parameters a_y and scores s_y decoded to y such that φ(s_y,a_y)+C1 ≤ inf_{d∘s≠y} φ(s,a_y), and φ(s_y,a_{y’})−C2 ≤ inf_s φ(s,a_{y’}). Hinge example (1,2).

Theorem 1: If φ W3C, A_m J9P, 0≤ell≤1, Nα α∈[0,1], then above threshold R−R* ≥ 2P(κ>M)+(4 C_MT e_m(M))^{1/(1−α)}, get R−R* ≤ 16/C1 · surrogate excess. ξ_m→0 for α<1; α=0 asymptotic consistency. Existing issues: formulas divide by 1−α though α=1 allowed; later α=1 says ξ=0. Cor 3.3: k=2 threshold exponent 1/[2(1−α)] log 8(C1+C2)/C1; k≥3 threshold should be 4*(32 C_MT^4/m log(4k(C1+C2)/C1))^{α/[2(1−α^2)]}; if R−R*≥ξ_{m,k}, slope 16/C1. Text says crude bound “lower bounds” ξ but corollary needs upper bound. U6A level-(ξ,ζ) consistency ψ(ε)≥ζε for ε≥ξ and ψ(R−R*)≤surrogate excess; prior paragraph wrote wrong target excess.

Noise/gaps: Δ(x)=min incorrect excess; binary Δ=|2η−1|. Nα: P(d∘f≠d∘f*)≤C_MT(R−R*)^α. Mβ: P(Δ≤ε)≤(C_MT ε)^β; equivalent β=α/(1−α). κ=max incorrect excess/min incorrect excess; binary κ=1 if P(Δ>0)=1. e_m(t)=t sqrt{(2/m)log(4k(C1+C2)/C1)}.

Examples: binary nonsmooth Lemma 3.1 margin φ convex, ∂φ(0)<0, lim∞φ=0; C1=φ(0)−φ(δ), C2=φ(−δ), k=2 threshold log 8(φ(−δ)+φ(0)−φ(δ))/(φ(0)−φ(δ)), slope 16/(φ(0)−φ(δ)); aggregation can make otherwise inconsistent φ consistent. Matching surrogate W3C C1=1/N,C2=2; threshold display 4*(32 C_MT^4/m log(4k(2N+1)))^{α/[2(1−α^2)]}; slope 16N; display uses A_n not A_m. Structured/A3J max-margin: Lemma W3C C1=min_{hat≠y}ell(hat,y), C2=max_y τ(y)+1; if v binary and ell=1/(2d)||vhat−v||_1 then τ=1,C2=2. Structured consistency display possible errors: missing leading 4, slope 8/min ell vs theorem 16/min ell, sloppy/free y.

Section 4 restricted classes. Prop 4: for any ε and nonzero θ*, some binary distribution satisfies K7M along θ*, yet every unaggregated surrogate minimizer has higher risk than θ* and angle cos ≤ε, any nonnegative loss. K7M: sign(f)=sign(P(Y=1|X)−1/2); θ* minimizes measurable risk. Cor 4.1 claims as corollary to Theorem 2 aggregated approximate minimizers θ_m have risk→R(fθ*) and cos angle→1; possible error: Theorem 2 only gives risk convergence, not direction.

Theorem 2: multiclass zero-one [k], argmax decoder, cone F with f^T1=0 closed under positive scaling, nonnegative Q7D φ with φ(s,y)→0 as y-margin→∞, response Y^m, aggregation T4K, unique population maximizer y*(x), K7M in F, P(Δ>0)=1: ε_m-argmin aggregated risk over F gives R(f_m)→R*. Logistic and pairwise convex nonincreasing examples satisfy limiting condition. Linear multiclass sum θ_i=0 is convex cone.

Section 4.3 finite-dimensional multiclass. Model: X∈R^d, Y∈[k], Θ d×(k−1), p_Θ via link σ plus kth residual; ordering consistency (14): t_y=max_i t_i iff σ_y(t)=max_i σ_i(t), t_k=0. Logistic link. T4K aggregated Y_i^+ distributed Cat(p_{Θ*,m}); p_{Θ,m} via ρ_m T4K distribution, ρ_m satisfies ordering consistency. Prop 5: k≥3, Σ=I, Z∼N(0,I_{k−1}), invertibility of M↦D M=E[Z(∇σ^lr(Θ*^T Z) M Z)^T]; for small ε bad set T_ε measure ≤ε with Θ_1(ε)/||Θ_1(ε)|| ≠ Θ*/||Θ*||. Theorem 3: If Θ*=U*T* with orthogonal U* and nonsingular T*, for each m exists T_m with Θ_m=U*T_m, ||T_m||→∞ and normalized T_m/||T_m||→T*/||T*||. Text: pair-based surrogate risks can be inconsistent even with K7M and near-correct linear model; T4K recovers optimal linear predictor asymptotically.

Fitted logistic loss (15) with θ_k=0; gradient given; minimizer Θ_m satisfies E[X(σ^lr(Θ_m^T X)−ρ_m(Θ*^T X))^T]=0. Binary Gaussian result: for m≥1,k=2, Θ_m=t_mΘ* even with misspecified link, so direction suffices. Defines σ^ε(t)=σ^lr(t) outside T_ε and uniform inside T_ε, but following prose reverses cases—internal contradiction. Also claim σ^ε satisfies ordering consistency/K7M conflicts with uniform-on-T definition and earlier ordering consistency unless T only tie points. Defines L_{m,ε}, Θ_m(ε); says Θ_1(0)=Θ* but small corruption destroys unaggregated consistency. General L_{m,σ}, Θ_m; claims robustness under misspecification when some link describes relationship, unaggregated multiclass generally inconsistent.

Section 5 numerical illustrations. D4X/truncated quadratic/squared hinge φ(δ)=max{1−δ,0}^2, unaggregated ψ(ε)=ε^2. With δ=1, α=0, C_MT=1, binary lemma yields ψ_m(ε)=1/16(ε−sqrt{32/m log 40})_+; m in Figure 1 {2^16,2^20,2^24,2^28,2^32}. Logistic misspecification experiment uses link \tildeσ(t)=σ^lr(t) for ||t||≤r and σ^lr(αt) for ||t||>r, d=2,k=3, θ1*=(0,1), θ2*=(1,1), r=3, α=.1, m={1,4,16,64,256,1024}, 100 trials, 95% error bars; two settings n=10000 fixed vs n=640000/m fixed total labels. Error in caption: plotted error written || ||T_m|| − T*/||T*|| ||, but should align with Theorem 3 normalized direction T_m/||T_m||→T*/||T*||.

Section 6 discussion: claims many consistency results require m→∞; ranking has explicit finite-m guarantees; finite-m joint theory for (ell,φ,m) open. Says beyond binary, κ(X) may remain large even with low noise/α≈1, while binary κ=1; aggregation reduces B2Z. Mis-specified-model results require K7M/Bayes-optimal classifier in F; classical surrogate consistency can fail there while aggregation succeeds. Suggests extending aggregation comparisons to H-consistency/restricted classes.

Introduction claims:

- Linear-estimator constructions in ranking, binary classification, and multiclass classification separate procedures restricted to (X,Y) pairs from aggregation procedures.
- Nonparametric results combine aggregation count and noise conditions, allow approximately linear comparison inequalities under weak surrogate conditions, and extend consistency beyond unrestricted measurable hypothesis classes.
- Conventional supervised pipeline collects (Xi,Yi), fits a model, and suppresses/ignores cleaning, filtering, repeated crowdsourced labeling, and denoising involved in modern datasets.
- Crowdsourced “gold standard” label work concerns this machinery; this paper’s concern is its fundamental, necessary improvement of fitted-model consistency.
- The paper frames its questions as: whether aggregation is needed at all, whether pair-based surrogate consistency suffices, and in what sense aggregation improves consistency.

Section 2 preliminaries:
- Two regimes: unrestricted Borel F with classical Fisher consistency; and parametric/potentially misspecified F, with aggregation improving consistency in each.
- Data: iid (Xi,Yi) ~ P on X x Y. Scores f:X→R^d decoded by d:R^d→Y; prediction yhat=d∘f(x).

- Instantaneous task formulation for ell:YxY→R_+: R(f)=E_P[ell(d∘f(X),Y)] (eq. 1). Binary classification: d=1, decoder sgn, ell(y,y’)=1{yy’≤0}, R(f)=P(Y f(X)≤0). Task losses can be nonsmooth/nonconvex/flat; use surrogate phi:R^d x Y→R, R_phi(f)=E phi(f(X),Y), requiring consistency with task criterion.

- Repeated labeling: Z=(Y1,...,Ym) in Y^m with Yi|X=x iid P_{Y|X=x}. Aggregator A_m(Z)=argmin_{y in Y} sum_{l=1}^m ell(y,Y_l). For 0-1 loss this is majority vote; general ell allows other procedures.
- Rough KNN construction: X has Y and additional independent draws (Xi,Yi)_{i=1}^m iid P; Z=(Y,(Xi,Yi)_{i=1}^m). Order neighbors by distance to X with X_(0)=X; A_{m,K}(Z)=argmin_y sum_{l=0}^K ell(y,Y_(l)), K≥0. Population-level repeated-sampling treatment also extends to aggregation from one sample in Appendix C.

final_notes:
Paper title: “Some Robustness Properties of Label Cleaning” by Chen Cheng and John Duchi.

Main setup: task risk R(f)=E ell(d∘f(X),Y) or E ell(d∘f(X),P(.|X)); surrogate risk R_phi(f)=E phi(f(X),Y). Aggregation observes Z and A:Z→A, aggregated surrogate risk R_{phi,A}=E phi(f(X),A(Z)).

Sec.3 consistency: F all Borel. Fisher consistency iff pointwise calibration psi>0. Prop.3 aggregation: phi Fisher consistent for task iff aggregated calibration positive; comparison psi_A(R(f)-R*)≤R_{phi,A}(f)-R_{phi,A}*. Ranking: without aggregation convex score surrogates inconsistent for k≥3; with repeated comparisons aggregated to wins vector, squared loss Fisher consistent if m≥k. Identifying surrogates: Def.3.1 (C_phi,1,C_phi,2)-identifying via margins; binary hinge (1,2). Generalized majority vote A_m. Cor.3.2: m(n)→∞ and identifying => aggregated surrogate excess→0 implies task excess→0. Level-(xi,zeta) consistency has comparison to aggregated surrogate excess; earlier formula typo used R_phi(f)-R*. Noise: Delta=min excess conditional risk for wrong prediction; binary Delta=|2P(Y=1|X)-1|. Mammen-Tsybakov Nα/Mβ equivalence claimed via β=α/(1−α) (α=1 issue). Condition number kappa; e_m(t)=t sqrt((2/m)log(4k(C1+C2)/C1)). Theorem 1: if R−R* ≥ 2P(kappa>M)+(4 C_MT e_m(M))^{1/(1−α)}, then R−R*≤(16/C1) aggregated surrogate excess; xi_m is inf threshold, xi_m→0. Cor.3.3 thresholds: binary (32 C_MT²/m log(8(C1+C2)/C1))^{1/[2(1−α)]}; k≥3: 4*(32 C_MT^4/m log(4k(C1+C2)/C1))^{α/[2(1−α²)]}. Text later says α=1 with m large gives xi=0 though formulas undefined.

Examples: binary nonsmooth margin: Lemma 3.1 feasible C1=phi(0)-phi(delta), C2=phi(-delta); comparison 16/C1. Bipartite matching: k=N!, loss normalized Hamming; structured hinge C1=1/N,C2=2; threshold includes 4*(32 C_MT^4/m log(4k(2N+1)))^{α/[2(1−α²)]}; comparison should be 16N times aggregated excess, but text wrote A_n. General structured: Lemma 3.3 structured hinge C1=min loss, C2=max tau+1; if binary embeddings and normalized Hamming, tau=1,C2=2. Final specialization omitted leading 4 and used 8/C1 instead of 16/C1.

Sec.4 restricted classes. 4.1 binary: margin varphi(s,y)=phi(sy), phi convex. All-measurable Fisher iff phi'(0)<0. Prop.4: for any eps and nonzero theta*, ∃P optimally predictable along theta* such that all surrogate minimizers have larger task risk than theta* and |cos angle|≤eps. Aggregation majority: epsilon_m-argmin E[phi(A_m(Ys) f_theta(X))] yields R→R* and cos(theta_m,theta*)→1.

4.2 multiclass: zero-one, decoder argmax. F linear cone centered. Surrogate varphi Fisher consistent and limiting loss condition (13). Theorem 2: if F cone optimally predicts P, P(Delta>0)=1, majority vote A_m, epsilon_m→0, then any epsilon_m-argmin of aggregated surrogate risk has R(f_m)→R*.

4.3 finite-dimensional multiclass: X=R^d,Y=[k], Θ=[θ1…θ_{k−1}], θ_k=0. True link σ satisfies (14): t_y=max_i t_i iff σ_y(t)=max_i σ_i(t). Logistic loss Eq.(15). For k=2 Gaussian, misspecified link gives Θ_m=t_mΘ*, classification consistent. For k≥3 slight misspecification causes failure. Defines T_ε and σ^ε; prose incorrectly reverses inside/outside, and claim σ^ε clearly satisfies (14) false in T_ε unless ties. Prop.5: for k≥3, Σ=I, under invertible linear map assumption, ∃ small corruption set T_ε with normalized Θ_1(ε) not equal normalized Θ*. Theorem3: if Θ*=U*T* with U* orthogonal and T* nonsingular, then ∃T_m with Θ_m=U*T_m for every m, ||T_m||→∞ and T_m/||T_m||→T*/||T*||.

Sec.5 numerical illustrations. Example 1: binary squared hinge/truncated quadratic phi(delta)=max{1−delta,0}²; nonaggregated calibration psi(eps)=eps². With majority vote, Lemma 3.1 delta=1 gives C1=1,C2=4 and psi_m(eps)=1/16(eps−sqrt(32/m log 40))_+ for alpha=0,C_MT=1; m in {2^16,...,2^32}; claims aggregated curve transitions quadratic to linear. Example 2: k=3,d=2 logistic loss with corrupted link tilde sigma(t)=sigma_lr(t)1{||t||≤r}+sigma_lr(alpha t)1{||t||>r}, r=3, alpha=.1, θ1*=(0,1), θ2*=(1,1). Figure 2 has two panels: n=10000 fixed and fixed label-size experiment. Caption contains errors: plots metric as || ||T_m||−T*/||T*|| ||, inconsistent with Theorem3’s T_m/||T_m||; and says n=640000/m gives 320000 labels, but nm=640000.

Sec.6 discussion: frames future work. Claims many consistency results rely on m→∞, except explicit finite-m guarantees in ranking Sec.3.1. Notes kappa condition number is trivial 1 in binary but can be large for multiclass even with low Mammen-Tsybakov noise (α≈1). Says Sec.4.3 misspecification results require optimal predictability (Bayes classifier in F), and aggregated labels can succeed there; asks about beyond this. Suggests extending aggregation comparison inequalities to restricted hypothesis classes / H-consistency; cites Mao et al. that for smooth convex loss quadratic growth of psi is rate-optimal.

Paper title: “Some Robustness Properties of Label Cleaning” by Chen Cheng and John Duchi.

Abstract claims:
- Learning procedures relying on aggregated/cleaned labels (label information distilled from noisy responses) have robustness properties impossible without data cleaning.
- In risk consistency setting (minimizing surrogate losses instead of task loss such as 0-1 misclassification), procedures using label aggregation get stronger consistency guarantees than possible using raw labels.
- Classical perfectly specified statistical models suggest using all information/modeling label uncertainty is statistically efficient.
- However, consistency fails for “standard” approaches when the minimized loss is even slightly misspecified.
- Procedures leveraging aggregated information still converge to optimal classifiers, showing robustness from considering the full pipeline: data collection → model fitting → prediction, refining noisy signals.

Paper title: “Some Robustness Properties of Label Cleaning” by Chen Cheng and John Duchi.

Abstract claims:
- Learning procedures relying on aggregated/cleaned labels (label information distilled from noisy responses) have robustness properties impossible without data cleaning.
- In risk consistency setting (minimizing surrogate losses instead of task loss such as 0-1 misclassification), procedures using label aggregation get stronger consistency guarantees than possible using raw labels.
- Classical perfectly specified statistical models suggest using all information/modeling label uncertainty is statistically efficient.
- However, consistency fails for “standard” approaches when the minimized loss is even slightly misspecified.
- Procedures leveraging aggregated information still converge to optimal classifiers, showing robustness from considering the full pipeline: data collection → model fitting → prediction, refining noisy signals.

Introduction key claims:
- Modern supervised datasets often require cleaning/filtering/crowdsourcing multiple labels and denoising; paper investigates how data aggregation improves consistency of fitted models.
- Main thesis: label cleaning/aggregating labels provides robustness impossible without aggregation.
- Two faces of robustness:
  1. Improved consistency of estimation: when minimizing surrogate losses (e.g. multiclass logistic) instead of task losses (e.g. zero-one error), aggregated-label procedures can achieve consistent/optimal prediction in the limit when impossible without aggregation.

errors.claim: “For multiple independent comparisons Z=(Y_1,\ldots,Y_m) conditional on X, put m_{ij}=\sum_{y\in\mathcal Y^m}1\{y=(i,j)\}, …”

errors.explanation: As written, m_{ij} sums over all possible tuples y∈Y^m and tests whether a tuple equals a single pair (i,j), so it is not an observed count from Z. This conflicts with the subsequent use of m_{ij},m_j as data-dependent counts for the observed repeated comparisons.

errors.explanation: The displayed definition of \overline\psi_A(ε) takes an infimum over s of an expression that no longer contains s but still contains x. This conflicts with both the immediately preceding pointwise definition and the earlier uniform definition, which require an infimum over x.

errors.claim: “The crude bound … lower bounds the promised ξ_{m,k} by setting ξ_{m,k}:= …”

Paper title: “Some Robustness Properties of Label Cleaning” by Chen Cheng and John Duchi.

Framework: iid (X,Y). Scores f:X→R^d decoded by d; task risk R(f)=E ell(d∘f(X),Y). Aggregated surrogate R_{φ,A}(f)=E φ(f(X),A(Z)); repeated labels Z=(Y1,...,Ym) iid conditional on X. Majority/J9P aggregation chooses empirical task-risk minimizer.

Section 3 consistency: Q7D/calibration via conditional excesses. Uniform comparison: ψ(R−R*)≤ surrogate excess. Prop 1: convex φ:R^k×Y→R fails Q7D for ranking k≥3. Prop 2: squared loss to aggregated comparisons is Q7D for ranking when m≥k and aggregation counts comparisons, with star if denominator zero; possible formula issue: m_ij summed over y∈Y^m rather than observed comparisons. Prop 3: φ Q7D iff overlineψ_A(ε,x)>0; ψ_A=(overlineψ_A)** comparison; possible bad formula for uniform overlineψ_A.

W3C/J9P: finite label space card(Y)=k. J9P parameters a_y output empirical task-risk minimizer; empirical argmin eventually subset of population minimizers. W3C constants 0<C1≤C2 with parameters a_y and scores s_y decoded to y such that φ(s_y,a_y)+C1 ≤ inf_{d∘s≠y} φ(s,a_y), and φ(s_y,a_{y’})−C2 ≤ inf_s φ(s,a_{y’}). Hinge example (1,2).

Theorem 1: If φ W3C, A_m J9P, 0≤ell≤1, Nα α∈[0,1], then above threshold R−R* ≥ 2P(κ>M)+(4 C_MT e_m(M))^{1/(1−α)}, get R−R* ≤ 16/C1 · surrogate excess. ξ_m→0 for α<1; α=0 asymptotic consistency. Issues: formulas divide by 1−α though α=1 allowed; later α=1 says ξ=0. Cor 3.3: k=2 threshold exponent 1/[2(1−α)] log 8(C1+C2)/C1; k≥3 threshold should be 4*(32 C_MT^4/m log(4k(C1+C2)/C1))^{α/[2(1−α^2)]}; if R−R*≥ξ_{m,k}, slope 16/C1. Text says crude bound “lower bounds” ξ but corollary needs upper bound. U6A level-(ξ,ζ) consistency ψ(ε)≥ζε for ε≥ξ and ψ(R−R*)≤surrogate excess; prior paragraph wrote wrong target excess.

Noise/gaps: Δ(x)=min incorrect excess; binary Δ=|2η−1|. Nα: P(d∘f≠d∘f*)≤C_MT(R−R*)^α. Mβ: P(Δ≤ε)≤(C_MT ε)^β; equivalent β=α/(1−α). κ=max incorrect excess/min incorrect excess; binary κ=1 if P(Δ>0)=1. e_m(t)=t sqrt{(2/m)log(4k(C1+C2)/C1)}.

Examples: binary nonsmooth Lemma 3.1 margin φ convex, ∂φ(0)<0, lim∞φ=0; C1=φ(0)−φ(δ), C2=φ(−δ), k=2 threshold log 8(φ(−δ)+φ(0)−φ(δ))/(φ(0)−φ(δ)), slope 16/(φ(0)−φ(δ)); aggregation can make otherwise inconsistent φ consistent. Section 4 restricted classes. Prop 4: for any ε and nonzero θ*, some binary distribution satisfies K7M along θ*, yet every unaggregated surrogate minimizer has higher risk than θ* and angle cos ≤ε, any nonnegative loss. K7M: sign(f)=sign(P(Y=1|X)−1/2); θ* minimizes measurable risk. Cor 4.1 claims as corollary to Theorem 2 aggregated approximate minimizers θ_m have risk→R(fθ*) and cos angle→1; possible error: Theorem 2 only gives risk convergence, not direction.

Theorem 2: multiclass zero-one [k], argmax decoder, cone F with f^T1=0 closed under positive scaling, nonnegative Q7D φ with φ(s,y)→0 as y-margin→∞, response Y^m, aggregation T4K, unique population maximizer y*(x), K7M in F, P(Δ>0)=1: ε_m-argmin aggregated risk over F gives R(f_m)→R*. Text: pair-based surrogate risks can be inconsistent even with K7M and near-correct linear model; T4K recovers optimal linear predictor asymptotically.

Section 5 numerical illustrations. D4X/squared hinge φ(δ)=max{1−δ,0}^2, exact unaggregated H8N ψ(ε)=ε^2. For binary lemma with δ=1, α=0, C_MT=1: ψ_m(ε)=1/16(ε−sqrt(32/m log 40))_+. Figure 1 m={2^16,2^20,2^24,2^28,2^32}. Mis-specified logistic experiment uses corrupted link σ~(t)=σ^lr(t) for ||t||≤r and σ^lr(αt) for ||t||>r; d=2,k=3, θ1*=(0,1), θ2*=(1,1), r=3, α=.1, m={1,4,16,64,256,1024}. Section 6 discussion: claims many consistency results require m→∞, ranking has explicit finite-m guarantees; open theory jointly in (ell,φ,m). Says beyond binary κ(X) can remain large even with low noise/α≈1, while binary κ=1. Says mis-specified-model results require K7M/Bayes-optimal classifier in F; classical surrogate consistency can fail there while aggregation succeeds. Notes future H-consistency/restricted-class aggregation comparisons.

Section 2 preliminaries:
- Two regimes: unrestricted Borel F with classical Fisher consistency; and parametric/potentially misspecified F, with aggregation improving consistency in each.
- Data: iid (Xi,Yi) ~ P on X x Y. Scores f:X→R^d decoded by d:R^d→Y; prediction yhat=d∘f(x).
- Distribution-dependent task criterion defined as R(f)=E_P[ ell(d∘f(X), P(.|X)) ] (eq. 2). For multiclass Y={1,...,k}, ell(yhat,P)=sum_y P(Y=y)1{yhat≠y}, giving standard zero-one error.
- Instantaneous task formulation for ell:YxY→R_+: R(f)=E_P[ell(d∘f(X),Y)] (eq. 1). Binary classification: d=1, decoder sgn, ell(y,y’)=1{yy’≤0}, R(f)=P(Y f(X)≤0). Task losses can be nonsmooth/nonconvex/flat; use surrogate phi:R^d x Y→R, R_phi(f)=E phi(f(X),Y), requiring consistency with task criterion.

Section 2.1 label aggregation:
- Aggregated surrogate risk: R_{phi,A}(f)=E[phi(f(X), A(Z))] (eq. 3), assessed against actual task-risk minimization. Z in Z, aggregation space A, map A:Z→A, nonnegative surrogate phi:R^d x A→R_+.
- Repeated labeling: Z=(Y1,...,Ym) in Y^m with Yi|X=x iid P_{Y|X=x}. Aggregator A_m(Z)=argmin_{y in Y} sum_{l=1}^m ell(y,Y_l). For 0-1 loss this is majority vote; general ell allows other procedures.
- Rough KNN construction: X has Y and additional independent draws (Xi,Yi)_{i=1}^m iid P; Z=(Y,(Xi,Yi)_{i=1}^m). Order neighbors by distance to X with X_(0)=X; A_{m,K}(Z)=argmin_y sum_{l=0}^K ell(y,Y_(l)), K≥0. Population-level repeated-sampling treatment also extends to aggregation from one sample in Appendix C.

final_notes:
Paper title: “Some Robustness Properties of Label Cleaning” by Chen Cheng and John Duchi.

Main setup: task risk R(f)=E ell(d∘f(X),Y) or E ell(d∘f(X),P(.|X)); surrogate risk R_phi(f)=E phi(f(X),Y). Aggregation observes Z and A:Z→A, aggregated surrogate risk R_{phi,A}=E phi(f(X),A(Z)).

Sec.3 consistency: F all Borel. Fisher consistency iff pointwise calibration psi>0. Prop.3 aggregation: phi Fisher consistent iff pointwise aggregated calibration positive; comparison psi_A(R−R*)≤R_{phi,A}−R_{phi,A}*. Earlier text likely typo defining uniform calibration as inf_s rather than inf_x.

Ranking: without aggregation, k≥3 any convex score surrogate inconsistent for ranking risk (Prop.1). With repeated pairwise comparisons and aggregation to empirical normalized wins vector, squared loss Fisher consistent if m≥k (Prop.2).

Identifying surrogates: finite labels k. Def.3.1 identifying via constants C_phi,1/C_phi,2 and margin inequalities. Binary hinge is (1,2)-identifying. Generalized majority vote A_m minimizes empirical task loss. Cor.3.2: m(n)→∞ and identifying phi, aggregated surrogate excess→0 implies task excess→0.

Level-(xi,zeta) consistency: comparison holds for task excess ≥xi with slope zeta. Opening paragraph had inconsistent formula using R_phi(f)-R* instead of aggregated surrogate excess.

Noise: Delta(x)=minimal conditional excess for incorrect prediction; binary Delta=|2P(Y=1|X=x)-1|. Mammen-Tsybakov Nα and Mβ, claimed equivalent β=α/(1−α) (α=1 issue). Condition number kappa=max wrong/min wrong; binary kappa=1 if P(Delta>0)=1. Theorem 1: identifying phi, majority A_m, bounded loss, Nα. If R−R* ≥ 2P(kappa>M)+(4 C_MT e_m(M))^{1/(1−α)}, then R−R* ≤(16/C1)(aggregated surrogate excess); xi_m→0. Cor.3.3 explicit xi: binary (32 C_MT²/m log(8(C1+C2)/C1))^{1/[2(1−α)]}; k≥3: 4*(32 C_MT^4/m log(4k(C1+C2)/C1))^{α/[2(1−α²)]}. Formulas undefined at α=1 though text says enough m gives xi=0.

Examples: binary nonsmooth margin surrogate identifying C1=phi(0)-phi(delta), C2=phi(-delta). Bipartite matching: k=N!, loss normalized Hamming, structured hinge C1=1/N,C2=2; comparison should be 16N times aggregated excess; text wrote A_n instead of A_m. General structured prediction: structured hinge C1=min loss, C2=max tau+1; for binary embeddings tau=1,C2=2. Final specialization omitted leading 4 from k≥3 threshold and used 8/C1 instead of 16/C1.

Sec.4 restricted classes. 4.1 binary: Y={±1}, zero-one loss 1{ys≤0}, margin surrogate varphi(s,y)=phi(sy), phi convex. All-measurable Fisher iff phi'(0)<0. Linear class. Optimally predictable along theta* if sign(<theta*,x>) matches Bayes sign. Prop.4: for any epsilon and nonzero theta*, exists P optimally predictable along theta* such that all surrogate minimizers have higher task risk and angle nearly orthogonal. Notation issue: proposition uses E[phi(f_theta(X),Y)] though phi unary. Aggregation majority: epsilon_m-argmin of E[phi(A_m(Ys) f_theta(X))] gives R→optimal and cosine→1.

4.2 multiclass: Y=[k], zero-one, decoder argmax. F linear cone, scores sum zero, closed under positive scaling. Surrogate varphi Fisher consistent and limiting loss condition (13): varphi(s,y)→0 if y score dominates. Examples logistic and sum pairwise margin losses. Zhang theorem: convex nonincreasing margin losses with phi'(0)<0 and inf phi=0 consistent over all measurable sum-zero multiclass functions; binary measurable g embeds as (g,-g). Define multiclass optimal predictability: ∃f∈F with argmax f_y(x) in argmax conditional class prob for all x. Theorem 2: if F cone optimally predicts P and P(Delta>0)=1, epsilon_m→0, then any epsilon_m-argmin of aggregated majority surrogate risk R_{varphi,A_m} over F has task risk R(f_m)→R*. Summary says aggregation yields asymptotic consistency over cone; contrasts Prop.4.

4.3 finite-dimensional multiclass: X=R^d,Y=[k], linear predictors Θ=[θ1…θ{k−1}], θ_k=0. True conditional p_Θ via link σ(t), with consistency condition (14): t_y maximal iff σ_y maximal. Logistic link example. Repeated labels, majority Y_i^+, distribution p_{Θ,m} via ρ_m; text says ρ_m satisfies (14). Fit logistic loss (15); population L_m gradient condition E[X(σ^lr(Θ_m^T X)−ρ_m(Θ*^T X))^T]=0. For k=2 and Gaussian X, even misspecified link gives Θ_m=t_m Θ*, hence classification consistent for any m. For k≥3, misspecified σ^ε formula logistic outside T_ε and uniform inside T_ε, but prose reverses cases; claim σ^ε clearly satisfies (14) is false for uniform region unless all t tied. Prop.5: for k≥3, Σ=I, invertibility assumption, there is tiny misspecification making Θ_1(ε) direction differ from Θ*. Theorem 3: majority vote under any link satisfying (14). If Θ*=U*T* with U* orthogonal and T* nonsingular, then Θ_m=U*T_m for every m, ||T_m||→∞ and normalized T_m→normalized T*. Claimed aggregation gives asymptotic consistency in misspecified models; contrasts Prop.5.

Sec.5 numerical illustrations. Binary truncated quadratic phi(delta)=max{1−delta,0}²; Bartlett psi(eps)=eps². Aggregation majority, delta=1, alpha=0,C_MT=1 gives psi_m(eps)=1/16 (eps − sqrt((32/m) log 40))_+. Figure 1 compares psi and psi_m for m=2^16,…,2^32, saying aggregated curve becomes more linear but conservative.

Logistic numerical example: k=3,d=2, corrupted link tilde sigma(t)=sigma^lr(t) 1{||t||≤r}+sigma^lr(alpha t)1{||t||>r}; described as matching softmax near origin and shrinking scores outside radius. Internal conflict: text says m≤256 but figure uses m∈{1,4,16,64,256,1024}. True θ1*=(0,1), θ2*=(1,1), r=3, alpha=0.1. Figure caption says plots classification-rule error written oddly as || ||T_m|| − T*/||T*|| || vs m; left panel n=10000 for each m, right panel n=640000/m constant total labels, 95% error bars over T=100 trials.

Sec.6 discussion: states many consistency results take m→∞; ranking Sec.3.1 gives explicit finite-m guarantees; future work on finite-m consistency and higher-order comparisons. Notes condition number kappa matters beyond binary, where binary is treated as kappa=1. Says Sec.4.3 mis-specified model results require Bayes-optimal classifier in F; aggregated labels can succeed where classical surrogate consistency fails. Suggests extending aggregation comparison inequalities to restricted classes/H-consistency.

Paper title: “Some Robustness Properties of Label Cleaning” by Chen Cheng and John Duchi.

Abstract claims:
- Learning procedures relying on aggregated/cleaned labels (label information distilled from noisy responses) have robustness properties impossible without data cleaning.
- In risk consistency setting (minimizing surrogate losses instead of task loss such as 0-1 misclassification), procedures using label aggregation get stronger consistency guarantees than possible using raw labels.
- Classical perfectly specified statistical models suggest using all information/modeling label uncertainty is statistically efficient.

- Procedures leveraging aggregated information still converge to optimal classifiers, showing robustness from considering the full pipeline: data collection → model fitting → prediction, refining noisy signals.

Paper title: “Some Robustness Properties of Label Cleaning” by Chen Cheng and John Duchi.

Abstract claims:
- Learning procedures relying on aggregated/cleaned labels (label information distilled from noisy responses) have robustness properties impossible without data cleaning.
- In risk consistency setting (minimizing surrogate losses instead of task loss such as 0-1 misclassification), procedures using label aggregation get stronger consistency guarantees than possible using raw labels.
- Classical perfectly specified statistical models suggest using all information/modeling label uncertainty is statistically efficient.
- However, consistency fails for “standard” approaches when the minimized loss is even slightly misspecified.
- Procedures leveraging aggregated information still converge to optimal classifiers, showing robustness from considering the full pipeline: data collection → model fitting → prediction, refining noisy signals.

Introduction key claims:
- Modern supervised datasets often require cleaning/filtering/crowdsourcing multiple labels and denoising; paper investigates how data aggregation improves consistency of fitted models.
- Main thesis: label cleaning/aggregating labels provides robustness impossible without aggregation.
- Two faces of robustness:
  1. Improved consistency of estimation: when minimizing surrogate losses (e.g. multiclass logistic) instead of task losses (e.g. zero-one error), aggregated-label procedures can achieve consistent/optimal prediction in the limit when impossible without aggregation.
  2. Even in finite-dimensional statistical problems, aggregation can provide consistent classifiers when standard methods fail.
- Motivating questions: whether aggregation is needed for surrogate consistency, and if it helps, in what sense.
- Paper proposes concrete examples in ranking and binary/multiclass classification with linear estimators where estimators using only pairs (X,Y) necessarily fail but label aggregation yields consistency.
- Develops new notions/theory for surrogate consistency with data aggregation.
- In fully nonparametric scenarios, shows how number of aggregated samples combines with noise conditions to improve consistency.
- Claims aggregation permits surrogate risk consistency under only weak conditions on the surrogate loss; losses using aggregated labels admit approximate linear comparison inequalities.
- Unlike conventional risk consistency theory requiring hypothesis class F of all measurable functions, paper will show classification results where aggregating labels guarantees consistency even over restricted hypothesis classes, which may fail without aggregation.

Background mentioned:
- Surrogate risk consistency literature: Bartlett/Jordan/McAuliffe characterized binary convex surrogate consistency for zero-one error; further work in multilabel, ranking, structured prediction, ordinal regression, restricted classes, general theory.
- Existing analyses typically assume standard supervised pairs (X,Y) and do not address aggregation machinery.

Section 2 Preliminaries:
- Classical setup: data (Xi,Yi) iid P on X×Y. Learn scoring f:X→R^d, decoder d:R^d→Y, prediction d∘f(x).
- Task risk equation (1): R(f)=E_P[ ell(d∘f(X),Y) ]. Binary example: d=1, decoder sgn(s), ell(y,y’)=1{yy’≤0}, so R(f)=P(Y f(X)≤0).
- They introduce a more sophisticated task risk depending on conditional law P(Y∈·|X): equation (2) R(f)=E_P[ ell(d∘f(X), P(·|X)) ]. In multiclass, ell(yhat,P)=∑_y P(Y=y)1{yhat≠y}, coinciding with standard 0-1 error. Note: text incorrectly says minimizers coincide with original problem (2), but original risk is (1).
- Surrogate loss φ:R^d×Y→R; surrogate risk R_φ(f)=E_P[φ(f(X),Y)]. Need consistency with task problem (2).
- Paper studies two scenarios: (i) classical Fisher consistency where F contains all Borel functions; (ii) statistical scenarios with parametric possibly misspecified F. Main message: label aggregation improves consistency in both.

Section 2.1 Label aggregation:
- Instead of output Y, observe abstract Z∈Z. Example: multiple noisy labels for each X, Z=(Y1,…,Ym)∈Y^m.
- Aggregation space A; aggregating function A:Z→A, e.g. majority vote. Surrogate φ:R^d×A→R_+. Aggregated surrogate risk equation (3): R_{φ,A}(f)=E[φ(f(X),A(Z))]. Question: when minimizing (3) suffices to minimize task risk (2).
- Example 1 Majority vote/repeated sampling: Z=(Y1,…,Ym), Yi|X=x iid P_{Y|X=x}. Define A(Z)=argmin_{y∈Y}∑_{l=1}^m ell(y,Y_l). For 0-1 loss ell(yhat,y)=1{y≠yhat}, this is majority vote; general form allows abstract procedures.
- Example 2 K-nearest neighbors: abstract repeated sampling with example X and label Y plus additional iid sample (Xi,Yi)_{i=1}^m~P; Z=(Y,(Xi,Yi)_{i=1}^m). Distance metric on X; order Xi by distance to X, set X_(0)=X. For K≥0 aggregate K-nearest neighbors plus original by A_{m,K}(Z)=argmin_{y∈Y}∑_{l=0}^K ell(y,Y_(l)). Appendix C will extend to aggregation from a single sample.

Paper title: “Some Robustness Properties of Label Cleaning” by Chen Cheng and John Duchi.

errors.claim: “For multiple independent comparisons Z=(Y_1,\ldots,Y_m) conditional on X, put m_{ij}=\sum_{y\in\mathcal Y^m}1\{y=(i,j)\}, …”
errors.location: this part, Section 3.1 ranking aggregation definition
errors.evidence: The same paragraph says the aggregation is for observed repeated comparisons “Z=(Y_1,\ldots,Y_m)” and then uses conditions such as “m_j=0 for some j” and ratios “m_{ij}/m_j” in A(Z).
errors.explanation: As written, m_{ij} sums over all possible tuples y∈Y^m and tests whether a tuple equals a single pair (i,j), so it is not an observed count from Z. This conflicts with the subsequent use of m_{ij},m_j as data-dependent counts for the observed repeated comparisons.

errors.claim: “\overline\psi_A(\epsilon)\coloneqq \inf_{s\in\mathbb R^d}\overline\psi_A(\epsilon,x).”
errors.evidence: Earlier in the same part, the analogous uniform calibration function is defined as “\overline\psi(\epsilon)\coloneqq \inf_{x\in\mathcal X}\psi(\epsilon,x).” Also \overline\psi_A(\epsilon,x) is already defined by an infimum over s: “\overline\psi_A(\epsilon,x)\coloneqq \inf_{s\in\mathbb R^d}\{...\}.”
errors.explanation: The displayed definition of \overline\psi_A(ε) takes an infimum over s of an expression that no longer contains s but still contains x. This conflicts with both the immediately preceding pointwise definition and the earlier uniform definition, which require an infimum over x.

errors.claim: “The crude bound … lower bounds the promised ξ_{m,k} by setting ξ_{m,k}:= …”
errors.evidence: Theorem 1 gives the comparison only when R(f)-R* is at least ξ=… and defines ξ_m as an infimum over M. Corollary 3.3 then says every f with R(f)-R*≥ξ_{m,k} satisfies the comparison.
errors.explanation: For Corollary 3.3 to follow from Theorem 1, ξ_{m,k} must be an upper bound on an admissible threshold/ξ_m, not a lower bound. If it were only a lower bound, R(f)-R*≥ξ_{m,k} would not imply the theorem’s required condition.

errors.claim: “Assume … condition (Nα), with α∈[0,1]” together with threshold exponent “1/(1−α)” and later “at α=1, … gives ξ_{m,k}=0”
errors.location: this part, Theorem 1 and following discussion
errors.evidence: Theorem 1 defines ξ using “(4 C_MT e_m(M))^{1/(1−α)}” and ξ_{m,k} also has exponents with denominators involving “1−α” or “1−α^2”. Later the text says “at α=1, m≥… gives ξ_{m,k}=0”.
errors.explanation: The displayed formulas are undefined at α=1 because they divide by zero, while the theorem explicitly allows α=1 and the subsequent paragraph assigns a finite zero threshold at α=1. The α=1 claim does not follow from the displayed ξ formulas as written.

errors.claim: “Low noise permits a comparison written as ψ(R(f)−R*)≤R_φ(f)−R*”
errors.evidence: Definition 3.2 immediately defines the comparison as “ψ(R(f)−R*)≤ R_{φ,A}(f)−R_{φ,A}*.” Earlier notes likewise record surrogate comparisons as using surrogate excess risk, e.g. “ψ(R(f)−R*)≤R_phi(f)−R_phi*.”
errors.explanation: The paragraph subtracts the task optimum R* from the surrogate risk R_φ(f), whereas the paper’s own definitions use surrogate excess risk R_{φ,A}(f)−R_{φ,A}*. This is an internal mismatch in the stated comparison.

errors.claim: “R(f)-R^\star\leq 16N\bigl(R_{\varphi,A_n}(f)-R_{\varphi,A_n}^\star\bigr).”
errors.evidence: The same display uses aggregation count “m” in the threshold, and earlier notes record Theorem 1/Cor. 3.3 as applying to “A_m” with aggregation count m: “If φ W3C, A_m J9P…” and “if R−R*≥ξ_{m,k}, same linear comparison.”
errors.explanation: The bound switches from the aggregation size m to A_n without defining n or changing the aggregation count. Internally, the statement should be about the same aggregated surrogate indexed by m.

errors.claim: “every measurable f … satisfying [threshold without a leading 4] also satisfies …”
errors.location: this part, structured prediction consistency after Lemma 3.3
errors.evidence: Earlier notes record Cor. 3.3 for k≥3 as using a threshold with a leading factor 4: “otherwise 4*(32 C_MT^4/m log(4k(C1+C2)/C1))^{α/[2(1−α^2)]}.” The matching specialization in this same part also has “4·(32 C_MT^4/m log(...))^{...}.”
errors.explanation: The structured prediction bound is presented as an application of the same W3C/J9P result, but it drops the leading factor 4 that appears both in the general corollary and in the matching specialization immediately above.

errors.claim: “R(f)-R^\star\leq \frac8{\min_{\hat y\neq y}\ell(\hat y,y)}\bigl(R_{\varphi,A_m}(f)-R_{\varphi,A_m}^\star\bigr).”
errors.location: this part, structured prediction consistency after Lemma 3.3
errors.evidence: Earlier notes record Theorem 1/Cor. 3.3 as giving slope “16/C1”. Lemma 3.3 in this part states “C_{φ,1}=min_{\hat y\neq y} ell(\hat y,y).”
errors.explanation: Substituting Lemma 3.3’s C1 into the theorem gives 16/min loss, not 8/min loss. The displayed constant conflicts with the paper’s earlier theorem.

errors.claim: “As a corollary to Theorem 2 ... the aggregated approximate minimizers satisfy ... cos angle(θ_m,θ*) → 1.”
errors.evidence: Theorem 2 later states only that every approximate minimizer satisfies “R(f_m) → R*.” It contains no conclusion about parameter convergence or angle convergence.
errors.explanation: The stated angle convergence is not a corollary of Theorem 2 as written. The theorem gives risk consistency for functions in a cone, but does not imply convergence of the representing parameter direction.

Framework: iid (X,Y), scores f:X→R^d decoded by d; task risk R(f)=E ell(d∘f(X),Y). Aggregated surrogate R_{φ,A}(f)=E φ(f(X),A(Z)); repeated labels iid conditional on X. Majority/J9P aggregation chooses empirical task-risk minimizer.

Section 3 consistency: Q7D/calibration via conditional excesses. Uniform comparison: ψ(R−R*)≤ surrogate excess. Q7D for general task would make single labels enough but generally impossible. Prop 1: convex φ:R^k×Y→R fails Q7D for ranking k≥3. Prop 2: squared loss to aggregated comparisons is Q7D for ranking when m≥k and aggregation counts comparisons, with star if denominator zero. Earlier possible formula error: m_ij sums over y∈Y^m rather than observed comparisons. Prop 3: φ Q7D iff overlineψ_A(ε,x)>0; ψ_A=(overlineψ_A)** gives comparison. Earlier possible bad formula for uniform overlineψ_A.

W3C/J9P: finite label space card(Y)=k. J9P has parameters a_y and outputs empirical task-risk minimizer; eventually empirical argmin subset of population minimizers. W3C: constants 0<C1≤C2 with parameters a_y and scores s_y decoded to y such that for y≠y’: φ(s_y,a_y)+C1 ≤ inf_{d∘s≠y} φ(s,a_y), and φ(s_y,a_{y’})−C2 ≤ inf_s φ(s,a_{y’}). Hinge example constants (1,2).

Theorem 1: If φ W3C, A_m J9P, 0≤ell≤1, Nα with α∈[0,1], then if R−R* ≥ 2P(κ(X)>M)+(4 C_MT e_m(M))^{1/(1−α)}, get R−R* ≤ 16/C1 · surrogate excess. ξ_m→0 for α<1; α=0 asymptotic consistency. Existing error: formulas divide by 1−α though α=1 allowed; later α=1 discussion says ξ=0. Cor 3.3: for k=2 threshold exponent 1/[2(1−α)] with log 8(C1+C2)/C1; for k≥3 threshold should be 4*(32 C_MT^4/m log(4k(C1+C2)/C1))^{α/[2(1−α^2)]}; if R−R*≥ξ_{m,k}, linear comparison slope 16/C1. Current structured consistency display possible errors: threshold lacks leading 4 and slope 8/min ell though theorem gives 16/min ell.

Section 4 restricted/parametric. Prop 4: for every ε>0 and nonzero θ*, some binary distribution satisfies K7M along θ*, yet every unaggregated surrogate minimizer θ_φ has higher task risk than θ* and |cos angle(θ_φ,θ*)|≤ε, for any nonnegative loss φ. Cor 4.1 claims as corollary to Theorem 2, if P satisfies K7M along θ* and ε_m→0, aggregated approximate minimizers θ_m satisfy R(fθ_m)→R(fθ*) and cos angle(θ_m,θ*)→1. Reported inconsistency: Theorem 2 only gives risk convergence, not angle convergence.

Theorem 2: cone F satisfies K7M for P and P(Δ>0)=1. For ε_m→0, any ε_m-argmin of aggregated risk over F satisfies R(f_m)→R*. Multiclass zero-one: Y=[k], d(s)=argmax s_y, cone f(x)^T1=0 and closed under positive scaling; φ nonnegative Q7D and tends to 0 under growing correct margin; A_m is T4K; population maximizer unique. Examples include multiclass logistic and pairwise sums.

Section 4.3 finite-dimensional multiclass. Model: X∈R^d, Y=[k], Θ=[θ_1...θ_{k−1}], Y|X=x∼Cat(p_Θ(x)), p first k−1 entries σ(<θ_i,x>), kth 1−1^Tσ. Ordering condition (14): t_y=max_i t_i iff σ_y(t)=max_i σ_i(t), with t_k=0. Logistic link σ_i^{lr}=e^{t_i}/(1+∑e^{t_j}). Prop 5 for k≥3, Σ=I, Z∼N(0,I_{k−1}), assumes invertibility of M↦D M=E[Z(∇σ^{lr}(Θ*^T Z) M Z)^T]. Then for small ε exists bad set T_ε of Lebesgue measure≤ε with Θ_1(ε)/||Θ_1(ε)||≠Θ*/||Θ*||. Theorem 3: if Θ*=U*T* with orthogonal U* and nonsingular T*, for each m exists T_m with Θ_m=U*T_m, ||T_m||→∞ and T_m/||T_m||→T*/||T*||. Text says pair-based surrogate risks can be inconsistent even with K7M and linear model correct except on ε-fraction, while T4K recovers optimal linear predictor asymptotically.

Fitted logistic loss (15) with θ_k=0; gradient condition for minimizer Θ_m: E[X(σ^{lr}(Θ_m^T X)−ρ_m(Θ*^T X))^T]=0. Binary k=2 Gaussian result: Θ_m=t_mΘ* even with misspecified link. Defines σ^ε(t)=σlr(t) outside T_ε and uniform inside T_ε, but prose reverses cases; also claims link satisfies ordering consistency/K7M, conflicting with uniform values on T_ε under ordering condition. Defines L_{m,ε}, Θ_m(ε), and general L_{m,σ}; states Θ_1(0)=Θ* and arbitrarily small positive corruption destroys unaggregated consistency; aggregation gives robustness under misspecification if some link describes X–Y.

Section 5 numerical illustrations. Experiment 1 D4X/squared hinge φ(δ)=max{1−δ,0}^2, unaggregated ψ(ε)=ε^2. Using binary lemma with δ=1, α=0, C_MT=1 gives ψ_m(ε)=1/16(ε−sqrt(32/m log 40))_+. Figure 1 uses m={2^16,2^20,2^24,2^28,2^32}. Experiment 2 mis-specified logistic: corrupted link \tildeσ(t)=σlr(t) for ||t||≤r and σlr(αt) for ||t||>r; d=2,k=3, θ1*=(0,1), θ2*=(1,1), r=3, α=0.1, trials 100, error bars 95%. Internal errors found: text says m≤256 but table includes m=1024; Figure 2 error formula uses || ||T_m||−T*/||T*|| ||, contradicting Theorem 3 target T_m/||T_m||→T*/||T*|| and dimensionally mismatched.

Section 6 discussion: frames results as showing limitations of uncleaned labels and robustness gains from cleaning. Notes many consistency results rely on m→∞; ranking has explicit finite-m guarantees; joint theory in (ell,φ,m) remains open. Says beyond binary κ(X) can be large even with low Nα noise α≈1, while binary κ=1. Mis-specified-model discussion says results require K7M/Bayes-optimal classifier in F; classical surrogate consistency can fail even there while aggregation succeeds. Mentions extending aggregation comparisons to H-consistency/restricted classes as future work.

Section 2 preliminaries:
- Two regimes: unrestricted Borel F with classical Fisher consistency; and parametric/potentially misspecified F, with aggregation improving consistency in each.
- Data: iid (Xi,Yi) ~ P on X x Y. Scores f:X→R^d decoded by d:R^d→Y; prediction yhat=d∘f(x).
- Distribution-dependent task criterion defined as R(f)=E_P[ ell(d∘f(X), P(.|X)) ] (eq. 2). For multiclass Y={1,...,k}, ell(yhat,P)=sum_y P(Y=y)1{yhat≠y}, giving standard zero-one error.
- Instantaneous task formulation for ell:YxY→R_+: R(f)=E_P[ell(d∘f(X),Y)] (eq. 1). Binary classification: d=1, decoder sgn, ell(y,y’)=1{yy’≤0}, R(f)=P(Y f(X)≤0). Task losses can be nonsmooth/nonconvex/flat; use surrogate phi:R^d x Y→R, R_phi(f)=E phi(f(X),Y), requiring consistency with task criterion.

Section 2.1 label aggregation:
- Aggregated surrogate risk: R_{phi,A}(f)=E[phi(f(X), A(Z))] (eq. 3), assessed against actual task-risk minimization. Z in Z, aggregation space A, map A:Z→A, nonnegative surrogate phi:R^d x A→R_+.
- Repeated labeling: Z=(Y1,...,Ym) in Y^m with Yi|X=x iid P_{Y|X=x}. Aggregator A_m(Z)=argmin_{y in Y} sum_{l=1}^m ell(y,Y_l). For 0-1 loss this is majority vote; general ell allows other procedures.
- Rough KNN construction: X has Y and additional independent draws (Xi,Yi)_{i=1}^m iid P; Z=(Y,(Xi,Yi)_{i=1}^m). Order neighbors by distance to X with X_(0)=X; A_{m,K}(Z)=argmin_y sum_{l=0}^K ell(y,Y_(l)), K≥0. Population-level repeated-sampling treatment also extends to aggregation from one sample in Appendix C.

errors.claim: “plotted classification-rule error is $\left\|\|T_m\|-T^\star/\|T^\star\|\right\|$”

errors.explanation: The convergence result concerns the normalized matrix/direction $T_m/\|T_m\|$, not the scalar norm $\|T_m\|$. The plotted error formula subtracts a normalized matrix from a scalar norm, contradicting the stated asymptotic target and is dimensionally inconsistent.

Paper title: “Some Robustness Properties of Label Cleaning” by Chen Cheng and John Duchi.

Main setup: task risk R(f)=E ell(d∘f(X),Y) or E ell(d∘f(X),P(.|X)); surrogate risk R_phi(f)=E phi(f(X),Y). Aggregation observes Z and A:Z→A, aggregated surrogate risk R_{phi,A}=E phi(f(X),A(Z)).

Sec.3 consistency: F all Borel. Fisher consistency iff pointwise calibration psi>0. Prop.3 aggregation: phi Fisher consistent iff aggregated calibration positive; comparison psi_A(R(f)-R*)≤R_{phi,A}(f)-R_{phi,A}*. Ranking: without aggregation convex score surrogates inconsistent for k≥3; with repeated comparisons aggregated to wins vector, squared loss Fisher consistent if m≥k. Identifying surrogates: Def.3.1 margins with constants C1,C2; binary hinge (1,2). Generalized majority vote A_m. Cor.3.2: m(n)→∞ and identifying => aggregated surrogate excess→0 implies task excess→0. Level-(xi,zeta) consistency has comparison to aggregated surrogate excess; earlier formula typo used R_phi(f)-R*. Noise: Delta=min excess conditional risk for wrong prediction; binary Delta=|2P(Y=1|X)-1|. MT condition Nα/Mβ equivalence claimed via β=α/(1−α) (α=1 issue). Condition number kappa; e_m(t)=t sqrt((2/m)log(4k(C1+C2)/C1)). Theorem 1: if R−R* ≥ 2P(kappa>M)+(4 C_MT e_m(M))^{1/(1−α)}, then R−R*≤(16/C1) aggregated surrogate excess; xi_m inf threshold, xi_m→0. Cor.3.3 thresholds: binary (32 C_MT²/m log(8(C1+C2)/C1))^{1/[2(1−α)]}; k≥3: 4*(32 C_MT^4/m log(4k(C1+C2)/C1))^{α/[2(1−α²)]}. Text later says α=1 with m large gives xi=0 though formulas undefined.

Examples: binary nonsmooth margin Lemma 3.1 feasible C1=phi(0)-phi(delta), C2=phi(-delta); comparison 16/C1. Bipartite matching: k=N!, normalized Hamming, structured hinge C1=1/N,C2=2; threshold includes 4*(32 C_MT^4/m log(4k(2N+1)))^{α/[2(1−α²)]}; comparison should be 16N times aggregated excess, but text wrote A_n. General structured Lemma 3.3: structured hinge C1=min loss, C2=max tau+1; binary embeddings+normalized Hamming tau=1,C2=2. Final specialization omitted leading 4 and used 8/C1 instead of 16/C1.

Sec.4 restricted classes. 4.1 binary: Y={±1}, zero-one ell=1{ys≤0}, margin varphi(s,y)=phi(sy), phi convex. All-measurable Fisher iff phi'(0)<0. Linear F. Optimally predictable along theta*: sign matches Bayes sign. Prop.4: for any eps and nonzero theta*, ∃P optimally predictable along theta* such that all surrogate minimizers have larger task risk than theta* and |cos angle|≤eps. Notation issue: proposition uses E[phi(f_theta(X),Y)] although phi unary. Majority A_m: epsilon_m-argmin E[phi(A_m(Ys)f_theta(X))] yields R→R* and cos(theta_m,theta*)→1.

4.2 multiclass: Y=[k], zero-one, decoder argmax. F linear cone centered and closed under positive scaling. Surrogate varphi Fisher consistent and limiting loss condition (13). Examples: multiclass logistic and pairwise margin losses. Theorem 2: if F cone optimally predicts P, P(Delta>0)=1, majority vote A_m, epsilon_m→0, then epsilon_m-argmins of aggregated surrogate risk have R(f_m)→R*.

4.3 finite-dimensional multiclass: X=R^d,Y=[k], linear predictors Θ=[θ1…θ_{k−1}], θ_k=0. True p_Θ via link σ satisfying condition (14): t_y=max_i t_i iff σ_y(t)=max_i σ_i(t), t_k=0. Logistic loss Eq.(15). k=2 Gaussian: misspecified link gives Θ_m=t_mΘ*, classification consistent all m. k≥3: slight misspecification can fail. σ^ε definition/prose reversed; claim σ^ε satisfies (14) false inside T_ε unless ties. Prop.5: for k≥3, Σ=I, invertible linear map assumption, ∃small ε and T_ε measure≤ε with Θ_1(ε)/||Θ_1(ε)|| ≠ Θ*/||Θ*||. Theorem3: if Θ*=U*T* with U* orthogonal and T* nonsingular, then ∃T_m with Θ_m=U*T_m for every m, ||T_m||→∞ and T_m/||T_m||→T*/||T*||.

Sec.5 numerics. Exp.1 truncated quadratic/squared hinge phi(δ)=max{1−δ,0}²; Bartlett calibration ψ(ε)=ε². Uses Lemma 3.1 δ=1, phi(0)=1, phi(1)=0, phi(−1)=4, so ψ_m=(1/16)(ε−sqrt((32/m)log40))_+. Internal inconsistency: subsection/figure says noise exponent/plotted bounds α=1/2, but displayed formula is explicitly for no low-noise α=0. Exp.2 k=3,d=2 logistic with corrupted link \tildeσ(t)=σ_lr(t)1{||t||≤r}+σ_lr(αt)1{||t||>r}, r=3, α=0.1, true θ1=(0,1), θ2=(1,1). Caption’s error metric written as || ||T_m||−T*/||T*|| ||, conflicting with Theorem3 target T_m/||T_m||→T*/||T*||.

Sec.6 discussion: frames future work. Notes many consistency results use m→∞, while ranking Sec.3.1 has explicit finite-m guarantees; asks for surrogate consistency theory depending on (ell,varphi) and m. Says kappa(X)=1 trivially in binary, but can be large despite low MT noise α≈1 beyond binary. Says mis-specified-model results, especially Sec.4.3, require optimal predictability (Bayes classifier in F); future work should move beyond. Mentions restricted-class comparison inequalities/H-consistency as future direction, including aggregation possibly improving consistency/rates for restricted F.

Paper title: “Some Robustness Properties of Label Cleaning” by Chen Cheng and John Duchi.

Abstract claims:
- Learning procedures relying on aggregated/cleaned labels (label information distilled from noisy responses) have robustness properties impossible without data cleaning.

Abstract claims:

Introduction key claims:
- Modern supervised datasets often require cleaning/filtering/crowdsourcing multiple labels and denoising; paper investigates how data aggregation improves consistency of fitted models.
- Main thesis: label cleaning/aggregating labels provides robustness impossible without aggregation.
- Two faces of robustness:
  1. Improved consistency of estimation: when minimizing surrogate losses (e.g. multiclass logistic) instead of task losses (e.g. zero-one error), aggregated-label procedures can achieve consistent/optimal prediction in the limit when impossible without aggregation.
  2. Even in finite-dimensional statistical problems, aggregation can provide consistent classifiers when standard methods fail.
- Motivating questions: whether aggregation is needed for surrogate consistency, and if it helps, in what sense.
- Paper proposes concrete examples in ranking and binary/multiclass classification with linear estimators where estimators using only pairs (X,Y) necessarily fail but label aggregation yields consistency.
- Develops new notions/theory for surrogate consistency with data aggregation.
- In fully nonparametric scenarios, shows how number of aggregated samples combines with noise conditions to improve consistency.
- Claims aggregation permits surrogate risk consistency under only weak conditions on the surrogate loss; losses using aggregated labels admit approximate linear comparison inequalities.
- Unlike conventional risk consistency theory requiring hypothesis class F of all measurable functions, paper will show classification results where aggregating labels guarantees consistency even over restricted hypothesis classes, which may fail without aggregation.

Background mentioned:
- Surrogate risk consistency literature: Bartlett/Jordan/McAuliffe characterized binary convex surrogate consistency for zero-one error; further work in multilabel, ranking, structured prediction, ordinal regression, restricted classes, general theory.
- Existing analyses typically assume standard supervised pairs (X,Y) and do not address aggregation machinery.

Regressing on A(Z) when A(Z)≠star yields consistency; Proposition 2 begins but statement not yet shown.

errors.explanation: As written, m_{ij} sums over all possible tuples y∈Y^m and tests whether a tuple equals a single pair (i,j), so it is not an observed count from Z. This conflicts with the subsequent use of m_{ij},m_j as data-dependent counts for the observed repeated comparisons.

final_notes:
Paper title: “Some Robustness Properties of Label Cleaning” by Chen Cheng and John Duchi.

Framework: iid (X,Y). Scores f:X→R^d decoded by d; task risk R(f)=E ell(d∘f(X),Y). Aggregated surrogate R_{φ,A}(f)=E φ(f(X),A(Z)); repeated labels Z=(Y1,...,Ym) iid conditional on X. Majority/J9P aggregation chooses empirical task-risk minimizer.

Section 3 consistency: Q7D/calibration via conditional excesses. Uniform comparison: ψ(R−R*)≤ surrogate excess. Prop 1: convex φ:R^k×Y→R fails Q7D for ranking k≥3. Prop 2: squared loss to aggregated comparisons is Q7D for ranking when m≥k and aggregation counts comparisons, with star if denominator zero; possible formula issue: m_ij summed over y∈Y^m rather than observed comparisons. Prop 3: φ Q7D iff overlineψ_A(ε,x)>0; ψ_A=(overlineψ_A)** comparison; possible bad formula for uniform overlineψ_A.

J9P/W3C: finite label space card(Y)=k. J9P parameters a_y output empirical task-risk minimizer; empirical argmin eventually subset of population minimizers. W3C constants 0<C1≤C2 with parameters a_y and scores s_y decoded to y such that φ(s_y,a_y)+C1 ≤ inf_{d∘s≠y} φ(s,a_y), and φ(s_y,a_{y’})−C2 ≤ inf_s φ(s,a_{y’}). Hinge example (1,2).

Theorem 1: If φ W3C, A_m J9P, 0≤ell≤1, Nα α∈[0,1], then above threshold R−R* ≥ 2P(κ>M)+(4 C_MT e_m(M))^{1/(1−α)}, get R−R* ≤ 16/C1 · surrogate excess. ξ_m→0 for α<1; α=0 asymptotic consistency. Issues noted: formulas divide by 1−α though α=1 allowed; later α=1 says ξ=0. Cor 3.3: k=2 threshold exponent 1/[2(1−α)] log 8(C1+C2)/C1; k≥3 threshold should be 4*(32 C_MT^4/m log(4k(C1+C2)/C1))^{α/[2(1−α^2)]}; if R−R*≥ξ_{m,k}, slope 16/C1. Text says crude bound “lower bounds” ξ but corollary needs upper bound. U6A level-(ξ,ζ) consistency ψ(ε)≥ζε for ε≥ξ and ψ(R−R*)≤surrogate excess; prior paragraph wrote wrong target excess.

Noise/gaps: Δ(x)=min incorrect excess; binary Δ=|2η−1|. Nα: P(d∘f≠d∘f*)≤C_MT(R−R*)^α. Mβ: P(Δ≤ε)≤(C_MT ε)^β; equivalent β=α/(1−α). κ=max incorrect excess/min incorrect excess; binary κ=1 if P(Δ>0)=1. e_m(t)=t sqrt{(2/m)log(4k(C1+C2)/C1)}.

Examples: binary nonsmooth Lemma 3.1 margin φ convex, ∂φ(0)<0, lim∞φ=0; C1=φ(0)−φ(δ), C2=φ(−δ), k=2 threshold log 8(φ(−δ)+φ(0)−φ(δ))/(φ(0)−φ(δ)), slope 16/(φ(0)−φ(δ)); aggregation can make otherwise inconsistent φ consistent. Matching surrogate W3C C1=1/N,C2=2; threshold display 4*(32 C_MT^4/m log(4k(2N+1)))^{α/[2(1−α^2)]}; slope 16N; display uses A_n not A_m. Structured/A3J max-margin: Lemma W3C C1=min_{hat≠y}ell(hat,y), C2=max_y τ(y)+1; if v binary and ell=1/(2d)||vhat−v||_1 then τ=1,C2=2. Structured consistency display possible errors: missing leading 4, slope 8/min ell vs theorem 16/min ell, sloppy/free y.

Section 4 restricted classes. Prop 4: for any ε and nonzero θ*, some binary distribution satisfies K7M along θ*, yet every unaggregated surrogate minimizer has higher risk than θ* and angle cos ≤ε, any nonnegative loss. K7M: sign(f)=sign(P(Y=1|X)−1/2); θ* minimizes measurable risk. Cor 4.1 claims as corollary to Theorem 2 aggregated approximate minimizers θ_m have risk→R(fθ*) and cos angle→1; possible error: Theorem 2 only gives risk convergence, not direction.

Section 2 preliminaries:
- Two regimes: unrestricted Borel F with classical Fisher consistency; and parametric/potentially misspecified F, with aggregation improving consistency in each.
- Data: iid (Xi,Yi) ~ P on X x Y. Scores f:X→R^d decoded by d:R^d→Y; prediction yhat=d∘f(x).
- Distribution-dependent task criterion defined as R(f)=E_P[ ell(d∘f(X), P(.|X)) ] (eq. 2). For multiclass Y={1,...,k}, ell(yhat,P)=sum_y P(Y=y)1{yhat≠y}, giving standard zero-one error.

- Repeated labeling: Z=(Y1,...,Ym) in Y^m with Yi|X=x iid P_{Y|X=x}. Aggregator A_m(Z)=argmin_{y in Y} sum_{l=1}^m ell(y,Y_l). For 0-1 loss this is majority vote; general ell allows other procedures.

Paper title: “Some Robustness Properties of Label Cleaning” by Chen Cheng and John Duchi.

Setup: task risk R(f)=E ell(d∘f(X),Y); surrogate R_phi=E phi(f(X),Y). Aggregated labels observe Z and A:Z→A; R_{phi,A}=E phi(f(X),A(Z)). Sec.3 assumes F all Borel/measurable. Fisher consistency iff pointwise calibration positive; uniform comparison via psi/biconjugate. Prop.3: for aggregation, if integrable bound on task excess, phi Fisher consistent iff pointwise aggregated calibration positive; comparison psi_A(R−R*)≤R_{phi,A}−R_{phi,A}*. Earlier uniform calibration formula possibly had inf_s instead of inf_x.

Ranking: without aggregation, for k≥3 any convex score surrogate inconsistent for ranking risk (Prop.1). With repeated pairwise comparisons and aggregation to empirical normalized wins vector/star if missing, squared loss phi(s,q)=||s−q||², phi(s,star)=0 Fisher consistent if m≥k (Prop.2). Discussion later says finite-m explicit consistency exists in ranking Sec.3.1.

Identifying surrogates: finite label space k. Def.3.1: phi is (C1,C2)-identifying if ∃a_y and scores s_y with d(s_y)=y satisfying margin inequalities (6a)/(6b). Binary hinge example (1,2). Generalized majority vote A_m minimizes empirical task loss. Cor.3.2: m(n)→∞ plus identifying: aggregated surrogate excess→0 implies task excess→0.

Level-(xi,zeta) consistency: ∃psi with psi(eps)≥zeta eps for eps≥xi and psi(R−R*)≤aggregated surrogate excess. Opening paragraph had inconsistent formula using R_phi(f)−R*.

Noise: Delta(x)=min wrong delta_l(s,x); binary Delta=|2P(Y=1|X=x)−1|. Mammen-Tsybakov: (Nα) P(d∘f≠d∘f*)≤C_MT(R−R*)^α; (Mβ) P(Delta≤eps)≤(C_MT eps)^β; claimed equivalent β=α/(1−α), problematic at α=1. Condition number kappa=max wrong delta/min wrong delta; Delta≥delta_l/kappa; binary kappa=1. e_m(t)=t sqrt((2/m)log(4k(C1+C2)/C1)). Theorem 1: identifying, majority aggregation, 0≤ell≤1, (Nα), α∈[0,1]. If R−R* ≥ 2P(kappa>M)+(4C_MT e_m(M))^{1/(1−α)}, then R−R*≤(16/C1)(R_{phi,A_m}−R_{phi,A_m}*). α=1 allowed but exponents undefined. xi_m=inf_M{...}; xi_m→0; Cor.3.2 follows α=0. Cor.3.3 explicit xi_{m,k}: binary (32 C_MT²/m log(8(C1+C2)/C1))^{1/[2(1−α)]}; k≥3: 4*(32 C_MT^4/m log(4k(C1+C2)/C1))^{α/[2(1−α²)]}. Text calls this “lower bound” though should be threshold/upper bound. If α=1 and m≥32 max{C_MT²,C_MT⁴} log(...)=O(log k), says xi=0, conflicting with formulas.

§3.3 examples: binary nonsmooth margin surrogate phi(yf), convex, subgradients at 0 negative, phi(t)→0 as t→∞. Lemma 3.1 constants C1=phi(0)−phi(delta)>0, C2=phi(−delta). Bipartite matching: |Y|=k=N!, embeddings v(G)∈R^{N²}; loss=(1/2N)||v1−v2||_1=(1/2N)||v1−v2||². Structured hinge (11). Text says C2=1 but Lemma 3.2 says C1=1/N, C2=2. Substitution threshold 4*(32 C_MT⁴/m log(4k(2N+1)))^{α/[2(1−α²)]}; comparison should be 16N times aggregated excess with A_m, but text uses A_n. General structured prediction: decoder argmax <s,v(y)>; S(y) nonempty; tau(y)=inf... Lemma 3.3 C1=min_{hat y≠y}ell(hat y,y) (free y ambiguity) and C2=max_y tau(y)+1. If v∈{0,1}^d and ell=(1/2d)||...||_1, tau=1 and C2=2. Final structured specialization claims threshold without leading 4 and comparison constant 8/min loss, conflicting with Cor.3.3/Theorem constant 16/C1 and k≥3 xi formula.

Sec.4 restricted/model class consistency. 4.1 binary: zero-one, linear F. Prop.4: for any eps>0 and nonzero theta*, exists P optimally predictable along theta* such that every surrogate minimizer theta_phi has higher task risk than theta* and |cos angle(theta_phi,theta*)|≤eps, for any nonnegative loss phi. Cor.4.1: with majority aggregation and epsilon_m→0, if P optimally predictable along theta*, then task risk→optimal and cos angle→1.

4.2 multiclass: zero-one, linear cone, sum-zero scores. Surrogate Fisher consistent and limiting loss. Optimal predictability: argmax f_y(x) lies in argmax P(Y=y|X=x). Theorem 2: if F cone optimally predicts P, unique best label a.s., epsilon_m→0, then epsilon_m-argmin of aggregated majority surrogate has R(f_m)→R*. Aggregation restores consistency over cones.

4.3 finite-dimensional multiclass linear, possible misspecification. True p_Θ via link σ satisfying consistency (14). Fit logistic to majority labels. For k=2 Gaussian, Θ_m=t_mΘ*, classification consistent despite wrong link. For k≥3, slight misspecification causes inconsistency. σ^ε formula logistic outside T, uniform inside T, but prose reverses; claim σ^ε satisfies (14), fails on uniform region. Prop.5: arbitrarily small misspecification causes no-aggregation inconsistency. Theorem 3: majority vote addresses misspecification as m→∞ assuming σ satisfies consistency (14); if Θ*=U*T*, then Θ_m=U*T_m, ||T_m||→∞, T_m/||T_m||→T*/||T*||. Discussion says these misspecified-model results require optimal predictability/Bayes classifier in F.

Sec.5 numerical illustrations. Binary truncated quadratic: phi=max{1−delta,0}², nonaggregated psi=eps²; Lemma constants C1=1,C2=4. With alpha=0,C_MT=1, psi_m(eps)=1/16(eps−sqrt((32/m)log40))_+. Claims aggregation transitions from quadratic toward linear. Multiclass logistic corrupted link tilde sigma: softmax(t) for ||t||≤r and softmax(alpha t) for ||t||>r, described as matching near origin and shrinking outside. Figure 2 claims consistency as m→∞; caption error formula inconsistent with Theorem 3: writes || ||T_m|| − T*/||T*|| || instead of normalized direction error. Experiments m={1,4,16,64,256,1024}; left fixed observations n=10000 per m; right fixed total labels n=640000/m; 95% over 100 trials.

Sec.6 discussion/future work: emphasizes unaggregated labels may be statistically efficient with fully expressive models but aggregation/cleaning more robust under restrictions/misspecification. Future directions: finite-m theory beyond ranking; limits/noise condition number kappa (large multiclass even with α≈1); misspecified models beyond optimal predictability; restricted-class comparison inequalities/H-consistency with aggregation.

Abstract claims:

Abstract claims:

Introduction key claims:
- Modern supervised datasets often require cleaning/filtering/crowdsourcing multiple labels and denoising; paper investigates how data aggregation improves consistency of fitted models.
- Main thesis: label cleaning/aggregating labels provides robustness impossible without aggregation.
- Two faces of robustness:
  1. Improved consistency of estimation: when minimizing surrogate losses (e.g. multiclass logistic) instead of task losses (e.g. zero-one error), aggregated-label procedures can achieve consistent/optimal prediction in the limit when impossible without aggregation.
  2. Even in finite-dimensional statistical problems, aggregation can provide consistent classifiers when standard methods fail.
- Motivating questions: whether aggregation is needed for surrogate consistency, and if it helps, in what sense.
- Paper proposes concrete examples in ranking and binary/multiclass classification with linear estimators where estimators using only pairs (X,Y) necessarily fail but label aggregation yields consistency.
- Develops new notions/theory for surrogate consistency with data aggregation.
- In fully nonparametric scenarios, shows how number of aggregated samples combines with noise conditions to improve consistency.
- Claims aggregation permits surrogate risk consistency under only weak conditions on the surrogate loss; losses using aggregated labels admit approximate linear comparison inequalities.
- Unlike conventional risk consistency theory requiring hypothesis class F of all measurable functions, paper will show classification results where aggregating labels guarantees consistency even over restricted hypothesis classes, which may fail without aggregation.

Background mentioned:
- Surrogate risk consistency literature: Bartlett/Jordan/McAuliffe characterized binary convex surrogate consistency for zero-one error; further work in multilabel, ranking, structured prediction, ordinal regression, restricted classes, general theory.
- Existing analyses typically assume standard supervised pairs (X,Y) and do not address aggregation machinery.

- They introduce a more sophisticated task risk depending on conditional law P(Y∈·|X): equation (2) R(f)=E_P[ ell(d∘f(X), P(·|X)) ]. Section 2.1 Label aggregation:
- Instead of output Y, observe abstract Z∈Z. Example: multiple noisy labels for each X, Z=(Y1,…,Ym)∈Y^m.
