Paper title: “From Preferences to Prejudice: The Role of Alignment Tuning in Shaping Social Bias in Video Diffusion Models.” Main claim: alignment-tuned video diffusion yields smoother but more stereotyped and temporally persistent portrayals; biases in preference data enter reward models, are amplified, and propagate into videos. QX2/VideoBiasEval separates verbs/contexts from actor gender/ethnicity and uses ethnic skew, ethnicity-conditioned gender skew, cross-variant shifts, temporal persistence.

Definitions: aligned models optimized after likelihood training via reward-weighted fine-tuning/RLHF-style optimization with learned preference/aesthetic rewards; unaligned use likelihood alone. L2V/PBSG=(N_man−N_woman)/N_total, positive men, negative women, bounded [-1,1]. Ethnic P_e=N_e/N_total; F6N/RDS_e=P_e−1/7; W3H/SDI=1−ΣP_e². “—” means zero recognizable corresponding-ethnicity instances under J7K preventing subgroup computation.

§3 QX2: event=<p,a,c>. Claimed attribute space: 4 gender categories (man, woman, neutral person, non-binary person) and 7 ethnic groups over 42 verbs. Prompt protocol: J7K = 42 person-only prompts, no explicit demographics; V9R = 294 ethnicity+person prompts, 7 groups × 42 verbs; no gender prompts. Internal issues noted: §3.2 says demographics not introduced during generation, conflicting with V9R explicit ethnicity; later says J7K removes contextual and identity cues, but it retains verb/context. Evaluation uses three VLM judges on 16 frames, extracting binary g∈{man,woman} and 7 ethnicities; conflicts with claimed four gender categories. Human verification inconsistency: exact agreement for every label vs §4 99.0% gender and 83.3% ethnicity consensus.

§4 model pairs: D8P=ModelScope unaligned; K5X=InstructVideo/A3J-aligned. B7Q=VideoCrafter-2; H4M=T2V-Turbo-V1 using U8D, InternVid2-S2, ViCLIP rewards. Table 2: D8P avg L2V .4815, White F6N .7690, W3H .0538; K5X avg L2V .5295, White F6N .7833, W3H .0267. B7Q avg L2V .7581, White F6N .6905, W3H .1252; H4M avg L2V .8306, White F6N .6381, W3H .1119. Narrative: alignment increases average gender imbalance; all overrepresent White; K5X worsens White dominance; H4M reduces White dominance but lowers diversity. Human eval: 400 videos gender/400 ethnicity, Pearson .89/.73; κ .91/.78; Fleiss .92/.82; consensus 99.0%/83.3%; full-pool vs perfect-agreement subset L2V .846→.863, W3H .745→.761, p=.68.

§5.1 image reward datasets: R9C=HPDv2, 28,783 tuples, 29 verbs, 26 valid man–woman verbs, Men 69.23% (18/26), White pref 43.34%. N6T=Pick-a-Pic, 14,958 tuples, 19 verbs, 18 valid, Women 61.11% (11/18), White pref 40.08%. Both favor White; exceptions Black bake, East Asian fish.

§5.2 reward benchmark: FLUX controlled T2I. V9R 294 ethnicity prompts; C4Z 1176 ethnicity+gender prompts. Rewards: Y2F=CLIP base; A3J=HPSv2.0/R9C; U8D=HPSv2.1/X7H/HPDv2.1; E5W=PickScore/N6T. Table 4: Y2F avg L2V −.0726, White F6N .0182, W3H .8495. A3J avg L2V .6039, White F6N −.0423, W3H .8492. U8D avg L2V −.0984, White F6N −.0189, W3H .8470. E5W avg L2V −.1157, East Asian F6N .0316, W3H .8483. Internal issue: narrative says E5W East Asian F6N=.0352 vs Table 4 .0316.

§6 reward-specific video tuning: G4S=VCM distilled from VideoCrafter-V2/VCM-VC2. Table 5 G4S avg L2V .8034, White F6N .6405, W3H .1433. +A3J avg L2V .9116, White F6N .3667, W3H .1257; +U8D avg L2V .2267, White F6N .4286, W3H .0976; +E5W avg L2V .3714, White F6N .6833, W3H .1467. Internal errors: U8D Latino F6N misreported as −.4352 though table has missing Latino F6N and −.4352 is Δ Latino L2V; claim U8D/E5W yield woman-preferred outputs conflicts with positive L2V; claim A3J reinforces White-preferred base tendency conflicts with White F6N drop from .6405 to .3667. Temporal Table 6: G4S ethnicity mean T8Q .8904, gender .9763; +M1Y .9305/.9967; +U8D .9632/.9895; +E5W .9406/.9884. Alignment improves temporal consistency.

§7 controllable preference modeling: constructs two gender preference datasets, each said to contain 2.94M preference pairs from C4Z, plus 537,660 R9C image pairs. Prompts quoted as “A/An [ethnicity] person is [action]-ing [context]”; pairs fix action/ethnicity while changing gender, including M-1 vs W-1. Z6B=man-preferred reward/RMM; P3L=woman-preferred/RMW, both fine-tuned from Y2F encoders. Table 7 reward-model L2V: Y2F avg −.0726; Z6B avg 1.5280 and group values up to 1.6300; P3L avg −.7448. Internal error: Z6B L2V values exceed possible [-1,1]. Table 8 video L2V: G4S avg .8034; +Z6B avg .9584, all groups ~.94-.98; +P3L avg .3082, all groups still positive (.1008 to .3913). Internal error: text says P3L strongly shifts toward woman preference, but positive L2V means still male-preferred, only less so. §7 also claims no neutral reward trained; P3L is deliberate counter-bias/corrective toward equilibrium; mixtures could identify optimal bias-minimizing tradeoff. Figure 6/action sensitivity: Z6B amplifies exercise,row,cook male; P3L shifts bake,sleep,sweep toward women; sensitivity formula ΔL2V divided by each reward model’s baseline L2V.

§8 conclusion/limitations: says bias auditing/mitigation needed at every stage, alignment not independently sufficient. Limitations: predefined U.S.-Census/prior-literature gender/ethnicity categories are socially constructed and miss fluidity/intersectionality/cultural nuance; VLM judges are image-level classifiers with biases; alignment experiments chiefly use single-step latent consistency distillation and limited rewards; synthetic gender-preference manipulation shows targeted modulation but not broader value alignment; fixed socially associated action taxonomy limits open-ended/novel-action generalization. Internal error: limitation claims “Exact human agreement on every attribute” made larger annotation redundant, contradicting §4 consensus rates of 99.0% gender and 83.3% ethnicity.

Broader Impact: alignment/RLHF described as improving fidelity/temporal consistency but stabilizing/entrenching bias by making stereotypes polished and natural; curated preference data can be dual-use for mitigation or intentional exclusion/propaganda; developers should monitor social composition using event-centric audits such as QX2 and treat preference-data curation with design rigor. Supplement inventory lists additional per-verb analyses, WebVid-10M training-data effects, image-reward ethnicity distributions, reward-model implementation, reward/video post-training details, and plot numbers for model/reward/reward-aligned/controllable-preference gender and ethnicity analyses.

passage: For interpretability, a $PBS_{G}$ value of $0.5$ implies that male representations occur at twice the frequency of female representations (i.e., $N_{\text{man}}=3N_{\text{woman}}$ ), while a value of $-0.5$ indicates the inverse ratio.

reply.evidence: Current part defines PBSG as (N_man - N_woman) / N_total, where N_total = N_man + N_woman. Under this definition, PBSG = 0.5 implies N_man = 3N_woman, not that male representations occur at twice the frequency of female representations.
